description: Pin the latest MoonBit toolchain version in the repo's mise config (today it is 'latest', unpinned), move packages to the current moon.pkg format, fix deprecations, and make CI build and test on the pinned version. title: M1: MoonBit IR package, IR v4
description: A MoonBit package in finos/morphir-moonbit that models Morphir IR v4 (names, paths, FQNames, types, values, patterns, literals, access control, documentation, module, package and distribution) with JSON read and write that round-trips the v4 format. Tested against the IR fixtures and MCK documents in finos/morphir spec/ir. Done when every v4 fixture reads and writes back byte-identically or semantically equal, as the MCK defines. Spec: design of morphir-ukvn. Reprioritized by Damian 2026-09-26: MoonBit first, basics before the backend.

title: Track 5: Morphir to WASM
description: MoonBit first (Damian, 2026-09-26): the basics come before the backend. M0 latest toolchain, M1 to M4 a MoonBit IR package for v4 down to v1, M5 the Morphir SDK in MoonBit, then E1 the Morphir-to-MoonBit backend and E2 the wasm, JS and native targets. Compile times and the three targets are the reasons. Capabilities in the roadmap spec (design of morphir-ukvn).

- Workspace/host execution (.5.12): TOML discovery, Scheme configuration and host adapters; PR #23, b24d61e.
- M5 (.5.11): all 248 SDK bindings and Scheme adapters, hybrid execution/native bindings, 310 pinned Elm examples and 14 exact-integer extension cases; PRs #25 and #26, M5 completed at 3cabebc.
- Project list and structured CLI output (.5.13): repeatable frontend/target filters and global --json/--json-lines, including help, dry runs and failures; PR #27, c2eaf69. Final native suite has 543 passing tests; four-target CLI and installed npm integration and hosted CI pass.

Completed tooling acquisition (.5.5) and general embedding feasibility/adapters (.5.4): PR #28, 6cedfbe8eebbddc3fabb75ad3133a1c977c35d03. Shared host/provider contract, structured toolchain commands, pinned SHA-256 acquisition with matching-core smoke tests and reuse, Node/browser in-memory compilation and execution, host imports, dependency linking, cancellation and disposal. Final suite: 553 tests per MoonBit target, nine embedding tests, real Chromium, installed npm and actual macOS/Linux acquisition; all hosted CI passed and review findings were addressed. Embedding supports Wasm/Wasm GC package compilation with host-supplied dependencies. Full Moon workspace/package resolution and asynchronous engine bridging remain future integration, with acceptance boundaries recorded on .5.4.

Next: E1 (.5.2), a backend-only extension that emits MoonBit projects from IR and verifies that moon build accepts them. Acquisition is complete, so E1 is unblocked and does not wait for A7. E2 (.5.3) then executes generated models across Wasm GC/native/JS and compares with evaluator results; current CLI/SDK target tests do not fulfill E2. A7 (.1.10), the MoonBit frontend/backend extension, remains open under Track 1 and its A2 dependency. MoonBit maintainer permission is resolved as reported by Damian on 2026-09-30. Browser and non-browser embedding remain general host integration modes.

All CLI commands must support JSON and JSON Lines. Design and plans remain in beads; preserve host abstractions for external capabilities. Merge approval is recorded in roadmap-pr-merge-approval-2026-09-26, conditional on green CI and answered review findings. Earlier handoffs naming M0/M1/M5 as next are superseded by this note.

Record implementation, tests, merge evidence and completion separately for each repository. Completion here does not complete Rust CLI behavior, installation, extension integration or end-to-end acceptance in finos/morphir. Shared contracts and shared beads do not combine those completion states; upstream work must have its own issue and evidence.

Broader roadmap design and upstream protocol/release status are unchanged.

Ion is preferred for engine processing/storage and optimization opportunities. Components may prefer or require JSON and use supported Morphir JSON boundary adapters without native Ion support. title: Validate V4 metadata against signed provider declarations
description: Add trusted semantic validation after the basic metadata preview. Native provider declaration interpretation is merged in morphir-rust#280. CLI candidate in parent #997 freshly restores the exact provider Library and inventoried contexts before deriving declarations and validating consumer assertions. This task may land alongside the preview when green, but it does not block morphir-uqub.11.
acceptance_criteria: The released CLI can validate V4 metadata against declarations from a freshly authenticated provider Library; tests cover valid assertions, wrong type/role, absent provider, tampered bytes, and malformed declarations. Parsing-only query remains explicitly unvalidated. Docs state the trust boundary. Normal prerelease qualification passes.

title: Update IR V4 types to match latest finos/morphir spec
description:
The Classic ↔ V4 converter cannot be fully implemented until we update our IR V4 type definitions to match the most recent specification from finos/morphir.

## Background
The steel thread migrate command currently only supports same-format passthrough (V4→V4, Classic→Classic). Cross-format conversion is blocked because our IR V4 types are incomplete - they use `serde_json::Value` placeholders instead of typed expressions.

## References
- V4 Spec: https://github.com/finos/morphir/blob/main/docs/spec/ir/schemas/v4/
- What's New in V4: https://github.com/finos/morphir/blob/main/docs/spec/ir/schemas/v4/whats-new.md
- Complete Example: https://github.com/finos/morphir/blob/main/docs/spec/ir/schemas/v4/complete-example.json

## Current State (What Works)
- Distribution structure (Library/Specs/Application) - matches spec
- FormatVersion (string "4.0.0" or int 4)
- Wrapper object serialization in v4.rs
- TypeAttributes/ValueAttributes with source, constraints, extensions
- Core Type enum (7 variants) - Variable, Reference, Tuple, Record, ExtensibleRecord, Function, Unit
- Core Value enum (18+ variants) including V4-only Hole, Native, External
- Literal types with IntegerLiteral (alias WholeNumberLiteral)
- JSON-level converter works for Classic ↔ V4

## Tasks (Priority Order)

### Phase 1: Serde for Type<A>
- [ ] Implement Serialize for Type<A> with V4 wrapper object format
- [ ] Implement Deserialize for Type<A> with V4 format + shorthand support
- [ ] Add tests with sample V4 type expressions
- Files: `crates/morphir-core/src/ir/type_expr.rs`, add `serde_v4.rs`

### Phase 2: Serde for Value<TA,VA>
- [ ] Implement Serialize for Value<TA,VA> with V4 wrapper object format
- [ ] Implement Deserialize for Value<TA,VA> with V4 format
- [ ] Add tests with sample V4 value expressions
- Files: `crates/morphir-core/src/ir/value_expr.rs`

### Phase 3: Replace serde_json::Value placeholders
- [ ] Replace in TypeSpecification.type_expr
- [ ] Replace in ConstructorArgSpec.arg_type
- [ ] Replace in ValueSpecification.inputs/output
- [ ] Replace in TypeDefinition.type_expr
- [ ] Replace in ConstructorArg.arg_type
- [ ] Replace in ValueDefinition.output_type
- [ ] Replace in InputTypeEntry.input_type
- [ ] Replace in ValueBody::ExpressionBody.body
- [ ] Replace in ValueAttributes.inferred_type
- File: `crates/morphir-core/src/ir/v4.rs`

### Phase 4: Add IncompleteTypeDefinition
- [ ] Add IncompleteTypeDefinition variant to TypeDefinition enum
- [ ] Include incompleteness reason (similar to HoleReason)
- [ ] Add serialization support
- Files: `crates/morphir-core/src/ir/type_def.rs`, `v4.rs`

### Phase 5: Integration Tests
- [ ] Test with real V4 IR files from finos/morphir examples
- [ ] Test round-trip conversion: V4 JSON → typed IR → V4 JSON
- [ ] Test Classic → V4 conversion produces valid V4 JSON
- [ ] Add fixtures to integration-tests/fixtures/steel-thread/

## V4 Format Details

### Wrapper Object Format
```json
{"Variable": {"name": "a"}}
{"Reference": {"fqname": "morphir/sdk:list#map", "args": [...]}}
{"Tuple": {"elements": [...]}}
{"Record": {"field-name": type, ...}}
```

### Compact Shorthand (for deserialization)
- Type variable as bare string: `"a"` instead of `{"Variable": {"name": "a"}}`
- Simple reference as FQName: `"morphir/sdk:basics#int"` 
- Reference with args: `{"Reference": ["morphir/sdk:list#list", "a"]}`

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Type<A> and Value<TA,VA> implement Serialize + Deserialize
- [ ] All serde_json::Value placeholders replaced with typed expressions
- [ ] Round-trip V4 JSON works (deserialize → serialize = same structure)
- [ ] Classic → V4 converter produces valid typed V4 IR
- [ ] Integration tests pass with real Morphir IR files

## Blocks
- Steel thread P0 completion (cross-format migration)
- morphir-rust-steel-thread

title: Pin corrected core for exact portable integers
description:
Worksheet portability exposed silent decimal integer corruption in the pinned MoonBit core on Wasm GC. The current compiler/core release is 0.10.15+943464bfa, dated 2026-10-12. BigInt.from_string repeats of 3150 nines parse to a different 3149-digit value; 10000 nines produce a wrong 9980-digit value. Independent arithmetic construction prints correctly. Source diagnosis identifies underallocated limbs in bigint_default.from_string_dec, not worksheet preview rendering.

Official upstream fixes exist: correctness-only a951c067f909286603efada85c379197d589dc61 (2026-10-13), optimized 673edc7e0da5e8d9fe2fb3652d2de9d638963d83 (2026-10-14), upstream issue4345. Current stable compiler still stops at the October12 release. Candidate immutable official core archive https://codeload.github.com/moonbitlang/core/tar.gz/a951c067f909286603efada85c379197d589dc61 has SHA25637284b6d262d5d3aeef4fb3a5115e2b796e648238e023588ecd76b453b3802b0. It bundles all4targets with the existing pinnedcompiler and passes upstream WasmGC decimal parser tests16/16 in an isolated local experiment. Active installation has not been mutated.

Implement reproducible repository-owned corrected-core selection for normal development, CI and qualification. Prefer a workspace-local isolated overlay and explicit immutable provenance. Preserve shared installed toolchains and unrelated work. Use portable MoonBit automation and align all supported bootstrap/provenance checks. Do not use a Scheme-only parser workaround: execution/SDK/Ion also use the faulty parser. Preserve the failing 10000-digit production regression, add minimal3150-digit exactness checks across all4targets, rerun focused and required repository checks, and land the fix with the worksheet work before claiming portable qualification. Evidence: .dev/diagnose-bigint/minimized.jsonl and candidate-core experiments; new Scheme bounded_preview_test production guard is currently RED on oldWasmGCcore.

design:
Native untagged Union implementation

morphir-ukvn.7.9.1 · 2026-10-18 · U2 implementation decisions

  • Goal
  • Global constraints
  • Task 2: implementation and verification
  • Local decisions
  • Review focus
  • Delivery evidence

Goal

Implement the approved U1 contract in native IR v4. A member value can flow to a declared Union without a tag or conversion. Preserve the authored Union through codecs, identities and substitution. Unsupported consumers refuse before emission or execution.

Binding contract and reference corpus: U1 contract and its sibling cases.json. Baseline source is morphir-moonbit 0c4069c5. The focused wasm-gc baseline passed 126 tests. U2 is merged; qualification and landing are recorded below.

Global constraints

  • Add Union(TypeAttributes, Array[Type]) only to current v4. At least two authored entries are required. Preserve order, duplicates, nesting and every attribute in representation operations.
  • Accept compact {"Union":[...]} and an expanded object with attributes and alternatives fields. Bare arrays remain Tuples. Validate arity on read and write. Historical downgrades refuse Union recursively.
  • Semantic equivalence and assignability are distinct from structural equality. Union membership is inclusive. No first-arm priority, implicit numeric coercion, fabricated tags or unsafe narrowing. Every source alternative must have a justified destination.
  • Unknown semantic constraints cannot establish a proof. Keep union-level and member-level obligations separate; do not discard reference-site obligations during transparent alias expansion. Opaque identity remains nominal.
  • Raw decoding succeeds only for one distinct typed interpretation after every candidate is accounted for. Multiple distinct interpretations are ambiguous; an unsupported candidate prevents a unique claim unless a declared encoding rule excludes it.
  • Backend refusal covers all used type positions, reachable internal definitions and native fast paths. U3 owns conceptual projection and ecosystem qualification; U2 must still implement native typing and decoding foundations.
  • Use existing domain enums and error families. New automation is MoonBit. Keep plans in beads and ignored local files. Conventional commits, no AI attribution. Use the pinned toolchain through mise.

Task 2: implement native Union nodes, codecs and typing

This elaborates the existing delivery task. Work is sequential within the shared checkout because the new enum affects many exhaustive consumers. Review the completed U2 diff independently before landing.

StageImplementation ownersIndependent acceptance evidence
Representation and traversalv4 types/json; identities/logical and paths; all three migration adapters; placeholders; exhaustive auxiliary walkers and WorkbenchLiteral JSON fixtures fail before implementation, then compact/expanded round trips, malformed arity, nested attributes, duplicates, generic positions and identity paths pass. Historical nested Union downgrades fail explicitly.
Native typingmorphir-typing types, conversion, solver, comparison, environment, expression and definition checks; typing tooling walkersMember-to-union result and call checks pass; unsafe narrowing and unsupported obligations fail; generic substitution preserves duplicates and attributes; permutation/overlap equivalence honors one consistent variable mapping across the entire signature.
Decoding and unsupported consumersExisting IR wire/v4 codec owner; Scheme spec and backend; Elm and MoonBit generators; execution planningConcrete scalar decoding distinguishes int/float ambiguity from duplicate equal typed values, accounts for unsupported arms, and checks outer refinements. Backend tests cover reachable private helpers, alias chains, nested lets, inferred types, pattern types and native bypasses.
Qualification and landingFocused package tests, tracked APIs and consumer documentationFour supported targets remain coherent. Focused tests run on wasm, wasm-gc, js and native; required lint, format and validation pass. Independent review and PR checks/comments complete before the authorized squash merge.

Follow test-first development at each stage, recording the failing assertion and passing command. Compiler errors establish exhaustiveness but do not substitute for behavioral RED evidence. Use expected values independent of production encoders or self-generated snapshots.

mise exec -- moon check --target wasm

mise exec -- moon check --target native

mise run lint:moonbit
mise run validate

Local decisions

  • Use the existing Scheme specification DSL form (union A B ...) for default-attribute types. This is a local adapter syntax, not approval of a universal source grammar. Existing Scheme printer attribute limitations remain documented. Cost if wrong: revise that adapter and its syntax tests.
  • Use logical child paths /alternatives/<i>, preserving authored positions. Cost if wrong: migrate new Union identity paths before downstream adoption.
  • Keep inference unification symmetric; add directional assignment checks at explicit result and call boundaries. Preserve semantic obligations rather than treating Union as a speculative choice of one arm. Cost if wrong: revise inference interfaces and affected diagnostics.
  • Keep the existing tagged execution-value decoder unchanged. Place bounded raw-union interpretation in the native codec layer with concrete tests and a usable API; do not claim conceptual projection or general runtime membership is complete. Cost if wrong: relocate the small codec API during U3 integration.
  • Source coordinates belong to each authored occurrence. Shared inference variables must not transfer one occurrence's coordinates to another; reconstruct each occurrence from its authored template. Keep checked public substitution conflicts explicit, and restrict attribute-ignoring alias expansion to the documented legacy shape comparison. Cost if wrong: revise inference metadata reconstruction while preserving the authored fields.

Review focus

  1. Silent representation loss: sorted or deduplicated members, dropped attributes, invalid singleton output, or historical downgrades that erase Union.
  2. Unsound typing: arm-order-dependent meta bindings, greedy alpha-renaming, unproved narrowing, or lost outer/member obligations.
  3. Ambiguous decoding: first success accepted, unsupported arms ignored, or distinct typed numeric values collapsed.
  4. Capability bypass: hidden alias/member types, omitted generic signatures, native accelerators or direct emitter APIs skipping refusal.
  5. Overclaiming: fixture integrity presented as runtime coverage, single-target checks presented as portability, or U3 integration presented as complete.

Delivery evidence

PR 155 was squash-merged with the maintainer-authorized admin bypass on 19 October 2026 at 03:42 UTC. The resulting commit is ed57b4abb314112f96c9aceecbbefcb606f605c9. The exact reviewed head c74b6863257e328a35ee7c28df03c77eb7f3ce8c passed CI and had zero unresolved review threads before merging.

Implementation range: 0c4069c..c74b686, including a clean integration of main at 58288d4. PR 155 carries the reviewed change. The task review identified three substantive defects: reachable dependency signatures bypassed selected execution checks, descriptive scalar provenance was treated as a refinement, and a conformance helper lacked Union traversal. Fixes have regression tests and an independent scoped re-review found all three addressed.

The final whole-branch review found that let, recursive-let and destructuring continuations lost a declared expected Union. Public regressions failed 3 of 142 tests before the fix, then all 218 typing/frontend integration tests passed. The final scoped re-review confirmed preserved scopes, generalization, escape checks and node facts, with no new findings.

PR review identified a missing bundled Application dependency alias lookup. Commit e9447bd loads public dependency modules/types while retaining full visibility for the owning package. Independent literal tests failed 2 of 16 before the fix and all 16 passed afterward, including transitive aliases, ambiguity, visibility and alias obligations. The addressed thread was replied to and resolved. Commit c74b686 refreshes generated Scheme documentation line labels after README changes; the generator check and all 198 backend/spec tests pass. A scoped independent review found both fixes addressed with no new substantive findings.

U3 remains separate: conceptual Union projection, runtime membership and ecosystem consumer qualification are not delivered by U2. design:
Intent links and revision-scoped inspection

morphir-ukvn.7.7.4 · 18 October 2026 · M4 implementation brief

  • Goal
  • Boundaries
  • Task 4: Implement and qualify intent links
  • Review focus
  • Evidence and landing

Goal

Make source, intent, requirement and claim links useful before a compiler or implementation exists. A portable MoonBit library accepts constructed conceptual records and caller-supplied KB source snapshots, produces a read-only PRD view, and reports revision-scoped evidence without inventing proof.

This implements the existing M4 task, not a new campaign. The authority is morphir-ukvn.7 and M1's exact morphir-conceptual/0.1.0-draft.1 record contract. M1 and M2 are landed. The existing plan is morphir-ukvn.7.7; M3 codecs remain a separate task.

Boundaries

  • Preserve stable logical IDs, exact revisions, original excerpts and fragment anchors. No identity derives from file position, label or guessed URI. Source context names document IDs, not local source-record IDs.
  • Reuse M1 record meanings, relationship signatures and independent concerns. Keep the existing IRUnit and MorphirModel carriers; no new envelope, package authenticator or compatibility runner.
  • The KB service owns its lifecycle. Accept its caller-supplied identities, document revision, state and excerpt without discovery, network/file acquisition or lifecycle mutation. A Released intent and accepted review never create a contract, run observation or proof.
  • Functional, data, performance, operational, regulatory and explicitly namespaced extension categories coexist. EARS notation is separate. PRD output is a view over identified requirements, not an additional authority.
  • Use closed domain variants and validated identity/revision values at public boundaries. Use existing Ion values for retained rich data. Keep effects outside the portable library.
  • Compare complete revision contexts, including exact subject sets and model, source and implementation revisions. Missing required context is inconclusive; mismatched context is stale. Keep supporting and contradicting evidence simultaneously, and distinguish analysis, review and run evidence.
  • Implement inspection of constructed inputs. Parser/DSL implementation, rich codecs, expression evaluation, general contradiction detection, proof of equivalence to prose and KB command adoption remain their owning tasks.

Task 4: Implement and qualify intent links

Execution: subagent-driven development, test first. One implementer owns the library and shared examples; the controller owns review, tracker, cross-repository landing and cleanup.

FilesResponsibility
MoonBit pkgs/morphir-conceptual/moon.mod, README.md, intent/Portable domain records and pure KB adaptation, graph inspection, PRD projection and evidence assessment. Split types, source adaptation, inspection and tests by responsibility.
MoonBit moon.work, scripts/validate-packages.mbtxRegister and validate the new module. Existing workspace CI tests its packages on supported targets. Change CI selection only if a concrete omission is found.
Parent spec/conceptual/intent/Shared examples with literal expected observations, explicit M1 and KB service source pins, source-before/source-after snapshots, mixed requirement categories, and current/stale/inconclusive/conflicting evidence.
Parent existing KB narrative/index, if neededMake the examples discoverable under existing KB conventions. Keep lifecycle ownership and exact identity semantics explicit. Do not introduce another register.

Consumes: M1 Source, SourceRef, EntityRef, Relationship and RevisionContext semantics; existing Rust KB intent service identities and lifecycle vocabulary at the pinned parent submodule. No MoonBit conceptual or KB package currently exists. Constructed domain inputs can expose the M1 slice needed here without claiming a complete graph decoder.

Produces: public pure operations adapt_kb_source, inspect, prd_view and assess_claim, with typed inputs and results. KB adaptation returns retained source/intent metadata without synthesizing obligations. Inspection returns identified diagnostics and independent gaps. PRD rows retain category, exact text, intent/source links and formalization/evidence gaps. Claim assessment returns each supporting/contradicting observation with its kind and freshness, never a Boolean proof. The implementer fixes concrete type signatures against M1 before writing code and records them in the report.

  1. Read the M1 contract and existing KB service. Record exact public types/signatures and map every required behavior to a test. Report a real conflict before building; settle routine internal choices within these boundaries.
  2. Write failing tests for caller-supplied KB snapshots and preserved source text/anchors, renamed/moved sources, and two explicit edited model snapshots. Verify failures before implementation.
  3. Implement the typed records and pure source/intent adapter. Historical snapshots remain available; edits do not silently retarget old evidence.
  4. Write failing graph/PRD tests for mixed and extension requirement categories, many-to-many links, unresolved versus malformed resolved references, wrong endpoint kinds, duplicate identities and missing fragments. Implement inspection and the read-only view.
  5. Write failing evidence tests for exact current context, changes in each revision dimension, missing required context, reordered versus changed subject sets, simultaneous support/contradiction, unknown evidence and review/type-check results that are not behavioral proof. Implement assessment without invoking a checker.
  6. Test every existing KB lifecycle state as read-only input. Changing the supplied state alone must not create formalization or evidence. Add independently authored parent examples and a concise usage guide with source pins and documented limits.
  7. Run focused MoonBit tests on wasm, wasm-gc, JavaScript and native; check formatting, generated public interfaces and module registration. Run required repository checks, review both diffs, commit, open PRs, monitor and land only after green CI.

Review focus

  • Same short KB intent ID in two bundles must not alias; caller-supplied document identity and revision remain authoritative.
  • Source moves and changed wording keep stable links while historical excerpts and evidence remain scoped to their original snapshot.
  • Missing or extra context members and duplicate IDs must not make evidence appear current through subset matching or last-write-wins.
  • Unknown or unresolved references stay visible; fabricated resolved references and wrong relationship endpoint kinds cannot count as valid links.
  • Released lifecycle, accepted human review, generated scenarios and successful type analysis never silently become proof of requirement fulfillment.

Evidence and landing

MoonBit baseline: 0ee036c2459a0952a11de7e3f9db28edcaf3593f. Parent baseline: 7920a6b6. The shared specification export is preserved locally under .dev/m4/. Exact source revisions and API choices will be recorded with the implementation.

Baseline MoonBit formatting, YAML/package validation and the existing core wasm-gc test pass. Existing YAML line-length warnings predate this change. Runtime tests must establish the new behavior; fixture integrity alone is insufficient. Independent task and final reviews cover both repositories. M4 closes only when implementation and shared examples have landed, all required checks pass, and the tracker is synced.

This document is a task implementation brief. The owning M4 bead stores its full HTML; the parent plan retains execution ledger comments. Published examples are canonical in the parent repository. No consumer task is completed by this delivery.

# M4 implementer report

Status: DONE. The controller committed the frozen snapshots for review as primary
`205910d` and parent `c6e14057`. The implementer created no commits.

Implemented `morphir-ukvn.7.7.4` in the MoonBit workspace and its parent example
checkout. No beads commands, commits, pushes, merges or subagents were used.
The temporary cleanup stop preserved the unfinished work; implementation resumed
from those files when the controller explicitly resumed M4.

## Result and compatibility decisions

The new `finos/morphir-conceptual/intent` package provides four pure operations:

```moonbit
pub fn adapt_kb_source(KbSnapshot) -> AdaptedSource raise InvalidInput
pub fn inspect(Model) -> Inspection
pub fn prd_view(Model) -> PrdView
pub fn assess_claim(Model, ResolvedRef, RevisionContext) -> ClaimAssessment
```

The generated `intent/pkg.generated.mbti` is the complete public interface.

- `Id`, `Revision`, `Category` and `NonemptyText` are opaque validated types.
  IDs and revisions retain exact nonempty text. Categories require a namespace.
  Reasons and locators use descriptive text, not identity types.
- `KbSnapshot` requires caller-supplied document/source/intent identities and
  revisions plus an exact fragment. `AdaptedSource` returns the retained Source,
  intent and KB origin. It creates no requirements, contracts or evidence.
- The KB short ID is only leading filename digits, scoped to its bundle. The
  existing JSON view has no document revision. Bundle, number, slug and optional
  state remain provenance; none determines stable logical identity.

  decoder or replacement carrier. `Contract`, `Declaration`, `Scenario` and
  `Implementation` expose only the links needed here. The caller retains the
  full original records. Contract clause kinds retain their function/type
  subject requirements; full binder and signature checking remains outside M4.
- Resolved references select exact model/entity revisions in explicitly supplied
  dependency snapshots. Unresolved references retain locator, expected kind and
  reason. Duplicate records, missing resolved targets, wrong revisions, missing
  fragments and wrong endpoint kinds remain structural errors. Duplicate
  dependency snapshots and cycles are rejected rather than selecting one.

  links or assessed observations. Inspection also reports independent missing
  formalization, examples, implementation binding and evidence gaps.
- `RevisionContext::new` copies its arrays, rejects duplicate IDs in each list
  and exposes copied lists. Matching compares complete exact model, entity,
  source-document and implementation sets, ignoring order. Required dependencies
  combine the claim's declared set with its reachable link/source facts,
  claim/observation/relationship source refs and run clauses. Missing members or
  unavailable relevant sources are inconclusive. Changed revisions or additional
  set members are stale. Supplied snapshot revisions also participate, so two
  matching old contexts cannot hide a source edit. Run clauses must agree with
  the evidence's recorded entity revisions.
- `ClaimAssessment` retains every supporting and contradicting observation with
  its relationship identity, kind, payload and currency. No evidence is Unknown.
  Invalid graph/query is InvalidClaim. There is no proof Boolean. Current review,
  type analysis and absent run output retain their original meanings.
- Existing `moonrockz/ion/ion.IonValue` carries notation, descriptive data, scope,
  scenario data, analysis results, run inputs/outputs/configuration and provenance.
  Tests cover exact integers, decimal scale, symbols, typed nulls and annotations.

### Findings and changes

   closure. Their exact entity snapshot must have one supplied Contract owner;
   missing or ambiguous ownership yields inconclusive currency. The selected
   clause contributes its SourceRefs, contract declaration, declaration binding,
   implementation artifact and linked structured dependencies through the same
   traversal used for claims. This closes the case where both recorded/requested
   contexts omitted a structured dependency yet the run appeared current.
2. Inspection discovers Supports/Contradicts assertions across the supplied root
   closure. Each assertion is validated and its evidence resolved in the asserting
   model's scope. Dependency-owned claims and requirements no longer receive a
   false MissingEvidence gap for a root assertion; stale/inconclusive diagnostics
   agree with assessment while retaining the claim's diagnostic path. Assertion
   SourceRefs resolve against the asserting model, not the claim's model.
3. `EvidenceAssessment` now exposes `relationship_model: Snapshot` alongside
   `relationship: Id`. This identifies the exact enclosing model revision for
   each assertion, including two models with the same local relationship ID and
   identical evidence/claim endpoints. No compatibility wrapper was introduced.

## Result and compatibility decisions

The new `finos/morphir-conceptual/intent` package provides four pure operations:

```moonbit
pub fn adapt_kb_source(KbSnapshot) -> AdaptedSource raise InvalidInput
pub fn inspect(Model) -> Inspection
pub fn prd_view(Model) -> PrdView
pub fn assess_claim(Model, ResolvedRef, RevisionContext) -> ClaimAssessment
```

The generated `intent/pkg.generated.mbti` is the complete public interface.

- `Id`, `Revision`, `Category` and `NonemptyText` are opaque validated types.
  IDs and revisions retain exact nonempty text. Categories require a namespace.
  Reasons and locators use descriptive text, not identity types.
- `KbSnapshot` requires caller-supplied document/source/intent identities and
  revisions plus an exact fragment. `AdaptedSource` returns the retained Source,
  intent and KB origin. It creates no requirements, contracts or evidence.
- The KB short ID is only leading filename digits, scoped to its bundle. The
  existing JSON view has no document revision. Bundle, number, slug and optional
  state remain provenance; none determines stable logical identity.
- The state vocabulary exactly matches the pinned service: Backlog, Refinement,
  InProgress, Released, Cancelled, Superseded. Missing state stays absent. The
  service owns lifecycle transitions; no lifecycle API was added or replaced.
- The pinned KB service has no PRD operation. `prd_view` is a read-only projection
  of supplied requirements with exact text, category, notation, source refs and
  intent/source/contract/scenario/claim/evidence links.
- `Model` is a constructed M1 **inspection slice**, not a complete M1 graph
  decoder or replacement carrier. `Contract`, `Declaration`, `Scenario` and
  `Implementation` expose only the links needed here. The caller retains the
  full original records. Contract clause kinds retain their function/type
  subject requirements; full binder and signature checking remains outside M4.
- Resolved references select exact model/entity revisions in explicitly supplied
  dependency snapshots. Unresolved references retain locator, expected kind and
  reason. Duplicate records, missing resolved targets, wrong revisions, missing
  fragments and wrong endpoint kinds remain structural errors. Duplicate
  dependency snapshots and cycles are rejected rather than selecting one.
- Invalid graphs retain PRD rows and diagnostics but expose no usable assertion
  links or assessed observations. Inspection also reports independent missing
  formalization, examples, implementation binding and evidence gaps.
- `RevisionContext::new` copies its arrays, rejects duplicate IDs in each list
  and exposes copied lists. Matching compares complete exact model, entity,
  source-document and implementation sets, ignoring order. Required dependencies
  combine the claim's declared set with its reachable link/source facts,
  claim/observation/relationship source refs and run clauses. Missing members or
  unavailable relevant sources are inconclusive. Changed revisions or additional
  set members are stale. Supplied snapshot revisions also participate, so two
  matching old contexts cannot hide a source edit. Run clauses must agree with
  the evidence's recorded entity revisions.
- `ClaimAssessment` retains every supporting and contradicting observation with
  its relationship identity, kind, payload and currency. No evidence is Unknown.
  Invalid graph/query is InvalidClaim. There is no proof Boolean. Current review,
  type analysis and absent run output retain their original meanings.
- Existing `moonrockz/ion/ion.IonValue` carries notation, descriptive data, scope,
  scenario data, analysis results, run inputs/outputs/configuration and provenance.
  Tests cover exact integers, decimal scale, symbols, typed nulls and annotations.

   closure. Their exact entity snapshot must have one supplied Contract owner;
   missing or ambiguous ownership yields inconclusive currency. The selected
   clause contributes its SourceRefs, contract declaration, declaration binding,

design:
M3 rich conceptual model codecs

morphir-ukvn.7.7.3 · 2026-10-18 · Implementation brief for controller review

  • Goal
  • API and ownership
  • Operation coverage
  • Independent tests
  • Decisions and limits
  • Delivery evidence
  • Controller rulings

Goal

Retain the complete M1 graph and M2 traits inside the existing IRUnit unit-owned metadata entry, with useful typed inspection and explicit refusal of unsupported interpretation or lossy export. Reuse IonValue and the existing ion-text, ion-binary and morphir-json registry codecs. Inputs are the approved representation design and M1/M2 contracts from parent revision a009be246302cf7705f5ab64572bfdc74a5e5fd8. Baseline is MoonBit 53d6e2b9bb75e730cfbd1d5a25792dbd63189eb5 with 70 focused tests passing.

API and ownership

FilesResponsibility
Model packageGraph read/write against IonValue, versioned record views for sources, entities, relationships, capabilities, trait definitions and applications; closed entity-kind and reference variants; validated identities and revisions. Retain original Ion records and opaque content so unknown fields, rich values and independent concern records survive. Inspection exposes indexed records, source text, reference gaps, independent concerns, projection gaps and unsupported requirements. A record view is a lossless reading API, not a complete semantic validator.
Engine data adapterIRUnit attachment and extraction at unit:<id>; refuse occupied owner without modification. Definition-to-specification projection reuses the existing IR projection and retains graph, annotations, provenance and surviving sidecar owners; refuse owner loss. Explicit bare export delegates to the registry's existing refusal.
Manifests, generated APIs, scoped READMEs and testsAdd conceptual/model as engine dependency. Keep conceptual/intent untouched. Check in exact fixed fixture assets with upstream revision and case mapping.

Files: pkgs/morphir-conceptual/model/records.mbt, decode.mbt, inspection.mbt, and pkgs/morphir-engine/data/conceptual.mbt.

Graph and record constructors are private. Decode validates the structural fields used by the reader and rejects duplicate record members and logical IDs. Opaque Ion payloads, including nested descriptive structs, retain duplicate fields. Encoding returns the original validated graph value, rather than rebuilding a JSON subset. Public record APIs expose typed identity, kind, references and direct access to retained fields.

Operation coverage

OperationM3 behavior
roundTripActual existing Ion text and binary encode/decode, full semantic graph and IR equality, with independent fixed observations. M1 0001, 0003, 0010 and M2 0024, 0047.
attachGraph / exportBareIrUnit-owner conflict refusal and existing data.lossy_conversion refusal. M1 0019, 0012; M2 0025.
definitionToSpecificationPublic Library signature extraction with exact authored expected Specs asset, retaining the entire graph and surviving carrier metadata. M1 0021. Metadata targeting removed IR nodes causes refusal rather than silent deletion.
inspectExact-profile and duplicate-identity diagnostics, local revision-scoped reference validation, retained unresolved references, source pin gaps, independent elaboration/definition/recovery/review/implementation facts, unknown kinds and required semantic gaps, projection gaps and trait records/provenance. Authored fixture observations establish supported inspection behavior.
check / execute / typed trait validationExplicit unsupported result. Required profiles and critical members are exposed and refused by the interpretation gate. Storage remains lossless. No evaluator, payload assignability, provider authentication or execution evidence claim.
assessEvidence / linked-metadata projection / MEP transportRetain all records and contexts, without adding these operations. M4 owns its existing evidence/link inspection slice; negotiated MEP transport stays unchanged.

Independent tests

Copy authored fixture assets unchanged into test fixtures; compare exact known IDs, revisions, source whitespace, required diagnostics and independently authored expected projection IR. Literal expected data is never generated by the codec. Tests load JSON-compatible assets with the Ion reader and rich .ion assets directly. Include both complete graph equality and fixed field observations to prevent a paired encoder/decoder defect from passing unnoticed.

  • Prose-only, mixed graph, independent concerns, contract kinds, trait model and dictionary preservation.
  • Exact integer, decimal scale, symbol/string distinction, typed null, annotation order, opaque duplicate fields and unknown application members.
  • Duplicate graph/entity/reference members; duplicate IDs across record lists; absent/revision-mismatched local targets; unsupported draft profile.
  • Occupied and duplicate unit owners, unchanged sidecars, legacy graph-free profiles, bare-export refusal, projection gaps and required-semantic refusal.
  • Trait application provenance and competing assertions retained with no silent merge or invented validation.

Follow red/green evidence for each behavior family; run conceptual/model, conceptual/intent and engine/data tests, format/API checks and the repository suite. Controller owns independent review and pre-push checks.

Decisions and limits

The new model package owns lossless records and structural inspection. It does not expand the intentionally bounded M4 intent types into a second representation of the full graph. Unknown rich data remains Ion throughout. Distinct profile versions stay exact. Unknown required semantics prevent interpretation, not preservation. The graph remains one existing metadata entry; no new transport tuple, Distribution case, envelope or compatibility runner is introduced.

Inspection accepts an optional caller-supplied dependency context keyed by declared inputId and exact model snapshot. It resolves only declared, supplied snapshots. A claimed resolved reference with an absent or mismatched snapshot is invalid with the contract's missing/revision diagnostic; an intentionally unresolved reference remains a gap. Tests cover supplied exact success, missing input, wrong revision and undeclared supplied input. No ambient lookup or acquisition occurs. Public APIs must not expose mutable aliases that invalidate the privately validated graph.

Delivery evidence

Squash merged MoonBit PR 149 on 18 October 2026 as 0c4069c5. Reviewed commits were 000342d, 49b0544 and febd5dc, based on 53d6e2b. The maintainer authorized squash merge with admin bypass. The exact reviewed head passed 34 CI checks with two policy-selected skips, and its sole GitHub review thread was addressed and resolved before merge.

The task review found three structural defects, all repaired and approved in scoped re-review: digest shape and unverified pin reporting; resolved-only subject, parent and provenance references; exact model target resolution. The whole-branch review then found target kind/role and unsupported-target disclosure gaps plus double-prefixed dependency diagnostic paths. Both were repaired and approved. The same final repair explicitly owns Blob/Clob buffers, addressing the GitHub comment and passing independent scoped review. No review finding remains deferred.

Both fix waves added tests before production edits and reproduced six runtime failures each. The final focused command was mise exec -- moon test --target TARGET -p finos/morphir-conceptual/model -p finos/morphir-conceptual/intent -p finos/morphir-engine/data. All 109 tests passed on wasm, wasm-gc, JavaScript and native. Final lint, formatting and validation gates passed. Full initial-commit unit suites passed 2,096 wasm, 2,096 wasm-gc, 2,239 JavaScript and 2,198 native tests. These initial counts are distinguished from final-commit verification.

The controller independently compared all 11 fixture assets and embedded literals with the pinned parent input. Existing runtime setup required the repository's pinned-core setup and locked Bun dependencies. No task automation, carrier schema or parent repository source changed.

Final frozen-head CLI integration passed on all four targets and through the installed npm package. Compiler integration passed its native, Node and installed-package execution matrix, 60 fault cases, and rich pricing parity across js, wasm-gc and native in debug and release modes. All required lint, format and validation gates passed.

The first final-head JavaScript CI attempt failed an unchanged worksheet browser assertion with seven observations instead of three. Twelve narrow reproductions and the unchanged exported worksheet workflow passed locally. The single CI retry passed on identical source; the initial cause remains unconfirmed. No worksheet change was made. CI run 39164263333, attempt 2, is the final green evidence.

Controller rulings

  1. Use the already approved M1/M2 draft contracts without reopening design approval. Later draft changes may require adapter changes.
  2. Resolve only explicitly supplied graphs through declared input IDs and exact revisions. No ambient lookup or fallback. A broader resolver remains a separate integration.
  3. Preserve well-formed digest claims but keep unrevisioned sources unpinned because M3 has no byte-verification fact. Verified digest evidence will require an explicit later integration.
  4. Keep semantic validation, artifact/provider binding, expression and evidence execution, dictionary completeness, streaming guarantees and alternate transports outside this bounded reader. The relevant interpretation operations refuse or disclose gaps. Consumers needing those capabilities require separate implementations.
  5. Copy Blob/Clob buffers defensively even though the safe core Bytes API is immutable. Unsafe aliases can reach externally supplied Ion. The stronger private-ownership guarantee costs an extra allocation for binary fields.
acceptance_criteria: Ion text/binary semantic round-trips retain IDs, metadata, sidecars and unresolved facts; bare IR export refuses required loss; old consumers remain supported for their advertised profile.

Approved HTML brief stored and verified by exact export comparison; shared tracker push succeeded after one normal pull/retry.

# Domain examples and independently reviewed expectations

Goal: Build independent domain corpora in parallel so language and checker decisions are grounded in real requirements.

Spec: morphir-ukvn.7, design draft 0.16; roadmap morphir-ukvn. HTML delivery plan: .dev/beads-plans/morphir-ukvn.7.15.html.

These are delivery task briefs, not permission to treat open grammar, domain or profile choices as settled. Each task fixes its local interface and executable test details before code changes. Review artifacts use the repository HTML template and live in beads. Shared contracts/fixtures live in finos/morphir; MoonBit implementations live here. Proposed new paths must be reconciled with repository layout on pickup. Reuse existing model envelopes, KB identities and Gherkin/MCK runners. Preserve unrelated work. Run focused tests and required repository checks before code pushes; merges/releases require the existing maintainer authorization. No product implementation is performed by this decomposition.

Dependencies are task/artifact edges, never implied by list order or parent membership. Unlisted coordination is nonblocking. Implementation workers use the appropriate execution skill after reading the linked contract and task brief. Exact interfaces created by design tasks become inputs to their consumers.

title: Conceptual model, traits and intent graph
description:
# Conceptual model, traits and intent graph

Goal: Represent valid concepts, requirements, contracts and evidence before implementation, with stable identities and explicit elaboration state.

Spec: morphir-ukvn.7, design draft 0.16; roadmap morphir-ukvn. HTML delivery plan: .dev/beads-plans/morphir-ukvn.7.7.html.

These are delivery task briefs, not permission to treat open grammar, domain or profile choices as settled. Each task fixes its local interface and executable test details before code changes. Review artifacts use the repository HTML template and live in beads. Shared contracts/fixtures live in finos/morphir; MoonBit implementations live here. Proposed new paths must be reconciled with repository layout on pickup. Reuse existing model envelopes, KB identities and Gherkin/MCK runners. Preserve unrelated work. Run focused tests and required repository checks before code pushes; merges/releases require the existing maintainer authorization. No product implementation is performed by this decomposition.

Dependencies are task/artifact edges, never implied by list order or parent membership. Unlisted coordination is nonblocking. Implementation workers use the appropriate execution skill after reading the linked contract and task brief. Exact interfaces created by design tasks become inputs to their consumers.

design:
Untagged unions in Morphir IR v4

morphir-ukvn.7.2 · 18 October 2026 · U1 reference contract · profile morphir-untagged-union/0.1.0-draft.1

  • Scope and decisions
  • Wire contract
  • Semantic contract
  • Decoding and unsupported checks
  • Independent fixtures
  • MoonBit consumers
  • Ecosystem consumers
  • Adoption and verification

Scope and decisions

U1 specifies a first-class untagged Union expression, independent wire and semantic examples, and affected consumers. It does not implement a parser, codec, checker or backend. The binding input is the untagged-union section of ConceptualModel morphir-ukvn.7, stored draft 0.17. The delivery plan morphir-ukvn.7.9 still names draft 0.16; the Union semantics are retained in 0.17.

The public Type System draft carries the wire and semantic rules. This companion pins fixture interpretation and the inventory used by downstream tasks. Existing v4 rules, including decision 0005 on attributes, continue to apply.

StatusDecision
Maintainer directionFirst-class untagged unions alongside tagged custom types; inclusive membership, overlap, opaque identity, conservative narrowing and ambiguity diagnostics.
U1 draft contractPascalCase Union wrapper, compact array, expanded alternatives member, at least two authored entries, preservation of ordered syntax and annotations.
Still proposedApplication binds tighter than union, union tighter than arrow. The grammar owner must settle precedence. No fixture depends on that precedence.
Consumer-ownedExact resource budgets, capability advertisement, concrete backend representation mappings, and additional refinement/encoding profiles. These require qualification evidence, not an assumption that the node name grants support.

A tagged declaration such as type IdentifierValue = Text String | Number Int creates constructors. type alias Identifier = String | Int names existing values and creates none. type A = B declares a nullary constructor B; type alias A = B resolves an existing type B. Only constructor lists accept a leading pipe.

Wire contract

{"Union": ["morphir/SDK:string#string", "morphir/SDK:basics#int"]}

{"Union": {
  "attributes": {"source": {"startLine": 1, "startColumn": 1, "endLine": 1, "endColumn": 20}},
  "alternatives": ["morphir/SDK:string#string", "morphir/SDK:basics#int"]
}}

The abstract node is Union(TypeAttributes, Array[Type]). Every authored Union has at least two listed alternatives; repeated alternatives count as entries. Readers accept compact and expanded forms, including expanded empty attributes. Writers omit empty attributes and use the compact form. Child nodes select their own spelling independently. A bare array is always a Tuple. There is no legacy Union spelling.

The expanded payload requires an alternatives array. Invalid arity, missing alternatives, non-array alternatives, malformed child types and multiple node-kind wrapper keys are rejected. The ordinary v4 node/attribute grammar applies recursively. Decoders preserve order, duplicates, nesting and all attributes. JSON object member order is not a semantic distinction; array order remains observable as authored provenance.

Union occupies an existing Type position. An alias definition still uses TypeAliasDefinition and its existing typeExp member; no new distribution, definition or value wrapper is added. This profile specifies JSON Type forms. A future Ion representation must be specified and qualified by its codec owner; generic retention of the conceptual AST is not that representation.

Semantic contract

RuleConsequence
Inclusive membershipA value belongs when at least one alternative accepts it. Overlap succeeds without selecting an arm.
Order, duplicates and nestingMembership and assignability ignore reordering, repeated equivalent members and associative nesting. Codecs retain the original tree. Structural equality and byte equality are distinct from semantic equivalence.
Annotations and refinementsPreserve union and member annotations separately. A union-level obligation applies to the whole union; a member obligation applies to membership through that member. Another accepting alternative may suffice. No simplification may erase obligations or provenance.
SubstitutionVisit every alternative recursively and preserve attributes. Substituting String for a in a | String yields two listed String alternatives. It is still valid; do not collapse it to an invalid singleton Union.
Aliases and opaque typesExpand transparent aliases when justified. Keep opaque nominal identities and visibility. Equal representations do not authorize conversion between distinct opaque types.
AssignabilityEach possible source alternative needs a justified destination type. For a union destination, each source alternative needs a justified destination alternative. Failure to prove a more complex inclusion is not permission to guess. No implicit numeric coercion or refinement solver is introduced.
NarrowingA member widens without conversion. A union narrows only when every alternative is assignable, or a checked membership guard proves the narrower type. Member-specific operations require that proof.

A guard checks actual type, structure and required refinements. It does not inspect a fabricated Union tag. In overlapping unions, rejecting one member does not identify a unique remaining arm. An unknown check authorizes neither execution branch. Higher-order membership, unresolved variables and unavailable semantic profiles are outside the initial concrete first-order checker unless a consumer explicitly qualifies them.

Decoding and unsupported checks

Typed membership starts with an interpreted value. Raw decoding must determine an interpretation. Several members accepting the same typed value is success; several distinct typed interpretations is ambiguity. Int 1 and Float 1 are distinct typed values, as are different opaque identities with the same representation. Never select the first successful decoder.

An explicit codec mapping may settle ambiguity, for example an agreed integer-token rule. It must be named, documented and independent of alternative order. Smithy member-tagged unions and JSON Schema alternatives do not automatically supply that mapping.

OperationAvailable evidenceResult
Typed membershipAt least one alternative proves membershipMember; no selected arm, even if another member is unsupported
Typed membershipEvery alternative was checked and rejectedNot a member
Typed membershipNo acceptance proof and at least one unsupported or exhausted checkUnsupported/unknown; cannot prove a negative
Raw decodingExactly one distinct interpretation and all alternatives accounted forDecoded value
Raw decodingTwo or more distinct interpretationsAmbiguous; explicit codec decision required
Raw decodingNo interpretations and every alternative rejectedRejected
Raw decodingAn unevaluated alternative could add an interpretationUnsupported; cannot claim uniqueness, unless an explicit encoding rule excludes it

Independent fixtures

cases.json is an independently authored reference-only corpus. environment.json fixes primitive names, aliases, opaque identities, refinement meaning and raw JSON profiles. assets.json pins their bytes. Expected outcomes are hand-authored from this contract, not generated by the implementation being tested.

typeRef is a fixture lookup into environment.types, not IR syntax. Other type objects are literal draft v4 Type JSON. A fixture typed value is a typeRef plus an illustrative JSON value, not a new serialization protocol. An opaque typed value describes evidence that the value already has that nominal type; it does not authorize construction from its representation. Consumers translate these descriptions through their existing test adapters.

Each case names an operation and an expected outcome. wireDecode compares the decoded node and canonical JSON; wireRoundTrip preserves the supplied types and listed properties. equivalent checks meaning separately from structural equality. substitute uses the supplied free-variable map. membership, assignable, guard, use and rawDecode apply the rules above. declaration distinguishes source declaration forms; projection, downgrade and emit describe required capability boundaries. Diagnostic reason strings are corpus categories, not mandated public API codes. A path on a wireDecode failure is a JSON Pointer into input.wire.

The default context is outside opaque owners, with no optional refinement interpreters available and resource limits not exhausted. Explicit case inputs override that context. The positive-int extension is a fixture-only versioned semantic profile, not a new core attribute: it accepts precisely Int values greater than zero. Provenance notes are descriptive and have no membership effect. Real consumers must not infer a profile's implementation from retaining its bytes.

CasesContract covered
0001–0010Compact/expanded JSON, annotations, Tuple distinction, invalid arity and malformed nodes
0011–0019Positive/negative membership, order, duplicates, nesting, overlap and substitution
0020–0028Widening, conservative assignability, guarded operations and opaque identity
0029–0034, 0052–0054Refinements, retained provenance, unsupported checks and resource exhaustion
0035–0041Unique/ambiguous/rejected raw decoding, reordering and explicit codec decisions
0042–0045Tagged versus untagged declarations and invalid source forms
0046–0051Projection, dependent-signature gaps, bare export, downgrade, reachable code and enclosing types

The integrity test checks published assets, digests, fixture references, identities and HTML structure. It deliberately does not implement a second Union checker or treat expected outcomes as observed runtime results. Consumers should reuse MCK or their existing conformance adapter, retaining case IDs and recording implementation revision, profile, limits and actual outcomes. Passing integrity tests alone never grants Union capability.

MoonBit consumer inventory

Source audit at MoonBit 0c4069c5. Paths in this table are relative to that revision. These are source findings, not runtime qualification. None of these consumers is qualified for the new Union profile.

Owner and evidenceCurrent behaviorAdoption work
pkgs/morphir-ir/versions/v4/types.mbt, Type; json/expressions.mbt, read_type/write_typeSeven type constructors, no Union; unknown JSON tags reject with unknown_node.U2: node and recursive codecs, authored arity, lossless attributes, both spellings and all enclosing Type positions.
pkgs/morphir-ir/identities/logical.mbt, type_tag/Walk::type_; identities/nodes.mbt, collectLogical walker is type-specific; node collection walks encoded JSON generically. title: Task 7: Replace Workbench job terminology with execution
description:
### Task 7: Replace Workbench job terminology with execution

HTML detail: .dev/beads-plans/morphir-etg2.16.html#task-7

Current Workbench clients and hosts use execution vocabulary end to end. This is an intentional pre-1.0 breaking migration: old job names, duplicate identity fields, wrappers and routes are removed, with no compatibility aliases or silent fallback.

Inventory the current Workbench lifecycle across both repositories and distinguish execution request, accepted execution, operation and invocation. Update domain types, package/API names, identifiers, descriptors, endpoints, capability fields, worker messages, UI, scripts and documentation together. Publish the explicitly identified replacement contract/version and migrate normative profiles, schemas, fixed MCK fixtures and independent expected observations in finos/morphir. Model runtime/session states explicitly using validated identities and closed states; preserve the functional core and imperative shell. Preserve strict defaults, exact provider/runtime/policy negotiation, captured source and arguments, once-only claims, uncertain submission, cancellation, reconnection, stale results, terminal validation, cleanup and release. Historical qualification records stay evidence of their original contracts; they do not qualify the replacement contract.

Blocked by: morphir-etg2.16.3, morphir-etg2.16.4.
Type: AFK, subject to maintainer merge approval.

- [ ] A current client submits and observes a real execution through the migrated local/native/HTTP paths already supported today; this rename does not advertise pending permissive native/HTTP capabilities.
- [ ] Unknown or old job descriptors, fields and routes are rejected by current replacement interfaces; no old job aliases, duplicate fields or fallback are present.
- [ ] Reconnection observes the same execution; a new accepted request creates a new execution; rejection before acceptance creates none. A lost submission reply remains uncertain and must not trigger an automatic new submission. Preserve once-only claims, uncertain submission, cancellation, stale-result handling and separate cleanup failures.
- [ ] Independently qualify the replacement fixed MCK corpus and exact schemas and run real worker/browser/native/HTTP regressions appropriate to the affected current paths. Preserve historical receipt hashes and qualification scope.
- [ ] The breaking execution migration is merged and qualified in both repositories, all current affected consumers and UI use the new contract, the shared tracker and HTML checklists are synchronized, and Tasks 5/6 can build on execution terminology without a second rename.

description: Correct residual internal admission vocabulary and primitive obsession before native/HTTP capability integration. Use the existing closed engine policy as a capability-named domain type with a source-compatible alias. Decode policy and evaluator identifiers at explicit boundaries, keep browser state and messages typed, centralize the frozen selection codec, and preserve immutable execution snapshots and exact legacy wire contracts. Record functional domain modeling and functional core/imperative shell as implementation requirements. Historical records and frozen protocol names remain compatibility data.
design:
Capability domain model correction

morphir-etg2.17 · Follows merged Workbench PR #133 · Delivered in PR #134 · squash 2222c9e

  • Findings
  • Domain model
  • Compatibility boundaries
  • Checklist and next steps

Findings

The earlier documentation rename left internal policy types and comments using admission. It also left a user-visible terminal diagnostic stage named admission. Browser selection state stored policies and evaluator identities as unrestricted strings, including an empty-string sentinel.

The engine already used a closed policy enum and immutable execution plans. Job selection and receipt handling also contain domain types and validated state transitions. The confirmed gap is in how capability selections cross into the browser and worker adapter, rather than evidence that every part of the implementation lacks domain modeling.

Domain model

ConceptBeforeCorrection
Checking policyUI string, repeated string comparisonsOne closed engine CapabilityPolicy reused by UI state, events and controlled component
Recognized evaluatorArbitrary string or empty sentinelOptional Evaluator enum decoded from the actual worker catalog
Captured local evaluationSeparate mode boolean and unvalidated policy valueTypeScript discriminated union with a validated policy, captured before dispatch
External representationRepeated profile/version/string checks in state updatesPure compatibility codecs and offer predicates; worker effects remain in adapters

Functional core and imperative shell means decisions and validation remain pure, while adapters manage worker, filesystem, network and host effects. Wrapping every primitive is not the objective. Types must express a domain distinction, establish an invariant or prevent an invalid state. Derived predicates and independent facts can remain booleans.

Compatibility boundaries

The existing wire key admission, profile morphir/workbench/admission, version and strict/permissive wire values remain stable. The public AdmissionPolicy name becomes a source-compatible alias of CapabilityPolicy. The historical public error constructor remains for existing consumers. Frozen schemas, fixtures, operation names and historical records are not renamed.

These identifiers do not authorize new domain or user-facing vocabulary. Current prose uses runtime capabilities, capability verification and capability validation. Checking-policy labels remain Whole model before running and As code executes.

Checklist and next steps

The six-slice integration plan remains 4/6 delivered, 66.7%, with native Proton and authenticated HTTP integrations pending. This correction is delivered separately in PR #134, squash 2222c9e7c056850f4bc8937b4852c1a448ac667b. All 36 checks passed with two intentional skips, automated review completed without findings, and the full local repository check passed. The merged tree matches the qualified source.

The next transport slices must review the existing combinations of connected, jobs available, submission pending and disconnected state. Use explicit domain states for mutually exclusive modes and lifecycle transitions. Do not add another unrestricted profile string or independent flag to express a new state. Preserve exact negotiated authority, captured policy and existing cancellation and stale-result behavior.
