Full command behavior and delivery requirements

Deliver an offline portable library plus a CLI workflow. The library parses the preview DSL, resolves/types the supported subset, preserves the rich model, checks cases, generates artifacts and emits structured reports. Filesystem, process and publication operations remain in existing host/engine adapters. Native, JS, Wasm and Wasm-GC share core semantics.

Proposed command group: morphir spec inspect, morphir spec check, morphir spec generate and morphir spec run. Command spellings can be adjusted during planning to fit the CLI inventory. Preserve the existing meanings of verify and conform; their current generated-code/evaluator comparisons must not silently become requirement-satisfaction claims.

  1. Inspect. Open prose-only or partially formalized source/checkpoints; show requirements, constructs, links and execution gaps.
  2. Check. Resolve and typecheck declarations, then check supplied candidate states/results. An explicit selected case set is the execution scope.
  3. Generate. Emit event-style EARS, Gherkin and typed contract-test cases with trace manifests into an owned output directory.
  4. Run. Bind an operation by FQName to a caller-supplied current IR model or the explicitly mapped native SDK adapter. Check returned values against the retained contracts. Qualify the selected SDK operations, canonical rental request model and a separately authored partial-return implementation. The IR self-specification workflow also checks supplied model/wire instances against their selected profile.

All commands have text, JSON and JSON Lines output. Reports include selection, per-clause observations and coverage gaps. Any required selected case that is violated, invalid, unsupported, inconclusive or encounters an execution error fails the run, except negative cases whose explicit expectation is that observation. An empty selection is reported and cannot establish a passing coverage claim. Malformed invocation/configuration uses exit 2, unsuccessful required checks use exit 1, cancellation uses 130, and successfully completed requested operations use 0. Inspection of a valid but incomplete model can succeed while reporting gaps.

The first delivery includes the IR/SDK dogfooding slice, documented fixed fixtures, a thin shared Gherkin adapter and compatibility run upstream. Draft 0.11 proposes the text/template and Smithy representation additions listed in the coverage gate; full protocol execution remains separate. The subsequent early coverage milestone retires the remaining IR schema gates. It does not require a full Workbench authoring UI, public release/default switch, remote provider install, general Smithy/WIT import/export or new registry packaging. A later Workbench view uses the same inspect/check APIs.

Suggested code boundaries, subject to planning: a new portable conceptual-model package for graph/AST/profile logic; a separate engine frontend/operation adapter; CLI commands in apps/morphir; fixtures in the existing shared testing layout upstream. Reuse naming, current IR, rich data codecs, SDK exact integers, evaluator limits and typed execution results. The implementation plan chooses exact files and public API names after this design is accepted.

From intent to evidence

Intent → requirements → concepts and contracts → implementations → evidence. This is a reading order; the stored links form a graph.

Unfinished knowledge and unfinished source are different

Maintainer clarification: preserve the distinction between incremental domain elaboration and incomplete or invalid compiler/editor input. A valid concept can have an agreed meaning while its data representation remains undecided. An editor can also contain a broken reference to a fully understood concept.

ConcernExampleProposed representation
Domain elaborationBorrower is defined, but its identifying information is still under discussion.Concept identity, known facts and explicit open questions or missing aspects.
Definition work in progressA function body has been started but is unfinished.Authored partial definition with its own completeness state.
Compiler/editor recoveryA reference was broken by a rename, or an expression is temporarily invalid.Recovery information, diagnostics and source snapshot, with partial IR where supported.
Review lifecycleA complete rule awaits business approval.Review status, reviewer and applicable revision.
Implementation availabilityA complete function signature and contract have no implementation.A specification with no implementation binding.
Traits, existing IR nodes and lowering boundaries

Assistant proposal: use typed traits to attach domain elaboration information, including the unresolved aspect, question, rationale and source. Exact trait names and syntax remain open. The earlier conversational @incomplete type Borrower sketch is not a selected grammar or a decision to lower conceptual gaps to IR holes. A dictionary concept can exist before any corresponding type declaration.

The existing v4 IR has IncompleteTypeDefinition, IncompleteBody, Hole and Draft forms. The parent draft describes holes as broken references and Draft as author-marked work in progress; current MoonBit Draft carries no notes payload. These support best-effort compilation and partial definitions. They are not an automatic encoding of unresolved business knowledge or review lifecycle. A future lowering may reuse a form only when its semantics match, while retaining the reason and origin in the rich model.

Parser recovery and semantic holes also need separate treatment: the current HoleReason alternatives do not describe every possible syntax error. An LSP may retain a recoverable syntax tree and diagnostics before it can produce any typed IR. Incremental compilation also applies to valid source and does not itself imply incompleteness.

A bodyless fn can be a complete specification. Opaque means a representation is hidden, not unknown. A declared type variable is a polymorphic parameter, not a missing type. A concept used where a type is required needs an explicit representation mapping; the checker must report the missing mapping rather than invent Any, a generic parameter or an opaque representation.

Track these concerns independently. A single declaration can have an open domain question and a broken editor reference. Preserve both facts, and report which dependency prevents a requested check. No trait suppresses a type error or turns an unresolved predicate into satisfied evidence.

Full refinement and requirement rules

Intent → requirements → concepts and contracts → implementations → evidence is a useful reading order. The stored relationships form a graph: one requirement may constrain several operations, and several requirements may constrain the same type. Evidence can reveal a contradiction and prompt an earlier requirement to change.

A prose-only model is valid. Missing types, unresolved links and informal rules appear as gaps. Structural errors such as duplicate identities are invalid; an explicitly unresolved reference remains representable and cannot be executed as though resolved. The reader distinguishes a deliberately declared unresolved target from a misspelled reference to a supposedly known target.

Track independent facts rather than one maturity ladder: source captured, links resolved, expressions well typed, supported for evaluation, implementation bound, evidence available. Human acceptance of an interpretation is another independent fact. A model can contain implemented and conceptual modules together.

Existing morphir kb intent already stores prose with a lifecycle. Preserve and reference its identifiers and document revisions. The initial preview accepts a caller-supplied source reference and retained excerpt; it does not port the KB lifecycle. Likewise, OKF bundles and LLM-wiki documents are sources that can be linked without converting their whole format into the DSL. Automatic source discovery and synchronization are later adapters.

Requirement kinds use named vocabulary entries, initially functional, data, performance, operational and regulatory. A namespace allows additional kinds without changing the parser. EARS pattern categories are separate. A performance requirement can be structurally precise while awaiting measurements in its stated environment.

Data dictionaries and concept mappings

Maintainer requirement: Morphir must create and consume data dictionaries so model declarations can connect to known concepts. Dictionaries are versioned model content, available before implementations or concrete data representations exist.

Dictionary contentPurpose
ConceptStable identity, preferred name, aliases, definition, context and sources. For example, the quantity still owed on a loan.
Data elementA named representation of a concept with its type, units, format and constraints where known. Several elements may represent the same concept differently.
MappingAn explicit relationship from a declaration to a concept, or between concepts in different dictionaries, with scope, rationale, provenance and review state.

A lending model could first define the concept OutstandingQuantity, then link a typed field to it. Another system's field may express the same concept in different units or under different rules. Linking their meanings does not establish type equality or provide a conversion.

Proposed first delivery and preservation rules

Assistant proposal: first support authoring a dictionary in the rich model, publishing it as a versioned model artifact, and consuming an explicitly supplied dictionary dependency. Generate a readable dictionary view from that content and retain authored definitions on round-trip. Exact DSL declaration and trait syntax remain open. Evaluate Semantic Web mappings and exchange profiles while designing the model; adapter delivery and reasoning support can be staged without excluding their requirements from the architecture.

  • Give dictionary entries stable IDs independent of labels, file locations and local import aliases. References identify the dictionary and entry, with the revision or digest recorded in the dependency context. Homonyms in different contexts remain distinct; an alias alone never establishes equivalence.
  • Keep conceptual meaning separate from data representation. Types, record fields, function parameters/results, requirements and contract terms can link to dictionary entries. A concept is not automatically an IR type. Dictionary-only models are valid; generated views must identify missing definitions instead of inventing them.
  • Consume dependencies through the same explicit model/build context as imports. Do not fetch an external URL during type checking. Preserve intentionally unresolved links for inspection; malformed or unexpectedly missing declared dependencies produce diagnostics. Any dependent analysis reports the resolution gap.
  • Keep declaration-to-concept links, such as represents, separate from concept-to-concept mappings. Proposed mapping kinds include exact, close, broader, narrower and related, with explicit direction. Record source and target revisions, scope, rationale, author and review status. Suggested and accepted mappings remain distinguishable; AI suggestions never become accepted mappings automatically.
  • Use the SKOS mapping vocabulary as interoperability prior art. Exact and close mappings have different semantics, and close mappings must not be chained into an inferred equivalence. Specify RDF exchange and OWL reasoning capabilities independently. No semantic mapping grants assignability, unit conversion, contract satisfaction or proof without a separately defined and checked rule.
  • Preserve unknown descriptive dictionary properties in rich round-trips. Refuse or report unsupported required semantics and lossy exports. Dictionary revision changes make dependent mapping reviews and analysis evidence candidates for revalidation; retain the historical claims and observations.

This supports the intent funnel: requirement prose can cite a dictionary concept, a data element can represent it, a contract can constrain that element, and generated scenarios can retain those links. The dictionary helps bind vocabulary; executable meaning still requires typed declarations and explicit predicates.

Maintainer clarification: retain RDF, N-Quads, OWL, Turtle, TriG and JSON-LD as serious architectural and interoperability candidates. Their roles and delivery profiles need explicit evaluation; none is dismissed by the bounded first delivery.

RDF, exchange formats and ontology semantics
TechnologyRole to evaluate for Morphir
RDFA graph and dataset model for identified concepts, relationships and linked facts. Evaluate mappings to Morphir linked metadata and whether RDF is an exchange representation, an internal representation, or both.
TurtleReadable RDF graph interchange for vocabularies, dictionary entries and relationships.
TriG and N-QuadsRDF dataset interchange preserving default and named graphs. TriG offers readable graph grouping; N-Quads offers line-oriented exchange.
JSON-LDLinked-data integration with JSON tooling through explicit contexts, identifiers and graph representations.
OWLFormal ontology axioms and reasoning, including classification and consistency checks under a declared semantics and supported profile.

Assistant proposal: define a versioned mapping for concept IDs, typed traits, dictionary entries and claims. Preserve IRIs, literal datatypes, language tags, blank-node relationships and graph membership. Named graphs can organize assertions, but graph names alone do not establish provenance or trust; represent source, revision and assertion ownership explicitly. Pin JSON-LD contexts and ontology imports through dependency resolution so checking does not require uncontrolled network access.

Distinguish syntax support, semantic preservation, vocabulary interpretation, reasoning and executable validation in the capability inventory. OWL uses open-world reasoning: an absent fact need not be false. Its classes, restrictions and unions must not silently become Morphir types, mandatory record fields or runtime unions. A translation needs an explicit rule and stated assumptions. Keep asserted and inferred facts distinguishable, with the inference profile and input revisions recorded. Whether to use an embedded reasoner or an external adapter remains open.

Qualify each selected profile with independent fixtures for named-graph preservation, blank-node scope, literal identity, context/import resolution, and unsupported axioms. Check semantic round-trips up to graph/dataset isomorphism where applicable; byte identity and original formatting are separate source-preservation requirements. Exporting a dataset to graph-only Turtle must expose or refuse graph-boundary loss. Syntax parsing alone does not establish ontology or contract conformance.

The first generator renders authored, independently reviewed cases. It also includes one explicit finite quantity-boundary recipe around zero and the outstanding balance; the recipe lists generated inputs and invokes the contract checker as an oracle where a candidate is supplied. It does not infer a correct output for arbitrary predicates. Random property generation, shrinking, solver-based input synthesis and AI generation of proposed requirements are later capabilities.

Generator outputs carry a manifest of source model revision, entity IDs, generator profile/version and artifact digests. Repeating generation with the same semantic inputs and configuration is deterministic. Write to an owned output directory; fail on modified generated files unless replacement is explicitly requested. Authored scenarios live separately and can reference the generated model. Round-tripping arbitrary edited prose or Gherkin into exact original contracts is not assumed.

A generator cannot label a test runnable without an available checker/binding. Unsupported generation targets return a diagnostic. Generated test definitions and successful generation do not add passing execution evidence. Generating both implementation and tests from the same rule is useful but does not replace independent examples or review.

Claims need evidence

Connect prose to constructs through typed metadata, and connect claims to scoped evidence.

intent → requirement → contract → scenario
scenario → execution → evidence

Each observation names the relevant model, requirement and implementation revisions. Changed revisions make prior evidence stale for the new context.

Full metadata, claim and evidence rules

The built-in vocabulary declares relationship signatures such as requirement derivedFrom source fragment, requirement refines intent, contract formalizes requirement, operation governedBy contract, scenario exercises contract, and evidence supports/contradicts claim. Validate subject/object kinds. Extend the vocabulary through named schemas; descriptive unknown predicates remain opaque and retained.

Every authored entity has a stable logical ID independent of file position. Model revisions identify snapshots. A source reference records document identity, revision/content identity, fragment anchor and retained wording where available. External references are never implicitly fetched during checking; unresolved or unpinned references are reported as such. An explicitly requested source refresh creates new source facts and triggers reassessment.

A claim records subject, proposition, author/provenance, relevant model/requirement revisions, scope and links to evidence. Human acceptance of a proposed formalization is a review assertion. Runtime provider capability claims retain their existing separate meaning. A graph relation named implements is an assertion; it does not establish satisfaction.

Run evidence includes the specification and implementation identities, input and observed output, evaluated clauses, evaluator/profile version, relevant environment/configuration and limits. Generated cases additionally retain generator version and seed/configuration. Claims can have supporting and contradicting evidence simultaneously. Lack of evidence is unknown, not false; a type check alone is not behavioral evidence.

First-delivery inspection reports unresolved links, requirements without contracts or examples, unsupported clauses, missing implementation bindings and stale evidence. General contradiction detection and proof of equivalence to prose are not preview features. Independent domain review and manually established expected results remain necessary evidence about the formalization itself.

Full rental cases, generation recipe and Gherkin binding

The canonical fixture already in this repository defines request(availability, requestedQuantity): return Ok(requestedQuantity) when requestedQuantity is at most availability; otherwise return Err("Insufficient availability"). Its inputs are Int, with no nonnegative precondition. Preserve this behavior exactly in a compatibility example, including a negative-input case. Adding a nonnegative domain policy is a new requirement, not a correction to that fixture.

The new partial-return example is a separate educational extension. It describes one loan, one asset measured in indivisible units, and a pure operation. A caller has already selected the loan and verified asset identity. No settlement, custody, valuation, fee, event persistence or duplicate-event policy is implied. Those become named requirements in the securities-lending continuation.

Quantity is an exact integer at least zero. A Loan has id, asset and outstanding quantity. For acceptReturn(loan, returned), an amount at most the outstanding balance returns Ok with the outstanding balance reduced by that amount and id/asset preserved. A larger amount returns OverReturn. Zero is accepted as an unchanged loan. Inputs with negative quantities are invalid according to the type refinement. These are assistant-proposed rules for the demonstration.

Boundary generation for a concrete balance b emits the unique valid inputs from {0, 1, b-1, b, b+1}, omitting negatives. Invalid-input examples are a separate explicit suite. At b=0 this produces {0, 1}. Exact integers above 2^53 and machine integer range must also appear in independently supplied cases.

The generated EARS sentence for LENDING-RETURN-001 is: "When a return is accepted, the lending system shall reduce the outstanding quantity by the accepted quantity." Separate linked requirements express over-return rejection and identity preservation. Their existence is explicit; the generator does not invent them from the balance sentence.

A feature contains a tagged scenario outline that supplies loan data, returned quantity and candidate result, invokes the named contract checker, and compares its observation with the expected observation from the table. A separate bound feature invokes the implementation instead of supplying the candidate. The step adapter preserves exact integer lexemes and reports missing implementation bindings as unresolved. Requirement and clause identities are carried in tags and the trace manifest; fixture values remain in typed case data.

Full IR, identity and preservation rules

Retain a single logical Morphir model with independent model revision, IR format and representation/profile versions. For the preview, name the conceptual profile morphir-conceptual/0.1.0-draft.1; this is a proposed identifier, not a released format.

Use an existing IRUnit checkpoint. Its valid unit:<unit-id> metadata owner holds the conceptual document graph as typed Ion data. Identities of requirements and prose fragments are graph identities inside that payload, not invented IR metadata owners. Existing ownership validation remains intact. Other node metadata and unknown Ion properties/annotations are retained.

A prose-only model has an empty Specs distribution as its compatibility carrier. Resolved declarations project into the primary package supplied by the declared build/manifest context and its module specifications when the selected IR capability supports them. Source namespaces qualify model/module names; they do not introduce additional primary packages or select a package by splitting a dotted name. Unresolved constructs remain in the conceptual graph. Union declarations resolve in that graph and project to the proposed IR 4.0.0 Union node once the consumer implements it. An older carrier may preserve the complete typed declaration graph while omitting affected IR declarations and their dependent signatures, but must list those projection gaps; it is not a complete public specification. Bare IR export refuses the unsupported projection. Signature-only operations otherwise project into Specs; implementations supplied later remain separate identified model inputs bound by FQName.

Contract source and resolved typed expression are retained together. Compiled predicate functions live in a derived executable artifact, linked to their source contract and compiler profile; they are not alternative authored authority. The shared contract records how their binders map to function arguments. The preview may validate this graph using built-in profile semantics; optional metadata-provider authentication is not a baseline requirement.

Ion text and binary checkpoints retain equivalent information using the existing data layer. Standard bare IR JSON export must refuse when it would discard required conceptual content or contracts, using the existing loss-refusal behavior. This preview does not add a lossy JSON shortcut or claim native support for draft IR 4.1.0. JSON/JSON Lines command reports remain supported.

A rich consumer may preserve unknown descriptive facts. A consumer asked to check a required semantic contract must either support that profile or return unsupported. No generator may report checked contract fulfillment after silently erasing refinements. Converting a definition into a specification currently initializes annotations to empty; all new paths must preserve the separately retained contract graph and test that transition.

Changing identities requires an explicit mapping. For the preview, evidence matches exact recorded model/source/implementation revisions. A changed revision marks old evidence stale for the new evaluation context; it remains a valid historical observation. Fine-grained preservation proofs across unrelated changes are later work.

Review and acceptance

Use these review lenses; expand the exact acceptance cases below.

CheckEvidence to inspect
LanguageEnclosing scopes, multiple modules per file, imports, aliases, opacity, unions, generics, arbitrary tuple arity and named fn binders.
Self-specificationRecursive IR fixtures, encoding rules, native SDK cases and bootstrap comparisons.
ExecutionCorrect outcomes, deliberate mutants, refinement failures and honest unsupported/error reports.
PreservationRich round-trips, identity/revision links and refused lossy exports.
DeliveryPortable targets, installed CLI workflows and shared Gherkin compatibility.
Independent expected outcomes remain necessary alongside generated tests.
Exact acceptance criteria and independent checks
  1. Independent fixtures distinguish a valid concept awaiting representation, an unfinished definition, an editor recovery hole, a rule awaiting review, and a complete bodyless fn. Combined cases preserve each concern. No conceptual trait suppresses diagnostics or fabricates types, implementations or passing evidence.
  2. Create, export and consume a versioned dictionary with definitions, aliases, concept/data-element distinctions and declaration links. Round-trips preserve IDs, revisions and provenance. Cases cover homonyms, missing representations, unresolved external links, mapping direction, suggested versus accepted mappings, changed dictionary revisions and unsupported properties. Semantic mappings never silently enable assignment or conversion. Generated dictionary views do not fabricate missing definitions.
  3. A prose-only model round-trips through Ion text/binary with identity, source text and unknown descriptive metadata intact. Its inspection lists unresolved formalization honestly.
  4. Raw multiline literals work in requirement text, metadata and String-valued examples. Independent fixtures cover empty text, interior blank lines, final LF, significant spaces/tabs, indented markers, Unicode, quotes, backslashes, apparent interpolation, embedded markers and comment tokens. LF/CRLF source forms decode identically. Unprefixed lines end the block; malformed holes and invalid adjacent blocks produce diagnostics. Raw lines never interpolate. String values survive IR/model/source round-trips, with exact original spelling retained in source metadata when required.
  5. Typed templates retain declared parameters and source segments before rendering. Fixtures cover mixed raw/interpolated lines, literal delimiters, missing/unknown names, incompatible and optional arguments, empty/multiline inserted values, no recursive expansion, exact Int/Bool formatting, opaque-value rejection, deterministic output and evaluator limits. Imported Smithy placeholders retain their dialect and arguments; unsupported exports report gaps. Generated target documents pass their own syntax validators.
  6. The pinned Smithy inventory covers all four requested families and their dependencies, with no missing feature hidden as generic metadata. Validate and round-trip condition definitions, service/operation bindings, protocol applications and AI prompts. Include misplaced traits, unresolved references, nontrivial condition expressions, foreign template dialects, optional/default fields, precision and tagged-union cases. Reject document use in the inspected CBOR profile. Follow-on parity requires independent JMESPath and protocol wire/event-stream evidence; representation-only coverage cannot claim it.
  7. The pinned IR Type specification compiles and validates its dependency-closed fixture set, including recursive types, attributes, maps/lists and malformed nested data. Alias cycles fail; bounded recursive checking reports exhaustion without passing.
  8. The selected wire profile rejects malformed raw envelopes/tags/payloads before normalization loses information. Reviewed positive/negative fixtures and codec round-trips exercise every replaced schema obligation, with disagreements resolved against the versioned authority.
  9. Selected SDK integer add/subtract/abs bindings satisfy independent cases, including exact large integers. Deliberate SDK and codec mutants fail. Candidate compiler output is checked against the self-specification and compared with pinned bootstrap/independent fixtures.
  10. For a migrated gate, the compatibility workflow succeeds with its JSON Schema validator absent. A coverage manifest names unmigrated gates and unsupported rules. The follow-on early milestone removes the remaining IR schema dependencies only when the full inventory has passed equivalent or stronger checks.
  11. Equivalent nested, dotted and line-level enclosing-scope forms resolve to the same qualified model/module names. Namespace-plus-module and fully qualified module declarations resolve identically under the same explicit build package. Fixtures cover sibling headers, scope restoration, imports, conceptual links, reopening and normalized-name collisions. A namespace change does not select another IR package. Reject unresolved model/build contexts and conflicting model metadata. Rich round-trips preserve scope and artifact identity; a module-only source must not erase model metadata.
  12. A group of named types and operation signatures resolves within modules, with useful diagnostics for duplicate IDs, unresolved declared references, invalid links and ill-typed clauses.
  13. Two or more modules in one file compile like equivalent modules in separate declared source files. Block and successive-header forms produce identical module identities; imports do not leak between them. Fixtures cover forward imports, aliases, selected public names, explicit dependency aliases, conflicting/unknown/private imports, opaque constructors, guarded recursive types and invalid alias cycles. Splitting, combining or reordering source files preserves resolved semantics when each declaration retains its namespace/import environment and the same build context. Importing retains declaration identity/contracts and does not imply source fetching, textual inclusion, re-export or executable implementation.
  14. Bodyless fn declarations project named, ordered inputs and the exact output type. Contracts resolve those binders without a separate argument-name list. Duplicate/reserved binders fail; two inputs remain distinct from one tuple input, and a function-valued output is not flattened into inputs. Declaring a specification alone creates no executable implementation.
  15. Declarations distinguish type alias A = B from type A = B without name-resolution heuristics. Algebraic declarations with and without the optional leading pipe produce equivalent semantic models. Transparent record aliases retain structural identity; opaque records hide fields and opaque variants hide constructors outside their defining module. Aliasing an opaque type preserves its identity and encapsulation.
  16. Parameterized aliases, recursive algebraic types, phantom-parameter opaque types and rank-1 polymorphic signatures parse, resolve and preserve their binders through IR projection. Arity, unbound/duplicate declaration variables and inconsistent concrete substitutions produce diagnostics. Alpha-renaming preserves meaning; generic contract reports identify tested substitutions and do not imply universal proof or supported higher-order execution.
  17. Tuple types, values and patterns work beyond pairs/triples, including generic four- and eight-element fixtures. Projection and codec round-trips preserve exact arity and order; wrong arity or incompatible element types fail. A flat tuple and nested tuples remain distinct. Inspect the implementation for arbitrary tuple-arity caps in addition to these finite examples.
  18. Untagged union cases accept String and Int identifiers, reject Bool, and require narrowing before member-specific operations. Generic substitutions, reordered/duplicate/overlapping alternatives and nested unions preserve membership semantics. Ambiguous wire decoding produces a diagnostic rather than selecting the first member. Opaque members retain their identity.
  19. Union-aware IR projection preserves the first-class draft Union node, its member expressions and attributes. Consumers without that capability report unsupported projection/execution, and rich checkpoints retain the complete conceptual declarations and explicit projection gaps. Union support in the IR/SDK self-specification and compatibility corpus is an early tracked requirement.
  20. Opaque aliases with identical base types remain incompatible with each other and with their base type. Imported modules cannot access their representation constructors. A zero-valued PositiveQuantity fixture is rejected; a positive fixture is accepted. Public signature projection hides the representation, and rich model round-trips preserve nominal identity, source form and refinement obligations.
  21. The partial-return table produces the independently specified observations before an implementation exists, including frame-condition failure and exact large integers.
  22. A separate precondition example demonstrates not_applicable. Missing values, unsupported predicates and exhausted limits never masquerade as satisfied.
  23. Generation produces valid EARS for the supported pattern, shared-runner-accepted Gherkin and runnable contract cases with source/revision links. Repeating generation yields identical artifacts.
  24. The same contract cases run against an explicitly bound implementation. Deliberately incorrect balance, wrong error variant and changed-asset implementations are detected.
  25. The canonical rental request fixture retains its original semantics, including negative values. New domain refinements do not rewrite it.
  26. Changes to requirement/model/implementation revisions mark previous evidence stale for the new context. Historical observations remain inspectable.
  27. Unknown descriptive metadata survives; unknown required semantic clauses refuse execution. Bare IR export refuses required-content loss. Specs/implementation transitions preserve contract links.
  28. Portable library checks pass on supported MoonBit targets; installed native and npm CLI workflows exercise the public commands. Shared Gherkin acceptance runs with a pinned upstream runner/adapter.

Use manually established expected observations and existing canonical fixtures in addition to generated cases. Mutation examples test whether the checker notices a wrong implementation. Shared MCK integration adds cases to the existing runner/corpus; it does not redefine every model test as a compatibility test. Run repository-required lint, format and validation gates before any code push.

Vocabulary

Specification already means public IR types and signatures. An executable specification adds evaluable rules or scenarios linked to the intent they formalize.

Full glossary and module boundaries

The existing glossary uses Specification for public module/package types and signatures. The new term executable specification is separate and does not redefine that IR construct.

TermMeaning in this design
IntentAn identified statement of a desired outcome, retaining its author, sources, rationale and unresolved questions.
RequirementAn identified obligation or property derived from intent or an external source. Categories are extensible and independent of its notation or executability.
PRDAn authored document that organizes requirements and explains scope and rationale. It is one possible view of the model.
ConceptualModelA Morphir model profile retaining concepts, requirements and their relationships before all representations or implementations are known.

Enclosing naming scopeA hierarchical prefix for source model/module names. Namespace and package are alternative keyword candidates; examples use namespace provisionally.

Data dictionaryAn identified, versioned collection of concept and data-element definitions, their relationships and sources.
Concept mappingA scoped assertion relating concepts, with provenance and review status; it does not establish technical type equivalence.
ContractIdentified typed predicates specifying admissible values, states or input/output relationships.
Executable specificationRequirements expressed as evaluable rules or scenarios within a Morphir model, linked to the intent they formalize.
ScenarioSupplied inputs or states, an action or proposed result, and an expected observation. Its source and expected result remain identifiable.
ClaimAn assertion about a specified subject and proposition within an explicit revision and scope.
EvidenceA recorded observation, analysis result or review associated with a claim. A test definition is not execution evidence.

Assistant vocabulary proposal: call an extensible, typed property a trait, its schema a trait definition, and its attachment a trait application. Annotation describes an authoring notation such as @. Linked metadata remains the underlying mechanism; existing IR attributes and graph facts retain their distinct representation roles. A descriptive tag need not carry semantic obligations. Trait vocabulary and exact spelling remain under review.

A module groups domain declarations in Morphir's functional sense. An enclosing namespace supplies naming scope for models and modules; package is an alternative source spelling under discussion. A WIT world describes required/provided interfaces; a Smithy service describes an API grouping. Their mappings need explicit rules rather than treating them as synonyms.

Domain examples

EarlySubsequent domain examples
Morphir IR + SDKKanban; Go Fish; blackjack.
Canonical rentals + partial returnSecurities lending aligned with FINOS domain vocabulary.
Prose and source-linked requirementsScoped GAAP accounting and SCRA examples with reviewed source interpretations.

Financial examples need explicit applicability and arithmetic policies. They do not imply whole-standard or whole-regulation conformance.

Full domain scope and qualification boundaries
ExampleWhat it exercisesDelivery boundary
Morphir IR and SDKSelf-description, recursive types, collections, encoding rules, executable SDK contracts and compiler/implementation conformance evidence.Primary early delivery: dependency-closed IR Type and selected SDK operations, followed by full coverage of the IR schema gates being replaced.
Canonical rentals + partial returnSignatures, refinements, Result behavior, frame conditions, typed examples, generated artifacts and implementation binding.Companion domain example in the early delivery. Distinguish existing request behavior from proposed return rules.
KanbanCollections, cross-record identities, allowed transitions and WIP policy.Next contract-profile candidate. Full-column behavior remains deferred to the maintainer.
Go Fish / blackjackTurn state, hidden information, variant rule sets, supplied draws and conservation of cards.Choose an explicit variant before executable fixtures. Randomness is a supplied input; collection/temporal semantics need later profiles.
Securities lendingParties, agreements, fungible quantities, collateral and lifecycle events.Compare terminology and events with FINOS CDM. Canonical rentals are a teaching bridge; no automatic semantic equivalence is claimed.
GAAP accountingRecognition/measurement, journal entries, dates, money and accounting policies.US GAAP is a working assumption. Select an identified ASC topic and reviewed treatment; balanced entries alone are not GAAP conformance.
SCRAApplicability, effective intervals, evidence, exceptions, obligations and source-linked interpretations.Candidate scope is 50 U.S.C. §3937. Select an as-of source edition, applicability rules and review evidence before publishing executable claims. No whole-Act compliance claim.

First-design fixtures may retain these requirements as prose/structured records even when their predicate profile is unsupported. A future financial example must declare jurisdiction, source edition, effective period, exclusions, units/rounding/calendar assumptions and the status of domain review. Missing eligibility facts remain unknown. Consumer debt and securities lending remain distinct domains.

Ownership and next steps

OwnerResponsibility
finos/morphirShared specification, IR/SDK models, compatibility obligations and source documentation.
morphir-moonbitParser, checker, adapters, CLI and portable target qualification.
Ecosystem implementationsQualified consumers and backend-specific conformance.

Future direction: a full Morphir language with frontend and backend coverage, demonstrated by model → source → model checks. declare, file extensions and implementation markers remain open.

Tracked in morphir-ukvn.7; native union adoption in morphir-ukvn.7.2; Smithy coverage in morphir-ukvn.7.3; typed templates in morphir-ukvn.7.4; package/namespace scopes in morphir-ukvn.7.5; coordinate self-validation with morphir-uqub.

Full ownership, future-language and planning boundaries

Shared epic: morphir-ukvn.7. Design task: morphir-ukvn.7.1. This HTML document is stored as the epic's design and rendered locally under .dev/beads-specs. It is not committed as a repository spec. The delivery decomposition is now imported through the beads outline workflow: ten epics, 57 tasks and twenty initially ready tasks. See the parallel delivery map for workstream plans, current task IDs and dependency rules. Each plan HTML is stored in its epic's design; the overview is stored on morphir-ukvn.7.1. Local interface/profile decisions are scoped tasks rather than a blanket design-completion prerequisite.

Coordinate self-specification and shared compatibility evidence with the existing morphir-uqub / finos/morphir#883 self-validation work. Reuse its metadata and MCK contracts; this proposal supplies an early IR/SDK specification use case and schema-replacement path, not a competing test/report system.

OwnerResponsibility
finos/morphirShared conceptual vocabulary/profile, versioned IR/SDK self-specifications and encoding contracts, compatibility-gate inventory and migration, fixtures and Gherkin binding contract, KB/spec/docs, shared runner acceptance. Record draft status explicitly.
finos/morphir-moonbitFirst parser/model/checker/generators, recursive/collection validation, native SDK adapter, portable library, engine/CLI integration, local self-specification and domain example execution, target qualification.
Other ecosystem repositoriesLater consumers, authoring frontends, evaluator bindings and capability-specific conformance, independently tracked.

Candidate subsequent deliveries: Workbench inspection/editing; remaining EARS patterns and import tooling; collection/state-machine contracts for Kanban/games; source/OKF synchronization; bounded property generation; CDM-aligned lending and reviewed GAAP/SCRA examples; broader implementation bindings; Smithy/WIT projections with explicit loss reports. They retain separate acceptance evidence and do not block the first preview.

Full Morphir language direction: evolve the specification frontend into a language that can also express implementations, with a backend that renders supported Morphir models into that language. Qualify coverage against an explicit IR/model profile, including types, values/patterns, specifications/definitions, metadata, contracts, opaque types, unions and incomplete constructs. Require model-to-source-to-model preservation of the declared semantics and retained model information; source-to-model-to-source may normalize formatting and bound names. Source comments and exact formatting need a separate preservation policy. Unsupported profile features must be visible, never silently dropped. This is an intended future capability, not a current claim that the specification preview represents every Morphir feature. A bidirectional feature/coverage matrix and round-trip corpus should guide that work alongside the IR/SDK dogfooding models.

Planning can settle grammar punctuation, internal data structures, parser choice, exact module/file names and test fixture organization within these boundaries. A change to first-delivery scope, predicate semantics, the model profile/compatibility decision or financial-domain commitments returns to design review. The maintainer is being asked to review the concrete decisions in this document, not approve every later delivery.

References

Repository evidence and primary references are retained below, including Morphir IR/metadata work, Smithy, WIT, EARS, ML-family languages and the financial-domain sources.

All inspected repository paths and linked sources

Repository evidence inspected for this draft: CONTEXT.md; pkgs/morphir-ir/versions/v4/{packages,types,values}.mbt; pkgs/morphir-ir/identities/nodes.mbt; pkgs/morphir-engine/data/{README.md,types.mbt}; pkgs/morphir-scheme/spec/README.mbt.md; apps/morphir/README.md; and pkgs/morphir-elm/conformance/projects/elm-rentals/src/Morphir/Example/App/Rentals.elm. These paths describe current foundations, not completed support for this proposal.

  • W3C SKOS concept mappings: exact, close, broader, narrower and related mappings as prior art for dictionary interoperability.
  • Semantic Web references: RDF 1.1 Primer for graph/dataset concepts and Turtle, TriG and N-Quads exchange; JSON-LD 1.1 for contexts and linked-data representation; OWL 2 overview and primer for ontology profiles, reasoning and open-world semantics. These are inspected reference baselines, not a frozen choice of supported versions.
  • Incompleteness evidence: finos/morphir docs/spec/draft/{types,values}.md and local pkgs/morphir-ir/versions/v4/{types,values}.mbt distinguish best-effort recovery and authored partial definitions. These do not by themselves define conceptual elaboration semantics.
  • Morphir linked-metadata draft: scoped typed facts and assertion ownership; draft encoding examples are not a current version-support claim.
  • MoonBit multiline string lexical rules: raw line prefixes and newline handling, inspected 2026-10-17. Morphir's typed-template profile and preservation rules above are proposals, not claims of complete MoonBit syntax compatibility.
  • Existing KB intent commands: prose intent and lifecycle. The refine command changes lifecycle state; it does not already formalize requirements.
  • Gherkin foundation, beads morphir-1qhu: shared parsing, execution, MCK and itest. Read current task state when implementing; historical handoffs contain superseded steps.
  • Model package layouts and Morphir self-validation: related existing work, not duplicate initiatives.
  • Rich MorphirModel contract, beads morphir-opua.1.3.1.1: revision/evidence and transport boundaries. CLI adoption is morphir-ukvn.5.64.
  • Smithy model and traits and Smithy contract traits: useful extensibility and predicate prior art. Smithy conditions use JMESPath on eligible data shapes; a Morphir input/result contract needs its own defined semantics.
  • Smithy coverage sources, inspected 2026-10-17: AI traits, RPC v2 JSON, RPC v2 CBOR and the JMESPath data view. These living specifications need pinned revisions/digests in the coverage inventory.
  • WIT worlds: imports/exports and component boundaries.
  • EARS author's guide: structured requirement patterns; EARS permits one or more system responses. Its patterns do not themselves resolve domain terms into executable predicates.
  • Functional type design references: Elm custom types and aliases; OCaml variants, records and aliases; F# discriminated unions; and Gleam generic custom types. These are inspiration, not a commitment to adopt one grammar wholesale.
  • Gleam opaque types: public type identity with private constructors and controlled construction. Morphir's proposed opaque-alias spelling is its own syntax. Existing Morphir projection foundations include OpaqueTypeSpecification in pkgs/morphir-ir/versions/v4/types.mbt and nominal handling of opaque specifications/private constructors in pkgs/morphir-typing/env.mbt.
  • FINOS CDM product model: reference for securities-lending continuation.
  • FASB standards: authoritative-source boundary for a scoped US GAAP example.
  • 50 U.S.C. §3937 and DOJ explanatory material: candidate SCRA example sources; pin an edition for later fixtures.
acceptance_criteria: Agree a concrete first-use scenario and reviewed HTML design; define conceptual constructs, refinement and contract semantics with compatibility boundaries; land a narrow MoonBit workflow with independent positive and negative cases; publish shared specification and KB/docs incrementally in finos/morphir, with repository-specific delivery evidence.
notes:
Maintainer clarification, 2026-10-17: the motivating examples are specifying properties of an object or a group of types together with their operations/functions, such as the business rules of a Kanban work-tracking board or the rules for Go Fish or blackjack. This establishes domain structure plus behavior as the use case; it does not yet select one example or approve specific rules. Assistant proposes Kanban as the first worked example, with explicit state-transforming functions, type refinements, state invariants, transition contracts and modeled rejections. Rules such as WIP limits and preserving unrelated cards are proposed examples, not maintainer requirements. Before implementation, candidate tooling can check the specification and validate supplied before/after examples against supported predicates without claiming to execute an unimplemented operation. Next design question: what should the model say happens when moving a card into a full column?
Maintainer scope addition, 2026-10-17: hold the Kanban full-column question. Retain Kanban, Go Fish and blackjack, and add valid financial-services examples relevant to FINOS: lending using canonical rental examples as a bridge to securities lending; GAAP accounting rules; and SCRA. Correct name verified: Servicemembers Civil Relief Act, a US federal statute. This broadens the design example portfolio and does not select Kanban as the sole first slice.

Assistant proposals, pending design: locate and reuse the canonical rental examples; map securities-lending terminology and lifecycle boundaries against FINOS CDM (https://cdm.finos.org/docs/product-model/). Use US GAAP as an explicit working assumption until jurisdiction is settled, select a bounded rule/topic from FASB ASC, and distinguish balanced-entry examples from GAAP recognition/measurement compliance (https://fasb.org/Page/PageContent?PageId=%2Fstaticpages%2Fstandards.html). For SCRA, candidate first scope is 50 USC 3937 pre-service debt interest relief, with sourced applicability, dates, obligation categories, evidence/notice rules, interest definition, forgiveness, exceptions and boundary cases. Do not reduce it to an unconditional rate cap or claim complete SCRA compliance. Statute source: https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid:USC-prelim-title50-section3937&num=0&edition=prelim . DOJ explanatory source: https://www.justice.gov/servicemembers/your-rights-servicemember-6-interest-rate-cap-servicemembers-pre-service-debts .

Design implications to explore: exact amounts/currencies/rates and temporal rules; source-linked rule identities and versions; separation of authoritative source, interpretation, formal predicate, examples and evidence; explicit unknown/missing facts versus negative eligibility; examples covering valid, invalid and insufficient-information cases. Jurisdiction, rule edition/effective interval and reviewer status belong in example scope. Financial examples are separate domains sharing modeling capabilities, not an assumption that securities lending and consumer SCRA lending share identical rules. No outstanding Kanban question should be pressed while maintainer is expanding scope.
Maintainer scope addition, 2026-10-17: connect ConceptualModel to the "arrow of intent" / intent funnel. Intent can be refined into a PRD containing multiple requirements, including functional, non-functional, data and other categories. This extends the starting point earlier than types and function signatures; preserve prior Kanban/games/financial examples and keep the Kanban question deferred.

Assistant design proposals for discussion: connect intent, authored PRD content, individually identified requirements, domain constructs, contracts, implementations and scoped evidence through explicit relationships. A PRD organizes requirements; it is not itself a mandatory compiler phase. Treat the funnel as a reviewable refinement graph supporting branching, shared requirements and feedback. Preserve original intent, rationale, assumptions and open questions. Natural-language intent remains useful before it has an executable expression. Requirement kind and maturity are independent; functional/data requirements can map to types, transitions and predicates, while performance, accessibility, operational or other non-functional requirements may require deployment-specific observations, human review or external checks. Record environment and revision scope for evidence; typechecking alone does not establish fulfillment.

Candidate relationships, not finalized vocabulary: refines, contains, constrains, implements, verifiedBy, derivedFrom, supersedes. Distinguish an asserted implementation link from validated evidence and an intentionally uncovered requirement from a satisfied one. A semantic change should flag affected links/evidence for reassessment, not automatically claim every downstream artifact is wrong. Proposed PRD integration: retain authored prose and attach structured requirement identities/references, with navigable/generated views; no Markdown-only or new document-system requirement. Formal contracts are explicit interpretations of requirements and preserve source links. Financial examples should demonstrate a source rule -> scoped requirement -> domain contract -> implementation -> evidence chain without conflating stakeholder intent with external legal authority. No DSL grammar, universal requirement taxonomy, representation choice or implementation plan has been approved.
Maintainer agreement and scope addition, 2026-10-17: confirms prose-first intent capture and progressive refinement, and asks to allow specification language such as EARS. EARS support is part of the intended direction; exact grammar, tooling depth and first delivery are still open.

Verified primary reference https://alistairmavin.com/ears/ : Easy Approach to Requirements Syntax supports ubiquitous, state-driven (While), event-driven (When), optional-feature (Where), unwanted-behaviour (If/Then), and combined patterns. The author permits one or many system responses, so do not incorrectly claim EARS itself mandates exactly one response. These patterns classify requirement structure independently of functional/non-functional/data categories.

Assistant proposal: requirements retain stable identity, original wording, notation, rationale/source references and revision; EARS clauses can be parsed into explicit context, trigger, subject and response text, then linked to resolved Morphir concepts and typed predicates as those become known. Preserve raw prose, EARS and formal expressions together without requiring every requirement to pass through EARS. Parsing a pattern does not prove its domain meaning or make it executable. Preserve AI-proposed interpretations and human-accepted interpretations distinctly. EARS temporal conditions do not automatically equal function preconditions, and Where denotes feature inclusion rather than an ordinary runtime guard. Gherkin/scenarios can later provide examples/evidence using the existing shared testing work, not substitute for requirements.

Illustrative rental requirement: When a return is accepted, the lending system shall reduce the outstanding quantity by the accepted quantity. Formalization must resolve accepted return identity, matching loan/asset, quantity units, valid bounds and treatment of duplicate processing. Those details are explicit refinement decisions, not information silently inferred from the original sentence. Full examples and implementation remain pending the evolving design.
Maintainer design direction, 2026-10-17: build on Morphir metadata and linked-data properties, with a Smithy-like extensibility mechanism (traits/attributes/annotations/tags/hints; naming remains open), to link prose and requirements to conceptual/domain constructs. These connections should enable tests and analysis of claims about intent.

Existing foundation inspected: docs/design/draft/ir/linked-metadata.md in finos/morphir describes typed queryable facts, scoped predicates, explicit node links, external assertions and retained assertion ownership. Existing annotation entries and graph facts have distinct meanings; reuse this architecture without asserting every draft encoding/revision is implemented. Current CONTEXT.md defines guarantees scoped to model revisions and validated evidence, separately from enrichment. A requirement claim is not automatically a runtime capability claim.

Assistant proposal: use the existing linked-metadata mechanism for a versioned vocabulary connecting identified prose fragments, intents, requirements, domain concepts, types, operations, contracts, scenarios, analyses and evidence. Give sources document revisions and stable fragment anchors. Relations such as derivedFrom, formalizes, constrains and exercises are meaningful typed predicates, not free-form tags. An implements/satisfies assertion is itself a claim, not proof. Claims can be addressable records with proposition, subject, requirement, author/provenance, revision/scope and supporting or contradicting evidence. Distinguish structural link validation, observed test outcomes, bounded analysis and human review of faithfulness to intent. Test definitions and actual test-run evidence are separate.

Examples of intended analyses: requirements without formalization or acceptance evidence; operations with no linked rationale; contradictory scoped assertions; changed prose with potentially stale formalization; a supplied counterexample to a contract. Lack of evidence means unknown, not false. Passing tests validate selected cases of a formal interpretation, not equivalence to natural-language intent. Reuse shared testing/MCK and metadata work. Unknown metadata may be preserved; a tool cannot claim to enforce a required contract it does not understand. Exact names and DSL syntax remain provisional.
Maintainer outcome addition, 2026-10-17: explicitly wants generation of tests, Gherkin and potentially EARS from the available model/intent/requirements/contracts. Treat this as a product capability, not just trace links to manually authored artifacts.

Assistant proposal: provide generation appropriate to available semantics. Structured requirements can render EARS when trigger/state/subject/response are known. Accepted examples and transition contracts can produce Gherkin scenarios and scenario outlines. Typed predicates/invariants can support unit and property tests with valid inputs, supported boundary cases and declared failure outcomes. Executable tests also need a target implementation/evaluator and bindings; before those exist, emit a scenario or test specification with explicit unresolved bindings. Do not silently invent error semantics, fixtures, test oracles or bindings to make output executable. Distinguish deterministic rendering of formal/structured content from AI-proposed examples or interpretations requiring review.

Generated outputs should retain requirement/contract/scenario IDs, source/model revisions, generator identity/version and relevant seed/configuration. Test-run evidence remains separate from generated test definitions. Retain authored edits via explicit overlays or regeneration workflow; do not assume prose/EARS/Gherkin/contracts are universally lossless or bidirectionally equivalent. Formal-contract-derived tests assess that contract interpretation; independent examples and domain review address shared mistakes in generated implementation and tests.

Existing shared Gherkin foundation is morphir-1qhu / finos/morphir#946 (morphir-gherkin and morphir-bdd, MCK and itest integration); reuse its relevant representations/execution contracts rather than introducing a competing runner. Cross-repository implementation remains separately tracked. Candidate lending demonstration: requirement for accepted partial returns, contract relating before/accepted/after quantities, Gherkin case 100 minus 40 equals 60, generated test definition and eventually a linked run against an implementation. Exact syntax, generation coverage, first delivery slice and implementation plan remain undecided.
Maintainer names the intended capability, 2026-10-17: "executable specifications". This unifies the prior direction: intent/prose and EARS requirements, conceptual types and operations, linked metadata, formal contracts, generated tests/Gherkin/EARS, and evidence about intent. The preceding generation request remains in scope.

Assistant working definition captured in CONTEXT.md: requirements expressed as evaluable rules or scenarios within a Morphir model, linked to the intent they formalize; executing them produces scoped evidence about supplied examples or an implementation. Existing IR Specification remains the public types/signatures term; executable specification is separately defined.

Execution progresses with available semantics: check an example state against invariants; check a supplied before/after transition against a contract without a function body; generate selected cases and executable checks where generators, oracles and bindings are available; run implementation conformance later. Evaluating a relation does not necessarily synthesize a valid output or execute an absent implementation. Unresolved/informal rules remain represented with explicit gaps. Generated EARS/Gherkin are views/artifacts with traceability, and executing tests produces separately scoped evidence, not automatic proof of intent fidelity. Domain review and independent expectations remain relevant.

Proposed first demonstration for later design: an authored rental intent and identified requirement, a partial-return contract, explicit 100/40/60 accepted case plus rejected candidate transitions, generated EARS/Gherkin/test artifacts as supported, contract evaluation before implementation, then the same checks against an implementation. This is a candidate, not a selected scope or approved grammar. Financial/games/Kanban portfolio and deferred Kanban question are retained.
Maintainer clarification: the DSL must favor ML-family functional type definitions, with F#, OCaml, Elm and Gleam as non-exhaustive inspiration. This direction is agreed; exact grammar and remaining preview scope are not yet approved. Draft 0.2 replaces service-style operation syntax in the sketch with module-scoped type declarations, algebraic constructors, record aliases, type application and arrow function signatures. Added proposed alias/custom-wrapper/record semantics, generic declaration checking and explicit contract binders. First execution remains concrete and first-order; recursive declarations and higher-order checking are later profile work. Primary language references are linked in the draft. Independent builder re-review found nothing important left. HTML template/TOC/escaping checks pass.
Draft 0.3 incorporates maintainer direction: opaque type aliases for newtypes. Proposed nominal identity, hidden module representation, explicit checked construction, signature-only factories, validated definition-scoped fixtures, OpaqueTypeSpecification public projection and private-constructor internal encoding. Acceptance covers incompatible IDs and invalid refined construction. Remaining semantics are proposals; no product implementation yet.
Draft0.4 proposes unified type / opaque type syntax in response to maintainer question. Alias remains an IR semantic category. Required leading pipe distinguishes constructors from type expressions. Opaque records and variants encapsulate representation; transparent alias to opaque preserves identity. Builder review found no material gaps; HTML checks passed. Tracker remote fetch stalled and bounded retry failed this session; sync may remain pending.
Draft0.5 incorporates maintainer instructions: early IR/SDK self-specification replacing compatibility JSON Schema; restore Elm-style alias keyword, allow optional leading pipe on ADTs; generics/type variables core. Proposes dependency-closed v4 Type + native SDK integer first slice and early full gate migration; recursive types/collections promoted. Typed executable encoding/reference declarations interpreted by bounded versioned intrinsics resolve builder review gap. Rank1 generic type/signature binders and phantom opaque params preserved. Review then found no material gaps; HTML checks passed. Remote pull stalled again; sync remains to be confirmed.
Draft0.6: maintainer requires tuple support beyond pairs. Defined finite arity >=2 with no language-level maximum across declarations, values/patterns, generic substitutions, IR projection and execution; flat/nested structures remain distinct. Added 4/8-element fixtures and arity/order diagnostics. HTML checks pass; builder reviewer found nothing important left. No implementation.
Draft0.7 incorporates confirmed untagged unions plus first-class IR4.0.0 draft support. Local parent docs/spec/draft/{types,index,whats-new}.md updated with Union semantics, proposed encoding, migration/qualification boundary. New feature morphir-ukvn.7.2 tracks native adoption and self-specification coverage. Reviewer caught and resolved generic substitution example: a=String|Int permits distinct runtime members while sharing one type; behavior needs separate contracts. Final review found no material gaps. HTML validation, JSON example/link checks, and parent scoped git diff --check pass. Website build not run; MDX compiler dependency absent locally. Parent draft edits uncommitted; no product code changed.
Draft0.8 incorporates maintainer choice of plain fn bodyless specifications and direction toward a full Morphir language with first-class frontend/backend. Named params feed contract binders and IR ordered inputs. Function examples updated; generic implicit quantification retained, explicit binder syntax still candidate. declare/file-extension/other markers deliberately open. Future model-source-model feature coverage and source normalization policy recorded without extending first delivery to general implementation language. Reviewer found nothing important left; HTML/template/TOC/code/example checks passed; stored design readback matched.
Draft 0.9 reorganizes the review presentation without changing draft 0.8 semantics. Added an intent/evidence diagram, concise decision and syntax tables, staged dogfooding summary, and 22 expandable reference panels preserving all original section bodies. Default visible text reduced by about 85%. Verified template head unchanged, all 16 sections and anchors, full reference preservation, desktop/mobile and dark mode rendering, no horizontal overflow, and native keyboard panel interaction. Focused independent review found no remaining material issue. Full design remains under review.
Draft 0.10 adds the maintainer requirement for multiline strings and a MoonBit-inspired raw #| proposal. Visible requirement example plus expandable lexical rules cover significant payload whitespace, LF joins, empty/final lines, block boundaries and raw backslashes/quotes. Decoded values use existing String semantics; source metadata preserves original spelling when required. Interpolation is explicitly deferred as a proposal, not a maintainer decision. Added acceptance cases and official MoonBit reference. Template/anchor/reference-preservation checks passed; focused builder review found no material issue. No parser implementation claimed.
Draft 0.11 adds required Smithy representability across contract traits, RPC v2 JSON, RPC v2 CBOR and AI traits, grounded in official specifications. Added a concise coverage matrix and expandable representation, semantic and qualification obligations. Proposes typed extension schemas, service-to-function bindings and source-preserving foreign conditions/prompts. Distinguishes JSON versus CBOR support, tagged versus untagged unions, advisory preferWhen, and JMESPath data-view semantics. Replaces raw-only text proposal with typed interpolation/templates, deferred rendering and explicit formatting/provenance. Full parity remains a required target, not a current claim; .7.3 tracks exhaustive inventory, .7.4 template profile. Independent builder review found no material issue. Template head, 17-section TOC, unique anchors, code escaping and stored-design readback pass. Full design remains under review; no product implementation.
Draft 0.12 adds nested and line-level namespace/package examples including sibling switches, updates RentalRules with explicit package and namespace, and proposes ownership/naming/module distinctions. Defines block/header bases, scope resets/restoration, import regions, conceptual link resolution, cross-file reopening, duplicates and normalized-name collisions. Existing FQName and single-primary-package Specs/Library semantics were checked; multi-package source requires explicit per-package compilation/projection. .7.5 tracks design/adoption. Builder review caught and resolved root package/default-context double-prefixing and conceptual reference lookup; final review found no material issue. Template head, 17-section TOC, anchors and escaped code checks pass. Full design remains under review.
Draft 0.13 corrects a maintainer-identified misinterpretation: package OR namespace are alternative spellings for one enclosing naming scope, not two layers. Scope is outside model; qualified module authoring is supported. Namespace is an assistant recommendation, not a settled keyword. Removed inferred dual-layer and multi-package source machinery. Updated visible examples, RentalRules, naming semantics, glossary, carrier text and acceptance. Existing artifact/IR package ownership remains explicit in build context, with no guessed split of dotted names. Rewrote .7.5 around corrected scope. Independent review found no material issue or residual opposite nesting. Template, TOC, anchors and code escaping checks pass; overall design remains under review.
Draft 0.14 records multiple modules/file and declaration reuse as requirements. Proposed import syntax supports module aliases and selected public names with explicit cross-package dependency aliases. Blocks and successive headers are equivalent; full source-set collection allows forward imports without execution-order semantics. Importing preserves FQName, opacity, contracts and provenance and does not imply fetching or re-export. Source inclusion belongs to explicit build inputs; future include composition is separately scoped. Same-file/split-file and negative import acceptance added. Independent builder review and template/TOC/anchor/escaping checks passed. Overall design remains under review; no implementation claimed.
Draft 0.15 records maintainer clarification: domain elaboration must remain distinct from incremental compilation recovery and authored partial definitions. Bodyless signatures, opacity and type parameters retain their own meanings. Added required data dictionary creation/consumption and proposed stable IDs, versioned concept/data-element mappings, provenance and no implicit type equivalence. Trait names/syntax remain proposals. Builder review found nothing important left; HTML checks passed unchanged template head, 18 sections/TOC, unique anchors and escaped code. Dictionary follow-up morphir-ukvn.7.6. Overall design remains under review.
Draft 0.16 preserves RDF, N-Quads, OWL, Turtle, TriG and JSON-LD as architectural candidates following maintainer clarification. Added graph/dataset versus syntax versus reasoning roles, internal representation option, open-world boundaries, provenance and semantic round-trip qualification. Exact profiles/delivery remain proposals. Focused builder review found nothing important left; HTML validation passed.
Parallel delivery decomposition completed: 10 plan epics, 57 task briefs, 20 initially ready tasks and 84 artifact-level blocking edges. Two independent reviews corrected authoring ownership, shared Smithy records, raw-versus-typed validation and preview joins. Existing .7.2-.7.6 IDs/history retained and moved to workstream parents. RDF plan lives under existing morphir-uqub.15; no duplicate KB/Gherkin/MCK/carrier initiative. HTML plans and overview stored in beads. Remaining syntax/profile choices have scoped design owners. No product code or release performed.
