  • References

At a glance

A Morphir model should carry intent, types, contracts and evidence from an early idea to a delivered application.

Check examples before implementation. Use evidence to refine the model and the intent behind it.

Start hereWhat changes
Before implementationDescribe the domain, resolve contracts and check supplied examples.
As implementation arrivesBind actual functions and check their results against the same contracts.
First important useDefine and check Morphir’s own IR and SDK, then replace covered JSON Schema gates.

Review route: decisions → syntax → dogfooding → acceptance.

Full intent and agreed outcomes

Morphir should carry an idea from initial prose through requirements, domain concepts, contracts and implementations, retaining why each part exists. A person can begin with a paragraph, use a PRD to organize requirements, adopt EARS where useful, and progressively make selected rules executable. Functional, non-functional, data and other requirements can coexist at different degrees of formalization.

The maintainer wants a Morphir-specific DSL/IDL with functional modules, types and operations; type refinements, invariants, preconditions and postconditions; extensible linked metadata; and the ability to make and analyze claims about intent. Generating tests, Gherkin and potentially EARS is an explicit outcome. Early delivery belongs in morphir-moonbit, with shared specifications, KB content and documentation added incrementally to finos/morphir.

Maintainer clarification: type definitions must favor an ML-family functional style. F#, OCaml, Elm and Gleam are non-exhaustive sources of inspiration. The language should express algebraic data types, records, aliases, type parameters and function types naturally within Morphir modules. Choosing one existing language's exact grammar is still open.

Maintainer clarification: provide opaque type aliases for newtypes. Restore Elm-style type alias for transparent aliases and records, and opaque type alias for newtypes. Use type for algebraic declarations. Accept a leading pipe before the first constructor, but do not require it. This supersedes draft 0.4's proposed unified declarations and mandatory leading pipe. Generics and type variables are required core capabilities, including parameterized declarations and polymorphic signatures.

The example portfolio includes Kanban, Go Fish, blackjack, canonical rentals extended toward securities lending, GAAP accounting and a bounded SCRA example. The previously asked Kanban full-column question remains deferred. No specific Kanban policy has been selected.

Maintainer priority: define the Morphir IR and Morphir SDK themselves as Morphir specifications, and use Morphir tools to check implementations against those specifications. Land this dogfooding early. Replace JSON Schema as the definition/checking dependency in the compatibility kit and verification scenarios. The migration must cover its existing obligations before removing the corresponding gate.

Maintainer clarification: tuple support must extend beyond pairs, with no fixed small-arity ceiling. This applies to the core declaration and execution capabilities, including generic tuple elements.

Maintainer clarification: include untagged unions of existing types alongside constructor-based algebraic types. Add a first-class untagged union type expression to the Morphir IR 4.0.0 draft as well; this is a core type-system capability, not merely descriptive metadata.

Maintainer decision: begin function specifications with plain fn declarations and named, typed parameters. The intended direction is a full Morphir language with a first-class frontend and backend that map the supported Morphir features completely. Keep declare, separate file extensions and other specification/implementation markers as future options; none is selected now. This direction does not add a general implementation language to the first preview.

Success is a small model that remains useful before implementation: a user can inspect its requirements, evaluate supported rules against examples, generate readable scenarios, and later check an implementation without losing the original intent. The broader domain portfolio guides the model; completing every domain is not a prerequisite for the first preview.

Decided, proposed, still open

StatusDecision
DECIDEDFunctional modules; ML-family types; type alias and opaque newtypes; generics; tuples without a small-arity ceiling.
DECIDEDTagged and untagged unions; an optional leading pipe for tagged constructors; a first-class Union node in the IR 4.0.0 draft.
DECIDEDPlain fn specifications with named inputs. Early IR/SDK dogfooding. A future full Morphir language frontend and backend.
DECIDEDMultiline text strings are required, with MoonBit's approach as the preferred inspiration.
PROPOSEDRaw #| lines for the initial language. Interpolated $| strings remain a later decision.
PROPOSEDConceptualModel as a versioned profile; rich Ion checkpoints; bounded contract checking; a dependency-closed IR Type + integer SDK first slice.
OPENFinal contract punctuation, explicit function generic binders, full-language implementation markers, currying and call-site labels.
Review status: the agreed directions are recorded. The full design and implementation plan are not yet approved.
Decision rationale and first-delivery boundaries
Decision for reviewReason and consequence
ConceptualModel is a versioned profile of a Morphir model.It can mix prose-only concepts, resolved signatures and implementations. Keep existing distribution variants as IR projections while terminology develops.
Requirements and claims are identified model entities connected by typed metadata.Prose remains useful without an IR node. Each formalization and evidence record can refer to an exact requirement revision.
Early delivery centers on IR/SDK self-specification, with rentals as the domain-facing demonstration.Prove the language can describe Morphir itself and replace selected schema-based compatibility checks, then expand coverage to retire the remaining IR schema dependency. This supersedes the rental-only first-delivery proposal.
Use ML-family functional type declarations, alongside structured requirements and restricted pure contract expressions.The functional direction is a maintainer requirement. Exact syntax and the preview's execution profile remain proposals. Map declarations to Morphir's existing type semantics.
Reuse current rich Ion checkpoints and the existing Gherkin/testing contracts.A preview need not wait for all native linked-metadata, packaging or CLI adoption work. No separate universal test runner is introduced.
Use the existing IR evaluator adapter and a narrow native SDK binding adapter.Check rental implementation results and actual SDK behavior against retained contracts, with explicit binding provenance.

Rejected as first-delivery defaults: inventing a second model container; changing every Library/Application wire tag; requiring Smithy service shapes to represent functional modules; interpreting arbitrary prose automatically as executable logic; implementing an SMT solver, general theorem prover, full temporal logic or entire financial regulation; and making Workbench or remote services prerequisites for the portable core.

Read the language

These sketches put the selected forms together. Refinement and contract punctuation remain proposals.

type alias Quantity = Int where self >= 0
opaque type alias LoanId = String
type alias Quad a b c d = (a, b, c, d)

type ReturnError = OverReturn
type Status = | Pending | Returned Quantity
type alias Identifier = String | Int

fn acceptReturn(loan: Loan, returned: Quantity)
  -> Result ReturnError Loan
FormMeaning
type alias A = BA transparent name for an existing type.
opaque type alias A = BDistinct identity; the module controls construction and representation access.
type A = B | CNamed constructors. A leading pipe is also accepted.
type alias A = B | CAn untagged union of existing types.

Expand a topic below for binding, narrowing, tuple, construction and contract rules.

Multiline text should work wherever a String literal is allowed. Proposed raw form:

requirement ReturnBalance {
  id: "LENDING-RETURN-001"
  text:
    #|When a return is accepted,
    #|the lending system shall reduce the outstanding quantity
    #|by the accepted quantity.
    #|
    #|The loan's identity and asset must remain unchanged.
}
Multiline strings: whitespace, literal content and model preservation

Multiline text is a maintainer requirement. The following lexical rules are a design proposal inspired by MoonBit. They apply to intent, requirements, descriptions, metadata and String-valued examples wherever the surrounding grammar accepts a String literal. A text block does not introduce a new requirement kind or make its prose executable.

RuleProposed behavior
Line prefixConsecutive source lines beginning with optional indentation followed by #| form one literal. Indentation before the marker is syntax; everything after it is content, including spaces and tabs. No automatic dedent or optional padding space is removed.
NewlinesJoin payloads with LF. Accept LF and CRLF source line endings, producing the same value. Do not add an implicit opening or trailing newline. An empty prefixed line contributes an empty payload; a final empty prefixed line adds a trailing LF.
Literal contentQuotes, backslashes, braces, HTML, Markdown and Gherkin remain ordinary text. Escape sequences and interpolation are not evaluated. A marker or comment token after the initial marker is content.
Block boundaryThe first line without the prefix ends the literal. A blank line inside the value must carry its own #|. A bare blank line or comment cannot silently join two blocks. Normal surrounding syntax resumes on an unprefixed line.
InterpolationDefer $| and mixed raw/interpolated blocks in the initial profile. Diagnose unsupported syntax rather than silently interpreting it as raw text. Expression scope, formatting and deterministic evaluation need a separate decision.
#|first
#|second
#|

// The block above has the String value "first\nsecond\n".
// Spaces after the marker are significant:
#|  indented

// Raw content, including the backslash and braces:
#|"quoted" \n \{name}

Lower the decoded value to the existing String literal representation where supported; this syntax does not require a new IR literal node. Rich model/source metadata retains the original spelling, source spans and line endings when exact source preservation is required. Model-to-source generation may normalize formatting but must preserve the String value, including leading spaces, blank lines and final LF. EARS/Gherkin generation keeps the same requirement links and validation boundaries as other text; embedding their prose alone establishes no executable claim.

Full language overview and rental sketch

Provide a Morphir-specific textual frontend, provisionally called morphir-spec, with an explicit draft language version. Its type declarations follow the maintainer's ML-family direction and restored Elm-style distinction: type alias introduces a type expression, including a record, and type introduces constructor alternatives. opaque provides the abstraction boundary described below. F#, OCaml, Elm, Gleam and other functional languages remain inputs to the final design. The opaque-alias and where forms are proposed Morphir extensions, not claimed Elm syntax.

The semantic distinctions below are part of this draft. Plain fn is the selected starting function-specification form. Remaining delimiter choices and parser implementation are delegated to the implementation plan. A preview source extension can be chosen without committing the eventual full language to a specification/implementation file split. The examples are notation sketches, not currently accepted source. Intent and requirement notation may have its own structured forms; that does not require domain types to use a document-schema style.

model RentalRules {
  intent TrackReturns {
    text: "Track what borrowers still owe after accepted returns."
  }

  requirement ReturnBalance {
    id: "LENDING-RETURN-001"
    kind: functional
    refines: TrackReturns
    ears: event {
      when: "a return is accepted"
      system: "the lending system"
      shall: "reduce the outstanding quantity by the accepted quantity"
    }
  }

  module Rentals {
    type alias Quantity = Int where self >= 0

    type alias Loan =
      { id : String
      , asset : String
      , outstanding : Quantity
      }

    type ReturnError
      = OverReturn

    fn acceptReturn(loan: Loan, returned: Quantity)
      -> Result ReturnError Loan
    // Contracts refer directly to loan, returned and result.
    // Identified clauses define success, rejection and preserved fields.
  }
}
Functional type constructProposed notation / role
Transparent aliastype alias Label = String; a reusable name for a type expression.
Opaque alias / newtypeopaque type alias LoanId = String; distinct type identity with a module-private representation.
Record and tuple aliasestype alias Person = { name : String, age : Int } and type alias NamedAge = (String, Int); names for immutable structural product types.
Opaque recordopaque type alias Account = { id : String, balance : Int }; distinct type with fields accessible only inside its defining module.
Algebraic data typetype Status = Pending | Returned Quantity; named alternatives with typed constructor payloads and exhaustive matching.
Untagged uniontype alias Identifier = String | Int; values belonging to either existing type, without new constructors.
Type parameterstype Decision error value = Rejected error | Accepted value; explicit parametric type constructors, independent of metadata.
Explicit wrappertype LoanId = LoanId String; an alternative declaration using a named constructor, whose visibility follows module exports.
Function specificationfn acceptReturn(loan: Loan, returned: Quantity) -> Result ReturnError Loan; named inputs and a result type, with no implementation body required.

The alias keyword resolves the single-constructor ambiguity: type alias A = B names an existing type B, while type A = B introduces a nominal type with a nullary constructor B. Subsequent constructors use |; a leading pipe before the first constructor is accepted and optional. Thus type A = B and type A = | B have identical meaning. In a type expression, | combines existing types into an untagged union. A leading pipe is optional for constructor lists only. Resolve names according to the declaration form, without guessing from names currently in scope. An unresolved B in an alias produces an unresolved-type diagnostic.

opaque requires nominal identity and hides the representation across the defining module boundary. Applied to type alias, including a record alias, it creates a newtype. Applied to type, it hides the constructors of an already nominal algebraic data type, without adding another wrapper. A transparent alias to an existing opaque type preserves that type's identity and visibility; it does not reveal its representation or create a second newtype.

The early self-specification profile must accept transparent and opaque aliases, records, tuples and parameterized algebraic declarations with explicit annotations, including mutually recursive algebraic definitions and the finite collection types needed by the pinned IR. Resolve parameter arity and constructor payload types. Reject unproductive alias cycles; allow recursion guarded by algebraic constructors, and check supplied finite values under explicit depth/node limits. This replaces the earlier blanket deferral of recursive declarations. Operations checked by the first evaluator profile have concrete, first-order input/result types. The language can describe nested function types, but checking higher-order values and partial applications is outside that execution profile and reports unsupported when requested. General ML module signatures/functors and inference/generalization from implementation bodies remain later work; explicitly declared polymorphic signatures are included now.

Untagged unions

Untagged unions

type alias Identifier = String | Int
type alias Scalar = String | Int | Bool
type alias OneOf a b = a | b
type alias Identifiers = List (String | Int)

type IdentifierValue = TextId String | NumericId Int

Identifier accepts an existing String or Int value without adding a constructor or selecting a named variant. IdentifierValue is the separate tagged form. Union membership means membership in at least one alternative; overlapping alternatives are allowed and do not select a preferred branch. Reordering alternatives changes neither membership nor assignability. Repeated alternatives and nested unions are semantically idempotent/associative, while source order, annotations and refinements remain available for diagnostics. Do not simplify away an annotated/refined alternative and lose its obligations or provenance.

Unions compose with aliases, records, tuples, type parameters and opaque aliases. Generic substitution may make alternatives equal or overlapping. Union notation binds less tightly than type application and more tightly than the function arrow: a -> b | c means a -> (b | c). Parenthesize union inputs or collection elements. This precedence is an assistant proposal. Tagged constructors retain the existing optional-leading-pipe rule; an alias's alternatives are type expressions.

The initial checker allows a known member type to widen to a union without a runtime conversion. A union can flow to a narrower type only when every possible alternative is assignable to it or a checked type-membership guard establishes the narrower type in that branch. A value must be narrowed before using an operation specific to one alternative. Use explicit signatures and conservative structural/nominal checks; do not introduce solver-based refinement implication, numeric coercions or arbitrary subtyping inference. Opaque members retain their nominal identities and visibility.

The conceptual checker evaluates membership and narrowing for supported, concrete, first-order member types under the same resource limits as other checks. A guard checks the supplied value's type/structure and any required refinement, not a fabricated union tag. If several alternatives accept the same typed value, membership succeeds without choosing an arm. Raw decoding must report ambiguity when alternatives produce different typed interpretations of the same input; require an explicit codec decision instead of taking the first alternative. Unsupported checks are reported explicitly and cannot establish a negative membership result.

Propose Union(TypeAttributes, Array[Type]) in the IR 4.0.0 draft, with at least two listed alternatives in an authored union node. Members may become equivalent after substitution; this remains valid. Current MoonBit v4 has no such node. Implementing the node, codecs, traversal/substitution/equality rules and capability detection is an early dependency for full projection and compiled execution, tracked by morphir-ukvn.7.2. The conceptual checker may check supplied union cases before backend support exists; an implementation binding or compiled predicate that needs unsupported union semantics must refuse execution. No implicit lowering to an invented tagged ADT is allowed. Backend-specific lowering needs an explicit representation mapping that preserves observable semantics.

Generics and type variables

Generics and type variables

type alias Pair a b = (a, b)
type alias Triple a b c = (a, b, c)
type alias Quad a b c d = (a, b, c, d)
type Maybe a = Nothing | Just a
type Result error value = | Err error | Ok value
opaque type alias Id entity = String

fn identity(value: a) -> a
fn map(items: List a, transform: a -> b) -> List b

Lowercase type variables are scoped binders. A type declaration lists its parameters explicitly; its body may refer only to those parameters and resolved named types. Reject duplicate parameters and unbound variables in type declarations. A standalone function signature implicitly universally quantifies its free type variables over the whole signature, so both occurrences of a in identity refer to the same type. Variables in different declarations have separate scopes; renaming a bound variable preserves meaning. Constructors inherit their parent declaration's parameters. Contract binders share the operation's type-variable scope.

The named-parameter fn examples retain that implicit universal-binding rule. An explicit function binder list, such as fn[a, b], remains a syntax candidate; the plain-fn decision alone does not select it or change generic semantics.

The initial generic system is rank-1 parametric polymorphism with first-order type parameters: parameters stand for complete types, and named type constructors have checked arity. Support capture-avoiding substitution and fresh instantiation when checking uses. A repeated variable must use one consistent substitution across a signature. For a -> a instantiated at Int, both input and result must be Int. Instantiated at String | Int, the input and result may inhabit different members while both satisfy the same substituted type. Type membership alone does not verify the behavior of identity or prove parametricity of an external binding; preserving the original value needs its own contract. Higher-kinded parameters, higher-rank quantifiers and typeclass-style constraints are later features, not prerequisites for declaring the selected generic SDK APIs.

Opaque types preserve their parameters as part of nominal identity even when a parameter is absent from the representation. Thus Id Loan and Id Borrower are distinct types. The preview introduces no implicit coercions between those applications. IR projection retains parameter binders, Type.Variable occurrences and ordered reference arguments; rich round-trips preserve their relationships. Executing a polymorphic contract case requires a recorded concrete substitution. Testing selected instantiations provides evidence for those instantiations, not a proof for every type. A higher-order SDK signature can be represented and checked structurally while its execution coverage remains explicitly unsupported.

Tuple arity

Tuple arity

Support ordered heterogeneous tuples of any finite arity of two or more, with no language-level maximum. Each declaration fixes its arity and element types, which may contain type variables, nested tuples or other supported types. Tuple types, values and destructuring patterns must agree in arity and element order. A flat four-element tuple remains distinct from a nested pair of pairs. The parser, type checker, contract evaluator, case generator and codecs must preserve that distinction and must not impose a pair/triple-only restriction.

Morphir's existing v4 Tuple(TypeAttributes, Array[Type]) supports an ordered list of element types. Project directly to that representation, preserving generic substitutions. Execution limits may bound total input size, but are reported resource limits rather than a fixed tuple-arity rule. A target with a smaller native tuple limit needs an explicit semantics-preserving lowering or an unsupported diagnostic. Grouping parentheses and unit syntax are separate from this requirement for tuples of two or more elements.

Opaque aliases and construction

Opaque aliases and construction

module Lending {
  opaque type alias LoanId = String
  opaque type alias BorrowerId = String
  opaque type alias PositiveQuantity = Int where self > 0

  fn createQuantity(value: Int) -> Result QuantityError PositiveQuantity
  fn quantityValue(quantity: PositiveQuantity) -> Int
  type QuantityError = MustBePositive
}

Each opaque declaration has its own identity, resolved by fully qualified name and type arguments. LoanId, BorrowerId and String are incompatible without an explicit conversion, including within the defining module. The defining module can explicitly wrap and unwrap its representation; imported modules cannot use those private operations, pattern-match the representation or inherit its arithmetic/order operations. Public factories and observers are ordinary, explicitly declared functions. No public constructor, cast or accessor is generated automatically. Parameterized opaque aliases follow the same arity and concrete-instantiation rules as other declarations.

A refinement on an opaque alias evaluates self against the underlying representation in the defining module. Construction must establish that predicate; the preview checks it at the construction boundary. A factory can remain a signature with contracts before it has a body. That supports checking supplied candidates but does not make the factory callable. Definition-scoped fixtures may supply a representation tagged with its opaque type identity; the checker validates the representation and refinement before admitting the value. A public consumer needs a bound factory or declared validated codec to import raw data. Unsupported calls remain unsupported; declaring an observer does not add arbitrary function calls to the first predicate profile.

Project the public signature to Morphir's existing OpaqueTypeSpecification. A proposed internal encoding for a newtype uses a single-constructor CustomTypeDefinition with private constructors and retains the source declaration and refinement in the conceptual profile. Opaque variants use their declared constructors with private visibility. A signature-only projection must omit the representation; a complete authoring model may retain it. Opacity is an abstraction boundary, not a claim that the model package conceals sensitive data. Never lower a newtype to a transparent TypeAliasSpecification and lose its identity. Backends may optimize the wrapper while preserving semantics; this proposal promises no universal zero-allocation representation.

Function specifications and future implementations

Function specifications and future implementations

fn remaining(outstanding: Quantity, returned: Quantity) -> Quantity
contract {
  requires returned <= outstanding
  ensures result == outstanding - returned
}

A bodyless fn is a complete function specification. It is neither an executable implementation nor an incomplete-body placeholder. The contract block above is proposed attachment syntax; it contains predicates and does not supply the function body. This illustrative arithmetic helper is separate from acceptReturn, whose Result-based rejection behavior remains unchanged. Preconditions bind the declared input names; postconditions additionally bind result. Reject duplicate parameter names and use of the reserved result binder as an input name in this profile. Clause identities and source links remain required in the resolved contract graph even when omitted from a short sketch.

Project parameter names, order and types directly to Morphir ValueSpecification inputs, and the declared return type to its output. For acceptReturn the input list has two entries, loan and returned. Contracts evaluate after the complete declared input list has been supplied. fn f(x: A, y: B) -> C has two inputs; fn f(pair: (A, B)) -> C has one tuple input. A function-valued result remains the output type, not an extra input. Arrow notation remains available for function type expressions. Currying, partial application, call-site labels and the full language's callable-type representation need explicit semantics; comma-separated parameters alone do not settle them. The first preview does not execute partial applications or higher-order values.

A later full-language profile may distinguish specifications and definitions through optional bodies, declare fn, separate file extensions or another marker. Choose this when implementation syntax is designed. Preserve the meaning of existing specifications through an explicit language-version/migration rule; a contract block must not silently become a function implementation. Named parameter binders do not automatically make names into call-site labels.

Required authoring constructs for the preview: model/package identity, module, prose intent/concept, identified requirement with extensible kind, explicit source/relationship references, structured event-style EARS clauses, supported type declarations/refinements, operation signature, identified contract clauses, and typed example cases with expected observations. Express unresolved concepts explicitly. A general library/application implementation language is not part of this frontend's first profile.

Structured EARS authoring and deterministic rendering are in the first delivery. Arbitrary raw EARS sentences can be retained as source text with an unresolved interpretation; automatically extracting every EARS pattern from English is later work. Other EARS patterns remain documented portfolio cases. A Where feature condition must not silently become a runtime guard, and a While state condition must not automatically become a function precondition.

Do not route rich conceptual models through the current Scheme spec printer: its documented annotation losses make it unsuitable for this role. Reuse appropriate naming/type/evaluator facilities while preserving all profile data through the new frontend and the existing rich model boundary.

Morphir specifies itself

Primary early use case: Morphir defines its IR and SDK, then checks implementations against those specifications.

StageDeliverableEvidence
1 · BootstrapPinned source authority, toolchain and independent fixtures.The candidate compiler is not its only judge.

Specification layers and first-slice rules

This is a primary early use case. Publish versioned Morphir models for the IR and SDK in finos/morphir, with executable checks consumed by morphir-moonbit and the shared compatibility kit. The intended authority is the reviewed Morphir specification, including its encoding profiles and contracts. JSON Schema becomes unnecessary for the migrated compatibility/verification path. JSON remains a supported representation; optional schema exports for external tools are derived artifacts.

Structural validity and well-typedness are separate reported checks.

The first dogfooding slice is a dependency-closed IR Type model plus the integer specializations of SDK Basics add, subtract and abs. The Type model must include every constructor and its actual dependencies in the pinned version, including recursive children, attributes and collection representations. Use current v4 as the initial proposed version, with explicit source revision and no claim to cover all historical formats. Publish the module/constructor/rule coverage manifest alongside the fixture set. Full Type/Value/Pattern/module/package coverage and the remaining supported encoding/version gates form the next early milestone, before claiming the compatibility kit has abandoned JSON Schema.

Finite list/map structure validation and bounded traversal of recursive values are required in this early profile. Structural recursion belongs to the checker, not unrestricted user-authored recursion. Cross-reference/type-arity checks use declared, versioned validation rules with evidence linked to their requirements. An as-yet unsupported rule must appear as an uncovered obligation; no hard-coded rule may silently stand in for a complete executable specification. Arbitrary quantified business predicates, higher-order SDK execution and a general theorem prover remain outside the initial profile.

Proposed execution mechanism: encoding and reference rules are executable typed declarations in the model's versioned validation profile, not just names of handwritten validators. Encoding descriptors specify tags, payload counts, field presence, duplicate/unknown-field policy and scalar lexical constraints. Rules compose a closed set of structural operations: traverse supplied finite children, require unique keys, resolve a named reference in an explicit environment, and check type-argument arity. The bootstrap checker interprets these declarations through versioned intrinsics with specified behavior and independent conformance fixtures. Handwritten intrinsic implementations are permitted; an arbitrary host callback is not an authored rule. Raw parsing retains key occurrences and number lexemes until the applicable descriptors have checked them. Each failure reports its rule identity and source path. These bounded structural operations extend the self-specification profile without adding unrestricted recursive functions or unbounded quantification to the contract language.

The MoonBit SDK bindings are native functions, so qualify a small explicit adapter for the selected operations alongside the existing IR evaluator adapter. Pin the FQName-to-binding mapping, concrete integer semantics and implementation revision. For example, abs must return the input when nonnegative and its negation otherwise; fixtures include zero, both signs and integers beyond machine width. Keep hand-authored expected results and deliberate mutants. An oracle that delegates to the same SDK operation under test is not independent evidence.

Bootstrap and migration

Bootstrap and migration

  1. Pin the current specification sources, working codecs, positive/negative corpus and trusted compiler/checker revision. Inventory each schema-based compatibility gate and map its obligations to identified Morphir rules and independently established expected outcomes.
  2. Compile the reviewed IR/SDK specification sources to model artifacts with the pinned bootstrap toolchain. Validate their structure and selected semantics; execute the selected SDK contracts and codec fixtures. A self-describing IR model does not require the compiler implementation itself to be written in the DSL.
  3. Run the new checks beside the existing gates for the selected scope. Resolve disagreements against the versioned source authority and reviewed fixtures. Historical v1-v3 encoding must preserve the Elm codec authority recorded by this repository; do not copy known schema discrepancies into the new specification.
  4. Switch each fully covered compatibility gate to Morphir-owned validation and remove its JSON Schema execution dependency. Keep remaining gates explicitly unmigrated. Complete this inventory to retire the IR JSON Schema dependency from the compatibility/verification workflow; the narrow first slice alone cannot claim that outcome.

For compiler conformance, compile the pinned specification sources with a candidate toolchain, validate the emitted model against the IR/encoding specifications, and compare selected semantics and normalized artifacts against independent fixtures and the bootstrap result. Report these observations separately. Self-validation is evidence within its stated scope, not a proof that the compiler or specification is universally correct. Retain a reproducible bootstrap artifact so a broken candidate does not certify itself as its only judge.

Local evidence includes recursive v4 types in pkgs/morphir-ir/versions/v4/{types,values}.mbt, native SDK integer operations in pkgs/morphir-sdk/basics/basics.mbt, and docs/adr/0001-versioned-ir-models.md. The available finos/morphir checkout describes JSON Schema as the JSON profile's bootstrap definition in docs/user-guides/cli-tools/ir-migrate.md and contains website/static/schemas/morphir-ir-v*. The exact shared compatibility-gate inventory remains a required implementation-planning input; this draft does not claim those gates have already been located or migrated.

Check admissible inputs, supplied results and preservation rules. No implementation is required to check a candidate result.

ObservationMeaning
Satisfied / violatedAn applicable, supported contract was evaluated.
not_applicableThe operation’s precondition is false.
Invalid inputAn input argument fails its type or refinement.

A negative test can pass by detecting its expected violation. Keep the test outcome separate from the contract observation.
Full contract semantics and execution boundaries

The first predicate profile supports Bool, arbitrary-precision Int, String, transparent and opaque aliases with refinements, immutable records, tuples, untagged unions of supported member types and algebraic data types with finitely many named constructors, including Result. Parameterized declarations are instantiated at concrete argument types for checking examples. Named types resolve within functional modules and explicit imports. Quantity refinements constrain values without introducing implicit subtype coercions or solver-based assignability. Underlying representations project where the selected IR capability supports them; refinements remain explicit obligations, and public opaque signatures hide the representation.

The IR self-specification path also requires recursive declarations and finite collection validation. Declaration expressiveness, structural validation and executable predicate operations have separate capability inventories: representing a floating-point SDK signature, for example, does not imply that the initial predicate evaluator implements floating-point laws. The self-specification section defines the early coverage boundary.

The declaration language distinguishes transparent aliases, opaque aliases and custom types with constructors. A plain alias names an existing representation. An opaque alias introduces a distinct nominal type whose representation is hidden outside its defining module. A custom type also introduces a distinct identity, including a single-constructor wrapper. Records have structural Morphir record semantics unless enclosed in a nominal type. A refined alias additionally carries a named predicate obligation at its declared uses; erasing its alias name in an IR projection must not erase that obligation. Function types associate to the right. These are proposed semantic choices consistent with Morphir's existing IR, rather than an assertion that every ML-family language makes identical choices.

Supported expressions include literals, parameter/field references, arithmetic addition/subtraction, comparisons, Boolean connectives, conditionals, exhaustive matching and a small versioned set of pure predicates such as string non-emptiness. Bindings and operand types must resolve before execution. Calls to arbitrary user functions, recursion, host effects, clock access and random draws are outside the first predicate profile. There is no general quantifier or temporal-logic solver in this delivery.

ClauseBindings and interpretation
Type refinementself is a value of the underlying type. The predicate determines admissible values.
Record invariantself is the complete record. It can relate multiple fields.
Operation preconditionNamed input arguments only. False means the contract does not promise a result for that call.
Operation postconditionNamed inputs and result. All applicable postconditions must hold.
Frame conditionAn explicit postcondition states which identities or fields remain unchanged. No implicit preservation of unspecified fields is assumed.

Ordinary business rejection belongs in a Result alternative and its postconditions. A precondition is not automatically a guard that throws, returns an error or prevents an application action. A supported precondition that is false produces not_applicable for that operation contract. Invalid typed inputs produce an invalid-input diagnostic. Missing facts produce inconclusive; unsupported predicate semantics produce unsupported. Evaluator/resource errors are execution errors. None of these is a passing result.

When supplied inputs are well typed and preconditions hold, the checker validates the candidate result's type/refinements and then each postcondition, reporting satisfied or violated with clause identities. Cases record an expected observation so a negative conformance case can pass by correctly detecting a violation. Reports keep the contract observation separate from whether the case matched its expected observation.

Execution is bounded using explicit evaluator limits. Supported arithmetic preserves exact integer meaning; overflow through a machine integer is a defect. A bounded evaluation that exhausts its budget reports an error and cannot establish a guarantee. A supplied candidate can be checked before an operation implementation exists. Computing an output from an arbitrary relational specification is a separate capability and is not promised.

Future profiles can add exact decimals, currency/units, dates and calendars, collection quantification, richer state machines or proof backends. Their semantics and capability claims must be versioned. A single scalar Int example does not establish financial arithmetic or regulatory coverage.

  1. Inspect. Open prose-only or partially formalized source/checkpoints; show requirements, constructs, links and execution gaps.
  2. Check. Resolve and typecheck declarations, then check supplied candidate states/results. An explicit selected case set is the execution scope.
  3. Generate. Emit event-style EARS, Gherkin and typed contract-test cases with trace manifests into an owned output directory.

All commands have text, JSON and JSON Lines output. Reports include selection, per-clause observations and coverage gaps. An empty selection is reported and cannot establish a passing coverage claim. Malformed invocation/configuration uses exit 2, unsuccessful required checks use exit 1, cancellation uses 130, and successfully completed requested operations use 0. Inspection of a valid but incomplete model can succeed while reporting gaps.

The first delivery includes the IR/SDK dogfooding slice, documented fixed fixtures, a thin shared Gherkin adapter and compatibility run upstream. The subsequent early coverage milestone retires the remaining IR schema gates. A later Workbench view uses the same inspect/check APIs.

Suggested code boundaries, subject to planning: a new portable conceptual-model package for graph/AST/profile logic; a separate engine frontend/operation adapter; CLI commands in apps/morphir; fixtures in the existing shared testing layout upstream. Reuse naming, current IR, rich data codecs, SDK exact integers, evaluator limits and typed execution results. The implementation plan chooses exact files and public API names after this design is accepted.

From intent to evidence

Intent → requirements → concepts and contracts → implementations → evidence. This is a reading order; the stored links form a graph.

Full refinement and requirement rules

Intent → requirements → concepts and contracts → implementations → evidence is a useful reading order. The stored relationships form a graph: one requirement may constrain several operations, and several requirements may constrain the same type. Evidence can reveal a contradiction and prompt an earlier requirement to change.

A prose-only model is valid. Missing types, unresolved links and informal rules appear as gaps. Structural errors such as duplicate identities are invalid; an explicitly unresolved reference remains representable and cannot be executed as though resolved. The reader distinguishes a deliberately declared unresolved target from a misspelled reference to a supposedly known target.

Track independent facts rather than one maturity ladder: source captured, links resolved, expressions well typed, supported for evaluation, implementation bound, evidence available. Human acceptance of an interpretation is another independent fact. A model can contain implemented and conceptual modules together.

Existing morphir kb intent already stores prose with a lifecycle. Preserve and reference its identifiers and document revisions. The initial preview accepts a caller-supplied source reference and retained excerpt; it does not port the KB lifecycle. Likewise, OKF bundles and LLM-wiki documents are sources that can be linked without converting their whole format into the DSL. Automatic source discovery and synchronization are later adapters.

Requirement kinds use named vocabulary entries, initially functional, data, performance, operational and regulatory. A namespace allows additional kinds without changing the parser. EARS pattern categories are separate. A performance requirement can be structurally precise while awaiting measurements in its stated environment.

The first generator renders authored, independently reviewed cases. It also includes one explicit finite quantity-boundary recipe around zero and the outstanding balance; the recipe lists generated inputs and invokes the contract checker as an oracle where a candidate is supplied. It does not infer a correct output for arbitrary predicates. Random property generation, shrinking, solver-based input synthesis and AI generation of proposed requirements are later capabilities.

Use the existing shared Gherkin foundation, morphir-gherkin/morphir-bdd and its testing contracts. Parsing and execution compatibility is qualified with a pinned shared runner in finos/morphir. Generator outputs carry a manifest of source model revision, entity IDs, generator profile/version and artifact digests. Repeating generation with the same semantic inputs and configuration is deterministic. Write to an owned output directory; fail on modified generated files unless replacement is explicitly requested. Authored scenarios live separately and can reference the generated model. Round-tripping arbitrary edited prose or Gherkin into exact original contracts is not assumed.

A generator cannot label a test runnable without an available checker/binding. Unsupported generation targets return a diagnostic. Generated test definitions and successful generation do not add passing execution evidence. Generating both implementation and tests from the same rule is useful but does not replace independent examples or review.

Claims need evidence

Connect prose to constructs through typed metadata, and connect claims to scoped evidence.

intent → requirement → contract → scenario
scenario → execution → evidence

Each observation names the relevant model, requirement and implementation revisions. Changed revisions make prior evidence stale for the new context.

Full metadata, claim and evidence rules

The built-in vocabulary declares relationship signatures such as requirement derivedFrom source fragment, requirement refines intent, contract formalizes requirement, operation governedBy contract, scenario exercises contract, and evidence supports/contradicts claim. Validate subject/object kinds. Extend the vocabulary through named schemas; descriptive unknown predicates remain opaque and retained.

Every authored entity has a stable logical ID independent of file position. Model revisions identify snapshots. A source reference records document identity, revision/content identity, fragment anchor and retained wording where available. External references are never implicitly fetched during checking; unresolved or unpinned references are reported as such. An explicitly requested source refresh creates new source facts and triggers reassessment.

A claim records subject, proposition, author/provenance, relevant model/requirement revisions, scope and links to evidence. Human acceptance of a proposed formalization is a review assertion. Runtime provider capability claims retain their existing separate meaning. A graph relation named implements is an assertion; it does not establish satisfaction.

Run evidence includes the specification and implementation identities, input and observed output, evaluated clauses, evaluator/profile version, relevant environment/configuration and limits. Generated cases additionally retain generator version and seed/configuration. Claims can have supporting and contradicting evidence simultaneously. Lack of evidence is unknown, not false; a type check alone is not behavioral evidence.

First-delivery inspection reports unresolved links, requirements without contracts or examples, unsupported clauses, missing implementation bindings and stale evidence. General contradiction detection and proof of equivalence to prose are not preview features. Independent domain review and manually established expected results remain necessary evidence about the formalization itself.

Full rental cases, generation recipe and Gherkin binding

The canonical fixture already in this repository defines request(availability, requestedQuantity): return Ok(requestedQuantity) when requestedQuantity is at most availability; otherwise return Err("Insufficient availability"). Its inputs are Int, with no nonnegative precondition. Preserve this behavior exactly in a compatibility example, including a negative-input case. Adding a nonnegative domain policy is a new requirement, not a correction to that fixture.

The new partial-return example is a separate educational extension. It describes one loan, one asset measured in indivisible units, and a pure operation. A caller has already selected the loan and verified asset identity. No settlement, custody, valuation, fee, event persistence or duplicate-event policy is implied. Those become named requirements in the securities-lending continuation.

Quantity is an exact integer at least zero. A Loan has id, asset and outstanding quantity. For acceptReturn(loan, returned), an amount at most the outstanding balance returns Ok with the outstanding balance reduced by that amount and id/asset preserved. A larger amount returns OverReturn. Zero is accepted as an unchanged loan. Inputs with negative quantities are invalid according to the type refinement. These are assistant-proposed rules for the demonstration.

Full IR, identity and preservation rules

Retain a single logical Morphir model with independent model revision, IR format and representation/profile versions. For the preview, name the conceptual profile morphir-conceptual/0.1.0-draft.1; this is a proposed identifier, not a released format.

Use an existing IRUnit checkpoint. Its valid unit:<unit-id> metadata owner holds the conceptual document graph as typed Ion data. Identities of requirements and prose fragments are graph identities inside that payload, not invented IR metadata owners. Existing ownership validation remains intact. Other node metadata and unknown Ion properties/annotations are retained.

A prose-only model has an empty Specs distribution as its compatibility carrier. Resolved declarations project into its package/module specifications when the selected IR capability supports them. Unresolved constructs remain in the conceptual graph. Union declarations resolve in that graph and project to the proposed IR 4.0.0 Union node once the consumer implements it. An older carrier may preserve the complete typed declaration graph while omitting affected IR declarations and their dependent signatures, but must list those projection gaps; it is not a complete public specification. Bare IR export refuses the unsupported projection. Signature-only operations otherwise project into Specs; implementations supplied later remain separate identified model inputs bound by FQName.

Contract source and resolved typed expression are retained together. Compiled predicate functions live in a derived executable artifact, linked to their source contract and compiler profile; they are not alternative authored authority. The shared contract records how their binders map to function arguments. The preview may validate this graph using built-in profile semantics; optional metadata-provider authentication is not a baseline requirement.

Ion text and binary checkpoints retain equivalent information using the existing data layer. Standard bare IR JSON export must refuse when it would discard required conceptual content or contracts, using the existing loss-refusal behavior. This preview does not add a lossy JSON shortcut or claim native support for draft IR 4.1.0. JSON/JSON Lines command reports remain supported.

A rich consumer may preserve unknown descriptive facts. A consumer asked to check a required semantic contract must either support that profile or return unsupported. No generator may report checked contract fulfillment after silently erasing refinements. Converting a definition into a specification currently initializes annotations to empty; all new paths must preserve the separately retained contract graph and test that transition.

Changing identities requires an explicit mapping. For the preview, evidence matches exact recorded model/source/implementation revisions. A changed revision marks old evidence stale for the new evaluation context; it remains a valid historical observation. Fine-grained preservation proofs across unrelated changes are later work.

Exact acceptance criteria and independent checks
  1. A prose-only model round-trips through Ion text/binary with identity, source text and unknown descriptive metadata intact. Its inspection lists unresolved formalization honestly.
  2. Raw multiline literals work in requirement text, metadata and String-valued examples. Independent fixtures cover empty text, interior blank lines, final LF, significant spaces/tabs, indented markers, Unicode, quotes, backslashes, apparent interpolation, embedded markers and comment tokens. LF/CRLF source forms decode identically. Unprefixed lines end the block; unsupported interpolation and invalid adjacent blocks produce diagnostics. String values survive IR/model/source round-trips, with exact original spelling retained in source metadata when required.
  3. The pinned IR Type specification compiles and validates its dependency-closed fixture set, including recursive types, attributes, maps/lists and malformed nested data. Alias cycles fail; bounded recursive checking reports exhaustion without passing.
  4. The selected wire profile rejects malformed raw envelopes/tags/payloads before normalization loses information. Reviewed positive/negative fixtures and codec round-trips exercise every replaced schema obligation, with disagreements resolved against the versioned authority.
  5. Selected SDK integer add/subtract/abs bindings satisfy independent cases, including exact large integers. Deliberate SDK and codec mutants fail. Candidate compiler output is checked against the self-specification and compared with pinned bootstrap/independent fixtures.
  6. For a migrated gate, the compatibility workflow succeeds with its JSON Schema validator absent. A coverage manifest names unmigrated gates and unsupported rules. The follow-on early milestone removes the remaining IR schema dependencies only when the full inventory has passed equivalent or stronger checks.
  7. A group of named types and operation signatures resolves within modules, with useful diagnostics for duplicate IDs, unresolved declared references, invalid links and ill-typed clauses.
  8. Bodyless fn declarations project named, ordered inputs and the exact output type. Contracts resolve those binders without a separate argument-name list. Duplicate/reserved binders fail; two inputs remain distinct from one tuple input, and a function-valued output is not flattened into inputs. Declaring a specification alone creates no executable implementation.
  9. Declarations distinguish type alias A = B from type A = B without name-resolution heuristics. Algebraic declarations with and without the optional leading pipe produce equivalent semantic models. Transparent record aliases retain structural identity; opaque records hide fields and opaque variants hide constructors outside their defining module. Aliasing an opaque type preserves its identity and encapsulation.
  10. Parameterized aliases, recursive algebraic types, phantom-parameter opaque types and rank-1 polymorphic signatures parse, resolve and preserve their binders through IR projection. Arity, unbound/duplicate declaration variables and inconsistent concrete substitutions produce diagnostics. Alpha-renaming preserves meaning; generic contract reports identify tested substitutions and do not imply universal proof or supported higher-order execution.
  11. Tuple types, values and patterns work beyond pairs/triples, including generic four- and eight-element fixtures. Projection and codec round-trips preserve exact arity and order; wrong arity or incompatible element types fail. A flat tuple and nested tuples remain distinct. Inspect the implementation for arbitrary tuple-arity caps in addition to these finite examples.
  12. Untagged union cases accept String and Int identifiers, reject Bool, and require narrowing before member-specific operations. Generic substitutions, reordered/duplicate/overlapping alternatives and nested unions preserve membership semantics. Ambiguous wire decoding produces a diagnostic rather than selecting the first member. Opaque members retain their identity.
  13. Union-aware IR projection preserves the first-class draft Union node, its member expressions and attributes. Consumers without that capability report unsupported projection/execution, and rich checkpoints retain the complete conceptual declarations and explicit projection gaps. Union support in the IR/SDK self-specification and compatibility corpus is an early tracked requirement.
  14. Opaque aliases with identical base types remain incompatible with each other and with their base type. Imported modules cannot access their representation constructors. A zero-valued PositiveQuantity fixture is rejected; a positive fixture is accepted. Public signature projection hides the representation, and rich model round-trips preserve nominal identity, source form and refinement obligations.
  15. The partial-return table produces the independently specified observations before an implementation exists, including frame-condition failure and exact large integers.
  16. A separate precondition example demonstrates not_applicable. Missing values, unsupported predicates and exhausted limits never masquerade as satisfied.
  17. Generation produces valid EARS for the supported pattern, shared-runner-accepted Gherkin and runnable contract cases with source/revision links. Repeating generation yields identical artifacts.
  18. The same contract cases run against an explicitly bound implementation. Deliberately incorrect balance, wrong error variant and changed-asset implementations are detected.
  19. The canonical rental request fixture retains its original semantics, including negative values. New domain refinements do not rewrite it.
  20. Changes to requirement/model/implementation revisions mark previous evidence stale for the new context. Historical observations remain inspectable.
  21. Unknown descriptive metadata survives; unknown required semantic clauses refuse execution. Bare IR export refuses required-content loss. Specs/implementation transitions preserve contract links.
  22. Portable library checks pass on supported MoonBit targets; installed native and npm CLI workflows exercise the public commands. Shared Gherkin acceptance runs with a pinned upstream runner/adapter.

Use manually established expected observations and existing canonical fixtures in addition to generated cases. Mutation examples test whether the checker notices a wrong implementation. Shared MCK integration adds cases to the existing runner/corpus; it does not redefine every model test as a compatibility test. Run repository-required lint, format and validation gates before any code push.

Vocabulary

Specification already means public IR types and signatures. An executable specification adds evaluable rules or scenarios linked to the intent they formalize.

Full glossary and module boundaries

The existing glossary uses Specification for public module/package types and signatures. The new term executable specification is separate and does not redefine that IR construct.

TermMeaning in this design
IntentAn identified statement of a desired outcome, retaining its author, sources, rationale and unresolved questions.
RequirementAn identified obligation or property derived from intent or an external source. Categories are extensible and independent of its notation or executability.
PRDAn authored document that organizes requirements and explains scope and rationale. It is one possible view of the model.
ConceptualModelA Morphir model profile retaining concepts, requirements and their relationships before all representations or implementations are known.
ConstructAn identified declaration such as a domain concept, type or operation. Its declared kind determines the semantics of its properties.
ContractIdentified typed predicates specifying admissible values, states or input/output relationships.
Executable specificationRequirements expressed as evaluable rules or scenarios within a Morphir model, linked to the intent they formalize.
ScenarioSupplied inputs or states, an action or proposed result, and an expected observation. Its source and expected result remain identifiable.
ClaimAn assertion about a specified subject and proposition within an explicit revision and scope.
EvidenceA recorded observation, analysis result or review associated with a claim. A test definition is not execution evidence.

Use linked metadata for the mechanism. Attributes, annotations and graph facts keep their existing meanings at representation boundaries. A new user-facing word such as trait is optional syntax, not a reason to merge those existing representations.

A module groups domain declarations in Morphir's functional sense. A namespace supplies naming scope. A WIT world describes required/provided interfaces; a Smithy service describes an API grouping. Their mappings need explicit rules rather than treating them as synonyms.

Financial examples need explicit applicability and arithmetic policies. They do not imply whole-standard or whole-regulation conformance.

Full domain scope and qualification boundaries
ExampleWhat it exercisesDelivery boundary
Morphir IR and SDKSelf-description, recursive types, collections, encoding rules, executable SDK contracts and compiler/implementation conformance evidence.Primary early delivery: dependency-closed IR Type and selected SDK operations, followed by full coverage of the IR schema gates being replaced.
Canonical rentals + partial returnSignatures, refinements, Result behavior, frame conditions, typed examples, generated artifacts and implementation binding.Companion domain example in the early delivery. Distinguish existing request behavior from proposed return rules.
KanbanCollections, cross-record identities, allowed transitions and WIP policy.Next contract-profile candidate. Full-column behavior remains deferred to the maintainer.
Go Fish / blackjackTurn state, hidden information, variant rule sets, supplied draws and conservation of cards.Choose an explicit variant before executable fixtures. Randomness is a supplied input; collection/temporal semantics need later profiles.
Securities lendingParties, agreements, fungible quantities, collateral and lifecycle events.Compare terminology and events with FINOS CDM. Canonical rentals are a teaching bridge; no automatic semantic equivalence is claimed.
GAAP accountingRecognition/measurement, journal entries, dates, money and accounting policies.US GAAP is a working assumption. Select an identified ASC topic and reviewed treatment; balanced entries alone are not GAAP conformance.
SCRAApplicability, effective intervals, evidence, exceptions, obligations and source-linked interpretations.Candidate scope is 50 U.S.C. §3937. Select an as-of source edition, applicability rules and review evidence before publishing executable claims. No whole-Act compliance claim.

First-design fixtures may retain these requirements as prose/structured records even when their predicate profile is unsupported. A future financial example must declare jurisdiction, source edition, effective period, exclusions, units/rounding/calendar assumptions and the status of domain review. Missing eligibility facts remain unknown. Consumer debt and securities lending remain distinct domains.

Ownership and next steps

OwnerResponsibility
finos/morphirShared specification, IR/SDK models, compatibility obligations and source documentation.
morphir-moonbitParser, checker, adapters, CLI and portable target qualification.
Ecosystem implementationsQualified consumers and backend-specific conformance.

Future direction: a full Morphir language with frontend and backend coverage, demonstrated by model → source → model checks. declare, file extensions and implementation markers remain open.

Tracked in morphir-ukvn.7; native union adoption in morphir-ukvn.7.2; coordinate self-validation with morphir-uqub.

Full ownership, future-language and planning boundaries

Shared epic: morphir-ukvn.7. Design task: morphir-ukvn.7.1. This HTML document is stored as the epic's design and rendered locally under .dev/beads-specs. It is not committed as a repository spec. After approval, import an implementation plan through the repository's beads outline workflow.

Coordinate self-specification and shared compatibility evidence with the existing morphir-uqub / finos/morphir#883 self-validation work. Reuse its metadata and MCK contracts; this proposal supplies an early IR/SDK specification use case and schema-replacement path, not a competing test/report system.

OwnerResponsibility
finos/morphirShared conceptual vocabulary/profile, versioned IR/SDK self-specifications and encoding contracts, compatibility-gate inventory and migration, fixtures and Gherkin binding contract, KB/spec/docs, shared runner acceptance. Record draft status explicitly.
finos/morphir-moonbitFirst parser/model/checker/generators, recursive/collection validation, native SDK adapter, portable library, engine/CLI integration, local self-specification and domain example execution, target qualification.
Other ecosystem repositoriesLater consumers, authoring frontends, evaluator bindings and capability-specific conformance, independently tracked.

Candidate subsequent deliveries: Workbench inspection/editing; remaining EARS patterns and import tooling; collection/state-machine contracts for Kanban/games; source/OKF synchronization; bounded property generation; CDM-aligned lending and reviewed GAAP/SCRA examples; broader implementation bindings; Smithy/WIT projections with explicit loss reports. They retain separate acceptance evidence and do not block the first preview.

Full Morphir language direction: evolve the specification frontend into a language that can also express implementations, with a backend that renders supported Morphir models into that language. Qualify coverage against an explicit IR/model profile, including types, values/patterns, specifications/definitions, metadata, contracts, opaque types, unions and incomplete constructs. Require model-to-source-to-model preservation of the declared semantics and retained model information; source-to-model-to-source may normalize formatting and bound names. Source comments and exact formatting need a separate preservation policy. Unsupported profile features must be visible, never silently dropped. This is an intended future capability, not a current claim that the specification preview represents every Morphir feature. A bidirectional feature/coverage matrix and round-trip corpus should guide that work alongside the IR/SDK dogfooding models.

Planning can settle grammar punctuation, internal data structures, parser choice, exact module/file names and test fixture organization within these boundaries. A change to first-delivery scope, predicate semantics, the model profile/compatibility decision or financial-domain commitments returns to design review. The maintainer is being asked to review the concrete decisions in this document, not approve every later delivery.

References

Repository evidence and primary references are retained below, including Morphir IR/metadata work, Smithy, WIT, EARS, ML-family languages and the financial-domain sources.

All inspected repository paths and linked sources

Repository evidence inspected for this draft: CONTEXT.md; pkgs/morphir-ir/versions/v4/{packages,types,values}.mbt; pkgs/morphir-ir/identities/nodes.mbt; pkgs/morphir-engine/data/{README.md,types.mbt}; pkgs/morphir-scheme/spec/README.mbt.md; apps/morphir/README.md; and pkgs/morphir-elm/conformance/projects/elm-rentals/src/Morphir/Example/App/Rentals.elm. These paths describe current foundations, not completed support for this proposal.

  • Morphir linked-metadata draft: scoped typed facts and assertion ownership; draft encoding examples are not a current version-support claim.
  • MoonBit multiline string lexical rules: raw line prefixes and newline handling, inspected 2026-10-17. Morphir's initial raw-only profile and preservation rules above are proposals, not claims of complete MoonBit syntax compatibility.
  • Existing KB intent commands: prose intent and lifecycle. The refine command changes lifecycle state; it does not already formalize requirements.
  • Gherkin foundation, beads morphir-1qhu: shared parsing, execution, MCK and itest. Read current task state when implementing; historical handoffs contain superseded steps.
  • Model package layouts and Morphir self-validation: related existing work, not duplicate initiatives.
  • Rich MorphirModel contract, beads morphir-opua.1.3.1.1: revision/evidence and transport boundaries. CLI adoption is morphir-ukvn.5.64.
  • Smithy model and traits and Smithy contract traits: useful extensibility and predicate prior art. Smithy conditions use JMESPath on eligible data shapes; a Morphir input/result contract needs its own defined semantics.
  • WIT worlds: imports/exports and component boundaries.
  • EARS author's guide: structured requirement patterns; EARS permits one or more system responses. Its patterns do not themselves resolve domain terms into executable predicates.
  • Functional type design references: Elm custom types and aliases; OCaml variants, records and aliases; F# discriminated unions; and Gleam generic custom types. These are inspiration, not a commitment to adopt one grammar wholesale.
  • Gleam opaque types: public type identity with private constructors and controlled construction. Morphir's proposed opaque-alias spelling is its own syntax. Existing Morphir projection foundations include OpaqueTypeSpecification in pkgs/morphir-ir/versions/v4/types.mbt and nominal handling of opaque specifications/private constructors in pkgs/morphir-typing/env.mbt.
  • FINOS CDM product model: reference for securities-lending continuation.
  • FASB standards: authoritative-source boundary for a scoped US GAAP example.
  • 50 U.S.C. §3937 and DOJ explanatory material: candidate SCRA example sources; pin an edition for later fixtures.
