title: Adopt the MoonBit CLI and shared Workbench as primary Morphir experiences
description:
## Current priority and extension model
Prioritize useful user-approved extension interoperability in the manner of LSP/BSP. Present asserted author/publisher, origin, version and capabilities; the user/host selects the extension, then compatible operations run. Preserve ordinary protocol/model validation and actual host access controls. Cryptographically authenticated publisher/package/declaration workflows are optional profiles, not baseline runtime prerequisites. MEP semantics have JSON-RPC process, WIT/component and native bindings, with future Morphir-defined component contracts. Prefer WIT/WebAssembly Component Model after proving support in the main intended hosts and guest toolchain; retain Extism as a useful alternative or bridge where appropriate. This 2026-10-17 clarification supersedes the temporary Extism exclusion; authentication remains optional.

## Maintainer direction
On 2026-10-17 the maintainer requested beads to move the MoonBit CLI toward becoming the canonical primary Morphir CLI, with work as parallel as possible. The MoonBit/Rabbita shared Workbench and Try Morphir Playground (try-morphir) are also the intended official experiences. Record this as the target direction, not a claim that production defaults or releases have already switched.

## Outcome
Users can perform the adopted upstream CLI workflows through the MoonBit application, and reach the official Workbench and Playground through consistent commands and site links. Preserve pluggable/configurable pipeline components and make compatibility explicit. Keep finos/morphir as the shared contract, tracker and ecosystem integration repository; this campaign does not mandate repository relocation or a complete rewrite of Rust services.

## Evidence baseline
Comparison: finos/morphir main c60f313a67b926f4adc9adbf482767203a21ff56, command definitions in crates/morphir/src/main.rs and command modules; finos/morphir-moonbit 3b7ccd029c89ef5e3fe6173490c97906dfcae6e7, command definitions in apps/morphir/arguments.mbt and app/engine READMEs. Update and inspect current source on pickup.
Existing MoonBit commands: run, workspace, project list, execute, verify, conform and toolchain info/setup/build/run/exec. It already compiles qualified MoonBit/Elm/Scheme inputs, generates libraries, preserves rich Ion checkpoints and supports explicit build/evaluation providers.
Upstream command families to adopt or explicitly disposition: compile, generate, eval, extension and repositories, package/trust/registry, metadata, decoration, migrate/ir migrate, config, diagnostics, cache, tool, ui/desktop/playground, mck, itest, kb, gleam and version. Hidden validate/transform are placeholders, schema currently emits an unavailability notice, dist mainly records registry state; these require inventory/disposition, not invented parity claims. Usage/help metadata should support compatibility documentation.

## Parallel delivery
Each child delivers a real narrow end-to-end command/workflow using existing contracts and independent fixtures. No blanket design/framework prerequisite blocks implementation lanes. Parsing/version inventory, direct compile/generate, runtime hosting, catalog lifecycle, package consumption/authoring, metadata, migration, observability, MCK, KB, evaluation and UI/site work can start independently. Use explicit pinned artifact/provider/service inputs before discovery integration. Only installed end-to-end acceptance and final primary-CLI cutover join their actual prerequisites. Parent-child and related edges organize work; they do not serialize lanes.

## Shared ownership and existing work
Do not duplicate or reparent existing work. Rich guest/native host integration remains morphir-ukvn.5.55, including .55.2 in finos/morphir; it is interoperability work and not a prerequisite for every MoonBit CLI command. Authenticated project-scoped loading already landed as morphir-ukvn.1.10.11; reuse it. Native guest authority work stays .55.4-.55.6. Workbench protocol/native host work remains morphir-etg2/.15 and capability work .16. Shared MCK remains the authoritative upstream runner/corpus; the primary CLI can delegate through an explicit versioned adapter without forking ownership or rewriting it in MoonBit. Package/signature/trust services and extension-host implementations are reusable boundaries, not blanket Rust-to-MoonBit port requirements.

## Official experiences
Adopt the existing shared Workbench for Model Explorer and the Try Morphir experience as the official Workbench and Playground. Standalone, authenticated connected and Proton desktop modes remain distinct capability-qualified hosts of the shared frontend. Add launchers, packaged asset provenance, supported URL/fragment migration and ecosystem documentation/default-link changes. Preserve existing access controls, draft handling, cancellation and truthful runtime capability claims. No unrelated numeric, permissive-execution, portable-extension or full-Desktop milestone blocks the qualified browser rollout. Exact public routes and release packaging must be documented and tested; no unapproved DNS/domain switch is assumed.

## Compatibility and adoption
Inventory every upstream public command/important option as equivalent, implemented/delegated, explicitly deferred or retired with a documented repair. Functional equivalence does not require copying command internals or accidental defaults. Preserve existing MoonBit interfaces; add compatibility spellings where warranted. Keep semantic model identity/revision/context and exact rich payload/envelope facts across process boundaries. Authenticate provider authority through host grants, never metadata alone.
Use staged release/default-switch gates and rollback. Beads creation authorizes planning, not production publication. Close each bead with commit range and test evidence and sync the shared database.

## Pickup
All authoritative context is stored in shared beads and committed source; local .dev artifacts are optional renders. Pull the shared tracker, read this epic and selected task, claim only that task and push updates. Each task carries repository/lane labels, acceptance criteria and explicit blocking edges.
acceptance_criteria: All adopted command families have independently verified behavior or an explicit compatibility disposition; existing MoonBit commands remain usable. Installed extension compile/generation and official Workbench/Try Morphir launches pass with exact artifact evidence. Shared package/MCK/authentication contracts are reused, with versioned adapters where needed. Platform limitations and deferred commands are explicit. Maintainer-approved release/default-switch evidence and rollback are recorded before claiming primary/official production status.

Related edges preserve existing owners and never authorize replacing canonical services. Shared command-registration edits need routine coordination rather than a campaign-wide gate. Official experiences are explicitly the existing MoonBit/Rabbita Workbench and Try Morphir Playground (try-morphir), not merely optional alternative UIs. Production designation/publication is staged and maintainer-approved.

Existing finos/morphir CLI integration morphir-ukvn.5.55.2 remains useful interoperability work and is not a blanket prerequisite for this primary-CLI initiative.
2026-10-17 public campaign issue: https://github.com/finos/morphir-moonbit/issues/132. Includes problem statement, existing-versus-missing command table, modular/shared-service approach, all 32 child bead references grouped by lane, official Workbench and Try Morphir direction, integration gates, acceptance criteria and cross-machine pickup commands. Shared beads remain the authoritative execution/dependency tracker; issue creation does not claim production cutover.
2026-10-17 maintainer correction: prioritize an extensible tooling ecosystem analogous to LSP/BSP. Baseline flow is advertised publisher/author and capability descriptions -> explicit user/host selection -> compatible interface/feature negotiation -> useful operation and diagnostics. Authorship assertions, user approval, capability compatibility, model validation and cryptographically authenticated provenance are separate concepts. A user's approval need not depend on a signed registry or repeated runtime publisher authentication. Do not represent self-declared authorship as verified identity.

Support the existing JSON-RPC process path, standards-based WIT/component interfaces and native components; investigate contracts described directly in Morphir as an evolution path. Signed package restore, authenticated semantic declarations and remote-evidence verification remain optional profiles and should validate their explicit promises when selected, without blocking ordinary local/user-approved extensions.

This direction supersedes earlier recommendations to make .55.4 the next ecosystem task or authenticated restore/metadata a primary-CLI cutover gate. Focus next on actual host/guest compile/generate integration and installed source-to-consumer use; advance WIT/native-component contracts independently. Historical HTML designs remain evidence and must be revised to this direction before implementing changed assumptions.
2026-10-17 latest maintainer clarification supersedes the earlier Extism exclusion: Extism remains a useful supported extension path. Identify each host/runtime/version and actual embedding configuration, prove loading and invoking a real component with typed boundary/ownership/lifecycle behavior, and record unsupported combinations and required bridges. Also qualify MoonBit guest/component toolchain support. Retain Extism as a practical alternative or bridge when the preferred component route is unavailable or materially incomplete; avoid redundant runtime work while evidence is gathered. JSON-RPC processes and native components remain valid parallel bindings, with Morphir-defined contracts a future direction. Authentication stays optional and lower-priority; its removed primary-CLI gates remain removed.

title: Expose native compileModel for the qualified MoonBit frontend
description:
## Parent
morphir-ukvn.5.55

## What to build
Wrap the existing pure Boolean library frontend in the native framed MEP process. Produce a MorphirModel with explicit identity/revision, semantic IR, provenance and the existing versioned node-metadata carrier. Compose frontend and generator in the application layer, or extract shared protocol code into a lower-level module. The generator module must not depend on the frontend module, which already depends on it. Keep MorphirModel enrichments distinct from engine checkpoint metadata. Initially accept only the actually qualified source count, imports and dependencies; refuse unsupported combinations rather than dropping documents or context. No numeric implementation prerequisite.

Baseline: finos/morphir-moonbit main 06ac604, PR #119. Landed legacy/native generation and rich generation are historical foundations, not unfinished blockers. Approved design: morphir-ukvn.1.10.5.2, local .dev/designs/morphir-moonbit-f4-extension.html revision 0.15. Keep language moonbit and advertise qualified profiles only. Ion is preferred, checked Morphir JSON remains supported and IR 4.0.0 remains draft. Reuse exact MEP 0.2.0-draft.1 and envelope 0.1.0-draft.1 with complete bilateral tuples and immutable limits. Numeric source support is independent.

## Blocked by
morphir-opua.1.3.1.4
design:
Native MoonBit compileModel

morphir-ukvn.5.55.1 · 17 October 2026 · Implementation plan on main c42351e

  • Goal
  • Contract and boundaries
  • Task 1: compose a frontend provider
  • Task 2: compile and encode a model
  • Task 3: qualify protocol refusals
  • Task 4: exercise the native process and consumer
  • Task 5: validate and deliver

Goal

Compile the qualified single-document Boolean MoonBit library through the native framed MEP session, retain its names, references, origins and metadata in a MorphirModel, generate a library with the landed backend, then build and invoke a real consumer. Numeric support, canonical CLI routing and installed rich qualification remain independent follow-up tasks.

Contract and boundaries

Reuse approved F4 specification revision 0.15, exact MEP 0.2.0-draft.1, envelope 0.1.0-draft.1 and draft IR 4.0.0. The existing generator-owned protocol package accepts an injected, typed frontend provider; the native application supplies the pure frontend callback. No generator dependency on the frontend or engine is introduced.

ConcernRule
CapabilitiesLanguage moonbit; separate Boolean-library profile. Rich compilation is explicitly negotiated. Legacy compilation, multiple documents, imports, external dependencies, fragments, streaming and wire cancellation stay unadvertised.
ModelIon uses morphir_model with semantic IR, the existing versioned node carrier and provenance. It never uses the engine checkpoint envelope. Stable model identity binds package and document URI; logical revision binds source version/content, options and declared context independently of payload bytes.
JSONHonor explicit JSON selection through checked export; refuse data.lossy_conversion when naming/provenance would be lost. Never substitute codecs after refusal.
AdmissionExact operation tuple, options.irVersion agreement, language, source count, document version, root-relative module identity, package visibility and context are validated. Unsupported inputs are refused before calling the pure frontend. Emitted bytes/tree and response must fit immutable session limits.
AuthoritySource metadata and context attribution grant no host capability or remote guarantee. Cooperative cancellation is available to embedded callers; the sequential native transport does not advertise wire cancellation.

Task 1: compose a frontend provider

Add a typed provider/input/result seam to pkgs/morphir-moonbit/mep. Keep backend-only Session::new behavior. Configure apps/morphir-extension with the pure frontend, conservative source-path derivation and explicit supported profile/options. Test exact negotiated compile/generate operation separation and immutable selection.

Task 2: compile and encode a model

Validate the canonical request, call the supplied compiler and serialize its complete output with the existing node-metadata carrier. Bind identity, revision and compilation provenance. Check loss before JSON export, then validate output against the same budgets used for generation. Success requires a model; all failure paths omit it.

Task 3: qualify protocol refusals

Cover malformed source, source/dependency sets, language/profile/options, identity/root/context, tuple substitution, changed source revisions, budget boundaries, cancellation and recoverable failure. Use a plain test provider to prove successful checked JSON without discarding facts; the real source provider must refuse lossy JSON.

Task 4: exercise the native process and consumer

Extend apps/morphir-extension/acceptance to interactively compile then generate in a real framed session. Inspect node carrier, original names and origin identity, retain evidence, write returned artifacts only in the acceptance host, and build/run a consumer against the checked-in SDK. Keep existing legacy/rich generation cases.

Task 5: validate and deliver

Run focused protocol/provider tests, four-target portable checks, native process acceptance and repository pre-push lint/format/validation. Update README and beads with actual evidence, commit and open a focused PR. Monitor CI and address PR-caused failures. Merge and releases require separate maintainer approval.
acceptance_criteria: A real framed native session compiles supported source, retains original public names, references, origin identity and metadata, then feeds its model into landed generateModel and builds/invokes a consumer. Ion and checked JSON paths are qualified; success requires a model and failure forbids it, including null. Limits, malformed source, unsupported source/dependency sets, cancellation and context/identity consistency have focused tests. No dependency cycle or authority created by wire metadata. Existing legacy/native and four-target pure component checks pass.

title: Scheme modules: language reference as package-level docs
description:
Detailed Morphir Scheme language documentation, treated like MoonBit's language docs: one chapter per package as README.mbt.md (core language, models, running IR, transform scripts, specification notation, later the module layer), rendered by mooncakes on each package page and by the project site under /docs/packages/morphir-scheme/<chapter>/. Every scheme example is checked: scripts/scheme-docs.mbtx generates a test file per package from the chapters, and mise run scheme-docs:check fails CI on drift. The site generator learns README.mbt.md and sub-package README pages.

Lands before morphir-ukvn.5.45.1, which adds the model and module chapters through this pipeline. Spec: this bead's design (HTML).
design:
Scheme modules: language reference as package-level docs

Bead morphir-ukvn.5.45.4 (epic morphir-ukvn.5.45) · drafted 2026-10-16 · awaiting review

  • Goal
  • Context
  • Decisions
  • Non-goals
  • 1. Chapters
  • 2. The core language chapter
  • 3. Checked examples
  • 4. Tooling and CI
  • 5. The project site
  • 6. Mooncakes
  • 7. Writing rules
  • 8. Testing
  • 9. What morphir-ukvn.5.45.1 adds

Goal

Morphir Scheme has a detailed language reference, treated like MoonBit's language docs: ordered chapters, each covering one part of the language in depth, where every example is run by the test suite. The chapters are package-level docs of finos/morphir-scheme, so the same text appears on each package's page on mooncakes and under /docs/packages/morphir-scheme/ on the project site.

Context

  • MoonBit's convention is one README.mbt.md per package. Mooncakes renders it on the package page, and moon test runs its mbt check blocks, so MoonBit examples cannot drift. MoonBit's own language site has separate ordered chapters whose examples are also compiled and tested.
  • pkgs/morphir-scheme/README.md is today's only Scheme documentation: one page covering packages, embedding, transform scripts, the language boundary, limits and the specification notation. No sub-package has a README, and no Scheme example is tested from the docs.
  • The project site renders only pkgs/<name>/README.md for each package listed in site/site.json, at /docs/packages/<name>/ (apps/morphir-site/site/pages.mbt, sources.mbt). Other Markdown under pkgs/ becomes a GitHub link.
  • finos/morphir-scheme's root package shares its directory with the module, so one README.mbt.md there is both the module page and the root package page.
  • mise run sdk-spec:check is the precedent for a generated, checked-in artifact that CI verifies; it runs in the "Elm and Scheme end to end" job.

Decisions

DecisionWhy
One chapter per package, as README.mbt.mdMoonBit's convention; mooncakes renders every chapter on its package page with no extra publishing step
Plain ```scheme blocks with expected-result comments, checked through generated testsReaders see Scheme, not MoonBit wrappers, and the examples still cannot drift
The site renders a listed package's sub-package READMEs as pagesOne source for both venues; other packages can adopt the same layout later
This bead lands before morphir-ukvn.5.45.1Documenting today's language does not depend on modules; the module work then writes its chapters into a working pipeline

Non-goals

  • The module, type and package chapters: morphir-ukvn.5.45.1 writes them (section 9).
  • A separate documentation site or generator. The project site and mooncakes are the two venues.
  • Changing any Scheme behaviour. A doc example that exposes a bug gets a bead, not a fix in this work.
  • Package-level docs for other modules of the repository; the site support is general, but only finos/morphir-scheme adopts it here.

1. Chapters

FileChapterContent
pkgs/morphir-scheme/README.mbt.mdMorphir SchemeWhat the language is and where it runs, how to add the package, the chapter index, then the core language (section 2)
pkgs/morphir-scheme/frontend/README.mbt.mdWriting modelsCompiling Scheme to Morphir IR: compile_expression, compile_file, the functional subset, leading definitions and main, qualified references, type placeholders and inference, what the frontend rejects and why
pkgs/morphir-scheme/backend/README.mbt.mdRunning Morphir IRevaluate, emit_expression, emit_file, emit_unit, install, call_entry, run_file; the SDK bridge; externals, natives and accelerators; linking; the symbols sidecar and source comments
pkgs/morphir-scheme/pipeline/README.mbt.mdTransform scriptsScripts as IRFile -> IRFile procedures, every ir-* procedure, bottom-up rewriting, the JSON bridge, use from morphir.config.scm
pkgs/morphir-scheme/spec/README.mbt.mdSpecification notationToday's specification notation section, moved and checked
  • Every paragraph of today's README.md moves to one of these chapters; nothing is dropped. The old file is removed and moon.mod's readme points at README.mbt.md.
  • Each chapter opens with one paragraph on what it covers and links to the previous and next chapter and to the index. Links are relative (../frontend/README.mbt.md), so they work on GitHub and the site resolves them.
  • MoonBit API examples in a chapter are mbt check blocks, tested by moon test as in MoonBit core.

2. The core language chapter

The root chapter is the language reference proper, in this order:

  1. Overview: Morphir Scheme's purpose (writing transforms and executing Morphir IR), the targets it runs on, and how it relates to R6RS: an independent implementation of a subset, not R6RS.
  2. Lexical syntax: lists and dotted pairs, quotation, vectors, strings and their escapes, characters, escaped identifiers, booleans, numbers (exact integers, normalized exact rationals, finite inexact reals), line, nested block and datum comments, and the tokens the reader refuses.
  3. Values: every runtime value kind, its printed form, equality and truthiness (only #f is false in the interpreter).
  4. Special forms: define, set!, lambda (fixed and variadic), if, begin, and, or, let, let*, letrec and its read-before-initialization rule, named let, quote; each with its syntax, meaning and errors.
  5. Built-in procedures: grouped as arithmetic, comparison, lists, higher-order (map, fold-left, apply), strings, records and vectors; each with its signature and an example.
  6. Errors: what raises, the error kinds and their messages, error_message.
  7. Limits: steps, depth and frames, defaults, what they bound and what they do not, tail calls.
  8. Embedding: Runtime, sessions, define_native, closures bound to their session.
  9. Outside the language: macros, quasiquotation, continuations, ports, mutable pairs, the full numeric tower and library system.

The procedure list comes from the evaluator's registration code, and a test asserts that every registered procedure appears in the chapter, so the reference stays complete.

3. Checked examples

(define (inc x) (+ x 1))
(inc 41)
;; => 42

(letrec ((a b) (b 1)) a)
;; error: Uninitialized recursive binding: b
  • Every ```scheme block in a chapter is an example. Its trailing comment states the expectation: ;; => text for the printed result, ;; error: text for a failure whose error_message starts with text. A block with neither must run without error.
  • ```scheme notest marks a block that is shown but not run, for a sketch that contains … or a fragment. Each chapter keeps these rare; the test that lists examples reports their count.
  • A ;; file: path line at the top of a block puts it in an in-memory project at that path; consecutive file: blocks form one project, checked as a whole by the last block's expectation. This is for multi-file examples in the model chapters.
  • How a block runs depends on its chapter:
ChapterA block is
Morphir Scheme (core)Evaluated in a fresh Runtime; the result is printed with value_to_string
Writing modelsCompiled with compile_file, then main run with run_file
Running Morphir IREvaluated in a runtime with backend.install
Transform scriptsEvaluated in pipeline.new_runtime()
Specification notationRead with read_package or, for a lone type, read_type_text; ;; => compares the printed form

4. Tooling and CI

  • scripts/scheme-docs.mbtx, a MoonBit script per AGENTS.md, reads each chapter and writes docs_examples_test.mbt next to it: one blackbox test per example, named after the chapter, the example's number and its line, with the block's source and expectation as string literals. The file starts with a "generated by scripts/scheme-docs.mbtx; do not edit" comment.
  • A small harness in each package's test files implements the five run modes above, so the generated tests stay one-line calls.
  • mise run scheme-docs:generate rewrites the generated files. mise run scheme-docs:check fails when a generated file differs from what the chapters produce, with the chapter and line of the first difference; CI runs it in the "Elm and Scheme end to end" job, beside sdk-spec:check.
  • The generated tests run with every moon test, on native, js, wasm and wasm-gc.

5. The project site

  • The generator accepts README.mbt.md wherever it accepts README.md; with both present in one directory the build fails, naming the directory.
  • For a package listed in site/site.json, every sub-package directory with a README becomes a page at /docs/packages/<name>/<sub-path>/, listed below the package page in the sidebar, ordered by the package's optional chapters list in site/site.json, then by order front matter, then by title. Published package READMEs carry no front matter, because mooncakes and GitHub receive the file as it is; morphir-scheme lists its sub-packages there instead. (Revised by the final review of morphir-ukvn.5.45.4.)
  • Links between chapters resolve to their site pages; links to other repository files still become GitHub links.
  • ```mbt check and ```mbt test fences are highlighted as MoonBit; ```scheme notest as Scheme. The info string after the language never shows on the page.
  • docs/WRITING_FOR_THE_SITE.md documents sub-package pages and the README rule.

6. Mooncakes

  • Mooncakes renders each README.mbt.md on its package page and the root one on the module page. No publishing change is needed beyond moon.mod's readme field.
  • Before the bead closes, a dry run (moon publish --dry-run, or moon package) confirms that the chapters are in the published archive. Whether mooncakes resolves relative links between packages is checked on the first real publish; if it does not, chapters link to the project site instead, and the site rewrites those links to local routes.

7. Writing rules

  • The repository's writing rules apply (plain English, one idea per sentence, no unexplained acronyms).
  • Each form or procedure gets its syntax, its meaning, its errors and at least one checked example; an example shows one idea.
  • Tables for parallel facts (procedures, forms, error codes); prose for behaviour.
  • Describe what the language does today. Planned features appear only in a short "Planned" note that names the bead.

8. Testing

  • Script: unit tests for block extraction (expectations, notest, file: grouping, line numbers) and for the check mode's difference report.
  • Chapters: the generated tests pass on all four targets; the completeness test for built-in procedures passes.
  • Site: generator tests for README.mbt.md, sub-package pages, the sidebar entries, link resolution between chapters, and the failure when both README kinds exist; mise run test:site and check:site stay green.
  • Compatibility: every existing Scheme test is unchanged and green.

9. What morphir-ukvn.5.45.1 adds

  • The "Writing models" chapter gains sections for modules and submodules, the package manifest, provide and require, name resolution, type declarations, signatures, match, the two compilation modes and the error codes; package-mode examples use ;; file: blocks.
  • A new chapter, pkgs/morphir-scheme/modules/README.mbt.md, documents the module layer API.
  • The core chapter states that the evaluator refuses module and type forms until morphir-ukvn.5.45.2.
close_reason: Merged in https://github.com/finos/morphir-moonbit/pull/123 (squash commit ce311b31cb5f on main): five README.mbt.md chapters with generated example tests, the schemedocs generator and CI check, site sub-package pages. Follow-ups: .5.46, .5.48, .5.49, .5.50, .5.52, .5.53.

title: Scheme modules: module language, types and package-mode frontend
description:
The module language (module, provide, require, src/package.scm), Typed Racket-style types (define-type, define-record, define-variant, signatures, match), the shared module layer finos/morphir-scheme/modules, and the package-mode Scheme frontend (whole-project compiler selected by the manifest). File mode stays compatible. The design is this bead's spec (HTML).

Fixes morphir-ukvn.5.22.8 (references to top-level defines lower as Value::Reference).
design:
Scheme modules: module language, types and package-mode frontend

Bead morphir-ukvn.5.45.1 (epic morphir-ukvn.5.45) · drafted 2026-10-16 · awaiting review

  • Goal
  • Context
  • Decisions
  • Non-goals
  • A worked example
  • 1. Modules and submodules
  • 2. The package manifest
  • 3. provide
  • 4. require and module paths
  • 5. Name resolution
  • 6. Source names
  • 7. Type declarations
  • 8. Type expressions
  • 9. Signatures
  • 10. Records, variants and match
  • 11. Lowering to IR
  • 12. Compilation modes and the engine
  • 13. Code layout
  • 14. Errors
  • 15. Testing
  • 16. Documentation
  • 17. Later sub-projects

Goal

A Scheme project can declare a full Morphir model: type aliases, records, tagged custom types with constructors, typed values, and public or private access, with references that resolve across modules. The IR it produces equals what the Elm frontend produces for the same model, ignoring source locations. Existing Scheme files, transform scripts and the specification notation keep working unchanged.

Context

  • A Scheme file is one module today. The engine names it from its source-relative path (with project.module_prefix); the package is project.name. Every top-level define becomes a public value, and trailing expressions become main (pkgs/morphir-scheme/frontend/frontend.mbt, compile_file).
  • There is no export list, no import and no private value. Cross-module references are written inline as module#name or pkg:module#name.
  • A reference to another top-level define of the same module lowers as a local Value::Variable, so inference reports unknown_reference (bead morphir-ukvn.5.22.8).
  • Scheme source has no type declarations. Types exist only in the specification notation (finos/morphir-scheme/spec), which is read as data and never evaluated.
  • bind_name is Name::parse, which accepts only canonical names such as is-eligible; Shape and isEligible are refused.
  • The reader already records the offset of every sub-form (parse_program_located, line_column), so located errors need no reader change.
  • The engine can hold a plain frontend and a project compiler for the same language (select_source_frontend), but two providers with no selection rule would make every Scheme project ambiguous.
  • The SDK specification (pkgs/morphir-sdk-spec/sdk.scm) defines the modules basics, char, decimal, dict, int, list, local-date, maybe, result, set and string.

Decisions

DecisionWhy
Racket-inspired, not Racket-compatible: no #lang, Morphir module paths, Morphir SDK type namesFree to map cleanly to IR; Racket fidelity is secondary
A file is a module named by its path; (module name …) declares a nested moduleRacket's default; existing files keep their module names
provide and require with prefix-in, only-in, rename-in, except-inRacket's import vocabulary, familiar and sufficient
A data-only src/package.scm names the package and its exposed modulesClosest to WIT packages and Cargo's manifest; readable at plan time without running Scheme
Typed Racket-style types with explicit heads define-type, define-record, define-variantTyped Racket's U is an untagged union and would mislead; WIT's type, record and variant map one to one onto Morphir
A shared module layer, finos/morphir-scheme/modules, and a whole-project compiler selected by the manifestPlain require resolves against real provide lists; the evaluator and backend sub-projects reuse the layer

Non-goals

  • Evaluator namespaces (morphir-ukvn.5.45.2) and module-structured Scheme output (morphir-ukvn.5.45.3).
  • Documentation strings, extensible records, re-exports (all-from-out), match exhaustiveness checks.
  • Dependencies between Scheme packages and versioned imports.
  • Any change to the specification notation or to emit_file output.

A worked example

;; src/package.scm   (data, never evaluated)
(package "pricing"
  (exposed pricing/rates))

;; src/pricing/customers.scm   →  module pricing/customers
(provide (type-out Tier) (type-out Customer) customer-tier)
(define-variant Tier (Standard) (Gold) (Platinum [years : Int]))
(define-record Customer [name : String] [tier : Tier])
(: customer-tier (-> Customer Tier))
(define (customer-tier c) (Customer-tier c))

;; src/pricing/rates.scm   →  module pricing/rates
(provide quote-for Rate)
(require (only-in pricing/customers customer-tier Customer Tier Standard Gold Platinum))
(define-type Rate Decimal)
(: discount (-> Tier Float))
(define (discount tier)
  (match tier
    [(Standard) 0.0]
    [(Gold) 0.1]
    [(Platinum years) (if (> years 5) 0.25 0.2)]))
(: quote-for (-> Customer Float Float))
(define (quote-for c amount)
  (* amount (- 1.0 (discount (customer-tier c)))))

(module tiers                                 ; submodule pricing/rates/tiers
  (provide default-discount)
  (define default-discount 0.05))

Package pricing gets three modules. pricing/rates is Public; pricing/customers and pricing/rates/tiers are Private. In pricing/rates, quote-for and Rate are public; discount is private.

1. Modules and submodules

  • A file's module path is today's: its source-relative path without the extension, after project.module_prefix, as a canonical Morphir path.
  • (module name form …) declares the module <enclosing path>/<name>. It may appear anywhere at a module's top level, may nest, and accepts the same forms as a file's top level. A submodule is a separate Morphir module: it sees only what it requires, not its parent's definitions, and the parent sees only what the submodule provides and the parent requires by full path.
  • A submodule path that equals a file-derived module path is scheme.duplicate_module.
  • Trailing expressions keep today's meaning (a value main) in file mode. In package mode they are scheme.top_level_expression: a model module declares values by name.

2. The package manifest

(package "pricing"
  (exposed pricing/rates
           pricing/customers))
  • The file is package.scm at the root of project.source_directory. It is read with the Scheme reader as data and never evaluated. The planner never compiles it as a module, as it already skips morphir.config.scm.
  • (package "name" item …): the name is a canonical Morphir package path. A non-canonical name is scheme.manifest_invalid, with the canonical spelling in the message.
  • (exposed path …), at most once: canonical module paths within the package, submodules by full path. Listed modules are Public; every other module is Private. Without exposed, every module is Public. A listed path with no module is scheme.manifest_unknown_module.
  • Any other item is scheme.manifest_invalid. The (package …) head matches the specification notation, so later items, for example dependencies, can join the same file.
  • When configuration sets project.name or project.exposed_modules and the manifest sets the same fact differently, planning fails with scheme.manifest_conflict, naming both files. Equal values are accepted.

3. provide

SpecExports
name (a value)The value, Public
Name (a type)The type, Public; a variant's constructors stay Private (opaque); a record's constructor and accessors stay unexported
(type-out Name)The type and its constructors (variant), or its constructor and accessors (record)
(all-defined-out)Every value and type of the module, types as with type-out
(rename-out …), (all-from-out …)Refused in this sub-project with scheme.unsupported: IR names cannot differ from definition names, and IR has no re-exports
  • provide may appear several times; the exports are the union. A name provided but not defined is scheme.provide_unknown.
  • Compatibility. A module with no provide form makes everything public, as today. Once a module has any provide, unlisted values and types are Private.
  • Type access follows the Elm frontend: an opaque export is (Public, Private) for a custom type and its constructors, type-out is (Public, Public), not exported is (Private, Private).
  • A record's constructor and accessors have no IR existence: (Point 1.0 2.0) lowers to a Record value and (Point-x p) to a Field. Exporting them only decides whether importing Scheme modules may use those spellings; the record type alias itself has the access of the type.

4. require and module paths

SpecBinds
mEvery name m provides, unqualified
(prefix-in p: m)Every provided name n as p:n
(only-in m n …)Only the listed names; [n local] renames on import
(rename-in m [n local] …)All provided names, with the listed ones renamed
(except-in m n …)All provided names except the listed ones
  • The specs nest as in Racket, for example (prefix-in r: (only-in m a b)).
  • A module path is a canonical module path within the same package (pricing/customers), or package:module for another package (morphir/SDK:list), matching the pkg:module#name reference syntax.
  • Constructors and accessors are names in their own right: the provider exports them with type-out, and an importer binds them by their own spellings (Gold, Customer-tier), or by a plain require of the module.
  • SDK provide lists and types come from morphir-sdk-spec. Requiring a package other than the current one or morphir/SDK is scheme.unknown_module in this sub-project.
  • Requires may appear anywhere at a module's top level and apply to the whole module.
  • Modules that require each other, directly or through others, are scheme.require_cycle.

5. Name resolution

  1. Local binders: parameters, let bindings and match pattern variables.
  2. The module's own definitions, lowered to Value::Reference. This fixes morphir-ukvn.5.22.8.
  3. Names bound by require.
  4. Today's built-in primitives (+, if, …) and built-in type names (section 8).
  • A definition shadows an import of the same name, as in Racket. Two requires binding one name to different targets are scheme.import_conflict, reported at the second require.
  • Fully qualified module#name and pkg:module#name keep working everywhere and bypass resolution.
  • A name that resolves to nothing is scheme.unbound_name in package mode. File mode keeps today's behaviour for unknown lowercase names (a variable), so existing files compile unchanged; an unknown capitalized name, which today fails Name::parse, is scheme.unbound_name in both modes.

6. Source names

  • Source spellings convert to canonical Morphir names by splitting words at - and at case changes, as the Elm frontend's elm_words does: Shape becomes shape, isEligible becomes is-eligible, is-eligible stays. The splitter moves to finos/morphir-ir as Name::from_spelling, so the Scheme frontend can use it without depending on finos/morphir-elm. The Elm frontend keeps its own copy in this sub-project; the parity test (section 15) keeps them in step.
  • Two definitions whose spellings convert to the same name are scheme.duplicate_definition.
  • Prefixes from prefix-in are part of the local spelling only (list:map); they never reach IR.

7. Type declarations

(define-type Amount Decimal)                     ; alias
(define-type (Pair a) (Tuple a a))               ; alias with a parameter
(define-record Point [x : Float] [y : Float])    ; record
(define-record (Box a) [value : a])              ; record with a parameter
(define-variant Shape                            ; tagged custom type
  (Circle [radius : Float])
  (Square [side : Float]))
(define-variant (Tree a)
  (Leaf)
  (Node (Tree a) a (Tree a)))                    ; unnamed arguments
FormMorphir IR
(define-type Name T), (define-type (Name a …) T)TypeAliasDefinition(params, T)
(define-record Name [f : T] …)TypeAliasDefinition(params, Record([f: T …])), fields in source order
(define-variant Name (Ctor arg …) …)CustomTypeDefinition(params, constructors), constructors in source order
Constructor argument [name : T]Named argument
Constructor argument TArgument named arg-1, arg-2, … by position, as the specification notation does
  • Type and constructor names are capitalized spellings; a lowercase head is scheme.invalid_type_name.
  • A parameter used in the body must be declared, or the body has scheme.unknown_type. An unused declared parameter is allowed, since Morphir allows phantom parameters.
  • A record with no field, a variant with no constructor, or a duplicate field or constructor within one type is scheme.invalid_type. A constructor name used twice in one module is scheme.duplicate_definition.

8. Type expressions

SyntaxIR type
Int, Float, Bool, String, Char, DecimalReferences to the SDK types basics#int, basics#float, basics#bool, string#string, char#char, decimal#decimal
UnitType::Unit
(List a), (Maybe a), (Result e a), (Dict k v), (Set a)References to the SDK types, with arguments
(Tuple a b …)Tuple, at least two elements
(Record [f : T] …)Record
(-> A B C)Curried Function, A -> B -> C; at least two types
A lowercase symbol, for example aVariable
A capitalized symbol, or (Name T …)Reference to a type resolved like a value name (section 5), with the built-in names above as the last step
module#Name, pkg:module#NameFully qualified Reference

Applying a type to the wrong number of arguments is scheme.type_arity.

9. Signatures

(: area (-> Shape Float))
(define (area s) …)

(define (norm [p : Point]) : Float …)            ; inline, Typed Racket style
(: rate Float)
(define rate 1.5)
  • (: name T) types the definition of name in the same module, wherever it appears. The definition's parameters take the arrow's argument types in order, and the rest of the arrow is the output, as the Elm frontend lifts annotations. A definition with more parameters than the arrow has arguments is scheme.signature_mismatch; with fewer, the remaining arrow is the output.
  • Inline annotations: a parameter [p : T], and : T after the parameter list. A (:) signature and inline annotations on one definition must agree, else scheme.signature_mismatch.
  • A signature with no definition is scheme.signature_without_define; two signatures for one name are scheme.duplicate_definition.
  • Untyped parameters and outputs keep today's t-<n> placeholders with morphir.inference = unknown, so pipeline.inference = "fill" solves them.

10. Records, variants and match

ExpressionIR value
(Circle 2.0)Apply(Constructor(fq), 2.0); a constructor is a curried function and may be partially applied
(Leaf) or LeafConstructor(fq)
(Point 1.0 2.0)Record with fields in declaration order; must be fully applied, else scheme.record_arity
(Point-x p)Field(p, x); the accessor is the record type's spelling, -, and the field's spelling
(struct-copy Point p [x 3.0] …)UpdateRecord(p, {x: 3.0 …}); an unknown field is scheme.unknown_field
(tuple a b …)Tuple, at least two elements
 
(match shape
  [(Circle r) (* 3.14159 (* r r))]
  [(and (Square side) sq) (area-of sq side)]
  [_ 0.0])
PatternIR pattern
_WildcardPattern
x (a lowercase symbol)AsPattern(WildcardPattern, x)
A literal: number, string, character, #t or #fLiteralPattern
(Ctor p …), CtorConstructorPattern; the argument count must match, else scheme.pattern_arity
(tuple p …)TuplePattern
'(), (list p …), (cons h t)EmptyListPattern, nested HeadTailPattern
(and p x)AsPattern(p, x), Racket's way to name a matched value
  • Clauses are [pattern body …]; several body forms lower as today's begin. match lowers to PatternMatch. Exhaustiveness is not checked.
  • A pattern variable bound twice in one pattern is scheme.duplicate_binding.
  • Constructors and accessors are definitions of their module: a define whose spelling equals a constructor or an accessor (Point-x) is scheme.duplicate_definition.
  • No reader change is needed: every form uses symbols, lists and brackets the reader already accepts.

11. Lowering to IR

  • One Morphir module per file module and per submodule, in the package named by the manifest (package mode) or project.name (file mode).
  • Values keep today's lowering, extended by section 5 (references), section 9 (types) and section 10 (records, variants and match). Value and type access come from section 3; module access from section 2.
  • Value and pattern nodes carry the SourceLocation of their form, with rows and columns from 1, as the Elm frontend does.
  • Output is deterministic: modules, types, constructors and values keep a fixed order, independent of the order in which the host lists files.

12. Compilation modes and the engine

File mode (no src/package.scm)Package mode (with the manifest)
CompilerToday's per-file compiler; output is a plain IRFileWhole-project compiler; one unit per package, whose id is the canonical package path
New formsEvery form that needs only the file: provide, type declarations, signatures, match, submodules, SDK requires, qualified referencesAll forms
Same-package requirescheme.require_needs_package, pointing at src/package.scmResolved across files
BackendsAll, as today; ir-json stays the defaultCheckpoint (default, morphir-json, as for morphir.json projects), moonbit, elm, and the scheme unit backend; ir-json is refused with frontend.typed_backend_required
Engine::runWorksRefused, as for every project compiler
  • The plan and the workbench catalog report provider scheme with two profiles, file (the default) and package. The planner selects package when the manifest exists, unless frontend.profile says otherwise. Forcing package without a manifest is a planning error; forcing file with one compiles each file alone and ignores the manifest.
  • Package mode compiles every .scm and .ss file under the source directory, except the manifest and morphir.config.scm, in sorted path order. Transforms and components follow the existing project-compiler rules.
  • Package-mode units carry no node metadata, so the default morphir-json checkpoint accepts them.
  • The evaluator refuses provide, require, module, the type forms, (:), match and struct-copy with scheme.needs_frontend until morphir-ukvn.5.45.2. emit_file is unchanged until morphir-ukvn.5.45.3.

13. Code layout

PackageResponsibility
finos/morphir-irName::from_spelling (section 6)
finos/morphir-scheme/modules (new)Expand a located file into module syntax (provides, requires, type declarations, signatures, definitions, submodules); read the manifest; resolve names across a package and the SDK specification; collect located problems. It depends only on finos/morphir-scheme, finos/morphir-ir and finos/morphir-sdk-spec.
finos/morphir-scheme/frontendLower resolved modules to IR: compile_file (file mode, extended) and compile_package(sources, package_name) (package mode)
finos/morphir-engineThe package profile, manifest detection at plan time, the package-mode default checkpoint, and the conflict check with configuration

14. Errors

Package mode reports every problem in one pass, as the Elm frontend does, through RejectedSources: each problem has a code, a path relative to the source directory, and a SourceLocation. File mode raises the same codes as the message prefix of its errors; existing messages stay as they are.

CodeRaised for
scheme.unknown_moduleA require of a module that does not exist, or of a package other than the current one and the SDK
scheme.unknown_importA name in only-in, rename-in or except-in that the provider does not export
scheme.import_conflictTwo requires binding one name to different targets
scheme.require_cycleModules that require each other
scheme.require_needs_packageA same-package require in file mode
scheme.unbound_name, scheme.unknown_typeA value or type name that resolves to nothing (package mode)
scheme.provide_unknownprovide of something not defined
scheme.duplicate_definition, scheme.duplicate_module, scheme.duplicate_bindingA name, module or pattern variable declared twice
scheme.invalid_type, scheme.invalid_type_name, scheme.type_arityMalformed type declarations and applications
scheme.signature_without_define, scheme.signature_mismatchSignature problems
scheme.record_arity, scheme.unknown_field, scheme.pattern_arityRecord and pattern shape problems
scheme.top_level_expressionA trailing expression in package mode
scheme.manifest_invalid, scheme.manifest_unknown_module, scheme.manifest_conflictManifest problems
scheme.unsupportedrename-out, all-from-out and other Racket forms outside this design
scheme.needs_frontendThe evaluator meeting a module or type form

15. Testing

  • Module layer: expansion of every form; resolution order; each require spec and their nesting; opaque exports against type-out; submodule paths and isolation; manifest reading; every error code with its location.
  • Elm parity: one model written in Scheme package mode and in Elm, with aliases, a record, a variant with a parameter, signatures, match, cross-module requires, and private and public items. The two IRs are equal in types, constructors, access, inputs and outputs, ignoring source locations. This pins the goal.
  • Compatibility: every existing Scheme frontend, evaluator, pipeline, backend and engine test is unchanged and green, and emit_file output is unchanged.
  • Engine: the manifest selects package mode; frontend.profile overrides it; forcing package without a manifest fails; ir-json is refused in package mode; the default checkpoint is morphir-json; a manifest that conflicts with configuration fails; the catalog lists both profiles.
  • Inference: a typed package passes pipeline.inference = "check"; an untyped package with cross-define references passes "fill", closing morphir-ukvn.5.22.8 and restoring the end-to-end corpus programs it forced into self-contained form.
  • End to end: the Scheme-to-MoonBit and Scheme-to-Elm checks (e2e:scheme-moonbit, e2e:scheme-elm) run a typed package through each generator, covering what each generator supports.
  • New tests use moonrockz/expect.

16. Documentation

The Scheme language reference is package-level docs, built by morphir-ukvn.5.45.4, which lands first: one README.mbt.md chapter per package, on mooncakes and on the project site, with every ```scheme example checked by generated tests. This bead adds, through that pipeline:

  • "Writing models" (frontend/README.mbt.md): sections for modules and submodules, the package manifest, provide and require, name resolution, source names, type declarations, type expressions, signatures, records, variants and match, the two compilation modes, and the error codes. Package-mode examples use ;; file: blocks; every error code has an example.
  • "The module layer" (modules/README.mbt.md, new): the API of finos/morphir-scheme/modules, with mbt check examples.
  • The core chapter: a note that the evaluator refuses module and type forms until morphir-ukvn.5.45.2.
  • "Specification notation": a sentence that it remains the notation for package specifications, distinct from model modules.
  • pkgs/morphir-engine/README.md: the package profile and manifest detection.

17. Later sub-projects

  • morphir-ukvn.5.45.2: Racket-style namespaces in the evaluator, so transform scripts and morphir.config.scm can require script modules; this needs a host capability to read them.
  • morphir-ukvn.5.45.3: the Scheme backend emits one module per Morphir module with provide and require, keeping the symbols sidecar and source comments.

Native owner lifecycle qualification

morphir-etg2.15.5.7 · 17 October 2026 · complete

  • Scope and progress
  • Production boundaries

  • Behaviors and effects
  • Execution checklist

Scope and progress

The evaluation/job roadmap has 24 of 25 leaf tasks closed, 96% complete and 4% remaining, a 24:1 completed-to-remaining ratio. Native MCK leaf tasks have 7 of 7 closed, 100% complete. This does not close the parent platform qualification requirements. Counts measure tickets, not effort or the whole UI roadmap. Actual packaged OS/architecture acceptance remains separate required evidence within the parent work.

96%

Trusted-port checkpoint df98194 passed focused red/green tests and fresh real worker/bridge acceptance. Base: MoonBit ac78a96 and Morphir e651e637. Client draft.9 is merged in PRs #115/#1054. This task adds exact offline MCK draft.10, JSON-only run-native-owner, while preserving all historical MCK contracts and live native draft.1. Permissive admission planning remains the next evaluation roadmap task.

Production boundaries

Explore the source-backed owner MCK architecture. The diagram pins committed implemented ports at df98194, qualified candidate at347df73, retaining owner adapter at8a56da4 and parent contract at 684c2b9e; distinct branches show real native resources and controlled bindings. Archify automated artifact/browser checks pass. The desktop diagram and390px plan were visually reviewed.

The production bridge.Owner retains native session admission and orchestration. A typed ServiceFactories constructor supplies trusted jobs and workspace capabilities; presence enables the capability, which is published only after successful construction and awaited predecessor cleanup. Owner::new continues to wrap real native worker and filesystem services for the desktop. Renderer envelopes cannot provide factories, callbacks, executables or paths.

Workspace.Service keeps production picker generations, project discovery, immutable captures, sequence retirement and chunk offsets. Its RootAccess supplies only trusted current/snapshot/read/close IO. Production uses the existing Root and preserves its native checks; MCK uses explicit in-memory fixture bytes. The controlled job resource uses the production jobs.Host for submission, claims and receipts, with explicit completion and cleanup gates. These tests qualify owner coordination and portable receipt behavior; real NativeService process execution and exit need their separate existing acceptance gates.

Controlled contract

The existing Rust runner owns fixture admission, fixed expectations, verdicts, corpus hashes and independent report checking. It never links the implementation or decodes native reply sources. The native adapter uses the actual owner APIs. Model JSON, public entry, JSON/Ion arguments and every workspace manifest/checkpoint byte are inline in cases.json. Reuse the complete draft.9 Int-42 fixtures and separately verify them through the production importer/evaluator.

Input is a closed context, services configuration, evaluation, roots, pickers, per-session cleanups and actions. Root fixtures contain a complete morphir.json manifest and conventional checkpoint names only. Picker results reference declared fixture roots; shared cleanup gates ensure a second waiter cannot confirm cleanup before the held confirmation. Unique IDs and delivery references are infrastructure. A cleanup gate memoizes one settled result for every waiter of its retained service. Unresolved fixture aliases produce a visible reference failure without inventing a native token. A delivery before its boundary is entered is observed as unavailable, not a hang. Calls reference stable aliases for opaque sessions, grants, projects and jobs; the adapter uses consistent first-encounter bijections and never rewrites opaque source strings.

Actions call the thirteen native operations, change out-of-band context, revoke/close/shutdown the owner, deliver held callbacks, complete a controlled job or replace an existing fixture checkpoint. Replacement is a fixture host event, not renderer write authority. No elapsed time decides a verdict. Cooperative task boundaries settle synchronous work; only explicit actions advance held effects. Final teardown is outside the captured observation and drains every controlled gate.

Input is at most 491,520 encoded UTF-8 bytes, 8 roots with 4 checkpoints each, 128 picker/cleanup outcomes and 32 actions. Observations are at most 1 MiB per projection, with inherited aggregate/transport/report budgets. Closed snapshots retain ordered attempt states and dependency-call counts; final results retain canonical success values or portable code/effect errors. Consecutive full reply bodies are not copied into every step. Scalar literal guards precede typed conversion. Malformed infrastructure is an error; client/owner refusals are admitted observations, never domain-invalid MCK records.

Behaviors and effects

  • Wrong controlled caller context invokes no services. Same-page open/check is stable; page replacement is fresh and stale close cannot affect its successor.
  • Held pickers cannot create grants after revocation, replacement or shutdown. Cancellation preserves the old grant. Retired picker cleanup cannot cancel a newer picker.
  • Release before delayed open retires its sequence. Stale release cannot clear a newer capture; replayed offsets fail; JSON/Ion chunks retain original bytes and release/revoke closes the retained root.
  • Immutable submission reaches the controlled boundary once. Cancellation acknowledgement stays nonterminal until explicit completion; separate schedules cover returned-result and cancellation outcomes.
  • Held cleanup prevents a new executable offer or confirmed shutdown. Failure preserves uncertainty. Fresh authority is checked again after awaited cleanup.

The accepted native profile permits a precise no-effect rejection or conservative unknown effect when absence of an effect cannot be established. Some unexecuted abstract traces demand none too narrowly. Draft.10 fixed expectations may explicitly list permitted effects, such as [none, unknown], for those cases. Actual observations and saved reports still carry exactly one effect string. Only the shared Rust comparator evaluates these fixed alternatives. Post-effect uncertainty and established pre-admission refusals keep exact expectations. Historical abstract data and frozen contracts are not silently rewritten.

Controlled context is not OS provenance or top-level-frame authentication. In-memory roots do not establish native containment or filesystem race safety. Controlled cleanup acknowledgement does not prove worker exit. Actual packaged macOS/Linux/Windows GUI, resource and lifecycle evidence remains separate, and no additional platform is advertised.

Native client lifecycle qualification

  • Scope and progress

Scope and progress

92%

86%

The Workbench evaluation/job profile has 23 of 25 leaf tickets closed (92%, 2 remain). Its native qualification sequence has 6 of 7 closed (86%, 1 remains). These are ticket-count measures, not remaining-effort estimates. Packaged OS/architecture qualification is still required within the parent work and is not separately sized. Broader project-explorer and command-palette UI work is outside these counts.

Base: MoonBit 08dcb81a and Morphir 6619ecd8. Raw requests/replies qualify independently in exact offline drafts.7/.8. This slice exercises the shipped TypeScript native client, NativeAdapter, native job transport, workspace client and compiled MoonBit job cursor. Controlled replies are driver inputs, never native authority or actual host execution evidence. Live native draft.1 stays unchanged. Owner lifecycle .5.7 and actual platform qualification remain pending.

Contract and architecture

Exact offline MCK draft.9 adds only JSON run-native-client. The existing shared Rust runner admits a closed, bounded input and observation, sends inputs only and rechecks saved reports against the complete hashed corpus. It never implements client transitions or decodes native source. A separate implementation adapter drives the actual production client with explicit per-operation invocation outcomes (raw text, loss or held completion), user actions and deterministic polling barriers. Repeated valid authority checks are transparent; set-check changes their raw reply explicitly. Canonical JSON sorts object keys while retaining array order and opaque sources. Inputs are bounded to 491,520 encoded bytes, 128 invocation outcomes and 32 actions. No wall-clock sleeps determine verdicts. Fresh compiled core state is isolated for every case.

Each action yields a closed snapshot of session, retained job/flags, workspace transfer state, ordered attempts and emitted requests. Private error text is omitted. Concrete immutable model source, entry, typed JSON/Ion arguments and exact workspace bytes replace Q/P1. All assets remain inline in cases.json. Unconfigured calls and unexpected client behavior produce observable divergence; malformed fixture/transport/report infrastructure remains an error. Production clients run in Node and Chromium, using debug/release compiled cores. Portable cursor tests retain JS/native/Wasm/Wasm GC coverage; a TypeScript client is not claimed as a native executable adapter.

Behaviors

  • Open/bind descriptors, reject changed authority and prevent work after disposal or stale initialization.
  • Submit once, retain uncertainty after lost/malformed replies, distinguish none from unknown effects, reconcile only a known retained identity.
  • Observe receipt transitions, reject replay/conflicts, cancel before/after submission, preserve pending acknowledgement and ignore stale cancellation completions.
  • Retain terminal values and separate cleanup failures; retry release only after fresh matching authority.
  • Preserve workspace offers on picker cancellation, revoke late grants, transfer exact bytes with sequence/offset checks, and release before inspection. Lost reads/opens and failed releases must block unsafe reuse.

Task 1: parent-owned contract and runner


Task 2: production client adapter

Keep TypeScript strict, use checked Bun builds, and keep Node-only framing outside the browser-portable scenario driver. Expected observations never enter the adapter.

Four complete JSON/Ion assets import and evaluate to exact Int 42 through the production worker. Portable cursor tests pass JS/native/Wasm/Wasm GC. Task 3: qualification and landing

design:
Native reply qualification through the shared MCK

morphir-etg2.15.5.5 · 16 October 2026 · delivered

  • Goal and boundaries
  • Offline contract
  • Independent expectations
  • Task 1: shared runner
  • Task 2: production adapter
  • Task 3: qualification and landing

Goal and boundaries

Qualify the production native response decoder using parent-owned expected observations and the existing Rust morphir mck workbench run/check commands. Start from MoonBit 4df0872 and Morphir 63563784, including the latest MEP changes. Keep the native live profile at 0.1.0-draft.1 and preserve all seven historical offline kits.

Client and owner lifecycle execution remain separate follow-ups. Synthetic raw replies do not establish caller provenance, actual OS grants, process exit or packaged-platform qualification.

Offline contract

Exact MCK 0.1.0-draft.8 exposes only validate-native-reply, in JSON. The input is closed: expectedOperation is one of the thirteen native operations, expectedSession is a native session token or null, and encoding/source preserve the original reply bytes. Optional generate.prefix uses the existing bounded ASCII-space recipe. Compact input is limited to 1 MiB and materialization to 2 MiB.

Admitted success projects to {replyAccepted:true,ok:true,operation:...}. Admitted failure projects to {replyAccepted:true,ok:false,error:{code:...,effect:...}}. Messages, source, paths, session credentials and returned workspace/model bytes are omitted. Decoder rejections use exactly native.reply.limit, native.reply.utf8, native.reply.json, native.reply.shape, native.reply.operation or native.reply.authority.

The runner validates infrastructure literal token kinds, versions, shapes, limits and projections; it never interprets native source or links an implementation codec. Expected results and case identifiers never reach the adapter. Malformed infrastructure remains an exchange/report error, while a valid observation differing from the fixed expectation is a compatibility failure.

Independent expectations

Build the fixed corpus from the published native response contract and its structural fixtures, with explicit cross-field/runtime expectations. Cover every operation, both error effects, receipt and descriptor authority, operation mismatch, whole-frame and workspace-picker limits, strict UTF-8, duplicate decoded names, parser budgets, exact integer tokens, project-ID uniqueness and canonical base64 chunks. Include valid counterparts for rejection cases. Keep every source byte and compact recipe within the hashed cases file.

Historical tests and corpora remain unchanged. Report-tampering and literal-private-object cases must prove that infrastructure cannot fabricate acceptance or qualification.

Task 1: shared runner


Files: Morphir spec/workbench/draft.8, spec/workbench/mck/draft.8, shared Workbench contract/corpus/report/run modules and CLI integration tests. Tests exercise opaque input admission, exact capabilities, projection comparison and recomputed report qualification through the existing runner.

Task 2: production adapter

Files: MoonBit apps/morphir-workbench/mck, its imports and README. Preserve historical capability negotiation and fixture-number semantics. Extract compact source materialization only where shared behavior remains exact; do not duplicate production reply admission.

Task 3: qualification and landing



Keep exact source/corpus/report and merged-tree evidence. Public native conformance advertisement still waits for executable client/owner lifecycle MCK and actual packaged OS/architecture evidence.

title: Adopt TypeScript and Bun across UI and JavaScript tooling
description:
Replace handwritten, untyped JavaScript used by the Morphir UIs and their supporting scripts with TypeScript. Use the latest stable Bun for JavaScript/TypeScript package management, direct tooling execution, type checking and JavaScript builds. Active prerequisite work: Damian requested this epic be completed before resuming native Workbench qualification on 2026-10-16.

Repository: finos/morphir-moonbit. Parent: morphir-ukvn.5 (MoonBit ecosystem track). Requested by Damian on 2026-10-16.

The repository already pins Bun 1.4.3 in .config/mise/config.toml. The remaining adoption work includes Node/esbuild build paths, npm installs and package locks, handwritten browser/desktop glue, development servers and acceptance scripts. Existing Bun availability alone does not establish TypeScript coverage or CI enforcement.

Scope includes apps/morphir-workbench, apps/morphir-workbench-desktop, apps/morphir-site, apps/morphir build/test tooling and handwritten runtime wrappers, pkgs/morphir-host/embedding, pkgs/morphir-elm/scripts, and other handwritten JavaScript discovered by the inventory. Generated MoonBit JavaScript remains compiler output; add typed interfaces at its consumption boundaries rather than rewriting generated code.

Preserve browser standalone and daemon-connected operation, worker isolation, Proton/CEF desktop operation, and supported Node/npm package consumers and target smoke tests. Bun is the development toolchain; browser and published Node artifacts must continue to work in their supported runtimes without requiring Bun.
design:
## Toolchain decision and evidence

Verified 2026-10-16: Bun's official release index lists 1.4.3 (2026-10-10) as latest. This is already the repository mise pin. Recheck latest stable when implementation begins, validate it on supported development/CI platforms, then update exact pins and CI together. Do not use floating latest or canary in reproducible CI.

Use bun check as the explicit whole-project TypeScript gate; use bun build --check, or Bun.build with check: true, for checked JavaScript builds. Ordinary TypeScript execution/build does not automatically check types. Bun 1.4.3 includes a checker based on TypeScript 7. Bun does not emit declaration files; retain a pinned TypeScript declaration-emission step only where published APIs need .d.ts output, with editor/checker versions documented.

Primary references:
- https://bun.com/blog/bun-v1.4.3
- https://bun.com/docs/runtime/check
- https://bun.com/docs/typescript
- https://bun.com/docs/bundler
- https://bun.com/docs/pm/cli/install

## Migration stages

- [x] Inventory handwritten .js/.mjs/.cjs and inline JavaScript, dependencies, package roots, runtime assumptions, test runners, generated assets, CI and Proton hooks. Record ownership, runtime targets and explicit generated/vendor/fixture exceptions. Capture current install/build timings and functional baseline.
- [x] Establish shared strict TypeScript settings with separate browser, worker, Node and Bun tooling environments. Scope DOM and runtime globals correctly, enable noUncheckedIndexedAccess, use unknown plus narrowing at external boundaries, and check test code. Temporary allowJs during migration must have a removal checklist; it is not the completion state.
- [x] Deliver one complete Workbench browser/worker/desktop slice: TypeScript source, typed generated-MoonBit and Proton interfaces, Bun JavaScript build, and existing behavior tests. Then migrate remaining UI/editor/artifact/session/workspace/job modules in independently verifiable slices. Keep published protocol contracts authoritative; avoid parallel, divergent wire models.
- [x] Migrate the site and supporting build/dev/test/embedding/Elm scripts and npm CLI wrappers to TypeScript. Bun executes development scripts; Bun emits Node-compatible JavaScript for published Node entrypoints. Preserve package exports, dynamic imports, workers, asset layout, source maps, lifecycle commands, startup and cleanup behavior. Existing MoonBit application code and .mbtx automation stay MoonBit; invoke Bun from existing task orchestration where needed.
- [x] Adopt bun install/add/update with committed bun.lock files, a deliberate package-root/workspace layout, frozen installs in CI and documented dependency lifecycle requirements. Remove superseded package-lock files once the relevant root is migrated; maintain one authoritative lockfile per dependency graph. Update mise tasks, Proton hooks, CI caches and contributor instructions together. Replace esbuild bundling with Bun build after equivalent emitted browser/Node artifacts pass acceptance.
- [x] Enforce complete type coverage, checked builds and clean installs in CI; finish supported platform qualification and compare install/build/typecheck timings. Keep existing Node, Playwright and packaged CEF tests as compatibility evidence. Adopt Bun test only where runner behavior and coverage are demonstrated equivalent; package management/build adoption does not require a blanket test-runner rewrite. Update the existing .dev/design HTML plans with completed/pending checkboxes as slices land, and record task evidence in beads.

## Contract and compatibility requirements

TypeScript types complement production runtime admission. Keep bounded, duplicate-aware JSON/Ion decoding, authentication/authority checks, native envelopes and exact protocol payload behavior. Type assertions must not replace runtime validation of daemon/worker/native/file input. In-memory structures can be strongly typed after validated admission; transport input remains unknown until admitted.

Browser/worker and CEF bundles must contain compatible JavaScript and their required assets, without Bun/Node-only dependencies or globals. Do not introduce a Bun runtime requirement for users of the installed npm CLI or embedding package. Preserve the current MoonBit JS/Wasm/Wasm GC/native test lanes and existing support claims; this migration does not enable new platforms or alter public wire versions.

Prefer explicit interfaces and discriminated unions for editor callbacks, transport requests/replies, jobs, session state, workspace handles, artifact metadata and errors. Avoid broad any, unchecked casts and ts-ignore/ts-nocheck as migration shortcuts. Document narrow unavoidable interop exceptions with an owner and follow-up.

## Scheduling

Active epic, prioritized before native reply/lifecycle MCK and packaged-platform qualification by Damian on 2026-10-16. Create implementation child beads from the inventory as vertical slices; each should build, type-check and preserve behavior before expanding scope. Keep canonical planning and execution evidence in shared beads. Implementation starts from finos/morphir-moonbit main 215e80f, including PR #108 Scheme metadata sidecars and source comments.
