title: Make YAML the primary migrate output format
description: Specify and implement YAML as a native persisted serialization of the concrete Morphir IR, with v4 as the primary target and v3 compatibility where the concrete model permits it. YAML is an equal IR storage format, not a frontend language, generated projection, or documentation view. The migrate command should default v3-to-v4 output to YAML, infer single-file encoding from the destination extension, support document-tree output, and convert stored IR bidirectionally between JSON and YAML. Update v4 so JSON Schema is clearly a bootstrap definition mechanism rather than a restriction of IR storage to JSON.
acceptance_criteria:
EARS acceptance requirements:
AC-01 ubiquitous: The IR codec system shall provide an explicit YAML representation for every valid concrete v3 and v4 IR node.
AC-02 event-driven: When the YAML decoder reads an explicit or preferred readable form, it shall normalize that form into exactly one versioned semantic IR value.
AC-03 event-driven: When the YAML encoder writes an IR value, it shall emit the specified deterministic readable form where one exists and the explicit structural form otherwise.
AC-04 event-driven: When JSON is converted to YAML to JSON without a version transform, the result shall be semantically equal to the original IR.
AC-05 event-driven: When YAML is converted to JSON to YAML without a version transform, the result shall be semantically equal to the original IR.
AC-06 ubiquitous: The codec system shall retain JSON input and output support for every previously supported IR version.
AC-07 unwanted: If YAML contains ambiguous shorthand, duplicate keys, unsupported tags, unsafe aliases, lossy numbers, or invalid coercions, then the decoder shall reject it with a located diagnostic.
AC-08 event-driven: When v3 is migrated to v4 without a selected format or recognized output extension, the command shall emit canonical YAML.
AC-09 event-driven: When resolving single-file output, the command shall apply explicit output format, recognized extension, then YAML default.
AC-10 unwanted: If output format conflicts with a recognized extension, then the command shall diagnose the conflict and shall not publish.
AC-11 event-driven: When resolving single-file input, the command shall apply explicit input format, recognized extension, then bounded JSON-first detection.
AC-12 event-driven: When --json is used without an output path, the command shall write migrated JSON IR to stdout.
AC-13 event-driven: When --json is used with an output path, the command shall write the artifact and emit JSON status and diagnostics to stdout.
AC-14 event-driven: When writing a YAML document tree, the command shall use manifest.yaml, module.yaml, *.type.yaml, and *.value.yaml.
AC-15 ubiquitous: A generated document tree shall use one serialization profile.
AC-16 unwanted: If discovery finds multiple supported manifests, then the reader shall diagnose ambiguity and shall not choose implicitly.
AC-17 event-driven: When a single file is converted to a document tree and back without version change, the result shall be semantically equal.
AC-18 event-driven: When a JSON document tree is converted to YAML and back, the result shall be semantically equal.
AC-19 ubiquitous: Each transform shall declare event, definition, module, or distribution retention.
AC-20 state-driven: While all transforms are event-local, definition-local, or module-local, the pipeline shall retain no more than the largest declared scope plus bounded codec buffers.
AC-21 unwanted: If a transform needs a whole distribution, then the pipeline shall report that requirement before processing.
AC-22 event-driven: When LCR v3 is migrated to v4 YAML as a file or tree, the pipeline shall use its streaming path without retaining the complete distribution.
AC-23 ubiquitous: The pipeline shall carry semantic IR events rather than JSON or YAML value trees.
AC-24 ubiquitous: Public codec options shall keep IR version, layout, format, vocabulary, normalization, and publication independent.
AC-25 event-driven: When a new codec is registered, existing migration transforms and codec callers shall compile unchanged.
AC-26 optional: Where YAML style selection is later exposed, the system shall use existing codec options without changing the semantic model.
AC-27 unwanted: If any pipeline or publication stage fails, then existing output shall remain unchanged.
AC-28 optional: Where --allow-partial is enabled, migration shall recover only through target-version incompleteness constructs.
AC-29 unwanted: If serialization would drop, coerce, or ambiguously reinterpret IR, then --allow-partial shall not permit publication.
AC-30 ubiquitous: Each diagnostic shall include stable code, stage, severity, cursor, guidance, and source location when available.
AC-31 ubiquitous: The v4 specification shall separate the semantic model, JSON profile, YAML profile, and document-tree layout.
AC-32 ubiquitous: The v4 specification shall define logical document identities without physical serialization extensions.
AC-33 event-driven: When a normative YAML example round-trips through normalized IR and JSON, the result shall be semantically equal.
notes:
Design approved and written locally at .dev/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-28-native-yaml-ir-storage-design.md. Native YAML and JSON normalize to versioned semantic IR. Semantic equivalence defines losslessness. Canonical YAML uses deterministic readable shorthand with explicit structural fallback. Current CLI phase adds --input-format and --output-format for JSON/YAML; YAML style selection remains a compatible follow-up. Output resolution is explicit flag, known extension, then YAML default. Input uses explicit flag, known extension, then bounded JSON-first detection. Preserve the legacy context-dependent --json behavior. Homogeneous document trees default to YAML and use manifest.yaml, module.yaml, *.type.yaml, and *.value.yaml. Approved pipeline uses semantic cursor events, composable transforms, declared event/definition/module/distribution buffering, format encoders, layout sinks, and atomic publication. Open codec identifiers leave room for TOML, Markdown, Jupyter, and other adapters without implementing them now. Approved strict diagnostics keep --allow-partial from weakening serialization correctness. Approved v4 spec split: serialization-neutral semantic model, JSON profile, YAML profile, and document-tree profile. JSON Schema remains a bootstrap definition for JSON, not a persistence restriction. Logical identities omit physical extensions; resolve format versus manifest in favor of manifest. V3 semantics remain stable with complete explicit YAML coverage; v4 schema changes are allowed with documented migration behavior. Verification uses TDD, local quality gates, real morphir-elm and morphir-scala fixtures, semantic round-trips, single-file and document-tree acceptance paths, and instrumented bounded-scope LCR streaming. title: Design validated typestate MEP sessions
description: Separate untrusted MEP wire DTOs from validated application state, then assess a generic typestate session controller shared by Extism, spawned-process, and connected-daemon transports. The current session enum prevents some field combinations but still admits identity and capability drift, duplicate capability kinds, stringly typed operation calls, invalid JSON-RPC response envelopes, and uncertain lifecycle outcomes after cancellation or transport failure.
design: Recommended direction from the dedicated review: define an object-safe MepTransport that only exchanges wire requests and responses; put validation and lifecycle rules in Session<T, Loaded|Ready|Indeterminate|Stopped>; expose typed compile, generate, validate, and transform operations on Ready; use a ManagedSession enum only where registries or actors need runtime state erasure. Keep wire::InitializeResult deserializable even when peers disagree, then validate it into NegotiatedSession. Do not silently merge discovery and initialization claims.
acceptance_criteria: Document wire DTO versus validated domain boundaries; decide identity and capability drift policy; cover response JSON-RPC version, request ID correlation, and exactly-one-of-result-or-error validation; represent uncertain lifecycle outcomes explicitly; provide compile-fail tests for invalid state transitions; define migration from the object-safe ExtensionSession API without duplicating state machines across transports.
notes:
Rebased PR #93 onto connected-daemon main commit 6351b3e. New head 294991c integrates ConnectedDaemonTransport with MepTransport and migrates real HTTP conformance, 64 MiB payload, refusal, and timeout tests to Session typestates. Refusal and request timeout now retain Indeterminate because HTTP cannot prove remote state; acknowledged shutdown proves Stopped. Local connected/process/Extism/unit/doc/clippy checks pass. Replacement CI pending.
PR #93 head eee6cf2 boxes the state-bearing Session values in FailedSession, with a concrete ConnectedDaemonTransport size regression capped at 128 bytes. PR #93 is CLEAN and MERGEABLE, all five review threads are resolved, and a final Codex review of eee6cf2 is pending. Final Codex review of head eee6cf2 posted two P2 findings: Session::loaded can wrap a SpawnedProcessSession already advanced through the compatibility API and reset lifecycle/request IDs; failure abort can still wait the full request timeout while collecting a stderr pipe inherited by a descendant. Both were assigned to the dedicated typestate worktree for TDD fixes. PR #93 remains open and must rerun morphir-rust and umbrella consumer verification after its head changes.
PR #93 head fcb9364 addresses the two final-review P2s. title: Prove a distributed Morphir package registry
description: Turn the morphir-scala Package URL and MoonBit registry research and the approved ecosystem package design in finos/morphir#800 into a working Morphir IR-first model-package vertical slice. Establish the MCK package-suite specification foundation, then implement a pinned Git-file index and local-directory backend, exact resolution and locks, verified materialization, workspace overlays, and an Elm acceptance fixture with transitive unpublished dependencies.
design: Follow the IR-first model-package design in finos/morphir#800 and kb/bundles/morphir/morphir-package-system/package-system-design.md. MCK is the shared compatibility brand with domain-specific suites and versioned protocol/report integration. Baseline: Morphir 3fa56fccc8449d5f2d6ed34f73db76de1b77ac66 (PR #814), TypeScript 46197e289b437038427f964cca6f1f54c03044a1, Rust 933fcf580b9bfe191f0218964a588027fb86c2d6. Decision 0015 requires deps/<escaped-package-path>/@<version>/<escaped-module-path>; current IR accepts only bare @ and rejects populated or missing slots and duplicate dependency names. ModuleName is package-relative; QualifiedModuleName uses package:module. Core IR remains release-version-free; packaging binds dependencies to exact releases. The reserved layout slot does not implement resolution or multi-version support. Preserve separate model-package, extension, and tool contracts. Hash exact declared payload bytes and normalize manifest metadata separately. The first draft at spec/package covers Library manifest/lock-core structures and candidate compatibility cases. Shared compatibility execution and reference support belong in finos/morphir-typescript, with adapters for implementations; no parallel parent runner. Standalone TS/Python prototype checkers were retired. Generic schema checks do not run package cases or verify digests. Follow package decision 0001 and morphir-uhk3.9 for core integration; this is not full Stage 0 or an install lock. Require two independent implementations and no skipped required MCK cases; pin kit and driver separately. Rust naming-corpus drift is fixed; morphir-klsu retains test-coverage follow-up.
acceptance_criteria: The same logical Morphir package resolves from a pinned Git-file index, local-directory registry, immutable Git source, and workspace source; locks retain exact identities, transitive graph, registry revision, sources, and digests; materialization verifies identity and content; offline tests deny undeclared package egress. Required MCK package-suite cases pass at a pinned kit revision with no failures, kit errors, or skipped required cases. Stage 0 establishes the package suite at spec/package/mck/ and versioned driver/report integration across two independent implementations, preserving the existing IR contract. IR-only runs and two transports of the same implementation do not satisfy the package interoperability criterion.
notes:
Use a dedicated Morphir model-package index that may share a Git repository with the extension index. Support stable and preview update policy, insiders naming where appropriate, and optional segmented preview channels. Keep channels outside package identity and lock exact selections.

title: [UPDATED] Implement DirectRuntime for direct execution mode
description:
Implement DirectRuntime in morphir-ext for direct execution without actors or IPC, supporting CLI, Morphir-Live, and browser/WASM environments.

## PREREQUISITE: Gherkin Acceptance Tests Required

**BEFORE IMPLEMENTATION**: Prepare comprehensive Gherkin acceptance tests and present to user for approval/iteration. Implementation may NOT proceed without user verification of tests.

Gherkin tests must cover:
- DirectRuntime construction with ExtismRuntime
- execute() method with various function names and envelopes
- TEA lifecycle: init(), update(), subscriptions()
- Design-time operations: backend_generate(), frontend_compile()
- Error handling (WASM errors, envelope errors, missing functions)
- No dependency on Kameo or daemon infrastructure
- Works in WASM context (no_std compatible if needed)

## Background
DirectRuntime provides in-process extension execution without daemon/actor overhead. All clients (CLI, Morphir-Live, browser/WASM) can use DirectRuntime for embedded execution.

## Architecture

```
┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                     Client Layer                           │
│  (CLI, Morphir-Live, Browser/WASM, IDE)                   │
└──────────────────────┬─────────────────────────────────────┘
                       │
                       │ Choice: Direct or Daemon
                       │
            ┌──────────┴──────────┐
            │                     │
            ▼                     ▼
  ┌──────────────────┐   ┌─────────────────┐
  │  DirectRuntime   │   │  DaemonClient   │
  │  (morphir-ext)   │   │  (morphir-ext)  │
  └────────┬─────────┘   └────────┬────────┘
           │                      │
           │ No IPC               │ IPC (JSON-RPC)
           │                      │
           ▼                      ▼
  ┌──────────────────┐   ┌─────────────────┐
  │ ExtismRuntime    │   │  Daemon Service │
  │ (morphir-ext)    │   │  with actors    │
  └────────┬─────────┘   └─────────────────┘
           │
           │ Loads WASM
           ▼
  ┌──────────────────┐
  │  Extension       │
  │  (WASM module)   │
  └──────────────────┘

DirectRuntime Flow:
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
Client
  │
  └─> DirectRuntime::new(ExtismRuntime)
        │
        └─> execute("backend_generate", envelope)
              │
              └─> ExtismRuntime::call_envelope()
                    │
                    └─> Extism loads WASM
                          │
                          └─> Calls backend_generate()
                                │
                                └─> Returns envelope
```

- **Depends on**: `morphir-ext/src/runtime.rs` (ExtensionRuntime trait)

title: Morphir x WebAssembly Component Model Interactive Guide
description:
Build an interactive, self-guided tutorial that explains the WebAssembly Component Model ABI (canonical ABI, lifting/lowering) while being extremely aware of Morphir IR.

## Goals
1. Map Morphir IR programs and types to WebAssembly (core Wasm level)
2. Evaluate whether Morphir IR could serve as a practical replacement for WIT
3. Identify gaps preventing this substitution (semantic/ABI/tooling mismatches)
4. Determine how Morphir could be enhanced to support this use case

## Modules (Progressive)
- Core Wasm boundary constraints (i32/i64/f32/f64, linear memory)
- Canonical ABI: lifting and lowering
- Scalars (bool/int/float)
- Strings and byte sequences (ptr/len, encoding)
- Lists, records/structs, tuples
- Variants/enums, option/result
- Functions, multi-arg/multi-return, flattening rules
- Resources/handles (ownership, borrowing patterns)
- Error handling and traps vs typed errors
- Versioning and evolution patterns
- Performance considerations (copies, allocations, alignment)

## Deliverables per Module
- Conceptual explanation with ASCII diagrams
- Code snippets in F#, Scala, Go
- Morphir IR examples (types + functions)
- Core Wasm function signature and memory layout
- WIT replacement check (what Morphir has, what's missing, candidate enhancements)
- Confidence check questions

## Key Questions
- Can Morphir IR act as an IDL/interface definition layer analogous to WIT?
- Can we derive canonical ABI lowering/lifting rules from Morphir IR types?
- What semantics does WIT have that Morphir IR lacks?
- What additions would make Morphir IR more suitable?

title: Create reusable TUI framework for interactive morphir commands
description:
Build a shared TUI framework that provides consistent interactive experiences across morphir commands.

## Overview
Create a reusable TUI component in `cmd/morphir/internal/tui` that can be used by:
- `morphir` (main interactive mode)
- `morphir validate --tui`
- Future commands like `morphir explore`, `morphir inspect`, etc.

## Architecture
```
cmd/morphir/internal/tui/
├── app.go           # Main TUI application shell
├── layout.go        # Flexible layout manager (sidebar + main)
├── components/
│   ├── sidebar.go   # Collapsible sidebar with tree/list
│   ├── viewer.go    # Markdown/content viewer with paging
│   ├── statusbar.go # Bottom status/help bar
│   └── searchbar.go # Search/filter input
├── styles/
│   └── theme.go     # Consistent lipgloss styling
└── keymap/
    └── vim.go       # Vim-style keybindings
```

## Core Components

### AppShell
Main application container that manages:
- Layout (sidebar width, visibility)
- Focus management between panels
- Global keybindings (quit, help, toggle sidebar)
- Resize handling

### SidebarPanel
- Tree view for hierarchical content
- List view for flat content  
- Collapsible (toggle with `b` or `Ctrl+b`)
- Filterable

### ViewerPanel
- Glamour-rendered markdown
- Viewport with vim navigation (j/k, gg/G, Ctrl+d/u)
- Search within content (/)
- Line numbers (optional)

### StatusBar
- Current mode indicator
- Keybinding hints
- File/position info

## Usage Pattern
```go
// In validate command
app := tui.NewApp(
    tui.WithSidebar(fileList),
    tui.WithViewer(markdownContent),
    tui.WithTitle("Validation Report"),
)
return app.Run()

// In main morphir command
app := tui.NewApp(
    tui.WithSidebar(commandList),
    tui.WithViewer(welcomeContent),
    tui.WithTitle("Morphir"),
)
return app.Run()
```

## Keybindings (Vim-style)
| Key | Action |
|-----|--------|
| j/k | Scroll down/up |
| h/l | Switch panels |
| gg/G | Go to top/bottom |
| Ctrl+d/u | Page down/up |
| / | Search |
| n/N | Next/prev search result |
| b | Toggle sidebar |
| q | Quit |
| ? | Show help |

## Libraries
- `github.com/charmbracelet/bubbletea` - TUI framework
- `github.com/charmbracelet/bubbles` - Components
- `github.com/charmbracelet/glamour` - Markdown
- `github.com/charmbracelet/lipgloss` - Styling

## Blocked By
None - this is a foundational component

## Blocks
- morphir-tol (TUI validate command)

Outcome and scope

A fresh Node process loads a saved MoonBit extension, accepts a Boolean library through MEP compileModel, returns a MorphirModel, generates a buildable MoonBit library through generateModel, and exits cleanly after a consumer returns the expected result. Retain source, model, outputs, exact input sidecars and runtime receipts. This delivers issue 152. Installed canonical CLI qualification remains morphir-ukvn.5.55.9; broader numeric, registry and component work stays separate.

Baseline inspected: MoonBit repository 854af44, compiler 0.10.15+943464bfa, Node 24.22.0. Implementation at d57bb8a726f93e87e9d9b50a9932d51313f5f001 reuses the existing pure session, frontend and generator. Fresh native and saved portable processes each passed the independent shared guest suite and executed the shared kit's consumer. The candidate integrates main at ed57b4a, including native IR Union support. The shared runner is merged at 6564259f0992770b8207e6880bf3c4e142e73656. Implementation exact-head CI and tracker closure remain pending.

Execution route

Select the existing process binding around a saved core-Wasm library. Reuse the complete dependency assembly, packaged compiler and atomic Wasm/binary-Ion publication from PR 148. A thin portable entry point composes mep.Session with the existing Boolean frontend. A replaceable Node adapter supplies only byte callbacks. The guest receives and returns existing JSON-RPC bodies; the process bridge preserves Content-Length framing. No new MEP envelope or component claim is introduced.

Required-host reproduction, repeated with Node 24.22.0: WebAssembly.compile(new Uint8Array([0,97,115,109,13,0,1,0])) rejects the component header with expected version 01 00 00 00, found 0d 00 01 00 @+4. The production loader calls this core API; it has no component instantiator. Combined with the missing rich-model WIT contract, this justifies the demonstrated core-Wasm process route.

The shared MEP kit was reference-only at baseline 2b0cb1d64ccd0455aba3eaa2b143dbc7d276df70. The prerequisite morphir-opua.1.2.7.1 adds executable guest qualification to the existing Rust MCK engine and thin CLI. It uses the existing shared process transport; broader host qualification remains morphir-opua.1.2.7. Historical references: baseline kit, WIT frontend.

Sequence and ownership

The process owns one guest instance and one session. It copies an admitted request into host-owned storage, supplies indexed bytes only during a synchronous call, then copies response bytes before releasing the request. Guest pointers never escape. One call runs at a time. The portable ABI uses morphir_bytes_v1.input_len, input_byte, output_byte and exports handle: () -> i32. Positive results equal response length; zero means terminal exit; minus two means a notification with no response; minus one means terminal infrastructure failure. The distinct morphir/mep-bytes-v1/v1-draft profile hashes this complete contract, including the bounds and outcomes. Source profile, execution profile and negotiated model tuples are distinct identities.

Save model.wasm and manifest.ion, including compiler/core/SDK/package identities, actual imports, retained exports, artifact digest and profile digest. Runtime loading checks integrity, profile and imports before instantiation. It needs neither a compiler executable nor a build-process instance.

Limits and failures

BoundaryContract
Wire8 KiB header, 16 MiB request/response. Strict UTF-8; split headers/bodies supported. Invalid/truncated framing terminates the process with stderr diagnostics.
MEP/modelReuse existing complete bilateral tuples and minimum immutable peer limits. Current ceilings: encoded 5,592,408 bytes; decoded 4,194,304 bytes; depth 128; 100,000 nodes. Aggregate budgets include dependencies/evidence.
GuestNo filesystem, network, clock, browser or WASI imports. JSON-RPC errors and operation diagnostics preserve the session. A trap, inconsistent ABI outcome or callback violation disposes it and terminates the bridge. A fresh instance starts before initialize.
Memory and executionThe host validates one defined, unshared wasm32 memory with a finite maximum of 4,096 pages, 256 MiB. A dedicated Node worker enforces a 10-second load/call deadline and a 128 MiB JavaScript old-generation limit. Timeout, trap, exit and disposal await worker termination. Tests exercise actual memory growth refusal, repeated calls and response overflow. No wire cancellation is advertised.
LoggingProtocol stdout contains only frames. Infrastructure errors use stderr. This profile enables no file logging and binds no logging service. Existing host logging path rules remain separate.

Lifecycle remains before-initialize, ready, shutdown, exited. Initialization fixes model limits; retries cannot renegotiate. Unknown notifications produce no response. Shutdown refuses further operations; exit releases the host. Disposal is idempotent. Host timeout/trap failures are terminal and cannot reuse the session.

Model fidelity

Use unchanged MEP 0.2.0-draft.1, model envelope 0.1.0-draft.1 and draft IR 4.0.0. Advertise language moonbit and the qualified Boolean-library profile. Prefer morphir-model/ion-binary; retain annotations, source/target names, provenance and the exact input payload in generated sidecars. Supported morphir-ir/morphir-json calls remain available. Refuse conversion that would lose required metadata. Never fall back silently to JSON.

Ordinary explicit host selection and capability negotiation require no signed registry or authenticated publisher. Claims describe the guest; only actual supplied imports grant host services. Native process permissions and portable guest imports remain separate facts.

It must cover complete source-to-model-to-generated-consumer behavior, exact Ion and JSON tuples, repeated calls, invalid-request recovery, immutable limits, unsupported tuples, malformed/mismatched model payloads, lossy conversion refusal, traps, timeout, import refusal, memory limits, notification silence and clean disposal. Run required lint, MoonBit formatting and validation, focused behavior tests, CI-selection tests when editing policy, and exact-head PR CI. Address every review finding before an authorized merge. design:
Headless CLI semantic review

Independent source review and coordinated fixes · 18 October 2026 · local working-tree evidence

Contents
  1. Findings and resolutions
  2. Source provenance
  3. Semantic boundaries reviewed
  4. Validation
  5. Remaining qualification

Findings and resolutions

Two source-specific defects were reproduced and fixed after the coordinator authorized their narrow production changes. No additional defect was identified in the reviewed evaluation or publication paths.

Resolved P2: native generation omitted cancellation during model capture

generation.mbt started interruption handling after load_local_model, planning and log acquisition. With stdin held open, a SIGINT after 200 milliseconds terminated the native process by signal, with no JSON result. An equivalent eval control returned exit 130 and a JSON cancellation result.

{"operation":"generate","code":null,"signal":"SIGINT","stdout":""}
{"operation":"eval","code":130,"signal":null,"stdout":"{...Cancelled...}"}

The handler and deferred restoration now start immediately after the supported-host check. The focused generation regression holds stdin open and asserts exit 130, parseable cancellation JSON, no publication and no log creation. Node uses the maintained production worker launcher; native exercises the real console signal handler on this macOS host.

Resolved P2: retained plans aliased caller-owned model state

retained_generation.mbt validated the supplied IRUnit, then retained its public mutable arrays and nested semantic maps directly. A caller could change accepted metadata, provenance or model contents between planning and execution. The CLI did not expose such an interleaving, but the public engine service did.

The regression mutates nested Ion struct fields, metadata/provenance/annotation arrays, dependency maps and module maps after planning. It failed before the fix. Planning now freezes the accepted unit through the existing lossless binary Registry.checkpoint/open_checkpoint boundary. The test compares the complete captured checkpoint and confirms binary generation still succeeds. Default resource limits and malformed metadata ownership are rejected before plan acceptance.

Source provenance

Both capability and local-model MCK runners now import one sourceSnapshot helper. It inventories tracked and untracked, nonignored files under apps/morphir, apps/morphir-workbench, pkgs, types, tools, moon.mod and moon.work. Tracked deletions remain entries with a null digest. NUL-delimited Git output preserves unusual filenames; sorted entries produce a deterministic aggregate digest.

The model runner takes a snapshot before helper builds and qualification, compares it again after report rejection controls, and retains the full initial inventory in the provenance record. Existing producer, launcher, corpus, adapter and checker before/after digest checks remain. No second compatibility checker was introduced.

These hashes identify the reviewed files at report creation. Other workers are still editing the shared checkout; the coordinator must rerun final qualification after stabilization.

Semantic boundaries reviewed

  • Evaluation validates explicit codec/provider/policy selection, rejects competing stdin owners, starts cancellation before capture, uses the shared immutable Scheme plan, and publishes typed terminal evidence through the maintained outcome validator. Strict and permissive selection retain separate shared semantics. Timeout starts after capture and covers planning/evaluation; runtime resources remain bounded separately.
  • Retained generation keeps logical model identity independent of the fixed output folder, rejects rich-to-Elm loss through the existing checked projection boundary, and reuses the registered generators. The new snapshot preserves rich context and caller independence under default codec budgets.
  • Engine execution uses the retained unit instead of re-decoding a virtual source. CLI diagnostics map the virtual source back to the actual input. Metadata/provenance remain part of the unit handed to the generator.
  • Host publication performs generation, byte/file budget checks and required compiler validation before acquiring the existing publication transaction. It checks cancellation before commit and reports committed destinations explicitly. A cancellation after a completed commit is not evidence that no files were published.

Validation

CheckEvidence
Source inventory regressionDisposable Git repository covers a tracked deletion, untracked input, ignored build output, newline filename, changed source and restored source. Pass.
Retained engine suite94 JS tests pass, including the pre-fix failing alias regression, complete checkpoint preservation, malformed metadata refusal and default traversal-budget refusal.
Generation input cancellationReal native and production Node worker controls verify structured exit 130 before parsing, logs or publication.
Full focused generationNode/native commands retain six source representations, binary sidecars, source-only and required builds, Elm compilation, consumer result 42 and unchanged-output refusal controls. Final receipts are under .dev/generation-evidence.
Static checksNode TypeScript checking, Bun checked builds, targeted MoonBit formatting and scoped diff checks.

Remaining qualification

The source-bound model MCK suite is deliberately not rerun during concurrent edits. Root owns the stable-source Node/native rerun and the installed-package matrix. Existing prior 32-case observations remain historical evidence until refreshed with the new source inventory.

Windows process.kill('SIGINT') does not deliver a console control event. The regression explicitly records not-run on Windows. CI needs a real console or ConPTY control-event harness for the native handler and Node parent signal path. Cancellation-file controls still run everywhere.

Native Windows currently has no process/temp build adapter. Its test branch qualifies six source-only inputs, sidecars, logs, stdin and unchanged-output refusal of an explicit required process provider. It records the required build and consumer as unavailable. Node Windows retains real Elm, required MoonBit and consumer checks. These branches were type checked here; Windows behavior requires its actual CI host.

WASI and Wasm GC retain their documented effect refusals. No Windows, Linux or installed-release qualification is inferred from this local macOS run. No connected or Workbench compatibility suite was duplicated in this dispatch.

Connected artifact consumption

morphir-etg2.23.5 · 18 October 2026 · artifact slice implemented; original-model dependency remains open

  • Result
  • Maintained boundaries
  • Verification
  • Lifecycle limits
  • Original-model blocker
  • Coordinator integration
  • Preserved source packet

Result

The primary CLI now authenticates an explicitly selected artifact service, captures one generation, verifies every file, confirms its exact release, and publishes the complete byte inventory through the current ContentPublisher. Saved files are reported as CLI publications. No retained host bytes are described as server-published files.

morphir connected connect launch.txt --provider workbench-http --connection connection.json --connection-scope artifacts
morphir connected artifacts request.json --provider workbench-http --connection connection.json --output saved

The second command publishes saved/artifacts. Existing destinations are refused before submission and checked again under the publication lock. Execution setup remains the default connection scope.

Maintained boundaries

The unchanged PR147 transfer attempt, raw RPC channel and private VerifiedArtifactSet now live under pkgs/morphir-host/artifact-client. EXTRACTION.json pins published revision 4ce0f57a84f58fad3106d0de18105eeadf0822f9. The nested vendored upstream files, source hashes and Apache/Unicode notices are unchanged. This worker did not edit the PR147 branch or worktree.

The CLI helper uses that maintained literal decoder, profile selector, path validator, chunk capture, digest owner and transfer lifecycle. Shared node-session owns private credential reads, one-use setup, fresh authentication and the exact loopback transport. The maintained ws client bounds payloads and closes only the attempt socket after a 100 ms grace. There is no replacement protocol parser, evaluator or lifecycle validator.

Requests are bounded to a complete 1 MiB UTF-8 frame. The exact .21 profile permits 256 files, 16 MiB per file and 64 MiB per generation, with 64 KiB chunks and 128 KiB replies. The versioned native helper inventory is bounded separately. MoonBit validates the entire portable path set through the existing shared model-document inventory checker and precharges declared bytes before reading private scratch, then verifies every length and hash before starting publication.

Verification

CheckEvidence
Maintained consumer regressions51 passed after exact extraction; every EXTRACTION.json source hash still matches.
CLI publication and boundary tests23/23 Node and 23/23 native, including full-inventory corruption, release prerequisite, NUL/empty bytes, collision refusal, path-set prevalidation, precharged aggregate budget and exact 256-file cap.
Actual authenticated Rust producer and child Node CLIThe 11-case run passes in isolated fresh hosts, plus a focused interruption-after-release case: download; full 64 MiB indexed binary; full 64 MiB NUL text; digest mutation; length mutation; wrong profile; stale session; output collision; SIGINT; held-generation timeout; producer loss. The extra case interrupts after the first private staged file and confirms released remote retention with no accepted publication.
Actual native CLIThe same 11 cases pass in the consolidated final run, plus the focused interruption-after-release case. Native SIGINT exits within the asserted five-second deadline with owned scratch removed.
Exact saved bytesFull fixed hashes for all four 16 MiB binary files, every indexed byte of the 1,048,833-byte file, full NUL-file zero checks, exact BOM/CRLF text and exact empty files. Expectations were authored independently of actual CLI output.
Existing execution compatibilityActual authenticated normal Node and native execution scenarios pass after common-auth extraction.
Portable effectsCurrent Wasm and Wasm GC builds pass actual help and typed unavailable-effect refusals.
Static checksStrict Node TypeScript check passes. Windows typed no-network credential refusal cases are authored and remain actual-CI evidence, not local OS qualification.

The real installed SDK fixture was built from Rust source 2b0cb1d64ccd0455aba3eaa2b143dbc7d276df70 in an isolated target directory. Its SHA-256 is fcafe8a81de33dd8c342a5bca2f18adf48b5538742f1f52f67ff83e6d5b8a48b. The current source advances only MCK, schema and mise files; UI/provider/fixture/SDK runtime blobs are unchanged. Full receipts are in .dev/connected-transfers-source-receipt.json and .dev/headless-artifact-expectations.json.

Lifecycle limits

Lost replies never cause implicit generation retry, owner reselection or legacy profile fallback. An in-flight cancellation reports connection-closed/pending-exchange when no exact release was confirmed. The actual Rust RPC loop awaits dispatch before reading socket closure; a held producer can therefore remain host-owned after the CLI has closed and exited. The CLI neither claims confirmed remote cancellation nor kills the separately selected host. Fresh-host fixtures prevent this intentional held state from contaminating another case.

Local cancellation removes only known private helper files and closes the owned transport. It does not depend on an interruptible directory reader after SIGINT. Successful release evidence survives a later local integrity/publication refusal. Remote retention, local scratch and local publication remain distinct in reports.

The tests check complete file inventories and hashes, no partial publication, secret absence in stdout/stderr, private credential setup, owned scratch removal, one producer invocation, prompt local cancellation, and continued host liveness. Windows console SIGINT and Windows private-file protection are not claimed as supported.

Original-model blocker

The supplied current .22.1 snapshot remains in progress and explicitly has no advertised, qualified model-original service. Its remaining work includes exact schemas, encoded frame limits, deterministic inventory paging, chunk reads, release RPC, frozen-source headers, supported-format bounds and actual client/server qualification. The proposed morphir/workbench/model-originals 0.1.0-draft.1 is not consumed as though it were delivered.

Full Task5 therefore stays incomplete. Future integration must preserve exact JSON, YAML file/tree, Ion text/binary originals, complete declared companions and empty directories. Semantic projection, artifact profiles and MEP capabilities cannot substitute for those originals. Existing .22.1 owner work, schemas and authored cases remain with that owner; this worker introduced no competing service or speculative model-original wire validator.

Coordinator integration

The coordinator owns root schema, main, module imports, dependency/lock changes, ContentPublisher, aggregate tests, CI, staging, commits, packing and landing. This worker supplies transfers.mbt, the installed transfer helper, common auth/transport, shared maintained consumer, focused tests and the connected transfer guide.

PR147 is an explicit landing dependency. The local .dev/artifact-client-workbench-facades.patch reexports both the three outer modules and nested vendor modules so branded types and runtime ownership share one actual module. On integration, repoint the maintained source checker at the shared unchanged vendor location; do not hash compatibility facades as upstream source. Workbench facade joining and final current-source CI/packed-install qualification remain coordinator-owned.

The final source deltas reported to the coordinator tighten scratch reads to the precharged declaration, narrow the TypeScript observation union, add the exact native-boundary file-count test, and preserve the signal reason for interruption during synchronous private staging. No Rust/provider WIP, tracker, staging or git history was changed by this worker.

Preserved source packet

These receipts record the worker checkpoint. PR147 subsequently landed and the coordinator integrated the shared Workbench facades in97fff77, verified the canonical vendor hashes, passed102 independent client scenarios onBun/Node/Chromium and the actual browser download workflow. Final host CI and exact original-model service remain open.

title: Headless Morphir execution and Workbench parity
description:
# Headless Morphir execution and Workbench parity

Maintainer-requested campaign supplement, 18 October 2026. Full normative HTML: .dev/design/workbench-headless-cli.html. Targets the primary MoonBit CLI and shared services. Existing primary-CLI, Workbench and server owners remain in place. Command names are proposed until compatibility review. No implementation or worker assignment is claimed by importing this plan.
design:
Headless Morphir execution and Workbench parity

Campaign supplement · 19 October 2026 · Revision 4 · Execution checkpoint · YAML IR input explicitly required · Canonical owner: morphir-etg2.23

  • Outcome and scope
  • Existing code and roadmap
  • Required model input formats
  • Shared services and effect boundaries
  • Execution and CLI semantics
  • Parallel ownership and dependencies
  • Task 1: function evaluation
  • Task 2: worksheets
  • Task 3: local model originals
  • Task 4: connected executions
  • Task 5: connected model and artifact transfer
  • Task 6: independent verification
  • Task 7: installed CLI acceptance
  • Task 8: YAML IR input
  • Completion gates
  • Handoff and scope accounting

Outcome and scope

A user can evaluate Morphir functions and run supported Scheme worksheet expressions from a terminal or CI process, with the same capability checking policies, typed values, diagnostics and execution outcomes as the Workbench. No browser, CEF, DOM, Save dialog or running Workbench is needed. A local request does not require a daemon. A caller may explicitly select a compatible connected provider.

Here, an execution is the existing accepted, identified operation with captured inputs, lifecycle, outcomes and cleanup. A function invocation belongs to an execution. Compilation, generation, artifact publication and model release are separate operations; running generated libraries is already supported and remains distinct from evaluating a model or a Scheme worksheet.

This maintainer-requested addition extends the campaign rather than asserting that these commands already exist. It includes headless model inspection/original export and generated-artifact consumption as companion workflows. Reuse the existing generation task instead of creating a second generation command. The target is the primary MoonBit CLI; reusable Rust services remain available through their qualified adapters.

Model input formats required for this work are JSON, YAML, Ion text and Ion binary. YAML is a representation of Morphir IR, independent of the model's source language and generation target. Required local browser and CLI YAML workflows must work without a daemon.

Command spelling and new option names are proposed until the compatibility inventory and CLI owner reconcile them. Extend existing command families where their meaning matches. Never silently reinterpret an existing evaluation request, generated-library execute command or output envelope.

Shared services and effect boundaries

Keep the functional core independent of a frontend. Decode raw arguments, files and frames into existing validated domain values at adapters. Pure validation, checking-policy decisions and state transitions are shared. Host services execute those decisions using explicitly supplied capabilities. CLI and Workbench both call those services; neither imports the other's entry point.

Execution and CLI semantics

ConcernRequired behavior
InputsExplicit source/model/request files or bounded stdin. Reuse canonical versioned invocation/evaluation envelopes. Required model codecs are JSON, YAML, Ion text and Ion binary, without converting exact values through JavaScript Number or Unicode replacement. Checking policyExpose the existing whole-model-before-running and as-code-executes policies using the same typed policy. The latter allows an unsupported feature in code that is never reached, but still enforces identity, integrity, resource and input/output boundary checks. It is not tree shaking.
Provider selectionExplicit local or connected provider and exact advertised contract/profile. Unsupported language, target, policy or provider refuses clearly. No silent runtime, protocol or evaluation fallback. Do not download or start an unselected service.
OutputHuman text, one JSON result or typed JSON-lines records through the current formatter. Keep stdout parseable and send progress/logs to the appropriate existing channel. Preserve exact values, typed model errors, infrastructure failures and optional observations as separate facts.
Exit statusPreserve 0 success, 2 invalid invocation/configuration, 1 execution/publication failure and 130 cancellation where the existing command contract applies. Do not invent mappings separately in each adapter.
Local lifetimeCapture input/context before effects, retain explicit resources for the execution and release at command end. SIGINT, timeout and errors close only owned workers/connections; distinguish confirmed termination from cancellation requested.

Secure terminal connection setup must not depend on browser cookies, place secrets in command arguments/logs, or broaden host grants. Stop observing, cancel execution, release transfer and close model are separate actions. Cross-process durable recovery remains excluded unless separately designed.
PublicationExplicit destination and overwrite policy through the current writer's confinement, collision and atomicity rules. First verify the complete transfer. Refusal leaves no partial accepted result and reports uncertain publication separately. Never label generated/retained/downloaded bytes as server-published files.

title: Preserve literal JSON keys with shared bounded decoding
description:
Accepted implementation decision for morphir-etg2.22.1, 18 October 2026. This records the coordinator's routine implementation choices within the approved campaign, not new maintainer approval or qualification.

For the additive model-originals profile, JSON objects whose keys resemble serde_json private Number/RawValue markers retain their literal keys and string values. Ordinary duplicate members keep last-wins behavior, unknown members survive, and current numeric precision/map ordering remain. Historical connected v1 and strict RPC/declaration rules are unchanged. Recursive parsing of embedded marker strings is not introduced.

Share the existing extension-SDK single-pass delimiter traversal through a small serde-only morphir-json helper crate. Keep scalar/string syntax owned by serde, preserve the existing typed RawValue and 126-container SDK boundary, and verify feature-unification and Wasm compatibility. Avoid introducing an SDK dependency on core/common or a second JSON lexer.

Use validated source limits of 64 MiB bytes, root depth 0 through 128, 100000 source values across selected primary files, and a separate inclusive 64 Mi decoded key/string UTF-16-unit ledger. Keys do not count as JSON values. Use a separate assembled-model 100000-value/depth128/string-unit ledger; a borrowed postcondition over an already assembled Value is not evidence of enforcement before tree/typed-model growth. Parser scratch/work and retained decoded data are distinct; no RSS/heap equality is claimed.

The approved first local SDK slice is helper/budget/literal JSON and bounded JSON projection proof only. YAML, Ion, typed v3 and tree assembly, published declaration/writer integration, parent authority/wire, client and independent MCK remain required. No Ion fork, vendoring, dependency patch or publication is authorized by this decision. No public capability is advertised by this partial implementation.

The original 60+35+49 cases remain byte-identical. Sixteen additional JSON-policy cases were frozen before adapter execution, SHA256 72f54322bca8d115df04bd1de27aefe128264949ccbe2ccfaad48874a52e68ab. Full source-backed codec proposal and parent provider/wire plan are preserved in morphir-etg2.22.1 design. Implementation and qualification tasks remain open.

title: Package production codec adapters with explicit execution profiles
description: Reuse the qualified Workbench draft26 codec/comparison implementation and the landed assembly/publisher/loader pipeline. design:
Morphir hosting campaign · specification 0.4 · landed and qualified

Production codec adapters as portable artifacts

Package the shipped Workbench codec adapter with its complete libraries, publish Wasm and an Ion manifest, and run the saved artifact through the existing shared MCK runner. Then reuse the same artifact in Chromium and prove a second host-interface pairing.

  • Intended outcome
  • Call flow
  • Execution profiles
  • Complete assembly
  • Ownership and failures
  • MEP and MCK fit
  • Delivery plan
  • Acceptance evidence

Intended outcome

PR #143 supplies actual invocation transcoding and value comparison through apps/morphir-workbench/mck. PRs #141, #142 and #144 supply deterministic assembly, packaged compilation, default binary Ion publication and independent loading. This phase connects those reusable components. It does not implement a second evaluator or conformance runner.

The first deliverable uses exact offline Workbench 0.1.0-draft.26. Existing JSON NDJSON envelopes remain the external MCK transport. Ion remains the preferred artifact/intermediate representation, including binary payloads tested by the actual production codecs. Explicit Morphir JSON remains supported.

Delivery evidence

Delivered behaviorMeasured evidence
Full production graph121 packages built by the packaged compiler with empty PATH and no MOON_HOME. Compiler0.10.15+943464bfa; known corrected core checked by the workspace pin.
Saved baseline artifact1,235,456 Wasm bytes plus binary Ion manifest.
Saved diagnostics artifact1,235,536 Wasm bytes plus binary Ion manifest.
Independent MCK96 cases × 6 lanes = 576 observations. Existing Node/native and both saved profiles on Node24.22.0 and Chromium156.0.8078.4 match; all reports recheck.
Browser ownershipEach Chromium receipt records 98 requests, preflight and successful shutdown. The browser executes the saved artifact, with no alternate codec in its process bridge.

Implementation branch feat/packaged-codec-adapter starts at main 53d6e2b. PR #148 was squash merged as 8429d90fb25c8862ed081dc89fd0969d262de62c, range 53d6e2b..8429d90. Full PR CI completed successfully on exact head 402a54e, with no pending or failed checks. All 55 contexts succeeded or were intentionally skipped. Automatic review of implementation 926c840 had no findings; the later commit only formats automation. Main's complete tree matches the qualified PR tree, and fresh saved-artifact preflight passes on main for both profiles. The final qualification used an owned runner/corpus snapshot and verified its digests remained unchanged. This proves the selected offline draft26 corpus and two concrete hosts, not every linked dispatcher contract or every runtime.

The exact corpus SHA256 is 22920142b376bd8af223cf0dd2190b21f26f01e104d8c1a4a9cf8a52bdba9ba7; runner SHA256 is 15245caeaab05984dfe8de3b9e3e832dd00744594520e70d945165949dbe2ae4. Both are checked unchanged after qualification. Artifact/manifest/contract hashes, host versions and report paths are recorded in .dev/codec-adapter-mck-402a54e/qualification.ion.

Packaging runs mise run package:codec-adapter. Qualification runs mise run test:codec-adapter-mck with explicit MORPHIR_MCK_BIN and MORPHIR_WORKBENCH_KIT. The JavaScript compiler needs a 4MiB stack for this closure. Artifact consumption uses ordinary Node/Chromium settings. The reusable bridge and executable launcher are separate modules; importing the bridge never starts a stdin consumer.

The Node diagnostics profile appends response-size events beneath .morphir/logs/codec-adapter.jsonl by default. Its optional explicit path is honored outside that directory. Embedded hosts supply their own diagnostic callback. Infrastructure errors go to stderr; stdout retains only protocol observations.

Implementation paths
  • apps/morphir-workbench/mck/packaged and packaged-diagnostics: thin guest entrypoints calling the existing production handler.
  • pkgs/morphir-host/embedding/byte-adapter.mts: profile contract, bounded copied exchange, lifecycle and required services.
  • pkgs/morphir-host/embedding/node-recipe.mts: explicit source/core acquisition from validated dry-run recipes.
  • node-byte-adapter.mts and node-byte-adapter-cli.mts: reusable backpressured NDJSON bridge and separate executable.
  • scripts/package-codec-adapter.mbtx and scripts/codec-adapter-mck.mbtx: portable automation with independent report checking.

Call flow

Mermaid source
sequenceDiagram
  participant R as Shared MCK runner
  participant B as Process bridge
  participant L as Artifact loader
  participant G as Production codec guest
  B->>L: Saved Wasm + Ion and selected profile
  L-->>B: Verified compatible instance
  R->>B: Correlated NDJSON request
  B->>G: Bounded UTF-8 bytes and handle()
  G-->>B: Production observation bytes
  opt Diagnostics execution profile
    G-->>B: Response-byte count service event
  end
  B-->>R: Original observation with correlation
  R->>B: exit
  B->>G: handle exit then dispose
  Note over R,B: EOF without exit response; runner owns verdict/report

Execution profiles

A profile identifies a host contract and ABI. It is separate from source language, concrete library pins and the artifact digest. The language remains MoonBit. The local manifest schema and profile contracts remain drafts, independent of draft IR 4.0.0.

ProfileRequired interfacePurpose
Bounded byte exchange v1input_len() → i32, input_byte(i32) → i32, output_byte(i32), exported handle() → i32Run the unchanged production observation handler. Request and response bytes stay host-owned across calls.
Byte exchange with diagnostics v1Baseline plus response_bytes(i32)Emit one bounded response-size event after a successful observation. Same MCK response semantics. An explicit sink must be supplied.

The hash covers an exact versioned contract text including module names, signatures, byte budgets and return statuses. Select one closed profile, rather than composing arbitrary booleans. A baseline host refuses the diagnostics profile before instantiation. Missing imports and unknown hashes also refuse. Library code stays bundled; shared providers remain separate work.

Complete assembly

Use Moon's dry-run build recipe only as an explicit acquisition boundary to identify source files, dependency aliases, package targets and pinned core interfaces/cores. Never execute recipe text. Validate supported syntax and targets, then supply every package in the selected closure to the existing pure planner and embedded compiler. Unsupported source directives or native stubs fail visibly rather than silently changing compilation.

Record the full dependency graph and source/prebuilt identities, compiler/core versions, selected exports and actual imports in the existing manifest. Build both profiles from the same production adapter with different thin entry facades. Publish atomically as model.wasm and manifest.ion. Runtime loading needs saved bytes and an explicit compatible host, without installed compiler commands or build-process state.

Ownership and failures

The bridge owns stdin/stdout framing and the guest instance. The byte host owns one copied request and bounded response buffer per invocation; it clears both on success, exit and failure. The guest owns temporary codec values. No raw guest pointers or borrowed MoonBit strings cross the ABI.

Use a complete-frame limit of 3,146,752 bytes for the selected draft26 requests, a bounded observation response and a bounded diagnostic count. Match the production codec and shared runner's actual limits during implementation; do not lower accepted corpus cases for convenience. A partial final NDJSON line, malformed UTF-8, overflow or guest trap is an infrastructure failure. A normal invalid observation remains a response and permits the next request. Exit returns a dedicated status and no response.

Stdout contains only protocol responses. Diagnostics go to an explicit callback or stderr. Dispose is idempotent; calls after disposal refuse. Foreground synchronous Wasm is not interruptible by an AbortSignal. The external process runner owns deadlines and process termination; a browser worker is needed for hard interruption. No new sandbox or authentication claim is introduced.

MEP and MCK fit

The bridge implements the existing executable MCK adapter boundary. It preserves envelopes, IDs, exact selected contract, kit selection and errors. The shared runner still performs independent expected-value comparison and report rechecking. Packaging changes where the adapter runs, without changing the shared MCK protocol.

MEP compileModel/generateModel and MorphirModel retention remain authoritative and unchanged. This phase does not advertise a new MEP operation, WIT world or direct shared-runner Wasm loader. The artifact profile is local and explicit. A later direct component binding or shared-runner Wasm integration may require MEP/WIT or runner edits and must be designed against the accepted contract.

Qualification compares existing Node/native adapters and packaged adapters under the exact same independently authored draft26 kit. The Chromium host executes saved artifacts against the same request stream; the shared runner owns its verdict via a process bridge to that browser host. No adapter-authored goldens or replacement verdict calculator.

Delivery plan

  1. Store and review this specification, including sequence diagram and task dependencies.
  2. Package the production adapter through the complete assembly graph for both profiles.
  3. Add the bounded byte host and process bridge, then verify framing, lifecycle and compatibility failures.
  4. Qualify fresh Node and Chromium artifacts with the shared runner, recheck reports, compare existing adapter observations, and land the focused PR.

Task 2 and Task 3 depend on the contract in Task 1. Qualification waits for both. Native component facade fixes, registry solving, source numeric work and canonical CLI integration remain independent lanes.

Connected model-original transfer proposal

morphir-etg2.22.1 · 18 October 2026 · parent 149c55c9 / SDK ef481078 · proposed exact contract, not published or qualified

  • Companion ownership declaration

Scope and compatibility

Propose capability/profile morphir/workbench/model-originals with exact version 0.1.0-draft.1. Advertise it through the existing provider capability pair {name,version}. An authenticated, initialized connected protocolVersion 1 session may use four new methods only when its actual workspace provider implements and advertises this exact profile. Neither an offer nor an identity string grants new filesystem authority.

Existing morphir.project-model.open, connected v1 envelopes, artifact-transfer profile and frozen MCK draft 28 remain unchanged. V1 content stays a semantic projection with unavailable original provenance. No new remote semantic-model service, retained model RPC or Rust Scheme evaluator is introduced. New capture handles retain bounded byte snapshots only.

Source originals support 64MiB per file and64MiB aggregate. This is the connected source budget. Browser/native ordinary imports retain their separate 16MiB limit. A connected client needs an explicit 64MiB source owner and decode route; it must not pass these bytes through the 16MiB local-import owner and silently narrow connected support.

The primary artifact is the descriptor's exact file or complete directory tree, plus positively declared model companions for complete scope. Whole compile.dest, raw compile.json, mutable lock files and unrelated scratch outputs are excluded. The preceding 60+35 authored scenarios remain byte-identical. This proposal adds a separate review packet.

First actual Ion streaming checkpoint, accepted within its narrow scope

Root and independent semantic review accepted the first one-byte, no-newline tracer on 19 October 2026. Thirty-nine read-limit tests and two unchanged mutation tests pass, including eight new tests. Actual callbacks are [1,1], requested payload/residency W+1 and work W+5; the last retained owner releases resident credit. Drain, retry, held-primary reentry, unwind and constructor guards have scoped evidence.

General buffering, direct append, capacity growth, COW, shifts and incremental newline indexing are explicitly unfinished, including retained todo branches. All 37 frozen recipes, broader upstream/default-feature regressions, native64/Wasm32 probes, full replay and final review are still required before Task 2B completion. Root authorized the next isolated checkpoint within that same reviewed scope. No SDK selection, production policy, fork, vendor, publication or model-profile support is delivered by this checkpoint.

+//! Task2B source policy. Generic explicit quotas, not production defaults.
+use super::*;
+
+macro_rules! limits {
+    ($name:ident, $builder:ident, $($field:ident),+) => {
+        #[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug)]
+        pub struct $name { $(pub(super) $field: usize),+ }
+        #[derive(Default)]
+        pub struct $builder { $($field: Option<usize>),+ }
+        impl $name { pub fn builder() -> $builder { $builder::default() } }
+        impl $builder {
+            $(pub fn $field(mut self, value: usize) -> Self { self.$field=Some(value);self })+
+            pub fn build(self) -> IonResult<$name> {
+                $(let $field=self.$field.ok_or_else(||IonError::illegal_operation("every source limit must be explicit"))?;
+                  if $field>isize::MAX as usize { return Err(IonError::illegal_operation("source limit exceeds supported range")); })+
+                let value=$name { $($field),+ };
+                value.validate()?;
+                Ok(value)
+            }
+        }
+    }
+}
+limits!(
+    SourceLimits,
+    SourceLimitsBuilder,
+    source_bytes,
+    source_instances,
+    cumulative_requested_payload_bytes,
+    resident_requested_payload_bytes,
+    logical_location_entries
+);
+limits!(
+    StreamReadLimits,
+    StreamReadLimitsBuilder,
+    initial_capacity,
+    max_window_capacity,
+    max_read_span,
+    read_attempts,
+    requested_io_bytes,
+    allocation_events,
+    byte_operations
+);
+impl SourceLimits {
+    fn validate(&self) -> IonResult<()> {
+        Ok(())
+    }
+}
+impl StreamReadLimits {
+    fn validate(&self) -> IonResult<()> {
+        if self.initial_capacity == 0
+            || self.max_read_span == 0
+            || self.initial_capacity > self.max_window_capacity
+        {
+            return Err(IonError::illegal_operation(
+                "stream capacity and span must be positive, initial not above maximum",
+            ));
+        }
+        Ok(())
+    }
+}

+/// Explicit preparation work quota, retaining accepted3N+E units.
+#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug)]
+pub struct PreparationWorkLimits(pub(super) usize);
+impl PreparationWorkLimits {
+    pub fn try_new(work_units: usize) -> IonResult<Self> {
+        if work_units > isize::MAX as usize {
+            return Err(IonError::illegal_operation(

+        }
+        Ok(Self(work_units))

+            SourceModes::Streaming(s) | SourceModes::PreparedAndStreaming { streaming: s, .. } => {
+                Some(s)
+            }

+        }

+    pub(super) fn prepared(self) -> Option<PreparationWorkLimits> {

+                Some(p)
+            }

+#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq)]

+    #[default]
+    Idle,
+    Active,
+}
+
+#[derive(Debug)]
+pub(crate) struct LeasedByteBlock {
+    pub(crate) payload: Vec<u8>,
+    pub(crate) _lease: ResidentLease,
+}
+impl std::ops::Deref for LeasedByteBlock {

+    fn deref(&self) -> &[u8] {

+//! Isolated Task2B source candidate. General COW/growth/index paths are not implemented yet.

+/// Closed callback/source failures, separate from quota exhaustion.
+#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
+pub enum SourceInputFailureKind {
+    InvalidReadCount { offered: usize, reported: usize },
+    ReadUnwound,
+    ReentrantRead,
+    PayloadAllocationFailed,
+}
+/// Bounded typed source failure evidence.
+#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, thiserror::Error)]
+#[error("checked source failure {kind:?} at {position:?}")]
+pub struct SourceInputFailure {
+    kind: SourceInputFailureKind,
+    position: Position,
+}
+impl SourceInputFailure {
+    pub fn kind(&self) -> SourceInputFailureKind {
+        self.kind
+    }
+    pub fn position(&self) -> &Position {
+        &self.position
+    }
+    fn new(kind: SourceInputFailureKind, offset: usize) -> Self {
+        Self {
+            kind,
+            position: Position::with_offset(offset),
+        }
+    }
+}
+#[derive(Default)]
+enum SourceHealth {
+    #[default]
+    Healthy,
+    Failed(SourceInputFailure),
+}
+#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
+enum PassState {
+    Open,
+    EndObserved,
+}
+/// Factory-only input. The reader borrows the caller's source and owns no file authority.
+pub struct BudgetedIonStream<'r, R: Read + ?Sized> {
+    input: &'r mut R,
+    budget: ReaderBudget,
+    limits: StreamReadLimits,
+    block: Option<Rc<LeasedByteBlock>>,
+    locations: SourceLocationState,
+    local_offset: usize,
+    local_end: usize,
+    stream_offset: usize,
+    health: Rc<RefCell<SourceHealth>>,
+    pass: PassState,
+}
+#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
+enum ReadAuthority {
+    Structural,
+    Boundary,
+}
+enum GrantState {
+    Held { primary: usize },
+    Settled,
+}
+/// No budget borrow crosses Read or caller-controlled drop/unwind.
+struct ReadGrant {
+    budget: ReaderBudget,
+    health: Rc<RefCell<SourceHealth>>,
+    offset: usize,
+    state: GrantState,
+}
+impl ReadGrant {
+    fn settle(&mut self, spent: usize) {
+        let GrantState::Held { primary } = self.state else {
+            return;
+        };
+        let mut s = self.budget.state.borrow_mut();
+        s.usage.stream.held_source_bytes -= primary;
+        s.usage.preparation.source_bytes += spent;
+        s.usage.stream.read_phase = SourceReadPhase::Idle;
+        self.state = GrantState::Settled;
+    }
+    fn uncertain(&mut self) {
+        let spent = match self.state {
+            GrantState::Held { primary } => primary,
+            GrantState::Settled => 0,
+        };
+        self.settle(spent);
+    }
+}
+impl Drop for ReadGrant {
+    fn drop(&mut self) {
+        if let GrantState::Held { .. } = self.state {
+            self.uncertain();
+            *self.health.borrow_mut() = SourceHealth::Failed(SourceInputFailure::new(
+                SourceInputFailureKind::ReadUnwound,
+                self.offset,
+            ));
+        }
+    }
+}
+fn add(a: usize, b: usize) -> usize {
+    a.checked_add(b).unwrap_or(usize::MAX)
+}
+impl ReaderBudget {
+    /// Build a checked source using the identical shared budget selected by its policy.
+    pub fn stream_reader<'r, D: Decoder, R: Read + ?Sized>(
+        &self,
+        mut config: ReadConfig<D>,
+        source: &'r mut R,
+    ) -> IonResult<Reader<D, BudgetedIonStream<'r, R>>> {
+        self.check()?;
+        if let Some(selected) = &config.budget {
+            if !Rc::ptr_eq(&selected.state, &self.state) {
+                return Err(IonError::illegal_operation(
+                    "checked stream must use its owning budget",
+                ));
+            }
+        }
+        let policy = self.source_policy()?;
+        let limits = policy
+            .streaming()
+            .ok_or_else(|| IonError::illegal_operation("stream source mode not selected"))?;
+        let w = std::mem::size_of::<usize>();
+        let mut s = self.state.borrow_mut();
+        let instances = add(s.usage.preparation.source_instances, 1);
+        s.ensure(
+            ReaderLimitKind::SourceInstances,
+            policy.common.source_instances,
+            instances,
+            0,
+        )?;
+        let rows = add(s.usage.preparation.location_entries, 1);
+        s.ensure(
+            ReaderLimitKind::SourceLocationEntries,
+            policy.common.logical_location_entries,
+            rows,
+            0,
+        )?;
+        let storage = add(s.usage.preparation.storage_bytes, w);
+        s.ensure(
+            ReaderLimitKind::SourceStorageBytes,
+            policy.common.cumulative_requested_payload_bytes,
+            storage,
+            0,
+        )?;
+        let resident = add(s.usage.stream.resident_bytes, w);
+        s.ensure(
+            ReaderLimitKind::SourceResidentBytes,
+            policy.common.resident_requested_payload_bytes,
+            resident,
+            0,
+        )?;
+        let events = add(s.usage.stream.allocation_events, 1);
+        s.ensure(
+            ReaderLimitKind::SourceAllocationEvents,
+            limits.allocation_events,
+            events,
+            0,
+        )?;
+        let work = add(s.usage.stream.byte_operations, w);
+        s.ensure(
+            ReaderLimitKind::SourceByteOperations,
+            limits.byte_operations,
+            work,
+            0,
+        )?;
+        s.usage.preparation.source_instances = instances;
+        s.usage.preparation.location_entries = rows;
+        s.usage.preparation.storage_bytes = storage;
+        s.usage.stream.resident_bytes = resident;
+        s.usage.stream.allocation_events = events;
+        s.usage.stream.byte_operations = work;
+        drop(s);
+        let lease = ResidentLease::reserved(self, w);
+        let mut rows = Vec::new();
+        rows.try_reserve_exact(1).map_err(|_| {
+            SourceInputFailure::new(SourceInputFailureKind::PayloadAllocationFailed, 0)
+        })?;
+        rows.push(0);
+        let input = BudgetedIonStream {
+            input: source,
+            budget: self.clone(),
+            limits,
+            block: None,
+            locations: SourceLocationState::from_leased_stream_rows(rows, lease),
+            local_offset: 0,
+            local_end: 0,
+            stream_offset: 0,
+            health: Rc::new(RefCell::new(SourceHealth::Healthy)),
+            pass: PassState::Open,
+        };
+        config.budget = Some(self.clone());
+        Reader::new(config, input)
+    }

+impl<R: Read + ?Sized> BudgetedIonStream<'_, R> {
+    fn check(&self) -> IonResult<()> {
+        self.budget.check()?;
+        match &*self.health.borrow() {
+            SourceHealth::Healthy => Ok(()),
+            SourceHealth::Failed(e) => Err(e.clone().into()),
+        }
+    }
+    fn position_end(&self) -> usize {
+        self.stream_offset + self.local_end
+    }
+    fn grant(&self) -> IonResult<(ReadAuthority, ReadGrant)> {
+        self.check()?;

+        if s.usage.stream.read_phase == SourceReadPhase::Active {
+            return Err(SourceInputFailure::new(
+                SourceInputFailureKind::ReentrantRead,
+                self.position_end(),
+            )

+        }

+            s.usage.preparation.source_bytes,
+            s.usage.stream.held_source_bytes,
+        );
+        let (authority, primary) = if charged < policy.common.source_bytes {
+            (ReadAuthority::Structural, 1)
+        } else {
+            (ReadAuthority::Boundary, 0)
+        };
+        let requested = add(charged, primary);
+        s.ensure(
+            ReaderLimitKind::SourceBytes,
+            policy.common.source_bytes,
+            requested,
+            self.position_end(),
+        )?;
+        let attempts = add(s.usage.stream.read_attempts, 1);
+        s.ensure(
+            ReaderLimitKind::ReadAttempts,
+            self.limits.read_attempts,
+            attempts,
+            self.position_end(),
+        )?;
+        let io = add(s.usage.stream.requested_io_bytes, 1);
+        s.ensure(
+            ReaderLimitKind::RequestedIoBytes,
+            self.limits.requested_io_bytes,
+            io,
+            self.position_end(),
+        )?;
+        let work = add(s.usage.stream.byte_operations, 1);
+        s.ensure(
+            ReaderLimitKind::SourceByteOperations,
+            self.limits.byte_operations,
+            work,
+            self.position_end(),
+        )?;
+        s.usage.stream.held_source_bytes += primary;
+        s.usage.stream.read_attempts = attempts;
+        s.usage.stream.requested_io_bytes = io;
+        s.usage.stream.byte_operations = work;
+        s.usage.stream.read_phase = SourceReadPhase::Active;
+        drop(s);
+        Ok((
+            authority,
+            ReadGrant {
+                budget: self.budget.clone(),
+                health: self.health.clone(),
+                offset: self.position_end(),
+                state: GrantState::Held { primary },
+            },
+        ))
+    }
+    fn fail(&self, kind: SourceInputFailureKind) -> IonError {
+        let e = SourceInputFailure::new(kind, self.position_end());
+        *self.health.borrow_mut() = SourceHealth::Failed(e.clone());
+        e.into()
+    }

+        }

+        let scan = add(s.usage.stream.byte_operations, 1);
+        s.ensure(
+            ReaderLimitKind::SourceByteOperations,
+            self.limits.byte_operations,
+            scan,
+            self.position_end(),
+        )?;
+        s.usage.stream.byte_operations = scan;
+        drop(s);
+        if byte == b'\n' {
+            todo!("Task2B incremental checked index checkpoint");
+        }
+        let mut s = self.budget.state.borrow_mut();

+        let preferred = self.limits.initial_capacity;
+        let fits = |c: usize| {
+            add(s.usage.preparation.storage_bytes, c)
+                <= policy.common.cumulative_requested_payload_bytes
+                && add(s.usage.stream.resident_bytes, c)
+                    <= policy.common.resident_requested_payload_bytes
+                && add(s.usage.stream.byte_operations, add(c, 1)) <= self.limits.byte_operations
+        };
+        let capacity = if fits(preferred) { preferred } else { 1 };
+        let storage = add(s.usage.preparation.storage_bytes, capacity);
+        s.ensure(
+            ReaderLimitKind::SourceStorageBytes,
+            policy.common.cumulative_requested_payload_bytes,
+            storage,
+            self.position_end(),
+        )?;
+        let resident = add(s.usage.stream.resident_bytes, capacity);
+        s.ensure(
+            ReaderLimitKind::SourceResidentBytes,
+            policy.common.resident_requested_payload_bytes,
+            resident,
+            self.position_end(),
+        )?;
+        let events = add(s.usage.stream.allocation_events, 1);
+        s.ensure(
+            ReaderLimitKind::SourceAllocationEvents,
+            self.limits.allocation_events,
+            events,
+            self.position_end(),
+        )?;
+        let work = add(s.usage.stream.byte_operations, add(capacity, 1));
+        s.ensure(
+            ReaderLimitKind::SourceByteOperations,
+            self.limits.byte_operations,
+            work,
+            self.position_end(),
+        )?;
+        s.usage.preparation.storage_bytes = storage;
+        s.usage.stream.resident_bytes = resident;
+        s.usage.stream.allocation_events = events;
+        s.usage.stream.byte_operations = work;
+        drop(s);
+        let lease = ResidentLease::reserved(&self.budget, capacity);
+        let mut payload = Vec::new();

+            return Err(self.fail(SourceInputFailureKind::PayloadAllocationFailed));
+        }
+        payload.resize(capacity, 0);
+        payload[0] = byte;
+        self.block = Some(Rc::new(LeasedByteBlock {
+            payload,
+            _lease: lease,
+        }));
+        self.local_end = 1;
+        Ok(1)
+    }
+}
+impl<'r, R: Read + ?Sized> IonInput for BudgetedIonStream<'r, R> {
+    type DataSource = Self;
+    fn into_data_source(self) -> Self {
+        self
+    }
+}
+impl<R: Read + ?Sized> IoBufferHandle for BudgetedIonStream<'_, R> {
+    fn save_io_buffer(&self) -> IoBuffer {
+        IoBuffer::from_checked(
+            self.block
+                .as_ref()
+                .expect("value requires a received block")
+                .clone(),
+            self.locations.clone(),
+            self.stream_offset,
+            self.local_offset,
+            self.local_end,
+        )
+    }
+    fn source_location_state(&self) -> &SourceLocationState {
+        &self.locations
+    }
+}
+impl<R: Read + ?Sized> IonDataSource for BudgetedIonStream<'_, R> {
+    const IS_STREAMING: bool = true;
+    fn buffer(&self) -> &[u8] {
+        match &self.block {
+            Some(b) => &b[self.local_offset..self.local_end],
+            None => &[],
+        }
+    }
+    fn fill_buffer(&mut self) -> IonResult<usize> {
+        self.check()?;
+        if matches!(self.pass, PassState::EndObserved) {
+            return Ok(0);
+        }
+        let (authority, mut grant) = self.grant()?;
+        let mut scratch = [0u8; 1]; // Initialization work was reserved before this statement.

+            Err(e) => {

+                self.budget.check()?;

+                    offered: 1,
+                    reported: n,

+            Ok(0) => {
+                grant.settle(0);
+                self.budget.check()?;
+                self.pass = PassState::EndObserved;
+                Ok(0)
+            }
+            Ok(1) => match authority {
+                ReadAuthority::Boundary => {
+                    grant.settle(0);
+                    self.budget.check()?;
+                    let policy = self.budget.source_policy()?;
+                    let mut s = self.budget.state.borrow_mut();
+                    let requested = add(s.usage.preparation.source_bytes, 1);

+                        ReaderLimitKind::SourceBytes,
+                        policy.common.source_bytes,
+                        requested,
+                        self.position_end(),

+                ReadAuthority::Structural => {
+                    grant.settle(1);
+                    self.budget.check()?;
+                    self.receive_first_byte(scratch[0])
+                }
+            },
+            Ok(_) => unreachable!(),
+        }
+    }
+    fn begin_read_pass(&mut self) -> IonResult<()> {
+        self.check()?;
+        self.pass = PassState::Open;
+        Ok(())
+    }
+    fn consume(&mut self, n: usize) {
+        self.local_offset += n;
+        debug_assert!(self.local_offset <= self.local_end);
+    }
+    fn position(&self) -> usize {
+        self.stream_offset + self.local_offset
+    }
+}
