+//! Source-authored Task2B recipes. First vertical tracer uses actual Reader and Read.
+use super::*;
+use std::cell::RefCell;
+use std::io::{self, Read};
+use std::rc::Rc;
+struct ScriptedRead {
+    calls: Rc<RefCell<Vec<usize>>>,
+    steps: Vec<io::Result<Vec<u8>>>,
+}
+impl Read for ScriptedRead {
+    fn read(&mut self, b: &mut [u8]) -> io::Result<usize> {
+        self.calls.borrow_mut().push(b.len());
+        let bytes = self.steps.remove(0)?;
+        assert!(bytes.len() <= b.len());
+        b[..bytes.len()].copy_from_slice(&bytes);
+        Ok(bytes.len())
+    }
+}
+fn exact_budget(attempts: usize, io: usize, work: usize) -> ReaderBudget {
+    let w = std::mem::size_of::<usize>();
+    let common = SourceLimits::builder()
+        .source_bytes(1)
+        .source_instances(1)
+        .cumulative_requested_payload_bytes(w + 1)
+        .resident_requested_payload_bytes(w + 1)
+        .logical_location_entries(1)
+        .build()
+        .unwrap();
+    let stream = StreamReadLimits::builder()
+        .initial_capacity(1)
+        .max_window_capacity(1)
+        .max_read_span(1)
+        .read_attempts(attempts)
+        .requested_io_bytes(io)
+        .allocation_events(2)
+        .byte_operations(work)
+        .build()
+        .unwrap();
+    let policy = SourceReadLimits::new(
+        common,
+        SourceModes::PreparedAndStreaming {
+            prepared: PreparationWorkLimits::try_new(100).unwrap(),
+            streaming: stream,
+        },
+    )
+    .unwrap();
+    ReaderBudget::new(
+        ReaderLimits::builder()
+            .max_text_depth(8)
+            .cache_bytes(8192)
+            .child_steps(256)
+            .symbol_slots(128)
+            .created_symbol_slots(128)
+            .source_limits(policy)
+            .build()
+            .unwrap(),
+    )
+}
+#[test]
+fn exact_one_next_retains_one_byte_with_exact_source_storage_and_work() {
+    let w = std::mem::size_of::<usize>();
+    let budget = exact_budget(2, 2, w + 5);
+    let calls = Rc::new(RefCell::new(vec![]));
+    let mut input = ScriptedRead {
+        calls: calls.clone(),
+        steps: vec![Ok(vec![b'1']), Ok(vec![])],
+    };
+    let mut reader = budget
+        .stream_reader(crate::v1_0::Text.into(), &mut input)
+        .unwrap();
+    let v = reader.next().unwrap().unwrap();
+    assert_eq!(v.read().unwrap().expect_i64().unwrap(), 1);
+    let retained = v.to_owned();
+    drop(reader);
+    assert_eq!(&*calls.borrow(), &[1, 1]);
+    {
+        let s = budget.state.borrow();
+        assert_eq!(s.usage.preparation.source_bytes, 1);
+        assert_eq!(s.usage.preparation.storage_bytes, w + 1);
+        assert_eq!(s.usage.stream.resident_bytes, w + 1);
+        assert_eq!(s.usage.stream.byte_operations, w + 5);
+        assert_eq!(s.usage.stream.allocation_events, 2);
+        assert_eq!(s.usage.stream.held_source_bytes, 0);
+    }
+    assert_eq!(
+        crate::Element::try_from(&retained).unwrap().as_i64(),
+        Some(1)
+    );
+    drop(retained);
+    assert_eq!(budget.state.borrow().usage.stream.resident_bytes, 0);
+}
+#[test]
+fn drain_positive_spends_third_read_and_fresh_eof_pass() {
+    let w = std::mem::size_of::<usize>();
+    let budget = exact_budget(3, 3, w + 6);
+    let calls = Rc::new(RefCell::new(vec![]));
+    let mut input = ScriptedRead {
+        calls: calls.clone(),
+        steps: vec![Ok(vec![b'1']), Ok(vec![]), Ok(vec![])],
+    };
+    let mut reader = budget
+        .stream_reader(crate::v1_0::Text.into(), &mut input)
+        .unwrap();
+    let retained = reader.next().unwrap().unwrap().to_owned();
+    assert!(reader.next().unwrap().is_none());
+    assert_eq!(&*calls.borrow(), &[1, 1, 1]);
+    assert_eq!(budget.state.borrow().usage.stream.byte_operations, w + 6);
+    drop(reader);
+    assert_eq!(budget.state.borrow().usage.stream.resident_bytes, w + 1);
+    drop(retained);
+    assert_eq!(budget.state.borrow().usage.stream.resident_bytes, 0);
+}

Root and independent source review accepted this proposal for a fresh isolated implementation proof only. Structural probes with remaining primary capacity must hold that primary grant across the callback. One next call on input 1 has two callbacks and W+5 work; an additional drain call starts a new EOF pass and requires a third callback and W+6 work. The original v1 proposal remains below as history. Budgeted Ion streaming sources

morphir-etg2.22.1 · 19 October 2026 · Task 2B proposal, revision 2 · Review before implementation

The accepted fixed-source proof avoids hidden copies when lazy values retain captured bytes. Streaming still allocates, shifts and copies its buffer before it knows whether the next read returns a byte, EOF or an error. Task 2B should add a separate checked stream factory that reserves each library-owned read, byte operation and payload allocation before the effect. Retained values must keep their buffers charged until their last owner drops.

Opt-in API and shared policy

Use private validated fields and closed modes. Common source quotas span fixed and streaming owners on one ReaderBudget. Keep preparation work and streaming I/O/work distinct. Every quota is explicit; zero means no authority. Positive capacities and read span are tuning values that require at least 1. Validate all arithmetic against the existing supported usize/isize range, including row-byte multiplication and absolute offsets.

Quota preflight is pure and non-mutating. The planner first tries the preferred capacity and then exact required capacity against all relevant quotas. A rejected preference must not poison the budget. After choosing a plan, atomically reserve all of its credits once. If neither plan fits, record the first typed quota refusal in a documented fixed check order. Overflow becomes a refusal, not wraparound.

Do not hold a RefCell borrow across Read, allocation, payload destruction or caller-controlled drop. A held read grant protects primary allowance from reentrant fixed-source preparation. Its settlement must reconcile the grant even when a callback has already caused a sticky failure. An RAII read-phase guard prevents two checked Read callbacks on the same budget from running at once.

Requested payload excludes allocator rounding and fixed Rc/Vec metadata. Count metadata-producing blocks and source instances separately. This is not a heap/RSS guarantee. A caller's retained handles legitimately consume capacity. Library byte work excludes the parser's scans, numeric conversion, scalar materialization, location lookup and arbitrary work inside Read. Owners, COW and row indices

A checked byte block holds an initialized Vec payload and a resident lease in the same Rc owner. The initialized usable length is the charged requested capacity C; allocator-reported extra capacity is never made readable or used as free authority. Use try_reserve_exact before initialization and no reallocating conversion into Rc<[u8]>. Rc contains the Vec owner without a second payload copy. Rc allocation itself retains process OOM behavior; the proof promises quota checks and typed recoverable payload-reserve failures, not recovery from allocator abort.

Use Rc::get_mut, not a separate strong-count guess. If unique, shift only when tail room is exhausted and reserve L movement operations first. If shared, copy only L live unread bytes into a new authorized block at offset0. Fuse compaction and COW into that one copy. Growth holds old and new resident leases at once. Source payload drops before its lease, using field order or explicit destruction; no early resident release while old bytes remain allocated. The budget does not own sources, so leases do not create ownership cycles. The relevant upstream uniqueness/COW behavior is defined by Rc::get_mut and Rc::make_mut.

IoBuffer needs a private checked backing variant. save_io_buffer clones its owner handles with no source/index allocation. Public read_from and every private mutation helper refuse that snapshot before effects, as prepared snapshots already do. consume changes view offsets only. The active stream owns the only checked mutation path; it never calls a legacy Mutable helper on a checked owner.

A checked append-only row state shares all earlier absolute row offsets with every retained value. Later append does not invalidate their positions. An index replacement first reserves its new capacity G times W while the old block is live, then copies only the E logical existing offsets. New LF offsets append once. The last-row cache remains within the unchanged prefix; location lookup itself is outside this work quota. Keep raw LF, byte columns, CRLF behavior, malformed UTF8 bytes and empty public binary locations unchanged.

Only a private non-cloneable received-chunk capability can append rows. It binds source identity, absolute offset and validated n to actual newly received bytes. Generic update_from_source must reject this checked state. Reparse, move, COW, save and to_owned cannot mint that capability or index old bytes again.

Checked refill order

The pure planner selects a closed read plan. DirectAppend is allowed only with a unique initialized tail and q bounded by available primary authority, max read span and current tail. StructuralProbe applies when primary authority remains but shift, COW, initial allocation or growth would otherwise be needed. It reserves and holds exactly1 primary byte before Read, in addition to its read-attempt, requested-I/O and initialization credits. BoundaryProbe applies only when primary authority is exhausted. It holds no primary grant and offers one initialized stack byte as overflow scratch. Both probe kinds check their finite I/O/work credits before the callback.

Use distinct private plan variants carrying PrimaryReadGrant for DirectAppend or StructuralProbe, and a separate BoundaryProbe variant with no such grant. A callback cannot spend a held StructuralProbe byte through reentrant fixed-source preparation. Valid n=1 spends that grant, valid EOF or ordinary error releases its unused primary authority, and unwind/invalid-count cleanup conservatively spends the offered one-byte normal span. Boundary scratch never enters that settlement path.

  1. Check the first sticky quota failure and this source's terminal fault. Acquire the shared read-phase guard. Plan and reserve read authority without mutating payload/index. Do not call Read with an empty slice.
  2. Call Read with the chosen initialized span. Validate returned n no larger than q before length arithmetic, slicing, indexing or unsafe handout. Settle the normal held grant. Check whether a callback caused a global failure.
  3. On actual zero, remember EOF for this logical pass. On ordinary error, return it. Neither outcome shifts, COWs, grows or updates the row index when a probe was needed.
  4. On positive input, reserve n count operations before scanning its raw LF bytes. Use the count to plan logical entries, row capacity, byte capacity and all remaining copy/init/fill/write operations. Re-evaluate uniqueness after the callback, since it may have dropped retained owners.
  5. Reserve the chosen publication plan atomically. Complete every fallible candidate payload allocation before moving old bytes in place or changing published offsets. Initialize and copy authorized payloads, fill row offsets, then publish a coherent byte end and row prefix without a remaining fallible step.

For DirectAppend, the Read can dirty an uncommitted initialized tail, but published end does not advance until index/work checks pass. For a structural probe, a positive byte stays in one inline pending slot until the plan commits. A later quota/allocation failure can follow a bounded Read because its LF count was unknowable beforehand. It is not a transactional rewind of an external stream. The source becomes terminal on post-read allocation failure, and resource refusal poisons the shared budget. Retained old values remain intact.

Append a new row batch with n count-scan operations and, when it contains LF, n fill-scan operations plus K*W offset writes. No second scan when K is zero. Reserve E*W old-row copy operations for index growth. A new byte capacity C costs C initialization operations; copies/moves cost only the live L bytes. Candidate capacity fallback is decided before recording any failure.

Exact limits and temporary EOF

When source byte credit is exhausted, a separate one-byte BoundaryProbe distinguishes actual EOF from excess source. Actual0 permits completion; a valid one-byte result triggers sticky SourceBytes with requested charged+1 before the extra byte is appended or a truncated text scalar is returned. Never implement source limiting through Read::take, which substitutes EOF at its own cap and can make a larger token appear complete. This follows the pinned Take behavior and the existing text completion rule.

Structural probes avoid allocation just to find EOF, including a full shared window with no resident headroom. A valid empty source needs row 0 but no byte block. Probe work and I/O quota must still be available; spending the final primary byte does not grant free unlimited EOF checks.

Add begin_read_pass to the internal data-source protocol with a default no-op. Call it once at read_next entry. Checked streams reset a closed pass state to Open. An actual nonempty-span Read returning zero sets EndObserved. Repeated fill calls within that pass return cached zero without I/O; the next logical next or peek starts a new pass and can observe appended bytes. Do not use a permanently fused EOF flag. Ordinary legacy source callbacks keep their current behavior.

Rust permits temporary EOF, partial reads and blocking callbacks. Read errors report no successful byte count; Interrupted may be retried by a caller. Checked streaming returns one ordinary I/O error per invocation and does not install an unbounded automatic retry loop. These rules come from the pinned Rust 1.94.1 Read contract. Its source also warns that safe Read implementations cannot be trusted for unsafe memory safety. The checked source validates n itself.

Closed containers and binary values may yield before overall EOF. A caller must drain to None to establish whole-source byte compliance. This library cannot turn a mutable file into an immutable snapshot or stop a Read implementation from blocking, allocating, prefetching, or changing its hidden source. The checked claim ends at the supplied Read boundary. A caller-owned BufReader can prefetch beyond that offered span. Morphir's frozen finite original-byte capture remains the preferred fixed-source seam.

Errors, retries and reentry

OutcomeProposed behavior
Resource quota / arithmetic refusalExisting ResourceLimit with first kind/offset/limit/requested wins globally. All later checked factory/next/peek/prepare calls refuse before further source effects. Spent attempts, byte work, row entries and cumulative allocation credit do not refund.
Ordinary Read errorReturn existing IonError::Io without poisoning resource policy. Release unused held primary authority for DirectAppend or StructuralProbe because no valid n was returned. BoundaryProbe has no primary grant. Callback attempts/span and probe initialization remain spent. A caller retry reserves primary authority again and spends new I/O/work credit; do not reuse a dirty tail as published bytes.
Invalid count n>qNew typed SourceInput failure InvalidReadCount, terminal for that source before slice/index changes. Conservatively spend the held normal span q as uncertain input. Overflow-probe scratch is never published primary; its invalid callback poisons the source, not a fabricated valid byte receipt. No unbounded error-string formatting.
Read unwindsNo catch inside the library. RAII clears active-read state, conservatively spends the held normal span for DirectAppend or the held1 for StructuralProbe, and records terminal ReadUnwound without allocation/panic. BoundaryProbe has no primary grant to settle. If the caller catches unwind, retry refuses before Read. Process abort is outside cleanup guarantees.
Nested Read on same budgetTyped recoverable ReentrantRead before invoking the nested callback. The outer DirectAppend or StructuralProbe primary grant remains held. Other budget operations may run if they can reserve around it. A nested preparation quota failure remains the global first failure; outer settlement must still reconcile held authority even under that failure.
Post-read payload reserve failureTyped terminal PayloadAllocationFailed for this source. Release only unmaterialized resident reservations. Keep received/source/work/attempt/cumulative credits spent. No second Read can discard the pending byte or pretend the old input position was restored.
Wrong selected budget / wrong source modeIllegal configuration/use before factory construction effects; not a fabricated resource exhaustion. Old preparation shorthand selects prepared mode only.

Proposed IonError::SourceInput wraps a private-construction failure with closed kind and existing Position evidence. IonError is already non-exhaustive. Keep bounded scalar fields rather than caller strings; do not retain arbitrary input or exception text in a sticky failure. If a callback already triggered global ResourceLimit, settle its held reservation and return that first global failure instead of replacing it with a later source fault. No RefCell borrow may survive into a callback or destructor.

Every new safe/internal mutation route must either carry checked authorization or reject the checked backing. The proof must audit constructors, clone, save, to_owned, public read_from/consume, private grow/shift/make_data_mut, generic index update and active refill. It must also guard at pass entry, so a different source's failure prevents parsing buffered data under a now-failed budget. This does not retroactively claim every old already-yielded scalar/macro operation is guarded.

Review decisions

The recommendation is one common fixed/stream ledger, leased retained storage and probe-before-structural-mutation. Accept the per-pass EOF cache because it preserves future appended-data reads while removing repeated physical EOF calls inside one raw-reader pass. Keep all ordinary constructors unchanged.

  1. Approve or amend the proposed composed source policy and compatibility shorthand. This requires an internal leased prepared-owner extension in the new proof, not changes to the accepted artifact.
  2. Confirm resident versus cumulative requested payload, logical rows, byte-operation units and read-span charging. No production quota values are proposed.
  3. Confirm the one-byte lookahead boundary and explicit whole-stream drain requirement. A caller asking for a valid prefix has not qualified its unseen suffix.
  4. Confirm typed terminal source-input faults and the recoverable nested-read rejection. Arbitrary callback runtime, hidden I/O, process abort and unsafe external corruption remain outside the guarantee.
  5. Authorize only the smallest isolated source tracer if these choices are accepted. Implementation and a broader bounded-reader claim require separate evidence.

No unresolved need for an additional lexer or a new file protocol was found. The existing parser, source positions, lazy retention model and Read boundary suffice for this proposal. The concrete questions are policy composition, credit units and source-fault semantics, not Ion support removal.

<h1>Budgeted Ion streaming sources</h1>
<p class="meta">morphir-etg2.22.1 · 19 October 2026 · Task 2B proposal, revision 2 · Review before implementation</p>
<p>The accepted fixed-source proof avoids hidden copies when lazy values retain captured bytes. Streaming still allocates, shifts and copies its buffer before it knows whether the next read returns a byte, EOF or an error. Task 2B should add a separate checked stream factory that reserves each library-owned read, byte operation and payload allocation before the effect. Retained values must keep their buffers charged until their last owner drops.</p>
<div class="note">Design only. No Task 2B source patch, dependency selection, SDK integration or production resource numbers are authorized or delivered. This proposal preserves the accepted Task 1 and Task 2A proof files. It does not qualify a full bounded Ion reader.</div>
<p>This additive revision answers two independent review clarifications. A StructuralProbe holds one byte of normal primary authority across its callback. Only BoundaryProbe uses out-of-primary overflow scratch. The exact two-call tracer requests one value and drops it; separate recipes cover a later next-to-None with sufficient or exhausted read credit. The original v1 HTML, 34-recipe packet and final receipt remain byte-identical and guarded in this revision's source receipt.</p>

<section id="status"><h2>Scope and evidence</h2>
<ul><li><label><input type="checkbox" checked disabled> Trace the accepted source, retention and refill paths without changing them.</label></li>
<li><label><input type="checkbox" checked disabled> Author fixed recipes before any Task 2B implementation or observed output.</label></li>
<li><label><input type="checkbox" checked disabled> Verify all 885 accepted Task 2A source hashes and original model expectation packet hashes.</label></li>
<li><label><input type="checkbox" disabled> Obtain review of this proposal and authorization for an isolated proof.</label></li>
<li><label><input type="checkbox" disabled> Implement and independently review the checked streaming-source proof.</label></li>
<li><label><input type="checkbox" disabled> Complete scalar, scanner, arena and remaining encoding work before an SDK/profile claim.</label></li></ul>
<p>The source baseline is ion-rs 1.0.1 at upstream <code>a1df66475c76605dd31c8566ef11f50f07fe8111</code> plus accepted isolated Task 1 and Task 2A patches. Accepted Task 2A whole-source SHA256 is <code>0244a54b2233c61b134a237f33181c49de1b55c3542ea9eb9acd6a23a7e14676</code>. The receipt hashes nine inspected source files and records exact line anchors. The independent Task 2A review found no material issue within fixed-source/index/retention scope. Its disabled-Ion 1.1 lane remains failed with the same three baseline tooling failures; this design introduces no new passing reader qualification.</p>
<p>The Morphir model profile remains separate: aggregate primary input bytes, parsed application values, assembled application values, depth, decoded key/string UTF16 units and output bytes retain their own ledgers. This proposal selects no auxiliary production cap and does not combine input and output into one application-value quota.</p></section>
<section id="trace"><h2>Current source trace</h2>
<p>Line numbers below refer to the immutable accepted Task 2A source, not unpatched upstream. New implementation must extend a fresh verified replay in a new proof directory.</p>
<table tabindex="0"><thead><tr><th style="min-width:11rem">Route</th><th style="min-width:26rem">Current behavior and proposed insertion</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td><code>src/lazy/streaming_raw_reader.rs:618</code></td><td>IonStream::new allocates its 4096-byte buffer immediately. Keep that legacy constructor. Mint a checked input only through ReaderBudget::stream_reader; start with a charged row 0 and no byte block.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>.../streaming_raw_reader.rs:528</code></td><td>read_from shifts, grows and uses Rc::make_mut before calling Read. Add a distinct checked refill planner; do not route it through these legacy mutable helpers.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>.../streaming_raw_reader.rs:554,570,575,588</code></td><td>grow allocates and initializes a doubled block; make_data_mut may copy a shared block; shift updates positions and copies live bytes. Checked blocks use explicit authorized replacement or unique movement, with no hidden make_mut call.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>.../streaming_raw_reader.rs:131,144,187,232</code></td><td>read_next may call fill multiple times for one EOF pass; text scalars ending at the current buffer boundary need a further read. Add a default no-op read-pass hook and a checked-input EOF cache. Keep the existing scalar completion rule.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>.../streaming_raw_reader.rs:267,627</code><br><code>src/lazy/expanded/mod.rs:133,189</code><br><code>src/lazy/value.rs:260</code></td><td>save_io_buffer, context clone and to_owned retain byte/index handles. Every checked handle must retain the corresponding storage lease. Saving cannot allocate/copy a source or create a fresh index.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>src/location.rs:100,148,216,234</code></td><td>The index is shared and append-only, with cached lookup position. Keep one checked index per source; reserve row capacity and append only newly received bytes. Existing generic update must reject the checked variant.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>src/read_limits/prepared_source.rs:120,150,178</code></td><td>The fixed-source factory already owns source/index and enforces shared-budget identity. Compose its counters with checked streaming rather than grant each mode a separate source allowance.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>src/result/mod.rs:38</code><br><code>src/read_limits.rs:167,268</code></td><td>IonError is non-exhaustive; quota failure is already typed and sticky. Add typed source-input failures for invalid callbacks/unwind/allocation, with separate recovery rules below.</td></tr>
</tbody></table>
<p>Unbudgeted routes remain ordinary Reader::new inputs, legacy IonSlice, legacy IonStream and File/BufReader adapters. The new checked factory is the capability boundary. Passing a ReaderBudget to a legacy input does not turn that input into a checked source.</p></section>
<section id="api"><h2>Opt-in API and shared policy</h2>
<p>Use private validated fields and closed modes. Common source quotas span fixed and streaming owners on one ReaderBudget. Keep preparation work and streaming I/O/work distinct. Every quota is explicit; zero means no authority. Positive capacities and read span are tuning values that require at least 1. Validate all arithmetic against the existing supported usize/isize range, including row-byte multiplication and absolute offsets.</p>
<pre><code class="language-rust">// Proposed API shape. Opaque structs have validated builders, not public fields.
pub struct SourceLimits;        // common bytes, instances, storage, rows
pub struct StreamReadLimits;    // explicit I/O, allocation and byte-work quotas
pub struct PreparationWorkLimits;
pub enum SourceModes {
    Prepared(PreparationWorkLimits),
    Streaming(StreamReadLimits),
    PreparedAndStreaming {
        prepared: PreparationWorkLimits,
        streaming: StreamReadLimits,
    },
}
pub struct SourceReadLimits;    // validated SourceLimits + SourceModes

impl ReaderLimitsBuilder {
    pub fn source_limits(self, limits: SourceReadLimits) -> Self;
    // Existing source_preparation(...) remains a compatibility shorthand.
}
impl ReaderBudget {
    pub fn stream_reader<'r, D: Decoder, R: Read + ?Sized>(
        &self,
        config: ReadConfig<D>,
        source: &'r mut R,
    ) -> IonResult<Reader<D, BudgetedIonStream<'r, R>>>;
}</code></pre>
<p>BudgetedIonStream has private construction and implements the sealed input path. It borrows the caller's Read object, so it gains no ambient file or close authority. A concrete ReadConfig avoids invoking a caller-defined Into conversion inside the checked factory. Missing config budget inherits the owner; identical pointer identity is accepted; a different identity rejects before reserving a source instance, constructing a generic reader, allocating source payload or calling Read.</p>
<p>Keep source_preparation as an adapter into the common ledger. Its existing storage cap becomes both cumulative requested payload and resident requested payload. The resident bound is redundant because resident never exceeds cumulative. Its preparation work remains exactly 3N+E as accepted, and it authorizes no streaming. Reject simultaneous source_limits and source_preparation selections at build time; the final setter must not silently replace policy.</p>
<p>The fresh extension needs leased fixed-source owners as well as streaming owners, so mixed-mode residency is truthful. Moving the existing prepared byte Rc into a private leased owner adds no source copy; prepared IoBuffer snapshots must retain that leased owner. Initial row 0 and every new stream count against common row/source quotas, including empty streams. These internal changes belong in a new proof; the accepted Task 2A artifact stays immutable.</p></section>
<section id="ledger"><h2>Accounting before effects</h2>
<table tabindex="0"><thead><tr><th style="min-width:11rem">Validated quota</th><th style="min-width:26rem">Debit and lifetime</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>source_bytes</td><td>Common charged fixed lengths, received streaming bytes, conservative uncertain normal-read spans, and outstanding held read grants. Both DirectAppend and StructuralProbe are normal reads: DirectAppend holds its offered q and StructuralProbe holds exactly1 primary byte before the callback. Settle valid n as spent and release unused held authority. This does not refund any spent work. Only BoundaryProbe is separate out-of-primary lookahead and never published source.</td></tr>
<tr><td>source_instances</td><td>Cumulative successful reservation attempts for new logical source owners, including empty sources. Clones/reopen/snapshots are the same owner. Factory reservations are not refunded on later failure.</td></tr>
<tr><td>cumulative_requested_payload_bytes</td><td>Each requested byte-block capacity and row-block capacity times sizeof(usize), before allocation attempt. Count replacement blocks fully, even when old blocks are released. Failed allocations, retry and drop do not refund this credit.</td></tr>
<tr><td>resident_requested_payload_bytes</td><td>Live requested payload plus outstanding allocation reservations. Reserve transient old+new growth/COW/index blocks before allocating. A failed allocation releases only its unmaterialized residency reservation. A materialized lease releases after its actual last payload owner is destroyed.</td></tr>
<tr><td>logical_location_entries</td><td>Cumulative row 0 plus new raw LF offsets once per received chunk. Capacity slack and replacement copies do not create logical rows.</td></tr>
<tr><td>read_attempts / requested_io_bytes</td><td>Each actual Read invocation and its offered nonempty initialized span q, before the callback. Short reads, EOF and errors spend all q requested bytes and the attempt. No retry refund.</td></tr>
<tr><td>allocation_events</td><td>Each requested streaming byte or row payload block, including initial row 0 and replacement blocks. One event includes a bounded fixed amount of owner/header metadata. Retry still counts. Prepared blocks retain their accepted bounded count per source instance. No source-sized allocation may hide in metadata.</td></tr>
<tr><td>byte_operations</td><td>Library initialization C, copy/move live bytes L, count scan n, optional fill scan n and row writes/copies times sizeof(usize). One unit is one byte position processed in one explicit pass, not both a read and write charge. Stack probe initialization costs1. Preparation keeps its distinct accepted3N+E counter.</td></tr>
<tr><td>initial_capacity / max_window_capacity / max_read_span</td><td>Validated positive stream tuning values with initial no larger than max window. Capacities bound requested logical window length. Initial capacity is a preferred target, not a mandatory allocation; clamp to the exact needed1 if remaining quota cannot fit the preference. All arithmetic is checked before effects.</td></tr>
</tbody></table>
<p>Quota preflight is pure and non-mutating. The planner first tries the preferred capacity and then exact required capacity against all relevant quotas. A rejected preference must not poison the budget. After choosing a plan, atomically reserve all of its credits once. If neither plan fits, record the first typed quota refusal in a documented fixed check order. Overflow becomes a refusal, not wraparound.</p>
<p>Do not hold a RefCell borrow across Read, allocation, payload destruction or caller-controlled drop. A held read grant protects primary allowance from reentrant fixed-source preparation. Its settlement must reconcile the grant even when a callback has already caused a sticky failure. An RAII read-phase guard prevents two checked Read callbacks on the same budget from running at once.</p>
<p>Requested payload excludes allocator rounding and fixed Rc/Vec metadata. Count metadata-producing blocks and source instances separately. This is not a heap/RSS guarantee. A caller's retained handles legitimately consume capacity. Library byte work excludes the parser's scans, numeric conversion, scalar materialization, location lookup and arbitrary work inside Read. Each has separate remaining work.</p></section>

<p>A checked byte block holds an initialized Vec payload and a resident lease in the same Rc owner. The initialized usable length is the charged requested capacity C; allocator-reported extra capacity is never made readable or used as free authority. Use try_reserve_exact before initialization and no reallocating conversion into Rc<[u8]>. Rc contains the Vec owner without a second payload copy. Rc allocation itself retains process OOM behavior; the proof promises quota checks and typed recoverable payload-reserve failures, not recovery from allocator abort.</p>
<p>Use Rc::get_mut, not a separate strong-count guess. If unique, shift only when tail room is exhausted and reserve L movement operations first. If shared, copy only L live unread bytes into a new authorized block at offset0. Fuse compaction and COW into that one copy. Growth holds old and new resident leases at once. Source payload drops before its lease, using field order or explicit destruction; no early resident release while old bytes remain allocated. The budget does not own sources, so leases do not create ownership cycles. The relevant upstream uniqueness/COW behavior is defined by <a href="https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/blob/e408947bfd200af42db322daf0fadfe7e26d3bd1/library/alloc/src/rc.rs#L1917">Rc::get_mut</a> and <a href="https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/blob/e408947bfd200af42db322daf0fadfe7e26d3bd1/library/alloc/src/rc.rs#L2065">Rc::make_mut</a>.</p>
<p>IoBuffer needs a private checked backing variant. save_io_buffer clones its owner handles with no source/index allocation. Public read_from and every private mutation helper refuse that snapshot before effects, as prepared snapshots already do. consume changes view offsets only. The active stream owns the only checked mutation path; it never calls a legacy Mutable helper on a checked owner.</p>
<p>A checked append-only row state shares all earlier absolute row offsets with every retained value. Later append does not invalidate their positions. An index replacement first reserves its new capacity G times W while the old block is live, then copies only the E logical existing offsets. New LF offsets append once. The last-row cache remains within the unchanged prefix; location lookup itself is outside this work quota. Keep raw LF, byte columns, CRLF behavior, malformed UTF8 bytes and empty public binary locations unchanged.</p>
<p>Only a private non-cloneable received-chunk capability can append rows. It binds source identity, absolute offset and validated n to actual newly received bytes. Generic update_from_source must reject this checked state. Reparse, move, COW, save and to_owned cannot mint that capability or index old bytes again.</p>

<section id="refill"><h2>Checked refill order</h2>
<p>The pure planner selects a closed read plan. DirectAppend is allowed only with a unique initialized tail and q bounded by available primary authority, max read span and current tail. StructuralProbe applies when primary authority remains but shift, COW, initial allocation or growth would otherwise be needed. It reserves and holds exactly1 primary byte before Read, in addition to its read-attempt, requested-I/O and initialization credits. BoundaryProbe applies only when primary authority is exhausted. It holds no primary grant and offers one initialized stack byte as overflow scratch. Both probe kinds check their finite I/O/work credits before the callback.</p>
<p>Use distinct private plan variants carrying PrimaryReadGrant for DirectAppend or StructuralProbe, and a separate BoundaryProbe variant with no such grant. A callback cannot spend a held StructuralProbe byte through reentrant fixed-source preparation. Valid n=1 spends that grant, valid EOF or ordinary error releases its unused primary authority, and unwind/invalid-count cleanup conservatively spends the offered one-byte normal span. Boundary scratch never enters that settlement path.</p>
<ol><li>Check the first sticky quota failure and this source's terminal fault. Acquire the shared read-phase guard. Plan and reserve read authority without mutating payload/index. Do not call Read with an empty slice.</li>
<li>Call Read with the chosen initialized span. Validate returned n no larger than q before length arithmetic, slicing, indexing or unsafe handout. Settle the normal held grant. Check whether a callback caused a global failure.</li>
<li>On actual zero, remember EOF for this logical pass. On ordinary error, return it. Neither outcome shifts, COWs, grows or updates the row index when a probe was needed.</li>
<li>On positive input, reserve n count operations before scanning its raw LF bytes. Use the count to plan logical entries, row capacity, byte capacity and all remaining copy/init/fill/write operations. Re-evaluate uniqueness after the callback, since it may have dropped retained owners.</li>
<li>Reserve the chosen publication plan atomically. Complete every fallible candidate payload allocation before moving old bytes in place or changing published offsets. Initialize and copy authorized payloads, fill row offsets, then publish a coherent byte end and row prefix without a remaining fallible step.</li></ol>
<p>For DirectAppend, the Read can dirty an uncommitted initialized tail, but published end does not advance until index/work checks pass. For a structural probe, a positive byte stays in one inline pending slot until the plan commits. A later quota/allocation failure can follow a bounded Read because its LF count was unknowable beforehand. It is not a transactional rewind of an external stream. The source becomes terminal on post-read allocation failure, and resource refusal poisons the shared budget. Retained old values remain intact.</p>
<p>Append a new row batch with n count-scan operations and, when it contains LF, n fill-scan operations plus K*W offset writes. No second scan when K is zero. Reserve E*W old-row copy operations for index growth. A new byte capacity C costs C initialization operations; copies/moves cost only the live L bytes. Candidate capacity fallback is decided before recording any failure.</p></section>
<section id="eof"><h2>Exact limits and temporary EOF</h2>
<p>When source byte credit is exhausted, a separate one-byte BoundaryProbe distinguishes actual EOF from excess source. Actual0 permits completion; a valid one-byte result triggers sticky SourceBytes with requested charged+1 before the extra byte is appended or a truncated text scalar is returned. Never implement source limiting through Read::take, which substitutes EOF at its own cap and can make a larger token appear complete. This follows the pinned <a href="https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/blob/e408947bfd200af42db322daf0fadfe7e26d3bd1/library/std/src/io/mod.rs#L1239">Take behavior</a> and the existing text completion rule.</p>
<p>Structural probes avoid allocation just to find EOF, including a full shared window with no resident headroom. A valid empty source needs row 0 but no byte block. Probe work and I/O quota must still be available; spending the final primary byte does not grant free unlimited EOF checks.</p>
<p>Add begin_read_pass to the internal data-source protocol with a default no-op. Call it once at read_next entry. Checked streams reset a closed pass state to Open. An actual nonempty-span Read returning zero sets EndObserved. Repeated fill calls within that pass return cached zero without I/O; the next logical next or peek starts a new pass and can observe appended bytes. Do not use a permanently fused EOF flag. Ordinary legacy source callbacks keep their current behavior.</p>
<p>Rust permits temporary EOF, partial reads and blocking callbacks. Read errors report no successful byte count; Interrupted may be retried by a caller. Checked streaming returns one ordinary I/O error per invocation and does not install an unbounded automatic retry loop. These rules come from the pinned <a href="https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/blob/e408947bfd200af42db322daf0fadfe7e26d3bd1/library/std/src/io/mod.rs#L732">Rust 1.94.1 Read contract</a>. Its source also warns that safe Read implementations cannot be trusted for unsafe memory safety. The checked source validates n itself.</p>
<p>Closed containers and binary values may yield before overall EOF. A caller must drain to None to establish whole-source byte compliance. This library cannot turn a mutable file into an immutable snapshot or stop a Read implementation from blocking, allocating, prefetching, or changing its hidden source. The checked claim ends at the supplied Read boundary. A caller-owned <a href="https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/blob/e408947bfd200af42db322daf0fadfe7e26d3bd1/library/std/src/io/buffered/bufreader.rs#L338">BufReader can prefetch</a> beyond that offered span. Morphir's frozen finite original-byte capture remains the preferred fixed-source seam.</p></section>
<section id="faults"><h2>Errors, retries and reentry</h2>
<table tabindex="0"><thead><tr><th style="min-width:11rem">Outcome</th><th style="min-width:26rem">Proposed behavior</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>Resource quota / arithmetic refusal</td><td>Existing ResourceLimit with first kind/offset/limit/requested wins globally. All later checked factory/next/peek/prepare calls refuse before further source effects. Spent attempts, byte work, row entries and cumulative allocation credit do not refund.</td></tr>
<tr><td>Ordinary Read error</td><td>Return existing IonError::Io without poisoning resource policy. Release unused held primary authority for DirectAppend or StructuralProbe because no valid n was returned. BoundaryProbe has no primary grant. Callback attempts/span and probe initialization remain spent. A caller retry reserves primary authority again and spends new I/O/work credit; do not reuse a dirty tail as published bytes.</td></tr>
<tr><td>Invalid count n>q</td><td>New typed SourceInput failure InvalidReadCount, terminal for that source before slice/index changes. Conservatively spend the held normal span q as uncertain input. Overflow-probe scratch is never published primary; its invalid callback poisons the source, not a fabricated valid byte receipt. No unbounded error-string formatting.</td></tr>
<tr><td>Read unwinds</td><td>No catch inside the library. RAII clears active-read state, conservatively spends the held normal span for DirectAppend or the held1 for StructuralProbe, and records terminal ReadUnwound without allocation/panic. BoundaryProbe has no primary grant to settle. If the caller catches unwind, retry refuses before Read. Process abort is outside cleanup guarantees.</td></tr>
<tr><td>Nested Read on same budget</td><td>Typed recoverable ReentrantRead before invoking the nested callback. The outer DirectAppend or StructuralProbe primary grant remains held. Other budget operations may run if they can reserve around it. A nested preparation quota failure remains the global first failure; outer settlement must still reconcile held authority even under that failure.</td></tr>
<tr><td>Post-read payload reserve failure</td><td>Typed terminal PayloadAllocationFailed for this source. Release only unmaterialized resident reservations. Keep received/source/work/attempt/cumulative credits spent. No second Read can discard the pending byte or pretend the old input position was restored.</td></tr>
<tr><td>Wrong selected budget / wrong source mode</td><td>Illegal configuration/use before factory construction effects; not a fabricated resource exhaustion. Old preparation shorthand selects prepared mode only.</td></tr>
</tbody></table>
<p>Proposed IonError::SourceInput wraps a private-construction failure with closed kind and existing Position evidence. IonError is already non-exhaustive. Keep bounded scalar fields rather than caller strings; do not retain arbitrary input or exception text in a sticky failure. If a callback already triggered global ResourceLimit, settle its held reservation and return that first global failure instead of replacing it with a later source fault. No RefCell borrow may survive into a callback or destructor.</p>
<p>Every new safe/internal mutation route must either carry checked authorization or reject the checked backing. The proof must audit constructors, clone, save, to_owned, public read_from/consume, private grow/shift/make_data_mut, generic index update and active refill. It must also guard at pass entry, so a different source's failure prevents parsing buffered data under a now-failed budget. This does not retroactively claim every old already-yielded scalar/macro operation is guarded.</p></section>

<p>The packet contains 37 proposed recipes authored from source contracts and fixed byte literals before any Task 2B run. Its small finite test controls are not production policy. W means size_of::<usize> and must be established on each actual architecture. Instrumentation records calls, requested spans, allocation/copy attempts, committed end/index, lease lifetimes and typed failures. It must not derive expected data from adapter output.</p>

<p>The positive-drain companion increases attempts and requested I/O to3 and byte work to W+6. A second next starts a new pass, performs its own one-byte EOF probe and returns None, without allocating a new byte/index block. The exhausted-drain companion leaves attempts at2 while giving I/O/work room for that third probe. Its second next must return ReadAttempts limit2 requested3 before a third callback, rather than reuse old EOF or fabricate None.</p>
<p>The StructuralProbe error/retry companion returns Interrupted, byte0x31, then EOF. Each of the first two callbacks holds primary grant1. The error releases unspent primary authority but retains its I/O/work cost; the retry can hold that authority again. Total callbacks3 and work W+6 produce the same single-byte owner. The unwind and reentrant-preparation cases explicitly check grant reconciliation and no publication after a first global failure.</p>
<p>Other recipes cover empty and temporary EOF, interrupted/error/read limits, invalid n, panic cleanup, reentry, shared fixed/stream source authority, wrong identity, COW transient peaks, owner drop during callbacks, unique compaction, index growth and LF refusal, cumulative allocation after drop, CRLF/emoji byte locations, split binary IVM, malformed UTF8, checked mutation refusal, exact-capacity fallback and externally buffered prefetch.</p>

<section id="review"><h2>Review decisions</h2>
<p>The recommendation is one common fixed/stream ledger, leased retained storage and probe-before-structural-mutation. Accept the per-pass EOF cache because it preserves future appended-data reads while removing repeated physical EOF calls inside one raw-reader pass. Keep all ordinary constructors unchanged.</p>
<ol><li>Approve or amend the proposed composed source policy and compatibility shorthand. This requires an internal leased prepared-owner extension in the new proof, not changes to the accepted artifact.</li><li>Confirm resident versus cumulative requested payload, logical rows, byte-operation units and read-span charging. No production quota values are proposed.</li><li>Confirm the one-byte lookahead boundary and explicit whole-stream drain requirement. A caller asking for a valid prefix has not qualified its unseen suffix.</li><li>Confirm typed terminal source-input faults and the recoverable nested-read rejection. Arbitrary callback runtime, hidden I/O, process abort and unsafe external corruption remain outside the guarantee.</li><li>Authorize only the smallest isolated source tracer if these choices are accepted. Implementation and a broader bounded-reader claim require separate evidence.</li></ol>
<p>No unresolved need for an additional lexer or a new file protocol was found. The existing parser, source positions, lazy retention model and Read boundary suffice for this proposal. The concrete questions are policy composition, credit units and source-fault semantics, not Ion support removal.</p></section>

Reviewed parent-only trusted output binding and 32 fixed cases

After root and independent source review, the corrected v2 boundary was authorized for private parent-only implementation on 19 October 2026. The immutable proposal below retains its pre-authorization wording. Use existing genuine Current and OutContext semantics, actual startup-issued authority, real guest membership, unchanged output grants, validated compiler module, real attempt ownership and bounded retained witness. No new SDK parser/API or whole-host-config hardening is required for this slice.

The independent review caught a source-description error: existing capture_compiled captures originals only. V2 corrects it and explicitly retains checked frozen-primary headers, same-snapshot semantic projection and bounded required-format codec/decode/assembly/output integration as pending before advertisement. All 32 scenarios remain source-authored expectations, not 32 passing production tests. Implementation must preserve original provider WIP before isolated work, freeze recovery evidence and qualify actual callers before review. No public offer, wire, PR, push, registry or release is authorized by this internal checkpoint.

Trusted host output binding for model originals

morphir-etg2.22.1 · 19 October 2026 · smaller proposal v2 for review · no implementation authorized

The contract we need

The connected model-originals owner must open the output that the existing host compiler policy selects for the actual project. It must preserve the provider's directory authority, the real compiler module and the original explicit output overrides. That requires the existing Current resolver, not portable discovery's filtered configuration sidecars.

This proposal reuses the actual SDK configuration loader as a trusted host service. It does not promise a new limit inside every config parser, OS environment snapshot, merge clone or member-pattern step. Model-source, guest, framing, inventory, decode/projection and retained-owner limits remain fully required.

The earlier full-config proposal and its 53 scenarios remain immutable optional-hardening history. This is a new review proposal. It does not close .22, .22.1 or .22.2, advertise unfinished capability support or change any frozen protocol.

An explicit trusted host resolver

Introduce a parent-private TrustedHostOutputLookup only at the CLI startup/provider registration boundary. The issuer must receive the actual stored provider directory and its verified absolute label, original host ConfigLoadOptions, original OutOverrides and an explicit AmbientAuthority from trusted CLI code. It is not deserializable and exposes no arbitrary-path, config-file, module or environment setter.

This grant deliberately authorizes the existing host configuration lookup policy, including its real ancestor, system, global, explicit-user, alias and Process environment behavior. It does not authorize a guest or HTTP caller to choose those locations. Its broad host lookup is an explicit trust decision, not a claim that the provider-root directory alone confines ancestor reads. The actual old ambient loader cannot serve as authority merely because a caller knows a matching string.

Issue the grant after the provider has its actual workspace_dir, stored root label and final original output overrides, before registering the additive model-originals service. Verify root-label identity against the held directory. Store it with that provider/session/source owner. Each resolve checks the same held root against the stored label again. Do not create a grant from fields in a capture request or from portable canonical_root metadata.

Before lookup, validate the requested source against the provider's stored source, perform actual native or installed discovery and locate the selected key in that actual response. Validate the returned relative path and open the project through the original held provider directory using the existing nofollow helper. Verify that the host-derived absolute project label still identifies that opened directory before and after resolution. Replacement or a changed label refuses. The host never hands that identity-check handle to a guest as new read authority.

The grant's only operation accepts this validated selected project and returns the actual output binding. Actual guest membership remains a parent responsibility. A source/project key identifies a request; neither it nor a page revision is a filesystem permission.

Keep the actual Current policy

Use discover_config_at on the genuine selected project label. If it returns a primary, call load_config_context_with with the provider's original options and ProjectSelection::Current. This constructs a genuine ConfigContext through the existing loader and merged LayerStack. Do not construct a lookalike context, merge layers again or extract output settings from portable details.

Native and installed discovery keep their existing capability-rooted request construction. For installed mode, send that exact request to the real guest and use the actual guest response as membership. Do not consume into_typed_details solely to obtain every project's config: the host Current loader supplies the selected host output facts, and the all-project sidecar copy is unnecessary. These are two deliberate policies, portable membership and trusted host compiler-output selection. Their configurations are not claimed to be the same immutable config snapshot.

Bind the real selected output

Pass the genuine optional context to existing OutContext::resolve. It already delegates to the SDK's shared output and module rules. Preserve the v1 special base: no context and no explicit override means the selected project directory; otherwise use the genuine attempt cwd. Preserve flag, original nonempty output-env, config workspace.out_dir and default precedence.

Open an implicit output only through the provider-owned directory after the same confinement check used by v1. An ancestor workspace configuration may select an output outside that grant; that remains a refusal. An explicit original flag or original nonempty output-env may authorize its additional directory using trusted host ambient authority. A newly received request value, a config path, a diagnostic label or a guest response cannot become an explicit override.

TrustedHostOutputLookup  // actual provider Dir + verified label + host intent
SelectedProject         // actual membership + opened project Dir identity
ResolvedProjectSource   // existing owned output Dir + SelectedModule
BindingWitness = {
  actual_provider_and_source,
  provider_root_identity,
  project_directory_identity,
  output_directory_identity,
  compiler_module,
  original_output_grant_kind
}

Reuse the parent ResolvedProjectSource and SelectedModule domains rather than introduce another output/module model. Extend its private authority comparison only where needed for root/source/grant ownership. The witness is not supplied by the client or serialized as a permission. Compact path/key copies and retained handles must fit the existing host's retained metadata policy before they are stored. No raw config AST, process environment snapshot, secret-bearing context or entire project-details map is retained with a ready capture.

Currentness and compile capture

  1. The parent reserves the real active worker/attempt slot before discovery, config resolution or any new owned capture copy. A zero local SDK metadata budget is not evidence of that host reservation.
  2. Resolve actual membership, project directory and output binding. Keep the attempt bound to the original authenticated provider/session/source and owner connection.
  3. Call the existing bounded capture_compiled path with that held output directory and validated compiler module. It opens the real shared compile lock before record/descriptors/originals, validates the record/module/declaration, and retains the original inventory under its existing limits. It does not yet produce a checked source header or semantic projection. No config lookup or guest invocation needs to run while that lock is held.
  4. After capture, perform a fresh actual membership and trusted-host output resolution. Compare provider/source ownership, provider root, project/output directory identities, compiler module and original output-grant category. Changed or inaccessible binding, revoked source, missing membership, cancellation or a disconnected owner refuses publication and drops retained state.
  5. Release only through the real attempt owner. A timed-out or cancelled waiter does not free an active blocking worker's permit before it settles. A late worker cannot publish to a retired attempt or close another connection's ready capture.

Proposed currentness meaning. The check establishes that the captured model still belongs to the actual selected output binding at the fresh observation. It does not claim that every unrelated configuration byte or OS environment entry stayed unchanged. An edit that leaves the same actual source/project/output/module/grant binding unchanged need not invalidate an immutable captured model.

The compile lock gives consistency among cooperating writers while original bytes and record binding are captured. If a later compile finishes before publication, the retained capture still identifies its exact older record/inventory; it is not silently relabeled as the latest compile. This contract does not add a latest-compile promise or require rereading the full inventory after the lock is released. If the existing reviewed wire contract already requires a stronger exact record-currentness check, retain that requirement through the existing capture owner; do not infer it from the fresh config lookup.

These are observed checks, not an atomic filesystem/config/environment transaction or a claim that the compiler used today's configuration. Noncooperating writers and change-away/change-back races remain outside the advisory lock's guarantee. Root must review this precise currentness meaning before implementation; retaining a digest of all host config inputs would be a stronger optional contract.

Bounds and the trust boundary

Still pending before profile advertisement: checked source-header evidence from the frozen primary, a separately labeled semantic projection from that same frozen original inventory, and before-growth model codec/decode/assembly/output integration across all required formats and layouts. Do not pair capture with an unrelated v1 open or reread mutable live sources to produce these results. The prospective projection-unavailable case remains a requirement, not evidence that the existing capture core implements projection.

All original model-profile guarantees remain. Connected original source supports its full 64 MiB per-file and aggregate budget, separately from 16 MiB ordinary local imports. Keep the reviewed inventory/path/metadata/framing/slot limits, actual source/projection retained-byte credits, before-growth model decode/assembly/output checks, authenticated connection ownership and cancellation cleanup. TOML configuration is not model YAML, and trusted config parsing does not satisfy or replace bounded JSON/YAML/Ion model codecs.

Workspace discovery retains its existing confined traversal, alias, payload and guest protocol bounds. Its host worker reservation precedes request-time capture/invocation. The new output witness gets a small checked retained-evidence reservation for actual keys, paths and handles; no second unmetered retained pool or all-project detail inventory is added.

The genuine ConfigContext and config parser intermediates are temporary trusted host computation, using the current loader's costs and semantics. This proposal does not claim pre-allocation OS snapshot limits, cancellation inside TOML, a universal config AST ledger, per-clone provenance bounds, matcher CPU bounds or RSS equality. A blocked config operation keeps its real worker permit until it ends. These limitations must be documented in the implementation receipt. If the product threat model treats host configuration itself as hostile input requiring those guarantees, the earlier hardening work becomes a separately approved prerequisite.

Numerical production policy is not introduced here. Existing model/discovery limits are preserved; exact additional retained-witness limits require review before the witness is copied. Refusal must name actual authority, capacity, cancellation or lookup failure. Incomplete code cannot masquerade as a legitimately unavailable capability.

<h1>Trusted host output binding for model originals</h1>
<p class="meta">morphir-etg2.22.1 · 19 October 2026 · smaller proposal v2 for review · no implementation authorized</p>

<section id="scope"><h2>The contract we need</h2>
<p>The connected model-originals owner must open the output that the existing host compiler policy selects for the actual project. It must preserve the provider's directory authority, the real compiler module and the original explicit output overrides. That requires the existing Current resolver, not portable discovery's filtered configuration sidecars.</p>
<p>This proposal reuses the actual SDK configuration loader as a trusted host service. It does not promise a new limit inside every config parser, OS environment snapshot, merge clone or member-pattern step. Model-source, guest, framing, inventory, decode/projection and retained-owner limits remain fully required.</p>
<p class="note">The earlier full-config proposal and its 53 scenarios remain immutable optional-hardening history. This is a new review proposal. It does not close .22, .22.1 or .22.2, advertise unfinished capability support or change any frozen protocol.</p>
<ul><li><label><input type="checkbox" checked disabled> Scope audit distinguishes original model requirements from added whole-host-config hardening.</label></li><li><label><input type="checkbox" disabled> Actual host-issued resolver and parent integration implemented and reviewed.</label></li><li><label><input type="checkbox" disabled> Independent cases run through real native/installed providers and current model owners.</label></li></ul>
</section>
<section id="authority"><h2>An explicit trusted host resolver</h2>
<p>Introduce a parent-private <code>TrustedHostOutputLookup</code> only at the CLI startup/provider registration boundary. The issuer must receive the actual stored provider directory and its verified absolute label, original host <code>ConfigLoadOptions</code>, original <code>OutOverrides</code> and an explicit <code>AmbientAuthority</code> from trusted CLI code. It is not deserializable and exposes no arbitrary-path, config-file, module or environment setter.</p>
<p>This grant deliberately authorizes the existing host configuration lookup policy, including its real ancestor, system, global, explicit-user, alias and Process environment behavior. It does not authorize a guest or HTTP caller to choose those locations. Its broad host lookup is an explicit trust decision, not a claim that the provider-root directory alone confines ancestor reads. The actual old ambient loader cannot serve as authority merely because a caller knows a matching string.</p>
<p>Issue the grant after the provider has its actual <code>workspace_dir</code>, stored root label and final original output overrides, before registering the additive model-originals service. Verify root-label identity against the held directory. Store it with that provider/session/source owner. Each resolve checks the same held root against the stored label again. Do not create a grant from fields in a capture request or from portable <code>canonical_root</code> metadata.</p>
<p>Before lookup, validate the requested source against the provider's stored source, perform actual native or installed discovery and locate the selected key in that actual response. Validate the returned relative path and open the project through the original held provider directory using the existing nofollow helper. Verify that the host-derived absolute project label still identifies that opened directory before and after resolution. Replacement or a changed label refuses. The host never hands that identity-check handle to a guest as new read authority.</p>
<p>The grant's only operation accepts this validated selected project and returns the actual output binding. Actual guest membership remains a parent responsibility. A source/project key identifies a request; neither it nor a page revision is a filesystem permission.</p>

<section id="policy"><h2>Keep the actual Current policy</h2>
<p>Use <code>discover_config_at</code> on the genuine selected project label. If it returns a primary, call <code>load_config_context_with</code> with the provider's original options and <code>ProjectSelection::Current</code>. This constructs a genuine <code>ConfigContext</code> through the existing loader and merged <code>LayerStack</code>. Do not construct a lookalike context, merge layers again or extract output settings from portable details.</p>

No fixed-depth substitute or guessed child workspace.</td></tr><tr><td>Layers</td><td>Defaults, system, global, selected root with early typed decode, actual selected member, root/member or explicit user overrides, environment and final typed decode. Preserve all existing source selection modes, first errors, provenance, per-layer ir.mode normalization and member out_dir removal.</td></tr><tr><td>Current selection</td><td>Do not expand default members or siblings. Actual compiler module can be packages/orders when portable project relativePath is dot.</td></tr><tr><td>Formats</td><td>Existing TOML, strict configuration YAML and legacy JSON semantics. Known-field JSON duplicate errors and ignored unknowns remain unchanged. This is not a new literal-JSON policy.</td></tr><tr><td>Environment and cwd</td><td>Use existing Process/Explicit/Skip semantics. Original output-env value stays startup-captured by OutOverrides. <p>Native and installed discovery keep their existing capability-rooted request construction. For installed mode, send that exact request to the real guest and use the actual guest response as membership. Do not consume <code>into_typed_details</code> solely to obtain every project's config: the host Current loader supplies the selected host output facts, and the all-project sidecar copy is unnecessary. These are two deliberate policies, portable membership and trusted host compiler-output selection. Their configurations are not claimed to be the same immutable config snapshot.</p>
</section>
<section id="binding"><h2>Bind the real selected output</h2>
<p>Pass the genuine optional context to existing <code>OutContext::resolve</code>. It already delegates to the SDK's shared output and module rules. Preserve the v1 special base: no context and no explicit override means the selected project directory; otherwise use the genuine attempt cwd. Preserve flag, original nonempty output-env, config workspace.out_dir and default precedence.</p>
<p>Open an implicit output only through the provider-owned directory after the same confinement check used by v1. An ancestor workspace configuration may select an output outside that grant; that remains a refusal. An explicit original flag or original nonempty output-env may authorize its additional directory using trusted host ambient authority. A newly received request value, a config path, a diagnostic label or a guest response cannot become an explicit override.</p>
<pre><code class="language-moonbit">// Proposed parent-private ownership, not a new wire schema.
TrustedHostOutputLookup  // actual provider Dir + verified label + host intent
SelectedProject         // actual membership + opened project Dir identity
ResolvedProjectSource   // existing owned output Dir + SelectedModule
BindingWitness = {
  actual_provider_and_source,
  provider_root_identity,
  project_directory_identity,
  output_directory_identity,
  compiler_module,
  original_output_grant_kind
}</code></pre>
<p>Reuse the parent <code>ResolvedProjectSource</code> and <code>SelectedModule</code> domains rather than introduce another output/module model. Extend its private authority comparison only where needed for root/source/grant ownership. The witness is not supplied by the client or serialized as a permission. Compact path/key copies and retained handles must fit the existing host's retained metadata policy before they are stored. No raw config AST, process environment snapshot, secret-bearing context or entire project-details map is retained with a ready capture.</p>
</section>
<section id="freshness"><h2>Currentness and compile capture</h2>
<ol><li>The parent reserves the real active worker/attempt slot before discovery, config resolution or any new owned capture copy. A zero local SDK metadata budget is not evidence of that host reservation.</li><li>Resolve actual membership, project directory and output binding. Keep the attempt bound to the original authenticated provider/session/source and owner connection.</li><li>Call the existing bounded <code>capture_compiled</code> path with that held output directory and validated compiler module. It opens the real shared compile lock before record/descriptors/originals, validates the record/module/declaration, and retains the original inventory under its existing limits. It does not yet produce a checked source header or semantic projection. No config lookup or guest invocation needs to run while that lock is held.</li><li>After capture, perform a fresh actual membership and trusted-host output resolution. Compare provider/source ownership, provider root, project/output directory identities, compiler module and original output-grant category. Changed or inaccessible binding, revoked source, missing membership, cancellation or a disconnected owner refuses publication and drops retained state.</li><li>Release only through the real attempt owner. A timed-out or cancelled waiter does not free an active blocking worker's permit before it settles. A late worker cannot publish to a retired attempt or close another connection's ready capture.</li></ol>
<p><strong>Proposed currentness meaning.</strong> The check establishes that the captured model still belongs to the actual selected output binding at the fresh observation. It does not claim that every unrelated configuration byte or OS environment entry stayed unchanged. An edit that leaves the same actual source/project/output/module/grant binding unchanged need not invalidate an immutable captured model.</p>
<p>The compile lock gives consistency among cooperating writers while original bytes and record binding are captured. If a later compile finishes before publication, the retained capture still identifies its exact older record/inventory; it is not silently relabeled as the latest compile. This contract does not add a latest-compile promise or require rereading the full inventory after the lock is released. If the existing reviewed wire contract already requires a stronger exact record-currentness check, retain that requirement through the existing capture owner; do not infer it from the fresh config lookup.</p>
<p>These are observed checks, not an atomic filesystem/config/environment transaction or a claim that the compiler used today's configuration. Noncooperating writers and change-away/change-back races remain outside the advisory lock's guarantee. Root must review this precise currentness meaning before implementation; retaining a digest of all host config inputs would be a stronger optional contract.</p>
</section>
<section id="limits"><h2>Bounds and the trust boundary</h2>
<p class="note">Still pending before profile advertisement: checked source-header evidence from the frozen primary, a separately labeled semantic projection from that same frozen original inventory, and before-growth model codec/decode/assembly/output integration across all required formats and layouts. Do not pair capture with an unrelated v1 open or reread mutable live sources to produce these results. The prospective projection-unavailable case remains a requirement, not evidence that the existing capture core implements projection.</p>
<p>All original model-profile guarantees remain. Connected original source supports its full 64 MiB per-file and aggregate budget, separately from 16 MiB ordinary local imports. Keep the reviewed inventory/path/metadata/framing/slot limits, actual source/projection retained-byte credits, before-growth model decode/assembly/output checks, authenticated connection ownership and cancellation cleanup. TOML configuration is not model YAML, and trusted config parsing does not satisfy or replace bounded JSON/YAML/Ion model codecs.</p>
<p>Workspace discovery retains its existing confined traversal, alias, payload and guest protocol bounds. Its host worker reservation precedes request-time capture/invocation. The new output witness gets a small checked retained-evidence reservation for actual keys, paths and handles; no second unmetered retained pool or all-project detail inventory is added.</p>
<p>The genuine <code>ConfigContext</code> and config parser intermediates are temporary trusted host computation, using the current loader's costs and semantics. This proposal does not claim pre-allocation OS snapshot limits, cancellation inside TOML, a universal config AST ledger, per-clone provenance bounds, matcher CPU bounds or RSS equality. A blocked config operation keeps its real worker permit until it ends. These limitations must be documented in the implementation receipt. If the product threat model treats host configuration itself as hostile input requiring those guarantees, the earlier hardening work becomes a separately approved prerequisite.</p>
<p>Numerical production policy is not introduced here. Existing model/discovery limits are preserved; exact additional retained-witness limits require review before the witness is copied. Refusal must name actual authority, capacity, cancellation or lookup failure. Incomplete code cannot masquerade as a legitimately unavailable capability.</p>
</section>

<section id="scope"><h2>The contract we need</h2>
<p>The connected model-originals owner must open the output that the existing host compiler policy selects for the actual project. It must preserve the provider's directory authority, the real compiler module and the original explicit output overrides. That requires the existing Current resolver, not portable discovery's filtered configuration sidecars.</p>
<p>This proposal reuses the actual SDK configuration loader as a trusted host service. It does not promise a new limit inside every config parser, OS environment snapshot, merge clone or member-pattern step. Model-source, guest, framing, inventory, decode/projection and retained-owner limits remain fully required.</p>
<p class="note">The earlier full-config proposal and its 53 scenarios remain immutable optional-hardening history. This is a new review proposal. It does not close .22, .22.1 or .22.2, advertise unfinished capability support or change any frozen protocol.</p>
<ul><li><label><input type="checkbox" checked disabled> Scope audit distinguishes original model requirements from added whole-host-config hardening.</label></li><li><label><input type="checkbox" disabled> Actual host-issued resolver and parent integration implemented and reviewed.</label></li><li><label><input type="checkbox" disabled> Independent cases run through real native/installed providers and current model owners.</label></li></ul>
</section>
<section id="authority"><h2>An explicit trusted host resolver</h2>
<p>Introduce a parent-private <code>TrustedHostOutputLookup</code> only at the CLI startup/provider registration boundary. The issuer must receive the actual stored provider directory and its verified absolute label, original host <code>ConfigLoadOptions</code>, original <code>OutOverrides</code> and an explicit <code>AmbientAuthority</code> from trusted CLI code. It is not deserializable and exposes no arbitrary-path, config-file, module or environment setter.</p>
<p>This grant deliberately authorizes the existing host configuration lookup policy, including its real ancestor, system, global, explicit-user, alias and Process environment behavior. It does not authorize a guest or HTTP caller to choose those locations. Its broad host lookup is an explicit trust decision, not a claim that the provider-root directory alone confines ancestor reads. The actual old ambient loader cannot serve as authority merely because a caller knows a matching string.</p>
<p>Issue the grant after the provider has its actual <code>workspace_dir</code>, stored root label and final original output overrides, before registering the additive model-originals service. Verify root-label identity against the held directory. Store it with that provider/session/source owner. Each resolve checks the same held root against the stored label again. Do not create a grant from fields in a capture request or from portable <code>canonical_root</code> metadata.</p>
<p>Before lookup, validate the requested source against the provider's stored source, perform actual native or installed discovery and locate the selected key in that actual response. Validate the returned relative path and open the project through the original held provider directory using the existing nofollow helper. Verify that the host-derived absolute project label still identifies that opened directory before and after resolution. Replacement or a changed label refuses. The host never hands that identity-check handle to a guest as new read authority.</p>
<p>The grant's only operation accepts this validated selected project and returns the actual output binding. Actual guest membership remains a parent responsibility. A source/project key identifies a request; neither it nor a page revision is a filesystem permission.</p>

<section id="policy"><h2>Keep the actual Current policy</h2>
<p>Use <code>discover_config_at</code> on the genuine selected project label. This constructs a genuine <code>ConfigContext</code> through the existing loader and merged <code>LayerStack</code>. Do not construct a lookalike context, merge layers again or extract output settings from portable details.</p>

<section id="binding"><h2>Bind the real selected output</h2>
<p>Pass the genuine optional context to existing <code>OutContext::resolve</code>. It already delegates to the SDK's shared output and module rules.
