Preserve flag, original nonempty output-env, config workspace.out_dir and default precedence.</p>
<p>Open an implicit output only through the provider-owned directory after the same confinement check used by v1. An ancestor workspace configuration may select an output outside that grant; that remains a refusal. An explicit original flag or original nonempty output-env may authorize its additional directory using trusted host ambient authority. A newly received request value, a config path, a diagnostic label or a guest response cannot become an explicit override.</p>
<pre><code class="language-moonbit">// Proposed parent-private ownership, not a new wire schema.

  actual_provider_and_source,
  provider_root_identity,
  project_directory_identity,
  output_directory_identity,
  compiler_module,
  original_output_grant_kind
}</code></pre>
<p>Reuse the parent <code>ResolvedProjectSource</code> and <code>SelectedModule</code> domains rather than introduce another output/module model. Extend its private authority comparison only where needed for root/source/grant ownership. The witness is not supplied by the client or serialized as a permission. Compact path/key copies and retained handles must fit the existing host's retained metadata policy before they are stored. No raw config AST, process environment snapshot, secret-bearing context or entire project-details map is retained with a ready capture.</p>

<section id="freshness"><h2>Currentness and compile capture</h2>
<ol><li>The parent reserves the real active worker/attempt slot before discovery, config resolution or any new owned capture copy. No config lookup or guest invocation needs to run while that lock is held.</li><li>After capture, perform a fresh actual membership and trusted-host output resolution. Compare provider/source ownership, provider root, project/output directory identities, compiler module and original output-grant category. Changed or inaccessible binding, revoked source, missing membership, cancellation or a disconnected owner refuses publication and drops retained state.</li><li>Release only through the real attempt owner. A timed-out or cancelled waiter does not free an active blocking worker's permit before it settles. A late worker cannot publish to a retired attempt or close another connection's ready capture.</li></ol>
<p><strong>Proposed currentness meaning.</strong> The check establishes that the captured model still belongs to the actual selected output binding at the fresh observation. It does not claim that every unrelated configuration byte or OS environment entry stayed unchanged. An edit that leaves the same actual source/project/output/module/grant binding unchanged need not invalidate an immutable captured model.</p>
<p>The compile lock gives consistency among cooperating writers while original bytes and record binding are captured. If a later compile finishes before publication, the retained capture still identifies its exact older record/inventory; it is not silently relabeled as the latest compile. This contract does not add a latest-compile promise or require rereading the full inventory after the lock is released. If the existing reviewed wire contract already requires a stronger exact record-currentness check, retain that requirement through the existing capture owner; do not infer it from the fresh config lookup.</p>
<p>These are observed checks, not an atomic filesystem/config/environment transaction or a claim that the compiler used today's configuration. Noncooperating writers and change-away/change-back races remain outside the advisory lock's guarantee. Root must review this precise currentness meaning before implementation; retaining a digest of all host config inputs would be a stronger optional contract.</p>
</section>
<section id="limits"><h2>Bounds and the trust boundary</h2>
<p>All original model-profile guarantees remain. Connected original source supports its full 64 MiB per-file and aggregate budget, separately from 16 MiB ordinary local imports. Keep the reviewed inventory/path/metadata/framing/slot limits, actual source/projection retained-byte credits, before-growth model decode/assembly/output checks, authenticated connection ownership and cancellation cleanup. TOML configuration is not model YAML, and trusted config parsing does not satisfy or replace bounded JSON/YAML/Ion model codecs.</p>
<p>Workspace discovery retains its existing confined traversal, alias, payload and guest protocol bounds. Its host worker reservation precedes request-time capture/invocation. The new output witness gets a small checked retained-evidence reservation for actual keys, paths and handles; no second unmetered retained pool or all-project detail inventory is added.</p>
<p>The genuine <code>ConfigContext</code> and config parser intermediates are temporary trusted host computation, using the current loader's costs and semantics. This proposal does not claim pre-allocation OS snapshot limits, cancellation inside TOML, a universal config AST ledger, per-clone provenance bounds, matcher CPU bounds or RSS equality. A blocked config operation keeps its real worker permit until it ends. These limitations must be documented in the implementation receipt. If the product threat model treats host configuration itself as hostile input requiring those guarantees, the earlier hardening work becomes a separately approved prerequisite.</p>
<p>Numerical production policy is not introduced here. Existing model/discovery limits are preserved; exact additional retained-witness limits require review before the witness is copied. Refusal must name actual authority, capacity, cancellation or lookup failure. Incomplete code cannot masquerade as a legitimately unavailable capability.</p>
</section>

What this proposal would implement

The next working caller should capture the complete configuration evidence needed for ProjectSelection::Current, then run the existing layer policy over those frozen inputs. The private two-ancestor metadata tracer is a tested starting point for directory binding. It does not establish a complete lookup, raw bytes, a configuration value, an output location or final currentness.

Who can issue the complete lookup grant

A trusted host startup producer receives the actual CLI-supplied provider directory, original host load options, stabilized startup labels and original output overrides. It creates a private StartupCurrentLookup before provider registration. Clients cannot create or widen it with project IDs, paths, source labels or JSON fields. The SDK API should require actual held directory capabilities and an explicit host-only startup authority argument, with private fields and validating construction.

  1. Seal the actual provider directory identity and its absolute lexical label. Walk the entire trusted-startup ancestor chain through Dir::open_parent_dir using the explicit startup ambient-authority token, then retain each resulting held capability up to the platform root. This issuance operation may acquire parents; no request-time adapter exposes it. Verify label/identity correspondence and parent progress, including platform root termination, before accepting the chain. Retain ordered roots and identities. Bound every handle, label and component before retention. Reaching a configured issuance limit refuses scope construction; it never returns a shortened successful chain. A two-level or fixed-depth trace cannot satisfy this step.
  2. Keep ancestor handles private behind exact supported candidate operations. They cannot enumerate a directory, return arbitrary files, authorize output opening or enter a guest request. For a selected descendant, validate the actual provider membership and walk ordinary components from the held provider root. Its ancestors inside that grant and the sealed chain above the provider together form the complete lexical search.
  3. Seal system/global/explicit source locations using the existing native candidate builders and the original SourceSelection roles. Capture the lookup-location inputs, such as HOME, XDG, MORPHIR_HOME and PROGRAMDATA, separately from ordinary configuration environment values. Stabilize relative explicit source paths using the genuine host cwd used for issuance; a later location/cwd change that would choose a different source is ScopeChanged, not authority to rebase the source from a request. Historical path APIs remain unchanged. Skip creates no file-read grant. Explicit grants only the selected file through its held parent and leaf binding.
  4. For adjacent user sources, the selected primary layout chooses the existing two candidate names. The scope permits those exact operations through the selected source directory. No arbitrary adjacent file or caller-provided suffix is allowed.
  5. Present directories, missing layout components and missing candidate slots all need a closed binding. Missing records an exact granted location; it grants no write authority and does not prove permanent absence. Its later appearance must affect a fresh capture. Open new regular components only inside an already held directory grant, with nofollow checks. Replaced sealed components refuse. New aliases to an unsealed external target require a new trusted scope.

Existing config-file or layout aliases require a positive bounded alias binding. Record the link identity/text and actual target capability at trusted issuance, charge each hop and retained target, and recheck before use. Confined new aliases may resolve only within the original held grant. Out-of-grant targets cannot be discovered from a client request. The current metadata tracer rejects all aliases and is therefore incomplete for legacy config lookup. Extending it must preserve ordinary supported aliases, or explicitly refuse changed authority. Source alias policy must not be confused with the parent v1 project-directory opener, which already refuses project-directory symlinks. Sources S3, S4, S17, S19.

Review decision needed. Approve this exact startup alias-target binding rule, including refusal of a newly introduced external alias until trusted scope refresh. It preserves stable v1 configurations without turning a runtime label into ambient read authority. No alias implementation is proposed as already complete.

The actual request-time capture

The parent first reserves the real worker, attempt and retained-byte capacity. Failure makes no SDK lookup or guest call. The SDK receives its own validated local budget; a zero local budget is not a host permit. After actual guest discovery selects the project, the source driver validates project identity and walks the selected path through the original provider capability.

Probe the six modern selected-directory primary slots first. Exactly one regular target selects that source; two are the existing ambiguity error. Probe legacy morphir.json only when no modern primary exists. If the selected directory has no primary, return the existing no-context output case with module empty. Do not probe attempt-time ancestors, system/global sources or environment configuration for that path. Startup scope issuance is a distinct earlier operation.

Once a primary exists, preserve the actual loader order: defaults, system, global, nearest matching raw ancestor, root layer and early root decode, the selected member if any, root/member user layers, environment, final typed decode and context facts. Capture lazily in that order so ordinary first errors remain meaningful. Do not read every optional source eagerly for convenience. Modern conflict checks inspect all modern candidate slots, but do not read all contents.

For an ancestor, an ordinary ambiguity, access/read error, parse error, non-workspace or member nonmatch still permits the legacy search to continue. A typed budget, ungranted alias, changed root/component, cancellation or capture-race failure stops the attempt. These failures cannot become a harmless nonmatch. Record skipped invalid ancestors because a later valid edit can change the winner. No source above the selected winning ancestor is examined on that attempt; a new nearer workspace is detected from the complete considered prefix on revalidation.

  1. Before an effect, reserve its I/O unit and all retained handle/label/observation growth. Inspect only fixed candidate operations. A directory or other nonregular object is evidence of a non-file, not readable bytes.
  2. Open a regular candidate from the held parent with nofollow and nonblocking semantics where available. Inspect the actual opened handle, compare the bound component/leaf identity and require a regular file. A FIFO or symlink swap must not block or reach a new target. The parent already uses cap_fs_ext for such opens; the SDK needs a reviewed additive dependency/API seam or equivalent platform proof, not an unchecked ambient File::open.
  3. Read through that held file into a separately reserved scratch buffer. Before extending the owned raw buffer, reserve exact logical retained bytes and destination growth. Choose a finite read allowance q from the remaining per-file allowance, total allowance and validated scratch quantum. Reserve q read-work units and one read operation before calling read into that scratch slice. Even a short read or EOF consumes the reserved read allowance; work is never refunded. After m bytes return, reserve m destination-copy units and m hash-work units before append and hash update. Metadata length is a hint, never authority to skip the EOF check. A file that grows past allowance refuses without retaining the excess byte.
  4. At the inclusive per-file or total retained limit, reserve one bounded excess-probe byte and one read operation. EOF permits the exact limit. A returned byte yields a typed raw-byte limit error, not a truncated successful file. Keep this probe accounting separate from retained bytes. I/O work still needs finite credit if a file returns many short reads.
  5. Hash the exact captured bytes, then recheck opened-file metadata and path/component bindings. Length or observed identity/change mismatches refuse. Stable-size concurrent overwrite cannot be proven absent from metadata alone. The capture is one immutable byte sequence; later bounded digest recapture checks the selection again. No claim of an atomic filesystem snapshot is made.

Own each raw buffer once and move it into the frozen snapshot. Reserve a full bounded UTF-8 validation scan before borrowing validated UTF-8 from it; do not call read_to_string or copy it into a second complete string. Share identical physical captures only when identity and digest really agree. Source occurrences still retain their declaring lexical path, role and sequence, so physical deduplication cannot change provenance or first-error order. Reuse the same frozen winner bytes for ancestor membership and the final root layer, rather than reopen mutable source between them. Root-label identity checks inspect only the startup-sealed labels for identity comparison and are charged before opening. Those ambient metadata handles never become content-read or new ancestor authority.

Legacy JSON must retain its own semantics

parse_config decodes morphir.json directly into LegacyProjectConfig and then normalizes. Known fields are name, sourceDirectory, exposedModules, dependencies and localDependencies. Required fields and known duplicates use derived Serde errors. Unknown fields are ignored, including repeated unknown members. Normalization retains the existing defaults and deliberately drops localDependencies; it does not add an output directory. Sources S7, S8.

The model-originals literal JSON reader is useful infrastructure, but using it as Value then from_value here would erase known duplicate fields, retain previously ignored fields and risk serde-private marker transformations at a second decode. This new config path has no authorization to change those semantics.

A generic counting deserialize_any preflight is also insufficient. Serde's actual IgnoredAny uses ignore_value, which lexically skips numbers without numeric conversion and stores a separate nesting scratch stack. A large exponent in an ignored field can therefore differ from generic Value decoding. Ignored nesting must still be bounded under the new policy, but a scalar conversion error cannot silently replace acceptance. Source S16.

Recommended seam: a bounded wrapper around the actual deserializer and visitors, preserving the existing derived LegacyProjectConfig semantic consumer. Intercept known owned strings/arrays/maps before copies. Delegate numeric/string syntax and ordinary errors to Serde. For deserialize_ignored_any, use a separately reviewed count/skip facility that preserves the actual lexical skip semantics and checks depth/work before scratch growth. Reuse the existing forward delimiter infrastructure only if extended with a non-materializing skip mode, borrowed RawValue scalar handling and string-discard behavior, all tested against Serde. No new JSON lexer or model policy is needed.

Feasibility boundary. The public current Serde API has no nested budget callbacks inside ignore_value. A typed seed alone cannot prove that hidden scratch path bounded. Either review a small reusable skip extension with explicit semantic regressions, or pre-reserve a proven source-derived upper bound for the unchanged skip scratch/work and enforce any separately required depth policy before entering it. The latter is only valid with a complete bound proof and cannot claim per-value hard cancellation. This choice is an implementation prerequisite, not a completed parser.

  1. Parent holds the reserved attempt through actual source capture, discovery and output resolution. Installed mode submits the same captured discovery request to the real guest; guest membership remains authoritative. Native typed details cannot replace an installed guest's project list.
  2. Before publishing, reacquire through the same fixed scope and recapture the considered candidate prefix, missing slots, selected alias/component identities, raw digests and configuration environment facts. Recompute selection and output facts with the same bounded reducer. A new nearer workspace, changed ambiguity, changed formerly invalid ancestor, removed user override or changed output facts is stale.
  3. Compare actual selected project-directory identity, actual output-directory identity, actual module and the structured config fingerprint. Fingerprint includes role/selection/location inputs, source identities/content or closed missing/invalid evidence, environment policy and exact relevant captured entries, plus output overrides and supported parser policy. Preserve the captured ordering of equal normalized environment paths, whose first-entry behavior is part of the actual environment reducer. Do not fingerprint an independently reordered equivalent-looking map. Use explicit canonical encoding, not ambiguous concatenation or mutable labels as identity.
  4. Capture compile record and model-original inventory under the actual compiler lock using the verified output authority and module. Recheck selection/config/output evidence at the publication boundary while retention and connection ownership remain valid. A changed record/inventory/currentness, revoked scope or cancellation refuses and cleans up. No binding or token is published early.

Two bounded equal checks establish a stated observation interval, not a global transaction or permanent freshness. Config files and environment are not protected by the compiler lock; ABA and concurrent in-place changes need an explicit documented limit. Do not claim that an existing compile used the current configuration unless a genuine compiler record proves it. Source identity, config fingerprint, document revision, capture token and execution identity remain different domain facts.

<section id="review"><h2>What this proposal would implement</h2>
<p>The next working caller should capture the complete configuration evidence needed for <code>ProjectSelection::Current</code>, then run the existing layer policy over those frozen inputs. The private two-ancestor metadata tracer is a tested starting point for directory binding. It does not establish a complete lookup, raw bytes, a configuration value, an output location or final currentness.</p>
<p class="note">Design for review, 19 October 2026. No new source implementation, public API, provider registration or numerical production limit is authorized by this document. Full support still includes TOML, strict configuration YAML, legacy JSON, system/global/user sources, process environment, actual Current membership, merge/provenance, output authority and final revalidation.</p>
<p>Recommended implementation route: one capability-backed source driver feeding one shared Current orchestration and the existing <code>LayerStack</code>. Add fallible checks inside the real parser, matcher and merge operations. A second reducer over already-filtered portable discovery details would lose host output facts and repeat policy. Sources S1–S10 show why.</p>
<ul><li><input type="checkbox" checked disabled> Existing pure stages and private metadata checkpoint reviewed locally.</li><li><input type="checkbox" checked disabled> Source-authored proposal and separate future acceptance cases prepared without reading adapter outputs.</li><li><input type="checkbox" disabled> Full grant, raw capture and real reducer caller implemented.</li><li><input type="checkbox" disabled> Parser/environment prerequisites resolved and full pipeline qualified on actual hosts.</li></ul>
</section>
<section id="authority"><h2>Who can issue the complete lookup grant</h2>
<p>A trusted host startup producer receives the actual CLI-supplied provider directory, original host load options, stabilized startup labels and original output overrides. It creates a private <code>StartupCurrentLookup</code> before provider registration. Clients cannot create or widen it with project IDs, paths, source labels or JSON fields. The SDK API should require actual held directory capabilities and an explicit host-only startup authority argument, with private fields and validating construction.</p>

<ol><li>Seal the actual provider directory identity and its absolute lexical label. Walk the entire trusted-startup ancestor chain through <code>Dir::open_parent_dir</code> using the explicit startup ambient-authority token, then retain each resulting held capability up to the platform root. This issuance operation may acquire parents; no request-time adapter exposes it. Verify label/identity correspondence and parent progress, including platform root termination, before accepting the chain. Retain ordered roots and identities. Bound every handle, label and component before retention. Reaching a configured issuance limit refuses scope construction; it never returns a shortened successful chain. A two-level or fixed-depth trace cannot satisfy this step.</li>
<li>Keep ancestor handles private behind exact supported candidate operations. They cannot enumerate a directory, return arbitrary files, authorize output opening or enter a guest request. For a selected descendant, validate the actual provider membership and walk ordinary components from the held provider root. Its ancestors inside that grant and the sealed chain above the provider together form the complete lexical search.</li>
<li>Seal system/global/explicit source locations using the existing native candidate builders and the original <code>SourceSelection</code> roles. Capture the lookup-location inputs, such as HOME, XDG, MORPHIR_HOME and PROGRAMDATA, separately from ordinary configuration environment values. Stabilize relative explicit source paths using the genuine host cwd used for issuance; a later location/cwd change that would choose a different source is ScopeChanged, not authority to rebase the source from a request. Historical path APIs remain unchanged. <code>Skip</code> creates no file-read grant. <code>Explicit</code> grants only the selected file through its held parent and leaf binding.</li>
<li>For adjacent user sources, the selected primary layout chooses the existing two candidate names. The scope permits those exact operations through the selected source directory. No arbitrary adjacent file or caller-provided suffix is allowed.</li>
<li>Present directories, missing layout components and missing candidate slots all need a closed binding. New aliases to an unsealed external target require a new trusted scope.</li></ol>
<p>Existing config-file or layout aliases require a positive bounded alias binding. Record the link identity/text and actual target capability at trusted issuance, charge each hop and retained target, and recheck before use. Confined new aliases may resolve only within the original held grant. Out-of-grant targets cannot be discovered from a client request. The current metadata tracer rejects all aliases and is therefore incomplete for legacy config lookup. Extending it must preserve ordinary supported aliases, or explicitly refuse changed authority. Source alias policy must not be confused with the parent v1 project-directory opener, which already refuses project-directory symlinks. Sources S3, S4, S17, S19.</p>
<p><strong>Review decision needed.</strong> Approve this exact startup alias-target binding rule, including refusal of a newly introduced external alias until trusted scope refresh. It preserves stable v1 configurations without turning a runtime label into ambient read authority. No alias implementation is proposed as already complete.</p>

<section id="capture"><h2>The actual request-time capture</h2>
<p>The parent first reserves the real worker, attempt and retained-byte capacity. Failure makes no SDK lookup or guest call. The SDK receives its own validated local budget; a zero local budget is not a host permit. After actual guest discovery selects the project, the source driver validates project identity and walks the selected path through the original provider capability.</p>
<p>Probe the six modern selected-directory primary slots first. Exactly one regular target selects that source; two are the existing ambiguity error. Probe legacy <code>morphir.json</code> only when no modern primary exists. If the selected directory has no primary, return the existing no-context output case with module empty. Do not probe attempt-time ancestors, system/global sources or environment configuration for that path. Startup scope issuance is a distinct earlier operation.</p>
<p>Once a primary exists, preserve the actual loader order: defaults, system, global, nearest matching raw ancestor, root layer and early root decode, the selected member if any, root/member user layers, environment, final typed decode and context facts. Capture lazily in that order so ordinary first errors remain meaningful. Do not read every optional source eagerly for convenience. Modern conflict checks inspect all modern candidate slots, but do not read all contents.</p>
<p>For an ancestor, an ordinary ambiguity, access/read error, parse error, non-workspace or member nonmatch still permits the legacy search to continue. A typed budget, ungranted alias, changed root/component, cancellation or capture-race failure stops the attempt. These failures cannot become a harmless nonmatch. Record skipped invalid ancestors because a later valid edit can change the winner. No source above the selected winning ancestor is examined on that attempt; a new nearer workspace is detected from the complete considered prefix on revalidation.</p>
<ol><li>Before an effect, reserve its I/O unit and all retained handle/label/observation growth. Inspect only fixed candidate operations. A directory or other nonregular object is evidence of a non-file, not readable bytes.</li><li>Open a regular candidate from the held parent with nofollow and nonblocking semantics where available. Inspect the actual opened handle, compare the bound component/leaf identity and require a regular file. A FIFO or symlink swap must not block or reach a new target. The parent already uses <code>cap_fs_ext</code> for such opens; the SDK needs a reviewed additive dependency/API seam or equivalent platform proof, not an unchecked ambient <code>File::open</code>.</li><li>Read through that held file into a separately reserved scratch buffer. Before extending the owned raw buffer, reserve exact logical retained bytes and destination growth. Choose a finite read allowance q from the remaining per-file allowance, total allowance and validated scratch quantum. Reserve q read-work units and one read operation before calling read into that scratch slice. Even a short read or EOF consumes the reserved read allowance; work is never refunded. After m bytes return, reserve m destination-copy units and m hash-work units before append and hash update. Metadata length is a hint, never authority to skip the EOF check. A file that grows past allowance refuses without retaining the excess byte.</li><li>At the inclusive per-file or total retained limit, reserve one bounded excess-probe byte and one read operation. EOF permits the exact limit. A returned byte yields a typed raw-byte limit error, not a truncated successful file. Keep this probe accounting separate from retained bytes. I/O work still needs finite credit if a file returns many short reads.</li><li>Hash the exact captured bytes, then recheck opened-file metadata and path/component bindings. Length or observed identity/change mismatches refuse. Stable-size concurrent overwrite cannot be proven absent from metadata alone. The capture is one immutable byte sequence; later bounded digest recapture checks the selection again. No claim of an atomic filesystem snapshot is made.</li></ol>
<p>Own each raw buffer once and move it into the frozen snapshot. Reserve a full bounded UTF-8 validation scan before borrowing validated UTF-8 from it; do not call <code>read_to_string</code> or copy it into a second complete string. Share identical physical captures only when identity and digest really agree. Source occurrences still retain their declaring lexical path, role and sequence, so physical deduplication cannot change provenance or first-error order. Reuse the same frozen winner bytes for ancestor membership and the final root layer, rather than reopen mutable source between them. Root-label identity checks inspect only the startup-sealed labels for identity comparison and are charged before opening. Those ambient metadata handles never become content-read or new ancestor authority.</p>
</section>
<section id="states"><h2>Closed evidence and failure states</h2>
<pre><code class="language-moonbit">// Proposed private domain, not an advertised API.
StartupCurrentLookup   // complete sealed ancestor/source grants
CurrentCapture         // request-local immutable evidence + real ownership
CurrentResolution      // actual Current output facts, never a read grant

CandidateObservation =
  NotConsulted(PolicyReason) | Missing(ParentBinding) |
  NonRegular(ObservedIdentity) | Unavailable(CandidateIoEvidence) |
  Regular(RawConfigSnapshot)
CandidateIoEvidence = { stage: IdentityProbe | Open | Read,
                        kind: std::io::ErrorKind,
                        identity: Observed(ActualIdentity) | NotObserved }
RawConfigSnapshot = { source: ConfigSourceKind, declaring_path,
                      opened_identity, raw_bytes, byte_length, sha256 }
AncestorDecision = Match | NonWorkspace | MemberNonmatch |
                   OrdinaryInvalid(LegacyFailureKind)
CaptureFailure = Budget(Unit) | ScopeChanged | UngrantedTarget |
                 ChangedDuringCapture | Cancelled | RequiredSourceFailure
CurrentCheck = Unchanged | Stale(ChangeReason) | Refused(CaptureFailure)
</code></pre><p><code>NotConsulted</code> reasons include explicitly skipped, legacy fallback shadowed by modern selection, ancestor search gated by missing selected primary and above a known winner. They are not counterfeit <code>Missing</code> observations. Root/alias inaccessibility remains distinct from replacement; ordinary unreadable candidate evidence may be tolerated only where the legacy loader tolerates it. A typed inaccessible outcome records its role and actual error class, not a fake empty file or digest. A dangling candidate alias has explicit absent-target evidence, not a regular-file snapshot. An inaccessible or looping alias retains its actual resolution failure and is ignored only in the same legacy discovery/search positions; a changed sealed binding or ungranted target always refuses. This distinction must be tested separately from ordinary missing slots.</p>
<p>These are proposed private additions around the existing <code>ConfigSourceKind</code>, <code>SourceSelection</code>, <code>EnvSelection</code> and <code>ProjectSelection</code>. Reuse those types rather than publish parallel roles. <code>PresentMetadata</code> remains metadata-only; only a completed read can construct <code>RawConfigSnapshot</code>. No optional digest or placeholder hash stands in for unread content. Cancellation is checked before each closed I/O operation and parser/matcher/merge work step. It drops raw/parsed state and actual permits exactly once after the actual worker settles. A pending blocking regular-file operation is not assumed aborted by cancelling the async waiter; retain its real worker credit until settlement. Finite local work counters are not a filesystem latency guarantee. No replay, retry or widening fallback follows a refusal.</p>
</section>
<section id="accounting"><h2>Every allocation and traversal has a payer</h2>
<p>Validate an explicit generic policy with checked arithmetic. This proposal sets no production numbers and imports no IR limits as config defaults. Zero credit is a meaningful effect-free refusal. Use monotonic work/copy counters and separate live-retention reservations released on actual drop. <section id="json"><h2>Legacy JSON must retain its own semantics</h2>
<p><code>parse_config</code> decodes <code>morphir.json</code> directly into <code>LegacyProjectConfig</code> and then normalizes. Known fields are <code>name</code>, <code>sourceDirectory</code>, <code>exposedModules</code>, <code>dependencies</code> and <code>localDependencies</code>. Required fields and known duplicates use derived Serde errors. Unknown fields are ignored, including repeated unknown members. Normalization retains the existing defaults and deliberately drops <code>localDependencies</code>; it does not add an output directory. Sources S7, S8.</p>
<p>The model-originals literal JSON reader is useful infrastructure, but using it as <code>Value</code> then <code>from_value</code> here would erase known duplicate fields, retain previously ignored fields and risk serde-private marker transformations at a second decode. This new config path has no authorization to change those semantics.</p>
<p>A generic counting <code>deserialize_any</code> preflight is also insufficient. Serde's actual <code>IgnoredAny</code> uses <code>ignore_value</code>, which lexically skips numbers without numeric conversion and stores a separate nesting scratch stack. A large exponent in an ignored field can therefore differ from generic Value decoding. Ignored nesting must still be bounded under the new policy, but a scalar conversion error cannot silently replace acceptance. Source S16.</p>
<p>Recommended seam: a bounded wrapper around the actual deserializer and visitors, preserving the existing derived <code>LegacyProjectConfig</code> semantic consumer. Intercept known owned strings/arrays/maps before copies. Delegate numeric/string syntax and ordinary errors to Serde. For <code>deserialize_ignored_any</code>, use a separately reviewed count/skip facility that preserves the actual lexical skip semantics and checks depth/work before scratch growth. Reuse the existing forward delimiter infrastructure only if extended with a non-materializing skip mode, borrowed RawValue scalar handling and string-discard behavior, all tested against Serde. No new JSON lexer or model policy is needed.</p>
<p><strong>Feasibility boundary.</strong> The public current Serde API has no nested budget callbacks inside <code>ignore_value</code>. A typed seed alone cannot prove that hidden scratch path bounded. Either review a small reusable skip extension with explicit semantic regressions, or pre-reserve a proven source-derived upper bound for the unchanged skip scratch/work and enforce any separately required depth policy before entering it. The latter is only valid with a complete bound proof and cannot claim per-value hard cancellation. This choice is an implementation prerequisite, not a completed parser.</p>
</section>

    -> Result<CurrentResolution, CurrentFailure>

<p>Shared source selection and reducer stages preserve first error and role/provenance order on stable inputs. New capture/limit failures are explicit additive refusals. A failed stage consumes work but publishes no partial resolution. <section id="outputs"><h2>Output binding and real final currentness</h2>
<p>The pure result is a decision, not a filesystem grant. Apply existing flag, original nonempty output environment, configuration workspace.out_dir and default precedence. Capture the genuine host cwd at the same request stage as the existing v1 caller. Resolve original explicit flag/env relative to that immutable attempt cwd; use actual workspace/project/config base facts for configuration paths. Module comes from the actual selected lexical project path relative to the actual enclosing workspace. A project opened as provider root can therefore have nonempty <code>packages/orders</code> module. Do not infer module from portable relative <code>.</code>.</p>
<p>Preserve the v1 no-primary special case: absent context and absent original explicit override defaults under the selected project directory. Preserve implicit output confinement to the original provider directory, even when configuration lookup found a workspace above it. An ancestor config grant cannot authorize reading that ancestor's output. Only the original trusted flag/nonempty output environment can grant an additional output directory. The actual host output resolver opens that original override with the same cwd rule; configuration lookup scope does not manufacture a new explicit output mount. Cwd/location changes that escape an already sealed source or output binding require explicit scope refresh or refusal, never a client-created grant. Sources S10, S17, S18.</p>
<ol><li>Parent holds the reserved attempt through actual source capture, discovery and output resolution. Installed mode submits the same captured discovery request to the real guest; guest membership remains authoritative. Native typed details cannot replace an installed guest's project list.</li><li>Before publishing, reacquire through the same fixed scope and recapture the considered candidate prefix, missing slots, selected alias/component identities, raw digests and configuration environment facts. Recompute selection and output facts with the same bounded reducer. A new nearer workspace, changed ambiguity, changed formerly invalid ancestor, removed user override or changed output facts is stale.</li><li>Compare actual selected project-directory identity, actual output-directory identity, actual module and the structured config fingerprint. Fingerprint includes role/selection/location inputs, source identities/content or closed missing/invalid evidence, environment policy and exact relevant captured entries, plus output overrides and supported parser policy. Preserve the captured ordering of equal normalized environment paths, whose first-entry behavior is part of the actual environment reducer. Do not fingerprint an independently reordered equivalent-looking map. Use explicit canonical encoding, not ambiguous concatenation or mutable labels as identity.</li><li>Capture compile record and model-original inventory under the actual compiler lock using the verified output authority and module. Recheck selection/config/output evidence at the publication boundary while retention and connection ownership remain valid. A changed record/inventory/currentness, revoked scope or cancellation refuses and cleans up. No binding or token is published early.</li></ol>
<p>Two bounded equal checks establish a stated observation interval, not a global transaction or permanent freshness. Config files and environment are not protected by the compiler lock; ABA and concurrent in-place changes need an explicit documented limit. Do not claim that an existing compile used the current configuration unless a genuine compiler record proves it. Source identity, config fingerprint, document revision, capture token and execution identity remain different domain facts.</p>
</section>

+//! Configurable local metadata units, never a parent host-capacity permit.
+//!
+//! Handle units debit ownership of an incoming Dir and each clone/open attempt,
+//! including transient label-identity handles. Path units debit newly retained
+//! native-encoded labels. Candidate units debit the full requested observation
+//! length before each append, conservatively covering possible relocation.
+//! These are logical operation/retention units, not allocator bytes or RSS.
+use super::LookupError;
+
+#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
+pub(super) enum MetadataUnit {
+    IoOperations,
+    HandleUnits,
+    PathBytes,
+    CandidateUnits,
+}
+#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq)]
+pub(super) struct MetadataCost {
+    pub(super) io_operations: usize,
+    pub(super) handle_units: usize,
+    pub(super) path_bytes: usize,
+    pub(super) candidate_units: usize,
+}
+pub(super) struct MetadataLimits(MetadataCost);
+impl MetadataLimits {
+    pub(super) fn new(cost: MetadataCost) -> Result<Self, LookupError> {
+        if [
+            cost.io_operations,
+            cost.handle_units,
+            cost.path_bytes,
+            cost.candidate_units,
+        ]
+        .into_iter()
+        .any(|n| n > isize::MAX as usize)
+        {
+            return Err(LookupError::InvalidLimits);
+        }
+        Ok(Self(cost))
+    }
+}
+pub(super) struct MetadataBudget {
+    limits: MetadataLimits,
+    usage: MetadataCost,
+    failure: Option<MetadataUnit>,
+}
+impl MetadataBudget {
+    pub(super) fn new(limits: MetadataLimits) -> Self {
+        Self {
+            limits,
+            usage: MetadataCost::default(),
+            failure: None,
+        }
+    }
+    pub(super) fn reserve(&mut self, cost: MetadataCost) -> Result<(), LookupError> {
+        if let Some(unit) = self.failure {
+            return Err(LookupError::Limit(unit));
+        }
+        let mut next = self.usage;
+        for (unit, used, additional, limit) in [
+            (
+                MetadataUnit::IoOperations,
+                &mut next.io_operations,
+                cost.io_operations,
+                self.limits.0.io_operations,
+            ),
+            (
+                MetadataUnit::HandleUnits,
+                &mut next.handle_units,
+                cost.handle_units,
+                self.limits.0.handle_units,
+            ),
+            (
+                MetadataUnit::PathBytes,
+                &mut next.path_bytes,
+                cost.path_bytes,
+                self.limits.0.path_bytes,
+            ),
+            (
+                MetadataUnit::CandidateUnits,
+                &mut next.candidate_units,
+                cost.candidate_units,
+                self.limits.0.candidate_units,
+            ),
+        ] {
+            let requested = used.checked_add(additional).unwrap_or(usize::MAX);
+            if requested > limit {
+                self.failure = Some(unit);
+                return Err(LookupError::Limit(unit));
+            }
+            *used = requested;
+        }
+        // Commit only once all counters permit the effect. Never refund.
+        self.usage = next;
+        Ok(())
+    }
+}
+
+#[cfg(test)]
+mod tests {
+    use super::*;
+    #[test]
+    fn reservations_are_atomic_inclusive_sticky_and_cumulative() {
+        let all = MetadataCost {
+            io_operations: 1,
+            handle_units: 1,
+            path_bytes: 1,
+            candidate_units: 1,
+        };
+        let mut budget = MetadataBudget::new(MetadataLimits::new(all).unwrap());
+        budget.reserve(all).unwrap();
+        assert_eq!(budget.usage, all);
+        assert!(matches!(
+            budget.reserve(MetadataCost {
+                candidate_units: 1,
+                ..MetadataCost::default()
+            }),
+            Err(LookupError::Limit(MetadataUnit::CandidateUnits))
+        ));
+        assert_eq!(budget.usage, all);
+        assert!(matches!(
+            budget.reserve(MetadataCost::default()),
+            Err(LookupError::Limit(MetadataUnit::CandidateUnits))
+        ));
+        let mut atomic = MetadataBudget::new(MetadataLimits::new(all).unwrap());
+        assert!(matches!(
+            atomic.reserve(MetadataCost {
+                io_operations: 1,
+                handle_units: 2,
+                ..MetadataCost::default()
+            }),
+            Err(LookupError::Limit(MetadataUnit::HandleUnits))
+        ));
+        assert_eq!(atomic.usage, MetadataCost::default());
+    }
+    #[test]
+    fn limits_require_supported_integers_and_checked_costs_cannot_wrap() {
+        assert!(MetadataLimits::new(MetadataCost::default()).is_ok());
+        assert!(matches!(
+            MetadataLimits::new(MetadataCost {
+                path_bytes: usize::MAX,
+                ..MetadataCost::default()
+            }),
+            Err(LookupError::InvalidLimits)
+        ));
+        let mut budget = MetadataBudget::new(
+            MetadataLimits::new(MetadataCost {
+                io_operations: isize::MAX as usize,
+                ..MetadataCost::default()
+            })
+            .unwrap(),
+        );
+        assert!(matches!(
+            budget.reserve(MetadataCost {
+                io_operations: usize::MAX,
+                ..MetadataCost::default()
+            }),
+            Err(LookupError::Limit(MetadataUnit::IoOperations))
+        ));
+        assert_eq!(budget.usage, MetadataCost::default());
+    }
+}

@@ -0,0 +1,245 @@
+//! Closed operations over startup labels and fixed config candidate names only.
+use super::budget::{MetadataBudget, MetadataCost, MetadataLimits};
+use super::{
+    BoundDirectory, Candidate, CandidateMetadata, Component, ComponentState, LookupError,
+    PresentMetadata, TraceLevel,
+};
+use cap_std::{AmbientAuthority, fs::Dir};
+use same_file::Handle;
+use std::{io, path::Path};
+
+#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
+enum MetadataEffect {
+    DirectoryIdentity(TraceLevel),
+    LabelIdentity(TraceLevel),
+    OpenParent(TraceLevel),
+    ComponentMetadata(TraceLevel, Component),
+    OpenComponent(TraceLevel, Component),
+    ComponentIdentity(TraceLevel, Component),
+    Candidate(TraceLevel, Candidate),
+}
+pub(super) struct MetadataIo {
+    budget: MetadataBudget,
+    #[cfg(test)]
+    effects: Vec<MetadataEffect>,
+}
+impl MetadataIo {
+    pub(super) fn new(limits: MetadataLimits) -> Self {
+        Self {
+            budget: MetadataBudget::new(limits),
+            #[cfg(test)]
+            effects: Vec::new(),
+        }
+    }
+    #[cfg(test)]
+    pub(super) fn effect_count(&self) -> usize {
+        self.effects.len()
+    }
+    #[cfg(test)]
+    pub(super) fn candidate_effect_count(&self) -> usize {
+        self.effects
+            .iter()
+            .filter(|e| matches!(e, MetadataEffect::Candidate(..)))
+            .count()
+    }
+    #[cfg(test)]
+    pub(super) fn configuration_effect_count(&self) -> usize {
+        self.effects
+            .iter()
+            .filter(|effect| {
+                matches!(
+                    effect,
+                    MetadataEffect::ComponentMetadata(..)
+                        | MetadataEffect::OpenComponent(..)
+                        | MetadataEffect::ComponentIdentity(..)
+                        | MetadataEffect::Candidate(..)
+                )
+            })
+            .count()
+    }
+    fn before(&mut self, effect: MetadataEffect, handle_units: usize) -> Result<(), LookupError> {
+        self.budget.reserve(MetadataCost {
+            io_operations: 1,
+            handle_units,
+            ..MetadataCost::default()
+        })?;
+        #[cfg(test)]
+        self.effects.push(effect);
+        #[cfg(not(test))]
+        let _ = effect;
+        Ok(())
+    }
+    pub(super) fn bind(
+        &mut self,
+        level: TraceLevel,
+        directory: Dir,
+        label: &Path,
+    ) -> Result<BoundDirectory, LookupError> {
+        self.budget.reserve(MetadataCost {
+            path_bytes: label.as_os_str().as_encoded_bytes().len(),
+            handle_units: 1,
+            ..MetadataCost::default()
+        })?;
+        self.before(MetadataEffect::DirectoryIdentity(level), 1)?;
+        let identity = Handle::from_file(directory.try_clone()?.into_std_file())?;
+        let mut bound = BoundDirectory {
+            level,
+            directory,
+            label: label.to_owned(),
+            identity,
+            components: [
+                ComponentState::Absent,
+                ComponentState::Absent,
+                ComponentState::Absent,
+            ],
+        };
+        self.verify_label(&bound)?;
+        let opened = self.open_components(&bound)?;
+        let mut identities = [
+            ComponentState::Absent,
+            ComponentState::Absent,
+            ComponentState::Absent,
+        ];
+        for (component, state) in Component::ALL.into_iter().zip(opened) {
+            identities[component.index()] = match state {
+                ComponentState::Absent => ComponentState::Absent,
+                ComponentState::NonDirectory => ComponentState::NonDirectory,
+                ComponentState::Present(dir) => {
+                    self.before(MetadataEffect::ComponentIdentity(level, component), 0)?;
+                    ComponentState::Present(Handle::from_file(dir.into_std_file())?)
+                }
+            };
+        }
+        bound.components = identities;
+        Ok(bound)
+    }
+    pub(super) fn verify_label(&mut self, bound: &BoundDirectory) -> Result<(), LookupError> {
+        self.before(MetadataEffect::LabelIdentity(bound.level), 1)?;
+        if bound.identity != Handle::from_path(&bound.label)? {
+            return Err(LookupError::RootChanged);
+        }
+        Ok(())
+    }
+    pub(super) fn parent(
+        &mut self,
+        child: &BoundDirectory,
+        level: TraceLevel,
+        ambient: AmbientAuthority,
+    ) -> Result<Dir, LookupError> {
+        self.before(MetadataEffect::OpenParent(level), 1)?;
+        Ok(child.directory.open_parent_dir(ambient)?)
+    }
+    fn child(
+        &mut self,
+        parent: &Dir,
+        level: TraceLevel,
+        component: Component,
+    ) -> Result<ComponentState<Dir>, LookupError> {
+        let leaf = component.leaf();
+        self.before(MetadataEffect::ComponentMetadata(level, component), 0)?;
+        let metadata = match parent.symlink_metadata(leaf) {
+            Ok(m) => m,
+            Err(e) if e.kind() == io::ErrorKind::NotFound => return Ok(ComponentState::Absent),
+            Err(e) => return Err(e.into()),
+        };
+        if metadata.file_type().is_symlink() {
+            return Err(LookupError::UnsealedAlias);
+        }
+        if !metadata.is_dir() {
+            return Ok(ComponentState::NonDirectory);
+        }
+        self.before(MetadataEffect::OpenComponent(level, component), 1)?;
+        let directory = parent.open_dir(leaf)?;
+        // The actual held Dir is used for subsequent candidate probes. A race
+        // that introduces a link refuses, without following an ambient path.
+        self.before(MetadataEffect::ComponentMetadata(level, component), 0)?;
+        let after = parent.symlink_metadata(leaf)?;
+        if after.file_type().is_symlink() {
+            return Err(LookupError::UnsealedAlias);
+        }
+        if !after.is_dir() {
+            return Err(LookupError::RootChanged);
+        }
+        Ok(ComponentState::Present(directory))
+    }
+    pub(super) fn open_components(
+        &mut self,
+        bound: &BoundDirectory,
+    ) -> Result<[ComponentState<Dir>; 3], LookupError> {
+        let morphir = self.child(&bound.directory, bound.level, Component::Morphir)?;
+        let config = self.child(&bound.directory, bound.level, Component::DotConfig)?;
+        let config_morphir = match &config {
+            ComponentState::Absent => ComponentState::Absent,
+            ComponentState::NonDirectory => ComponentState::NonDirectory,
+            ComponentState::Present(dir) => {
+                self.child(dir, bound.level, Component::DotConfigMorphir)?
+            }
+        };
+        Ok([morphir, config, config_morphir])
+    }
+    pub(super) fn verify_components(
+        &mut self,
+        bound: &BoundDirectory,
+        opened: &[ComponentState<Dir>; 3],
+    ) -> Result<[ComponentState<Handle>; 3], LookupError> {
+        let mut evidence = [
+            ComponentState::Absent,
+            ComponentState::Absent,
+            ComponentState::Absent,
+        ];
+        for component in Component::ALL {
+            let observed = match &opened[component.index()] {
+                ComponentState::Absent => ComponentState::Absent,
+                ComponentState::NonDirectory => ComponentState::NonDirectory,
+                ComponentState::Present(directory) => {
+                    self.before(MetadataEffect::ComponentIdentity(bound.level, component), 1)?;
+                    ComponentState::Present(Handle::from_file(
+                        directory.try_clone()?.into_std_file(),
+                    )?)
+                }
+            };
+            if let ComponentState::Present(expected) = &bound.components[component.index()] {
+                match &observed {
+                    ComponentState::Present(actual) if expected == actual => {}
+                    _ => return Err(LookupError::RootChanged),
+                }
+            }
+            evidence[component.index()] = observed;
+        }
+        Ok(evidence)
+    }
+    pub(super) fn candidate(
+        &mut self,
+        bound: &BoundDirectory,
+        opened: &[ComponentState<Dir>; 3],
+        candidate: Candidate,
+    ) -> Result<CandidateMetadata, LookupError> {
+        let (component, leaf) = candidate.location();
+        let directory = match component {
+            None => &bound.directory,
+            Some(component) => match &opened[component.index()] {
+                ComponentState::Absent => return Ok(CandidateMetadata::Absent),
+                ComponentState::NonDirectory => return Ok(CandidateMetadata::NonRegular),
+                ComponentState::Present(dir) => dir,
+            },
+        };
+        self.before(MetadataEffect::Candidate(bound.level, candidate), 0)?;
+        Ok(match directory.symlink_metadata(leaf) {
+            Ok(metadata) if metadata.is_file() => {
+                CandidateMetadata::Present(PresentMetadata { metadata })
+            }
+            Ok(metadata) if metadata.file_type().is_symlink() => {
+                return Err(LookupError::UnsealedAlias);
+            }
+            Ok(_) => CandidateMetadata::NonRegular,
+            Err(error) if error.kind() == io::ErrorKind::NotFound => CandidateMetadata::Absent,
+            Err(error) => return Err(error.into()),
+        })
+    }
+    pub(super) fn reserve_candidate(&mut self, requested_units: usize) -> Result<(), LookupError> {
+        self.budget.reserve(MetadataCost {
+            candidate_units: requested_units,
+            ..MetadataCost::default()
+        })
+    }
+}

+//! Incomplete private metadata tracer. No configuration bytes or policy results.
+//!
+//! This staged building block is deliberately unwired. It is not a production
+//! lookup scope, host permit, Current resolver or advertised capability.
+use cap_std::fs::{Dir, Metadata};
+use same_file::Handle;
+use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};
+mod budget;
+mod io;
+use io::MetadataIo;
+
+struct TwoAncestorLookupTrace {
+    directories: [Option<BoundDirectory>; 3],
+}
+struct BoundDirectory {
+    level: TraceLevel,
+    directory: Dir,
+    label: PathBuf,
+    identity: Handle,
+    components: [ComponentState<Handle>; 3],
+}
+
+#[derive(Debug, thiserror::Error)]
+enum LookupError {
+    #[error("lookup metadata I/O failed: {0}")]
+    Io(#[from] std::io::Error),
+    #[error("lookup label must be an absolute host path")]
+    InvalidLabel,
+    #[error("lookup directory identity changed")]
+    RootChanged,
+    #[error("invalid local metadata limits")]
+    InvalidLimits,
+    #[error("unsealed lookup alias")]
+    UnsealedAlias,
+    #[error("local metadata limit exceeded: {0:?}")]
+    Limit(budget::MetadataUnit),
+}
+
+struct CandidateMetadataSnapshot {
+    observations: Vec<CandidateObservation>,
+    components: [Option<[ComponentState<Handle>; 3]>; 3],
+}
+
+#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
+enum TraceLevel {
+    Selected,
+    Parent,
+    Grandparent,
+}
+#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
+enum Candidate {
+    RootToml,
+    RootYaml,
+    MorphirToml,
+    MorphirYaml,
+    ConfigToml,
+    ConfigYaml,
+    LegacyJson,
+}
+impl Candidate {
+    const ALL: [Self; 7] = [
+        Self::RootToml,
+        Self::RootYaml,
+        Self::MorphirToml,
+        Self::MorphirYaml,
+        Self::ConfigToml,
+        Self::ConfigYaml,
+        Self::LegacyJson,
+    ];
+    fn location(self) -> (Option<Component>, &'static str) {
+        match self {
+            Self::RootToml => (None, "morphir.toml"),
+            Self::RootYaml => (None, "morphir.yaml"),
+            Self::MorphirToml => (Some(Component::Morphir), "morphir.toml"),
+            Self::MorphirYaml => (Some(Component::Morphir), "morphir.yaml"),
+            Self::ConfigToml => (Some(Component::DotConfigMorphir), "config.toml"),
+            Self::ConfigYaml => (Some(Component::DotConfigMorphir), "config.yaml"),
+            Self::LegacyJson => (None, "morphir.json"),
+        }
+    }
+}
+#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
+enum Component {
+    Morphir,
+    DotConfig,
+    DotConfigMorphir,
+}
+impl Component {
+    const ALL: [Self; 3] = [Self::Morphir, Self::DotConfig, Self::DotConfigMorphir];
+    fn leaf(self) -> &'static str {
+        match self {
+            Self::Morphir => ".morphir",
+            Self::DotConfig => ".config",
+            Self::DotConfigMorphir => "morphir",
+        }
+    }
+    fn index(self) -> usize {
+        match self {
+            Self::Morphir => 0,
+            Self::DotConfig => 1,
+            Self::DotConfigMorphir => 2,
+        }
+    }
+}
+enum ComponentState<T> {
+    Absent,
+    NonDirectory,
+    Present(T),
+}
+// Opaque native metadata only. No content digest or semantic source evidence.
+struct PresentMetadata {
+    metadata: Metadata,
+}
+enum CandidateMetadata {
+    Absent,
+    NonRegular,
+    Present(PresentMetadata),
+}
+struct CandidateObservation {
+    level: TraceLevel,
+    candidate: Candidate,
+    state: CandidateMetadata,
+}
+
+impl TwoAncestorLookupTrace {
+    fn seal_startup(
+        selected: Dir,
+        label: &Path,
+        ambient: cap_std::AmbientAuthority,
+        io: &mut MetadataIo,
+    ) -> Result<Self, LookupError> {
+        if !label.is_absolute() {
+            return Err(LookupError::InvalidLabel);
+        }
+        let mut directories = [
+            Some(io.bind(TraceLevel::Selected, selected, label)?),
+            None,
+            None,
+        ];
+        for (index, level) in [(1, TraceLevel::Parent), (2, TraceLevel::Grandparent)] {
+            let Some(child) = directories[index - 1].as_ref() else {
+                break;
+            };
+            let Some(parent_label) = child.label.parent() else {
+                break;
+            };
+            let parent = io.parent(child, level, ambient)?;
+            directories[index] = Some(io.bind(level, parent, parent_label)?);
+        }
+        Ok(Self { directories })
+    }
+
+    fn capture_metadata(
+        &self,
+        io: &mut MetadataIo,
+    ) -> Result<CandidateMetadataSnapshot, LookupError> {
+        let mut observations = Vec::new();
+        let mut components = [None, None, None];
+        for (index, bound) in self.directories.iter().enumerate() {
+            let Some(bound) = bound else { break };
+            if bound.level != TraceLevel::Selected
+                && !observations.iter().any(|x: &CandidateObservation| {
+                    x.level == TraceLevel::Selected
+                        && matches!(x.state, CandidateMetadata::Present(_))
+                })
+            {
+                break;
+            }
+            io.verify_label(bound)?;
+            let opened = io.open_components(bound)?;
+            components[index] = Some(io.verify_components(bound, &opened)?);
+            for candidate in Candidate::ALL {
+                io.reserve_candidate(observations.len() + 1)?;
+                let state = io.candidate(bound, &opened, candidate)?;
+                observations
+                    .try_reserve_exact(1)
+                    .map_err(|_| std::io::Error::other("metadata observation allocation failed"))?;
+                observations.push(CandidateObservation {
+                    level: bound.level,
+                    candidate,
+                    state,
+                });
+            }
+        }
+        Ok(CandidateMetadataSnapshot {
+            observations,
+            components,
+        })
+    }
+}

The independent Task 2A review found no material issue within fixed-source/index/retention scope. Its disabled-Ion 1.1 lane remains failed with the same three baseline tooling failures; this design introduces no new passing reader qualification.

The Morphir model profile remains separate: aggregate primary input bytes, parsed application values, assembled application values, depth, decoded key/string UTF16 units and output bytes retain their own ledgers. This proposal selects no auxiliary production cap and does not combine input and output into one application-value quota.

Opt-in API and shared policy

Use private validated fields and closed modes. Common source quotas span fixed and streaming owners on one ReaderBudget. Keep preparation work and streaming I/O/work distinct. Every quota is explicit; zero means no authority. Positive capacities and read span are tuning values that require at least 1. Validate all arithmetic against the existing supported usize/isize range, including row-byte multiplication and absolute offsets.

BudgetedIonStream has private construction and implements the sealed input path. It borrows the caller's Read object, so it gains no ambient file or close authority. A concrete ReadConfig avoids invoking a caller-defined Into conversion inside the checked factory. Missing config budget inherits the owner; identical pointer identity is accepted; a different identity rejects before reserving a source instance, constructing a generic reader, allocating source payload or calling Read.

Keep source_preparation as an adapter into the common ledger. Its existing storage cap becomes both cumulative requested payload and resident requested payload. The resident bound is redundant because resident never exceeds cumulative. Its preparation work remains exactly 3N+E as accepted, and it authorizes no streaming. Reject simultaneous source_limits and source_preparation selections at build time; the final setter must not silently replace policy.

The fresh extension needs leased fixed-source owners as well as streaming owners, so mixed-mode residency is truthful. Moving the existing prepared byte Rc into a private leased owner adds no source copy; prepared IoBuffer snapshots must retain that leased owner. Initial row 0 and every new stream count against common row/source quotas, including empty streams. These internal changes belong in a new proof; the accepted Task 2A artifact stays immutable.

Accounting before effects

Validated quotaDebit and lifetime
source_bytesCommon charged fixed lengths, received streaming bytes, conservative uncertain normal-read spans, and outstanding held read grants. Reserve a normal offered span before the callback. Settle valid n as spent and release unused held authority. This does not refund any spent work. The one-byte overflow probe is separate lookahead and never published source.

A failed allocation releases only its unmaterialized residency reservation. A materialized lease releases after its actual last payload owner is destroyed.

Retry still counts. Prepared blocks retain their accepted bounded count per source instance. No source-sized allocation may hide in metadata.

One unit is one byte position processed in one explicit pass, not both a read and write charge. Stack probe initialization costs1. Preparation keeps its distinct accepted3N+E counter.
initial_capacity / max_window_capacity / max_read_spanValidated positive stream tuning values with initial no larger than max window. Capacities bound requested logical window length. Initial capacity is a preferred target, not a mandatory allocation; clamp to the exact needed1 if remaining quota cannot fit the preference. All arithmetic is checked before effects.

Quota preflight is pure and non-mutating. The planner first tries the preferred capacity and then exact required capacity against all relevant quotas. A rejected preference must not poison the budget. After choosing a plan, atomically reserve all of its credits once. If neither plan fits, record the first typed quota refusal in a documented fixed check order. Overflow becomes a refusal, not wraparound.

Do not hold a RefCell borrow across Read, allocation, payload destruction or caller-controlled drop. A held read grant protects primary allowance from reentrant fixed-source preparation. Its settlement must reconcile the grant even when a callback has already caused a sticky failure. An RAII read-phase guard prevents two checked Read callbacks on the same budget from running at once.

Requested payload excludes allocator rounding and fixed Rc/Vec metadata. Count metadata-producing blocks and source instances separately. This is not a heap/RSS guarantee. A caller's retained handles legitimately consume capacity. Library byte work excludes the parser's scans, numeric conversion, scalar materialization, location lookup and arbitrary work inside Read. Each has separate remaining work.

Owners, COW and row indices

A checked byte block holds an initialized Vec payload and a resident lease in the same Rc owner. The initialized usable length is the charged requested capacity C; allocator-reported extra capacity is never made readable or used as free authority. Use try_reserve_exact before initialization and no reallocating conversion into Rc<[u8]>. Rc contains the Vec owner without a second payload copy. Rc allocation itself retains process OOM behavior; the proof promises quota checks and typed recoverable payload-reserve failures, not recovery from allocator abort.

Use Rc::get_mut, not a separate strong-count guess. If unique, shift only when tail room is exhausted and reserve L movement operations first. If shared, copy only L live unread bytes into a new authorized block at offset0. Fuse compaction and COW into that one copy. Growth holds old and new resident leases at once. Source payload drops before its lease, using field order or explicit destruction; no early resident release while old bytes remain allocated. The budget does not own sources, so leases do not create ownership cycles. The relevant upstream uniqueness/COW behavior is defined by Rc::get_mut and Rc::make_mut.

IoBuffer needs a private checked backing variant. save_io_buffer clones its owner handles with no source/index allocation. Public read_from and every private mutation helper refuse that snapshot before effects, as prepared snapshots already do. consume changes view offsets only. The active stream owns the only checked mutation path; it never calls a legacy Mutable helper on a checked owner.

A checked append-only row state shares all earlier absolute row offsets with every retained value. Later append does not invalidate their positions. An index replacement first reserves its new capacity G times W while the old block is live, then copies only the E logical existing offsets. New LF offsets append once. The last-row cache remains within the unchanged prefix; location lookup itself is outside this work quota. Keep raw LF, byte columns, CRLF behavior, malformed UTF8 bytes and empty public binary locations unchanged.

Only a private non-cloneable received-chunk capability can append rows. It binds source identity, absolute offset and validated n to actual newly received bytes. Generic update_from_source must reject this checked state. Reparse, move, COW, save and to_owned cannot mint that capability or index old bytes again.

Checked refill order

The pure planner selects a closed read plan. DirectAppend is allowed only with a unique initialized tail and q bounded by available primary authority, max read span and current tail. StructuralProbe applies when shift, COW, initial allocation or growth would otherwise be needed. BoundaryProbe applies when primary authority is exhausted. Both probes offer one initialized stack byte; they spend read-attempt, requested-I/O and initialization credits before Read.

  1. Check the first sticky quota failure and this source's terminal fault. Acquire the shared read-phase guard. Plan and reserve read authority without mutating payload/index. Do not call Read with an empty slice.
  2. Call Read with the chosen initialized span. Validate returned n no larger than q before length arithmetic, slicing, indexing or unsafe handout. Settle the normal held grant. Check whether a callback caused a global failure.
  3. On actual zero, remember EOF for this logical pass. On ordinary error, return it. Neither outcome shifts, COWs, grows or updates the row index when a probe was needed.
  4. On positive input, reserve n count operations before scanning its raw LF bytes. Use the count to plan logical entries, row capacity, byte capacity and all remaining copy/init/fill/write operations. Re-evaluate uniqueness after the callback, since it may have dropped retained owners.
  5. Reserve the chosen publication plan atomically. Complete every fallible candidate payload allocation before moving old bytes in place or changing published offsets. Initialize and copy authorized payloads, fill row offsets, then publish a coherent byte end and row prefix without a remaining fallible step.

For DirectAppend, the Read can dirty an uncommitted initialized tail, but published end does not advance until index/work checks pass. For a structural probe, a positive byte stays in one inline pending slot until the plan commits. A later quota/allocation failure can follow a bounded Read because its LF count was unknowable beforehand. It is not a transactional rewind of an external stream. The source becomes terminal on post-read allocation failure, and resource refusal poisons the shared budget. Retained old values remain intact.

Append a new row batch with n count-scan operations and, when it contains LF, n fill-scan operations plus K*W offset writes. No second scan when K is zero. Reserve E*W old-row copy operations for index growth. A new byte capacity C costs C initialization operations; copies/moves cost only the live L bytes. Candidate capacity fallback is decided before recording any failure.

Exact limits and temporary EOF

When source byte credit is exhausted, a separate one-byte BoundaryProbe distinguishes actual EOF from excess source. Actual0 permits completion; a valid one-byte result triggers sticky SourceBytes with requested charged+1 before the extra byte is appended or a truncated text scalar is returned. Never implement source limiting through Read::take, which substitutes EOF at its own cap and can make a larger token appear complete. This follows the pinned Take behavior and the existing text completion rule.

Structural probes avoid allocation just to find EOF, including a full shared window with no resident headroom. A valid empty source needs row 0 but no byte block. Probe work and I/O quota must still be available; spending the final primary byte does not grant free unlimited EOF checks.

Add begin_read_pass to the internal data-source protocol with a default no-op. Call it once at read_next entry. Checked streams reset a closed pass state to Open. An actual nonempty-span Read returning zero sets EndObserved. Repeated fill calls within that pass return cached zero without I/O; the next logical next or peek starts a new pass and can observe appended bytes. Do not use a permanently fused EOF flag. Ordinary legacy source callbacks keep their current behavior.

Rust permits temporary EOF, partial reads and blocking callbacks. Read errors report no successful byte count; Interrupted may be retried by a caller. Checked streaming returns one ordinary I/O error per invocation and does not install an unbounded automatic retry loop. These rules come from the pinned Rust 1.94.1 Read contract. Its source also warns that safe Read implementations cannot be trusted for unsafe memory safety. The checked source validates n itself.

Closed containers and binary values may yield before overall EOF. A caller must drain to None to establish whole-source byte compliance. This library cannot turn a mutable file into an immutable snapshot or stop a Read implementation from blocking, allocating, prefetching, or changing its hidden source. The checked claim ends at the supplied Read boundary. A caller-owned BufReader can prefetch beyond that offered span. Morphir's frozen finite original-byte capture remains the preferred fixed-source seam.

Errors, retries and reentry

OutcomeProposed behavior
Resource quota / arithmetic refusalExisting ResourceLimit with first kind/offset/limit/requested wins globally. All later checked factory/next/peek/prepare calls refuse before further source effects. Spent attempts, byte work, row entries and cumulative allocation credit do not refund.
Ordinary Read errorReturn existing IonError::Io without poisoning resource policy. Release unused held primary authority because no valid n was returned. Callback attempts/span still spent. A caller retry spends again; do not reuse a dirty tail as published bytes.
Invalid count n>qNew typed SourceInput failure InvalidReadCount, terminal for that source before slice/index changes. Conservatively spend the held normal span q as uncertain input. Overflow-probe scratch is never published primary; its invalid callback poisons the source, not a fabricated valid byte receipt. No unbounded error-string formatting.
Read unwindsNo catch inside the library. RAII clears active-read state, conservatively settles a normal grant and records terminal ReadUnwound without allocation/panic. If the caller catches unwind, retry refuses before Read. Process abort is outside cleanup guarantees.
Nested Read on same budgetTyped recoverable ReentrantRead before invoking the nested callback. The outer normal grant remains held. Other budget operations may run if they can reserve around it. A nested preparation quota failure remains the global first failure; outer settlement must still occur.
Post-read payload reserve failureTyped terminal PayloadAllocationFailed for this source. Release only unmaterialized resident reservations. Keep received/source/work/attempt/cumulative credits spent. No second Read can discard the pending byte or pretend the old input position was restored.
Wrong selected budget / wrong source modeIllegal configuration/use before factory construction effects; not a fabricated resource exhaustion. Old preparation shorthand selects prepared mode only.

Proposed IonError::SourceInput wraps a private-construction failure with closed kind and existing Position evidence. IonError is already non-exhaustive. Keep bounded scalar fields rather than caller strings; do not retain arbitrary input or exception text in a sticky failure. If a callback already triggered global ResourceLimit, settle its held reservation and return that first global failure instead of replacing it with a later source fault. No RefCell borrow may survive into a callback or destructor.

Every new safe/internal mutation route must either carry checked authorization or reject the checked backing. The proof must audit constructors, clone, save, to_owned, public read_from/consume, private grow/shift/make_data_mut, generic index update and active refill. It must also guard at pass entry, so a different source's failure prevents parsing buffered data under a now-failed budget. This does not retroactively claim every old already-yielded scalar/macro operation is guarded.

The packet contains 34 proposed recipes authored from source contracts and fixed byte literals before any Task 2B run. Its small finite test controls are not production policy. Review decisions

The recommendation is one common fixed/stream ledger, leased retained storage and probe-before-structural-mutation. Accept the per-pass EOF cache because it preserves future appended-data reads while removing repeated physical EOF calls inside one raw-reader pass. Keep all ordinary constructors unchanged.

  1. Approve or amend the proposed composed source policy and compatibility shorthand. This requires an internal leased prepared-owner extension in the new proof, not changes to the accepted artifact.
  2. Confirm resident versus cumulative requested payload, logical rows, byte-operation units and read-span charging. No production quota values are proposed.
  3. Confirm the one-byte lookahead boundary and explicit whole-stream drain requirement. A caller asking for a valid prefix has not qualified its unseen suffix.
  4. Confirm typed terminal source-input faults and the recoverable nested-read rejection. Arbitrary callback runtime, hidden I/O, process abort and unsafe external corruption remain outside the guarantee.
  5. Authorize only the smallest isolated source tracer if these choices are accepted. Implementation and a broader bounded-reader claim require separate evidence.

No unresolved need for an additional lexer or a new file protocol was found. The existing parser, source positions, lazy retention model and Read boundary suffice for this proposal. The concrete questions are policy composition, credit units and source-fault semantics, not Ion support removal.

<h1>Budgeted Ion streaming sources</h1>
<p class="meta">morphir-etg2.22.1 · 19 October 2026 · Task 2B proposal, revision 1 · Review before implementation</p>
<p>The accepted fixed-source proof avoids hidden copies when lazy values retain captured bytes. Streaming still allocates, shifts and copies its buffer before it knows whether the next read returns a byte, EOF or an error. Task 2B should add a separate checked stream factory that reserves each library-owned read, byte operation and payload allocation before the effect. Retained values must keep their buffers charged until their last owner drops.</p>
<div class="note">Design only. No Task 2B source patch, dependency selection, SDK integration or production resource numbers are authorized or delivered. This proposal preserves the accepted Task 1 and Task 2A proof files. It does not qualify a full bounded Ion reader.</div>
