<section id="status"><h2>Scope and evidence</h2>
<ul><li><label><input type="checkbox" checked disabled> Trace the accepted source, retention and refill paths without changing them.</label></li>

<p>The source baseline is ion-rs 1.0.1 at upstream <code>a1df66475c76605dd31c8566ef11f50f07fe8111</code> plus accepted isolated Task 1 and Task 2A patches. Accepted Task 2A whole-source SHA256 is <code>0244a54b2233c61b134a237f33181c49de1b55c3542ea9eb9acd6a23a7e14676</code>. The receipt hashes nine inspected source files and records exact line anchors. The independent Task 2A review found no material issue within fixed-source/index/retention scope. Its disabled-Ion 1.1 lane remains failed with the same three baseline tooling failures; this design introduces no new passing reader qualification.</p>
<p>The Morphir model profile remains separate: aggregate primary input bytes, parsed application values, assembled application values, depth, decoded key/string UTF16 units and output bytes retain their own ledgers. This proposal selects no auxiliary production cap and does not combine input and output into one application-value quota.</p></section>

<section id="api"><h2>Opt-in API and shared policy</h2>
<p>Use private validated fields and closed modes. Common source quotas span fixed and streaming owners on one ReaderBudget. Keep preparation work and streaming I/O/work distinct. Every quota is explicit; zero means no authority. Positive capacities and read span are tuning values that require at least 1. Validate all arithmetic against the existing supported usize/isize range, including row-byte multiplication and absolute offsets.</p>
<pre><code class="language-rust">// Proposed API shape. Opaque structs have validated builders, not public fields.
pub struct SourceLimits;        // common bytes, instances, storage, rows
pub struct StreamReadLimits;    // explicit I/O, allocation and byte-work quotas
pub struct PreparationWorkLimits;
pub enum SourceModes {
    Prepared(PreparationWorkLimits),
    Streaming(StreamReadLimits),
    PreparedAndStreaming {
        prepared: PreparationWorkLimits,
        streaming: StreamReadLimits,
    },
}
pub struct SourceReadLimits;    // validated SourceLimits + SourceModes

impl ReaderLimitsBuilder {
    pub fn source_limits(self, limits: SourceReadLimits) -> Self;
    // Existing source_preparation(...) remains a compatibility shorthand.
}
impl ReaderBudget {
    pub fn stream_reader<'r, D: Decoder, R: Read + ?Sized>(
        &self,
        config: ReadConfig<D>,
        source: &'r mut R,
    ) -> IonResult<Reader<D, BudgetedIonStream<'r, R>>>;
}</code></pre>
<p>BudgetedIonStream has private construction and implements the sealed input path. It borrows the caller's Read object, so it gains no ambient file or close authority. A concrete ReadConfig avoids invoking a caller-defined Into conversion inside the checked factory. Missing config budget inherits the owner; identical pointer identity is accepted; a different identity rejects before reserving a source instance, constructing a generic reader, allocating source payload or calling Read.</p>
<p>Keep source_preparation as an adapter into the common ledger. Its existing storage cap becomes both cumulative requested payload and resident requested payload. The resident bound is redundant because resident never exceeds cumulative. Its preparation work remains exactly 3N+E as accepted, and it authorizes no streaming. Reject simultaneous source_limits and source_preparation selections at build time; the final setter must not silently replace policy.</p>
<p>The fresh extension needs leased fixed-source owners as well as streaming owners, so mixed-mode residency is truthful. Moving the existing prepared byte Rc into a private leased owner adds no source copy; prepared IoBuffer snapshots must retain that leased owner. Initial row 0 and every new stream count against common row/source quotas, including empty streams. These internal changes belong in a new proof; the accepted Task 2A artifact stays immutable.</p></section>
<section id="ledger"><h2>Accounting before effects</h2>
<table tabindex="0"><thead><tr><th style="min-width:11rem">Validated quota</th><th style="min-width:26rem">Debit and lifetime</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>source_bytes</td><td>Common charged fixed lengths, received streaming bytes, conservative uncertain normal-read spans, and outstanding held read grants. Reserve a normal offered span before the callback. Settle valid n as spent and release unused held authority. This does not refund any spent work. The one-byte overflow probe is separate lookahead and never published source.</td></tr>
<tr><td>source_instances</td><td>Cumulative successful reservation attempts for new logical source owners, including empty sources. Clones/reopen/snapshots are the same owner. Factory reservations are not refunded on later failure.</td></tr>
<tr><td>cumulative_requested_payload_bytes</td><td>Each requested byte-block capacity and row-block capacity times sizeof(usize), before allocation attempt. Count replacement blocks fully, even when old blocks are released. Failed allocations, retry and drop do not refund this credit.</td></tr>
<tr><td>resident_requested_payload_bytes</td><td>Live requested payload plus outstanding allocation reservations. Reserve transient old+new growth/COW/index blocks before allocating. A failed allocation releases only its unmaterialized residency reservation. A materialized lease releases after its actual last payload owner is destroyed.</td></tr>
<tr><td>logical_location_entries</td><td>Cumulative row 0 plus new raw LF offsets once per received chunk. Capacity slack and replacement copies do not create logical rows.</td></tr>
<tr><td>read_attempts / requested_io_bytes</td><td>Each actual Read invocation and its offered nonempty initialized span q, before the callback. Short reads, EOF and errors spend all q requested bytes and the attempt. No retry refund.</td></tr>
<tr><td>allocation_events</td><td>Each requested streaming byte or row payload block, including initial row 0 and replacement blocks. One event includes a bounded fixed amount of owner/header metadata. Retry still counts. Prepared blocks retain their accepted bounded count per source instance. No source-sized allocation may hide in metadata.</td></tr>
<tr><td>byte_operations</td><td>Library initialization C, copy/move live bytes L, count scan n, optional fill scan n and row writes/copies times sizeof(usize). One unit is one byte position processed in one explicit pass, not both a read and write charge. Stack probe initialization costs1. Preparation keeps its distinct accepted3N+E counter.</td></tr>
<tr><td>initial_capacity / max_window_capacity / max_read_span</td><td>Validated positive stream tuning values with initial no larger than max window. Capacities bound requested logical window length. Initial capacity is a preferred target, not a mandatory allocation; clamp to the exact needed1 if remaining quota cannot fit the preference. All arithmetic is checked before effects.</td></tr>
</tbody></table>
<p>Quota preflight is pure and non-mutating. The planner first tries the preferred capacity and then exact required capacity against all relevant quotas. A rejected preference must not poison the budget. After choosing a plan, atomically reserve all of its credits once. If neither plan fits, record the first typed quota refusal in a documented fixed check order. Overflow becomes a refusal, not wraparound.</p>
<p>Do not hold a RefCell borrow across Read, allocation, payload destruction or caller-controlled drop. A held read grant protects primary allowance from reentrant fixed-source preparation. Its settlement must reconcile the grant even when a callback has already caused a sticky failure. An RAII read-phase guard prevents two checked Read callbacks on the same budget from running at once.</p>
<p>Requested payload excludes allocator rounding and fixed Rc/Vec metadata. Count metadata-producing blocks and source instances separately. This is not a heap/RSS guarantee. A caller's retained handles legitimately consume capacity. Library byte work excludes the parser's scans, numeric conversion, scalar materialization, location lookup and arbitrary work inside Read. Each has separate remaining work.</p></section>
<section id="owners"><h2>Owners, COW and row indices</h2>

<p>A checked byte block holds an initialized Vec payload and a resident lease in the same Rc owner. The initialized usable length is the charged requested capacity C; allocator-reported extra capacity is never made readable or used as free authority. Use try_reserve_exact before initialization and no reallocating conversion into Rc<[u8]>. Rc contains the Vec owner without a second payload copy. Rc allocation itself retains process OOM behavior; the proof promises quota checks and typed recoverable payload-reserve failures, not recovery from allocator abort.</p>
<p>Use Rc::get_mut, not a separate strong-count guess. If unique, shift only when tail room is exhausted and reserve L movement operations first. If shared, copy only L live unread bytes into a new authorized block at offset0. Fuse compaction and COW into that one copy. Growth holds old and new resident leases at once. Source payload drops before its lease, using field order or explicit destruction; no early resident release while old bytes remain allocated. The budget does not own sources, so leases do not create ownership cycles. The relevant upstream uniqueness/COW behavior is defined by <a href="https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/blob/e408947bfd200af42db322daf0fadfe7e26d3bd1/library/alloc/src/rc.rs#L1917">Rc::get_mut</a> and <a href="https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/blob/e408947bfd200af42db322daf0fadfe7e26d3bd1/library/alloc/src/rc.rs#L2065">Rc::make_mut</a>.</p>
<p>IoBuffer needs a private checked backing variant. save_io_buffer clones its owner handles with no source/index allocation. Public read_from and every private mutation helper refuse that snapshot before effects, as prepared snapshots already do. consume changes view offsets only. The active stream owns the only checked mutation path; it never calls a legacy Mutable helper on a checked owner.</p>
<p>A checked append-only row state shares all earlier absolute row offsets with every retained value. Later append does not invalidate their positions. An index replacement first reserves its new capacity G times W while the old block is live, then copies only the E logical existing offsets. New LF offsets append once. The last-row cache remains within the unchanged prefix; location lookup itself is outside this work quota. Keep raw LF, byte columns, CRLF behavior, malformed UTF8 bytes and empty public binary locations unchanged.</p>
<p>Only a private non-cloneable received-chunk capability can append rows. It binds source identity, absolute offset and validated n to actual newly received bytes. Generic update_from_source must reject this checked state. Reparse, move, COW, save and to_owned cannot mint that capability or index old bytes again.</p>

  Reader->>Read: initialized span q

  Reader->>NewBlock: allocate only if positive input needs it
  Reader->>Rows: append received chunk once
  Reader->>Retained: share byte and index leases
  Retained-->>Budget: release resident only at last owner drop</code></pre></details>

<section id="refill"><h2>Checked refill order</h2>
<p>The pure planner selects a closed read plan. DirectAppend is allowed only with a unique initialized tail and q bounded by available primary authority, max read span and current tail. StructuralProbe applies when shift, COW, initial allocation or growth would otherwise be needed. BoundaryProbe applies when primary authority is exhausted. Both probes offer one initialized stack byte; they spend read-attempt, requested-I/O and initialization credits before Read.</p>
<ol><li>Check the first sticky quota failure and this source's terminal fault. Acquire the shared read-phase guard. Plan and reserve read authority without mutating payload/index. Do not call Read with an empty slice.</li>
<li>Call Read with the chosen initialized span. Validate returned n no larger than q before length arithmetic, slicing, indexing or unsafe handout. Settle the normal held grant. Check whether a callback caused a global failure.</li>
<li>On actual zero, remember EOF for this logical pass. On ordinary error, return it. Neither outcome shifts, COWs, grows or updates the row index when a probe was needed.</li>
<li>On positive input, reserve n count operations before scanning its raw LF bytes. Use the count to plan logical entries, row capacity, byte capacity and all remaining copy/init/fill/write operations. Re-evaluate uniqueness after the callback, since it may have dropped retained owners.</li>
<li>Reserve the chosen publication plan atomically. Complete every fallible candidate payload allocation before moving old bytes in place or changing published offsets. Initialize and copy authorized payloads, fill row offsets, then publish a coherent byte end and row prefix without a remaining fallible step.</li></ol>
<p>For DirectAppend, the Read can dirty an uncommitted initialized tail, but published end does not advance until index/work checks pass. For a structural probe, a positive byte stays in one inline pending slot until the plan commits. A later quota/allocation failure can follow a bounded Read because its LF count was unknowable beforehand. It is not a transactional rewind of an external stream. The source becomes terminal on post-read allocation failure, and resource refusal poisons the shared budget. Retained old values remain intact.</p>
<p>Append a new row batch with n count-scan operations and, when it contains LF, n fill-scan operations plus K*W offset writes. No second scan when K is zero. Reserve E*W old-row copy operations for index growth. A new byte capacity C costs C initialization operations; copies/moves cost only the live L bytes. Candidate capacity fallback is decided before recording any failure.</p></section>
<section id="eof"><h2>Exact limits and temporary EOF</h2>
<p>When source byte credit is exhausted, a separate one-byte BoundaryProbe distinguishes actual EOF from excess source. Actual0 permits completion; a valid one-byte result triggers sticky SourceBytes with requested charged+1 before the extra byte is appended or a truncated text scalar is returned. Never implement source limiting through Read::take, which substitutes EOF at its own cap and can make a larger token appear complete. This follows the pinned <a href="https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/blob/e408947bfd200af42db322daf0fadfe7e26d3bd1/library/std/src/io/mod.rs#L1239">Take behavior</a> and the existing text completion rule.</p>
<p>Structural probes avoid allocation just to find EOF, including a full shared window with no resident headroom. A valid empty source needs row 0 but no byte block. Probe work and I/O quota must still be available; spending the final primary byte does not grant free unlimited EOF checks.</p>
<p>Add begin_read_pass to the internal data-source protocol with a default no-op. Call it once at read_next entry. Checked streams reset a closed pass state to Open. An actual nonempty-span Read returning zero sets EndObserved. Repeated fill calls within that pass return cached zero without I/O; the next logical next or peek starts a new pass and can observe appended bytes. Do not use a permanently fused EOF flag. Ordinary legacy source callbacks keep their current behavior.</p>
<p>Rust permits temporary EOF, partial reads and blocking callbacks. Read errors report no successful byte count; Interrupted may be retried by a caller. Checked streaming returns one ordinary I/O error per invocation and does not install an unbounded automatic retry loop. These rules come from the pinned <a href="https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/blob/e408947bfd200af42db322daf0fadfe7e26d3bd1/library/std/src/io/mod.rs#L732">Rust 1.94.1 Read contract</a>. Its source also warns that safe Read implementations cannot be trusted for unsafe memory safety. The checked source validates n itself.</p>
<p>Closed containers and binary values may yield before overall EOF. A caller must drain to None to establish whole-source byte compliance. This library cannot turn a mutable file into an immutable snapshot or stop a Read implementation from blocking, allocating, prefetching, or changing its hidden source. The checked claim ends at the supplied Read boundary. A caller-owned <a href="https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/blob/e408947bfd200af42db322daf0fadfe7e26d3bd1/library/std/src/io/buffered/bufreader.rs#L338">BufReader can prefetch</a> beyond that offered span. Morphir's frozen finite original-byte capture remains the preferred fixed-source seam.</p></section>

<tr><td>Read unwinds</td><td>No catch inside the library. RAII clears active-read state, conservatively settles a normal grant and records terminal ReadUnwound without allocation/panic. If the caller catches unwind, retry refuses before Read. Process abort is outside cleanup guarantees.</td></tr>

<tr><td>Wrong selected budget / wrong source mode</td><td>Illegal configuration/use before factory construction effects; not a fabricated resource exhaustion. Old preparation shorthand selects prepared mode only.</td></tr>

<p>Proposed IonError::SourceInput wraps a private-construction failure with closed kind and existing Position evidence. IonError is already non-exhaustive. Keep bounded scalar fields rather than caller strings; do not retain arbitrary input or exception text in a sticky failure. If a callback already triggered global ResourceLimit, settle its held reservation and return that first global failure instead of replacing it with a later source fault. No RefCell borrow may survive into a callback or destructor.</p>
<p>Every new safe/internal mutation route must either carry checked authorization or reject the checked backing. The proof must audit constructors, clone, save, to_owned, public read_from/consume, private grow/shift/make_data_mut, generic index update and active refill. It must also guard at pass entry, so a different source's failure prevents parsing buffered data under a now-failed budget. This does not retroactively claim every old already-yielded scalar/macro operation is guarded.</p></section>

<tr><td>location.rs</td><td>Leased checked append-only index with row 0; generic update refuses. Exact zero-LF path has no hidden location constructor/copy.</td></tr>
<tr><td>result/mod.rs / lib.rs</td><td>Typed bounded source faults, narrow exports; actual compilation checks private construction and returned input type.</td></tr>
<tr><td>New source tests / architecture probe</td><td>Freeze packets before red run; prove actual callback not reached on preflight refusal, exact calls and lease lifetimes. Run real native 64-bit and Wasm 32-bit rather than infer pointer size.</td></tr></tbody></table>
<p>Subsequent work inside the same narrowly scoped source proof adds planner-driven shift/growth/COW and incremental row replacement, then adversarial callbacks and complete mutation audits. Independent review must inspect each path. Until those paths pass, do not describe the minimal tracer as qualified general checked streaming.</p>

<section id="review"><h2>Review decisions</h2>
<p>The recommendation is one common fixed/stream ledger, leased retained storage and probe-before-structural-mutation. Accept the per-pass EOF cache because it preserves future appended-data reads while removing repeated physical EOF calls inside one raw-reader pass. Keep all ordinary constructors unchanged.</p>
<ol><li>Approve or amend the proposed composed source policy and compatibility shorthand. This requires an internal leased prepared-owner extension in the new proof, not changes to the accepted artifact.</li><li>Confirm resident versus cumulative requested payload, logical rows, byte-operation units and read-span charging. No production quota values are proposed.</li><li>Confirm the one-byte lookahead boundary and explicit whole-stream drain requirement. A caller asking for a valid prefix has not qualified its unseen suffix.</li><li>Confirm typed terminal source-input faults and the recoverable nested-read rejection. Arbitrary callback runtime, hidden I/O, process abort and unsafe external corruption remain outside the guarantee.</li><li>Authorize only the smallest isolated source tracer if these choices are accepted. Implementation and a broader bounded-reader claim require separate evidence.</li></ol>
<p>No unresolved need for an additional lexer or a new file protocol was found. The existing parser, source positions, lazy retention model and Read boundary suffice for this proposal. The concrete questions are policy composition, credit units and source-fault semantics, not Ion support removal.</p></section>

Outcome and review boundary

Bind a private, candidate-only configuration lookup scope once at trusted host startup. A later Current-project attempt may inspect the same approved configuration locations to derive the real compiler writer root, module and output path, without granting an enclosing workspace to a provider, guest or browser.

Task 1 is merged in PR #307. Its private LayerStack preserves one ordered policy reducer. This document proposes the next authority and resource seams; none is implemented or advertised. An implementation that is missing must omit the additive profile entirely. A future qualified implementation may separately refuse a legitimate missing or changed runtime grant.

The original 31 source-authored cases remain byte-identical. The accompanying additions are prospective acceptance cases, authored from source and this proposal before any new implementation. No client/model adapter outputs were read or executed.

The startup issuer lives in the trusted CLI shell before provider registration, where run_ui already receives the workspace and original OutOverrides. It deliberately uses ambient authority only there to open required ancestor/mount handles. The SDK can expose an explicit host-only constructor accepting that authority and the existing provider Dir; no constructor takes a wire request, project ID or deserialized grant. The resulting type exposes no Dir, parent traversal, arbitrary candidate path or general read method.

Bind labels to actual handle identities. Preserve both lexical declared paths, which determine compiler module identity, and actual target identities, which authorize reads. Never substitute canonical target spelling for a declared module. Dir::open_parent_dir(AmbientAuthority) is an explicit escalation primitive, not a confined request-time operation. Actual platform acquisition and rename tests must prove the chain; canonical strings alone are insufficient.

Inside the original provider grant, the selected project may be opened after real membership selection. Above that grant, the ancestor chain is fixed at startup. Existing permitted outside aliases need exact startup-sealed targets or existing source-grant proof. A newly introduced outside target refuses; it is not followed by an ambient retry. Missing source directories use the nearest sealed existing directory plus exact candidate-relative suffix, and never expose that parent to guests.

Closed host types and ownership seam

The full ownership API below describes the future output-binding pipeline. The first tracer returns a distinct CandidateMetadataSnapshot. It never constructs CapturedCurrentConfig, a policy result, output binding or raw-content digest.

// Private structural proof types, no public API or wire data.
struct TwoAncestorLookupTrace { /* selected + parent + grandparent grants */ }
struct CandidateMetadataSnapshot { /* observed fixed candidate slots only */ }
struct PresentMetadata { /* identity, regular-file kind, observed length */ }
enum CandidateMetadata { Absent, NonRegular, Present(PresentMetadata) }
// No rawDigest field or digest placeholder; no config content reads.
// No CapturedCurrentConfig, winning-workspace or output-currentness claim.

The fixed trace contains the selected directory and its two explicitly sealed ancestor levels when they exist. It is incomplete structural evidence, not a truncated production scope or full Current search. Without configuration parsing it cannot identify a winning workspace, infer that unexamined ancestors are irrelevant, or emit above-winner Unvisited evidence. Its candidate observations describe only the operations actually performed. Full scope issuance remains pending.

// Existing ConfigLoadOptions, SourceSelection, ConfigSourceKind, RelativePath,
// MorphirConfig and output policy remain the domain vocabulary.
struct CompilerConfigLookup { /* private provider/ancestor/mount handles */ }
struct StartupLookupInputs { /* private host paths, options, cwd, overrides */ }

struct CapturedCurrentConfig { /* immutable source evidence + ordered inputs */ }
struct ResolvedCompilerOutput { /* actual writer root/module + original grant */ }

CompilerConfigLookup::acquire(provider_dir, host_inputs, ambient, issue_budget)
    -> Result<CompilerConfigLookup, LookupIssueError>;

// Parent-only wrapper owns genuine worker/attempt/copy reservations.
owned_attempt.capture_current(&lookup, &selected, &mut lookup_budget)

    -> Result<ResolvedCompilerOutput, BindingError>; // shared reducer, no I/O

owned_attempt.check_current(&lookup, &resolved, &mut verification_budget)
    -> Result<CheckedCurrentBinding, CurrentnessError>;

// All fields/constructors private; no Serialize/Deserialize; Debug redacts
// bytes, secrets, env values and raw identities. No public capability claims.

StartupLookupInputs freezes source-selection intent and path-location inputs, not configuration content. It reuses the actual ConfigLoadOptions source enums and forces Current only at the selected-output operation. Path-affecting environment inputs such as home/XDG/PROGRAMDATA/MORPHIR_HOME are bound at startup. If their later resolution would select an ungranted location, refuse changed scope and require a fresh trusted startup; never auto-expand. Configuration environment values remain attempt inputs under their existing prefix/Skip/Explicit/Process semantics, subject to a bounded capture prerequisite below.

The parent, not a generic SDK ledger, owns host-wide concurrency/copy reservations. Its private worker wrapper makes the reserve-before-effects sequence concrete. An SDK budget does not manufacture that host permit. Selected project proof comes from the actual provider response and owned project directory, not from a raw relative path. A resolved output retains the original grant category and validated compiler module together; RelativePath::root() and an empty compiler module remain distinct domain representations.

Closed candidate evidence is Unvisited | Absent | NonRegular | Present. Present holds privately validated format, file identity, length and raw digest; absent/nonregular records parent/component identity and the exact candidate slot. Unvisited is necessary for shadowed legacy files and ancestors above the winning workspace. It must never masquerade as missing. Failures distinguish scope identity change, authority refusal, unsupported/unproven resource path, I/O, source syntax/profile, and named resource-limit failure. No free-form error string controls fallback.

These proposed numbers refine the earlier plan into separate capture/final-verification phases and require review. They are not generic SDK defaults, wire limits or an adopted numerical profile. Each ledger is a private validated domain type with closed refusal reason, checked arithmetic, cumulative nonrefund semantics and atomic multi-counter reservation before its effect. A parser source preflight plus decoding the same immutable document is one logical source model; both real scans and all actual temporary/materialized copies still consume work/storage credits. The proposed256 MiB cumulative scan cap is a reviewed-policy candidate for multiple passes, not permission for an unmetered rescan. Scalar-parser internals still need a source-derived scan bound or real charge hook; token counts alone do not prove it. Do not hide multiple allocations behind that one-model convention.

Logical payload, allocator capacity, metadata and scratch must be inventoried separately. A64 MiB source cap alone is neither a heap bound nor proof that an eager parser cannot multiply memory. Startup path inputs are already host-owned outside capture, but each new internal copy and every retained handle/slot is bounded. Acquisition needs its own finite metadata/path budget; an externally owned input is not permission to copy it unmetered.

<h1>Current output binding: startup lookup proposal v2</h1><p class="meta">morphir-etg2.22.1 · 19 October 2026 · Task2 clarified design · Task1 merged · private metadata tracer only</p><nav class="toc" aria-label="Contents"><ul><li><a href="#outcome">Outcome and review boundary</a></li><li><a href="#authority">Keep four authorities separate</a></li><li><a href="#types">Closed host types and ownership seam</a></li><li><a href="#capture">Exact candidate capture and lookup order</a></li><li><a href="#limits">Candidate finite policy with exact charging</a></li><li><a href="#parsers">Parser feasibility and remaining proof seams</a></li><li><a href="#freshness">Final currentness and compiler lock sequence</a></li><li><a href="#cases">Source-authored acceptance additions</a></li><li><a href="#task-1">Task 1: private startup lookup tracer</a></li><li><a href="#task-2">Task 2: bounded policy capture and reducer</a></li><li><a href="#task-3">Task 3: parent integration and release boundary</a></li><li><a href="#sources">Evidence and decisions still needed</a></li></ul></nav><section id="outcome"><h2>Outcome and review boundary</h2><p>Bind a private, candidate-only configuration lookup scope once at trusted host startup. A later Current-project attempt may inspect the same approved configuration locations to derive the real compiler writer root, module and output path, without granting an enclosing workspace to a provider, guest or browser.</p><p>Task 1 is merged in PR #307. Its private <code>LayerStack</code> preserves one ordered policy reducer. This document proposes the next authority and resource seams; none is implemented or advertised. An implementation that is missing must omit the additive profile entirely. A future qualified implementation may separately refuse a legitimate missing or changed runtime grant.</p><p>The original 31 source-authored cases remain byte-identical. The accompanying additions are prospective acceptance cases, authored from source and this proposal before any new implementation. No client/model adapter outputs were read or executed.</p></section><section id="authority"><h2>Keep four authorities separate</h2><figure style="margin:1rem 0"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="340" height="380" viewBox="0 0 340 380" style="max-width:100%;height:auto" role="img" aria-labelledby="scope-diagram-title scope-diagram-desc"><title id="scope-diagram-title">Host lookup stays separate from provider and output authority</title><desc id="scope-diagram-desc">Trusted startup seals configuration lookup only. A reserved attempt captures exact candidates, then the shared policy derives output facts. Original provider, guest and output grants remain unchanged.</desc><g fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5"><rect x="10" y="10" width="320" height="64" rx="8"/><path d="M170 74 V100 M165 95 L170 100 L175 95"/><rect x="10" y="102" width="320" height="64" rx="8"/><path d="M170 166 V192 M165 187 L170 192 L175 187"/><rect x="10" y="194" width="320" height="64" rx="8"/><path d="M170 258 V284 M165 279 L170 284 L175 279"/><rect x="10" y="286" width="320" height="78" rx="8" stroke-dasharray="5 4"/></g><g fill="currentColor" text-anchor="middle" font-family="system-ui,sans-serif" font-size="14"><text x="170" y="36">Trusted CLI startup</text><text x="170" y="57">seals exact config lookup handles</text><text x="170" y="128">Owned attempt reserves first</text><text x="170" y="149">captures present and missing slots</text><text x="170" y="220">Shared Current policy</text><text x="170" y="241">writer root + module + fingerprint</text><text x="170" y="310">Original grants stay unchanged</text><text x="170" y="332">provider / guest root</text><text x="170" y="353">provider-confined or explicit output</text></g></svg><figcaption>Configuration lookup supplies policy facts. It does not widen source or output authority.</figcaption></figure><div style="max-width:100%;overflow-x:auto" tabindex="0" role="region" aria-label="Comparison table; scroll horizontally if needed"><table><thead><tr><th>Authority</th><th>Producer and permitted use</th><th>Never implies</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>Provider directory</td><td>The original trusted CLI workspace and its existing confined source/alias policy. Actual installed guest membership remains authoritative.</td><td>An enclosing workspace or sibling source grant.</td></tr><tr><td>Configuration lookup</td><td>Host startup obtains exact directory handles and supported candidate templates needed by existing Current lookup; only private candidate operations use them.</td><td>Generic file reads, output reads, guest root expansion or client-selected mounts.</td></tr><tr><td>Output read grant</td><td>The existing provider-root-confined path, or the original explicit flag/nonempty captured output environment override.</td><td>Any grant merely because configuration resolved outside the provider root.</td></tr><tr><td>Attempt ownership</td><td>Parent worker/copy/attempt reservation acquired before request-time metadata, reads, parser work or guest invocation.</td><td>A caller-created label, public serialized permit or client refresh that expands scope.</td></tr></tbody></table></div><p>The startup issuer lives in the trusted CLI shell before provider registration, where <code>run_ui</code> already receives the workspace and original <code>OutOverrides</code>. It deliberately uses ambient authority only there to open required ancestor/mount handles. The SDK can expose an explicit host-only constructor accepting that authority and the existing provider Dir; no constructor takes a wire request, project ID or deserialized grant. The resulting type exposes no Dir, parent traversal, arbitrary candidate path or general read method.</p><p>Bind labels to actual handle identities. Preserve both lexical declared paths, which determine compiler module identity, and actual target identities, which authorize reads. Never substitute canonical target spelling for a declared module. <code>Dir::open_parent_dir(AmbientAuthority)</code> is an explicit escalation primitive, not a confined request-time operation. Actual platform acquisition and rename tests must prove the chain; canonical strings alone are insufficient.</p><p>Inside the original provider grant, the selected project may be opened after real membership selection. Above that grant, the ancestor chain is fixed at startup. Existing permitted outside aliases need exact startup-sealed targets or existing source-grant proof. A newly introduced outside target refuses; it is not followed by an ambient retry. Missing source directories use the nearest sealed existing directory plus exact candidate-relative suffix, and never expose that parent to guests.</p><a href="https://github.com/finos/morphir/blob/19b05c00acd6e2493a37ae3374f7754e795723da/crates/morphir/src/commands/ui/mod.rs#L39">crates/<wbr>morphir/<wbr>src/<wbr>commands/<wbr>ui/<wbr>mod.rs:39</a>; <a href="https://github.com/finos/morphir/blob/19b05c00acd6e2493a37ae3374f7754e795723da/crates/morphir/src/commands/ui/provider/project_model.rs#L54">crates/<wbr>morphir/<wbr>src/<wbr>commands/<wbr>ui/<wbr>provider/<wbr>project_model.rs:54</a></section><section id="types"><h2>Closed host types and ownership seam</h2><p class="note">The full ownership API below describes the future output-binding pipeline. The first tracer returns a distinct <code>CandidateMetadataSnapshot</code>. It never constructs <code>CapturedCurrentConfig</code>, a policy result, output binding or raw-content digest.</p><pre><code class="language-rust">// Private structural proof types, no public API or wire data.
struct TwoAncestorLookupTrace { /* selected + parent + grandparent grants */ }
struct CandidateMetadataSnapshot { /* observed fixed candidate slots only */ }
struct PresentMetadata { /* identity, regular-file kind, observed length */ }
enum CandidateMetadata { Absent, NonRegular, Present(PresentMetadata) }
// No rawDigest field or digest placeholder; no config content reads.
// No CapturedCurrentConfig, winning-workspace or output-currentness claim.
</code></pre><p>The fixed trace contains the selected directory and its two explicitly sealed ancestor levels when they exist. It is incomplete structural evidence, not a truncated production scope or full Current search. Without configuration parsing it cannot identify a winning workspace, infer that unexamined ancestors are irrelevant, or emit above-winner Unvisited evidence. Its candidate observations describe only the operations actually performed. Full scope issuance remains pending.</p><pre style="max-width:100%;box-sizing:border-box;overflow-x:auto"><code class="language-rust">// Proposed ownership API, not implemented public API or wire data.
// Existing ConfigLoadOptions, SourceSelection, ConfigSourceKind, RelativePath,
// MorphirConfig and output policy remain the domain vocabulary.
struct CompilerConfigLookup { /* private provider/ancestor/mount handles */ }
struct StartupLookupInputs { /* private host paths, options, cwd, overrides */ }
struct SelectedCompilerProject { /* actual selection + owned project identity */ }
struct CapturedCurrentConfig { /* immutable source evidence + ordered inputs */ }
struct ResolvedCompilerOutput { /* actual writer root/module + original grant */ }
struct CheckedCurrentBinding { /* private final observed-currentness evidence */ }

// Only trusted startup, with an explicit authority token. Does no config parsing.
CompilerConfigLookup::acquire(provider_dir, host_inputs, ambient, issue_budget)
    -> Result<CompilerConfigLookup, LookupIssueError>;

// Parent-only wrapper owns genuine worker/attempt/copy reservations.
owned_attempt.capture_current(&lookup, &selected, &mut lookup_budget)
    -> Result<CapturedCurrentConfig, CaptureError>;

captured.resolve_current(&mut policy_budget)
    -> Result<ResolvedCompilerOutput, BindingError>; // shared reducer, no I/O

owned_attempt.check_current(&lookup, &resolved, &mut verification_budget)
    -> Result<CheckedCurrentBinding, CurrentnessError>;

// All fields/constructors private; no Serialize/Deserialize; Debug redacts
// bytes, secrets, env values and raw identities. No public capability claims.
</code></pre><p><code>StartupLookupInputs</code> freezes source-selection intent and path-location inputs, not configuration content. It reuses the actual <code>ConfigLoadOptions</code> source enums and forces Current only at the selected-output operation. Path-affecting environment inputs such as home/XDG/PROGRAMDATA/MORPHIR_HOME are bound at startup. If their later resolution would select an ungranted location, refuse changed scope and require a fresh trusted startup; never auto-expand. Configuration environment values remain attempt inputs under their existing prefix/Skip/Explicit/Process semantics, subject to a bounded capture prerequisite below.</p><p>The parent, not a generic SDK ledger, owns host-wide concurrency/copy reservations. Its private worker wrapper makes the reserve-before-effects sequence concrete. An SDK budget does not manufacture that host permit. Selected project proof comes from the actual provider response and owned project directory, not from a raw relative path. A resolved output retains the original grant category and validated compiler module together; <code>RelativePath::root()</code> and an empty compiler module remain distinct domain representations.</p><p>Closed candidate evidence is <code>Unvisited | Absent | NonRegular | Present</code>. Present holds privately validated format, file identity, length and raw digest; absent/nonregular records parent/component identity and the exact candidate slot. <code>Unvisited</code> is necessary for shadowed legacy files and ancestors above the winning workspace. It must never masquerade as missing. Failures distinguish scope identity change, authority refusal, unsupported/unproven resource path, I/O, source syntax/profile, and named resource-limit failure. No free-form error string controls fallback.</p></section><section id="capture"><h2>Exact candidate capture and lookup order</h2><div style="max-width:100%;overflow-x:auto" tabindex="0" role="region" aria-label="Comparison table; scroll horizontally if needed"><table><thead><tr><th>Phase</th><th>Exact behavior and evidence</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>Startup issuance</td><td>Seal provider handle identity, lexical/canonical labels, fixed ancestors and selected system/global/explicit-user mount locations. Limit/open metadata before copying metadata/path arrays; read no config contents. Preserve original output overrides and cwd, with no broader output grant.</td></tr><tr><td>Selected primary</td><td>Probe six modern candidate spellings. Zero modern files then probes morphir.json; one modern shadows legacy; multiple modern files are ambiguity, never fallback. If no selected primary exists, the parent v1 path has no ConfigContext and performs no ancestor lookup.</td></tr><tr><td>System, global</td><td>For a selected primary, process the original Skip/Explicit/Discover roles first, exactly as the legacy loader. System/global workspace.out_dir survives. Portable discovery filtering stays separate.</td></tr><tr><td>Nearest ancestor</td><td>Start at selected root parent and inspect raw primary configuration only. Reuse the existing pure Current member/exclude predicate and actual directory acceptance. Stop at nearest matching workspace. Ambiguous, unreadable, malformed or typed-invalid ordinary ancestor sources are skipped like legacy. Quota/authority/change refusal propagates, never becomes a nonmatch.</td></tr><tr><td>Shared layers</td><td>Apply Task1 LayerStack: defaults/system/global/root with early typed root decode, selected member with scoped out_dir removal, root then member discovered user overrides or one explicit root override, then environment and final typed decode.</td></tr><tr><td>Output decision</td><td>Reuse/factor the same pure flag → nonempty original runtime env → workspace out_dir → default resolver. Return actual root and compiler module. No fake ConfigContext, sidecar-based guess or all-project DetailsCollector.</td></tr></tbody></table></div><p>Candidate templates reuse the existing <code>project_config_candidates</code>, legacy fallback, global/system candidate builders and <code>user_override_candidates</code>. The selected source layout determines its two adjacent override spellings. A configured Explicit user override never activates the member-adjacent discovered user file. Existing path stabilization, per-layer <code>ir.mode</code> normalization, warnings, provenance and first-error sequencing remain meaningful compatibility checks.</p><p>Request-time capture opens only through sealed capabilities. Reserve before every raw buffer growth and actual retained copy; enforce byte limits while reading, not from metadata alone. Bind an open regular file to pre/post identity metadata and hash the bytes actually read. Capture directory-component and alias bindings and both existing/missing competing candidates that affected selection. A shadowed/unvisited file is not read just to fill an inventory. Retain failed ancestor parse evidence without retaining all ancestor ASTs.</p><p>Selected config discovery happens before system/global errors in the actual parent v1 path. Within the SDK, system/global normalization precedes ancestor search, then root/member/user/environment and final decode. Resource checks necessarily add explicit additive refusals, but under-limit valid/error cases must preserve this existing order. Do not eagerly parse every ancestor before a system error or read past a winning ancestor.</p><a href="https://github.com/finos/morphir-rust/blob/3db422d4a40a5378ed2959522f9f11dc55ea4096/crates/morphir-devkit/src/config/discovery.rs#L23">crates/<wbr>morphir-devkit/<wbr>src/<wbr>config/<wbr>discovery.rs:23</a>; <a href="https://github.com/finos/morphir-rust/blob/3db422d4a40a5378ed2959522f9f11dc55ea4096/crates/morphir-devkit/src/config/loader.rs#L226">crates/<wbr>morphir-devkit/<wbr>src/<wbr>config/<wbr>loader.rs:226</a>; <a href="https://github.com/finos/morphir-rust/blob/3db422d4a40a5378ed2959522f9f11dc55ea4096/crates/morphir-devkit/src/config/loader.rs#L453">crates/<wbr>morphir-devkit/<wbr>src/<wbr>config/<wbr>loader.rs:453</a></section><section id="limits"><h2>Candidate finite policy with exact charging</h2><div style="max-width:100%;overflow-x:auto" tabindex="0" role="region" aria-label="Comparison table; scroll horizontally if needed"><table><thead><tr><th>Ledger</th><th>Proposed inclusive ceiling</th><th>Charge before</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>Lookup topology</td><td>128 startup ancestor directories and selected-path depth128;256 retained lookup directory handles;1 MiB new native-encoded path/label bytes. At most1,024 candidate probes/evidence slots in one capture, plus one equally bounded final verification. All checked integer arithmetic.</td><td>Opening/retaining the next handle, constructing path/identity entries, or each candidate metadata probe. Refuse excess, never truncate ancestry.</td></tr><tr><td>Raw config ownership</td><td>64 MiB aggregate retained bytes per capture, shared with the real parent attempt/global byte reservation; max1,024 distinct read slots.</td><td>Read buffer growth and each new owned copy. Share immutable repeated role bytes; reread/parse work still counts each actual pass.</td></tr><tr><td>Final verification</td><td>At most the same1,024 probes and64 MiB bytes hashed using one reserved64 KiB buffer. No second retained64 MiB configuration inventory.</td><td>Each probe/read span; refuse growth or changed length before exceeding reservation. No parser or semantic clone on equal-byte verification.</td></tr><tr><td>Source semantics</td><td>Root0/depth128;100,000 visited source values;64 Mi decoded UTF16 key/string units, aggregate across accepted and attempted source parses.</td><td>Container/scalar creation and retained decoded string copy. Dotted/implicit TOML tables count created values, not merely bracket nesting. Failed work/duplicate visits do not refund.</td></tr><tr><td>Parser work/scratch</td><td>1,000,000 token/event delivery attempts and256 MiB scan-byte debit aggregate across all actual parser passes;64 MiB cumulative requested temporary payload for token/event/scalar scratch, separate from retained semantic string credit. No single source pass scans more than the64 MiB input bound.</td><td>Next token/event and container/scratch growth. Existing APIs do not yet prove all of these stop hooks; no CPU/RSS equality is claimed.</td></tr><tr><td>Normalization/merge/typed copies</td><td>Independent100,000 constructed or copied values,64 Mi UTF16 copied units, depth128;1,000,000 visits/path/origin operations.</td><td>Every clone, insertion, key/path/provenance copy and typed retained string/vector/map. Source and merged-result ledgers never share a single semantic count.</td></tr><tr><td>Patterns</td><td>1,000,000 actual matcher steps, depth128, plus charged character/segment arrays.</td><td>Each recursive ** alternative, character retry/comparison and buffer copy. Exhaustion returns typed refusal, never false nonmatch.</td></tr><tr><td>Environment</td><td>Raw key/value bytes included in64 MiB raw pool; entry/path/node/string copies use the same capture/policy ledgers. A separate bounded process-enumeration API remains required.</td><td>New owned entry, normalization/sort storage, nested-JSON parse and nested-map insertion. A too-large JSON candidate is refusal, not invalid-JSON string fallback.</td></tr></tbody></table></div><p>These proposed numbers refine the earlier plan into separate capture/final-verification phases and require review. They are not generic SDK defaults, wire limits or an adopted numerical profile. Each ledger is a private validated domain type with closed refusal reason, checked arithmetic, cumulative nonrefund semantics and atomic multi-counter reservation before its effect. A parser source preflight plus decoding the same immutable document is one logical source model; both real scans and all actual temporary/materialized copies still consume work/storage credits. The proposed256 MiB cumulative scan cap is a reviewed-policy candidate for multiple passes, not permission for an unmetered rescan. Scalar-parser internals still need a source-derived scan bound or real charge hook; token counts alone do not prove it. Do not hide multiple allocations behind that one-model convention.</p><p>Logical payload, allocator capacity, metadata and scratch must be inventoried separately. A64 MiB source cap alone is neither a heap bound nor proof that an eager parser cannot multiply memory. Startup path inputs are already host-owned outside capture, but each new internal copy and every retained handle/slot is bounded. Acquisition needs its own finite metadata/path budget; an externally owned input is not permission to copy it unmetered.</p></section><section id="parsers"><h2>Parser feasibility and remaining proof seams</h2><div style="max-width:100%;overflow-x:auto" tabindex="0" role="region" aria-label="Comparison table; scroll horizontally if needed"><table><thead><tr><th>Source</th><th>Reusable actual seam</th><th>Compatibility and unresolved proof</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>Generic JSON</td><td>Merged morphir-json ReadBudget checks before_value/before_string before owned Value/string construction. Model DecodeBudget supplies separate source/assembly ledgers.</td><td>Config legacy JSON instead derives LegacyProjectConfig from source and normalizes it. Preserve duplicate-known-field errors, unknown-field ignoring and string dependencies. Do not replace it with model last-wins/literal Value semantics. A same-byte count-only visitor or audited deserialization seed must guard before growth, including ignored subtrees and normalization.</td></tr><tr><td>YAML</td><td>PR305 bounded physical IR reader sets granit flow/block nesting before parsing and checks AST values/strings before ownership; config parse.rs separately has validate_yaml_profile plus serde-saphyr Options/budgets.</td><td>Config forbids null, requires mapping root and quoted timestamp-like scalars, and rejects anchors/aliases/tags/merge/duplicate keys. IR reader is a useful design seam, not a drop-in config decoder or new core dependency. The config preflight currently uses default scanner options; both passes need finite parser depth/scratch before event delivery and actual event limits. Preserve current error roles.</td></tr><tr><td>TOML</td><td>Pinned toml_parser1.1.3 has lazy Lexer iteration, EventReceiver, RecursionGuard, Source Raw::decode_key/decode_scalar and fallible bool StringBuilder push hooks.</td><td>Pinned toml1.1.6 first allocates token Vec with source-length-derived capacity, then events Vec, DeTable, toml::Value and normalized JSON. Public parse_document returns(), and most EventReceiver callbacks cannot stop parsing. A sticky callback alone cannot promise hard work abortion. Need a reviewed stop-capable parser seam or a source-derived reserved upper bound for the complete pass, plus dotted/implicit-table and conversion-copy proofs. No fork/dependency mutation approved.</td></tr><tr><td>Environment</td><td>Existing parse_env_value preserves bool/i64 parsing, JSON only when leading[/{ succeeds, otherwise original raw string; sorted paths preserve shorter-path wins.</td><td>std::env::vars_os may allocate a complete platform snapshot before filtering. Existing code additionally owns lossy strings and parses entries before sorting. Skip/Explicit can support a private first tracer; bounded dynamic Process enumeration remains an eventual prerequisite, not a completed default path. Private-marker/numeric JSON compatibility needs source tests, no silent adoption of the model policy.</td></tr><tr><td>Reducer/provenance</td><td>Task1 LayerStack and morphir-config deep_merge_with_provenance are the one actual policy.</td><td>merge.rs clones base maps and origins, recursively copies descendants and builds provenance path vectors; loader decode_config clones Value before typed decoding. Meter the actual shared pipeline and normalization/typed copies, or pre-reserve a source-proved operation/copy plan. A final postcondition or root+member-only inventory alone is insufficient.</td></tr></tbody></table></div><p>No second JSON/TOML/YAML lexer is proposed. No dependency on core from morphir-config is proposed. The smallest later shared helper extraction should keep serialization-independent budget hooks near existing policy code, with legacy unbounded adapters preserving behavior. Source syntax remains owned by the actual serializer. At present there is no complete pre-growth/work proof for all config formats. This gap blocks any advertised bounded output-binding profile, not Task2's private metadata-only tracer.</p><a href="https://github.com/finos/morphir-rust/blob/3db422d4a40a5378ed2959522f9f11dc55ea4096/crates/morphir-config/src/parse.rs#L64">crates/<wbr>morphir-config/<wbr>src/<wbr>parse.rs:64</a>; <a href="https://github.com/finos/morphir-rust/blob/3db422d4a40a5378ed2959522f9f11dc55ea4096/crates/morphir-config/src/merge.rs#L108">crates/<wbr>morphir-config/<wbr>src/<wbr>merge.rs:108</a>; <a href="https://github.com/finos/morphir-rust/blob/3db422d4a40a5378ed2959522f9f11dc55ea4096/crates/morphir-config/src/env.rs#L59">crates/<wbr>morphir-config/<wbr>src/<wbr>env.rs:59</a></section><section id="freshness"><h2>Final currentness and compiler lock sequence</h2><p>Before final publication, compare the actual selected project and output-directory identities, exact compiler module and configuration fingerprint using the same fixed lookup scope. Fingerprint records scope identity, source-selection options, considered candidate order and states, file/directory/alias identities, raw byte lengths/digests and private environment evidence. Do not expose secret values or a public unkeyed hash oracle for secrets. Startup-authorized source-location inputs are revalidated separately from attempt-time configuration environment values.</p><ol><li>Reserve the parent worker/attempt/copy and local ledgers before request effects.</li><li>Capture and derive Current policy from the actual selected primary and source roles.</li><li>Validate resolved output against the unchanged original output grant, open it through that grant and retain its actual identity.</li><li>Under the genuine existing shared compile lock, validate the record and its module, descriptor, original inventory and content digests. Do not use raw compiler extras as authority.</li><li>Immediately before committing publication, verify the same considered candidate states and source bytes with bounded hash-only reads; recheck source-location/env policy and selected/output identities. Refuse if changed, unavailable, or verification credit is exhausted. Never retry with broader scope, reselect a different output silently or re-invoke a producer.</li><li>Publish the immutable result and release transient capture/verification resources under the parent lifecycle rules.</li></ol><p>Missing-slot evidence is essential: adding a nearer workspace, a competing modern primary, a user override or previously absent global config invalidates the binding. A file moving from malformed to valid can change ancestor selection, so skipped-source bytes are part of observed evidence. Ancestors beyond the chosen workspace remain unvisited and cannot affect that choice unless a considered winner changes.</p><p>Config files are not protected by compile.lock. This sequence observes and compares bounded snapshots; it is not an atomic multi-file filesystem transaction, proof that the compiler used the same config historically, or a forever-latest claim. The new fixed-source factory checks and reserves its source bytes, requested row-index storage and preparation work before allocating them. Readers and retained values share that immutable backing. What is done

The accepted earlier proof covers only its documented text container/cache and symbol-table work. This extension adds prepared fixed-source ownership. It keeps both scopes explicit and leaves the original 883-file proof intact.

The opt-in contract

// Generic configuration variables below are supplied explicitly by the caller.
// This proof selects no Morphir production policy.
let preparation = SourcePreparationLimits::builder()
    .source_bytes(source_bytes)
    .source_instances(source_instances)
    .storage_bytes(requested_payload_bytes)
    .location_entries(row_entries)
    .work_units(preparation_operations)
    .build()?;
let limits = ReaderLimits::builder()
    .max_text_depth(text_depth).cache_bytes(text_cache)
    .child_steps(child_attempts).symbol_slots(symbol_slots)
    .created_symbol_slots(created_slots)
    .source_preparation(preparation).build()?;
let budget = ReaderBudget::new(limits);
let source = budget.prepare_fixed_source(frozen_bytes)?;
let mut reader = source.reader(ion_rs::v1_0::Text)?;

PreparedIonSource has private construction and does not implement IonInput. Only its reader helper creates PreparedIonInput. The helper installs the owner's shared budget when none was selected, accepts that identical budget when supplied, and rejects a different identity before reader construction. It never routes prepared bytes through a fresh IonSlice with empty ownership/location OnceCells.

CounterExact proof meaning
source_bytesCumulative lengths N of newly prepared source owners. Clone/reopen shares an owner without charging primary bytes again; a new owner of equal byte contents is charged again.
source_instancesCumulative owners, including empty sources. Covers the fixed number of owner/header allocations; no equality with heap bytes or RSS.
storage_bytesCumulative requested payload N+E*sizeof(usize), where E is the row count including initial row 0. Allocator rounding and Rc metadata are separate from requested payload.
location_entriesCumulative requested E=1+raw LF count, including empty and binary sources. No Unicode or line-ending conversion.
work_unitsPreparation only: one N-byte counting scan, one N-byte fill scan, one N-byte source copy and E row-offset writes. Total 3N+E. It is not parser scan work, numeric work, location-lookup work, CPU time or total reader work.

Every field is private and validated. Zero is allowed; no default values exist. Overflowing requests become typed refusals before the relevant allocation. Phase one atomically reserves an owner, primary bytes and the count pass. Phase two reserves row entries, requested payload and remaining work before copying/index allocation. Spent credits are never refunded on retry, drop or reader advance. The first quota refusal is sticky across the shared budget.

A prepared source always includes initial row 0, even when empty. Malformed UTF8 remains byte-exact and is rejected later by the existing text parser. Text locations remain 1-based rows and byte columns. Binary public locations remain empty. Source allocation failure is not presented as a quota or heap-availability guarantee; source Rc allocation retains upstream OOM behavior, while row Vec try-reserve failure follows an explicit illegal-operation error path.

The zero-allocation probe is scoped to ownership and location operations on already prepared small literals. Scalar reads, materialization, new reader contexts, Debug formatting, downstream caller-owned copies and other arena/table resources can allocate. These are not covered by a source-payload ownership claim.

+/// Validated, explicitly selected quotas for preparing fixed source ownership.
+/// No numerical defaults or Morphir policy are defined here.
+#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug)]
+pub struct SourcePreparationLimits {
+    source_bytes: usize,
+    source_instances: usize,
+    storage_bytes: usize,
+    location_entries: usize,

+}

+pub struct SourcePreparationLimitsBuilder {
+    source_bytes: Option<usize>,
+    source_instances: Option<usize>,
+    storage_bytes: Option<usize>,
+    location_entries: Option<usize>,
+    work_units: Option<usize>,
+}
+impl SourcePreparationLimits {
+    pub fn builder() -> SourcePreparationLimitsBuilder {
+        SourcePreparationLimitsBuilder::default()
+    }

+impl SourcePreparationLimitsBuilder {
+    pub fn source_bytes(mut self, n: usize) -> Self {
+        self.source_bytes = Some(n);
+        self
+    }
+    pub fn source_instances(mut self, n: usize) -> Self {
+        self.source_instances = Some(n);

+    pub fn storage_bytes(mut self, n: usize) -> Self {
+        self.storage_bytes = Some(n);
+        self
+    }
+    pub fn location_entries(mut self, n: usize) -> Self {
+        self.location_entries = Some(n);
+        self
+    }
+    pub fn work_units(mut self, n: usize) -> Self {
+        self.work_units = Some(n);
+        self
+    }
+    pub fn build(self) -> IonResult<SourcePreparationLimits> {
+        let (
+            Some(source_bytes),
+            Some(source_instances),
+            Some(storage_bytes),
+            Some(location_entries),
+            Some(work_units),
+        ) = (
+            self.source_bytes,
+            self.source_instances,
+            self.storage_bytes,
+            self.location_entries,
+            self.work_units,
+        )
+        else {
+            return Err(IonError::illegal_operation(
+                "all source preparation limits must be set explicitly",
+            ));
+        };
+        if [
+            source_bytes,
+            source_instances,
+            storage_bytes,
+            location_entries,
+            work_units,
+        ]
+        .iter()
+        .any(|&n| n > isize::MAX as usize)
+        {
+            return Err(IonError::illegal_operation(
+                "source preparation limit exceeds supported integer range",
+            ));
+        }
+        Ok(SourcePreparationLimits {
+            source_bytes,
+            source_instances,
+            storage_bytes,
+            location_entries,

+impl PreparedIonSource {
+    pub fn reader<D: Decoder>(
+        &self,
+        config: impl Into<ReadConfig<D>>,
+    ) -> IonResult<Reader<D, PreparedIonInput>> {
+        self.budget.check()?;
+        let mut config = config.into();
+        if let Some(selected) = &config.budget {
+            if !Rc::ptr_eq(&selected.state, &self.budget.state) {
+                return Err(IonError::illegal_operation(
+                    "prepared source reader must use its owning budget",
+                ));
+            }
+        }
+        config.budget = Some(self.budget.clone());
+        Reader::new(
+            config,
+            PreparedIonInput {
+                data: self.data.clone(),
+                position: 0,
+            },
+        )
+    }

+impl ReaderBudget {
+    pub fn prepare_fixed_source(&self, bytes: &[u8]) -> IonResult<PreparedIonSource> {
+        self.check()?;
+        let mut state = self.state.borrow_mut();
+        let limits = state.limits.source_preparation.ok_or_else(|| {
+            IonError::illegal_operation("source preparation limits were not selected")
+        })?;
+        let n = state
+            .usage
+            .preparation
+            .source_bytes
+            .checked_add(bytes.len())
+            .unwrap_or(usize::MAX);
+        state.ensure(ReaderLimitKind::SourceBytes, limits.source_bytes, n, 0)?;
+        let instances = state
+            .usage
+            .preparation
+            .source_instances
+            .checked_add(1)
+            .unwrap_or(usize::MAX);
+        state.ensure(
+            ReaderLimitKind::SourceInstances,
+            limits.source_instances,
+            instances,
+            0,
+        )?;
+        let work = state
+            .usage
+            .preparation
+            .work_units
+            .checked_add(bytes.len())
+            .unwrap_or(usize::MAX);
+        state.ensure(
+            ReaderLimitKind::SourcePreparationWork,
+            limits.work_units,
+            work,
+            0,
+        )?;
+        // Atomic first reservation precedes even the nonallocating LF count pass.
+        state.usage.preparation.source_bytes = n;
+        state.usage.preparation.source_instances = instances;
+        state.usage.preparation.work_units = work;
+        drop(state);
+
+        let entries = memchr::memchr_iter(b'\n', bytes)
+            .count()
+            .checked_add(1)
+            .unwrap_or(usize::MAX);
+        let mut state = self.state.borrow_mut();
+        let location_entries = state
+            .usage
+            .preparation
+            .location_entries
+            .checked_add(entries)
+            .unwrap_or(usize::MAX);
+        state.ensure(
+            ReaderLimitKind::SourceLocationEntries,
+            limits.location_entries,
+            location_entries,
+            0,
+        )?;
+        let payload = entries
+            .checked_mul(std::mem::size_of::<usize>())
+            .and_then(|n| n.checked_add(bytes.len()))
+            .unwrap_or(usize::MAX);
+        let storage = state
+            .usage
+            .preparation
+            .storage_bytes
+            .checked_add(payload)
+            .unwrap_or(usize::MAX);
+        state.ensure(
+            ReaderLimitKind::SourceStorageBytes,
+            limits.storage_bytes,
+            storage,
+            0,
+        )?;
+        let remaining_work = bytes
+            .len()
+            .checked_mul(2)
+            .and_then(|n| n.checked_add(entries))
+            .unwrap_or(usize::MAX);
+        let work = state
+            .usage
+            .preparation
+            .work_units
+            .checked_add(remaining_work)
+            .unwrap_or(usize::MAX);
+        state.ensure(
+            ReaderLimitKind::SourcePreparationWork,
+            limits.work_units,
+            work,
+            0,
+        )?;
+        state.usage.preparation.location_entries = location_entries;
+        state.usage.preparation.storage_bytes = storage;
+        state.usage.preparation.work_units = work;
+        drop(state);
+
+        // Every requested payload and preparation operation has been reserved.
+        // No boxed-slice conversion/shrink or lazy OnceCell can copy these later.
+        let mut rows = Vec::new();
+        rows.try_reserve_exact(entries)
+            .map_err(|_| IonError::illegal_operation("source row-index allocation failed"))?;
+        rows.push(0);
+        rows.extend(memchr::memchr_iter(b'\n', bytes).map(|n| n + 1));
+        let owned: Rc<[u8]> = Rc::from(bytes);
+        Ok(PreparedIonSource {
+            data: Rc::new(PreparedSourceData {
+                bytes: owned,
+                locations: SourceLocationState::from_prepared_rows(rows),
+            }),
+            budget: self.clone(),
+        })
+    }
+}

+struct AllocationProbe;
+#[global_allocator]
+static ALLOCATOR: AllocationProbe = AllocationProbe;
+unsafe impl GlobalAlloc for AllocationProbe {
+    unsafe fn alloc(&self, layout: Layout) -> *mut u8 {
+        let _ = ALLOCATION_COUNT.try_with(|c| {
+            if let Some(n) = c.get() {
+                c.set(Some(n + 1));
+            }

+        unsafe { System.alloc(layout) }

+        let _ = ALLOCATION_COUNT.try_with(|c| {

+            }

+        unsafe { System.alloc_zeroed(layout) }

+        let _ = ALLOCATION_COUNT.try_with(|c| {

+    unsafe fn dealloc(&self, ptr: *mut u8, layout: Layout) {
+        unsafe {

+    ALLOCATION_COUNT.with(|c| {

+    let _reset = Reset;
+    let result = f();
+    let count = ALLOCATION_COUNT.with(|c| c.get().unwrap());

+                offset,

+    }

+    pub fn prepare_fixed_source(&self, bytes: &[u8]) -> IonResult<PreparedIonSource> {

+        let mut state = self.state.borrow_mut();
+        let limits = state.limits.source_preparation.ok_or_else(|| {
+            IonError::illegal_operation("source preparation limits were not selected")

+        let n = state
+            .usage
+            .preparation
+            .source_bytes
+            .checked_add(bytes.len())
+            .unwrap_or(usize::MAX);
+        state.ensure(ReaderLimitKind::SourceBytes, limits.source_bytes, n, 0)?;
+        let instances = state
+            .usage
+            .preparation
+            .source_instances
+            .checked_add(1)
+            .unwrap_or(usize::MAX);
+        state.ensure(
+            ReaderLimitKind::SourceInstances,
+            limits.source_instances,
+            instances,
+            0,
+        )?;
+        let work = state
+            .usage
+            .preparation
+            .work_units
+            .checked_add(bytes.len())
+            .unwrap_or(usize::MAX);
+        state.ensure(
+            ReaderLimitKind::SourcePreparationWork,
+            limits.work_units,
+            work,
+            0,
+        )?;
+        // Atomic first reservation precedes even the nonallocating LF count pass.
+        state.usage.preparation.source_bytes = n;
+        state.usage.preparation.source_instances = instances;
+        state.usage.preparation.work_units = work;
+        drop(state);

+        let entries = memchr::memchr_iter(b'\n', bytes)
+            .count()
+            .checked_add(1)
+            .unwrap_or(usize::MAX);
+        let mut state = self.state.borrow_mut();
+        let location_entries = state
+            .usage
+            .preparation
+            .location_entries
+            .checked_add(entries)
+            .unwrap_or(usize::MAX);
+        state.ensure(
+            ReaderLimitKind::SourceLocationEntries,
+            limits.location_entries,
+            location_entries,
+            0,
+        )?;
+        let payload = entries
+            .checked_mul(std::mem::size_of::<usize>())
+            .and_then(|n| n.checked_add(bytes.len()))
+            .unwrap_or(usize::MAX);
+        let storage = state
+            .usage
+            .preparation
+            .storage_bytes
+            .checked_add(payload)
+            .unwrap_or(usize::MAX);
+        state.ensure(
+            ReaderLimitKind::SourceStorageBytes,
+            limits.storage_bytes,
+            storage,
+            0,
+        )?;
+        let remaining_work = bytes
+            .len()
+            .checked_mul(2)
+            .and_then(|n| n.checked_add(entries))
+            .unwrap_or(usize::MAX);
+        let work = state
+            .usage
+            .preparation
+            .work_units
+            .checked_add(remaining_work)
+            .unwrap_or(usize::MAX);
+        state.ensure(
+            ReaderLimitKind::SourcePreparationWork,
+            limits.work_units,
+            work,
+            0,
+        )?;
+        state.usage.preparation.location_entries = location_entries;
+        state.usage.preparation.storage_bytes = storage;
+        state.usage.preparation.work_units = work;
+        drop(state);
+
+        // Every requested payload and preparation operation has been reserved.
+        // No boxed-slice conversion/shrink or lazy OnceCell can copy these later.

+            .map_err(|_| IonError::illegal_operation("source row-index allocation failed"))?;

+        rows.extend(memchr::memchr_iter(b'\n', bytes).map(|n| n + 1));

+        Ok(PreparedIonSource {
+            data: Rc::new(PreparedSourceData {
+                bytes: owned,
+                locations: SourceLocationState::from_prepared_rows(rows),
+            }),
+            budget: self.clone(),
+        })
+    }

+thread_local! { static ALLOCATION_COUNT: Cell<Option<usize>> = const { Cell::new(None) }; }
+struct AllocationProbe;
+#[global_allocator]
+static ALLOCATOR: AllocationProbe = AllocationProbe;
+unsafe impl GlobalAlloc for AllocationProbe {
+    unsafe fn alloc(&self, layout: Layout) -> *mut u8 {
+        let _ = ALLOCATION_COUNT.try_with(|c| {
+            if let Some(n) = c.get() {
+                c.set(Some(n + 1));
+            }
+        });
+        unsafe { System.alloc(layout) }
+    }

+        let _ = ALLOCATION_COUNT.try_with(|c| {

+            }

+        let _ = ALLOCATION_COUNT.try_with(|c| {
+            if let Some(n) = c.get() {

+fn allocations<T>(f: impl FnOnce() -> T) -> (T, usize) {
+    struct Reset;
+    impl Drop for Reset {

+        }
+    }
+    ALLOCATION_COUNT.with(|c| {
+        assert!(c.get().is_none());
+        c.set(Some(0));
+    });
+    let _reset = Reset;
+    let result = f();
+    let count = ALLOCATION_COUNT.with(|c| c.get().unwrap());

+#[test]
+fn incomplete_stream_retries_do_not_refund_cache_or_iterator_work() {
+    use std::{cell::Cell, io::Read};
+    struct OneByte<'a> {
+        remaining: &'a [u8],
+        count: Rc<Cell<usize>>,
+    }
+    impl Read for OneByte<'_> {
+        fn read(&mut self, out: &mut [u8]) -> std::io::Result<usize> {
+            let n = out.len().min(self.remaining.len()).min(1);
+            out[..n].copy_from_slice(&self.remaining[..n]);
+            self.remaining = &self.remaining[n..];
+            self.count.set(self.count.get() + n);
+            Ok(n)
+        }
+    }
+    let source = b"[0,0,0,0]";
+    let mut policy = limits(10);
+    policy.cache_bytes = 7 * text_expr_size();
+    let budget = ReaderBudget::new(policy);
+    let read = Rc::new(Cell::new(0));
+    let input = crate::lazy::streaming_raw_reader::IonStream::new(OneByte {
+        remaining: source,
+        count: read.clone(),
+    });
+    let mut reader = Reader::new(
+        Text.with_catalog(EmptyCatalog).with_budget(budget.clone()),
+        input,
+    )
+    .unwrap();
+    assert!(
+        matches!(reader.next(),Err(IonError::ResourceLimit(e)) if e.kind()==ReaderLimitKind::TextCacheBytes)
+    );
+    let usage = budget.state.borrow().usage;
+    assert!(usage.cache_bytes > 0);
+    assert!(usage.child_steps > usage.cache_pushes);
+    assert!(
+        read.get() < source.len(),
+        "refuse while source is still partial"
+    );
+    assert_eq!(usage.active_containers, 0);
+}

Ion fixed-source preparation: reviewed proposal and isolated implementation scope

This complete proposal is historical design evidence. Root review authorized only Task 2A: five explicitly configured generic counters, preparation work 3N+E, factory-only same-budget readers, shared immutable byte/index owners and refusal before every payload mutation. No production numbers, streaming, scalar/numeric implementation, SDK dependency selection, vendor fork or release were authorized. The implementation is isolated in a fresh proof directory; the accepted original Task 1 packet remains immutable. Source review found no material issue within that scope. Final replay and target receipts remain pending before acceptance.

Ion reader budgets: the next isolated proof

morphir-etg2.22.1 · 18 October 2026 · Task 2 proposal, revision1 · Implementation and numerical policy await review

Prepare a fixed source once, before the reader exposes lazy values. Reserve its owned bytes and row index before allocation, then share those immutable owners through retention and location calls. This is the smallest next proof that matches Morphir's already captured finite sources.

This document proposes Task 2A. It does not change the accepted Task 1 proof, the SDK, dependency selection, original fixtures or production limits. Ordinary borrowed and streaming inputs keep their existing behavior. Task 2A alone would not qualify a complete bounded Ion reader.

Scope and evidence

The broader Morphir profile retains separate limits for primary source, parsed application values, assembled model and output. Primary source is 64 MiB aggregate; application depth uses root 0 / depth 128, with 100,000 application values across files. Annotations count according to the MoonBit envelope. Each parsed and assembled phase has its own 64 Mi decoded key/string UTF16-unit budget. Output has its own 64 MiB budget. These semantic counters are independent of the physical reader counters below. None are new generic ion-rs defaults.

Task 1's physical reader proof is partial. Its shared sticky refusal does not promise that every already-yielded lazy scalar read is guarded. This proposal preserves that distinction. It also preserves original bytes when a later checked decode refuses.

Why preparation must precede lazy values

A fallible wrapper around Reader::new is insufficient. The current fixed source can allocate after it has yielded a value, through APIs that cannot return a limit error.
