Task 1: prepared source contract

This task numbering belongs to this proposal; the accepted earlier proof remains Task 1 in its original report. Call this tranche Task 2A in the campaign. Add an optional validated preparation block to the existing proof's ReaderLimits. Absence preserves the original partial configuration; trying the new preparation method without it returns a configuration error.

// Proposed API shape. Not implemented or compiled.
pub struct SourcePreparationLimits { /* private validated counters */ }
pub struct PreparedIonSource { /* private shared owner and ReaderBudget */ }
pub struct PreparedIonInput { /* public return type, no public constructor */ }

// SourcePreparationLimits::builder() requires all five explicit counters:
// source_bytes, source_instances, storage_bytes, location_entries, work_units.
// ReaderLimitsBuilder::source_preparation(validated_limits) is optional.
impl ReaderBudget {
    pub fn prepare_fixed_source(&self, bytes: &[u8])
        -> IonResult<PreparedIonSource>;
}
impl PreparedIonSource {
    pub fn reader<D: Decoder>(&self, config: impl Into<ReadConfig<D>>)
        -> IonResult<Reader<D, PreparedIonInput>>;
}
// Ordinary Reader::new(config, borrowed_bytes_or_stream) stays legacy.
// PreparedIonSource intentionally does not implement IonInput.
// PreparedIonInput implements IonInput internally; only reader() constructs it.

The reader helper installs the owner's shared budget if config has none, accepts exactly the same budget identity if already supplied, and rejects a different identity before reader construction. A private prepared datasource directly shares the owner. It never creates an IonSlice with empty OnceCells. This avoids changing the public IonInput trait or making existing infallible ownership APIs fallible. A type name that is only externally constructible through a checked factory records the invariant.

CounterProposed meaning
source_bytesCumulative original byte lengths of newly prepared owners across files. Reopening or cloning the same owner does not charge it again; preparing the same byte contents as a new owner does.
source_instancesCumulative prepared owners, including empty sources. Bounds fixed owner/header overhead; no equality with allocated heap bytes or RSS.
storage_bytesCumulative requested payload bytes: N source bytes plus E*sizeof(usize) row offsets. Reserve before requesting either allocation. Allocator rounding, Rc headers and allocator failure are not counted as exact payload equality.
location_entriesCumulative requested row entries E=1+number of LF bytes, including initial row 0 for empty and binary inputs. Checked before index allocation.
work_unitsOnly preparation operations: N bytes for the counting scan, N for source copy, N for the index-fill scan, E row-offset writes. Total3N+E. Counts logical operations, not CPU time, parser scan work or location lookup work.

All counters have private validated fields, permit zero, and use checked arithmetic. Requested per-allocation lengths must fit isize::MAX; cross-file additions and E*sizeof(usize) are checked before allocation. No generic default numbers are proposed. This preparation ledger is separate from the 100,000-value application ledger, Task 1 arena/cache attempts and output.

  1. Check the shared sticky failure, then atomically reserve one owner, N primary bytes and N counting-scan units before scanning or allocating payload.
  2. Use the existing raw LF rule to count E without allocating. Checked-reserve E row entries, requested payload N+E*sizeof(usize), and remaining2N+E work before any source/index allocation.
  3. Allocate one immutable byte backing and a row-index buffer with the checked requested capacity. Fill bytes once and row offsets once. A private constructor wraps that completed index without first allocating vec[0]. Avoid an extra Vec-to-Rc/boxed-slice payload conversion that silently copies or shrinks into another allocation.
  4. Publish the prepared owner only after construction succeeds. The index is immutable thereafter; last-row lookup cursor may remain a Cell. One owner counter covers a fixed, documented number of metadata allocations.
  5. Pass existing Reader construction the private prepared datasource. All returned IoBuffer views use a private prepared constructor that directly shares byte and location state.

A first quota failure becomes the existing typed sticky refusal with a new closed ReaderLimitKind case for the relevant counter. Later guarded calls return that same refusal before scanning or allocating. Work and allocation credits are never refunded on retry, reader advance, drop or failed preparation. Failure during the count pass consumes the reserved scan work. No partial owner escapes. Invalid configuration and attempts to mutate an immutable retained view use existing illegal-operation errors; they are not manufactured quota failures.

The proposal does not convert allocator OOM into a quota guarantee. Try-reserve errors should propagate through the existing allocation/error policy where APIs support them. Exact source-level preflight and requested payload limits are the proof target; generic heap availability is a separate property.

Decimal input work derivation

This is a source-backed derivation for later numeric work. It does not adopt a numeric quota or make the proposed Task 2A patch larger. The old 65536-byte token cap and earlier weighted decimal formula are not used.

Ion text integer and decimal coefficient reading first copy sanitized digits. UIntData tries u128, then calls BigUint only on positive overflow. Floats instead use Rust f64 parsing. These are different paths with different costs. See matched integer, float, decimal and UIntData fallback.

For num-bigint 0.4.8, BigDigit is 32 bits on 32-bit targets and64 bits on 64-bit targets. Decimal grouping uses the largest power of10 that fits a digit, so p=9 or 19. This follows cfg_digit, BigDigit and get_radix_base, not the host used to write this proposal.

Let d be the nonempty sanitized decimal digit count passed to BigUint after the u128 overflow branch. BigUint creates a d-byte normalized digit vector, then groups the digits into m=ceil(d/p) chunks. The head has h=d-p*(m-1) digits, with 1≤h≤p. For each later chunk, it may push one zero limb, traverses the current limbs with mac_with_carry, folds the chunk into a primitive digit, then adds that digit. See from_radix_digits_be, digit normalization and add2 carry propagation.

// Mathematical visit bounds for the BigUint decimal fallback only.
// W=32 => p=9. W=64 => p=19. d>=1.
m = ceil(d / p)
h = d - p * (m - 1)
// Before tail iteration j, 1<=j<=m-1, data.len() <= j+1.
multiply_limb_visits <= sum(k, k=2..m) = m*(m+1)/2 - 1
add_limb_visits      <= sum(k, k=2..m) = m*(m+1)/2 - 1
primitive_digit_folds = d
peak_logical_data_len <= m
// Distinct counters. No invented weighting into CPU time or wall-clock units.

The induction starts with one limb. A later iteration adds at most one limb before multiplication. The one-limb add visits its first limb and, only if carry remains, at most the remaining limbs. This bounds both walks by the same sum. Debug-build validation and normalization walks add linear work and are not hidden inside a CPU claim. Leading zero limbs and early carry termination reduce actual work; the bound is deliberately conservative.

The table is symbolic arithmetic, stored in numeric-derivation.json. It is not measured conversion output. Forty ASCII 9 digits force u128 overflow. They give S32=14 and S64=5. A future numeric proof can accept exactly these separate credits, reject one less, and instrument the BigUint entry so refusal occurs before its digit-vector allocation or arithmetic. A decimal coefficient with many leading zeros that still fits u128 must retain its fast path and receive only the relevant scan/copy checks.

The smallest future insertion is a private preflight callback or checked sibling at the UIntData positive-overflow branch, immediately before BigUint::from_str_radix. Preserve the existing helper for legacy callers. The caller supplies counted digits and radix from the existing matched parser; no second lexer. Original token scan and SmallVec sanitization need their own earlier guards. Thus this insertion alone would bound costly BigUint conversion, not all scalar allocation.

Validate every counter sum/product before conversion. d=0 follows the parser's existing invalid-input behavior. For decimal result size, bits ≤4d is a safe integer upper bound and limbs≤ceil(4d/W); the loop also bounds peak logical data length by m. Neither bound is an exact allocation request. The std implementation estimates initial limb Vec capacity using floating log2, while no_std uses another estimate. Vec growth, normalization/shrink and downstream integer conversion may allocate or copy. A storage proposal must cover those actual requests before claiming a physical byte bound. This document does not adopt an unproved aggregate storage formula.

Binary, floats and formatting

Binary magnitude conversion does not use repeated decimal multiply/add. Ion 1.0 read_int calls DecodedUInt; the BigUint fallback from_bytes_be copies and reverses the input bytes, then bitwise packing visits bounded-size chunks. This is linear byte/limb materialization with distinct copy/storage obligations. Binary decimal coefficients use the binary integer path. Hex/binary text radix conversion likewise uses bitwise packing after normalization. Charging these paths the decimal quadratic bound would unnecessarily restrict valid within-profile sources.

Text float parsing calls f64::from_str after a sanitized copy; it does not call BigInt. The standard library's actual conversion work, error formatting and scratch storage need their own audit. Text decimal exponent parsing uses i64. Its scan/copy and error-message allocation differ again. Current MatchedDecimal uses u16 token-offset/length fields, so existing lexical acceptance constraints must be checked before any future claim about arbitrary large valid decimal tokens.

A bounded output writer cannot by itself bound formatting. Decimal::fmt calls coefficient.to_string before writing. Integer/decimal text formatting delegates Display, while count_decimal_digits formats large numbers just to count digits. Do not call that function as a cheap preflight.

num-bigint output pathActual work and missing proof
to_radix_digits_lePreallocates output digits, clones magnitude, then selects full or half radix base depending on architecture. Full decimal grouping is 9/19 digits; half grouping is 4/9.
Small conversion, div_rem_digitRepeated division visits each current limb. A small-number output bound must count these divisions and primitive digit emission, not reuse input's multiplication counter.
32-limb switch and divide and conquerAt ≥32 limbs, build large bases by repeated squaring; divide by a large base; recursively process two chunks; below 8 limbs use the small routine and pad. General division, multiplication, recursion and scratch storage need a separate derivation.

There is no complete numeric formatting-work formula in this proposal. The reviewed code disproves a blanket claim that formatting always follows the simple quadratic input loop. A later tranche must guard magnitude clone, output digit storage, base squaring, division scratch and Decimal's temporary string before entering Display. Use bit-length metadata for a conservative output-size preflight without decimal formatting, then prove the conversion-work/storage model against the locked implementation. Keep exact formatting and negative-zero semantics unchanged.

There is also an error-propagation obligation. Decimal::fmt unwraps the write of its negative sign. If a bounded formatter returns fmt::Error at that write, this path can panic instead of propagating refusal. A future bounded formatter must prove its stop/error behavior as well as its byte and work bounds. This is a source finding, not a newly executed failing test or an authorized source fix.

Review decisions

The remaining technical questions are the exact private prepared backing/index representation and allocator-error mapping within upstream conventions. These require source review of an authorized patch. They do not justify new production caps. A full numeric formatter bound also remains genuinely unresolved; the evidence here identifies the actual divide-and-conquer path rather than pretending the input bound covers it.

<h1>Ion reader budgets: the next isolated proof</h1>
<p class="meta">morphir-etg2.22.1 · 18 October 2026 · Task 2 proposal, revision1 · Implementation and numerical policy await review</p>
<p>Prepare a fixed source once, before the reader exposes lazy values. Reserve its owned bytes and row index before allocation, then share those immutable owners through retention and location calls. This is the smallest next proof that matches Morphir's already captured finite sources.</p>
<div class="note">This document proposes Task 2A. It does not change the accepted Task 1 proof, the SDK, dependency selection, original fixtures or production limits. Ordinary borrowed and streaming inputs keep their existing behavior. Task 2A alone would not qualify a complete bounded Ion reader.</div>
<nav class="toc" aria-label="Contents"><ul>
<li><a href="#scope">Scope and evidence</a></li><li><a href="#paths">Why preparation must precede lazy values</a></li>
<li><a href="#task-1">Task 1: prepared source contract</a></li><li><a href="#ownership">Ownership proof obligations</a></li>
<li><a href="#task-2">Task 2: proposed proof tests</a></li><li><a href="#numeric">Decimal input work derivation</a></li>
<li><a href="#formatting">Binary, floats and formatting</a></li><li><a href="#remaining">Remaining reader work</a></li>
<li><a href="#decisions">Review decisions</a></li><li><a href="#sources">Source and preservation receipt</a></li>
</ul></nav>

<section id="scope"><h2>Scope and evidence</h2>
<ul><li><label><input type="checkbox" checked disabled> Task 1 has a reviewed isolated patch for opt-in text container depth/cache attempts and symbol/import growth. Its fourteen focused tests and source packet remain unchanged.</label></li>
<li><label><input type="checkbox" checked disabled> This proposal traces source ownership, locations, decimal conversion and formatting in pinned sources.</label></li>
<li><label><input type="checkbox" disabled> Implement and qualify prepared fixed sources, after review of this proposal.</label></li>
<li><label><input type="checkbox" disabled> Complete streaming, scalar, scanner, numeric, storage, application and output checks before a full profile claim or SDK integration.</label></li></ul>
<p>The broader Morphir profile retains separate limits for primary source, parsed application values, assembled model and output. Primary source is 64 MiB aggregate; application depth uses root 0 / depth 128, with 100,000 application values across files. Annotations count according to the MoonBit envelope. Each parsed and assembled phase has its own 64 Mi decoded key/string UTF16-unit budget. Output has its own 64 MiB budget. These semantic counters are independent of the physical reader counters below. None are new generic ion-rs defaults.</p>
<p>Task 1's physical reader proof is partial. Its shared sticky refusal does not promise that every already-yielded lazy scalar read is guarded. This proposal preserves that distinction. It also preserves original bytes when a later checked decode refuses.</p></section>

<section id="paths"><h2>Why preparation must precede lazy values</h2>
<p>A fallible wrapper around <code>Reader::new</code> is insufficient. The current fixed source can allocate after it has yielded a value, through APIs that cannot return a limit error.</p>
<table><thead><tr><th>Current path</th><th>Allocation or work</th><th>Insertion requirement</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td><a href="https://github.com/amazon-ion/ion-rust/blob/a1df66475c76605dd31c8566ef11f50f07fe8111/src/lazy/streaming_raw_reader.rs#L343">IonSlice::save_io_buffer</a></td><td>First call copies the entire source into an Rc slice through OnceCell.</td><td>Prepared datasource must already own the source. Do not wrap it in a fresh IonSlice.</td></tr>

<section class="task" id="task-1"><h3>Task 1: prepared source contract</h3>
<p>This task numbering belongs to this proposal; the accepted earlier proof remains Task 1 in its original report. Call this tranche <strong>Task 2A</strong> in the campaign. Add an optional validated preparation block to the existing proof's ReaderLimits. Absence preserves the original partial configuration; trying the new preparation method without it returns a configuration error.</p>
<pre><code class="language-rust">// Proposed API shape. Not implemented or compiled.
pub struct SourcePreparationLimits { /* private validated counters */ }
pub struct PreparedIonSource { /* private shared owner and ReaderBudget */ }
pub struct PreparedIonInput { /* public return type, no public constructor */ }

// SourcePreparationLimits::builder() requires all five explicit counters:
// source_bytes, source_instances, storage_bytes, location_entries, work_units.
// ReaderLimitsBuilder::source_preparation(validated_limits) is optional.
impl ReaderBudget {
    pub fn prepare_fixed_source(&self, bytes: &[u8])
        -> IonResult<PreparedIonSource>;
}
impl PreparedIonSource {
    pub fn reader<D: Decoder>(&self, config: impl Into<ReadConfig<D>>)
        -> IonResult<Reader<D, PreparedIonInput>>;
}
// Ordinary Reader::new(config, borrowed_bytes_or_stream) stays legacy.
// PreparedIonSource intentionally does not implement IonInput.
// PreparedIonInput implements IonInput internally; only reader() constructs it.</code></pre>
<p>The reader helper installs the owner's shared budget if config has none, accepts exactly the same budget identity if already supplied, and rejects a different identity before reader construction. A private prepared datasource directly shares the owner. It never creates an IonSlice with empty OnceCells. This avoids changing the public IonInput trait or making existing infallible ownership APIs fallible. A type name that is only externally constructible through a checked factory records the invariant.</p>
<table><thead><tr><th>Counter</th><th>Proposed meaning</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>source_bytes</td><td>Cumulative original byte lengths of newly prepared owners across files. Reopening or cloning the same owner does not charge it again; preparing the same byte contents as a new owner does.</td></tr>
<tr><td>source_instances</td><td>Cumulative prepared owners, including empty sources. Bounds fixed owner/header overhead; no equality with allocated heap bytes or RSS.</td></tr>
<tr><td>storage_bytes</td><td>Cumulative requested payload bytes: N source bytes plus E*sizeof(usize) row offsets. Reserve before requesting either allocation. Allocator rounding, Rc headers and allocator failure are not counted as exact payload equality.</td></tr>
<tr><td>location_entries</td><td>Cumulative requested row entries E=1+number of LF bytes, including initial row 0 for empty and binary inputs. Checked before index allocation.</td></tr>
<tr><td>work_units</td><td>Only preparation operations: N bytes for the counting scan, N for source copy, N for the index-fill scan, E row-offset writes. Total3N+E. Counts logical operations, not CPU time, parser scan work or location lookup work.</td></tr>
</tbody></table>
<p>All counters have private validated fields, permit zero, and use checked arithmetic. Requested per-allocation lengths must fit isize::MAX; cross-file additions and E*sizeof(usize) are checked before allocation. No generic default numbers are proposed. This preparation ledger is separate from the 100,000-value application ledger, Task 1 arena/cache attempts and output.</p>
<ol><li>Check the shared sticky failure, then atomically reserve one owner, N primary bytes and N counting-scan units before scanning or allocating payload.</li>
<li>Use the existing raw LF rule to count E without allocating. Checked-reserve E row entries, requested payload N+E*sizeof(usize), and remaining2N+E work before any source/index allocation.</li>
<li>Allocate one immutable byte backing and a row-index buffer with the checked requested capacity. Fill bytes once and row offsets once. A private constructor wraps that completed index without first allocating vec[0]. Avoid an extra Vec-to-Rc/boxed-slice payload conversion that silently copies or shrinks into another allocation.</li>
<li>Publish the prepared owner only after construction succeeds. The index is immutable thereafter; last-row lookup cursor may remain a Cell. One owner counter covers a fixed, documented number of metadata allocations.</li>
<li>Pass existing Reader construction the private prepared datasource. All returned IoBuffer views use a private prepared constructor that directly shares byte and location state.</li></ol>
<p>A first quota failure becomes the existing typed sticky refusal with a new closed ReaderLimitKind case for the relevant counter. Later guarded calls return that same refusal before scanning or allocating. Work and allocation credits are never refunded on retry, reader advance, drop or failed preparation. Failure during the count pass consumes the reserved scan work. No partial owner escapes. Invalid configuration and attempts to mutate an immutable retained view use existing illegal-operation errors; they are not manufactured quota failures.</p>
<p>The proposal does not convert allocator OOM into a quota guarantee. Try-reserve errors should propagate through the existing allocation/error policy where APIs support them. Exact source-level preflight and requested payload limits are the proof target; generic heap availability is a separate property.</p></section>

<section id="ownership"><h2>Ownership proof obligations</h2>
<p>The guarantee applies to the prepared source/index payload and its ownership operations. Reading a retained scalar can still allocate unrelated scalar or arena data until later tranches are complete.</p>

<tr><td>Prepared source/input clone</td><td>Clone Rc handles and positions only. No fresh source object, OnceCell, Vec, row fill or primary-source reservation.</td><td>Rc pointer identity, unchanged payload capacities and preparation counters over repeated clones/readers.</td></tr>

LazyElement stores EncodingContext by value and rebinds spans into those same bytes. It does not allocate a fresh Rc<EncodingContext>.</td><td>Retain a literal then advance/drop original reader and owner. Read/location remain correct without additional source/index allocation.</td></tr>

<p>Insertion files are <code>src/read_limits.rs</code>, a new prepared-source module, <code>src/lazy/streaming_raw_reader.rs</code>, <code>src/location.rs</code> and exports in <code>src/lib.rs</code>. Reuse existing shared failure state and ReadConfig. Do not redesign the parser, add another lexer, change ownership method return types or alter Task 1 frozen tests.</p>
<p>Malformed UTF8 stays malformed. Preparation counts raw LF bytes and copies raw bytes without UTF8 decoding, normalization or replacement. The existing parser remains responsible for lexical errors. Existing text locations are 1-based row and <em>byte</em> column; CRLF and multibyte text preserve that rule. Binary LazyValue locations remain empty even though preparation may build a raw newline index. Fixed source and file/tree semantics must later be checked through real Morphir materialization, not inferred from dependency ownership tests.</p></section>

<section id="numeric"><h2>Decimal input work derivation</h2>
<p>This is a source-backed derivation for later numeric work. It does not adopt a numeric quota or make the proposed Task 2A patch larger. The old 65536-byte token cap and earlier weighted decimal formula are not used.</p>
<p>Ion text integer and decimal coefficient reading first copy sanitized digits. UIntData tries u128, then calls BigUint only on positive overflow. Floats instead use Rust f64 parsing. These are different paths with different costs. See <a href="https://github.com/amazon-ion/ion-rust/blob/a1df66475c76605dd31c8566ef11f50f07fe8111/src/lazy/text/matched.rs#L178">matched integer</a>, <a href="https://github.com/amazon-ion/ion-rust/blob/a1df66475c76605dd31c8566ef11f50f07fe8111/src/lazy/text/matched.rs#L218">float</a>, <a href="https://github.com/amazon-ion/ion-rust/blob/a1df66475c76605dd31c8566ef11f50f07fe8111/src/lazy/text/matched.rs#L276">decimal</a> and <a href="https://github.com/amazon-ion/ion-rust/blob/a1df66475c76605dd31c8566ef11f50f07fe8111/src/types/integer/int_data.rs#L87">UIntData fallback</a>.</p>
<p>For num-bigint 0.4.8, BigDigit is 32 bits on 32-bit targets and64 bits on 64-bit targets. Decimal grouping uses the largest power of10 that fits a digit, so p=9 or 19. This follows <a href="https://github.com/rust-num/num-bigint/blob/65330056d6c00def4c6cda78c87453f4c2a76913/src/macros.rs#L3">cfg_digit</a>, <a href="https://github.com/rust-num/num-bigint/blob/65330056d6c00def4c6cda78c87453f4c2a76913/src/big_digit.rs#L3">BigDigit</a> and <a href="https://github.com/rust-num/num-bigint/blob/65330056d6c00def4c6cda78c87453f4c2a76913/src/biguint/convert.rs#L839">get_radix_base</a>, not the host used to write this proposal.</p>
<p>Let d be the nonempty sanitized decimal digit count passed to BigUint after the u128 overflow branch. BigUint creates a d-byte normalized digit vector, then groups the digits into m=ceil(d/p) chunks. The head has h=d-p*(m-1) digits, with 1≤h≤p. For each later chunk, it may push one zero limb, traverses the current limbs with mac_with_carry, folds the chunk into a primitive digit, then adds that digit. See <a href="https://github.com/rust-num/num-bigint/blob/65330056d6c00def4c6cda78c87453f4c2a76913/src/biguint/convert.rs#L91">from_radix_digits_be</a>, <a href="https://github.com/rust-num/num-bigint/blob/65330056d6c00def4c6cda78c87453f4c2a76913/src/biguint/convert.rs#L210">digit normalization</a> and <a href="https://github.com/rust-num/num-bigint/blob/65330056d6c00def4c6cda78c87453f4c2a76913/src/biguint/addition.rs#L60">add2 carry propagation</a>.</p>
<pre><code class="language-rust">// Mathematical visit bounds for the BigUint decimal fallback only.
// W=32 => p=9. W=64 => p=19. d>=1.
m = ceil(d / p)
h = d - p * (m - 1)
// Before tail iteration j, 1<=j<=m-1, data.len() <= j+1.
multiply_limb_visits <= sum(k, k=2..m) = m*(m+1)/2 - 1
add_limb_visits      <= sum(k, k=2..m) = m*(m+1)/2 - 1
primitive_digit_folds = d
peak_logical_data_len <= m
// Distinct counters. No invented weighting into CPU time or wall-clock units.</code></pre>
<p>The induction starts with one limb. A later iteration adds at most one limb before multiplication. The one-limb add visits its first limb and, only if carry remains, at most the remaining limbs. This bounds both walks by the same sum. Debug-build validation and normalization walks add linear work and are not hidden inside a CPU claim. Leading zero limbs and early carry termination reduce actual work; the bound is deliberately conservative.</p>
<table><thead><tr><th>d</th><th>m32</th><th>Each limb-visit bound 32</th><th>m64</th><th>Each limb-visit bound 64</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>39</td><td>5</td><td>14</td><td>3</td><td>5</td></tr><tr><td>40</td><td>5</td><td>14</td><td>3</td><td>5</td></tr><tr><td>64</td><td>8</td><td>35</td><td>4</td><td>9</td></tr><tr><td>128</td><td>15</td><td>119</td><td>7</td><td>27</td></tr><tr><td>129</td><td>15</td><td>119</td><td>7</td><td>27</td></tr></tbody></table>
<p>The table is symbolic arithmetic, stored in <code>numeric-derivation.json</code>. It is not measured conversion output. Forty ASCII 9 digits force u128 overflow. They give S32=14 and S64=5. A future numeric proof can accept exactly these separate credits, reject one less, and instrument the BigUint entry so refusal occurs before its digit-vector allocation or arithmetic. A decimal coefficient with many leading zeros that still fits u128 must retain its fast path and receive only the relevant scan/copy checks.</p>
<p>The smallest future insertion is a private preflight callback or checked sibling at the UIntData positive-overflow branch, immediately before BigUint::from_str_radix. Preserve the existing helper for legacy callers. The caller supplies counted digits and radix from the existing matched parser; no second lexer. Original token scan and SmallVec sanitization need their own earlier guards. Thus this insertion alone would bound costly BigUint conversion, not all scalar allocation.</p>
<p>Validate every counter sum/product before conversion. d=0 follows the parser's existing invalid-input behavior. For decimal result size, bits ≤4d is a safe integer upper bound and limbs≤ceil(4d/W); the loop also bounds peak logical data length by m. Neither bound is an exact allocation request. The std implementation estimates initial limb Vec capacity using floating log2, while no_std uses another estimate. Vec growth, normalization/shrink and downstream integer conversion may allocate or copy. A storage proposal must cover those actual requests before claiming a physical byte bound. This document does not adopt an unproved aggregate storage formula.</p></section>

<section id="formatting"><h2>Binary, floats and formatting</h2>
<p>Binary magnitude conversion does not use repeated decimal multiply/add. Ion 1.0 <a href="https://github.com/amazon-ion/ion-rust/blob/a1df66475c76605dd31c8566ef11f50f07fe8111/src/lazy/binary/raw/value.rs#L566">read_int</a> calls <a href="https://github.com/amazon-ion/ion-rust/blob/a1df66475c76605dd31c8566ef11f50f07fe8111/src/binary/uint.rs#L14">DecodedUInt</a>; the BigUint fallback <a href="https://github.com/rust-num/num-bigint/blob/65330056d6c00def4c6cda78c87453f4c2a76913/src/biguint.rs#L637">from_bytes_be</a> copies and reverses the input bytes, then <a href="https://github.com/rust-num/num-bigint/blob/65330056d6c00def4c6cda78c87453f4c2a76913/src/biguint/convert.rs#L33">bitwise packing</a> visits bounded-size chunks. This is linear byte/limb materialization with distinct copy/storage obligations. Binary decimal coefficients use the binary integer path. Hex/binary text radix conversion likewise uses bitwise packing after normalization. Charging these paths the decimal quadratic bound would unnecessarily restrict valid within-profile sources.</p>
<p>Text float parsing calls f64::from_str after a sanitized copy; it does not call BigInt. The standard library's actual conversion work, error formatting and scratch storage need their own audit. Text decimal exponent parsing uses i64. Its scan/copy and error-message allocation differ again. Current MatchedDecimal uses u16 token-offset/length fields, so existing lexical acceptance constraints must be checked before any future claim about arbitrary large valid decimal tokens.</p>
<p>A bounded output writer cannot by itself bound formatting. <a href="https://github.com/amazon-ion/ion-rust/blob/a1df66475c76605dd31c8566ef11f50f07fe8111/src/types/decimal/mod.rs#L512">Decimal::fmt</a> calls coefficient.to_string before writing. Integer/decimal <a href="https://github.com/amazon-ion/ion-rust/blob/a1df66475c76605dd31c8566ef11f50f07fe8111/src/text/text_formatter.rs#L379">text formatting</a> delegates Display, while <a href="https://github.com/amazon-ion/ion-rust/blob/a1df66475c76605dd31c8566ef11f50f07fe8111/src/types/integer/int_data.rs#L74">count_decimal_digits</a> formats large numbers just to count digits. Do not call that function as a cheap preflight.</p>
<table><thead><tr><th>num-bigint output path</th><th>Actual work and missing proof</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td><a href="https://github.com/rust-num/num-bigint/blob/65330056d6c00def4c6cda78c87453f4c2a76913/src/biguint/convert.rs#L677">to_radix_digits_le</a></td><td>Preallocates output digits, clones magnitude, then selects full or half radix base depending on architecture. Full decimal grouping is 9/19 digits; half grouping is 4/9.</td></tr>
<tr><td><a href="https://github.com/rust-num/num-bigint/blob/65330056d6c00def4c6cda78c87453f4c2a76913/src/biguint/convert.rs#L745">Small conversion</a>, <a href="https://github.com/rust-num/num-bigint/blob/65330056d6c00def4c6cda78c87453f4c2a76913/src/biguint/division.rs#L87">div_rem_digit</a></td><td>Repeated division visits each current limb. A small-number output bound must count these divisions and primitive digit emission, not reuse input's multiplication counter.</td></tr>
<tr><td><a href="https://github.com/rust-num/num-bigint/blob/65330056d6c00def4c6cda78c87453f4c2a76913/src/biguint/convert.rs#L707">32-limb switch</a> and <a href="https://github.com/rust-num/num-bigint/blob/65330056d6c00def4c6cda78c87453f4c2a76913/src/biguint/convert.rs#L768">divide and conquer</a></td><td>At ≥32 limbs, build large bases by repeated squaring; divide by a large base; recursively process two chunks; below 8 limbs use the small routine and pad. General division, multiplication, recursion and scratch storage need a separate derivation.</td></tr>
</tbody></table>
<p>There is no complete numeric formatting-work formula in this proposal. The reviewed code disproves a blanket claim that formatting always follows the simple quadratic input loop. A later tranche must guard magnitude clone, output digit storage, base squaring, division scratch and Decimal's temporary string before entering Display. Use bit-length metadata for a conservative output-size preflight without decimal formatting, then prove the conversion-work/storage model against the locked implementation. Keep exact formatting and negative-zero semantics unchanged.</p>
<p>There is also an error-propagation obligation. Decimal::fmt unwraps the write of its negative sign. If a bounded formatter returns fmt::Error at that write, this path can panic instead of propagating refusal. A future bounded formatter must prove its stop/error behavior as well as its byte and work bounds. This is a source finding, not a newly executed failing test or an authorized source fix.</p></section>

Current-selection compiler output binding

Concrete candidate plan, 19 October 2026. Design direction reviewed; implementation awaits approval. No wire/MCK version allocated.

Issue a sealed host configuration-lookup scope at trusted CLI startup. At each selected-model attempt, capture bounded configuration facts through that same scope and run one shared legacy Current-selection reducer. Preserve the original provider/guest root and output read grants. Return the actual writer root and compiler module together, with identities and a configuration fingerprint.

Authority and ownership API

The trusted run_ui shell owns the supplied workspace, startup cwd, ConfigLoadOptions and original OutOverrides. Before provider registration it obtains the exact ancestor/configuration directory capabilities needed by the existing host lookup policy and seals them. The scope never exposes those Dir values or a generic read method. A browser label, project ID or installed response cannot create or widen it.

// Proposed shape, names and error variants still reviewable.
// Only the CLI startup issuer constructs the private grant bundle.
CompilerOutputScope::from_startup_grants(grants, source_options, startup_cwd)
    -> Result<CompilerOutputScope, ScopeError>

// Called only after the parent reserves attempt/worker/copy capacity.
scope.capture_current(selected_provider_relative_path, attempt_budget)
    -> Result<CapturedCompilerConfiguration, CaptureError>

captured.resolve_output()
    -> Result<ResolvedCompilerOutput, OutputBindingError>

// Accessors lend validated facts; no deserialization/public-field constructor.
resolved.compiler_module() // validated relative module, root represented explicitly
resolved.output_grant()    // borrowed issuer-owned grant, not a caller path
resolved.fingerprint()     // source/candidate evidence for this capture

The scope has distinct private components: provider directory identity; narrow supported-config lookup handles for its ancestor chain and selected mounts; original source-selection policy; and the existing output-read grant. Implicit output remains confined to the provider directory. Only the original explicit flag/nonempty runtime output environment can grant an additional output directory. A resolved enclosing configuration directory is never converted into that extra grant.

Trusted startup may open only the configuration roots the legacy host would inspect. It records actual handle identities and supported candidate spellings. Request-time code performs no ambient open or parent traversal. Missing source directories are represented by a permitted existing parent capability plus an exact confined candidate path, or explicit inability to grant the lookup. There is no generic sibling enumeration. Previously permitted aliases are resolved at startup to sealed exact targets; later retargeting outside the sealed candidate set refuses.

The installed guest still receives the original provider-root request and remains membership authority. Selected output bindings are issued after the real guest selection. Native discovery is not substituted, and the wider host-only configuration facts are not sent to the guest.

Attempt capture and source roles

  1. The parent reserves worker/attempt/raw/copy credits before any request-time configuration metadata, file read or installed invocation required by the operation. Rejection has no lookup/copy/lock effects.
  2. Validate the real selected project's ordinary confined path, provider identity and owned directory identity. These checks establish source/config lookup eligibility, not guest membership. Membership was checked against the actual provider response.
  3. Resolve exact supported primary candidates from the selected directory upward through the startup-approved chain. Capture missing slots as well as present files. Use existing primary layout precedence, including .morphir, .config and legacy morphir.json. Do not call the ambient loader or expand sibling-member globs.
  4. Read each retained source from its owned handle. Reserve credit before every buffer growth/copy, enforce the byte bound during reads even if metadata is wrong, and keep the exact bytes/UTF-8 outcome. Metadata alone is not a content or budget proof.
  5. Capture the selected system/global candidates, correctly scoped root/member or explicit override slots, and configured environment values. The original SourceSelection intent remains private in the scope. In particular Explicit override does not accidentally activate a member-adjacent override that portable discovery happened to retain.
  6. Run the shared Current-selection predicate and reducer over these immutable facts. Return typed output facts and a fingerprint including scope ID, source roles, source/candidate paths, directory/file identities, absence evidence, byte digests and captured environment/source-option evidence. Do not expose secrets or fabricated native provenance.
  7. Before publication the parent recaptures/checks within the same sealed scope, compares actual project/output directory identities, selected module and fingerprint, and refuses a changed binding. It then validates the exact compile record/module and retains original bytes under the existing shared compile lock. Config changes are not locked by compile.lock; a final currentness check is required. No filesystem transaction or forever-latest claim is made.

Proposed finite budgets

These are candidate policy values requiring review, not frozen protocol claims. They apply to the additive bounded path; legacy public path APIs keep their existing behavior. All counters are validated private domain types with checked arithmetic and named refusal reasons.

LedgerCandidate ceiling and before-growth rule
Configuration directories/candidate slots128 selected-to-root lookup directories and 1,024 exact candidate probes per attempt. Reuses the existing confined traversal depth scale. Seven primary slots per directory plus selected override/mount slots fit under the probe ceiling. Longer valid legacy ancestry refuses explicitly in the new profile, never silently truncates selection.
Raw retained configuration64 MiB aggregate, shared across captured discovery/output facts and selected mounts within the attempt, also charged to the host's real global reservation. Reserve before growing a read/copy buffer; no second unmetered 64 MiB pool. Shared immutable bytes need no duplicate copy; an actual copy consumes credit.
Source decodeRoot depth0, max depth128, 100,000 logical values and 64 Mi UTF-16 key/string units across the attempt's accepted source documents. Known duplicate/error semantics remain format-specific. Failed candidate parsing still consumes its separate parser-work budget.
Parser work1,000,000 token/event operations across actual passes, independently from logical source values. Preflight and semantic decode of the same immutable bytes do not count as two logical models, but both consume real work. Charge tokenizer/event scratch separately from retained source strings.
Merge/typed materializationIndependent aggregate 100,000 constructed/copied values and 64 Mi UTF-16 key/string-copy units, depth128. Check before each clone/insert/typed retained copy. Borrowed final-value validation alone is not a pre-growth proof.
Pattern selection1,000,000 actual matcher steps and bounded recursion depth128. Resource exhaustion is an error, not a nonmatch. Existing recursive ** matching is not assumed cheap merely because source bytes are finite.

All configuration formats stay in scope. Current config TOML first materializes toml::Value, then JSON; a post-Value count cannot qualify it. Pinned toml_parser1.1.3 exposes Source.lex iteration, public EventReceiver/RecursionGuard and scalar decoding. A bounded token/event/logical-expansion preflight can run before the unchanged TOML semantic decoder on the same bytes. Its retained token pushes and dotted/implicit-table work must themselves be checked before growth. No second lexer or TOML dialect is proposed.

Config YAML already has an event/profile validator and serde-saphyr budgets; the bounded route must set reviewed finite input/event/node/depth/scalar limits before Value construction while retaining existing duplicate/alias/merge policy. Legacy JSON needs bounded same-byte preflight followed by the existing derived LegacyProjectConfig decoder, preserving its duplicate-known-field errors. Do not replace that semantic decoder with a generic last-wins map.

Per-format preflight/normalization and every reducer-copy hook need actual red/green allocation/operation tests before any production resource claim. Existing parser APIs are seams, not qualification evidence. A future direct morphir-json dependency from morphir-config would require separately reviewed package-order/CI changes. No dependency, parser or source-format change is authorized by this plan alone.

Vertical slices and acceptance

Task 1: share the existing pure Current stages

Implemented and locally qualified extraction in devkit only, preserving ordinary legacy APIs and all format/error/source cases. First tracer is system/global out_dir retained by the actual writer reducer, while portable membership remains filtered. Test early root decode, member override scoping, explicit-user omission, ir.mode and atomic-secret/null semantics. No new provider capability or host grant is enabled.

Task 2: issue the sealed trusted-startup lookup scope

Bind actual directory identities and static candidate paths without exposing raw capabilities. Refuse replacement/retargeting, missing required authority and limit violations. Test that client values cannot cause a new ambient open or grant; retain the original provider and output boundaries. Startup invocation precedes provider registration, and every later attempt reserves before lookup.

Task 3: capture and derive one bounded selected output binding

Implement before-growth readers, per-format parser/merge budgets and currentness fingerprints. Return actual root/module/output grant together. Test all present/absent candidate transitions, atomic config replacement, source/mount/env roles, nested workspaces and exact/oneover limits. No all-project sidecar inventory or hidden live reread.

Task 4: integrate actual native and installed host ownership

Parent owns provider/worker integration. Prove original real guest membership/request root, no output widening, genuine identities/record.module under shared lock, currentness refusal and capacity-before-effects. Then qualify the new shared MCK role with independent fixed expectations. No frozen historical kit is broadened.

The separate source-authored packet current-output-source-cases-2026-10-19.json contains 31 acceptance scenarios derived from the cited source and proposed policy, not observed adapter outputs. It covers system/global/root/user/env precedence; member/root/module translation; explicit grants; nested/added/replaced configuration; missing output; installed selection; config-absent limits; malformed/format errors; and capacity/work refusal. It is a design packet, not published MCK.

Review decisions and scope

No new user permission is needed for a design that preserves existing host configuration lookup and output grants exactly. A policy decision is required if the implementation would read configuration locations outside the legacy host lookup, grant enclosing outputs/siblings implicitly, send wider configuration to a guest, or allow client refreshes to expand sealed authority. This proposal does none of those.

Review is still required for the candidate finite limits, exact grant-bundle construction, per-format before-growth proof and shared reducer factoring. Scope issuance failure should leave ordinary workspace browsing/v1 available and advertise the additive output capability as unavailable, rather than turn model-output limitations into a general startup failure.

Code remains paused. Original144/discovery7/JSON16 cases are unchanged. The first b23 capability implementation has a separate immutable receipt and has been rebased by root; this plan does not alter that source or its validation claims.

Ion reader budget: isolated Task 1 proof

morphir-etg2.22.1 · 18 October 2026 · Local proof complete · SDK integration pending

The isolated ion-rs 1.0.1 patch refuses text-container depth/cache growth and symbol-table slot expansion before the guarded operations run. It preserves the legacy unbounded default and reuses the parser and catalog APIs. Fourteen focused tests pass; independent review found no material defect within this scope.

Configurable API and exact accounting

// Rust API in the isolated patch. These are explicit test settings.
let limits = ReaderLimits::builder()
    .max_text_depth(0)
    .cache_bytes(4096)
    .child_steps(8)
    .symbol_slots(3)
    .created_symbol_slots(6)
    .build()?;
let budget = ReaderBudget::new(limits);
let config = Text.with_catalog(catalog).with_budget(budget.clone());
let reader = Reader::new(config, input)?;
// Reader::new(Text, input) retains the existing unbounded default.

All five builder fields must be supplied. Private validated fields allow useful zero limits; unsupported integer ranges are rejected. The depth field is restricted to u16 range, and capacity/counter fields to isize range. This validates representation, not stack safety for every requested depth. No Morphir profile number is built into the dependency.

LimitImplemented meaningWhat it does not mean
max_text_depthText container roots start at zero. Each nested container enters a scoped guard before its child iterator. Success, syntax errors and typed refusals unwind depth.Application-value depth, binary child depth and every Ion 1.1 macro stack are not covered.
cache_bytesCumulative requested text-container cache capacity bytes. The bounded path explicitly grows capacities 1, 2, 4, 8. Every requested capacity block is charged before reserve. Credits remain spent after arena reset, retained-owner replacement and retry.It is not the BumpAllocator's actual block size, total arena usage, live memory or RSS.
child_stepsEvery container child-iterator next attempt, including terminal None. Charge before recursive parsing. Incomplete-stream retries spend more attempts.It is not a complete byte-scanner or arithmetic work meter.
symbol_slotsCombined pending import/local slots and active Ion 1.0 user slots at append commit. Imported placeholders count. Check an entire max_id batch before extending any prefix or resizing.Fixed system prefixes, retained-table storage, COW bytes and symbol text byte length are not charged by this slot count.
created_symbol_slotsCumulative reserved new import/local slots across resets, append and shared budget owners. Failed later decoding does not refund a prior accepted reservation.It is not an application-value count or a source/assembled-model ledger.

ReadConfig stores an optional budget. EncodingContext clones share the same Rc-owned state; no budget borrow spans recursive parsing or Catalog callbacks. The first IonError::ResourceLimit carries a typed kind and bounded numeric metadata. Parser Cut conversion preserves it. Guarded reader iteration checks failure before arena reset or table commit and returns the same refusal without advancing counters. Already-yielded lazy values retain upstream read behavior; this partial patch does not promise sticky enforcement for every scalar or lazy API.

+// Local proof modification, 18 October 2026. Partial opt-in reader-budget experiment.
+//! Isolated, partial reader-budget proof. This is not a complete bounded Ion reader.
+//! No Morphir application limits or default numerical policy are defined here.
+use crate::result::IonFailure;
+use crate::{IonError, IonResult};
+use std::cell::RefCell;
+use std::rc::Rc;
+
+#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
+pub enum ReaderLimitKind {
+    TextContainerDepth,
+    TextCacheBytes,
+    ChildSteps,
+    SymbolSlots,
+    CreatedSymbolSlots,
+}
+
+#[derive(Clone, Debug, Eq, PartialEq, thiserror::Error)]
+#[error("reader resource limit {kind:?} at {offset}: requested {requested}, limit {limit}")]
+pub struct LimitExceeded {
+    kind: ReaderLimitKind,
+    offset: usize,
+    limit: usize,
+    requested: usize,
+}
+impl LimitExceeded {
+    pub fn kind(&self) -> ReaderLimitKind {
+        self.kind
+    }
+    pub fn offset(&self) -> usize {
+        self.offset
+    }
+    pub fn limit(&self) -> usize {
+        self.limit
+    }
+    pub fn requested(&self) -> usize {
+        self.requested
+    }
+}
+
+#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug)]
+pub struct ReaderLimits {
+    max_text_depth: usize,
+    cache_bytes: usize,
+    child_steps: usize,
+    symbol_slots: usize,
+    created_symbol_slots: usize,
+}
+#[derive(Default)]
+pub struct ReaderLimitsBuilder {
+    max_text_depth: Option<usize>,
+    cache_bytes: Option<usize>,
+    child_steps: Option<usize>,
+    symbol_slots: Option<usize>,
+    created_symbol_slots: Option<usize>,
+}
+impl ReaderLimits {
+    pub fn builder() -> ReaderLimitsBuilder {
+        ReaderLimitsBuilder::default()
+    }
+}
+impl ReaderLimitsBuilder {
+    pub fn max_text_depth(mut self, value: usize) -> Self {
+        self.max_text_depth = Some(value);
+        self
+    }
+    pub fn cache_bytes(mut self, value: usize) -> Self {
+        self.cache_bytes = Some(value);
+        self
+    }
+    pub fn child_steps(mut self, value: usize) -> Self {
+        self.child_steps = Some(value);
+        self
+    }
+    pub fn symbol_slots(mut self, value: usize) -> Self {
+        self.symbol_slots = Some(value);
+        self
+    }
+    pub fn created_symbol_slots(mut self, value: usize) -> Self {
+        self.created_symbol_slots = Some(value);
+        self
+    }
+    pub fn build(self) -> IonResult<ReaderLimits> {
+        let (
+            Some(max_text_depth),
+            Some(cache_bytes),
+            Some(child_steps),
+            Some(symbol_slots),
+            Some(created_symbol_slots),
+        ) = (
+            self.max_text_depth,
+            self.cache_bytes,
+            self.child_steps,
+            self.symbol_slots,
+            self.created_symbol_slots,
+        )
+        else {
+            return Err(IonError::illegal_operation(
+                "all partial proof limits must be set explicitly",
+            ));
+        };
+        if max_text_depth > u16::MAX as usize
+            || [cache_bytes, child_steps, symbol_slots, created_symbol_slots]
+                .iter()
+                .any(|v| *v > isize::MAX as usize)
+        {
+            return Err(IonError::illegal_operation(
+                "reader proof limit is outside its supported integer range",
+            ));
+        }
+        Ok(ReaderLimits {
+            max_text_depth,
+            cache_bytes,
+            child_steps,
+            symbol_slots,
+            created_symbol_slots,
+        })
+    }
+}
+#[derive(Clone)]
+pub struct ReaderBudget {
+    state: Rc<RefCell<BudgetState>>,
+}
+#[derive(Debug)]
+struct BudgetState {
+    limits: ReaderLimits,
+    failure: Option<LimitExceeded>,
+    symbol_offset: usize,
+    usage: Usage,
+}
+#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq)]
+struct Usage {
+    active_containers: usize,
+    cache_bytes: usize,
+    child_steps: usize,
+    cache_pushes: usize,
+    created_slots: usize,
+    imported_slots: usize,
+    local_slots: usize,
+    local_text_copies: usize,
+}
+impl ReaderBudget {
+    pub fn new(limits: ReaderLimits) -> Self {
+        Self {
+            state: Rc::new(RefCell::new(BudgetState {
+                limits,
+                failure: None,
+                symbol_offset: 0,
+                usage: Usage::default(),
+            })),
+        }
+    }
+    pub(crate) fn check(&self) -> IonResult<()> {
+        match self.state.borrow().failure.clone() {
+            Some(e) => Err(e.into()),
+            None => Ok(()),
+        }
+    }
+    // Charge every requested bump-vector capacity block. Old blocks and credits are
+    // retained across growth, arena resets, source retries and cloned contexts.
+    pub(crate) fn reserve_cache_growth(
+        &self,
+        len: usize,
+        capacity: usize,
+        element_bytes: usize,
+        offset: usize,
+    ) -> IonResult<usize> {
+        self.check()?;
+        if len < capacity {
+            return Ok(capacity);
+        }
+        let target = if capacity == 0 {
+            1
+        } else {
+            capacity.checked_mul(2).unwrap_or(usize::MAX)
+        };
+        let bytes = target.checked_mul(element_bytes).unwrap_or(usize::MAX);
+        let mut state = self.state.borrow_mut();
+        let requested = state
+            .usage
+            .cache_bytes
+            .checked_add(bytes)
+            .unwrap_or(usize::MAX);
+        let limit = state.limits.cache_bytes;
+        state.ensure(ReaderLimitKind::TextCacheBytes, limit, requested, offset)?;
+        state.usage.cache_bytes = requested;
+        Ok(target)
+    }
+    pub(crate) fn note_cache_push(&self) {
+        self.state.borrow_mut().usage.cache_pushes += 1;
+    }
+    // Reservation is atomic across the pending and cumulative-created caps.
+    // Imported unknown-text placeholders consume slots just like known symbols.
+    pub(crate) fn reserve_symbol_batch(
+        &self,
+        pending: usize,
+        additional: usize,
+        offset: usize,
+    ) -> IonResult<()> {
+        let mut state = self.state.borrow_mut();
+        let requested = pending.checked_add(additional).unwrap_or(usize::MAX);
+        let limit = state.limits.symbol_slots;
+        state.ensure(ReaderLimitKind::SymbolSlots, limit, requested, offset)?;
+        let created = state
+            .usage
+            .created_slots
+            .checked_add(additional)
+            .unwrap_or(usize::MAX);
+        let limit = state.limits.created_symbol_slots;
+        state.ensure(ReaderLimitKind::CreatedSymbolSlots, limit, created, offset)?;
+        state.usage.created_slots = created;
+        state.symbol_offset = offset;
+        Ok(())
+    }
+    pub(crate) fn check_table_commit(&self, requested: usize) -> IonResult<()> {
+        let mut state = self.state.borrow_mut();
+        let limit = state.limits.symbol_slots;
+        let offset = state.symbol_offset;
+        state.ensure(ReaderLimitKind::SymbolSlots, limit, requested, offset)
+    }
+    pub(crate) fn note_local_text_copy(&self) {
+        self.state.borrow_mut().usage.local_text_copies += 1;
+    }
+    pub(crate) fn note_local_symbol(&self) {
+        self.state.borrow_mut().usage.local_slots += 1;
+    }
+    pub(crate) fn note_import(&self, slots: usize) {
+        self.state.borrow_mut().usage.imported_slots += slots;
+    }
+    pub(crate) fn step_child(&self, offset: usize) -> IonResult<()> {
+        let mut state = self.state.borrow_mut();
+        let requested = state.usage.child_steps.checked_add(1).unwrap_or(usize::MAX);
+        let limit = state.limits.child_steps;
+        state.ensure(ReaderLimitKind::ChildSteps, limit, requested, offset)?;
+        state.usage.child_steps = requested;
+        Ok(())
+    }
+    pub(crate) fn enter_text_container(&self, offset: usize) -> IonResult<TextDepthGuard> {
+        self.check()?;
+        let mut state = self.state.borrow_mut();
+        let requested = state.usage.active_containers;
+        let limit = state.limits.max_text_depth;
+        state.ensure(
+            ReaderLimitKind::TextContainerDepth,
+            limit,
+            requested,
+            offset,
+        )?;
+        state.usage.active_containers += 1;
+        Ok(TextDepthGuard(self.clone()))
+    }
+}
+impl BudgetState {
+    fn ensure(
+        &mut self,
+        kind: ReaderLimitKind,
+        limit: usize,
+        requested: usize,
+        offset: usize,
+    ) -> IonResult<()> {
+        if let Some(error) = &self.failure {
+            return Err(error.clone().into());
+        }
+        if requested > limit {
+            let error = LimitExceeded {
+                kind,
+                offset,
+                limit,
+                requested,
+            };
+            self.failure = Some(error.clone());
+            return Err(error.into());
+        }
+        Ok(())
+    }
+}
+pub(crate) struct TextDepthGuard(ReaderBudget);
+impl Drop for TextDepthGuard {
+    fn drop(&mut self) {
+        self.0.state.borrow_mut().usage.active_containers -= 1;
+    }
+}

+// Local proof modification, 18 October 2026. Partial opt-in reader-budget experiment.
+use super::*;

+fn limits(depth: usize) -> ReaderLimits {
+    ReaderLimits::builder()
+        .max_text_depth(depth)

+#[test]
+fn text_container_depth_is_root_zero_and_refuses_before_descending() {
+    let budget = ReaderBudget::new(limits(0));
+    let mut root = Reader::new(
+        Text.with_catalog(EmptyCatalog).with_budget(budget.clone()),
+        "[0]",
+    )
+    .unwrap();
+    assert!(root.next().unwrap().is_some());
+    assert_eq!(budget.state.borrow().usage.active_containers, 0);
+    let budget = ReaderBudget::new(limits(0));
+    let mut nested = Reader::new(
+        Text.with_catalog(EmptyCatalog).with_budget(budget.clone()),
+        "[[]]",
+    )
+    .unwrap();
+    assert!(
+        matches!(nested.next(),Err(IonError::ResourceLimit(e)) if e.kind()==ReaderLimitKind::TextContainerDepth)
+    );
+    assert_eq!(budget.state.borrow().usage.active_containers, 0);
+}

+#[test]
+fn text_cache_capacity_is_reserved_before_the_next_allocation_or_push() {
+    let size = text_expr_size();
+    let mut exact = limits(10);
+    exact.cache_bytes = 7 * size;
+    let mut over = exact;
+    over.cache_bytes -= 1;
+    let denied = ReaderBudget::new(over);
+    let mut reader = Reader::new(
+        Text.with_catalog(EmptyCatalog).with_budget(denied.clone()),
+        "[1,2,3,4]",
+    )
+    .unwrap();
+    assert!(
+        matches!(reader.next(),Err(IonError::ResourceLimit(e)) if e.kind()==ReaderLimitKind::TextCacheBytes)
+    );
+    let usage = denied.state.borrow().usage;
+    assert_eq!(usage.cache_pushes, 2, "refuse before the third push");
+    assert_eq!(
+        usage.cache_bytes,
+        3 * size,
+        "refuse before allocating capacity4"
+    );
+    let accepted = ReaderBudget::new(exact);
+    let mut reader = Reader::new(
+        Text.with_catalog(EmptyCatalog)
+            .with_budget(accepted.clone()),
+        "[1,2,3,4]",
+    )
+    .unwrap();
+    let value = reader.expect_next().unwrap();
+    assert_eq!(
+        value.read().unwrap().expect_list().unwrap().iter().count(),
+        4
+    );
+    assert_eq!(accepted.state.borrow().usage.cache_bytes, 7 * size);
+    assert_eq!(accepted.state.borrow().usage.cache_pushes, 4);
+}

+#[test]
+fn incomplete_stream_retries_do_not_refund_cache_or_iterator_work() {
+    use std::{cell::Cell, io::Read};
+    struct OneByte<'a> {
+        remaining: &'a [u8],
+        count: Rc<Cell<usize>>,
+    }
+    impl Read for OneByte<'_> {
+        fn read(&mut self, out: &mut [u8]) -> std::io::Result<usize> {
+            let n = out.len().min(self.remaining.len()).min(1);
+            out[..n].copy_from_slice(&self.remaining[..n]);
+            self.remaining = &self.remaining[n..];
+            self.count.set(self.count.get() + n);
+            Ok(n)
+        }
+    }
+    let source = b"[0,0,0,0]";
+    let mut policy = limits(10);
+    policy.cache_bytes = 7 * text_expr_size();
+    let budget = ReaderBudget::new(policy);
+    let read = Rc::new(Cell::new(0));
+    let input = crate::lazy::streaming_raw_reader::IonStream::new(OneByte {
+        remaining: source,
+        count: read.clone(),
+    });
+    let mut reader = Reader::new(
+        Text.with_catalog(EmptyCatalog).with_budget(budget.clone()),
+        input,
+    )
+    .unwrap();
+    assert!(
+        matches!(reader.next(),Err(IonError::ResourceLimit(e)) if e.kind()==ReaderLimitKind::TextCacheBytes)
+    );
+    let usage = budget.state.borrow().usage;
+    assert!(usage.cache_bytes > 0);
+    assert!(usage.child_steps > usage.cache_pushes);
+    assert!(
+        read.get() < source.len(),
+        "refuse while source is still partial"
+    );
+    assert_eq!(usage.active_containers, 0);
+}

SHA256 733f7b7faaa9b52eb3a4f46ba5548695fa076a646ce831b5a10555bfc937516b

{
  "status": "Independent inputs and intended outcomes frozen before proof execution; tests added one slice at a time",
  "baseArchiveSHA256": "285b4429808446f30da668d210beaeb7ab82defb6045e261c6cdfaeafe565552",
  "policy": "Configurable small proof limits only; no Morphir semantic or production auxiliary policy adopted",
  "cases": [
    {
      "id": "root-depth-zero",
      "source": "[0]",
      "depth": 0,
      "expected": "accepted"
    },
    {
      "id": "nested-depth-oneover",
      "source": "[[]]",
      "depth": 0,
      "expected": "ResourceLimit(TextContainerDepth), depth unwound to0, sticky"
    },
    {
      "id": "mixed-container-depth",
      "source": "[{k:([])}]",
      "depth": 2,
      "expected": "ResourceLimit(TextContainerDepth), all guards unwind"
    },
    {
      "id": "same-depth-adjacent-roots",
      "source": "[] []",
      "depth": 0,
      "expected": "both accepted"
    },
    {
      "id": "cache-exact-capacity",
      "source": "[1,2,3,4]",
      "cacheBudget": "7 * sizeof(text1.0 value expr), requested capacities1+2+4",
      "expected": "accepted4 entries"
    },
    {
      "id": "cache-onebyte-over",
      "source": "[1,2,3,4]",
      "cacheBudget": "7 * sizeof(text1.0 value expr) -1",
      "expected": "ResourceLimit(TextCacheBytes) before third entry push or4-entry allocation"
    },
    {
      "id": "no-arena-refund",
      "source": "[1] [2]",
      "cacheBudget": "sizeof(text1.0 value expr)",
      "expected": "first accepted; second ResourceLimit(TextCacheBytes)"
    },
    {
      "id": "stream-retry-no-refund",
      "source": "[0,0,0,0]",
      "reader": "one byte per Read",
      "cacheBudget": "7 * sizeof(text1.0 value expr)",
      "expected": "ResourceLimit(TextCacheBytes) before complete source; same complete slice fits"
    },
    {
      "id": "known-import-exact",
      "catalog": {
        "name": "T",
        "version": 1,
        "symbols": [
          "alpha",
          "beta"
        ]
      },
      "source": "$ion_symbol_table::{imports:[{name:\"T\",version:1,max_id:3}]} $10 $11 $12",
      "symbolSlots": 3,
      "expected": "alpha,beta,unknown"
    },
    {
      "id": "known-import-oneover",
      "catalog": {
        "name": "T",
        "version": 1,
        "symbols": [
          "alpha",
          "beta"
        ]
      },
      "source": "$ion_symbol_table::{imports:[{name:\"T\",version:1,max_id:4}]} $10",
      "symbolSlots": 3,
      "expected": "ResourceLimit(SymbolSlots) before any import append/resize"
    },
    {
      "id": "known-import-amplification",
      "catalog": {
        "name": "T",
        "version": 1,
        "symbols": [
          "alpha",
          "beta"
        ]
      },
      "source": "$ion_symbol_table::{imports:[{name:\"T\",version:1,max_id:2147483647}]} $10",
      "symbolSlots": 3,
      "expected": "ResourceLimit(SymbolSlots) before any import append/resize"
    },
    {
      "id": "local-symbol-oneover",
      "source": "$ion_symbol_table::{symbols:[\"alpha\",\"beta\"]} $10",
      "symbolSlots": 1,
      "expected": "ResourceLimit(SymbolSlots) before second Arc/push"
    },
    {
      "id": "created-slots-no-refund",
      "source": "$ion_symbol_table::{symbols:[\"alpha\"]} $10 $ion_symbol_table::{symbols:[\"beta\"]} $10",
      "symbolSlots": 1,
      "createdSymbolSlots": 1,
      "expected": "first alpha; ResourceLimit(CreatedSymbolSlots) before second local push"
    },
    {
      "id": "append-active-cap",
      "source": "$ion_symbol_table::{symbols:[\"alpha\"]} $10 $ion_symbol_table::{imports:$ion_symbol_table,symbols:[\"beta\"]} $11",
      "symbolSlots": 1,
      "createdSymbolSlots": 2,
      "expected": "first alpha; ResourceLimit(SymbolSlots) before active append commit"
    },
    {
      "id": "legacy-defaults",
      "source": "$ion_symbol_table::{symbols:[\"alpha\",\"beta\"]} [1,2,3,4] $10 $11",
      "expected": "legacy public parser remains unlimited by proof caps"
    },
    {
      "id": "syntax-unwinds",
      "source": "[0",
      "expected": "syntax error; depth returns0; counters already spent are retained"
    },
    {
      "id": "attempt-exact-oneover",
      "source": "[0]",
      "childAttempts": 2,
      "expected": "accepted; cap1 rejects final iterator advance before it runs"
    },
    {
      "id": "limits-validation",
      "expected": "reject depth greater than u16::MAX and capacities greater than isize::MAX; zero useful limits accepted"
    }
  ]
}

Discovery from the provider-owned directory

morphir-etg2.22.1 · 18 October 2026 · SDK prerequisite proposal, no SDK implementation

The new originals path needs configuration and project membership from the directory the provider actually owns. Existing discovery already has confined traversal and effective-config details. The missing public seam accepts that existing directory instead of reopening its ambient path.

The current local contribution only adds private capture preparation and publication. It does not resolve provider authority, advertise a profile, or call a projection codec. All API names below are proposed, not published.

Actual sourceMeaning for the new path
provider/native.rs:30–67Native provider stores an actual Dir, but initial discovery precedes opening that provider directory.
provider/extension.rs:174–202Installed discovery builds a request from the ambient workspace path, then calls the actual installed guest. Its response is the provider snapshot.
provider/project_model.rs:42–109Legacy v1 checks a confined project directory, then reads config through an ambient path. The earlier check cannot authorize that later read. Keep v1 unchanged; do not reuse this sequence for originals.

Parent paths above are relative to crates/morphir/src/commands/ui/. SDK paths are relative to ecosystem/morphir-rust/crates/, whose pinned revision is ef4810782db135986e74c503a7bc3003834a3dd9. This proposal changes neither repository yet.

Proposed SDK ownership and API

Introduce two opaque SDK types with private fields. The provider supplies a clone of its real startup directory and a host-selected root label. Labels assist diagnostics and existing absolute-symlink policy; they grant no file access. Identity verification must occur before any config read. A mismatching or replaced ambient root is an explicit binding failure, not a request to read the replacement.

// Proposed additive API in morphir-devkit.
pub struct WorkspaceDiscoveryRoot { /* Dir + verified host labels */ }
pub struct CapturedWorkspaceDiscovery { /* immutable request + labels */ }

impl WorkspaceDiscoveryRoot {
    pub fn from_directory(
        directory: cap_std::fs::Dir,
        host_root: &std::path::Path,
    ) -> anyhow::Result<Self>;

    pub fn capture(
        &self,
        options: &ConfigLoadOptions,
    ) -> anyhow::Result<CapturedWorkspaceDiscovery>;
}
impl CapturedWorkspaceDiscovery {
    pub fn request(&self) -> &morphir_workspace::DiscoveryRequest;
    pub fn into_typed_details(self)
        -> Result<NativeWorkspaceDiscovery, NativeWorkspaceDiscoveryError>;
}

The root wrapper owns the directory and does not expose a mutable request, a constructor from a serialized source identity, or an accessor that opens its ambient label. capture rechecks label identity and traverses the same owned directory. The request and all selected mounts are captured once. into_typed_details factors out the existing pure discover_with_details and typed effective-config decode, without another filesystem or environment read.

Implement the new seam by factoring the existing binder after root binding, keeping the old public path APIs and their behavior. Reuse existing alias and traversal limits, including 65,536 real directories, 262,144 real entries, depth 128 and request-wide 64 MiB config payload. These bounds do not imply a new cancellation guarantee. A started blocking traversal retains its work permit until it actually exits.

Host-selected system/global configuration and explicit user override continue through the existing ConfigLoadOptions policies. They are additional startup grants, not remote-request paths. If those policies open ambient mounts, the SDK must keep their explicit authority and existing bounds visible in the API documentation. Do not replace them with a caller-supplied path field or quietly omit those overlays.

Native and installed flows

flowchart TD
  D[Actual provider-owned Dir] -- bounded capture --> R[One immutable DiscoveryRequest]
  R -- native --> N[Pure details + typed configs]
  R -- installed checked Session --> G[Actual guest discovery snapshot]

Native uses into_typed_details for both membership and config. Installed sends request() through the current checked installed SDK discovery path, then consumes the frozen request for local typed config details. The actual guest snapshot remains its membership authority. Selected member paths must resolve in that actual snapshot and the same-request config sidecar. Inconsistent or missing selection fails explicitly; it cannot switch silently to native membership or reload an ambient project config.

Serializing the borrowed immutable request for the guest may require an owned transport value. Any such bounded copy remains charged to active work; the host cannot label a second live discovery request as the same snapshot. Reuse the existing checked invocation and its actual activation/digest checks.

Output and configuration policy

Retain startup OutOverrides precedence: flag, nonempty environment override, effective workspace output config, default. Preserve workspace-root and member-module semantics from OutContext, resolve_out_root and module_path. Factor a typed helper from the existing config/output policy if current ConfigContext cannot be assembled truthfully from typed discovery details. Do not reconstruct merge policy in the parent.

Only an explicit process override grants a separate output directory. Configuration/default output roots stay under the provider-owned directory and use nofollow confined traversal. Member selection comes from the actual provider snapshot; it does not gain authority by matching a project ID string. Bind the resulting directory capability and validated SelectedModule inside a private ResolvedProjectSource.

The SDK public type/accessor for positive original-source declarations is a separate prerequisite. Do not publish an empty-companion declaration by default. The temporary parent-private duplicate-aware record boundary remains isolated until that API replaces it.

Authority and publication

Existing native and installed providers validate stored provider/source selection but do not expose a revocation epoch. A new ID comparison or an AuthenticatedBinding constructor would add labels, not authority. Before capture and again before publication, the real provider must validate its current selected source, run fresh capability-bound discovery, find the selected member in the actual result, and resolve its output under the same startup grants.

Compare actual selected directory identities and typed module/output selection with the pre-capture authorization. Project removal, changed output grant, changed root binding, provider removal or closed connection refuse publication and drop private preparation. Ordinary compiled-source replacement does not turn frozen bytes into live bytes; the captured record and primary inventory remain the exact source for header and semantic projection.

The current PreparedModelCapture is a sealed ownership stage. It cannot be looked up with its ID and it exposes no retained sources. It holds the same one work credit while a future provider performs revalidation. Cancellation, timeout, close and stale-attempt checks are necessary lifecycle checks; possession of the token is insufficient provider authorization. The storage-only wait() convenience publishes internally only for the existing confined-storage API.

Future orchestration must reserve slot/work before capture-related resolution, discovery or guest effects. The current storage entry point reserves before its capture work only; it does not yet cover earlier provider resolution. The permit must remain inside actual blocking/guest work across dropped waiters, and preparation keeps it until publication or drop. A future owned-source invalidation mechanism and idle-ready revocation policy require an explicit separate decision and tests.

Depth, retry and storage

  1. At each known container opening, acquire a scoped depth guard before recursively parsing a child. Drop it on success, Cut, Backtrack, Incomplete and panic unwinding. Return to the parent depth, never reset to root during a child read. Cached expressions retain their relative-depth provenance. Binary child iterators require the same guard even though binary parsing skips text's recursive matcher.
  2. Before each iterator advance, reserve event credit. Before BumpVec push/reserve, reserve the planned capacity bytes. The existing for-loop advances the iterator before its body; move that preflight ahead of next(). A check after receiving the child is too late.
  3. Only logical speculative reservations that never caused work/allocation may be cancelled. Scan, copy, allocated capacity and attempted events never refund on backtracking. Streaming reparse can consume the work budget even for unchanged bytes. Retry cannot turn a limit into more input demand.
  4. Use checked addition/multiplication for lengths, capacities, max_id, offsets and numeric-work formulas. An arithmetic overflow refuses before allocation. Bump arenas may retain old growth blocks; charge each requested block rather than only final vector length. Rc-retained arenas and table snapshots retain resident credits until their actual owner drops; cumulative storage credits never refund.
  5. Preflight imports atomically. After trusted Catalog lookup, check the selected import count plus max_id placeholders before extend or resize. Never allocate the prefix and then discover the placeholder overflow. Prepare table changes before resetting the active table; failure leaves no partially committed table and remains sticky. User-provided Catalog code is a trusted callback outside the reader's heap guarantee.

Physical attempts do not need an unbounded deduplication set. Application counts are committed by one ordered source materialization, not by every parser revisit. Any range/cache bookkeeping itself consumes the physical storage/event budget. If a later semantic decoder revisits the same owned Element, it does not re-charge source nodes; any new assembled model is a separate phase.

wire-proposal-2026-10-18.types.ts is the exact proposed structural vocabulary. Every displayed object and union variant is closed and all listed members are required. The method determines the parameter and reply roles. JSON-RPC remains {jsonrpc:"2.0",id,method,params}; replies have either result or error, never both. IDs use the existing connected unsigned-u64 token syntax. Counts/ranges use exact mathematical integer validation before floating point. Reject duplicate members and ill-formed Unicode at every structural boundary; opaque original bytes never enter a JSON Value.
