Coverage is {kind:"primary"} or {kind:"complete",declaration:"0.1.0-draft.1"}. Compiled origin exposes only record:{byteLength,sha256,schema:1,task:"compile",module,ir:{path,layout,format,version}}. Legacy origin is {kind:"legacy-json",path:"morphir-ir.json"}; legacy complete scope is unavailable without a declaration-capable writer.

No raw record bytes, install target, timestamp-derived revision or unknown bookkeeping are public. Record length/digest bind the exact captured record internally. The record selector v3/v4, exact original header version and semantic projection version are distinct. sourceFormatVersion is {status:"reported",release} only when an existing bounded header/codec path establishes that actual release before migration; otherwise {status:"not-reported"}. Never synthesize a patch release from the descriptor.

Inventory pages use next:{kind:"more",startIndex} or next:{kind:"complete"}. More requires nonempty progress and its startIndex equals the preceding start plus actual returned entry count. Complete is valid only at the summary entryCount. Reading the terminal index returns an empty complete page. A page always returns the largest nonempty prefix fitting both maxEntries and the complete reply byte bound. An entry that cannot fit alone refuses; no entry is truncated.

A file entry is {kind:"file",entryId,path,byteLength,sha256}; a directory entry is {kind:"directory",entryId,path}. Read target is {kind:"original",entryId} or {kind:"semantic-projection"}. A directory cannot be read as bytes. Projection bytes use the separate target and never appear as an original file entry or contribute to the original inventory digest.

Complete inventory and exact bytes

Frozen source-version evidence. sourceFormatVersion is derived only from the captured immutable primary snapshot. Never reopen live source to produce it. semantic:none still requires a bounded header probe on those frozen bytes or an explicit not-reported result.

The main available-projection fixture uses CRLF and leading ASCII whitespace, which the existing JSON path accepts. It is a literal client-peer frame, not an expected server serializer output. A separate BOM fixture retains the exact original while the current host JSON conversion reports projection unavailable/invalid_model; no new BOM stripping is silently proposed. A reported4.0.0 release must follow the existing validated normalization of an actual numeric source header4, never the descriptor's v4 selector.

Deterministic page measurement. Measure each candidate as a complete compact UTF-8 JSON-RPC reply with numeric id18446744073709551615, including the exact binding, capture/entry ids, digest, startIndex and candidate next variant. Always use this pessimistic id even for shorter actual request ids. Emit no insignificant whitespace or optional non-ASCII escaping; escape quotes, backslash and controls normally. Member order does not affect byte length. Choose the largest prefix fitting 128KiB and maxEntries. The independent packet includes a long escaped/Unicode binding where n entries fit and n+1 do not.

Enumerate every selected root and every descendant, including empty directories, empty files, unknown metadata and sidecars. Selected roots may not overlap or alias each other. Root paths remain relative to compile.dest; legacy uses the project model filename. Intermediate ancestors outside a selected root are implicit containers, not evidence that their other children were captured. Explicit directory entries preserve emptiness within the selected boundary. Consumers must not drop empty directories while claiming an exact inventory save.

Order entries by unsigned lexicographic UTF-8 bytes of the complete original path. Opaque entry ids are unique within the capture and immutable but do not grant authority elsewhere. Counts satisfy entryCount=fileCount+directoryCount. File byte lengths sum exactly to sourceByteLength. Every page repeats the same binding, capture and inventory digest. Clients verify the complete contiguous entry set, sorted order, roots, file/directory conflicts and all original file digests before publishing a verified original owner.

Source paths reuse ordinary-component confinement, portable filename checks and the artifact profile's explicit C0/DEL/C1 exclusion and normalized alias checks where compatible. Do not reuse the artifact path's1024 UTF-16-unit ceiling: current tree storage defaults to a 4000-character path budget. This proposed source profile allows up to 4000 Unicode scalar values,16000 UTF-8 bytes and 8000 UTF-16 units, at most 128 path components for a selected root, and128 descendant levels below it. No empty, dot, parent, absolute, drive, backslash or colon-bearing component is accepted. Enforce component portability and prefix conflicts. A host-only path outside this explicit export profile causes a whole capture refusal; v1 remains unchanged and nothing is silently omitted.

The digest is over the entry inventory, not over a reserialized semantic model or a remote revision. Define the byte preimage as ASCII morphir/workbench/model-originals/0.1.0-draft.1, one zero byte, unsigned u32 big-endian entryCount, then every sorted entry. An entry contributes kind byte0 for directory or1 for file, u32 big-endian path UTF-8 byte length, exact UTF-8 path bytes, and for files only u64 big-endian byteLength plus the32 raw SHA-256 bytes. SHA-256 of that entire preimage is inventory.sha256. IDs and page boundaries do not change it. These finite length prefixes avoid dependence on a language's JSON member ordering or Unicode escaping.

Each source file may be64MiB, including exact64MiB. Aggregate source bytes may be64MiB independently of record and projection budgets. For an empty file, canonical content is the empty base64 string and SHA-256 is the standard empty digest. EOF reads return an empty chunk; beyond EOF refuses. Nonempty reads return min(maxBytes,length-offset). Source chunks and projection chunks are independently hashed against their respective descriptor. No runtime normalizes BOM, CRLF, metadata, annotations or original numeric spelling.

Semantic projection without format loss

Requiring every client to decode every original storage format would regress connected YAML/tree support. The host may therefore derive a separately labeled semantic JSON projection from the same frozen byte snapshot, using its existing read_value_from_vfs path. Capture record, descriptor, primary and companions under the same shared compile lock; after ownership is copied, conversion may run on that immutable snapshot after releasing the lock. A second unrelated v1 open call can never supply the projection for this capture.

Projection is exactly one of not-requested; unavailable with reason unsupported_representation / invalid_model / decode_limit / projection_limit / capacity / timeout; or available with codec morphir-json, byteLength, sha256 and actual formatVersion. It has its own64MiB retention/serialization budget. Projection byte hashes verify transport integrity; independent server fixtures compare its decoded semantic content rather than require one implementation's member ordering. Client fixtures may use independently authored literal projection bytes.

Existing host JSON/YAML/Ion and single-file/tree codec paths remain authoritative for representations they support. The current writer emits v4 in both layouts and rejects v3 tree writes; a reader capability is not a writer capability. An optional capable client may request semantic:none and decode supported originals locally. It is not required to introduce a new YAML/tree codec service merely to open a connected project.

Projection unavailability does not discard or relabel ready original bytes. The client can retain/download verified originals while reporting inspection unavailable. It must not atomically adopt a usable semantic model until its current-opening guard, projection digest and decode requirements succeed. Preserve the last usable model and its owner separately; never attach a new source owner to an unrelated old semantic model. Rich conceptual metadata and graph identity remain in original sources; a semantic-only projection cannot imply the rich graph was absent.

The connected decode lane must explicitly allow64MiB serialized input, depth128 and100,000 values, counting before recursive materialization where possible. Host conversion uses the same finite structural guard and bounded output writer, not an unchecked allocation followed only by a length test. Local browser/native imports remain 16MiB and their current structure limits. A structural or codec refusal is an inspection limitation, not loss of retained original bytes or permission to fall back to a smaller claimed original. This is proposed work, not a claim that the current16MiB worker already accepts64MiB.

Authority and lifecycle

Connection state is Empty → Capturing → Ready → Released, with Closed retaining only actual worker-owned pending cleanup when needed. Before filesystem access, validate initialized authenticated session, exact currently offered capability, source/provider resolution and project membership in the selected source. Capture ID is freshly generated by the host and scoped to that session, provider and owning connection. A source location, project string, document revision, local opening token and execution identity are separate concepts.

A second capture while Capturing or Ready returns active_capture without replacing the first. File reads, inventory pages and release use the same owning connection and capture; another connection cannot replay them. Repeated inventory/pages/reads are immutable and do not reread or recompile. There is no remote backend execution in capture. The last released capture supports same-connection idempotent release; a subsequent capture retires that tombstone.

Revocation/disconnect closes the owner and drops retained bytes, metadata and slots. If capture/conversion is still running, mark it abandoned and keep its one active credit until completion; its result must be dropped without publication. Lost capture reply or uncertain release requires closing the owning connection, with no retry or v1 fallback. No claim is made that cancellation interrupts an uncooperative OS read. Advisory compile locking guarantees consistency only against cooperating Morphir writers.

Client adoption records an opening before any effects, verifies summary/page/source/projection binding, inventory completeness, file/projection digests and current opening after every await, then confirms release before publishing a verified owner. Local Close Model and replacement keep all existing retained/pending/unknown/disconnected host-work guards. Capture release is not model close or execution release. No handle creates installation, publication or ambient filesystem authority.

Errors and unavailable outcomes

Domain RPC errors use existing JSON-RPC framing and bounded messages, with closed data {profile,contractVersion,code}. Code is one of model_originals.invalid_request / invalid_identity / invalid_path / invalid_path_set / invalid_range / invalid_declaration / unavailable / unknown_handle / active_capture / capacity / source_limit / inventory_limit / reply_limit / capture_failed / timeout. Invalid shape/number requests use JSON-RPC -32602; capability/ownership/lifecycle/resource/IO refusals use -32000. Parse failure uses -32700 and null id only when no valid request id was captured. Otherwise preserve the exact existing request id.

Stable unavailable capture results have only profile,contractVersion,status:unavailable,reason. Reasons are not_compiled / companions_undeclared / unsupported_representation. They allocate no handle and leave Empty. Projection-unavailable belongs inside an otherwise Ready source summary and never becomes an infrastructure success flag. Errors do not echo raw host paths, source text, record extras or unbounded exceptions. Messages are at most 512 UTF-16 units and complete replies remain 128KiB; overflow uses a fixed reply_limit response. Error classification remains exact in compatibility fixtures while UI prose stays separate.

At immutable parent 149c55c9, Workbench registered versions stop at draft 28; draft 29 appears available. It is a candidate only, to be rechecked before publication. Propose separately scoped operations model-originals-server and model-originals-client under that one new exact MCK draft, plus the explicitly mapped seven discovery cases. The server tracer drives actual confined capture/provider/storage code and independently measures complete files, directories, record binding, semantic projection and cleanup. Client tracer uses independently fixed peer frames/byte recipes while exercising actual capture/verification/adoption transitions. Fixed peer projection bytes need not match a server serializer's formatting; server projection compatibility compares decoded semantic content and verifies its actual byte hash. Saved-report tamper checks cover role confusion, empty-directory omission, missing/extra entries, wrong binding/page index, source 64MiB versus projection budgets, declaration absence/invalidity and original-ready/projection-unavailable outcomes.

Capture-core evidence and bounded projection/lifecycle implementation plan

Model originals: bounded projection and owned lifecycle

morphir-etg2.22.1 · 18 October 2026 · next-slice proposal after local commit 29667141

Capture exact originals first, then derive a bounded semantic projection from those same immutable bytes. The current storage core is implemented and tested. Existing codec entry points cannot yet establish every proposed structural and output bound, so no model-originals capability is advertised.

  • Implemented checkpoint
  • Actual codec limits
  • Task 1: checked header and projection
  • Task 2: owned host lifecycle
  • SDK coordination and remaining work

Implemented checkpoint

Parent base 149c55c9b52beb19520bf59770f26ef001674dce; local DCO commit 29667141cd22fbd2c06c0626deea8681c138b460. Rust SDK pin is ef4810782db135986e74c503a7bc3003834a3dd9. Fresh fetch found no upstream changes. The first slice changes six parent source files, including the new crates/morphir/src/commands/ui/model_originals/ module.

  • Exact descriptor primary plus positively declared companions under one shared compile lock.
  • Immutable files, empty directories, independent record/source/metadata limits, portable path conflicts and digest framing.
  • Raw record is privately hashed and dropped; no raw bookkeeping is retained or exposed.
  • Frozen-primary projection plan, without a codec or source-release claim.
  • 20 new storage tests; 137 default-feature UI tests; all-target/all-feature Clippy and formatting pass.
  • Header/projection, host capacity/authority, wire, SDK writer, client and independent MCK qualification.

The receipt is .dev/model-originals/first-capture-receipt.json, SHA256 30f7dd8331f2f8c109779fc582a1d529e01d0a03330d1e3728d26c053ea3b745. The source commit is local only. Existing v1 and TaskResult behavior remain unchanged.

Actual codec limits at the pinned source

The current parent crates/morphir/src/commands/ir_storage.rs:212 helper is a semantic reference, not a resource-qualified conversion route. It reads snapshot files into new buffers, creates complete JSON or typed IR values, and uses unbounded intermediate output vectors. A bounded final writer alone cannot constrain earlier allocations.

Its skip routines recurse without the new profile's depth/value counter; the reader probe can replay through temporary storage.Check finite syntax depth/value work before calling the existing probe, or add an opt-in checked probe. Use captured slices, preserving BOM refusal and leading-whitespace behavior. Do not infer release from descriptor v4.
JSON semanticJsonCodec::decode has no shared 100000-value budget. v4 constructs a typed IR file before emitting events; the parent's direct v4 branch constructs a Value. v3 normalizes through its typed classic reader.Charge depth and values before insertion/allocation; retain the existing v3/v4 semantics. Guard normalized output and every write, rather than measuring a completed output vector.

Its profile reader uses depth1000 and builds a Value without a value-count budget. probe_yaml_header parses the whole value and returns observations, not a reusable bounded release result.Opt-in input64MiB/depth128/value100000 limits in the existing parser before growth, with a shared tree aggregate. The existing JSON event encoders write through a supplied Write, which is a usable output enforcement seam. It does not by itself bound materialization inside a decoder or queued event source. All of these gaps are future implementation requirements, not evidence that malformed input is accepted or that every route currently exhausts memory.

Task 1: checked header and same-snapshot projection

Add a pure preparation boundary over FrozenProjectionPlan. Return a closed SourceReleaseEvidence and ProjectionOutcome, with the canonical existing ReleaseTriplet domain. Separate selector version, actual original header and generated projection version. The unavailable reasons remain the reviewed unsupported_representation | invalid_model | decode_limit | projection_limit | capacity | timeout.

enum SourceReleaseEvidence { Reported(ReleaseTriplet), NotReported }
enum ProjectionOutcome {
    NotRequested,
    Unavailable(ProjectionRefusal),
    Available(OwnedProjection), // private bytes, exact digest, actual release
}
// Existing builtin semantics + new opt-in shared limits; no live filesystem.
prepare(plan: FrozenProjectionPlan, policy: SemanticSelection,
        credit: ProjectionCredit, control: CaptureControl) -> PreparedCapture

For semantic:none, a checked header probe may report a release or explicitly return not-reported. It must not run a full unbounded decoder just to make a version claim. A tree probes only its frozen manifest with the descriptor's format. Preserve exact BOM originals and do not add silent BOM stripping.

For projection, acquire the worst-case64MiB projection credit before any semantic conversion; failure leaves originals ready with capacity-unavailable projection. Existing codecs need an additive opt-in DecodeLimits/DecodeBudget boundary, with builtins enforcing byte/depth/value limits before AST/container growth and before semantic assembly. Historical entry points/default limits stay unchanged. Unsupported custom codecs fail closed when asked for limits. This is a coordinated Rust SDK change, not a new handwritten Morphir codec.

A parent ProjectionWriter checks remaining64MiB output credit and cancellation before extending its private vector, updates its hash incrementally, and refuses one-over writes without retaining the excess. Shared decode budget spans the complete selected primary tree. Companion bytes are preserved originals and are not fed to the semantic codec implicitly. Successful output becomes immutable only after the complete codec finishes, the actual output header is established, and current attempt authority is rechecked.

  • Red/green checked-probe tests for CRLF/whitespace, numeric4 normalization, late header, duplicate/invalid header, BOM, depth/value exact and one-over.
  • Actual JSON/YAML/Ion file/tree projections with existing writer fixtures, exact originals preserved, and invalid source retaining originals.
  • Output64MiB exact/one-over, aggregate tree nodes, pre-copy limits, stale/cancelled conversion, no read of changed live source.
  • SDK parser tests proving refusal occurs before forbidden node/container growth, not just after conversion.

Task 2: owned host lifecycle before RPC publication

Add an independent HostModelCaptureCapacity with closed RAII credits for one active worker,64 retained/reserved slots,128MiB retained/reserved source+projection, and64MiB metadata. Keep artifact capacity unchanged. Reserve active work and a slot before opening storage; reserve bytes before each retained copy. Derive a private attempt binding from the authenticated actual provider, selected source and selected project. No caller path or matching identity string supplies filesystem authority.

Mermaid source
flowchart LR
 A[Authenticated selected source] -- reserve slot and work --> B[Capture exact roots under shared lock]
 B -- immutable primary --> C[Checked header and optional projection]
 C -- recheck current authority --> D[Retain ready capture or discard]
 C -- cancelled or expired --> E[No publication; worker owns cleanup credit]
 D -- release or disconnect --> F[Drop exact owned capture]

The connection state is Empty | Capturing(OwnedAttempt) | Ready(OwnedCapture) | Released | Closed. A timeout/cancel result does not drop a permit held by a still-running blocking worker. Move credits into that worker; transfer only retained credits on a successful current result. A single worker owns raw-record/codec temporary work. Closing a connection makes publication impossible and eventually drops its capture. Release is distinct from semantic model release or execution release.

The preparation API must accept reservation callbacks or an owned credit object before copying each source file and metadata entry. Merely checking host totals after the current standalone capture returns is insufficient. The currently committed storage core enforces per-capture bounds only; it does not claim host-wide retention/concurrency qualification.

  • Two authenticated connections: exact provider/source/project, cross-handle refusal, one active worker,64 slots including zero-byte captures.
  • Byte/metadata exact capacity, rollback on each IO/decode failure, release/disconnect and subsequent reuse.
  • Held worker after timeout/close retains active credit, cannot publish late, and cannot close or free another connection's ready owner.
  • One-over source remains a capture failure; projection failure preserves ready originals and exact record binding.

SDK coordination and remaining work

The SDK declaration seam is morphir-devkit/src/out/result.rs: add a typed optional writer/accessor over reserved TaskResult.extra.morphirModelOriginals, preserving unknown extras and historical deserialization. The parent-private declaration parser is temporary and should be replaced by that one published domain, not maintained as a parallel declaration model. Actual compile/prepare.rs:615 can publish it only after the storage writer positively declares its model-owned companions in the same atomic record under the existing exclusive lock. No inferred default empty declaration.

Coordinate SDK changes before editing its separately owned checkout. The codec work belongs in morphir-common::ir_transport and the existing core JSON/YAML/Ion/layout parsers; the parent owns the profile policy, frozen-source adapter, bounded writer and host lifecycle. A first checked JSON route can be a local vertical proof while the other builtin routes are implemented, but is not permission to mark the profile or campaign complete with those formats omitted.

Legacy originals, schemas, complete encoded reply limits, deterministic inventory paging, chunk reads, release RPC, actual browser/native owner, original-inventory saves, independent corpus authorship and MCK allocation remain pending. Existing artifact draft28 and the 60+35+49 authored model cases are untouched. No new MCK version is allocated in this note.
acceptance_criteria: Normative mapping and fixed independent fixtures/schemas cover provider separation, same project names, original versus semantic version, release/replacement and discovery compatibility. Parent checker rejects forged evidence and keeps all frozen contracts intact.

title: Preserve model sources and publish reference mappings
description: Close original model/revision coordination requirements by explicitly mapping existing identities, preserving original bytes and versions alongside private semantic IR on ordinary import/connected project opening, and adding a named local model-release transition. Independently qualify the declared shared Rust/TypeScript/MoonBit discovery intersection using the existing MCK and real production paths. Keep frozen connected v1 and capture/execution authority distinct.
design:
Workbench model and reference mapping

Model preservation plan · 18 October 2026 · local owner PR #150 published; parent/UI landed; connected inventory contract pending

  1. Original requirement
  2. Existing identities
  3. Source and authority flow
  4. Concrete gaps
  5. Reference intersection
  6. Current import paths and compiled layouts
  7. Source version foundation
  8. Local document ownership
  9. Published implementation
  10. Original inventory ownership
  11. Remaining requirements and verification

Original requirement

The campaign accepts a normative profile that adopts or explicitly maps existing contracts and coordinates Rust, TypeScript and MoonBit model/revision semantics. The candidate design proposes importing/releasing a distribution, inspecting symbols, searching definitions and retaining original IR versions, with runtime handles mapped to existing provider/source identities. These describe a service seam; they do not require every operation to become a remote RPC or require Rust to implement the Scheme evaluator.

Existing immutable execution snapshots and native capture cleanup are real implementations. They cannot substitute for every model/document lifetime or original-version requirement. This draft distinguishes what can be mapped today from behavior still requiring implementation and independent fixtures.

Existing identities

ConceptActual representationMeaning and scope
Source locationRust/TS source_key/sourceKey = JSON.stringify([providerId,locator])Provider-scoped location, independent of display label and session-persistence hint. It is not an immutable revision or filesystem permission.
Project locationproject_key/projectKey = [providerId,locator,relativePath]Distinct same-named projects retain path identity. WorkspaceSnapshot.id is a location key, not a content digest.
Logical unit ownershipMoonBit SourceSnapshot.unit_id and IRUnit.idCodec/metadata ownership. Raw JSON checkpoint opening uses the logical default workbench. These values confer no host authority.
Current UI modelmodel_revision, request ID and current semantic projectionPage-local stale-reply and selection guard. It is distinct from Morphir IR formatVersion, project manifest version and provider source identity.
Native transfersessionId + grantId + sequenceOS-authorized bounded byte capture. Release retires a capture; revoke closes the root grant. Neither is an execution snapshot identity.
Accepted executionFive-part host/session/provider/execution/snapshot identityImmutable captured rich unit and invocation suite. Terminal release frees owner retention; cancellation acknowledgement alone does not finish it.

Evidence: crates/morphir/src/commands/ui/protocol.rs:65,266,544; UI packages/morphir-workspace/src/model.ts; MoonBit pkgs/morphir-engine/data/types.mbt:28 and execution/executions/session.mbt:69–152.

Source and authority flow

On narrow screens, scroll the diagram horizontally. Focus its frame to use the arrow keys.

Mermaid source
flowchart LR
 A[Provider source + captured original] --> B[Private current IR]
 B --> C[Inspect / search]
 B --> D[Replace / release local reference]
 B --> E[Accepted execution snapshot]
 E --> F[Terminal owner release]

LocalAdapter creates and terminates a fresh worker for each operation (browser/transport.ts:59–81). Inspection/search need no remote retained-model service. NativeWorkspaceClient confirms transfer release before local inspection (native-workspace.ts); its byte capture is not an enduring loaded-model handle.

Concrete gaps

Connected compile/generate is already careful: transport.test.ts:93 proves the host IR and negotiated IR version survive private inspection migration. The missing retention concerns imported/project-model source documents, not that proven compilation behavior.

Reference intersection

MoonBit has seven pinned discovery fixtures from revision 5c5307d8. All seven equal the pinned TypeScript UI corpus cases exactly. Current Rust has 22 cases and moved discovery protocolVersion from numeric 1 to 0.1.0-draft.1, adding project origin. It is therefore incorrect to claim all three current raw corpora are identical.

An explicit compatibility projection—map discovery version to frozen connected-v1 semantics and omit origin from that older UI snapshot—makes every request/expected pair in the seven-case intersection equal. This is a measured data comparison, not new execution evidence. Rust provider conformance exercises 11 selected current cases; TypeScript browser/desktop suites use 21 older cases; MoonBit tests replay seven. A current cross-language run and named projection remain required. The TypeScript discovery path wraps a generated Rust Wasm engine; it is a real cross-language consumer/reference path, not an independently implemented discovery algorithm.

Fixture sourceCount / SHA-256
MoonBit workspace/fixtures/upstream.json7 · 4ef9e5a30231986b71b4b67304908e10de08db52419d6c2a51d21e11324efe62
Rust workspace-discovery/corpus.json22 · effd9cd958670223ad4e50caa16d0110a468739fe11e53602d9eaa85075ea0c1
UI generated/workspace-discovery-corpus.json21 · fa4028f2da4d0110343a9451f8ab7ae77f96c3fd6e328766dfccfcf7cab232d0

Sources: parent provider/conformance.rs:18,224; UI apps/morphir-web/test/workspace-conformance.test.ts, apps/morphir-desktop/test/workspace-conformance.test.ts; MoonBit workspace/protocol_test.mbt. UI reference tests also cover source identity and retained last-usable model in model.test.ts and project-model-state.test.ts.

Import paths and compiled layouts at the earlier audit

The current source audit preserves all pending requirements above. It changes the implementation plan for connected models: the returned JSON can be a semantic projection reconstructed from a recorded compile output. Preserving that response cannot prove preservation of the original stored artifact.

PathCurrent evidenceRequired implementation and proof
Browser Importbootstrap.ts:importModel calls File.text() and passes only text. Inspection migrates to current IR.Capture bounded original bytes and filename before decoding. Keep the original format version beside the semantic version. Historical JSON fixtures with BOM, CRLF, whitespace and exact numeric lexemes must download byte for byte. A text decoder must not erase the retained original.
Native file selectionnative-workspace.ts:open passes captured base64/codec to inspection and returns originalArtifact after capture release and session revalidation.Adopt the same original-document ownership model while preserving existing picker, capture, cleanup and stale-reply guards. Continue supporting JSON, Ion text and Ion binary without conflating model release with capture release.
Connected legacy JSONproject_model.rs:read_legacy reads bounded bytes and requires valid UTF-8; v1 returns them as a content string. ConnectedAdapter.execute currently returns only private inspection.Retain the returned original text and its validated UTF-8 bytes when the provider identifies it as the original document. Preserve source/provider/project identity separately from filename and model revision. Do not parse and reserialize the original through JavaScript numbers.
Connected compiled outputsproject_model/compiled.rs:load follows compile.json, confines and snapshots a single artifact or document tree, decodes through read_value_from_vfs, then serializes JSON. The current loader tests JSON/YAML and both layouts.Keep frozen v1 semantics. Publish an explicit additive mapping for original artifact inventories, format/layout/version and source identity before offering original-source download for this path. Capture the actual confined files under the same compile lock. Independently compare original files and tree inventory, including unknown metadata and sidecars. Never label reconstructed JSON as the original file.

The source-document owner should distinguish a retained original file or inventory from a semantic projection whose originals are unavailable. This is a proposed domain boundary, not an implemented capability. Reuse existing validated codec, path, version and source-identity concepts. Do not introduce a collection of unrelated optional strings and booleans.

A named local release clears the active model, original-document owner, selection and navigation references, and invalidates late replies. It must obey the existing retained-host-execution replacement guard. Capture release, execution cancellation and terminal execution release remain separate operations. Releasing a displayed model does not acquire filesystem or publication authority.

The independent fixture matrix must cover every accepted import path, historical versions 1–4, original versus semantic version, identical project names under distinct providers, replacement, explicit local release, delayed replies and complete original inventories for both compiled layouts. Use the existing shared Rust checker and actual production adapters. Data equality among old discovery corpora remains insufficient for a current cross-language compatibility claim.

Inspected sources: MoonBit b80f7380e84f80ebc1dba2e18f0f5260f6145aff, browser/bootstrap.ts, browser/transport.ts, browser/native-workspace.ts, pipeline.mbt and morphir-ir/conformance/migration_test.mbt; parent 7709b00c7af3ffbcfc731ec3ccac4a4001068530, commands/ui/provider/project_model.rs and project_model/compiled.rs. This checkpoint is source inspection and planning. No new preservation behavior or platform acceptance is claimed.

Source version foundation

Registry::inspect_checkpoint returns a privately constructed CheckpointInspection with the existing validated FormatVersion. JSON and rich Ion readers capture the original checkpoint version before migrating its distribution. open_checkpoint shares the same validation path. Ion checkpoint opening now parses its input once. Existing byte, tree, profile, metadata and diagnostic rules remain in force.

The Workbench pipeline emits sourceFormatVersion beside its migrated formatVersion. This describes the supplied input. It does not establish that a connected provider response is an original source document. The returned engine unit also retains its existing mutable collections; it is not a new immutable snapshot or a retained-model authority.

Verification: 19 data-boundary tests and 85 Workbench pipeline tests pass on each of JS, native, Wasm and Wasm GC. Fixed v1, v2, v3, v3.1 and v4 source documents exercise JSON, Ion text and Ion binary. Additional cases cover nonzero patch releases, migrated-version separation, strict profile/byte/tree failures and rich Ion annotation order, duplicate metadata fields, exact large integers and provenance.

The next implementation remains morphir-etg2.22.2: bounded original-byte ownership for browser and native imports, atomic current-attempt adoption, and a named Close Model transition. Capture an opening identity before the picker or read. Refuse closure while a host submission is pending, retained, disconnected or uncertain. Clear both active model and model-owned prior output, and sanitize model navigation history, so delayed replies and Back cannot restore a closed document. Keep native capture cleanup and execution lifetime separate.

Connected v1 remains a semantic projection whose originals are not provided. Additive confined source-inventory mapping, actual connected adoption and final cross-language/platform qualification are still required by morphir-etg2.22.1, .22.2 and .22.3. None of those tasks is closed by this foundation.

Local document ownership

Implemented locally: b790248..f7d7cb2ff8a8cb17cf2dfcb59af6b6c7fcf5c99c in the isolated model-lifecycle worktree. Not pushed or landed.

Opening identities are captured before the picker/read. Document revisions bind both Original File and rich Source Unit download controls to the displayed document. Close Model refuses pending, running, disconnected and unknown host submissions. Its cancellation only targets its own inspect/project request. Native transfer cleanup and execution release keep their separate owners; unconfirmed capture cleanup still prevents another native open.

Verification: 7 pure owner tests pass on JS, native, Wasm and Wasm GC; 65 browser state tests and 169 application tests pass. The full browser workflow passes, including existing Elm/MoonBit workspaces, generated sources, worksheet, connected v1 and exact typed values. A byte-import error-message regression found by that workflow was fixed with a pipeline regression test. A later UTF-16 wait timed out once; isolated and full reruns passed without a production change to that evaluation path.

Still required: normative source/project identity and inventory mapping, actual connected original inventories, independent shared MCK model/reference fixtures and production adapter runs, packaged desktop qualification and reviewed landing. Native OS Save-dialog verification remains incomplete because accessibility reads are blocked despite the user's permission toggle. No child of morphir-etg2.22 is closed by this local implementation.

Published implementation and main integration

The local-file ownership slice is published in PR #150 at 7dcafe122364eab2dc6824b1dee73a6f02232b69. Main #149 is integrated. Compiler regeneration preserves both the checkpoint source-version API and the new conceptual model records. The model document's internal phase is private, and its generated public interface is checked in. The desktop workspace includes the conceptual module required by the new main dependency.

All 27 engine data tests pass on JS, native, Wasm and Wasm GC after integration. The complete real Chromium workflow also passes after integration, including exact original-file bytes, failed replacement, closing during a held File read, preserved editor content and existing language/worksheet/connected-v1 flows. TypeScript checks pass 198 files in five projects and account for all 161 handwritten sources. Required lint, formatting, validation and normal push gates pass. The earlier owner/pipeline/full-repository receipts below retain their earlier source scope.

PR #150 is monitored for exact-head CI and all four comment channels. It is a reviewable local-file ownership slice, not completion of connected original inventories or shared model/reference qualification. No .22 child is closed by publication.

Original inventory ownership

The connected contract will capture the exact descriptor file or complete descriptor tree, plus positively declared model companions. Preserve all unknown bytes inside each declared source root. A whole compile.dest directory is task scratch, so it does not implicitly establish model ownership of unrelated siblings.

Raw compile.json is an internal binding by default. Current writers include absolute installed-target keys, source-selection paths and unknown task extras. Bind its exact digest and length together with validated public schema/task/module/descriptor facts; do not expose raw host bookkeeping through the model-original download. Leave the original on-disk record intact. A single-file descriptor requires an explicit writer/provider declaration before sibling sidecars can be claimed as a complete inventory. Refuse an incomplete promised inventory rather than silently dropping companions.

The cooperating Morphir compile lock must cover binding reads and every captured root. This provides consistency among cooperating writers and does not make an advisory lock a universal filesystem snapshot. Capture, document and execution authorities remain separate, bounded and revocable.

Main #149 adds conceptual graph records with their own identity and version, carried in unit metadata. An empty IR symbol set can still carry a rich conceptual graph. Neither graph presence nor successful structural inspection proves original-byte retention or evaluator capabilities. Keep graph identity/version distinct from the source location, document revision and IR format version.

This ownership decision follows independent immutable-source review of parent f29685e9, Rust SDK ef481078 and MoonBit 0c4069c5. The original 60 independent scenarios remain unchanged. A separate dated addition proposes 35 policy and conceptual cases without reading implementation outputs. These are drafting inputs, not a frozen normative MCK or completed compatibility run.

Still specify the writer/provider companion declaration, additive capability and wire semantics, framing and manifest budgets, cleanup and shared MCK allocation. Then freeze independent fixtures and run real Rust, TypeScript and MoonBit paths. The .22.1 mapping and .22.3 qualification tasks remain open.

Independent source-addition receipt SHA-256 d9763d025038c7956c6fc032c3aefc383d7ec8719d9bf664c1174a41ae9a3d71; additional 35-scenario JSON SHA-256 a38de0e8750a3111ea28541d76a4965c0e4402924f93b1504de42bdca60953d0. External files under .dev/model-reference-contract/ must accompany the HTML for full source/case review.

Remaining requirements and verification

  1. Publish a normative mapping of existing source/project identities, private semantic inspection and independently scoped capture/execution authority. Preserve frozen v1 methods.
  2. Retain original source/format alongside private migrated IR for ordinary Import and connected project opening; validate this using historical version files and exact numeric payloads.
  3. Independently qualify and land the named local model-release transition across the remaining connected and desktop paths. Keep separate native transfer and terminal execution cleanup obligations explicit.
  4. Use the existing shared Rust MCK and explicit production adapters/reference paths for fixed mapping fixtures: provider separation, identical project names, original versus semantic version, replacement/release, and the declared seven-case discovery projection. No second runner or Rust Scheme evaluator is required by this slice.

This draft does not claim completion, current execution of the TypeScript suites, or new platform support. It is local review material; the owning campaign must store and publish an approved revision before closure.

What the package smoke must prove

  1. Build the complete distribution from the selected commit. Launch its public entry with PROTON_HEADLESS=1, a new temporary profile and a loopback CDP port owned by the test. Remove development runtime/helper/frontend overrides and MORPHIR_WORKBENCH_LAUNCH_URL from the child's environment. A dev server or an externally supplied CEF runtime must not satisfy the smoke.
  2. Decode real trusted-page replies through the production native-policy-response codec. Verify the exact native .2 descriptor, stable page authority and operations: [], with no execution offer or capability-check offer. Verify unknown-session refusal.
  3. Run browser-worker compilation and execution, then import the existing typed-pricing fixture and evaluate strict fields, JSON and Ion inputs. Assert concrete expected values and typed validation errors. Capture bridge calls to prove there was no native execution submission. Capability-policy and workspace controls must remain unavailable.
  4. Reload the actual CEF page. Obtain a new session and verify that the old session cannot check or perform effects. Verify the current session closes and a later session has different authority. Use actual raw protocol requests and replies, not a mocked adapter.
  5. Send correctly framed unsupported execution/workspace requests and verify the production refusal with no worker or grant effect. Opening a valid page session must never add operations that the descriptor omits.
  6. Navigate the bundled frontend to explicit standalone mode. Compile and evaluate typed inputs through the browser worker, with no native-session invocation. This proves the portable browser client is present in the distributed frontend.
  7. Attempt the platform's real browser-window close path and record its actual outcome. CDP target/window close needs live verification on each host. Keep forced cleanup separate from an observed normal exit. Confirm all app/helper processes owned by the test exit, and remove its profile. Linux and Windows have no enabled native owner workers in this baseline.

The existing desktop smoke assumes executions and workspace are offered. Reuse its real UI fixtures and helpers, but give the fallback package path its own assertions. Do not weaken the richer macOS test to make an empty descriptor pass. The macOS lifecycle acceptance continues to prove actual owner-spawned native worker removal and normal AppKit quit independently.

Portable CI and dispatch

Extend the existing dispatchable qualification workflow with a packaged matrix. Its current installed Workbench jobs explicitly run without CEF. They cannot count as package qualification. Use ubuntu-24.04 and windows-2022, fail-fast: false, and require both selected lanes to report success on the same candidate commit.

scripts/workbench-packaged-targets.mbtx uses a closed target and validated digest values for acquisition, builds, acceptance invocation and receipt verification. The application TypeScript acceptance owns its real package fixture through the installed CLI's already qualified process-group/Windows Job adapter and performs page assertions. Keep this OS adapter reuse explicit; add no second root JavaScript, Bash, PowerShell or Python task orchestrator. Workflow steps invoke maintained task commands and existing bootstrap tools.

For a new workflow, GitHub requires its dispatch definition on the default branch before manual triggering. Extending the already registered qualification workflow avoids inventing a dispatch target. After the implementation is reviewable and authorized, select the candidate branch explicitly and verify the resulting run's SHA before using its receipts. GitHub manual dispatch documentation.

gh workflow run qualification.yml --ref <candidate-branch>
gh run watch <run-id>

These are proposed dispatch operations. This design task has not performed them. The implementation must expose an explicit packaged-target input or run the required matrix unconditionally; an omitted or skipped matrix cannot count as a successful acceptance.

Evidence and limits

The inspected Morphir source was 564308e. The local macOS lifecycle receipt records candidate b544fc4, app PID 57497, actual native worker PIDs 57602, 57740 and 58743, all removed, and a normal application exit with code 0 and no signal. Its three phases cover reload, explicit session close and AppKit terminate. A separate PR review fix subsequently reran the same package with PID/birth-based removal checks and an actual unreaped-child regression. Its new macOS receipt records app PID 74498 and workers 74622, 74785 and 74905 removed at the same three boundaries, again with exit code 0 and no signal. The binary digest is unchanged. Neither receipt extends to another candidate or operating system.

Linux and Windows baseline receipts will qualify the packaged shell, page authority and browser-worker client. They will not qualify native worker ownership, cancellation, native workspace grants, OS file pickers, normal AppKit quit, Windows installer behavior, Linux FUSE integration or GPU acceleration. Any later enablement of native operations needs its own actual worker and OS lifecycle acceptance before changing the platform gate.

title: Transfer negotiated generated artifacts byte-exactly
description: Close the original campaign artifact negotiation gap with an exact additive profile, bounded authenticated manifest/chunk/release methods, real Rust producer bytes, verified TypeScript downloads and coordinated upstream client support. design:
Negotiated artifact bytes

Campaign completion design · 18 October 2026 · Revision 14 · Parent and UI integrations landed; final client and all native Save workflows pass; Workbench landing pending

A generated file should arrive with its original bytes intact, even when it is binary or larger than one RPC reply should carry. The Rust producer already has a binary representation. The missing boundary is an explicit agreement between the authenticated host and its clients, followed by verified, bounded transfer and download.

  • What the source proves

  • Landed upstream source and current checks
  • Parent service landed
  • Current client qualification

What the source proves

Inspected sources are Workbench 564308e4, parent Morphir 8e6636f1, pinned morphir-rust af122ed0 and pinned morphir-ui 8e4bbf2f. These findings do not claim that the proposed profile is implemented.

Primary sourceFinding
Rust SDK ArtifactThe SDK explicitly defines binary:true content as base64. Its Rust String does not imply arbitrary raw bytes or lossy UTF-8 decoding.
Actual WASM producerThe backend uses standard base64 over the generated WASM bytes, then constructs an SDK artifact. This is direct producer evidence, not a guess based on a field name.
Parent provider projection and PlaygroundArtifactThe connected host copies path/content/binary unchanged into a closed v1 artifact structure. It does not transmit an encoding selection, byte length, digest, or transfer handle.
Workbench transport.ts:280–288 and artifact-download.ts:5–51The client intentionally discards unnegotiated extra encoding fields. Binary downloads require a declared canonical base64 encoding, so a connected binary artifact currently remains opaque. Local declared binary bytes already download and archive exactly.
RPC boundaryInbound RPC messages are limited to 1 MiB, binary frames are refused, and every response is currently one JSON text message. The inbound limit does not establish an outbound or retained-artifact bound.
Loopback host, session authenticationA one-use launch token creates an HttpOnly SameSite cookie. WebSocket upgrade checks cookie, Host and Origin, then initialization checks the exact session. New artifact methods should reuse this authority.
Upstream TypeScript schemasThe upstream client also models the frozen v1 artifact shape. Capabilities are already name/version entries, so a new profile can be offered without changing that shape.
Proton app/main.mbt:28The actual desktop host allows a main-window Blob export from its bundled or authenticated connected origin and shows a save dialog. A verified transfer can reuse that path.

The WASM producer's binary encoder is real, but its current backend advertises no supported IR versions and explicitly rejects standard Morphir IR roots. That does not qualify a current frontend-to-WASM workflow. Artifact transfer must not silently make that backend appear compatible in the dropdown.

Changes since the original audit

The original 18 October audit above remains the historical baseline. Revision 2 checked Workbench 970f44d, including merged main 0ee036c2 (#144), parent main 4c447d7c (#1067) and its pending worksheet candidate 60f2b265. The Rust and UI gitlinks remain af122ed0 and 8e4bbf2f. At that audit, artifact transfer was unimplemented and unqualified. Revision 6 implementation evidence is recorded separately below.

Current source evidenceEffect on this plan
#144 production generator fixture and generated-library qualificationReal generated multi-module MoonBit source is assembled with its SDK/core graph, selected exports, dead-code removal and initialization. The embedding test publishes manifest.ion and model.wasm, then loads and executes them independently. These are additional genuine local byte inputs. Assembly, saved-artifact publication and authenticated artifact transfer remain separate operations; this does not qualify the required Rust producer/host lane or a Rust frontend-to-Wasm target.
Current assembly-check.mbtx and corrected-core selectionThe integrated assembly gate selects the corrected pinned core explicitly. Use the settled worksheet/toolchain baseline for final qualification; do not infer an ordinary command's core selection from a version label alone.
#1067 source example and revision-scoped evidenceThe six changed files are conceptual documentation/examples. They introduce no live provider, RPC, source-handle or SDK operation. Preserve revision-scoped evidence language, without treating those examples as implemented artifact handles or adding conceptual-intent implementation as a prerequisite.
At the Revision 2 audit parent main ended at shared MCK draft 26; worksheet draft 27 has now landed through #1068.Reserve the next exact artifact evidence contract as 0.1.0-draft.28, after rechecking authoritative parent state once worksheet 27 lands. Preserve every frozen kit, including codec 26 and worksheet 27. The independently versioned artifact profile remains morphir/workbench/artifacts at 0.1.0-draft.1.

The Revision 2 parent projected one actual SDK generate result to the frozen three-field v1 artifact, with no connection-owned transfer store. Its provider already resolves the selected backend and invokes it with a bound. Factor that one invocation into a typed SDK-result/provenance helper; both v1 and the additive profile must project the same result. A read or release must never invoke generation again.

Parent Morphir's profile, schemas, shared MCK draft 28 and authenticated Rust host have landed through #1069. Rust response-budget and literal-input prerequisites landed through #303. Remaining coordinated landings are morphir-ui's final source pin and morphir-moonbit's verified-byte Workbench flow, with full packaged native saved-file evidence still pending. The existing Rust SDK base64 contract and path/digest types suffice; no SDK schema bump is required.

Reuse the existing Rust morphir_distribution::RelativeArtifactPath and Sha256Digest value types. The first validates portable relative components; the second parses and hashes exact bytes. Do not reuse ModelPayload for arbitrary generated data: its codec and validation semantics are specifically Morphir JSON/Ion models.

enum GeneratedContent {
    Utf8Text(Arc<[u8]>),
    Binary(Arc<[u8]>),

    digest: Sha256Digest,

// Smart constructors validate a complete artifact set before retaining it.

A manifest binds generation ID, authenticated session ID, provider ID, actual resolved producer ID/version, selected target and IR version, and an ordered inventory of {id,path,kind,byteLength,sha256}. kind is the closed utf8-text | binary distinction. Paths are display/archive hints. IDs are connection-bound correlations and are never treated as independent bearer credentials. Keep the client capture of source/request identity with this binding; the wire fields above do not imply a new live model-revision API.

Use semver::Version in Rust and the repository's canonical SemVer parser in TypeScript. Exact drafts match literally after canonical validation. A type alias for an arbitrary string is not a validated ID or digest.

Bytes and limits

BoundaryNormative proposed rule
SDK conversionFor text, retain String::as_bytes() exactly. For binary:true, decode the SDK's documented standard base64, require canonical padded spelling by round-trip comparison, and retain the resulting bytes. Reject malformed binary content; never treat its UTF-8 characters as the file.
Complete setAt most 256 files, 16 MiB per file and 64 MiB decoded aggregate. Validate paths, contents, lengths and all collisions before publishing a ready manifest. A failed or malformed backend result exposes diagnostics without a partial transfer inventory.
PathsReuse RelativeArtifactPath: at most 4,096 UTF-8 bytes and 1,024 UTF-16 units for the complete path, with each component bounded at 255 UTF-8 bytes and 255 UTF-16 units. Reject device names (including COM/LPT superscript forms), trailing dots/spaces, forbidden characters and control characters. Reject duplicate names, normalization/casefold collisions and file/directory prefix conflicts under one published portable key. Reuse the parent writer's pure NFKC → full default casefold → NFC key: unicode-normalization 0.1.25 uses Unicode 17.0.0; unicode-casefold 0.2.0 uses Unicode 9.0.0. Freeze both data versions and matching TS behavior, with common fixtures and provenance. Runtime-dependent normalize() and toLowerCase() alone do not establish this policy. Legal Unicode scalar text under the 1,024-UTF-16-unit cap can reach at most 3,072 UTF-8 bytes, so 4,096 is not an achievable positive path boundary. Do not invent such a fixture. The additive profile rejects C0, DEL and C1 controls without changing legacy path constructors. Never join these names to a host output root.
FramesThe complete new generation request envelope retains the existing 1 MiB UTF-8 JSON bound. Read/release requests fit 16 KiB; complete encoded manifest, chunk and failure/diagnostic reply envelopes fit 128 KiB. Encode and check the whole manifest plus diagnostics before entering Ready: 256 otherwise legal long paths can exceed that cap. Refuse without a partial inventory, release reservations and use a bounded diagnostic; do not recursively echo oversized input in the failure. Read chunks carry at most 65,536 decoded bytes, with at most 87,384 base64 characters. Existing RPC's 1 MiB input limit and text-only framing remain unchanged.
ReadsOffsets and counts are finite integral bytes, within the advertised file. Read min(maxBytes, length-offset). A repeated identical read returns identical bytes. Requests beyond EOF, wrong IDs or zero/oversized counts refuse. An EOF read may return an empty chunk; clients normally stop once the declared length is complete.
Client acceptanceCheck exact profile, generation context, unique safe paths and IDs, bounded declared lengths and canonical lowercase SHA-256 spelling before allocating. The reused Rust digest parser also accepts uppercase; profile decoding must enforce lowercase canonical round-trip. Validate chunk IDs, offset progression, base64 length and decoded count. Hash the complete assembled bytes and compare length/digest before any downloadable Blob or ZIP entry is created.
TextStrict UTF-8 decode only for preview. A hostile utf8-text declaration with invalid UTF-8 may still own downloadable bytes after exact context, length and digest verification; preview returns the closed InvalidUtf8 unavailable result. The declared kind does not construct a validated String. Preserve BOM, CRLF, trailing newlines and original bytes for downloads. A lossy preview, newline normalization or re-encoding must not become the download payload.
MemoryOne active generation per connection, 64 reserved/retained generation slots across the host, and 64 MiB decoded byte reservation/retention, with bounded descriptors. Reserve a generation slot before actual invocation; hold the single host producer invocation credit through conversion and retention. The slot, invocation and byte limits are distinct. Derive decoded lengths from validated encoded lengths and reserve aggregate capacity before conversion/retention. Reject capacity exhaustion before allocation or publishing a manifest, and roll back reservations on every failure. Account for retained bytes, host reservations, in-flight decoded bytes and client ZIP working memory separately; these limits do not claim to bound every allocation made by the existing generator or MEP host.

Make the encoded and decoded limits explicit in the published profile and exercise their boundaries independently. A larger transfer is a documented refusal, not an unbounded buffering fallback. The profile transfers already generated bytes in chunks; it does not claim that backends generate output incrementally.

Policy provenance: portable component/path constructors, digest value type, parent collision key and pinned casefold/normalization packages. Publish the data-table provenance and common fixtures with the new profile; this plan does not alter those existing contracts.

Authority and lifecycle

Store retained transfers in the existing authenticated RPC connection's ownership. The session and artifact capability must still be available when each method is dispatched. A later backend registry change does not mutate bytes already accepted into a ready manifest. A second connection with the same cookie cannot read another connection's handles. Bind new methods to the selected provider; do not broaden the arbitrary source provider's permissions.

EventRequired transition
GenerateEmpty/Released → Generating → Ready only after one bounded successful invocation, complete artifact validation and successful encoded-manifest/diagnostic budget check. On failure return to empty and release reservations. Do not let a second request replace an active generation silently.
ReadPure byte-slice selection from the immutable ready generation. A read does not invoke the generator or publish files.
Complete, cancel retrieval or replace outputClient releases the exact generation. Host drops its bytes/reservation and retains only a bounded last-release identity for idempotence. Late reads fail and late replies cannot mutate a newer client generation.
Socket/session closes or host shuts downDrop all connection-owned transfers and reservations when closure is observed. An in-flight synchronous generator retains its existing invocation bound; this does not promise immediate generator interruption. No recovery promise and no filesystem cleanup transaction are needed because no output files were written.
Generation reply lostAcceptance/retention may be unknown. Do not auto-generate again. Closing the owning socket clears its state once the bounded invocation ends. A new connection starts without those handles.
Cancel before manifestThe existing generation invocation is synchronous within RPC dispatch. Stopping client waiting does not prove generator cancellation. Label that action honestly; provider timeout/abandon remains the existing bounded behavior. This transfer profile adds cancellation of retained-byte retrieval, not remote evaluator cancellation.

Generated bytes, assembled modules, server-retained bytes, user-downloaded files and published files are different states. A ready manifest means generated and retained. A Blob click means a download was requested. An actual saved file can establish its bytes independently. No path hint grants publication authority, and no UI status should say that the server published a project to disk.

Keep morphir generate's existing artifact writer and the embedding API's prepareArtifact/publishArtifact separate. The writer has filesystem ownership, locks and rollback rules; the embedding publisher persists assembled artifacts for a later loader. Neither is the in-memory manifest/read/release service. This work adds no publication, package installation, durable session or restoration operation.

Client coordination

Workbench captures the selected provider/profile, target, IR version, cloned generation input and source/request identity before its first await. Existing connected document version, request epoch and captured compiled IR can supply this identity; use a model revision when one is actually provided. Do not invent a live model-handle API from conceptual examples. Keep a closed transfer state such as Unavailable | Generating | Receiving | Verified | Failed | Released. A validated VerifiedArtifactBytes object privately owns bytes and metadata; the constructor becomes available only after length and digest checks.

Reconcile the captured context after every await: generation, each chunk, digest verification and release. The current legacy generation path lacks the post-generation current-request check; the new profile must add its own explicit checks. A late manifest or chunk cannot replace newer output. Release the exact old generation on completion, failure, cancellation, replacement or a late obsolete manifest, without clearing or releasing a newer generation. When the generation ID was never received or release cannot complete, close the owning socket so host cleanup can resolve uncertain retention after the bounded invocation. Make this failure visible rather than silently retaining an unknown generation.

The settled transport design uses one authenticated socket owned by one generation attempt. It performs the existing v1 initialization, then accepts raw artifact-only reply frames for the selected exact profile. On unknown retention or release failure, close only that attempt’s socket so its server-owned generation can be cleaned up. Preserve the separate legacy compile connection. The raw channel is implemented at 92d607a, private verified-byte factory at 091a893, controller foundation at 52935a5, and production ConnectedAdapter integration at 269ffb6. The actual ConnectedAdapter now binds source/target revisions and the private download registry to the selected exact profile. Context reconciliation, cleanup and invalidation have production tests and actual Chromium evidence; complete independent client-role MCK and Proton save-dialog qualification remain pending.

Keep previews separate from download bytes. Validate strict UTF-8 over the full file, then display only a bounded text prefix at Unicode boundaries; bound aggregate preview work across the inventory. A bounded preview is not permission to skip validation of the undisplayed suffix. The generated-files tree and source view can continue to show text, binary summaries and Ion inspection. The existing editor and export components remain their respective owners. Route downloads through the verified byte set, including ZIP creation, instead of converting a new transfer back to an ambiguous content/binary/encoding flag combination. Adapt the existing trusted local-worker envelope into the same domain at its boundary.

On a host without the exact offer, use current v1 text behavior and retain current undeclared-binary refusal. On a selected profile, reject malformed manifests or chunks and release the transfer; never salvage a string as presumed base64. Preserve compile/inspection results when artifact generation or transfer fails, with a distinct generation/transfer diagnostic.

Coordinate reusable profile schemas, capability selection and shared fixtures with morphir-ui/packages/morphir-workspace. Add a separate exported artifact-transfer module and tests; preserve the existing v1 schemas and the vendored bundle's version literal. Current supports() checks version 1; the new exact SemVer profile needs separate validated selection. Existing upstream UI consumers may continue using v1 until they explicitly select the new module. Prove that old clients ignore the new capability and still decode the old reply shape. Land shared TypeScript decoding upstream and update the parent coordinated gitlink. The MoonBit repository has no existing UI gitlink or package dependency: consume a real tracked, pinned package/submodule or hash-checked upstream source closure with its license/provenance, never an ignored workspace import. A future coordination note does not complete this requirement.

For Proton, reuse the existing authenticated connected launch and main-window Blob save-dialog policy. Do not introduce a generic native file-writing command. Test actual bytes saved through that dialog. A rendered preview or a triggered click is weaker evidence than a saved-file comparison.

Actual Chromium saved-byte evidence

The maintained mise test:workbench-artifacts workflow passes through a real Gleam frontend, installed SDK process, authenticated parent host and production Workbench UI, then compares actual saved files and ZIP entries. Three Chromium 156.0.8078.4 reports pass. Each records exactly one SDK fixture invocation, exact compiled IR, zero legacy generation fallback, source-edit stale-download refusal and a subsequent real Gleam backend probe. No intercepted route or browser-only mock supplies artifact replies.

Mixed downloadThree files: 23-byte original BOM/CRLF text, 1,048,833-byte indexed binary and empty binary, plus their project ZIP. Original file hashes and ZIP entry bytes agree with independent expectations.Actual download report. Independent qualification

The parent repository owns the exact artifact profile, schemas, immutable cases, expected digests and shared Rust MCK implementation. Add distinct production server and client observations to the one morphir mck workbench runner. Publish independently scoped server and client kits: a one-sided adapter can qualify its matching kit, while a full transfer claim requires both. Unsupported observations never count as qualification. Independent report checking recomputes fixed comparisons; it must not link the Workbench client decoder or derive expectations from a producer reply.

EvidenceRequired cases
Producer contractRust SDK artifact conversion with real standard-base64 bytes, UTF-8 text and a binary payload covering all 256 byte values, NUL and invalid UTF-8 sequences. Test canonical base64 rejection and retain original text BOM/CRLF. Existing WASM codegen tests prove its encoder separately.
Actual Rust host laneA Rust qualification fixture backend runs through the actual registry, selected invoker, NativePlaygroundProvider and authenticated loopback host. It advertises an explicit compatible fixture target/IR version and produces fixed binary/text artifacts. This qualifies transfer behavior, not a newly supported production language backend. Include a current real Rust text-producing backend workflow too.
Large transferFreeze byte fixtures or immutable generation recipes with literal independently authored expected SHA-256 values. Cover empty, 65,535, 65,536, 65,537, 131,073 and greater-than-1-MiB artifacts, multiple mixed files, exact 16 MiB per-file and 64 MiB aggregate bounds, and one-over-limit refusal. Verify final bytes and ZIP entries against the immutable source, never against a digest copied from the received manifest alone.
NegotiationAbsent, unavailable, wrong-version and wrong-provider offers; exact selection; legacy client/new host and new client/legacy host; unknown fields and duplicate members; no auto-downgrade after a selected transfer fails.
Server authority and lifecycleWrong cookie, Origin, Host or session; uninitialized connection; stolen handle on another connection; wrong generation/artifact; release twice; read after release; connection close; generation/byte capacity; unavailable provider; lost reply. Assert actual retained-byte reservations and cleanup.
Client reconciliationCapture before await; wrong profile/context/producer; unsafe and colliding paths; malformed base64, dishonest lengths, altered digest, skipped/overlapping/wrong-offset chunks, stale reply after replacement and cancellation. Reject before Blob/ZIP creation. Exercise real release behavior.
Rust → TypeScript → browserUse the real authenticated Rust host and actual production TypeScript transport. No JavaScript route interception substitutes artifact replies. Download single binary and project ZIP in Chromium, compare saved bytes/entries to frozen bytes, and verify text preview versus exact original download bytes.
Rust → TypeScript → packaged ProtonLaunch the packaged app against the same actual host. Complete real OS save dialogs and compare files and ZIP entries. Record executable hash, OS/architecture, source revisions, selected profile and producer. A CDP download event without a saved file is insufficient.
Independent tampering checksMutate saved observations in byte payload, offset, path, digest, offer, result identity or release effect. The final parent runner's report-check command rejects each forged report independently.

Design large-case evidence before freezing the corpus. The existing runner bounds the corpus at 16 MiB, aggregate observation values at 16 MiB and the report at 32 MiB. Existing observation projections also have their selected draft's individual bounds. Full base64 of a 16 MiB file cannot be one observation. Use bounded, closed byte recipes, literal independent hashes and bounded chunk evidence; validate the recipe and aggregate work budget before expansion. Keep requests/reports within the selected exact draft's limits and reject forged recipe, length, offset, digest or release evidence in saved-report checks. Add this support to the existing runner rather than a second checker or a global budget increase. Actual saved-file verification still reads and compares the complete bytes independently.

The fixture backend must be a real Rust producer using the production SDK contract and invocation path. It is a qualification fixture, not a fake fetch response and not an extra production dropdown target. If a supported production binary backend is available, qualify it additionally using its actual supported IR input. Do not infer that support from the legacy WASM fixture.

Required landing evidence includes parent schema/MCK gates, Rust tests and lint, Workbench typecheck/tests and required checks, upstream TypeScript package tests, exact source revisions, independent report rechecks and actual browser/Proton saved-byte receipts.

New parent spec/workbench/artifacts/0.1.0-draft.1/ and next fixed shared MCK draft, currently 28 after settled worksheet 27. Add an additive typed provider method that retains resolved producer provenance and the SDK result; make old generation project its frozen reply from that same invocation helper. Other provider implementations default to unavailable and must not advertise the new offer. Do not re-invoke generation just to obtain bytes. Add a typed artifact domain/store and SDK conversion under crates/morphir/src/commands/ui/; extend protocol.rs, rpc.rs, provider capability wiring and the existing provider invocation path without changing legacy response serialization. Add actual Rust producer/server adapters and independent shared-MCK parsing/report checks. Reuse distribution digest/path types. No SDK schema bump is needed because its documented base64 representation already exists.

Task 2: clients and downloads

Workbench browser/contracts.ts, transport.ts, a focused artifact-transfer domain module and tests, artifact-download.ts and tests, generated-files component, UI request/result transitions and browser workflows. Add exact profile schemas/selection to upstream morphir-ui/packages/morphir-workspace/src/artifact-transfer.ts, exports and compatibility tests using the same published fixtures. Preserve v1 and existing local binary import/export behavior.

Task 3: runtime qualification and coordinated landing

Run actual Rust producer/server, TypeScript client, Chromium and packaged Proton lanes. Independently recheck their shared-MCK reports and compare saved bytes. Run required gates in each changed repository, address review findings, land the coordinated parent/Workbench/upstream-TypeScript changes and record merged revisions. Update campaign checkboxes from observed evidence. No publication or durable recovery work belongs in this slice.

The SDK-process/authenticated-host/production-UI vertical proof passes in three actual Chromium runs, including mixed files, greater than 1 MiB indexed binary, exact 64 MiB aggregate binary and NUL text, individual saves and project ZIPs, fixed expected bytes, one invocation and stale download refusal. Every run also probes the subsequent real Gleam backend. The shared MCK now qualifies 102 independent client cases in Bun, Node and Chromium, including hostile frames and authority/lifecycle/capacity boundaries. Packaged Proton OS saves, final pins, final-source rechecks and coordinated client landing remain required before completing the epic.
