Contract decision

The implemented parent contribution defines morphir/workbench/worksheet, exact version 0.1.0-draft.1, and independent shared-MCK draft 27 after the merged codec draft 26. The parent profile landed through #1068 at 8b9e44fd, whose whole tree equals qualified 60f2b265. Workbench #146 and its final automatic CI are complete; functional merged-checkout verification is complete. The canonical HTML store, database sync and final tracker closure are complete. The coordinator’s final readable-mirror publication is in flight and is not yet verified. The profile describes bounded local Scheme worksheet evaluation. It does not add a remote RPC method.

The request captures a logical source identity, revision and exact source text before asynchronous work starts. A report returns that capture and ordered, located observations. Each row uses the existing execution.TerminalOutcome. Its returned payload is the existing execution.Value. A separate completion outcome describes whether the evaluator reached the end of the worksheet.

"Typed" means a validated tagged execution value. It does not claim static Scheme type inference or Morphir IR lowering. A formatted preview is presentation evidence only and cannot establish a returned value.

Ownership and flow

Mermaid source
flowchart TD
  UI[Capture source ID, revision, exact text] --> Adapter[Own worker, deadline and cancellation]
  Adapter --> Pipeline[Production worksheet pipeline]
  Pipeline --> Reader[Parse ranged forms before evaluation]
  Reader --> Eval[Evaluate ordered forms in one fresh runtime]
  Eval --> Project[Project to execution.Value and TerminalOutcome]
  Project --> Validate[Validate report against captured request]
  Validate --> Current{Capture still current?}
  Current -->|yes| Marks[Render rows and reveal exact ranges]
  Current -->|no| History[Retain earlier-revision output without current marks]

The parser, source validation, coordinate conversion, value projection and report reconciliation belong in the functional core. Worker creation, timeout, termination and editor effects remain in adapters. An observed capability does not grant host execution authority.

Source identity and ranges

The implementation uses validated WorksheetId, SourceRevision, FormId, Utf16Offset and Utf16Range wrappers with private representations and smart constructors. CapturedWorksheetSource wraps engine/data.SourceSnapshot; its constructor accepts only text content and a validated logical ID. The source ID is not a filesystem path and creates no file access permission.

RuleRequired behavior
CaptureFreeze {id, revision, text} before posting to a worker. ID is nonempty, at most 128 UTF-16 units and excludes control characters. Revision is an integer from 0 through 2,147,483,647. Reject ill-formed UTF-16 input before the scalar reader; do not replace unmatched surrogates silently. Exact text is at most 262,144 UTF-16 units and 1 MiB of encoded UTF-8.
Revision lifetimeEvery edit changes the revision. Restoring text also changes it. If the counter reaches its bound, allocate a new source identity before revision zero. A response must match ID, revision and text, not revision alone.
RangesUse zero-based UTF-16 half-open [start,end) offsets over the captured text. Form ranges are nonempty, ordered, nonoverlapping and within the source. Ranges exclude surrounding trivia and retain original spelling.
UnicodeRanges never split a valid surrogate pair. Convert parser scalar indexes with a prefix table once per source. Do not infer an end from pretty-print length or the next form's start.
NewlinesCapture CRLF unchanged. A CRLF occupies two UTF-16 units. The protocol's authoritative coordinates are offsets; editor boundary maps captured CRLF offsets to CodeMirror's normalized document explicitly, or captures the normalized editor value before the run. Do not apply raw CRLF offsets directly to a normalized LF document.
Form identityGenerate form-0, form-1, and so on within a single capture. A FormId is meaningful only with its capture. Reject duplicated or reordered form identities.
Diagnostic positionA diagnostic may use a zero-width range, including EOF. A runtime diagnostic identifies the whole top-level form. Do not claim nested runtime location precision that the evaluator does not provide.
BudgetsAt most 1,000 forms, value depth 64 and 100,000 value nodes; keep the existing bounded Scheme runtime limits. The complete encoded request and report each fit 2 MiB. Bound diagnostics to 512 UTF-16 units and display previews to 4,000. Reserve a source-captured failure envelope before evaluation; if it cannot fit, reject before starting the runtime. Account encoded row bytes incrementally and stop with worksheet.output_limit before the reply limit is exceeded.

Implemented parse_program_ranged shares the existing Reader. It records each top-level start after skip and end immediately after read. parse_program, Located and parse_program_located remain source-compatible. The worksheet needs exact top-level form ranges; extending all nested AST nodes is unnecessary for this slice.

Domain types and wire example

The following excerpt reflects implemented private domain relationships; helper definitions are omitted. Constructors validate against the capture, and external callers cannot construct raw identities, revisions or offsets.

pub struct CapturedWorksheetSource {
  priv snapshot : @data.SourceSnapshot
  priv revision : SourceRevision
}
pub struct Observation {
  priv form : WorksheetForm
  priv preview : String
  priv outcome : @execution.TerminalOutcome
}
pub struct WorksheetReport {
  priv source : CapturedWorksheetSource
  priv observations : Array[Observation]
  priv completion : @execution.TerminalOutcome
  priv diagnostic : WorksheetDiagnostic?
}
// WorksheetForm retains its validated FormId, range, exact expression and datum.
// Existing execution terminal/value helpers remain authoritative.

Completion accepts only Returned(Unit), Failed(...) or Cancelled. Its returned unit means the evaluator reached the end, even if one row could not produce a portable value. It does not assert that every row succeeded. Row and completion failure consistency is validated by the profile.

The exact request is {profile, contractVersion, source}. The private worker boundary uses the existing WorkRequest envelope with operation:"worksheet" and canonical serialized worksheetRequest. Its compatibility source field must equal the captured source; the production pipeline rejects a mismatch before evaluation. That field grants no independent source authority. The result carries canonical serialized worksheetReport, which the client validates through the production core before UI adoption.

{
  "profile": "morphir/workbench/worksheet",
  "contractVersion": "0.1.0-draft.1",
  "source": {"id": "worksheet-source", "revision": 4, "text": "(+ 1 2)"},
  "observations": [{
    "id": "form-0", "range": {"start": 0, "end": 7},
    "expression": "(+ 1 2)", "preview": "3",
    "outcome": {"status": "returned", "value": {"type": "int", "value": "3"}}
  }],
  "completion": {"status": "returned", "value": {"type": "unit"}},
  "diagnostic": null
}

The example uses the existing value encoding from pkgs/morphir-execution/rich_values.mbt:271. The existing execution codec remains authoritative for terminal and value payloads. Both request and report reject duplicate or unknown fields and accept only the named exact profile/version. A present malformed typed report is rejected without falling back to legacy success or value strings.

The implemented WorksheetDiagnostic holds a validated range and closed Read | Evaluate | Project | Transport stage. Failure details stay in the existing terminal payload; row and completion failures must agree where the profile requires it. execution/diagnostics.Warning remains a separate recoverable-warning contract with producer-specific line/column coordinates.

Scheme value projection

The projection inspects runtime variants. It never parses value_to_string. Preserve exact arithmetic, UTF-16 text, negative zero and runtime data structure meaning. The Scheme preview remains available beside typed details. An unavailable projection is labelled "Typed value unavailable"; it does not turn the Scheme evaluation itself into a runtime failure.

Scheme runtime valueExisting execution value
Integer, boolean, text, character, unitInteger, Boolean, Text, Character, Unit. Text and character payloads use the existing UTF-16-unit representation.
Finite inexact realFloat64 with exact binary bits. Do not convert through a JSON number.
Exact rationalTyped projection unavailable in this exact profile. Keep the Scheme preview and worksheet.value_unsupported projection diagnostic. Whole numbers already normalized by the runtime remain Integer. Never round a nonintegral rational to Float64 or relabel it as Decimal.
SymbolTyped projection unavailable; preserve its Scheme preview and projection diagnostic. Do not misreport 'hello as the text "hello".
Nil and proper listSequence, including an empty list. Values may be heterogeneous because this is dynamic observation, not a declared homogeneous Morphir parameter type.
Dotted pairTyped projection unavailable; retain the Scheme preview and projection diagnostic. Do not relabel an improper pair as a proper list or vector.
Vector and runtime recordProduct and Record. Order record fields canonically for reproducible observation. Do not make a vector indistinguishable from a Scheme list.
Closure, native procedure, native function, IR wrappers, unknown tagged valueFailed with stable worksheet.value_unsupported. Keep the bounded Scheme preview. No fabricated text value, guessed custom owner, or closure serialization.

This profile adds no execution.Value variant, Scheme custom owner, or extension to frozen morphir-invocations-v1 and terminal-outcome contracts. Reuse existing value decoding and budgets. If any nested child cannot be projected faithfully, the whole row has an unavailable typed projection; do not insert placeholder values. A future fully typed Scheme data profile requires its own exact version and independent cases. Implement worksheet-specific projection in the worksheet domain package; the existing IR-evaluation scheme_output(value, expected, definitions) is private and requires a declared output type, so it is not a dynamic worksheet decoder.

Failures and cancellation

EventRequired report
Empty or comments-only sourceZero observations, completion Returned(Unit). No invented call and no use of the nonempty Outcomes envelope.
Read/syntax failureParse the whole source before evaluating any form. Zero observations, completion Failed, source-mapped read diagnostic. Do not execute a valid prefix.
Successful formOne located observation with Returned(Value). A definition normally returns Unit. Preserve bindings for subsequent forms.
Runtime failureKeep completed preceding rows. Append the failing row with Failed, then stop; completion carries the same failure. Attach its top-level form range.
Projection failureAppend a row with Failed and its original preview. Evaluation itself succeeded, so continue later forms in the same runtime. Completion is Returned(Unit) if the loop reaches the end; overall UI success is false when any row failed.
Model errorUse ModelError only for an actual recognized existing Morphir model-error value. Ordinary Scheme errors use Failed. Do not infer model errors from display strings.
Local cancellationThe adapter terminates its owned worker and returns a validated report for its captured source with completion Cancelled. Without streaming, no partial rows are claimed. This records termination of owned work, not proof that no form ran.
Timeout or worker crashA transport diagnostic and completion Failed with a distinct code. A timeout is not user cancellation. Keep no invented value or unobserved partial rows.
Late or mismatched replyCheck request ID and captured source identity/revision/text. Settle the operation once. Reject forged captures, invalid ranges, wrong expression slices, incompatible profile versions and malformed terminal payloads.

Each explicit run starts a fresh runtime. No durable worksheet session, worker restart recovery or generated-backend execution is part of this profile.

Editor and result presentation

The implemented UI keeps the expression/result rows, derives each expression from its exact source slice, retains the Scheme preview, and adds a compact typed-details disclosure. A row activation reveals its range only when its full capture still matches the current editor document. Use a button with an intention-revealing accessible label such as "Show expression in source".

Source-mapped diagnostics use the existing Problems area and editor. Earlier-revision results retain their captured expression and revision label; the implementation disables reveal and marks on unrelated current text. Source previews and diagnostics remain text, never HTML.

The editor component remains the only CodeMirror owner. Validated range reveal and marks enter through that component boundary. The existing line/column marks helper clamps coordinates, which is useful for presentation but cannot validate protocol evidence. Validate evidence before presentation; do not silently clamp an invalid report into acceptance.

Connected protocol v1 continues to run Scheme worksheets through the local worker. Browser and packaged Proton share the same profile and core. Their independent runtime probes must establish both paths; neither a screenshot nor an MCK-only adapter proves that the shipped UI uses the new report.

Lossless codec qualification

The shared Rust runner owns fixed inputs and expected semantic projections. An explicit MoonBit adapter decodes a captured source, encodes the admitted invocation suite into the requested destination format, and decodes those actual output bytes. Added requirement: headless CLI parity

Maintainer scope addition · 18 October 2026 · Full plan: morphir-etg2.23 design, Revision 2

The expanded campaign must also expose function evaluation, both existing capability checking policies, source-mapped Scheme worksheets and applicable model/artifact workflows through the primary MoonBit CLI without a browser, CEF or a running Workbench. Local operations do not require a daemon; connected operations select an exact compatible provider and maintain existing authority and lifecycle semantics. This is a new explicit completion requirement, not a claim about the original historical acceptance.

CLI and Workbench adapters share typed application/domain services and narrow effect interfaces. Reuse existing execution/evaluator providers, codecs, ownership, transfer validation and artifact writers; keep presentation, parsing, transport and filesystem authority at adapters. The standalone Workbench and headless CLI must accept YAML through the existing normative profile with bounded parsing/assembly, exact values, supported version/layout normalization and original-byte preservation. Reuse and coordinate .22.1's bounded YAML reader and typed conversion; physical parsing progress alone is not end-to-end support.

design:
Build and run a complete generated library

morphir-ukvn.5.55.7.1 · 18 October 2026 · implementation specification 0.3

Outcome and first delivery

Turn a supported Morphir model into generated MoonBit, compile its complete library graph with the packaged compiler, persist a Wasm artifact and an Ion manifest, then invoke the saved artifact in a fresh compatible host. MoonBit source can enter after generation. The deployed artifact does not carry the compiler unless its actual operation requires compilation.

This implements the next delivery recommended by the hosting study, revision 0.8 in morphir-ukvn.5.55.7. The initial deliverable starts with explicitly supplied dependencies. Registry/package-manager resolution and compilation are different components. A complete graph must include all supplied modules and every referenced transitive library, including matching MoonBit core and Morphir SDK assets.

The planner, asynchronous executor and binary Ion publisher/loader are implemented and landed. A production-generated library with its complete supplied SDK/core graph passes persisted-artifact invocation in fresh Node processes. All three delivery PRs are squash merged, with successful exact-head CI evidence. Native Wasmoon callback/resource gaps remain separate from this JavaScript compiler/core-Wasm path.

Implemented components and qualification

Each component has an independent boundary. The MoonBit planner decides graph order; the host adapter verifies assets and performs asynchronous compiler requests; the publisher and loader own persistence and runtime compatibility checks.

ComponentImplementationLanding state
Planner and compiler executorassembly/plan.mbt and embedding/assembly.mts; separate build and link provider operations.PR #141 landed as 6b24f71. All exact-head CI gates ultimately passed.
Ion artifact publisher and loaderembedding/artifacts.mts, embedding/node-artifacts.mts and the MoonBit Ion bridge. Draft manifest, atomic staged publication and checks before instantiation.PR #142 landed as 09faf7a after green CI and addressed review findings.
Generated-library qualificationassembly/qualification, embedding/test/generated.mts and scripts/assembly-check.mbtx.PR #144 landed as 0ee036c after all 54 check contexts passed or were intentionally skipped, with no review findings.

Paths above are beneath pkgs/morphir-host/ except the task script. The test uses a real three-module Morphir model with a cross-module reference and an SDK addition call. It supplies every selected source file from the SDK root, integer, list and basics packages, plus their 38-package pinned core closure. All 44 supplied packages remain recorded in the artifact manifest after linking.

Source build and linkerWasm bytesResultsInitialization
Optimized17,282answer = 42; cross-module result 40; boolean true.Exactly once.
Unoptimized18,476The same results in a separate fresh process.Exactly once.

Both runs use compiler 0.10.15+943464bfa, identical source/model/package identities and the same already optimized prebuilt core bytes. Each prebuilt package records its own setting; the selected assembly setting controls source compilation and final linking. Both modes remove the deliberately unreachable payload. These measurements do not imply that noOpt disables all linker elimination.

Reproduce and interpret the evidence 
mise run test:assembly
Model SHA-256:
4811cdf72e7e659b6e9e92d9cca2cc79c4f9df5ea390e08a4fd62d4bd030265e

Preparation invokes Moon to generate the fixture and obtain official dry-run SDK recipes and the pinned core graph. It never executes the compiler commands printed by those recipes. Actual package compilation uses the packaged provider with an empty PATH and no MOON_HOME. A separate process then reads only the saved Wasm/manifest pair and declared host services. Successful temporary publications are removed after independent consumption; failed workspaces are retained at the printed path.

The fixture also refuses a missing SDK package and corrupted core bytes, checks retained exports and initialization, and verifies absence of the unreachable payload. The complete embedding suite has 24 tests, including npm installation followed by compiler-payload deletion before a fresh loader runs. Chromium separately qualifies dependency assembly and binary Ion loading. The full generated SDK/core fixture is qualified in Node; it does not establish native compiler hosting, Component Model, production CLI or shared MEP/MCK integration.

Model bytes and persisted manifests use binary Ion. The dry-run/generation boundary and diagnostic report .dev/assembly-qualification-report.json are explicit JSON test boundaries. The local artifact schema remains draft and does not stabilize draft Morphir IR 4.0.0.

Call sequence

The coordinator owns effects; the planner returns a decision. The compiler owns package compilation and linking. A fresh consumer validates saved bytes and host compatibility before invoking them.

Mermaid source
sequenceDiagram
  participant C as Coordinator
  participant P as Pure planner
  participant T as Compiler provider
  participant S as Artifact store
  participant H as Fresh host
  C->>P: Supplied packages and exact dependency pins
  P-->>C: Ordered graph or refusal
  loop Dependency order
    C->>T: Source plus direct/indirect/standard interfaces
    T-->>C: Diagnostics, interface and compiled core
  end
  C->>T: Link all cores with explicit retention roots
  T-->>C: Wasm and actual import requirements
  C->>S: Publish Wasm plus Ion manifest
  C->>H: Invoke saved reference
  H->>S: Read and verify manifest and artifact
  H-->>C: Result or actionable diagnostic

Component responsibilities

ComponentOwnsBoundary
Existing engine/backendMorphirModel validation, supported lowering, generated sources, module symbols and provenance.Does not become a filesystem or asynchronous compiler host.
Dependency providerAcquisition and exact source/prebuilt inputs, compiler/core/SDK identities.First delivery accepts supplied inputs; registry semantics remain outside the planner.
Pure MoonBit plannerPin matching, import aliases, complete graph validation, cycle diagnostics and deterministic dependency order.No compiler, process, filesystem or network effects. A content pin is an identity assertion until the host verifies actual bytes.
Compiler adapterBuild packages with matching interfaces, link required cores once, propagate diagnostics and cancellation.Reuse the asynchronous embedded provider. Cross the synchronous engine boundary explicitly.
Artifact publisher/loaderIon encoding, durable bytes, integrity and compatibility checks, failure cleanup.Artifact bytes and a completed manifest become visible together. Explicit JSON remains a supported boundary choice.
Host adapterSelected ABI, Wasm features/imports, invocation and lifecycle.Scope evidence separately to Node, browser/Workbench and native hosts.

Complete assembly graph

The planner consumes a supplied assembly set, not an unrestricted registry inventory. Every supplied package participates in validation and ordering, even when later linking can remove its unused code. The selected root must exist at the exact requested pin. Import aliases belong to the referring package and can differ across packages without changing dependency identity.

generated model package ──> application library ──> referenced library
         │                           │                      │
         └──────────────> shared SDK/core assets <───────────┘

Package pin = canonical MoonBit package path + SHA-256 content identity
Dependency  = local import alias + exact package pin
Plan        = selected root + every supplied package in dependency order

Reject malformed package names/digests/aliases, duplicate package identities, duplicate aliases, missing dependencies, incompatible pins and cycles. Diagnostics identify the referring package and requested dependency; cycle diagnostics retain the cycle path. Shared dependencies appear once. Input ordering must not affect output ordering. Use an iterative traversal so a long valid graph does not depend on the host call stack.

Content pins do not prove authorship or authorize execution. Source/compiled assets are checked against their actual bytes by the provider. The executor checks compiler/core/target compatibility and supplies direct, indirect and standard interfaces. A broken unused package is refused before final linking.

Model and artifact states

MorphirModel remains the semantic pipeline value. Generation preserves its model revision, metadata, naming facts and numeric provenance. Assembly planning is a separate build value; successful planning grants no new model guarantee.

// Conceptual stage boundaries, not a new wire format.
SuppliedAssembly -> Plan
Plan + verified assets -> CompiledAssembly
CompiledAssembly -> PublishedArtifact
PublishedArtifact + compatible host -> InvocationOutcome

Use closed enums and opaque validated values for these states. A published manifest must never describe a partially built artifact as complete. Cancellation or a failed package stops downstream linking/publication; retain useful diagnostics without returning a success artifact. A native ABI, a component ABI and the current core-Wasm API have distinct qualified bindings.

Known libraries and host interfaces

An execution profile is the proposed versioned contract pairing guest base-library requirements with a host interface, ABI, codecs and Wasm features. It is independent of the source language. MoonBit stays the language; compiler packaging and host implementation stay separately identifiable.

Start with one small real consumer and bundled libraries. Record contract identity separately from concrete library/compiler/core hashes. A second profile adds one concrete host service, such as diagnostics, to prove variation and refusal of unsupported requirements. Do not create an arbitrary matrix of independent feature flags or assume that all hosts implement every profile.

Ion artifact manifest

Ion is the default pipeline/intermediate encoding. Use the repository's pinned Ion codecs; retain annotations, exact integers and binary values. A checked JSON representation is an explicit boundary option. The manifest schema is local and draft until shared contract review establishes a public format.

GroupRequired information
IdentityManifest schema/revision, artifact hash/size, source MorphirModel revision and generated source identities.
AssemblyFull supplied/resolved graph, exact pins, local aliases, package order, compiler/core/SDK identities and source or prebuilt form.
InvocationSelected exports and ABI, actual imports, required Wasm features, execution-profile contract and encoding requirements.
OptimizationActual compiler/linker settings, retention roots and measured output size. Preserve original graph identity after code elimination.
QualificationOptional scoped evidence references. Packaging alone does not certify semantics, MEP/MCK conformance, sandboxing or publisher identity.

A loader verifies artifact integrity and explicit compatibility before invoking it. It must not discover compatibility by executing unvalidated code. A fresh-host test reads only the published artifact, manifest and declared host services; it must not depend on hidden build-process state or installed compiler commands.

Linking and tree shaking

Resolve and validate the whole supplied graph first. Link each required compiled core once. Derive retention roots from selected public exports, required initialization and declared indirect registrations. Dynamic discovery requires explicit roots or a conservative fallback.

Qualify the pinned compiler/linker's existing elimination before adding another shaker. Compare supported optimization settings using the same model, dependency graph and invocation. Check equal results, retained exports and initialization, and a deliberately unreachable fixture. Measure sizes without promising a percentage or assuming a no-optimization flag disables every linker elimination pass.

MEP and MCK fit

The first planner introduces no MEP schema or transport change. Existing compile/generate/model semantics remain authoritative. A later adapter must explicitly negotiate its artifact/host binding; core-Wasm loading does not establish Component Model support.

An MCK adapter can package production libraries against a known profile and use an executable bridge behind the existing process boundary. Preserve exact envelopes, correlation, session limits, independent kit selection and runner-owned verdicts/reports. Direct Wasm loading in the shared runner remains separate upstream work. A codec-adapter tracer and a generated-model tracer can reuse the same assembly/publishing/loader components.

Implementation and evidence

Task 1: Pure assembly planner

Add pkgs/morphir-host/assembly with immutable validated pins, dependency aliases and an opaque plan. Test dependency order, diamond sharing, input permutations, missing/mismatched dependencies, duplicates, cycles, invalid inputs, mutation isolation and a deep graph. No new host capability is advertised.

Task 2: Execute the planned package graph

After Task 1, supply source/prebuilt assets to the existing compiler adapter, validate compiler/core/target identity, compile in order and link once with explicit roots. Test a real transitive graph, aliasing, cancellation and compiler diagnostics. Keep acquisition pluggable.

Task 3: Publish and load Ion artifact records

After Task 1, implement draft typed manifest codecs and publication/load adapters. This can run alongside Task 2. Test annotation/binary/exact-value preservation, integrity/compatibility refusal, partial-write cleanup and fresh-host invocation.

Task 4: Qualify the real generated-library path

After Tasks 2 and 3, generate a supported multi-module Morphir library with an external reference, transitive dependency and real shared SDK assets. Compile without spawning the installed compiler, persist artifacts and consume them in fresh hosts. Qualify optimization equivalence, retention and missing/incompatible-library diagnostics. Record what is still outside the production CLI.

Follow-on work selects the smallest real execution profile, proves a second host and profile variation, and packages a production MCK codec adapter. Registry resolution, shared runtime providers, native Wasm compiler hosting, Extism and native Component Model facade fixes can advance separately. They are not invented prerequisites for Tasks 1–4.

Existing evidence

  • morphir-ukvn.5.55.7, research revision 0.8, owns the full host/package study and six diagrams.
  • pkgs/morphir-host/embedding/api.mts defines compile requests with direct/indirect/standard interfaces and linked cores.
  • pkgs/morphir-host/embedding/index.mts owns serialized compiler requests, linking and core-Wasm execution.
  • pkgs/morphir-host/embedding/test/toolchain.test.mts already proves in-process/worker compilation and explicit dependency linking.
  • pkgs/morphir-moonbit/README.md defines generated-library artifacts and their semantic dependency requirements.
  • tests/wasm-host/README.md distinguishes qualified Node/Chromium component fixtures from native facade gaps and production integration.

Original design baseline: 6e80df8c379aaff21c847fce03b8d3899b2de45e. Revision 0.3 records the landed delivery and independently measured qualification above. The broader execution-profile, component-hosting and MEP/MCK proposals remain distinct from the supplied-graph/core-Wasm path.

title: Reduce redundant CI work while preserving platform and release coverage
description:
## Current status and delivered work

Status reconciled on 17 October 2026. Existing parallelism and focused/full workflow separation are the starting point for this epic, not new implementation work. PR #100 is superseded by merged PR #125; do not restore its duplicate top-level generated-qualification jobs or older bootstrap. The suites compile their own inputs and do not require native CLI artifacts.

| Work | Current status | Record |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Compiler/frontend parallelism | Delivered through PR #125. PR #100 is closed as superseded, without merging. | morphir-ukvn.5.31, closed; PR #125, c42351e |
| Focused checks and separate full qualification | Delivered through PR #125. This epic refines the existing dependency selection and qualification triggers. | morphir-ukvn.5.58, closed |
| Complete Unix MoonBit setup and ARM64 install qualification | Delivered through PR #129; retain fresh-install platform coverage when setup changes. | morphir-ukvn.5.61, closed |
| Linux-only static TypeScript checks | Implemented locally and validated; not yet committed or landed. | morphir-ukvn.5.63, in progress |
| Further CI optimization | Proposed and open: measurement, duplicate validation/setup, narrower selection, safe caching and verified artifact reuse. | morphir-ukvn.5.65; GitHub #131 |

## Problem statement

CI in finos/morphir-moonbit repeats static validation, dependency setup and builds, and selects expensive qualification more broadly than the changed components require. Contributors wait longer for useful feedback and the project consumes unnecessary runner time, including macOS capacity.

In successful run 39065090591 on 17 October 2026, checks spanned approximately 23 minutes from the first job starting to ci-ok completing. Installed lifecycle took about 13 minutes on Linux and 17 minutes on macOS; signed-provider acceptance took about 13 and 14 minutes respectively. These are single-run elapsed job durations, not billed minutes or a representative statistical baseline. The repeated TypeScript checks took 12 seconds on Linux, 17 seconds on macOS and 45 seconds on Windows. The long qualification jobs, repeated prerequisites and broad selection therefore deserve attention beyond removing the TypeScript OS matrix.

Evidence: https://github.com/finos/morphir-moonbit/actions/runs/39065090591

## Outcome

Reduce CI runner consumption and time to actionable feedback while preserving platform-specific behavior checks, supported compiler/backend coverage, exact-candidate release qualification and fail-closed aggregate gates.

## High-level proposed solutions

| Solution | Proposed change | Coverage and safety requirements |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Measure first | Record queue and execution time, critical path, runner minutes by OS, cache hits, and setup/build/test costs for comparable focused and full runs. | Separate elapsed time from billing; compare like workloads and cache states. Set targets from the baseline. |
| Remove duplicate static work | Finish Linux-only TypeScript checks (morphir-ukvn.5.63) and run YAML lint once instead of in both Lint and Validate Configuration Files. | Keep checked-build rejection tests and package validation. Follow the MoonBit migration policy when changing legacy task wrappers. |
| Separate setup from compilation | Let static-only jobs install pinned tools and frozen dependencies without generating runtime JavaScript. Evaluate same-run reuse for runtime consumers. | Build runtime JavaScript where consumers need it; keep dependency versions pinned. |
| Refine component selection | Extend scripts/ci-changes.mbtx so isolated changes avoid unrelated embedding/browser, Elm/Scheme, site and acceptance work. | Test direct/transitive dependencies, renames and shared inputs. Unknown or ambiguous paths retain conservative coverage. |
| Refine full-qualification triggers | Distinguish workflow wiring changes from compiler, dependency, platform-setup and shared CI-policy changes; exercise affected workflows and gates. | Retain full toolchain/policy checks until a tested narrower mapping is justified. Preserve scheduled full runs and exact-candidate release qualification. |
| Cache reproducible downloads | Evaluate Bun and Mooncakes registry/package downloads first, with keys covering relevant OS/architecture, toolchain and lockfile/dependency identities. | Keep cache misses and stale caches safe. Do not cache trust decisions, signing state, mutable fixtures or acceptance receipts. |
| Reuse verified build outputs | Audit repeated JavaScript/native compilation and extend same-run artifact reuse where measurements show a benefit. | Verify source, target, compiler and dependency identities. Keep distinct backend, fresh-install and debug/release coverage. |

## Delivery approach

Start with measurement and duplicate static/setup work, then improve selection rules, then introduce caches and artifact reuse only where the measurements support them. Deliver reviewable slices with before/after evidence and an explicit coverage comparison. This epic is a proposal for implementation; it does not authorize removing acceptance criteria or bypassing required checks.

## Acceptance criteria

- Baseline and after-change measurements are recorded for comparable focused and full workflows, with queue time and execution time distinguished. Target reductions are selected from that baseline rather than invented in advance.
- TypeScript static checking runs once; runtime OS matrices and Wasm, Wasm GC, JavaScript and native behavior coverage remain where required.
- YAML lint and other identified static checks run once per relevant workflow path; static-only jobs avoid unnecessary runtime compilation.
- Selection changes have positive and negative tests, including transitive/shared dependencies and conservative unknown-path behavior. Selected failures or cancellations cannot produce a green aggregate gate.
- Scheduled full qualification and exact-candidate release qualification remain available and required at the appropriate boundaries.
- Cache misses and invalid artifacts exercise safe fallbacks; stale, incompatible or untrusted state cannot satisfy qualification.
- Each optimization records its retained coverage and measured impact. Material regressions have a documented rollback path.

## Scope and non-goals

Scope: .github/workflows/, .github/actions/, scripts/ci-changes.mbtx, scripts/ci-gate.mbtx, related portable task scripts and CI documentation. Do not remove process-supervision OS matrices, collapse distinct MoonBit backend behavior tests, weaken signed-provider/artifact admission, change release policy or alter repository protection settings as an incidental optimization. Cost estimates and percentage reduction targets remain open until baseline data is collected.

## Related work

- `morphir-ukvn.5.31`: completed through [PR #125](https://github.com/finos/morphir-moonbit/pull/125); [PR #100](https://github.com/finos/morphir-moonbit/pull/100) closed as superseded.
- `morphir-ukvn.5.58`: completed focused/full qualification restructuring, the baseline for further selection improvements.
- morphir-ukvn.5.63: Linux-only static TypeScript checks; implemented locally but not yet landed at the time this epic was written.
- morphir-ukvn.5.61 / PR #129: complete pinned Unix MoonBit setup, including Linux ARM64; preserve its fresh-install platform checks when setup changes.
- morphir-ukvn.5.59: migration of legacy mise automation to portable MoonBit scripts.

CI optimization evidence

Issue #131 · morphir-ukvn.5.65 · 18 October 2026 · Qualification pending

  • Scope and targets
  • Measurements
  • Coverage comparison
  • Cache and artifact evaluation
  • Rollback
  • Validation and landing

Scope and targets

Measure first, remove duplicate static/setup work, and select independent baseline jobs for proven isolated components. Keep conservative shared/unknown dependencies and full policy/toolchain qualification. The existing parallelism and native artifact reuse are baseline behavior.

The baseline shows TypeScript/setup is a small fraction of full qualification. Set count-based targets: remove the two redundant TypeScript OS jobs, stop runtime emission in the static job, lint YAML once, and remove three supervision jobs, embedding and Elm/Scheme for browser-only Workbench edits. Preserve all applicable behavior checks. Do not claim a general speedup from noisy elapsed times.

Measurements

Raw exact-attempt, paginated API measurements and cache observations were collected with mise run ci:measure -- RUN_ID --logs. All units below are seconds. Runner occupancy is unweighted and is not billing. Queue sums overlap, and elapsed time includes dependency waits. API job creation/start intervals measure observed scheduling delay; they do not reconstruct a complete dependency DAG.

RunSourceExecuted jobsElapsedQueue sumExecution sumRunner seconds by OS
39065090591000983063e9f50150219399343{'Linux': 6410, 'macOS': 2821, 'Windows': 112}
390931992032c506716c7df49196727609583{'Linux': 6705, 'macOS': 2787, 'Windows': 91}

39093199203 uses the same application/tooling source as the optimization base, 2c50671. 39065090591 is historical context only, not the controlled comparison. Both baseline full runs have available cache logs and no reported cache misses. Exact keys and cache observations are retained in the raw local JSON. Baseline Bun setup and frozen package installs cost roughly 3–6 seconds together on Linux; JavaScript workspace compilation costs about 12–16 seconds in installed jobs. Installed execution and signed-provider acceptance dominate the full critical path. The last-finishing ci-ok gate depends on those chains; the script reports elapsed makespan rather than pretending the API provides a full critical-path model.

Controlled focused comparison uses draft PR #137 with the same harmless Workbench CSS comment before and after, unchanged dependency locks, and per-job cache observations. Full after-change evidence comes from PR #139 with the same retained suite set apart from the two static OS jobs. After-change results remain pending.

Coverage comparison

OptimizationRemoved workRetained coverage and evidence
Static checksmacOS/Windows typecheck duplication, static runtime emission, duplicate YAML lintLinux whole-project checks, environment/type-error rejection tests, frozen installs, YAML lint and package configuration validation remain. Process supervision still executes on three OSes when selected.
Component selectionUnrelated supervision, embedding and Elm/Scheme for proven isolated components; site builds for embedding/MEP-only sourceAll four MoonBit test backends, Wasm/Wasm GC/JS release builds, native CLI/MEP, applicable acceptance and site remain. Shared IR/engine/host, unknown inputs and combinations retain conservative selection. Workbench samples explicitly retain Elm/Scheme freshness.
QualificationNo platform/mode or trust checks removedLinux/macOS installed lifecycle, required LLVM, debug/release, signed providers, fresh Linux x64/ARM64/macOS installation, scheduled full runs and exact-candidate receipts are unchanged. Policy/setup/workspace/mise changes still select full qualification. Known site workflow wiring selects its own build.
Aggregate gateOptional jobs may skipSelected missing/skipped/failed/cancelled jobs fail. Any failed/cancelled optional dependency also fails. Real Git rename/deletion, divergent push, PR, queue and dispatch tests remain.

Cache and artifact evaluation

No new Bun/Mooncakes download cache is introduced. Warm Bun setup and frozen installs take a few seconds, so an additional archive restore/save has no demonstrated benefit. Existing pinned tool caches remain. Cache misses use the existing install path; the qualification matrix explicitly disables the tool cache and exercises fresh installation.

No new JavaScript artifact transfer is introduced. A 12–16 second workspace build is small beside 8–20 minute installed execution, while verified transfer needs its own producer, catalog, download and admission checks. Preserve independent backend/debug/release compilation. Existing same-run native artifact reuse already verifies source revision, run/attempt, target, compiler/core and dependency identities. Its self-tests reject missing/tampered/symlinked/stale/incompatible artifacts and invalid release proof. Rejected artifacts fail closed; no stale artifact or receipt may substitute for qualification. Trust, signing state, mutable fixtures and receipts remain uncached.

Rollback

Revert e59362a to restore the static matrix/setup behavior. Revert the selector slice 4d59a10 and its freshness follow-up 7f3f6a3 together to restore broad baseline selection. Workflow conditions and gate requirements must change together. Keep native artifact admission, full qualification and exact-candidate receipts. The measurement command, 300e3cd with compatibility follow-up 74f4361, can remain independently. Material regressions in required coverage or runner occupancy warrant reverting the affected slice rather than weakening qualification.

Validation and landing

Local mise run test:ci, lint, MoonBit formatting, package validation, whitespace and moon run scripts/ci-artifact.mbtx --self-test pass. The review finding is verified, fixed in 74f4361, answered and resolved. GitHub CLI 2.96.0 collected all 50 reference job logs with the same 108 cache observations and runner totals. Hosted checks for PR #139 remain pending. Draft #137 will close without merge after the controlled comparison. Merge authority is recorded in beads memory roadmap-pr-merge-approval-2026-09-26, conditional on green CI and answered review findings.

CI optimization qualification and measurements

GitHub #131 · morphir-ukvn.5.65 · 18 October 2026 · Qualified and landed

  • Outcome
  • Comparison method
  • Measurements and critical paths
  • Selection and retained coverage
  • Caches, artifacts and trust
  • Requirement audit
  • Rollback
  • Landing and records

Outcome

PR #139 landed as db4c0178a16abcd093325a0e5e4f218b66320312. All 54 check-rollup entries for head 11d2b608a9a3c690097787376a0330b06b6a936e were successful or expected skips, and the review finding was fixed, answered and resolved. The qualified and merged Git trees both equal d9cc45ac93e34736c8b71b27e24dc229fa886891.

The static TypeScript check changes from three OS jobs consuming 103 runner seconds to one Linux job consuming 9 seconds in the matched samples. YAML lint runs once and static setup skips runtime emission. The complete full workload changes from 50 successful jobs and 10,236 runner seconds to 48 jobs and 10,111 seconds. The Workbench-only comparison changes from 28 successful effective results and 2,869 runner seconds to 21 jobs and 2,554 seconds. These are individual observations, not billed minutes or a general percentage claim.

The full run took longer in elapsed time, 1,943 seconds versus 1,574. Queue sums also increased. No full wall-clock speedup is claimed. The count-based targets were selected from the baseline: remove two duplicate static OS jobs, remove repeated YAML/static compilation, and remove seven jobs from a browser-only Workbench change while preserving applicable behavior checks.

Comparison method

The matched full baseline is 39097533093, PR #136 head 85c7d7378cd9a95049e3e64e94f0b50117c68fb6. Its tree b1cc95e395a537fa169d2c0f7aac769c604615aa exactly equals optimization base 0339126. Both full samples are PR runs and include site work. Comparing a main run that skips the site with a PR run would confound the result.

The controlled focused fixture is the same harmless CSS comment in apps/morphir-workbench/workbench.css, first at 74f9803 and then at 196d95e after merging optimized main into the temporary branch. Git diff verified identical app/package/tool/type sources, workspace membership, dependency locks and TypeScript configurations across these two fixture commits. The PR diff contains only that CSS file. Draft #137 passed the post-merge comparison and was closed without merging.

Measurements use mise run ci:measure -- RUN_ID --logs, authenticated read-only GitHub APIs, pagination and exact run-attempt snapshots. All units below are unweighted seconds. Runner occupancy is not billing. Queue sums overlap. Elapsed time includes dependencies, queues and any retry/idle delay. The API does not expose a complete DAG critical-path model.

All 50 full-before, 48 full-after, 28 focused-before and 21 focused-after job logs were available. They reported tool-cache hits and no matching cache-miss messages. The full setup matrix intentionally disables tool caching on three fresh-install hosts. These observations identify tool-cache state; they do not invent package-cache hits. No extra package or compiled-output cache was introduced. Dependency locks and tool versions remained pinned.

The first focused attempt failed a Workbench polling-window assertion. The same job passed on the same SHA without source changes, and the aggregate gate rejected the failed attempt. GitHub retains earlier successful results on retries while resetting their creation times. The corrected measurement command marks those results as retained, leaves their original queue times unknown, and separates effective workload totals from new execution totals. The before snapshot has 26 retained jobs and two newly executed jobs. Saved attempt-1 timestamps recover the original queues for the retained results by matching name, completion time and duration. This gives a comparable complete successful job set without counting retained work twice.

Focused attempt 1 consumed 2,753 runner seconds, attempt 2 added 437, and actual observed cumulative consumption was 3,190 seconds. The effective successful job set consumed 2,869 seconds. Retry waste is separate from the 315-second effective-workload difference. CLI 2.96.0 collected all 50 reference logs and the same 108 cache observations as the newer CLI. Tests cover overlapping job times, OS totals, retained results, unknown queues and both CLI flag variants.

Measurements and critical paths

WorkloadRunEffective jobsElapsed secondsQueue seconds, overlappingEffective execution secondsRunner seconds by OS
Full before39097533093501574114910236{'linux': 7077, 'windows': 135, 'macos': 3024}
Full after39101220076481943284210111{'linux': 6973, 'windows': 68, 'macos': 3070}
Focused before, successful effective job set39099538112, attempt 2281596, includes retry/idle2801, recovered from saved attempts2869{'linux': 2729, 'windows': 106, 'macos': 34}
Focused after, first-attempt success3910326517121458612554{'linux': 2554}

The static TypeScript subcomparison is 3 jobs / 103 runner seconds / 62 queue seconds before, versus 1 job / 9 runner seconds / 3 queue seconds after. Its samples show the same pinned Bun binary cache hit. All projects, frozen installs, environment/type-error checks and checked-build rejection tests remain.

The full-before last-finishing acceptance chain was native CLI/provider-tools production to Linux installed signed-provider acceptance, then native/full/root gates. That consumer had 2 queue seconds and 1,195 execution seconds. The full-after last-finishing acceptance chain was macOS installed lifecycle to installed/full/root gates, with 461 queue seconds and 1,337 execution seconds for lifecycle. These are observed finishing chains read alongside workflow dependencies, not a reconstructed full DAG. The mandatory installed checks still dominate feedback time.

The focused-before elapsed value includes an initial failure, retry and operator delay. The after value is a first-attempt success. The full samples also have different observed queues. Use retained job sets and execution totals for the workload comparison; do not attribute the entire elapsed-time difference to this patch.

Diagnostic and historical runs excluded from the matched comparison

Historical runs 39065090591 and 39093199203 informed the initial cost review. Superseded full run 39099691341 failed an Elm compiler file-lock operation and was cancelled after the required measurement correction was ready. It consumed 10,206 observed runner seconds and is diagnostic cost, not an optimized successful sample. The final full run passed unchanged Elm/Scheme test code without an unrelated repair.

Selection and retained coverage

Changed inputsIndependent baseline jobsRetained checks
Browser Workbench and native Workbench componentsTypeScriptAll build/test backends, native CLI/MEP, installed Workbench and site where affected
Workbench samples and sample generatorTypeScript, Elm/SchemeGenerated sample freshness and applicable Workbench/backend checks
Embedding sourcesTypeScript, embedding/ChromiumBuild/test backends and native CLI/MEP; documentation still selects site
MoonBit generator, bindings, SDK and frontendTypeScript, Elm/SchemeBuild/test backends and transitive compiler/frontend/conformance/provider/lifecycle/Workbench acceptance
MEP/extension or telemetry-only componentsTypeScriptBackends/native CLI/MEP and applicable installed checks
Shared IR/engine/host, tools/locks and unknown codeConservative baseline suitesExisting conservative acceptance dependency rules

Tests cover direct and transitive dependencies, shared inputs, unknown paths, unions, empty diffs, actual Git renames/deletions, divergent force-push semantics, PR/merge-queue/main/dispatch events, automation-policy refusal and output append behavior. Sample freshness was identified in review and given an explicit transitive exception. Job conditions and the aggregate required-job list derive from the same selection.

The complete successful full job sets are identical apart from replacing the three TypeScript OS jobs with one Linux job. The focused successful sets differ only by those two static jobs, three supervision jobs, embedding and Elm/Scheme. Every other successful job remains. The temporary fixture therefore proves the expected 28-to-21 reduction with a green aggregate gate.

Runtime process supervision retains Linux, macOS and Windows whenever selected. Workspace tests retain Wasm, Wasm GC, JavaScript and native. Release CLI builds retain Wasm, Wasm GC and JavaScript, with separate native CLI artifacts and default-compiler native workspace release. Installed lifecycle retains Linux/macOS, required isolated macOS LLVM and debug/release behavior. Signed providers, browser checks and native Workbench workers/workspaces remain. Full fresh setup retains Linux x64, Linux ARM64 and macOS.

qualification.yml, ci-native.yml and ci-installed.yml are unchanged from the application base. Shared policy/setup/workspace/mise changes still select full qualification. Known site workflow wiring exercises site work. Further narrowing needs a tested mapping. Scheduled full qualification and the exact github.sha candidate receipt remain; no release or protection settings were changed.

Caches, artifacts and trust

Frozen Bun installs and pinned tool acquisition remain the miss path. The fresh setup matrix disables the tool cache and passed on all three supported Unix hosts. No trust decision, signing state, mutable fixture or qualification receipt is cached by this change.

No additional Bun/Mooncakes download cache was added. The sampled Linux Bun setup/frozen installs take seconds. No net benefit from another restore/save layer was established. No JavaScript artifact transfer was added: matched baseline installed-job JS workspace builds took 13, 27, 14 and 16 seconds, while installed execution takes hundreds or over a thousand seconds. A verified transfer adds a producer, identities, transfer and admission; the measurements do not establish a benefit that justifies that path here. Distinct backend and debug/release compilations stay independent.

Existing same-run native artifact reuse remains. Admission verifies source/run/attempt, target, compiler/core and dependencies. Its self-test passes native/released/cross reuse and refuses stale source/run/core/target/compiler, missing/tampered catalogs, symlinks, wrong kinds, bad release proof and invalid binary formats. Missing or incompatible artifacts fail closed, rather than satisfying qualification with stale outputs or receipts. Actual signed-provider and installed artifact acceptance passed on both hosts.

Requirement audit

Acceptance requirementEvidence
Comparable before/after queue, execution and runner evidenceMatched complete full samples, identical focused fixture, recorded cache observations and retry accounting above; raw JSON snapshots retained locally
Duplicate static/setup work removed without dropping validationOne TypeScript job, frozen dependencies and rejection tests; runtime setup defaults on for consumers; one YAML lint plus package/task validation; latest full CI passed
Direct/transitive/unknown selection and fail-closed gatesPolicy tests pass; real focused job set is exactly 28 to 21; selected failure/cancellation/skip refusal tests pass; baseline failed JS made ci-ok fail and unchanged retry made it pass
OS/backend/fresh-install/trust/debug-release coverage preservedFull job-set equality apart from redundant statics; native/installed/qualification files unchanged; actual full qualification passed all retained hosts and modes
Scheduled full and exact-candidate release qualification intactUnchanged scheduled/callable qualification workflow and candidate-bound receipt gate; candidate match/mismatch self-tests pass; qualified/merged source trees match
Cache misses and incompatible state remain safeNo new persisted trust/build state; uncached installation matrix passed; admission rejection tests and actual signed-provider qualification pass
Reviewable slices, measured impact, coverage comparison and rollbackSix source commits under PR #139, measurements and coverage above, rollback below, repository documentation and this HTML record

Local mise run test:ci, mise run lint, mise run lint:moonbit, mise run validate, moon run scripts/ci-artifact.mbtx --self-test and git diff --check passed. The exact final-head full CI and post-merge focused CI passed. Existing YAML line-length warnings were not introduced by this patch.

Rollback

Revert squash db4c017 to restore the previous complete policy. For a narrower rollback, static slice e59362a restores the static matrix/setup behavior. Selector 4d59a10 and sample exception 7f3f6a3 should be reverted together; workflow conditions and required-job selection must agree. Measurement 300e3cd, CLI compatibility 74f4361 and retry accounting 11d2b60 can be treated independently. Keep the qualification workflow, native artifact admission and exact-candidate receipt. A material coverage regression warrants rollback; variable elapsed observations alone do not establish causality.

Landing and records

Implementation PR #139 merged on 18 October 2026. The ordinary merge command encountered disabled auto-merge on the merge-queue path. The previously recorded roadmap-pr-merge-approval-2026-09-26 permits maintainer bypass after green CI and answered findings; those conditions were verified, and the merge was bound to the exact qualified head. The temporary fixture PR #137 is closed without merge.

Tracker records are morphir-ukvn.5.65, children .1 through .3, and static task morphir-ukvn.5.63. A concurrent tracker conflict in unrelated morphir-ukvn.5.66 was resolved row by row using the newer remote title and both appended notes; no conflict remains. Source, qualification and measurement work are complete. The enclosing bead and GitHub issue hold the final tracker-publication and closure state. The approved epic requirements and design were verified unchanged. No release was published.

title: Provide Gleam compile, generate and roundtrip compatibility
description:
## Parent
morphir-ukvn.5.64

## What to build
Expose gleam compile/generate/roundtrip through the existing pinned Gleam provider and explicit host adapter. Reuse canonical provider contracts rather than writing a new frontend/backend. Use a known prebuilt provider and fixture project so install/catalog and general compile aliases are not blockers; share command helpers once landed. title: Select CI qualification by semantic mise config changes
description:
> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

Purpose
Make CI selection understand the semantic impact of changes to .config/mise/config.toml, so adding an unrelated task does not automatically select the expensive full qualification workflow.

Current behavior and evidence
PR #125 merged the focused/full CI split as c42351e5f9536c694d5ce34e494290c2eb3cab72. scripts/ci-changes.mbtx requires_full currently returns true for every change to .config/mise/config.toml. PR #128 demonstrates the over-selection: its config diff only adds tasks."test:workbench-capability-job-mck", an opt-in task, but triggers full installation/platform qualification. No failed CI check was observed when this task was requested.

Scope
Compare the base and head TOML configuration semantically using the same verified revision range as CI selection. Classify added, removed and modified settings by their actual effect on checks. Distinguish comments/formatting and unrelated opt-in task declarations from toolchain, bootstrap, shared environment, dependency and CI-invoked task changes. Account for task dependencies and shared/inherited configuration that can affect CI. Select the relevant focused suites when their behavior changes; require full qualification when the changed configuration affects that pathway. A task-only diff is not automatically safe just because it is under tasks.

Preserve conservative full qualification when parsing, base/head retrieval or impact classification is uncertain. Keep existing full triggers for workflow and CI policy changes. Retain baseline lint, formatting and configuration validation and required aggregate-check behavior.

Implementation entry points
- scripts/ci-changes.mbtx and its self-tests
- scripts/ci-gate.mbtx
- .github/workflows/ci.yml and .github/workflows/qualification.yml
- .config/mise/config.toml
Follow repository policy: portable MoonBit .mbtx automation, pinned imports, and mise run test:ci for policy changes. Explain the selection reason in CI diagnostics.

Out of scope
No immediate CI code changes, check removal, toolchain/setup fixes, or changes to PR #128 are authorized by filing this task. The ARM64 installation fix in PR #129 / morphir-ukvn.5.61 is separate.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Comment/format-only changes and adding an unrelated opt-in task, including the PR #128 example, do not select full qualification solely because the config path changed.
- [ ] Toolchain pins, installation/bootstrap hooks and settings affecting full qualification still select the full pathway.
- [ ] Changes to CI-invoked tasks, task dependencies, shared environment and inherited settings select all affected checks; demonstrate direct and transitive cases.
- [ ] Additions, edits, removals, renamed/quoted task keys and mixed safe/expensive changes are covered with base/head fixtures.
- [ ] Invalid TOML, unavailable revisions/config and unknown or ambiguous changes conservatively select full qualification with a visible reason.
- [ ] Existing workflow/CI-policy full triggers, baseline checks and aggregate gate semantics remain intact.
- [ ] mise run test:ci and required lint/format/validation checks pass; document the classification rules and demonstrate expected selection for representative historical diffs.
notes: Additional concrete over-selection example: morphir-moonbit PR148/head402a54e, CI39161511054. The mise config delta only adds opt-in package:codec-adapter and test:codec-adapter-mck task declarations. Existing conservative config-path rule selects the full qualification workflow, including Linux/macOS installed signed-provider, lifecycle, telemetry and toolchain lanes, although the new codec artifact flow uses ordinary user-selected local profiles with no authentication prerequisite. Baseline embedded-toolchain/portable/type/site checks passed much earlier; final source-test tail was installed signed-provider qualification. description:
Task 2 implementation choices for morphir-etg2.16.2, within the approved capability checking policy:

Reserve the next available exact offline Workbench MCK version 0.1.0-draft.12 for run-capability-policy. Drafts 1 through 11 remain immutable. The new operation observes ordered multi-call production terminal outcomes or explicitly labelled validation of caller-supplied completion evidence against the actual retained plan. Supplied completion checks are not execution evidence.

Keep plan_scheme/evaluate and the narrow draft.11 adapter unchanged. A new policy-aware Scheme planner/terminal API routes permissive selected execution through backend emit_selected/run_selected_in. Whole-source and selected-boundary validation remain mandatory.

Represent known unsupported executable semantics with a fixed internal helper raising only the reserved structured pair Stage("evaluate", "execution.unsupported_reached"). Match that exact pair when producing the typed failure, without converting arbitrary compiler, parser, provider or resource errors into unsupported traps. Keep fixed bounded human diagnostics independent of model source.

Constructor metadata retained by selected static references must satisfy the existing arity cap of 256 during preparation, even in dormant branches. This is a resource refusal (scheme.limit), not a deferred unsupported semantic operation. Unrelated constructors remain pruned as in Task 1; the cap is not increased. Complete selected public boundary limits remain stricter and unchanged.

Missing native/external bindings in permissive execution are resolved at the original reference dereference before application arguments, with distinct unbound diagnostics and deterministic candidate/arity selection. An invoked native failure never retries a fallback. Backend tests with explicitly registered trusted bindings are backend evidence only. Production SchemePlan registers no caller-supplied native implementations and advertises no external provider authority.

This decision introduces no UI, jobs, native/HTTP mapping, generated-target or packaged-platform capability. Task 2 must complete its shared and actual-runtime qualification before any scoped claim.
notes: Decimal evidence scope clarified from existing published profile normalization law and SDK normalize/from_string: actual Scheme execution emits exact numeric Decimal values in normalized coefficient/exponent form (123400/-4 ->1234/-2, zero->0/0), without a scale/cohort guarantee. Supplied completion validation performs no arithmetic and preserves valid wire representation under the frozen codec. Independent fixtures retain both canonical and noncanonical-input controls.
close_reason: Accepted implementation decision for Task2: exact draft12 run-capability-policy reserved and implemented; frozen draft11 path stays separate; constructor256 retained preparation cap, lexical/source integrity, binding dereference timing and exact reached-unsupported trap preserve required semantics. Decimal normalization follows existing SDK law. Independent review and all182cases x6 real lanes qualify/recheck. Opaque SDK allocation remains separate discovered task morphir-be5t; specific budget scope documented.

description:
# Scheme modules, types and package mode: implementation plan

Plan: .dev/beads-plans/morphir-ukvn.5.45.1-plan.html (HTML, per AGENTS.md). Spec: the design of morphir-ukvn.5.45.1.
design:
Scheme modules, types and package mode: implementation plan

Bead morphir-ukvn.5.45.1 (epic morphir-ukvn.5.45) · plan drafted 2026-10-17 · spec .dev/beads-specs/morphir-ukvn.5.45.1.html

For agentic workers: REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task by task. Each step is one action with a checkable result.
  • Overview
  • Rulings made while planning
  • Global constraints
  • Review focus
  • File structure
  • Error codes by task
  • Task 1: acceptance features
  • Task 2: source names and form ends
  • Task 3: module syntax and expansion
  • Task 4: the package manifest
  • Task 5: name resolution
  • Task 6: file mode over the module layer
  • Task 7: types and signatures
  • Task 8: records, variants and match
  • Task 9: package mode compiler
  • Task 10: evaluator refuses module forms
  • Task 11: engine package profile
  • Task 12: manifest conflicts and defaults
  • Task 13: Elm parity and inference
  • Task 14: end-to-end corpus
  • Task 15: documentation and wrap-up

Overview

Goal: a Scheme project declares a full Morphir model (aliases, records, tagged custom types, typed values, public and private access) across modules, and the IR equals what the Elm frontend produces for the same model, ignoring source locations. Existing Scheme files, scripts and the specification notation keep working.

Architecture: a new package finos/morphir-scheme/modules turns located source into module syntax, reads src/package.scm, and resolves names across a package and the SDK specification. The frontend lowers resolved modules: compile_file (file mode) is rebuilt on that layer, and the new compile_package (package mode) compiles a whole package and reports every problem in one pass. The engine's built-in Scheme frontend gains a second profile, package, chosen when the manifest exists. Acceptance features in Markdown with Gherkin, with Scheme and Elm code examples, state the spec's criteria first; each task turns its own scenarios on.

Tech stack: MoonBit 0.10.15, moonrockz/expect 0.6.1 for new tests, moonrockz/moonspec 0.11.0 with moonbitlang/async 0.22.4 for acceptance features, the existing engine, Elm frontend and inference (finos/morphir-typing).

Spec: .dev/beads-specs/morphir-ukvn.5.45.1.html. Read it with this plan; it is the binding authority and its section numbers are cited as §N below.

Branch: DamianReeves/scheme-modules-frontend in the worktree C:\Users\damre\orca\workspaces\morphir-moonbit\scheme-backend-metadata-support-sidecar-and-sour, cut from main at ce311b3. Push with -u origin DamianReeves/scheme-modules-frontend.

Rulings made while planning

The spec leaves these open or meets a fact of the code it did not foresee. Each is binding for the tasks; a task that finds one wrong records a new ruling in the ledger.

#RulingWhy
R1The reader's Located gains end : Int32, the character offset just after the form. The change is additive.A SourceLocation needs an end. The spec's "no reader change" assumed starts were enough.
R2File mode writes no source locations; package mode does (§11).The Scheme backend turns value locations into source comments (backend/source_hints.mbt), so locations in file mode would change emit_file output and existing tests.
R3Names: package mode uses Name::from_spelling only. File mode tries Name::parse first and falls back to from_spelling only for spellings parse refuses.Keeps every existing file's IR names: x1 stays x1 in file mode, while from_spelling would give x-1.
R4In file mode, a require between modules of the same file (a parent and its submodule, by full path) resolves. Only a same-package module outside the file is scheme.require_needs_package.§12 allows submodules in file mode, and such a require needs only the file.
R5A qualified name without a package, module#name, means the current package. The part after # is a source spelling, so pricing/customers#Tier works.Today's FQName::parse needs a package and a canonical local name; §5 and §8 promise both forms.
R6Four codes the spec does not list: scheme.invalid (an Invalid error from lowering), scheme.invalid_name (a package-mode spelling with characters other than letters, digits, - and _), scheme.limit (a Limit error), and scheme.manifest_missing (profile package forced without a manifest).Package mode must code every problem, and §12 needs a planning error for a forced profile.
R7The prefix in prefix-in must be a symbol ending in :. Any other prefix is scheme.unsupported.A prefix that ends in : is how a key splits back into prefix and name (local_key). All of the spec's examples end in :.
R8In package mode the manifest reaches the project compiler as an ordinary source with relative path package.scm. In file mode the planner leaves it out of the sources. The planner also reads it at plan time, for the package name and the conflict check.The project-compiler callback has no host, so it can read only its sources.
R9Configuration "sets" project.name when the effective document has that key or a script calls (package-name …). It sets the backend the same way, through pipeline.backend or (backend …). Package mode defaults the backend to checkpoint only when configuration does not set it, and defaults the checkpoint format to morphir-json only when pipeline.checkpoint_format is absent.The default document sets neither key (workspace.mbt:197).
R10In package mode, a lowering error gives one problem per failing definition, located at the failing form when it is known and at the definition otherwise.The compiler stops at the first error inside a definition, but must go on to the other definitions (§14, one pass).
R11Existing tests that pin facts this spec changes are updated, and nothing else is:
  • the frontend chapter's "a call to another top-level definition is a variable today" (now a Reference, §5);
  • source_providers_test.mbt:459-462, Scheme's offer: no profile becomes file plus package;
  • the engine README's paragraph on morphir-ukvn.5.22.8.
§5 closes morphir-ukvn.5.22.8 and §12 adds profiles; the compatibility rule in §15 cannot keep a test that asserts the old fact.
R12An accessor that is not applied, Point-x, lowers to FieldFunction(x). A record constructor that is not applied is scheme.record_arity.Spec silent; the IR has the node.
R13Tests in finos/morphir-ir and finos/morphir-elm/mapping use assert_eq, as their files do.Neither module depends on moonrockz/expect; adding a dependency to the base IR module for tests is not worth it.
R14The evaluator refuses a module or type form only when its head is not bound, so a script that defines match keeps working.Special forms are dispatched before lookup (eval.mbt:118); no source or test in the repository binds these names today.
R15A Problem carries legacy : @scheme.SchemeError?. When a check that today's frontend already makes fires, file mode raises that exact error. Otherwise file mode raises @scheme.Domain(code, "code: detail at L:C").§14: "existing messages stay as they are", and new codes are the message prefix.
R16finos/morphir-scheme now imports finos/morphir-sdk-spec@0.1.0, so the SDK specification must be published before the Scheme module.§13 names the dependency.
R17Type nodes carry no source location.§11 names value and pattern nodes only, and parity ignores locations.
R18The parity model exposes the modules whose types appear in public signatures, and keeps one private helper module whose function is used only in a body.The Elm frontend makes a module public when an exposed signature uses its types (implicitly_exposed, elm/frontend/compile.mbt:129-135). §2 does not, so a model that relies on that difference would not be equal.
R19A docs project whose files include src/package.scm compiles its src/ files in package mode. A later file outside src/ compiles in file mode, and its trailing expression can call package values by qualified name; that gives package examples a value.Package mode refuses trailing expressions, so it has no main to run.
R20The acceptance tests live in a new unpublished module, pkgs/tests/morphir-scheme-acceptance (finos/morphir-scheme-acceptance), listed with the unpublished modules in scripts/validate-packages.mbtx.moonspec is test tooling, and a published module would carry it, with moonbitlang/async, as a dependency. A spike on 2026-10-17 found that moonspec 0.11.0 resolves with this repository's moonrockz/expect 0.6.1.
R21The Scheme and Elm parity test is an acceptance scenario whose doc strings hold the model in both languages. It replaces a separate parity package.The criterion and its demonstration become one readable page, with no second copy of the model.
R22The acceptance scenarios are written first, in Task 1, from the spec. A scenario that today's code does not satisfy is tagged @pending and skipped. The task that satisfies it removes the tag, and Task 15 checks that no tag is left. moonspec's async tests run on native, js and wasm; on wasm-gc they have no entry and report no tests.Acceptance-test-driven: each task's gate includes the criteria it meets, and the CI matrix keeps them green on three targets. The spike found that wasm-gc reports "no test entry found" and does not fail.
R23Each feature file has one hand-written async test, which runs it with run_or_fail. There are no moonspec build rules, and the scenario count is checked by a dry run.Build rules would need the moonspec CLI at every build, in CI and here. run_or_fail reports each failing scenario by name, with suggestions.
R24Acceptance tests live under pkgs/tests/, one unpublished module per area (pkgs/tests/<area>-acceptance). Task 1 writes the pattern down, and bead morphir-ukvn.5.60 moves today's acceptance packages there.The maintainer's direction (2026-10-17): this module sets the pattern for acceptance tests.

Global constraints

  • The spec is the authority. Where this plan and the spec disagree, follow the spec and record a ruling.
  • Compatibility (§15): every existing Scheme frontend, evaluator, pipeline, backend and engine test stays unchanged and green, except the facts listed in R11. Do not change emit_file (pkgs/morphir-scheme/backend/emit.mbt) or the specification notation (pkgs/morphir-scheme/spec).
  • finos/morphir-scheme/modules depends only on finos/morphir-scheme, finos/morphir-ir and finos/morphir-sdk-spec (§13), plus moonrockz/expect for tests.
  • Error codes are exactly the spec's (§14) plus R6. Package mode reports problems with a code, a path relative to the source directory, and a SourceLocation whose rows and columns count from 1.
  • Output is deterministic (§11): modules sorted by path; types, constructors, fields and values in source order; nothing depends on the order the host lists files.
  • New tests use moonrockz/expect (§15), except R13.
  • Acceptance criteria are moonspec features with code examples (R20–R23). A task is not complete until the scenarios it owns pass on native and js, and every earlier task's scenarios still pass.
  • Commits use Conventional Commits in plain English, with no AI attribution and no Co-Authored-By line (AGENTS.md).
  • On this machine run ~/.moon/bin/moon.exe (written moon below); for Bun use C:\Users\damre\AppData\Local\mise\installs\bun\1.4.2\bin\bun.exe; prepend C:\Users\damre\AppData\Local\mise\installs\node\24.21.0 to PATH for js tests. The mise shims fail on Windows ARM64, so run a mise task's run line directly (for example moon run scripts/scheme-docs-generate.mbtx).
  • Run tests per package with moon test -p <package> from the repository root. moon fmt and moon info touch every package: restore unrelated files before committing. Run moon fmt --check and moon check before every commit, not after a push.
  • When a chapter's ```scheme examples change, run moon run scripts/scheme-docs-generate.mbtx and commit the generated files with the chapter.

Review focus

  1. Recursion through references at run time. A file-mode define that calls itself or another define now lowers to Reference (§5). Running the file must give the same values as today, including mutual recursion. Pinned in Task 6 ("recursive and mutually recursive definitions still run").
  2. Host listing order. The same package listed in reverse order must give identical IR and identical problems. Pinned in Task 5 (resolution) and Task 9 (IR).
  3. Spellings that collide. isEligible and is-eligible, a constructor Circle and a value circle, an accessor Point-x and a define point-x: all are one name and must be scheme.duplicate_definition, not a silent overwrite. Pinned in Task 3.
  4. A definition named like a built-in. (define (length xs) …) or (define (list x) …) must make later calls refer to the definition, not the primitive or the list form (§5 order). Pinned in Task 6.
  5. Windows line endings. A source with CRLF must give the same start rows and columns as LF. Pinned in Task 9.
