Task 1: Acceptance features and harness

Files: create the unpublished module pkgs/tests/morphir-scheme-acceptance/: moon.mod, README.md, src/{moon.pkg,world.mbt,steps.mbt,features_wbtest.mbt} and features/*.feature.md, and pkgs/tests/README.md. Modify moon.work (add "./pkgs/tests/morphir-scheme-acceptance"), scripts/validate-packages.mbtx (list it with the unpublished modules, beside pkgs/morphir-typing-tools) and docs/ARCHITECTURE.md (the repository structure gains pkgs/tests/).

The pattern (R24). This module is the first under pkgs/tests/, which holds every acceptance-test module from now on. pkgs/tests/README.md states the pattern, and docs/ARCHITECTURE.md links to it from its repository structure:

  • One unpublished module per area, pkgs/tests/<area>-acceptance/, named finos/<area>-acceptance. It is a moon.work member and is listed as unpublished in scripts/validate-packages.mbtx.
  • Acceptance criteria are moonspec features, features/*.feature.md, in Markdown with Gherkin. Each scenario names the spec section it checks, and its doc strings hold the code it demonstrates.
  • Steps and a plain-valued world are in src/. Each feature file has one hand-written async test, plus a dry-run count test.
  • A criterion that is not met yet is tagged @pending, and the work that meets it removes the tag.
  • The tests run on native, js and wasm with moon test. moonspec has no wasm-gc test entry.
  • Existing acceptance packages move here over time. Bead morphir-ukvn.5.60 tracks the move.

Why first: the features are the spec's acceptance criteria written as code examples (R22). Every scenario starts tagged @pending. A later task removes the tag from the scenarios it satisfies and adds the steps they need; the acceptance step of that task names them. Task 15 checks that none is left.

The world holds plain values, so it compiles before the APIs that later tasks add:

struct SchemeWorld {
  files : Map[String, String]                       // project-relative path → text ("src/pricing/rates.scm", "morphir.toml")
  mut ir : @ir.IRFile?                              // the last Scheme compilation
  mut elm_ir : @ir.IRFile?                          // Task 13
  mut problems : Array[(String, String, Int32, Int32)]  // (code, path, line, column) of the last failure
  mut error : String?                               // @scheme.error_message of the last failure
  mut value : String?                               // the last evaluation or run result
  mut plan : String?                                // Task 11: a summary of the last engine plan, as the steps read it
} derive(Default)

Expansion rules:

  • Top-level forms are classified by head: provide, require, module, define-type, define-record, define-variant, :, define. Anything else is an expression.
  • Today's definition shapes and their errors keep their exact messages, set as legacy, with code scheme.invalid or scheme.unsupported by error class:
    • "Incomplete definition"
    • "define needs one expression"
    • "Top-level function requires at least one parameter"
    • "Duplicate definition: x", for a repeated spelling, with code scheme.duplicate_definition
    • "Definitions must precede expressions", in file mode only. In package mode an expression is top_level_expression (Task 5) wherever it appears.
  • A parameter is a symbol or [name : T]. : T directly after the parameter list is the output.
  • Type and constructor names must start with an upper-case letter, else scheme.invalid_type_name. A record with no field, a variant with no constructor, or a repeated field or constructor within one type is scheme.invalid_type, located at the repeated element.
  • Names of one module are one namespace for values: definitions, constructors, record constructors (the type's spelling) and accessors (the type's spelling, -, the field's spelling). Two whose local_key is equal are scheme.duplicate_definition, at the later one. Types are a second namespace with the same rule. Signatures: two for one name are scheme.duplicate_definition; one with no definition is scheme.signature_without_define.
  • rename-out, all-from-out, any other provide or require form, and a prefix-in prefix not ending in : are scheme.unsupported, located at that spec (R7).
  • Two submodules of one file with the same path are scheme.duplicate_module.
  • A require module path is pkg:module or module, spelled as written. Validation is Task 5.
  • Every problem of the file is collected; raise ModuleProblems(sort_problems(…)) once.

module Pricing.Customers exposing (Tier(..), Customer, Tree(..), Token, customerTier)

type Tier = Standard | Gold | Platinum Int
type alias Customer = { name : String, tier : Tier }
type Tree a = Leaf | Node (Tree a) a (Tree a)
type Token = Token String
type alias Points = Int

customerTier : Customer -> Tier
customerTier c = c.tier

module Pricing.Util exposing (bounded)

bounded : Float -> Float
bounded x = if x < 0.0 then 0.0 else x

import Pricing.Util exposing (bounded)

type alias Rate = Float
type alias Pair a = ( a, a )

discount : Tier -> Float
discount tier =

        Standard -> 0.0
        Gold -> 0.1
        Platinum years -> if years > 5 then 0.25 else 0.2

quoteFor : Customer -> Float -> Float
quoteFor c amount = bounded (amount * (1.0 - discount (customerTier c)))

title: Use capabilities vocabulary for Workbench checks
description:
The maintainer directs Workbench documentation and domain vocabulary to use capabilities instead of admission.

Runtime capabilities are the supported behavior of a particular implementation and context. Capability verification gathers scoped evidence for provider/runtime claims under an exact contract, implementation and platform. Capability validation checks the requirements of a particular selected function, model revision and run against those capabilities, under an explicit checking policy.

Whole model before running and As code executes describe validation scope and timing. They do not expand supported capabilities, waive mandatory integrity/identity/resource checks or the complete selected input/output type closure, or establish a formal proof or business-rule correctness. Input, output, receipt and authorization validation remain separate checks. Provider-authored claims, offline MCK adapter claims and live session offers remain distinct.

Compatibility identifiers remain unchanged: existing admission keys, profile/operation IDs, versions, file paths, API names and strict/permissive wire values. No frozen fixture, schema or runtime behavior is changed. Historical records remain historical.

The six-slice implementation remains morphir-etg2.16, 1 complete / 5 remaining (16.7%, 1:5). Task 2 remains next, not started by this documentation change. Related documentation task: morphir-p65j.

design:
MoonBit String source semantics

morphir-ukvn.1.10.13.1 · revision 0.1 · 17 October 2026 · approved by maintainer on 17 October 2026

  • A runnable MoonBit String example first
  • Compiler evidence that changes the design
  • Additive profiles and dependency boundaries
  • Concrete grammar and type rules
  • Executable IR semantics, rather than descriptive width or encoding facts
  • A source String is well-formed UTF-16
  • Ordering and four pinned source predicate methods
  • Length and owned slices wait only for N1
  • Metadata ownership and format preservation
  • Proposed limits and failure policy
  • Implementation contracts and shared ownership
  • Reproducible evidence and its limits
  • Decisions to review before implementation

A runnable MoonBit String example first

Compile explicitly typed MoonBit String/Bool libraries through the existing engine and CLI, evaluate their typed IR, generate callable MoonBit, and expose a working greeting sample in the workbench. String basics consumes the shared typed-library milestone, independently of numeric N2-N6. Keep the original Boolean APIs and default profiles compatible.

Semantic specification revision 0.1 approved by the maintainer in this session. Scheduling is also approved. These probes qualify raw source/core and hand-authored typed IR, not a completed String source frontend or installed profile.

fn prefix() -> String { "Hello, " }
pub fn greet(name : String) -> String {
  let greeting : String = prefix()
  greeting + name
}
pub fn welcome(name : String, enabled : Bool) -> String {
  if enabled { greet(name) } else { "" }
}

The workbench sample is MoonBit source in the additive String basics profile. Evaluate greet("Morphir") as "Hello, Morphir"; evaluate both branches of welcome; inspect the generated library and invoke its public entries. Private prefix remains inaccessible to external consumers.

Compiler evidence that changes the design

OperationPinned MoonBit source/coreMorphir SDK TextDecision
Equality"é" differs from "e + combining acute"Exact UTF-16 units also differNo Unicode normalization or locale coercion.
Ordering"b" < "aa" is true, shortlexLexical comparison says falseLength-first comparison, then UTF-16 lexical tie-break.
Length"a😀b" has 4 UTF-16 unitsSDK length also yields 4Expose Int32 result only with the indexed slice after N1.
Split surrogate"a😀b"[1:2].to_owned() is emptySDK slice retains the high surrogate 55357Use source-specific slice lowering, never a direct SDK slice substitution.
Negative slice start[−1:3] clamps start to zero, returns "a😀"SDK negative offset is relative to the end, returns emptyClamp source indexes to [0, length].
Uppercase"Straße" becomes "STRAßE"SDK becomes "STRASSE"Defer case conversion; source ASCII mapping differs from SDK Unicode mapping.
Lowercase"ΟΣ" stays "ΟΣ"SDK becomes "ος"Defer case conversion.
Invalid source literalCompiler refuses \u{d800}, diagnostic 4064SDK Text can store isolated halvesSource String must remain well-formed UTF-16.
Host conversionSource String is well formedText::to_string raises UnrepresentableText for a lone surrogateReject source-boundary invalid input; preserve general Morphir Text behavior.

Additive profiles and dependency boundaries

Keep source language moonbit. The following profile IDs are proposed versioned contracts, not current registrations. Separate immutable profiles let each complete slice be offered without silently changing a previously qualified subset. The combined profile is offered only after the final join.

Proposed profileAdmitted source subsetPrerequisites
moonbit-model-string-library-v1String/Bool basics onlyReviewed design + shared typed foundation morphir-ukvn.1.10.12.3
moonbit-model-string-ordered-library-v1Basics + <, <=, >, >= on StringString basics; no source numeric types required
moonbit-model-string-indexed-library-v1Basics + qualified N1 Int32 forms + length and owned slicesString basics + full N1 Int32 qualification
moonbit-model-string-sdk-library-v1Basics + four pinned source predicate methodsString basics + shared resolver morphir-ukvn.1.10.12.4
moonbit-model-string-qualified-library-v1Union of the four individually qualified String subsetsAll String slices + installed String qualification

Existing Boolean profiles/default remain as they are. The new source descriptors list actual grammar, concrete signatures, runtime-extension requirements and target/mode qualification; they do not claim every String SDK binding or grant a host capability. Numeric N6 and String installed qualification remain independent.

Concrete grammar and type rules

  • Basics accepts one-file acyclic libraries, explicitly typed ordinary functions with positional named parameters and explicit String/Bool results, public or unexported visibility, ordinary cooked String literals, Boolean literals, parameter/local references, grouping, same-type constraints, immutable single-name lets, direct fully applied same-file calls, and if/else with Bool conditions and identical branch types.
  • String + String returns String. String == String and String != String return Bool. Existing Boolean operations keep their semantics. No String/Bool coercion, interpolation, multiline strings, Char, StringView parameters/results, generics, closures, partial applications, imports, mutation, effects, early returns, loops or recursion is admitted by basics.
  • Collect concrete signatures before resolving bodies. Resolve binders and calls once, type every expression, require exact arguments/results and reject unresolved or mismatched uses. Preserve readable names, lexical shadowing, source evaluation order, visibility and existing cancellation/observation phases.
  • Validate lexer errors before accepting parser output. The pinned parser accepts the proposed String syntax, while the current Boolean frontend rejects it with moonbit_frontend.unsupported_type. Parser acceptance alone does not count as frontend admission.
  • Retain original source literal spelling and its validated source location separately from cooked text. Use the lexer coordinate adapter and original token/source record, never reconstruct the authored token from the decoded AST.

Executable IR semantics, rather than descriptive width or encoding facts

Reuse the checked mixed-type library pipeline from the shared foundation. Source String uses classic morphir/SDK:string#string as its semantic IR value carrier and sdk.Text in the generated ABI. Source Bool uses the existing Boolean carrier. Every expression, binding, call and type use carries its actual type and its own source origin.

Keep String validity and resource behavior executable. Introduce a separately declared, versioned source-runtime extension morphir-moonbit-source-string-v1 with the proposed identities below. These are internal compiler lowering targets, not source-importable SDK names. Their implementation must be registered consistently in the explicit extension specification/runtime inventory, evaluator, generator and invocation qualification. The classic 248-binding SDK inventory and its semantic pin remain unchanged.

Proposed internal identityContractNeeded by
morphir/moonbit-source:string#require-validText plus configured code-unit bound → same Text; reject malformed UTF-16 or excess lengthAll source String public entry boundaries
morphir/moonbit-source:string#append-boundedTwo valid Text operands plus bound → concatenated valid Text; check output size before allocationString basics + operator
morphir/moonbit-source:string#slice-owned-boundedValid Text and qualified Int32 bounds plus bound → source-clamped, pair-trimmed owned TextIndexed profile only

Do not duplicate classic Text append or storage. The source helpers add the missing validation, size preflight and slice policy around existing implementations. Typed IR references declare the required extension explicitly. Missing or wrong-signature runtime bindings refuse before publication; a similarly named package cannot register arbitrary native code.

Evaluate receiver, operands and arguments once in source order, using explicit temporaries before curried IR applications. Emit public entry checks after all source arguments have been evaluated and before the body. Internal calls retain the same source evaluation order. Direct generated consumers also execute these guards, so safety does not depend solely on an installed host recognizing metadata.

A source String is well-formed UTF-16

The source String invariant is stricter than general Morphir Text. Typed invocation may transport arbitrary Text code units, but a source String entry rejects isolated high or low surrogates, reversed pairs and truncated pairs before the body. A generated public export enforces the same rule. Well-formed input preserves its exact code units, including supplementary and combining sequences; it is never normalized, repaired or replaced.

Use existing SdkError.UnrepresentableText for direct consumer conversion/validity failures and the evaluator's existing sdk.unrepresentable_text classification. Use SdkError.OutOfRange and the existing SDK range classification for declared source-size policy refusals. Keep frontend typing/syntax failures contextual using the shared frontend diagnostic contract. New boundary/extension diagnostic spellings must be registered and tested, not inferred from metadata.

The first backend probes intentionally retain and compare a lone surrogate as SDK Text and verify host String conversion refusal. This remains legal in general Morphir Text programs. It does not become legal source String input because backend Text operations can retain it.

Proposed invocation sequence

This is the planned source entry contract, not a claim that the current workbench implements it. Open the explorable sequence.

Ordering and four pinned source predicate methods

String ordering is shortlex over UTF-16 units. Evaluate both operands once; compare lengths first; if equal, use the SDK UTF-16 lexical ordering. The design probe demonstrates this explicit typed-IR composition through Scheme and generated consumers, including equal-length supplementary versus BMP text. Do not lower source ordering directly to classic Basics Text comparison. The ordered profile initially exposes only Boolean comparison operators; Int32-returning compare methods remain outside it.

Pinned source methodCanonical implementation targetArgument policy
s.is_empty()morphir/SDK:string#is-emptyValid String receiver, no arguments
s.contains(needle)morphir/SDK:string#containsReceiver and String needle; swap into SDK needle-first argument order
s.has_prefix(prefix)morphir/SDK:string#starts-withReceiver and String prefix; explicit pinned String-to-view coercion
s.has_suffix(suffix)morphir/SDK:string#ends-withReceiver and String suffix; explicit pinned String-to-view coercion

The original compiler accepts String variables as predicate arguments through its implicit StringView coercion. Freeze that exact builtin mapping in the shared resolver. No first-class or escaping StringView value is admitted. Unknown methods, wrong signatures, shadowed bindings or non-admitted coercions refuse; the name alone cannot select a package or runtime function.

Case conversion, trimming, replacement, reverse, regex, locale behavior, interpolation, iteration, callback-based methods, List/Maybe-returning methods and numeric parsing/formatting are deferred. In particular, current MoonBit ASCII-only to_upper/to_lower must not be mapped to SDK Unicode case conversion. Future additions need their own contract and per-function evidence.

Length and owned slices wait only for N1

The indexed profile uses qualified N1 Int32 source boundaries and its actual SDK wrapper ABI. s.length() returns the UTF-16 unit count as Int32 after exact checked conversion. Do not equate it with grapheme or Unicode scalar count.

Initially admit only an owned slice expression s[start:end].to_owned(), with both bounds supplied as Int32 expressions and the receiver a String. The view is an internal intermediate and cannot escape into variables, parameters or results. Fully evaluate receiver, start and end once before lowering.

n = UTF-16 unit length
start = clamp(start, 0, n)
end = clamp(end, 0, n)
if start is inside a surrogate pair: start += 1
if end is inside a surrogate pair: end -= 1
if start >= end: return empty String
otherwise return the exact units in [start, end)

Negative indexes clamp to zero; they are not relative offsets. Split supplementary characters disappear from that slice rather than becoming isolated halves. Combining marks may be sliced independently because the contract is code-unit based, not grapheme based. Reject exact_view/get_view/legacy view and borrowed StringView APIs until separately specified. No unchecked slicing or panic-based partial match is a lowering strategy.

Metadata ownership and format preservation

Propose a schema-validated moonbit-source-string-v1 representation payload on each String parameter/output type use and original expression. Record language, authored/canonical type spelling, UTF-16 encoding, well-formedness invariant, compiler/profile identity and owning source origin. Record literal token spelling/cooked units on the original literal, and conversion/synthetic-operation policy on the implementing expression with an origin link.

Use existing TypeAttributes.extensions, ValueAttributes.extensions and addressed IRUnit.metadata. Share the ownership and schema dispatch conventions with the numeric foundation, without overwriting numeric or unknown neighboring facts. Final extension keys must be declared with the shared schema owner; this document's contract ID is a proposal, not a registered Morphir predicate.

Literal text and authored source facts describe the program. Required validation and ordering/slicing behavior reside in executable IR and declared runtime-extension dependencies. Wire metadata cannot register a runtime binding, authenticate a provider, authorize an optimization or grant host access.

Ion text/binary remains the preferred checkpoint representation. Preserve unknown metadata and source/target naming records on replay. Morphir JSON remains supported where the current checked projection retains facts; preserve data.lossy_conversion refusals rather than discarding engine metadata/provenance. No new IR revision or native property-graph codec support is claimed.

Proposed limits and failure policy

Keep the existing library compile limits: 65,536 UTF-8 source bytes, 64 functions, 16 parameters, 256 lets per function, 4,096 visited expressions, 1,024 call sites, depth 64 and call-graph depth 32. Enforce the shared foundation's existing cancellation and resource checks.

Propose a source String maximum of 1,048,576 UTF-16 code units per value. A host may lower this bound; it cannot increase the qualified profile's hard bound. Validate entry arguments before invoking the body. Check append result length before allocation using exact intermediates or a proved non-overflowing bound check. Validate results before returning them. Store the selected bound in the immutable lowering/runtime contract, not an unauthenticated metadata instruction.

This is a per-value bound. Existing evaluator fuel and provider deadlines/memory isolation remain necessary for cumulative work; this design does not claim a total allocation cap or preemptible parsing. Test lower configured limits, concatenation at/over the cap, cancellation and repeated calls. Resource refusals remain distinguishable from malformed text and unsupported operations.

Implementation contracts and shared ownership

Preserve N1's in-progress issue, ownership, existing SDK/invocation handoff and qualification scope. The published handoff contains SDK/invocation work, not an implemented typed frontend. Coordinate shared type/schema/resolver edits before implementation; do not build a competing String parser or resolver. The shared milestones may land with the original numeric slices while retaining separate evidence.

Proposed source-to-consumer flow

The evaluator/generated branches need independent expected original-source rows. Open the explorable flow.

Reproducible evidence and its limits

Baseline commit 9e59e7a62e4d1fffcdeccccabb64ab8dc2174af9; compiler/core 0.10.15+943464bfa, parser 0.4.5, lexer 0.4.3. The local runner is a pinned-import MoonBit script.

The runner passes 22 tests on native, JS, Wasm and Wasm-GC in debug and release, 176 test results. Each lane includes 15 independent typed-IR Scheme outcomes, 16 generated-consumer tests, five raw source/core tests, and four parser/current-frontend refusal checks inside the Scheme/probe test. Separate compiler controls check a valid String function and implicit view coercion, and reject an isolated-surrogate escape and String + Bool.

Binary Ion receipt is the primary evidence record; Ion text and JSON inspection view record exact artifact/log hashes and scope. Binary and text decode/encode replay were verified. Probe source and expected rows remain local under .dev/strings-source-design/.

These are compiler/core, SDK and manually authored typed-IR probes. Current frontend String input remains refused. No source String frontend, source boundary helper, slice helper, size policy, engine profile, workbench sample or installed String qualification is implemented or proved by these receipts. Those require the implementation tasks and fresh evidence on their actual commits.

Decisions to review before implementation

  1. Use String/Bool basics first, with a real MoonBit greeting workbench sample, and separate additive qualified profiles for later operation subsets.
  2. Keep well-formed UTF-16 as the source invariant, with executable entry guards and a separately classified source-runtime extension instead of treating metadata or raw Text as sufficient.
  3. Preserve shortlex ordering and clamped, surrogate-trimmed owned slices; initially admit only the four named predicate methods through the shared resolver. Defer case conversion and other unqualified String methods.
  4. Use a 1,048,576-unit per-value hard bound, with hosts allowed to tighten it and append checked before allocation.

After review, refine the existing implementation beads and continue with the shared typed foundation and String basics; do not create duplicate tasks or mark source support complete from these probes.

comments.author: Damian Reeves
comments.text:
The maintainer directs Workbench documentation and domain vocabulary to use capabilities instead of admission.

Runtime capabilities are the supported behavior of a particular implementation and context. Capability verification gathers scoped evidence for provider/runtime claims under an exact contract, implementation and platform. Capability validation checks the requirements of a particular selected function, model revision and run against those capabilities, under an explicit checking policy.

Whole model before running and As code executes describe validation scope and timing. They do not expand supported capabilities, waive mandatory integrity/identity/resource checks or the complete selected input/output type closure, or establish a formal proof or business-rule correctness. Input, output, receipt and authorization validation remain separate checks. Provider-authored claims, offline MCK adapter claims and live session offers remain distinct.

Compatibility identifiers remain unchanged: existing admission keys, profile/operation IDs, versions, file paths, API names and strict/permissive wire values. No frozen fixture, schema or runtime behavior is changed. Historical records remain historical.

design:
MoonBit Wasm hosting: runtime and build-time routes

morphir-ukvn.5.55.7 · 18 October 2026 · research revision 0.8

Small interoperability probes passed on the pinned MoonBit 0.10.15 toolchain. This is partial evidence, not full MEP or installed-host qualification and not an approved runtime selection.

  • Findings
  • Packages
  • Hosting shapes
  • Build-time adaptation
  • moonx tool execution
  • Extism hosting
  • Javy-style packaging
  • Executed probes
  • Repeatable qualification
  • Callbacks and resources
  • Compiler and artifact packaging
  • Compilation and usage diagrams
  • Libraries and host interfaces
  • Next qualification
  • Sources

Findings

  • Core-Wasm tool hosting is useful independently of Component Model support. A MoonBit application can embed a runtime rather than launch an external compiler/runtime for every tool.
  • The tested wasm5 embedding itself runs as native, JavaScript, and ordinary core Wasm. The last case is a core-Wasm application interpreting another core module.
  • Wasmoon exposes an actual MoonBit component runtime facade. A native embedding using its interpreter invoked a component and rejected an absent export. Its native CLI also invoked that component.
  • jco successfully converted the same component to core Wasm plus JavaScript bindings. Node executed the generated entry point correctly.
  • Extracting modules with wasm-tools component unbundle leaves a component requiring orchestration and canonical lifting. It is not a complete conversion to one ordinary core module.
  • moonx already supplies registry acquisition, caching and process execution for tools. A pinned registry tool passed first-run and cache-reuse probes.
  • The official Extism JS host passed byte round trips. A native MoonBit adapter can use the official C API; a new pure MoonBit Extism SDK would require substantial additional host-contract work.
  • Javy-style runtime/program packaging is feasible with existing MoonBit runtime code. A small Scheme package ran as standalone Wasm. This is distinct from a new JavaScript implementation or an optimized Morphir backend.

Do not infer complete Component Model or arbitrary-tool support.

Hosting shapes inside Morphir

1. Ordinary Wasm tool

MoonBit app → ToolHost → core-Wasm instance
                        ↳ explicit argv, stdin/stdout, files and host imports
                        ↳ exit status, diagnostics, cancellation and cleanup

A formatter, parser, code generator or build helper can use this path without becoming a component. Supply the imports the actual artifact requires. A command entry such as _start and a persistent library/reactor need different invocation lifecycles. Module/instance caching should follow those semantics.

2. Direct component host

let runtime = @component.ComponentRuntime(
  engine=@component.interpreter_component_engine(),
)
defer runtime.close()
let instance = runtime.instantiate("morphir-host-probe", bytes)
let add = instance.bind("add")
let values = add.call([U32(20U), U32(22U)])

This exact shape ran in the Wasmoon native embedding. The facade exposes typed binding, resources, call cancellation and execution limits, but those broader contracts still need focused Morphir qualification. Keep this behind a replaceable ComponentHost capability. Explicit user selection and capability compatibility remain the baseline; no authenticated publisher prerequisite is introduced.

3. Component prepared for an existing JavaScript host

component.wasm → pinned jco build step
               → core module(s) + generated JavaScript bindings
               → Workbench worker / Proton renderer / JS CLI host

The app's JavaScript engine supplies core Wasm; generated bindings retain component interface and canonical ABI behavior. This is a credible browser/renderer route. It is not proof that our current browser/desktop production adapters already implement it, and it does not give a native-only app a JavaScript engine.

Keep shared MEP operations and model semantics above the binding. Prefer WIT when the required hosts and guests pass qualification; retain Extism where it delivers a useful supported route.

What a Javy-like system in MoonBit would mean

Javy packages a JavaScript runtime with a program. Its static output includes the runtime; dynamic output imports a compatible runtime provider. It is a useful packaging pattern, separate from the engine that runs the resulting Wasm.

The MoonBit proof imports finos/morphir-scheme, creates its runtime and evaluates (define (answer x) (+ x 2)) (answer 40). It asserts and prints 42. The resulting debug core-Wasm artifact is 582,788 bytes; Javy's default static fixture is 1,358,108 bytes. These different programs, runtimes and build modes are not a performance or size comparison.

A future Morphir packager could embed an Ion model and a compatible evaluator, record model/runtime/SDK versions, and expose the selected MEP binding. That remains a proposal. This probe used Scheme source and does not establish typed Morphir IR execution, a bytecode compiler, runtime snapshots, or optimized backend code generation. Preinitialization should only capture deterministic state, never live I/O handles.

These tools can combine. A packaged runtime/program could be published as a Mooncakes main package and acquired by moonx, or expose an Extism or component interface. Acquisition, runtime packaging and plugin protocol should remain separate configurable responsibilities.

Package the compiler and produce runnable Wasm

The maintainer proposes a self-contained compilation and hosting experience analogous to Shopify Functions/Javy. This is a useful delivery direction. Keep compiler invocation, dependency resolution, artifact packaging and runtime invocation as separate provider responsibilities, while presenting one coherent Morphir CLI workflow.

Morphir model
  → MoonBit backend → generated library + pinned SDK/dependency graph
  → packaged compiler provider → linked core Wasm
  → artifact + Ion manifest describing exports, imports and compatibility
  → selected host → function result and diagnostics

MoonBit source can enter at the compiler stage.
Javy-generated Wasm can enter at the compatible-host stage.

The existing @morphir/moonbit-toolchain embedding already exposes compile and run, produces Wasm bytes from in-memory source, accepts dependency interfaces/cores, supplies host imports and supports worker cancellation. Its tests run without an installed MoonBit CLI. The current morphir toolchain build/run commands use the process provider; the embedded package is not yet a complete embedded CLI build pipeline or replacement for the moon package resolver.

Required assembly of modules and referenced libraries

The compiler path must support assembling all modules we provide, together with their referenced libraries and transitive dependencies. Single-file or isolated-package compilation is only a probe. The assembly planner must resolve a complete, versioned dependency graph across workspace libraries, the matching MoonBit core, the Morphir SDK, generated modules and externally referenced libraries. Preserve package/module identity, required interfaces, linked cores and source/model provenance through the build.

  1. Resolve and validate the dependency closure. Report missing libraries, incompatible versions, unsupported features and invalid dependency cycles with actionable diagnostics.
  2. Build packages in dependency order with matching compiler/core/SDK assets. Supply direct, indirect and standard interfaces as required; link every required compiled core once. Reuse compatible compiled artifacts through the existing provider boundary.
  3. Assemble the selected application or library exports and retain its declared host imports. A standalone artifact contains its required code; a shared-provider form explicitly identifies its remaining runtime/library dependencies.
  4. Apply tree shaking from explicit roots, including entry points, selected public exports, required initialization and registered/indirectly invoked functions. Preserve initialization behavior and host/component interface contracts. Dynamic discovery requires declared retention roots or a conservative fallback.
  5. Write an Ion manifest identifying the resolved libraries and versions/digests, compiler/core/SDK identities, retained exports, required imports/runtime providers and optimization settings. Keep the original resolved dependency graph available even when unreachable code is removed from the final assembly.

Tree shaking reduces retained code and bundle/assembly size after correct dependency resolution. It must not conceal a missing or incompatible dependency. Reuse compiler/linker dead-code elimination where available, and qualify the exact behavior of our pinned toolchain rather than assuming that every assembly form receives the same optimization.

Acceptance needs a multi-module generated library that references another library with a transitive dependency and shared SDK code. Run the persisted artifact in a fresh host. Demonstrate semantic equivalence with and without the selected optimization, preservation of explicitly retained exports/initialization, removal of a deliberately unreachable fixture, and an actionable missing/incompatible-library failure. Record artifact sizes and dependency identities without promising an arbitrary reduction percentage. These acceptance cases remain planned work.

Compilation and usage diagrams

Read these as the proposed integration design. The compiler and runtime probes above demonstrate individual building blocks. They do not yet establish a complete generated-library build, package and installed-host workflow. Each diagram has an interactive standalone version; the inline SVGs remain readable without JavaScript.

1. Assemble the full program at build time

Start with a MorphirModel or authored MoonBit source. The assembly planner resolves all supplied modules, referenced libraries and transitive dependencies with the matching core and SDK. Compiler and linker providers build that graph in dependency order. Tree shaking follows declared retention roots and preserves required initialization and interface contracts. The saved Ion manifest keeps dependency provenance even when optimization removes unused code.

Explore the compilation flow

2. Choose what the artifact carries

MoonBit compiles program and library code to Wasm instructions. Javy compiles JavaScript to QuickJS bytecode, then either bundles the JavaScript engine or leaves explicit imports for a matching shared provider. All forms require a host with the right Wasm features and imports. A bundled artifact can still need host services such as WASI. “Bundled” describes its language runtime, not an absence of imports.

Compare compiled, bundled-runtime and shared-runtime artifacts

The same Wasmtime version ran our scalar MoonBit artifact and static Javy artifact. That proves a useful common engine path for those fixtures. Dynamic Javy consumption has not been qualified locally. Its provider must supply the exact import namespace and compatible exports used by the generated module, as described in Javy's dynamic-linking documentation.

3. Load and invoke the saved artifact

The consumer loads the Wasm and manifest, checks the selected ABI, codecs and runtime capabilities, binds declared imports, then instantiates and invokes the program. Shared-runtime forms add the matching provider before instantiation. The compiler is absent from this call path. Returning results, handling cancellation and releasing resources belong to the host adapter.

4. Package an MCK adapter as a reusable artifact

The maintainer identified MCK adapter creation and consumption as another useful application of this pipeline. An adapter author could supply a thin mapping from the exact MCK contract to a production library, then use the assembly pipeline to build that adapter and its dependencies into Wasm. Consumers would select the saved artifact and its manifest rather than reconstruct the author's compiler and source build on every machine.

The current shared Rust MCK launches an explicitly selected executable adapter with arguments. It does not directly load arbitrary Wasm adapters. The first integration can preserve that boundary with a generic executable bridge that loads the selected artifact and forwards the existing bounded request/response protocol. Direct Wasm loading inside MCK would be a separate upstream improvement. This proposal adds neither a second runner nor a second source of expected results.

Include malformed input, contract mismatch, timeout and cleanup cases. Keep native-only ownership and browser-specific tests on their actual platforms. A portable artifact cannot establish behavior that its host never exercises, and native-only implementations may need explicit host bindings rather than a fully linked Wasm library.

Current integration references: apps/morphir-workbench/mck/README.md documents the production codec adapter and parent-owned verdicts. In finos/morphir, docs/developers/mck-native-migration.md documents the explicit executable and separately pinned runner/kit/adapter; crates/morphir-mck/src/transport/session.rs owns process launch. This packaged-adapter bridge remains proposed work.

Known libraries and host interfaces

The maintainer identified a broader simplification opportunity. Tooling can supply a known base library and a known host interface, and support several such environments through the same compilation and packaging pipeline. Extension authors can build against that defined environment instead of assembling runtime plumbing for every tool and host. The deployed program carries its required library code or declares a qualified shared provider.

Separate the library, interface and implementation

ConceptMeaning in this proposed designIndependent choices
Base libraryVersioned reusable modules for code running inside the guest. Candidate modules include Morphir model operations, SDK functions, metadata, diagnostics and Ion/JSON codecs. “Base library” includes functions and types; it does not require an object-oriented class hierarchy.Libraries remain ordinary dependencies. Keep them modular and tree-shake from explicit roots. An author can add referenced libraries without changing the host interface.
Host interfaceThe external functions a guest may call, with argument/result types, error semantics, resource ownership, lifetime, cancellation and scheduling rules.A native CLI, Node worker or browser worker can implement the same interface differently. The selected interface and host policy determine available services. Advertising an interface does not grant filesystem or network access.
Execution profileProposed term for a named, versioned pairing of base-library contracts and host-interface requirements, including the required ABI, Wasm features and codec semantics.A profile is independent of source language, frontend profile, compiler packaging and the particular host implementation. MoonBit remains the language. Concrete compiler/core/library assets are pinned separately in the resolved build.
Host implementationAn adapter and engine that actually satisfy a selected profile on a particular platform.Several implementations can satisfy one profile. Support for a profile needs scoped evidence for that host; core-Wasm support alone does not establish component support.

The base library should own portable computation and model handling. The host interface should expose the effects that require the embedding application, such as diagnostics delivery, bounded data access or cancellation. This can keep codecs, SDK behavior and adapter logic in one reusable implementation while each host supplies a smaller boundary. Do not turn every library function into a host call.

Support several environments through one pipeline

A first profile could support pure model/value transformations with a small diagnostic interface. An MCK adapter could reuse those libraries and add its exact request/response contract. A workspace-tooling profile could add explicit project-data and artifact-output services. These are candidate compositions, not implemented profiles or finalized names. Start with the smallest profile needed by a real consumer, then add a second to prove the mechanism supports variation.

  1. The caller selects a versioned profile. The planner resolves its base libraries, all supplied modules and referenced dependencies, and matching compiler/core assets.
  2. The compiler checks against the selected host-interface declarations. The linker retains exported handlers, initialization and declared indirect-call roots, and removes unreachable library code where qualified.
  3. The artifact's Ion manifest identifies the profile contract and exact resolved assets, as well as retained exports, imports, target features, codecs and packaging form. Keep contract compatibility separate from concrete artifact identity.
  4. The consumer selects a host implementation supporting that contract and the artifact's actual requirements. Bind only declared and permitted services, then invoke through the chosen operation ABI.
  5. The same artifact can run on another compatible host. Loading, input/output checks, lifecycle handling and resource limits remain shared adapter responsibilities.

Profile versions need explicit compatibility rules. Refuse an unsupported required interface or feature with an actionable diagnostic. Optional extensions must be negotiated before use. Avoid independent flags that allow contradictory ABI, codec or lifetime combinations. Adding a richer profile should leave existing smaller profiles usable. A component/WIT mapping and a core-Wasm byte ABI may implement the same semantic operation, but require their own explicit bindings and qualification.

Where the simplification comes from

Work todayPotential shared implementationChecks that remain
Per-tool build and launch setupOne assembly planner and artifact loader, parameterized by the selected profile and providers.Resolve the complete library graph and validate exact asset compatibility. Package-manager behavior and target-specific dependencies still need implementation.
Repeated codecs and SDK plumbingPortable base-library modules linked into each guest, with tree shaking, or an explicitly qualified shared-provider form.Preserve arbitrary precision, source numeric metadata, annotations and unknown facts. Ion remains preferred; JSON is a supported explicit choice with checked conversions where required.
Separate adapter launchers for many small toolsA reusable launcher/bridge binds a known host interface and calls declared guest exports.Each operation still has an exact contract. MEP and MCK semantics do not appear merely because a module can execute.
Repeated platform integration effortImplement and qualify the profile on each intended host, then reuse it across tools that target it.Retain tool-specific conformance and actual native/browser lifecycle tests. Profile evidence can be reused within its scope; it does not eliminate every combination that changes behavior.

This changes the integration unit to a reusable environment contract. It can simplify model transforms, generators, MCK adapters and automation together. Keep MEP as the shared operation and lifecycle system, MCK as the independent compatibility authority, and the execution profile as the environment an implementation requires. They have different responsibilities.

A focused profile tracer can package a real production codec adapter against one small base-library/host-interface pairing, consume it through the existing MCK executable boundary, and reuse the loader in a second host. A second profile can add one concrete service to prove compatibility checks and provider selection. Reuse the same assembly work as the generated-Morphir-library tracer. Bundled libraries are a sufficient first packaging form; shared runtime/library providers remain separately qualified work.

Next qualification

  1. Advance the supported Morphir model through generated MoonBit, the packaged compiler, a persisted Wasm artifact and fresh-host invocation. Reuse existing providers and make the required dependency graph, codec and invocation contract explicit.
  2. Extend the successful moonx registry command probe to a real formatter/codegen tool and .mbtx task with argv, streams, files, failures and cancellation. Compare process execution with embedding before committing to a runtime dependency.
  3. Use the checked-in callback/resource evidence to choose a bounded production adapter slice. The JS fixtures pass; the pinned native public facade has explicit gaps. Compare a native host with public component callbacks/resources, such as the appropriate Wasmtime embedding API, before making a direct native route a capability claim.
  4. Run the same interface through the intended native CLI host, Workbench worker and Proton adapter. Keep per-host evidence; direct runtime and Node proofs do not qualify all main hosts.
  5. Compare native Wasmoon embedding, the existing canonical Wasmtime-based host, mizchi's C-API binding, and generated JS hosting. Measure representative start-up, memory, repeated calls and artifact/build cost before selection.
  6. Qualify the official Extism C API through a small native MoonBit wrapper and the JS SDK through the intended app adapter, using the same byte/model and lifecycle fixtures. Avoid writing a new Extism host until reuse has a demonstrated gap.
  7. Treat a static MoonBit runtime/program packager as a separate, optional delivery slice. Prove model/SDK compatibility and one chosen invocation ABI before shared runtime providers or snapshots. Signed package and publisher authentication profiles remain independent.

Bead morphir-ukvn.5.55.7 remains in progress. Native source-to-consumer integration and numeric language support can proceed independently.

  • Wasmoon inspected source

  • MoonBit component guest tooling and host example distinctions
  • Official MoonBit component guest tutorial

title: Runtime capability checks for selected Scheme execution
description:
# Runtime capability checks for selected Scheme execution

Implementation of the HTML design on morphir-etg2.6. Approved roadmap: morphir-ukvn. Runtime behavior remains unchanged until the corresponding tasks are implemented and qualified. Strict default and frozen contracts are mandatory.

Canonical HTML plan: .dev/beads-plans/morphir-etg2.16.html. Detailed spec: .dev/beads-specs/morphir-etg2.6.html. Planning task morphir-etg2.6 is separate from this implementation epic. 6 of seven implementation tasks are delivered, 85.7%, with 1 remaining and a 6:1 complete-to-remaining ratio. Desktop Task 5 is merged in MoonBit #136 and Morphir #1061. Connected HTTP Task 6 is next; its strict mapping remains unchanged until independently qualified.
design:
Runtime capability checks for selected Scheme execution

morphir-etg2.16 · 17 October 2026 · 7/7 implementation tasks complete

This is the implementation plan derived from morphir-etg2.6. Planning completion does not establish runtime support. The original 25-task evaluation/execution planning milestone and these seven implementation tasks, including the added breaking terminology migration are different scopes.

  • Shared requirements
  • Task 1: Run a supported function alongside unsupported code
  • Task 2: Report unsupported code only when execution reaches it
  • Task 3: Retain the chosen runtime and checking policy for each execution
  • Task 4: Expose capability checks in the standalone Workbench
  • Task 7: Replace Workbench job terminology with execution
  • Task 5: Carry capability checks through desktop executions
  • Task 6: Carry capability checks through connected executions
  • Desktop qualification
  • Connected checking policies

Shared requirements

Runtime capabilities describe what a particular runtime can execute. Capability verification gathers scoped evidence that an implementation behaves as claimed under an exact contract, implementation version and platform. Contract and MCK test results provide evidence; they are not a formal proof, a claim about every possible input, or validation of business rules.

Capability validation checks whether the selected runtime satisfies the requirements of a particular run, selected function and model revision. Its checking policy determines scope and timing: Whole model before running checks executable support up front; As code executes allows represented unsupported executable semantics to remain dormant and rejects them if reached. Both retain mandatory whole-source integrity, identity and resource checks and the complete selected input/output type closure before execution. Arguments, outputs, receipts and authorization still have their own validation rules.

Provider-authored capability claims remain distinct from verification evidence. An offline MCK adapter claim describes its exact test suite; it is not a live provider/session offer. A successful selected run does not expand the runtime capability set. Changing the checking policy changes when and where requirements are checked.

The earlier capabilities vocabulary change retained compatibility identifiers, including admission, morphir/workbench/admission and AdmissionPolicy. Task 7 is a separately approved breaking pre-1.0 migration to execution terminology. It replaces current job-based APIs and wire contracts without aliases, duplicate fields or compatibility routes. Strict/permissive checking semantics and capability advertisements do not expand as a result.

Latest main integration: PR #127 at 3b7ccd029c89ef5e3fe6173490c97906dfcae6e7 adds native MEP morphir.frontend.compileModel for the existing moonbit-model-bool-library-v1 source profile. Compilation and generation negotiate separate transport tuples; rich Ion preserves source provenance, while lossy JSON export rejects. This is a source-compilation capability, separate from Scheme execution policy and Workbench native/HTTP execution offers. The integration preserved the original six-task sequence; the maintainer has now added Task 7 before the remaining transports; completion checkboxes follow qualified merges. Task 4 retains source-profile-specific UI support; Tasks 5 and 6 now have separately qualified exact policy mappings and end-to-end evidence, recorded below. Merged setup PR #129 at 83283be6f7f761c2b5026f030df7af4e9b86129c also completes pinned Unix installs and adds Linux ARM64 setup qualification. This changes toolchain provisioning, not the remaining UI/policy tasks or packaged-desktop evidence. Local source support also advances through PR #130 at cac8f85f55e80f1c27b5b45137c974530d639179: the Workbench prefers moonbit-model-library-2026-10-17, a dated cumulative Bool/String/Int32 snapshot. Source-profile selection and checking policy remain separate controls. Task 4 must preserve pinned/narrow profiles and drafts, test bounded String/Int32 policy executions and retain the new SDK type checks. Native MEP compilation still advertises its separate Boolean library profile; local UI support never upgrades a remote offer. All integration qualification passes, including the full root check, current browser workflow, 20 worker/provider controls, 124 Node tests, native MEP process/consumer, TypeScript and the independently rechecked six-lane draft.13 corpus. PR #128 and paired #1059 are merged; delivered trees match the qualified sources.

Task 7 selects exact 0.2.0-draft.1 execution, host, native and execution-plan bundles. Replacement MCK drafts14–19 supersede frozen6–10/13. Capability policy 0.1.0-draft.1 and terminal outcomes 0.1.0-draft.5 retain their versions. Tests and historical evidence are qualified separately; only coordinated delivery completes the checkbox.

Strict default; new exact policy-aware profile; complete selected public boundary validation; global framing, identity and resource budgets; stable reached-unsupported failure; immutable submitted policy; actual output and terminal validation. Task 7 publishes and independently qualifies the breaking pre-1.0 execution contract; it removes old job aliases, fields and routes. Historical frozen drafts and qualification records retain their original scope. Existing compiled-target behavior stays unchanged. Only independently qualified runtime/provider/platform combinations are advertised.

Every slice uses focused meaningful red/green tests, the shared Rust MCK runner/checker and regression evidence appropriate to its claim. Tasks 1–2 establish the local semantics; 3–6 add separately qualified integrations; Task 7 migrates their execution vocabulary and contracts before Tasks 5/6. Implementation follows the separately tracked task state. Specs/plans stay local and in Beads, never in a code commit.

Delivery DAG: Task 1 → Task 2 → Tasks 3 and 4 in parallel → Task 7 breaking execution migration → Tasks 5 and 6 in parallel. Each pull request has clear scope and qualification evidence. Keep ordinary Result.Err, SDK model errors, runtime/provider failure, cancellation and cleanup distinct.

100%

All seven implementation tasks are delivered: 7/7, 100%, with 0 remaining and a 7:0 completed-to-remaining ratio. Task 7 migrated the current contracts to execution terminology. Task 5 delivered native checking policies; Task 6 delivers authenticated HTTP checking policies in MoonBit #140 and Morphir #1064. HTTP and native policy mappings use exact 0.2.0-draft.2, with separately qualified transport behavior. The bounded Scheme evaluator remains distinct from compiled targets and native MEP compilation.

Task 1: Run a supported function alongside unsupported code

Type: AFK, subject to existing maintainer merge authority. Blocked by: completion of planning task morphir-etg2.6. Repositories: repo:morphir, repo:morphir-moonbit.

A supported public Int42 entry can be planned and evaluated beside a valid but unsupported unused declaration under an explicit private permissive selection. Omitted and explicit strict keep their existing behavior. This is the first internal tracer; no public runtime capability is advertised yet.

Implementation and integration

Derive public signatures and their complete selected type closure directly from authoritative IR, independently of whole-library generation. Keep the existing compiled Plan and generated driver strict. Introduce a separate bounded Scheme plan with a closed AdmissionPolicy and immutable validated boundary context. Prepare global definitions on demand rather than linking unrelated definitions. Preserve parse/identity/resource checks for the entire source. Author the policy semantics upstream and a complete independently expected narrow draft.11 run-selected-scheme kit for this slice. Future branch cases and full checking-policy qualification use a later new exact kit; never mutate the published draft.11 inventory.

Current source areas:

  • pkgs/morphir-engine/execution/scheme_plan.mbt
  • pkgs/morphir-scheme/backend/selected.mbt
  • apps/morphir-workbench/mck/
  • finos/morphir: spec/workbench/ and crates/morphir-mck/src/workbench/
Acceptance evidence
  • Strict control and permissive Int42 with unused hole, incomplete body and unsupported native declaration.
  • Reject private/missing entry, duplicate identities, wrong arity, invalid selected recursive/custom type closure and exhausted source/input budgets before execution. Empty containers and absent alternatives cannot waive a declared boundary.
  • Run the real production adapter on this slice and the same old exact-version adapters on historical fixtures. Keep new capability advertisement disabled until Task 2 passes the full applicable corpus.

Done when: The internal tracer runs the actual selected plan and evaluator, with hand-authored upstream expectations and no fabricated manifests or placeholder generated libraries.

Task 2: Report unsupported code only when execution reaches it

Type: AFK, subject to existing maintainer merge authority. Blocked by: morphir-etg2.16.1. Repositories: repo:morphir, repo:morphir-moonbit.

The same known unsupported expression succeeds when its branch is not evaluated and fails with failed/evaluate/execution.unsupported_reached when reached. Supported results remain fully typed, and the complete local policy corpus passes independent checking before the local capability is exposed.

Implementation and integration

Lower only explicitly represented unsupported semantic operations to bounded runtime traps at their original evaluation positions. Preserve argument, condition, binding and pattern evaluation order. Never catch arbitrary compiler/parser/limit/provider errors and turn them into traps. Retain safe structural traversal of dormant expressions. Validate every terminal against the captured selected-boundary context through the new policy-aware operation, reusing unchanged codecs without invoking frozen whole-manifest validation on the deferred original model. Publish exact offline MCK 0.1.0-draft.12 with run-capability-policy and independently settled expectations, then qualify the production adapter. Actual execution and supplied-completion validation are explicitly different observation modes; supplied evidence does not execute or authenticate a execution. Keep the Task 1 narrow draft.11 kit immutable.

Current source areas:

  • pkgs/morphir-scheme/backend/emit.mbt
  • pkgs/morphir-scheme/backend/native.mbt
  • pkgs/morphir-engine/execution/
  • pkgs/morphir-execution/
  • apps/morphir-workbench/typed_evaluation.mbt and mck/
  • finos/morphir: new policy schemas, fixed corpus and existing Rust MCK runner/checker
Acceptance evidence
  • Paired conditional, fully applied and/or, first-class and partially applied Boolean operations, pattern guards, unused and reached functions; preserve operator-first and left-to-right argument order, and distinguish an uncalled lambda from an unused eager binding.
  • Constructor metadata and its arity limit, recursive public ADTs, mutual recursion, generic declarations and alias cycles need explicit support/rejection cases. An unrelated unsupported constructor must not fail through eager registration after value bodies are made lazy.
  • External fallback selection: missing native with usable fallback, selected native with an unsupported unused fallback, and a failing selected native with a usable fallback. A native invocation failure never retries fallback.
  • Recursive/custom type closure, wrong returned type, malformed/oversized output, exact integers, Float64 bits, UTF-16, JSON/Ion arguments, SDK model errors and ordinary Result.Err controls.
  • Missing native/external binding, resource limit, malformed IR and provider failure keep distinct stable failure classes. Full ordered terminal inventory, extensions, cancellation and primary/cleanup causes remain validated.
  • Run and independently check the new exact shared kit in supported Node/Chromium/native debug/release lanes, plus frozen draft regressions. Synthetic adapter replay is infrastructure evidence only.

Done when: The full local semantics matrix is qualified, unsupported operations reached at runtime produce the reserved failure, and no frozen contract or old strict path changes.

Task 3: Retain the chosen runtime and checking policy for each execution

Type: AFK, subject to existing maintainer merge authority. Blocked by: morphir-etg2.16.2. Repositories: repo:morphir, repo:morphir-moonbit.

A submitted policy, source, selected entry, arguments, boundary context and evaluator/provider selection are captured once. UI edits, reconnect, claim and replan cannot silently switch an accepted execution to another policy or runtime.

Implementation and integration

Extend immutable Scheme execution state and the actual worker/CLI claim with the effective exact policy. Resolve omission to strict once. Reconstruct only from retained source and policy; verify the retained public boundary context rather than trusting renderer manifests. A replan copies only retained source, suite and policy into fresh execution/snapshot/plan identities; the original execution remains independently claimable once. A changed model or arguments require a new submission. The separate morphir/workbench/job-plan exact 0.1.0-draft.1 projection echoes immutable selection without changing frozen receipts. Workbench MCK 0.1.0-draft.13 run-capability-executions qualifies actual Session traces; isolated-worker acceptance remains separate. Projection-limit failures mean evidence is unavailable, not owner rollback. Decision: morphir-09th. A replacement provider that cannot honor it rejects; no automatic downgrade or duplicate execution. Specify policy echo in a new submission/plan projection. Reuse frozen executions identity and receipt codecs when their shapes need not change; do not add fields to frozen envelopes.

Current source areas:

  • pkgs/morphir-engine/execution/executions/
  • apps/morphir-workbench/executions/scheme_boundary.mbt
  • apps/morphir-workbench/scripts/job-provider.ts and job-worker.ts
  • apps/morphir-workbench/mck/capability-jobs/
  • finos/morphir: spec/workbench/job-plan/draft.1, draft.13 MCK and Rust runner
Acceptance evidence
  • Submit permissive, mutate all caller-owned inputs/defaults, then inspect the actual plan and once-only worker claim; strict omission remains strict after a later default edit.
  • Replan, stale claim, replacement provider, policy mismatch, query/cancel/reconnect, lost reply, cancellation and cleanup outcomes. Verify actual returned values against the immutable accepted boundary.
  • Use the real worker/process boundary as well as fixed shared observations. Controlled completion or receipt replay alone does not prove policy propagation.

Done when: Actual execution execution honors the captured policy and provider; old execution receipt behavior remains unchanged and actual worker evidence accompanies independent MCK checks.

Task 4: Expose capability checks in the standalone Workbench

Type: AFK, subject to existing maintainer merge authority. Blocked by: morphir-etg2.16.2. Repositories: repo:morphir-moonbit.

Explorer and Try Morphir offer an explicit policy choice for a selected public function only when the local evaluator supports it. A known unsupported operation in an untaken branch can evaluate; reaching it produces the existing terminal diagnostic presentation.

Implementation and integration

Reuse the current evaluation components and compact controls. Keep strict selected by default and keep dynamic Scheme/worksheet mode a separate experience. Derive typed-entry availability independently of generated-code success while retaining generation diagnostics and original IR. Preserve fields/JSON/Ion drafts, CodeMirror components, results, bottom-panel diagnostics and navigation. Scope capability to evaluator, selected entry, boundary types and exact profile; a global boolean is insufficient. Preserve the local MoonBit dated cumulative Bool/String/Int32 profile introduced by PR #130, together with pinned/narrow profile selections and their drafts. Source profile and checking policy are independent; do not upgrade a restored draft or accepted execution to the newest profile. Retain canonical SDK Int32 boundary/range checks and bounded UTF-16 String semantics, including shortlex ordering. Native MEP compileModel support from PR #127 remains separately negotiated and does not expand that remote profile. Freeze the submitted policy, show it with the result, and report incompatibility explicitly on restored drafts or runtime changes.

Current source areas:

  • apps/morphir-workbench/typed_evaluation.mbt
  • apps/morphir-workbench/browser/evaluation/
  • apps/morphir-workbench/browser/main.mbt
  • apps/morphir-workbench/browser/contracts.ts
  • apps/morphir-workbench/scripts/elm-workflow.ts and browser acceptance helpers
Acceptance evidence
  • Real Chromium workflows for strict default, opt-in success, reached failure, unsupported selected boundary, JSON/Ion drafts, cancellation, stale results and edits during execution.
  • Compile or import a model whose generation fails but whose selected Scheme boundary is supported; preserve inspectable IR and distinguish generation and evaluation diagnostics.
  • Switch entry, model, experience, provider, source profile and stored draft; no silent policy fallback or profile upgrade. Responsive and keyboard/focus acceptance must keep the existing code area and bottom panel usable.
  • Exercise the dated cumulative MoonBit profile and pinned/narrow profiles with JSON/Ion inputs, String UTF-16 concatenation and shortlex ordering, and canonical Int32 minimum/maximum boundaries. Verify actual strict/permissive executions retain their accepted source/runtime/policy after profile edits; local source support must not enable an unsupported native/HTTP offer.

Done when: The real standalone browser makes only its qualified local claim, with explicit policy and correct results/errors; unsupported runtimes do not offer permissive evaluation.

Task 7: Replace Workbench job terminology with execution

Type: AFK, subject to existing maintainer merge authority. Blocked by: morphir-etg2.16.3, morphir-etg2.16.4. Repositories: repo:morphir, repo:morphir-moonbit.

Current Workbench clients and hosts use execution vocabulary end to end. This is an intentional pre-1.0 breaking migration: old job names, duplicate identity fields, wrappers and routes are removed, with no compatibility aliases or silent fallback.

Implementation and integration

Inventory the current Workbench lifecycle across both repositories and distinguish execution request, accepted execution, operation and invocation. Update domain types, package/API names, identifiers, descriptors, endpoints, capability fields, worker messages, UI, scripts and documentation together. Publish the explicitly identified replacement contract/version and migrate normative profiles, schemas, fixed MCK fixtures and independent expected observations in finos/morphir. Model runtime/session states explicitly using validated identities and closed states; preserve the functional core and imperative shell. Preserve strict defaults, exact provider/runtime/policy negotiation, captured source and arguments, once-only claims, uncertain submission, cancellation, reconnection, stale results, terminal validation, cleanup and release. Historical qualification records stay evidence of their original contracts; they do not qualify the replacement contract.

Current source areas:

  • Workbench execution lifecycle and identity types; engine execution owner and worker
  • Browser, native and HTTP execution clients, providers and transports
  • UI labels, diagnostics, acceptance helpers, scripts and current documentation
  • finos/morphir: normative execution contracts, schemas, fixed MCK fixtures and independent expected observations
Acceptance evidence
  • A current client submits and observes a real execution through the migrated local/native/HTTP paths already supported today; this rename does not advertise pending permissive native/HTTP capabilities.
  • Unknown or old job descriptors, fields and routes are rejected by current replacement interfaces; no old job aliases, duplicate fields or fallback are present.
  • Reconnection observes the same execution; a new accepted request creates a new execution; rejection before acceptance creates none. A lost submission reply remains uncertain and must not trigger an automatic new submission. Preserve once-only claims, uncertain submission, cancellation, stale-result handling and separate cleanup failures.
  • Independently qualify the replacement fixed MCK corpus and exact schemas and run real worker/browser/native/HTTP regressions appropriate to the affected current paths. Preserve historical receipt hashes and qualification scope.

Done when: The breaking execution migration is merged and qualified in both repositories, all current affected consumers and UI use the new contract, the shared tracker and HTML checklists are synchronized, and Tasks 5/6 can build on execution terminology without a second rename.

Task 5: Carry capability checks through desktop executions

Type: AFK, subject to existing maintainer merge authority. Blocked by: morphir-etg2.16.3, morphir-etg2.16.4, morphir-etg2.16.7. Repositories: repo:morphir, repo:morphir-moonbit.

A qualified native Proton session can explicitly negotiate and execute a permissive execution through its owned worker. Task 7 supplies the breaking execution contract; strict remains the default and unqualified combinations reject.

Implementation and integration

Publish a new exact native mapping for the policy descriptor, selected validation and accepted-policy echo. Bind the offer to page/session/provider authority and capture it at submission. Propagate the policy through the actual native Owner, executions Host, claim and worker. Preserve revocation, once-only execution, granted workspace snapshots, cancellation, shutdown, cleanup and opaque identity behavior. Extend independent native boundary/client/owner qualification in new exact MCK contracts without editing their frozen versions. Reuse the merged native MEP source compiler only when its exact transport/profile is negotiated; its compile/generate evidence does not qualify Proton policy executions.

Current source areas:

  • pkgs/morphir-workbench-native/bridge/owner.mbt
  • pkgs/morphir-workbench-native/ execution service and worker modules
  • apps/morphir-workbench/browser/native-session.ts
  • Workbench browser execution client (renamed by Task 7)
  • apps/morphir-workbench/scripts/desktop-test.ts
  • finos/morphir: new exact native mapping and fixed MCK fixtures
Acceptance evidence
  • The replacement execution descriptor rejects retired job names and unknown fields; its exact offer permits only qualified policy/evaluator combinations.
  • Actual packaged Proton execution: untouched unsupported declaration, untaken/taken branch, captured policy after edits, cancellation, navigation/reload/revocation and cleanup.
  • Shared Rust run/check for new mapping and lifecycle observations; real worker claim/exit tests remain separate from controlled IO. Qualify each advertised OS/architecture individually.

Done when: The new native policy works end to end on evidenced packages; controlled MCK or selected-file replay is never substituted for actual OS grant/dialog/platform evidence.

Task 6: Carry capability checks through connected executions

Type: AFK, subject to existing maintainer merge authority. Blocked by: morphir-etg2.16.3, morphir-etg2.16.4, morphir-etg2.16.7. Repositories: repo:morphir, repo:morphir-moonbit.

A policy-aware authenticated HTTP host can advertise and honor an explicit permissive submission. Task 7 supplies the breaking execution contract. Strict-only execution providers keep their explicit support limits without permissive fallback.

Implementation and integration

Publish a new exact HTTP host mapping and implement it in the actual test gateway/provider and client. Capture negotiated policy and provider once before accepting a execution; keep authenticated offers, closed request shapes, byte budgets, uncertain-submit handling and once-only claims. Reuse immutable policy state from Task 3. Native MEP compileModel negotiation is distinct from HTTP execution policy negotiation and must not enable a connected policy offer. A proxy/fake response is not execution evidence. The existing Rust protocol v1 with executions:false remains unchanged; production Rust daemon support requires its own implementation, exact negotiation and independent qualification before being advertised.

Current source areas:

  • Workbench browser execution client (renamed by Task 7)
  • Workbench execution transport (renamed by Task 7)
  • apps/morphir-workbench/scripts/server.ts
  • Workbench execution provider (renamed by Task 7)
  • authenticated browser/Proton execution acceptance helpers
  • finos/morphir: new exact HTTP host mapping and fixed client/host fixtures
Acceptance evidence
  • Actual authenticated request, selected provider execution, retained policy and returned typed terminal across browser and packaged Proton; expired authentication and changed offer cannot mutate an accepted execution.
  • The replacement execution mapping and actual supported daemon regressions qualify independently; unknown or retired profiles/policies/versions reject, absent support disables the UI, and explicit permissive never falls back to strict or another runtime.
  • Lost submit/query replies, reconnect, cancellation, release and cleanup preserve once-only execution and captured selection. Independent fixed mapping tests plus real host/provider logs.

Done when: The qualified HTTP gateway/provider honors the policy; the result identifies that actual host. No Rust v1, generated browser backend or unevidenced platform claim is inferred.

Domain-model correction morphir-etg2.17 is delivered in PR #134, squash 2222c9e. Tasks 5 and 6 retain the runtime/session lifecycle modeling work. Reuse the closed CapabilityPolicy type, decode evaluator identities and exact policy profiles into domain values, and model mutually exclusive runtime/session states explicitly. Keep validation and decisions in a functional core; transport and host effects belong in adapters. The separate Task 7 execution migration intentionally breaks pre-1.0 job-based contracts without compatibility aliases; unrelated historical identifiers remain outside that rename. Correction checklist and findings.

Desktop checking policies: qualified delivery

morphir-etg2.16.5 is delivered in MoonBit #136 and Morphir #1061. This implementation uses exact native 0.2.0-draft.2; the shipped strict mapping and frozen kits remain unchanged. At that desktop delivery completion was 6/7, 85.7%, with a 6:1 completed-to-remaining ratio. The HTTP delivery below completes the seventh task.

Session state retains its exact mapping. Replayed execution or plan identities refuse publication, the renderer checks its 256-execution page budget before submission, and native reply size is reserved before acceptance. HTTP policy adoption remains morphir-etg2.16.6.

Latest main integrates CI optimization #139 at db4c0178. Task 6 uses the current component selection and mise run test:ci policy checks. Shared setup, CI policy and toolchain changes retain full qualification; native policy MCK tasks remain available. Application and protocol sources match the qualified desktop delivery. The final HTTP delivery below completes the implementation plan.

Connected checking policies: qualified delivery

morphir-etg2.16.6 is delivered in MoonBit #140 at b544fc476912 and Morphir #1064 at b0ac9d14cfa7. Both were squash-merged after green CI and addressed comments; merged trees exactly match the qualified heads. The implementation phase is 7/7 complete, 100%, with a 7:0 completed-to-remaining ratio. Exact HTTP host 0.2.0-draft.2 offers the bounded Scheme evaluator and strict/permissive policies. Frozen HTTP 0.2.0-draft.1 remains strict; Rust protocol v1 retains executions:false. Native MEP compilation negotiates independently.

A submission captures the model, arguments, runtime, provider and checking policy before the first asynchronous effect. Acceptance reserves the complete escaped HTTP reply before publication. Reconnect reauthenticates and checks the retained exact descriptor; it cannot submit again or replace the selected plan.

Independent MCK23–25 qualification covers 116 fixed cases, ten debug/release lanes and 406 observations. Frozen MCK14–17/20–21 regressions add 24 lanes and 2,636 observations. All 34 reports were independently rechecked with the final protocol runner. Real Chromium and packaged Proton on macOS Apple Silicon exercised the authenticated gateway/provider, including JSON/Ion, immutable policy and inputs, reached unsupported code, cancellation, reconnect, lost replies and cleanup. The supported Rust daemon authentication, Gleam compilation/generation and workspace regression was tested separately.

Latest main includes the rich-design and beads companion workflow from #138 and the CI selection from #139. Updated CI self-tests and required checks passed. Review fixes enforce UTF-16 attempt-ID limits, export the public version constants, preserve literal JSON observations and keep complete protocol HTML documents. Follow-up morphir-0r6n tracks retirement of the scoped official schema-validator workaround.
