comments.text:
Design note for the explorer, palette, samples, failure details and Ion viewer (copied from the deleted workspace file .superpowers/sdd/explorer/design.md):

# Project explorer, context menu and command palette — design note

Bead: morphir-ukvn.5.22.4.4. Branch `DamianReeves/elm-wiring-projects`.

## Subject, audience, job

The subject is the Try Morphir editor of the Morphir workbench. The audience is a developer who writes Elm, MoonBit or
Scheme source and compiles it to Morphir IR. The job of this change: make the project files feel like a code editor
(VS Code, Zed, JetBrains). Find a file, open it, rename it, delete it and run a command without hunting for small
buttons.

## Visual direction

The explorer belongs to this app. It is not a VS Code skin. It uses the tokens in `workbench.css`:

| Token | Value | Role in the explorer |
|---|---|---|
| `--ink` | `#1c1e21` | labels |
| `--muted` / `--subtle` | `#606770` / `#80868e` | meta text, folder chevrons, shortcuts |
| `--selection` | `#e5f5fc` | active file row, palette option under the cursor |
| `--brand-blue` | `#00a3e2` | 2px inset bar on the active row and the palette option (the `.nav-item.active` device) |
| `--link` / `--link-strong` | `#00729e` / `#005878` | focus ring, fuzzy-match letters |
| `--danger-bg` / `--danger-ink` | `#fef3f2` / `#b42318` | problem counts, delete confirmation |
| `--warn-ink` | `#a34400` | folder icons (as in the generated-files tree) |

Type: the app's system-ui stack at 13px for rows, 12px for meta; no new typeface. Shortcut hints are `kbd` keycaps
(11px, 1px border, 2px bottom border so they read as keys).

The one bold element is the command palette: a sheet that drops from the top bar, with a mode chip ("Go to file",
"Run command", "Switch language") that tells the person what Enter does. The explorer stays quiet: dense 26px rows,
faint indent guides, no hover animation.

Review against the generic default: the first plan put a "PROJECT" eyebrow over the tree. That is a label with no
information, so the header is the package name itself with "Elm · 3 files" under it. The first plan also used a
cream background for the palette; that is a generated-design tell and not this app's palette, so the palette is
`--surface` on the app's `--paper` with the same border and radius as `.panel`.

## Layout

The explorer moves from the left edge of the source panel into the app sidebar, under the experience navigation.
The navigation is the activity bar, the sidebar context is the side bar, and the source panel becomes editor-only, so
the editor gets the full panel width.

```
┌ sidebar ───────────────────┐┌ main ─────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Morphir                    ││ Workbench / Try Morphir           Browser local│
│ ▢ Model Explorer           ││ Try Morphir            [Compile & inspect|WS] │
│ ▣ Try Morphir              ││ Language▾ Sample▾ Profile▾ Target▾  [Compile] │
│────────────────────────────││┌ source ───────────────┐┌ output ───────────┐ │
│ Workbench     [+][⇣][⊟][⋯] │││ src/Workbench/Main.elm ││ Morphir IR  Gen.. │ │
│ Elm · 2 files              │││ 1 module Workbench...  ││                   │ │
│ ⌄ src/Workbench            │││                        ││                   │ │
│     ◆ Main.elm      ↗    2 │││                        ││                   │ │
│     ◆ Broken.elm         1 │││                        ││                   │ │
│                            ││└────────────────────────┘└───────────────────┘ │
│                            ││ ─ panel bar ───────────────────────────────── │
│                            │└───────────────────────────────────────────────┘
└────────────────────────────┘
```

- Header: package name (a button that starts an inline rename when the language keeps packages, plain text
  otherwise), meta line (language and file count), "Not saved" chip when storage fails, and icon actions: New file,
  Import folder, Collapse folders, More actions (opens the root menu).
- Tree: one flat `role="tree"` list. Folders come from paths. Chains of single folders are compacted
  (`src/Workbench` is one row), as VS Code does. Folders sort before files; names sort by code unit.
- Rows: chevron, icon by file type (Elm, MoonBit, Scheme, JSON, other), name, exposed indicator (Elm), problem count.
  Folders show the sum of the problems in their files.
- Reset confirmation and refusals show inline under the tree.
- Worksheet and connected modes show no explorer. The sidebar has no examples list: examples and samples open from the
  command palette and the explorer's project menu (see Samples).
- Below 650px the sidebar is a band above the page (existing rule); the explorer scrolls inside it.

## Interaction model

- Click a file: open it. Click a folder: expand or collapse. Right-click any row: context menu for that row.
  Right-click the empty tree area or "More actions": root menu.
- Inline new file: a row with an input appears at the top of the target folder. The name is relative to the folder
  and can hold `/` to make subfolders. Enter commits, Escape cancels. A refusal shows under the input and keeps it
  open.
- Inline rename: the label becomes an input with the name selected up to the extension. Same keys and refusals.
- Delete: the row becomes "Delete Main.elm?" with Delete and Keep. Delete has focus, so Enter confirms; Escape keeps.
  No browser dialogs anywhere.
- Package name: the header name becomes an input; Enter commits, Escape cancels.
- Expose: the context menu has "Expose module" or "Stop exposing module" for Elm module files. Exposed files show an
  arrow icon with the tooltip "Exposed module".

## Context menu

`role="menu"` with `role="menuitem"` buttons, shown on a transparent backdrop that closes it on any outside click or
right-click. Opens at the pointer, or under the focused row for Shift+F10 / the menu key. The position is clamped to
the viewport by a pure function (fixed row heights make the menu size known).

| Target | Items |
|---|---|
| File | Open, New file (in its folder), Rename (F2), Delete (Del / ⌘⌫), Copy path, Expose / Stop exposing (Elm), Show problems (when it has problems) |
| Folder | New file (in it), Collapse / Expand, Copy path |
| Root | New file, Import folder, Collapse folders, New from sample (a headed section), Rename package (Elm), Reset project, Command palette |

Arrows move (wrapping, skipping separators), Home/End jump, Enter/Space activate, Escape closes and returns focus to
the row, Tab closes. Disabled items stay visible with their reason as a tooltip (the one-file reason names
morphir-ukvn.5.22.14).

## Keyboard map

Mod is ⌘ on macOS and Ctrl elsewhere.

| Keys | Where | Action |
|---|---|---|
| Mod+P | anywhere, also in the editor | Go to file (quick open) |
| Mod+Shift+P, F1 | anywhere, also in the editor | Command palette |
| Mod+Enter | anywhere, also in the editor | Compile (overrides CodeMirror's "insert blank line") |
| ↑ ↓ | tree | previous / next row |
| → | tree | expand folder, or go to its first child |
| ← | tree | collapse folder, or go to the parent folder |
| Home / End | tree | first / last row |
| Enter | tree | open file, toggle folder |
| a–z, 0–9 | tree | jump to the next row whose name starts with the letter |
| F2 | tree | rename |
| Delete, Mod+Backspace | tree | delete (inline confirmation) |
| Shift+F10, ContextMenu | tree | context menu |
| Enter / Escape | inline input | commit / cancel |
| ↑ ↓ PageUp PageDown Enter Escape | palette | move, open, close |

Tree keys never fire while typing in the inline input. Only the three global chords fire in the editor and other
text fields, as editors allow. Menus and the palette show the same chords, from the same keymap table.

## Command palette

- Mod+P opens it empty: quick open over the project's files. Typing `>` (or Mod+Shift+P / F1) switches to commands.
- Fuzzy matching: the letters of the query appear in order in the text, case-insensitively. Score rewards matches at
  the start, after `/ . _ -` and space, at camelCase humps and in runs; it penalises gaps and length. The best
  alignment is found by dynamic programming. A string matched against itself scores at least as high as against any
  other string. Matched letters are drawn in `--link-strong` at weight 650 (no background).
- Commands: Compile, Compile & run / Run worksheet (when available), Go to file, Switch language…, Set generation
  target…, New file…, Rename file…, Delete file, Copy path, Collapse folders, Expose / Stop exposing module, Rename
  package…, one "Open sample: …" entry per sample, Import folder…, Reset project…, Toggle panel, Switch layout, Open Model Explorer / Try
  Morphir. Unavailable commands are hidden; commands that exist but cannot run now are dimmed with their reason.
- With no query, recently run commands come first under "Recently used"; with a query, ties go to recent commands.
- "…" commands open a second list in the same palette (languages, targets), with its own mode chip.
- Keys: ↑/↓ wrap, PageUp/PageDown move by 8, Enter runs, Escape closes and returns focus to where it was, a click on
  the backdrop closes. Choosing a file focuses the editor.
- ARIA: `role="dialog"` with `aria-modal`, the input is a `combobox` with `aria-controls`, `aria-expanded` and
  `aria-activedescendant`; results are a `listbox` of `option`s with `aria-selected` / `aria-disabled`.

## Samples

One list, `sample_entries` in `main.mbt`, feeds both places that open a sample:

- the command palette, one entry per sample: "Open sample: Pricing & arithmetic";
- the explorer's project menu (header ⋯ or a right-click on empty explorer space): a "New from sample" section with
  a heading. Each item's accessible name carries the section ("New from sample: Pricing & arithmetic").

The list holds the four built-in examples for every language, since each opens its own language: Pricing &
arithmetic (Scheme), Elm constant (a Scheme program that targets Elm, so it stays a built-in), MoonBit Boolean and
MoonBit library. While Elm is selected, the Elm corpus samples follow. The worksheet lists only Pricing &
arithmetic, which also resets the worksheet. In a host session or while a job runs, the entries are disabled with
the reason. Every choice is a new sample request, so a late reply for an earlier Elm sample never replaces a later
choice. The sidebar examples list and the toolbar "New from sample" select are gone; they duplicated this list.

## Failure details in the tool panel

A failed compile must be readable where it is reported. Each entry that can fail opens its details in place:

- Diagnostics: every row has a "Details" disclosure after its location. The details list the engine's code, the
  severity, the stage (frontend, generation, or internal with the workbench stage), the location as a button that opens
  the file at that place plus the original coordinates, the full message, related declarations, the suggested fix,
  the job that reported it and that job's context.
- Logs and Output: a failed job (and a compile whose generation was refused) has a "Details" disclosure with the
  code, stage, message, job, language, profile, provider, target, project name and file count, source revision and
  duration. A worksheet shows its revision; an evaluation shows the function, runtime and inputs revision.
- "Copy details" copies a plain-text report for an issue: first "Messages can quote your source.", then one
  `Label: value` line each, then the reply.
- Details ids carry the panel prefix so they cannot clash with other page ids: `tool-details-log-12`,
  `tool-details-diagnostic-4-0`, `tool-details-outcome-9` and `tool-raw-log-12`. The open-state keys stay short.
- "Raw reply" opens the reply JSON, bounded to 8,000 characters. It is an allowlist, not a denylist:
  - Members that hold source, models or values (`content`, `generated`, `irSource`, `sourceUnitIon`, `sourceBase64`,
    `expression`, `text`, `value`, `ir`, `nodes`, `evaluations`, `typedEvaluations`) become
    `<omitted: N characters>` whatever their shape, so an array or an object under one of them goes too.
  - A `source` member stays only when it is a location: an object of numbers with a line and a column.
  - Text under a kept member (`code`, `stage`, `message`, `detail`, `generationMessage`, `path`, `target`,
    `provider`, `profile`, versions, ids and similar) stays at any length. Messages can quote the source line a
    failure points at, and the label says so.
  - Any other text longer than 32 characters becomes its size, at any depth and in arrays. A new member is therefore
    safe until someone adds it to the kept list.
  - The label and the report heading say exactly this: "source, models and values omitted; other text over 32
    characters replaced by its size, except messages, codes and paths".

The codes are the reply's own: engine problem codes, `workbench.invalid_request`, `workbench.invalid_model` and
`workbench.internal_error` for codec errors, which also keep the codec's code and detail. Nothing invents a code.

Design: the details are part of their entry, not a modal. They sit in a quiet `--surface-alt` box set in from the
entry, with a 3px left rule in the severity colour (`--danger-ink` for errors, `--brand-orange` for warnings), a
two-column `dt`/`dd` grid (one column below 650px), the code in the monospace code colour, and the two actions on
one line. Disclosures are buttons with `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls`; at most 50 stay open. The chevron
rotation stops under `prefers-reduced-motion`.

## Generated-file menu and binary Ion

The Generated tab's files open the same context menu as the project explorer: one component
(`browser/context-menu`) places the menu, moves through it with the WAI-ARIA keys and draws it; the explorer and the
generated files keep only their own entries. A file's menu opens on a right-click, on Shift+F10 or the menu key (the
shared keymap), or from the row's ⋯ button, which shows on hover or focus and always on touch screens.

| File | Entries |
|---|---|
| Binary Ion (starts with `E0 01 00 EA`, whatever its name) | View as Ion text, View raw (hex), Copy path, Download |
| Other binary | View as Ion text (disabled: not binary Ion), View raw (hex), Copy path, Download |
| Text | Copy path, Download |

"View as Ion text" runs a job in the worker (operation `decode-ion`): the busy rule, Cancel and late replies work as
for a compile. Each limit stops the work before it grows:
- input: at most 4 MiB, checked on the base64 length before decoding and on the bytes after;
- shape: at most 128 levels of nesting and 100,000 values (annotation wrappers included), the limits of an Ion model
  import, checked by a stack-based walk of the type descriptors before `read_binary` runs, so the reader never
  recurses deep or builds a large tree. The untyped null `0x0F` and typed nulls count as values; only NOP pads
  (type 0 with a length nibble below 0xF) do not. One integer or decimal may hold at most 64 KiB
  (`workbench.ion_number_too_large`), and an annotation wrapper around another is `ion.syntax`;
- output: at most 4 Mi characters, counted while the text is written. `ion_text_within` writes the containers itself
  in the same layout as `write_all_pretty` and every scalar through the library's `write_fragment`, and stops before
  a piece would pass the budget. A long string or blob is refused on its length before its text is built.
A connected workbench does not offer the decode: hosts have no `decode-ion` operation.
The viewer shows the text read-only with Ion highlighting, under a "Decoded Ion text · N values" badge and a "Show
binary summary" button back. A decode error (`ion.syntax`, `ion.data_model`, `ion.unsupported`,
`workbench.not_binary_ion`, `workbench.invalid_encoding`, `workbench.ion_input_too_large`,
`workbench.ion_too_deep`, `workbench.ion_too_many_values`, `workbench.ion_number_too_large`, `workbench.ion_text_too_large`) reaches Logs, Diagnostics and Output with the failure details (file, size, target).
"View raw (hex)" decodes only the first 64 KiB in the page and shows them as 16-byte rows; the size shown anywhere
comes from the base64 length and padding, without decoding. The editor is named "Decoded Ion text: <file>" or "Raw
bytes (hex): <file>" in those views. Download from a file's menu leaves the selection and the view. The palette offers "View as Ion text:
<file>" for the selected file, and the binary summary has a "View as Ion text" button.

Screenshots: `generated-file-menu.png`, `generated-ion-text.png`.

## Accessibility

- Roving tabindex: exactly one tree row has `tabindex="0"` (the focused row, else the active file, else the first).
- Rows carry `aria-level`, `aria-setsize`, `aria-posinset`, `aria-expanded` (folders) and `aria-selected` (the active
  file). The accessible name is the file or folder name; `aria-description` gives the folder, problems and exposure.
- Visible focus: 1px inset `--link` outline on rows, the app's 3px ring on buttons and inputs.
- `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` removes the chevron rotation and the palette entrance.
- Every icon button has an `aria-label` and a `title` that includes its shortcut.

## Architecture

Pure MoonBit, with tests:

- `browser/keys` (new): `Chord` (from a keyboard event, parse, label, `aria-keyshortcuts`), `CommandId`, the keymap
  table with scopes (anywhere / tree) and `resolve`.
- `browser/project-files` (evolved): tree building from paths, row flattening with roll-up counts, keyboard
  navigation and typeahead, the explorer state machine (inline new/rename/delete, package name, exposure, menu),
  menu items and placement. `apply` returns effects (focus a row, focus an input with a selection, focus a menu item,
  copy a path, show problems, import a folder, ask reset) that `main.mbt` turns into commands.
- `browser/command-palette` (new): fuzzy match and segments, the command record and filtering with recency, the
  palette state machine and its view.

JavaScript stays at the edges as inline `extern "js"` helpers in `main.mbt`: one window keydown listener in the
capture phase (prevents the browser's print dialog for Mod+P), focus with selection, remember/restore focus, viewport
size, the anchor of a row for keyboard menus, clipboard. No new files in `dist/`, so the desktop copy is unaffected.

title: P3b: implement MorphirModel SDK and host admission
description: Implement the approved P3b runtime stage after canonical contract #1051 (63563784). Work in independent finos/morphir-rust checkout on latest main 6a481ec; do not edit the umbrella submodule in place. Add typed SDK wire bindings, exact opt-in draft negotiation and frozen bilateral transport context, modelTransport-only static-claim narrowing, explicit rich-method admission, bounded opaque payload retention, and required evidence checks before dispatch. Keep legacy MEP 0.1 and existing JSON behavior. IR 4.0.0 remains draft with its existing wire spelling rules. Generated SDK types #241 remain a separate blocked delivery; never claim handwritten adapters are generated. Use reviewable commits/PRs with TDD and existing native MCK integration, not another compatibility runner.
design:
Skip to specification
Morphir / MoonBit

A2 + F4 integration
Specification revision 0.10
16 October 2026

01 / Outcome and status02 / Current contract evidence03 / Component ownership04 / Guest runtime choice05 / Ion and checked JSON06 / MEP gap analysis07 / MEP call flows08 / Claims and sessions09 / Packaging and installation10 / Implementation slices11 / Acceptance matrix12 / Sources and records
Pluggable library pipeline / extension delivery

Deliver the MoonBit pipeline to an upstream Morphir host.

Package the existing frontend and generator behind a thin extension adapter, retain native Ion models, and prove installation and use through an independently pinned host.

P1/P2 + shared P3 runtime landedLanguage: moonbitNumeric work independentIon preferred; JSON supported

Owned by A2 morphir-ukvn.1.3 and F4 morphir-ukvn.1.10.5. Compatibility study morphir-ukvn.1.3.1. P1 native bundling and P2 installed legacy-backend qualification have landed. P3a landed in canonical PR #1051. P3b SDK/host runtime landed in Rust PR #302, bead morphir-opua.1.3.1.2. Installed MoonBit rich round trips, portable guest qualification and F4 completion remain outstanding.

01 / outcome

Move from an in-process implementation to an installable provider

The local engine and CLI already compile Boolean MoonBit libraries, retain source and naming metadata, evaluate them, and generate callable libraries. F4 makes that functionality available through the ecosystem extension lifecycle. It uses the same pure components; it does not create a second compiler.

First useful installed flow

  1. Build and bundle a pinned MoonBit guest.
  2. Publish to a controlled test extension index.
  3. Install into an isolated upstream MORPHIR_HOME.
  4. Negotiate an existing Boolean library profile.
  5. Compile source into a rich MorphirModel, then generate a library.
  6. Compile and invoke a consumer; retain origins and exact evidence.

Separate completion states

The native bundler landed in Morphir #1050 at d74a506a; the MoonBit native backend landed in MoonBit #107 at 1f91ec2. Numeric implementation belongs to issue #98. Neither completes F4.

A2 supplies a reusable language-neutral packaging contract. F4 supplies the MoonBit guest and installed acceptance. B2/B3 retain the WIT/component roadmap. A native proof does not complete those component milestones.

Remaining integration gap. Language-neutral native bundling and an installed MoonBit legacy backend are implemented. The canonical model contract has landed. SDK and shared host transport/admission landed in PR #302; the MoonBit rich adapter and installed qualification remain to be implemented. An ordinary MoonBit WASM build and an extra JSON response member do not close those gaps.

02 / pinned evidence

Distinguish existing contracts from proposed additions

BoundaryObserved nowRequired integration
Upstream hostprocess channels use Content-Length-framed JSON-RPC. wasm uses Extism and requires its guest ABI.Choose and qualify the actual guest adapter. Keep runtime identity independent from artifact acquisition.
WASM ABIThe host calls morphir_extension_info and handle. The Rust SDK generates Extism exports.A MoonBit WASM adapter needs its own proven Extism imports, exports, memory and session behavior. WASI or Wasm-GC output is not that proof.
Native bundlingmorphir extension bundle accepts explicit executable, identity, version and native platform inputs; it probes exact bytes and stages an atomic three-file bundle without Cargo assumptions.P1 landed in #1050. Runtime/platform expansion and complete A2/F4 acceptance remain separately scoped.
VersionsFrozen legacy MEP 0.1; model-operation draft 0.2.0-draft.1; envelope 0.1.0-draft.1; claims 0.1.0-draft.2; bundle 2.0.0-draft.2.New model methods require the exact full-SemVer draft and bilateral tuple agreement. Contract declarations do not establish runtime support.
Compile resultThe compiled SDK probe drops an unrecognized top-level unit member during typed round trip.Define and negotiate explicit model operations in the canonical model, SDK, host and guest. Do not rely on unknown-field survival.
OptionsCompile vendor profile options and opaque generation option values survive SDK serialization.This permits explicit profile selection, but does not prove host propagation or authorize an undocumented metadata tunnel.
Request IDsThe SDK accepts unsigned numeric IDs; it rejects a string ID even though the canonical model includes string IDs.Test against the pinned SDK subset and separately resolve the model/implementation discrepancy before claiming general ID support.

Rust source snapshot 6a481ec17cf75d889ad363b008ece2ba0ea6e05f; ecosystem specification snapshot 5975da737b210c958ef57114a78dc6830bf67559; MoonBit work snapshot 9cf80a00ec694460c61e4bf16996cf67ee90aac5. The SDK probe uses Rust 1.98.1 and compiles actual source from the pinned archive. It does not activate a host.

Probe artifacts: SDK observations, MoonBit data-boundary observations, and primary evidence in Ion text. Binary Ion is the primary stored receipt. Exact code, lock and result digests are in that receipt.

03 / composition

Keep transport and distribution outside the pure pipeline

ComponentOwnsContract
Build driverPinned compiler/core, dependency trees and selected target; produces immutable guest bytes.Build identity is separate from extension capabilities. No registry download is hidden inside compilation.
A2 packagerArtifact inventory, hashes, actual guest describe probe, descriptor checks and atomic local staging.Receives explicit build/version inputs. Does not fabricate claims or require a Rust source layout.
HostResolve/install/activate, identity and capability checks, operation admission, process lifetime, workspace writes.Only invoke after negotiation. Local source-provider authentication and naming authority remain explicit.
Guest transportBounded frames, JSON-RPC envelope, lifecycle state, dispatch, diagnostic mapping and payload codecs.No logs on protocol stdout. The transport owns I/O and passes values into pure APIs.
Pure frontend and generatorParse, resolve, check, lower, metadata production and IR-to-artifact generation.Reuse existing library APIs and limits. No filesystem, host resolution or implicit executable lookup.
Model payload codecValidate negotiated profile, identity, size, digest and Ion envelope; check JSON loss.Unknown node metadata survives. Metadata cannot register behavior or grant host privileges.
04 / runtime

Propose a native process first, retain a portable guest path

Native backend adapter landed

The MoonBit native MEP process entry point is implemented for the legacy backend flow. Its build/bundle tasks use explicit platform artifacts and preserve identity/capability checks. Rich frontend/model methods follow shared SDK/host adoption; each platform still requires its own qualification.

A process keeps the ambient OS rights of its user. Clearing its environment is not a sandbox. Pure compiler boundaries remain valuable, but must not be advertised as process isolation. Network access, workspace reads and provider authority are not granted by annotations.

Portable core WASM, after an ABI proof

Implement or select a MoonBit Extism adapter only after a real host can call both required exports, exchange UTF-8 bytes, preserve session state and enforce budgets. Probe memory/import compatibility, error propagation and repeated calls. Keep that adapter replaceable; a native first delivery does not remove it from the roadmap.

Component-model target remains separate

B2 morphir-ukvn.2.2 defines MEP as WIT; B3 morphir-ukvn.2.3 proves component extensions. Both are open. The current host describes Extism, not a WIT/component runtime. Preserve those milestones and their acceptance; do not relabel an Extism or process artifact as a component.

The runtime selector remains process or wasm where those are the upstream contract values. Language remains moonbit; the generated target remains moonbit. Library/profile capabilities are separately negotiated. Production guest and package entry-point names will be fixed in the implementation plan.

05 / data preservation

Negotiate native models explicitly

Use model for the logical value and envelope for its representation

TermMeaning in this design
Compilation unitThe complete source set compiled together for one Morphir package, with explicit package and dependency context. Existing MEP CompileRequest.sources supplies that source set.
DistributionThe semantic Morphir package representation and dependency information. Library, specification and application retain their existing meanings.
Morphir model / MorphirModelThe complete identified logical pipeline value: a versioned distribution plus metadata, annotations and provenance. This is what components exchange and the host retains.
Model envelope / ModelPayloadThe storage or transport representation of a model, with the selected format, length, digest and other required envelope fields. Ion and JSON are format choices, not different logical identities.

Accepted terminology for the proposed public contract is MorphirModel, morphir.frontend.compileModel and morphir.backend.generateModel. Compile consumes a compilation unit and returns a model; generation consumes a model and returns artifacts. The model also remains useful for transformations, validation and evaluation.

Current implementation mapping. The existing MoonBit engine type is data.IRUnit. The public contract uses MorphirModel as the domain name; IR describes its underlying semantic representation. Its current Ion profile uses contract: "ir-unit" and unit_id. Those existing API and stored-format names remain accurate in source references and historical probe evidence. This design adopts the public model vocabulary; any implementation rename needs a separate source-compatibility and stored-format migration decision. New method and wire-field spellings require upstream agreement.

JSON-RPC may remain the control protocol while a negotiated payload carries binary Ion. The logical pipeline value is a MorphirModel with distribution, node metadata, ordered annotations and provenance. Preserve exact integers, Decimal scale, unknown neighbors and original naming facts.

Legacy operations retain their current JSON IR fields.
MEP 0.2.0-draft.1 model operations carry:
  MorphirModel {
    envelopeVersion: "0.1.0-draft.1",
    modelId, revision, irVersion, profile,
    payload: {
      codec, layout: "single-document",
      decodedByteLength, sha256, content: BASE64
    },
    evidence, critical
  }
Profiles first registered by the draft:
  morphir-model + ion-binary → complete IR, enrichments and provenance
  morphir-ir + morphir-json → checked, lossless plain IR
The logical revision is distinct from the exact payload-byte digest.

The canonical contract slice defines these fields and wire mappings. They are draft declarations; SDK/host implementation and executable conformance follow separately.

  1. Host and guest both advertise and understand the same model transport contract. Required/critical members must fail on older readers rather than be ignored.
  2. The admitted profile, codec, envelope revision and IR version form one supported tuple, frozen for the operation. No retry silently substitutes JSON after an Ion refusal.
  3. Validate frame size before allocation, base64 expansion and decoded byte length before parsing, then SHA-256, envelope identity and tree limits.
  4. Decode to the current engine representation and call the existing pure APIs. Return artifacts and structured diagnostics; the host decides when to write them.
  5. For legacy JSON, use the checked codec. A rich source-produced model that cannot be exported fails with the existing data.lossy_conversion diagnostic. Do not strip metadata to make a legacy host appear compatible.

Backward compatibility. Existing JSON IR backend requests remain supported where they are lossless. A legacy host may exercise that backend path, but it cannot be described as supporting rich MoonBit frontend round trips. An opaque generation option surviving serialization is not a negotiated transport.

Model variants and checked states evolve independently

A pipeline enriches a Morphir model through explicit transitions. Reuse the existing Distribution variants for library, specification and application content. Represent established guarantees through checked states or views, with runtime evidence at configurable component and MEP boundaries. A single parsed/resolved/typed/validated/optimized enum would conflate independent properties and imply one fixed pipeline order.

DimensionDesign direction
Structural variantA sum type describes mutually exclusive content shapes. Reuse existing semantic variants instead of repeating them in an outer model tag.
Established guaranteesType-state or checked views expose prerequisites established for a particular model revision and context. Several guarantees can hold together.
EnrichmentsExtensible facts carry origins, naming, source number precision and analysis results. Rich facts and proven guarantees have different admission semantics.
RepresentationIon, JSON and document-tree choices belong to model envelopes. They do not define semantic model states.

Each component declares what it requires, establishes, preserves and invalidates. Evidence identifies the model revision, dependency context, scope and producer. A structural rewrite may invalidate type or analysis evidence, even when it retains source metadata. Preservation must follow an explicit component contract; it cannot be assumed from a stage label such as optimized.

Within an implementation, checked constructors or views can enforce component prerequisites. Across MEP, received state labels and evidence are claims until the host admits them under its checking and trust policy. An unknown required guarantee prevents invocation; an opaque optional enrichment can remain preserved. Language-level extensibility does not replace protocol negotiation or grant authority. The P3 canonical draft now defines envelope/evidence wire fields. Checked constructors, trust policy and component-level invalidation remain implementation work.

Toolbelt option: MoonBit non-exhaustive enums

Awareness only; no adoption decision. MoonBit documents #non_exhaustive for library enums that may gain constructors in later releases. External matches handle the known cases and include Type::.. for future cases. It may help an intentionally evolving public variant boundary. MoonBit documentation.

Keep this distinct from extenum, which permits constructor contributions from other packages. Neither feature automatically supplies unknown-wire-value preservation or evidence of a model guarantee. The referenced documentation is the nightly edition; verify the intended behavior against our pinned MoonBit 0.10.15 before selecting it. This note requires no compiler upgrade and does not mark any current enum non-exhaustive.

06 / protocol analysis

Extend MEP at the model and negotiation boundaries

The flow needs shared contract edits. The existing lifecycle, framing, diagnostics and binary artifact representation are reusable. A rich frontend result, however, cannot reach generation through today's typed operation fields. Advertising Ion support alone does not change those fields.

Recommended direction. Add model-specific compile and generate operations, bilateral format/profile negotiation, and host admission for their selected tuple. Preserve the existing JSON operations. Reconcile the version documentation before publishing the contract change.

Change the canonical model first

The canonical MEP contract names spec/mep/contract/src/mep.gleam as its source of truth. Its compiled spec/mep/generated/mep.ir.json is the input for future language bindings, JSON Schema and WIT. Those generators and the conformance kit remain follow-up work. Editing draft prose or hand-written Rust types alone would leave the shared contract inconsistent.

AreaDecision for this flowWhere work belongs
Rich model payloadRequired addition. Carry a complete MorphirModel through compile result, host retention and generate input, including unknown metadata and ordered annotations.Canonical model and IR; SDK operation types; host storage/dispatch; MoonBit adapter.
NegotiationRequired addition. Exchange host offers and guest support; admit a supported combination of profile, codec, envelope revision and IR version. Treat absent offers as legacy-only.Initialization model, capability semantics and operation admission. Avoid independent lists that imply unsupported combinations.
Capability retentionImplementation work plus explicit model additions. Root extension capability extras survive; nested frontend profile members and a proposed host initialization offer do not survive today's typed SDK.Typed bindings and their preservation tests. Raw claim retention is insufficient.
IDs, progress and cancellationAlign implementations with existing contract declarations. These are not new MEP concepts.SDK request IDs, notification demultiplexing, guest cancellation polling and terminal-response handling.
Artifacts and diagnosticsReuse existing binary artifact content and structured diagnostics. Use warning codes, messages and related locations for naming recovery. RpcError.data can carry structured refusal details.Adapter mapping and tests. Translate parser offsets to zero-based UTF-16 diagnostic positions.
Bundling and executionLanguage-neutral build inputs, process artifacts and Extism ABI qualification remain separate from operation payload design.A2 distribution and runtime adapters. B2/B3 retain WIT/component obligations.

Keep JSON operations stable; add lossless model operations

The P3 canonical draft registers morphir.frontend.compileModel and morphir.backend.generateModel under exact MEP 0.2.0-draft.1. It reuses source sets, package context, diagnostics and artifact results. Rich dependencies carry model envelopes. A successful compile requires a model; a failed compile forbids that member, including null. The canonical contract landed without SDK/host runtime changes. PR #302 implements opt-in dispatch and admission in the shared Rust SDK and host.

The historical probe shows that adding an unknown unit member to a legacy compile result loses it in the SDK. Replacing the required ir member of a legacy generate request fails decoding. A union inside the old methods would change those requirements and needs a separate breaking-change assessment. The additive method family avoids changing existing JSON callers. Future validators and transforms should share the model payload type when their contracts are designed; do not advertise them early.

The host still composes the pipeline. Each request names a component operation. No monolithic pipeline-execution method is needed. A JSON-only backend can consume a checked, lossless projection when available; rich models retain the existing data.lossy_conversion refusal when that projection is impossible.

Select a tuple before invoking a component

  1. Describe declares supported model operations and exact supported tuples. The language is moonbit; a Boolean-library profile describes capabilities separately.
  2. Initialize carries optional host modelTransport offers; negotiated capabilities return optional guest modelTransport support restricted to the offered tuples. Each includes complete tuples, limits and interpreted guarantee IDs. Freeze the admissible set for the session. Missing offers mean legacy-only; support for a guarantee ID does not establish it.
  3. Each model operation selects one tuple from that set. Validate the method, profile, codec, envelope revision, semantic IR version and limits together before invoking pure compiler APIs.
  4. The host retains the resulting model and its identity. It forwards the complete payload to the next admitted consumer. If that consumer has no compatible tuple, refuse that handoff without dropping metadata.

New-draft admission rules. A selected modelTransport may narrow the extension's static claims: tuples and interpreted guarantee IDs are subsets of both claims and host offers, and selected limits cannot exceed either. This is a specific exception for the new exact MEP draft; legacy capability equality remains unchanged. The current SDK claim/session checker still compares arrays and scalar values exactly and requires follow-up alignment.

The selected operation tuple authorizes compileModel or generateModel. Frontend language/source-count and backend target capabilities still apply. Legacy compile/generate booleans authorize their legacy methods; they do not force a rich-only provider to advertise unsupported legacy operations.

The payload identifies its envelope contract revision, semantic IR version, logical model ID, codec, decoded byte length, digest and encoded content. For JSON-RPC, binary Ion bytes use base64; future WIT uses a byte sequence. The digest binds the exact payload bytes after base64 decoding and before profile parsing, not the base64 spelling or semantic equivalence between codecs. Model identity and logical revision remain separate. Verify consistency with the decoded envelope and negotiated tuple. Compression, chunking and out-of-band file references are not prerequisites for this first flow.

Aggregate budgets. maxEncodedBytes and maxDecodedBytes bound the sum of all model, dependency and evidence payloads in one request or response, as well as each payload. Encoded bytes count base64 content; decoded bytes count the resulting bytes. maxDepth applies to each decoded document with its root at depth one; maxNodes bounds total decoded value nodes. Many small evidence entries cannot bypass the operation's budget. Independent frame/parser bounds still apply before allocation.

Transport preservation and transformation semantics differ. A forwarding host must retain unknown facts exactly. A transform must declare what it changes, retain unrelated metadata, and record lineage or invalidate facts whose owners it replaces. Source number precision and original/target naming can travel as metadata without granting provider authority or changing the consumer's numeric semantics.

Critical members must identify the feature actually required

The claim reader rejects an unknown exact critical path. Marking only capabilities or capabilities.frontend as critical does not make unknown children understood. Register the precise model-contract requirement and its validation semantics. Older readers must reject a guest that requires it; an optional model feature may remain unavailable while legacy operations still work.

Claim/session agreement permits a session to omit unselected capabilities. Keep that behavior. Model admission must independently require explicit selected support. A requires.host version comparator is useful for known implementation requirements, but cannot substitute for negotiating the feature.

Host / guest combinationRequired result
Old host / new guest with optional model featureUse existing JSON operations only when the guest supports them and the conversion is lossless.
Old host / guest requiring model featureReject the precise unknown critical requirement before component execution.
New host / old guestNo model offer means legacy-only. The host must not infer Ion support from an extension version.
Both support models, but no matching tupleRefuse the operation or next handoff with the requested and supported combinations. No silent JSON retry.
Both support the same tupleValidate bounds, digest and envelope; preserve the model through host retention and consumption.
Unknown vendor methodKeep generic extension routing. Add explicit admission for standardized model methods without rejecting every vendor method.

Apply the accepted SemVer decision

The accepted SemVer decision governs the next MEP change. The prior README's no-prerelease/major.minor-only proposal is superseded for the new draft: rich model operations select full SemVer 0.2.0-draft.1 exactly. Legacy 0.1 remains frozen and supports the unchanged JSON methods; it never authorizes a model method. Future implementations may offer both versions.

The independent MorphirModel envelope starts at 0.1.0-draft.1 and also matches exactly. The fixtures target semantic IR 4.0.0. IR 4 remains a draft: the accepted input spelling formatVersion: "4.0.0" is distinct from the current canonical JSON writer's integer 4. This work does not introduce IR 4.1, add a prerelease suffix to IR formatVersion, change the support table or stabilize IR. Positive JSON fixture checks reuse the existing IR codec and reference support table; they do not implement MEP admission. Claims, bundle, IR, envelope and SDK package versions remain independent. Even an optional Rust struct field can affect source compatibility for callers using struct literals.

What this P3 contract slice establishes

Canonical source spec/mep/contract/src/mep.gleam, regenerated Morphir IR, normative wire mapping and 35 fixed reference cases under spec/mep/mck/. The opaque rich profile contains a complete semantic IR, unknown enrichments and provenance. Existing IR Distribution owns the structural sum. Evidence binds modelId, modelRevision, contextDigest and scope, and becomes an admitted guarantee only under the host's checking/trust policy.

The expanded SDK/host probe passes all 14 assertions against pinned source. Its expected outcomes include present gaps. This verifies serialization and transport-neutral admission helpers, not installed execution.

07 / message sequences

Follow the changes through the MEP lifecycle

These design sequences connect the proposed model operations to extension discovery, initialization, host orchestration and shutdown. They are not traces of an implemented guest. The first delivery uses the existing process binding; Extism uses the same message contract behind its own ABI. WIT remains a separate binding milestone.

Read the labels. E marks an existing MEP contract or value type. P marks a proposed wire addition or admission rule. L marks a local host, adapter or pure-library action. A marks implementation alignment with an existing declaration. Labels remain meaningful without color.

Existing MEP declarations do not imply every pinned host path implements them. In particular, morphir.initialized is defined, but the pinned JSON-RPC host currently becomes ready after checking the initialize response without sending that notification. Its emission belongs in the host-alignment work. The canonical P3 draft registers compileModel, generateModel and MorphirModel. The sequences define the required end-to-end flow. The shared runtime implements the P3b subset; the MoonBit adapter and installed rich path remain subsequent work.

Admission wraps every component call

The host verifies installed bytes before activation, then checks claims and initialization agreement. Describe may run in a separate probe lifetime. Proposed model offers extend initialization; they do not replace MEP version negotiation. Unsupported critical requirements stop admission before compiler execution.

08 / admission and lifecycle

Claims describe supported behavior; initialization locks it

Describe must be side-effect free. Package the guest's actual claim set and verify its ID, version, capability kinds, language, extensions, targets, IR versions and required transport against the declared release inventory. Capability declaration, host probing and semantic qualification remain separate evidence levels.

Start with the existing seed and Boolean library profile contracts. Do not advertise numeric source support, inference, recursion, multiple source documents or incremental compilation simply because the generator or SDK has related functionality. A legacy backend may use a documented vendor option. Rich model operations use the shared tuple admission proposed above.

New → describe / initialize → Ready → shutdown → Draining → exit → Stopped
Operations before initialization or after shutdown are refused.
Identity/capability mismatch prevents the first compiler or generator call.

FramingContent-Length is the UTF-8 byte count. Accept supported headers, refuse duplicate/missing/invalid length and oversized messages. Never emit human logs on stdout.

The proposed common bundle command receives a declared extension identity/version, immutable artifact paths and a pinned host/probe. title: Decide whether Elm declaration origins become the default
description:
Elm declaration origins are opt-in per project (`frontend.profile = "library-origins"`) because the default Morphir JSON checkpoint of a `morphir.json` project refuses unit metadata (`data.lossy_conversion`) instead of dropping it.

Options:
1. Keep the opt-in profile (current behaviour).
2. Make origins the default and let the Morphir JSON checkpoint drop hint-only metadata with a warning, as Plan B of `morphir-ukvn.5.22.4` did for Scheme before `morphir-ukvn.5.40`.
3. Make origins the default only for the `scheme`, `moonbit` and Ion checkpoint backends.

Maintainer decision. Context: finos/morphir-moonbit#108, spec `.dev/beads-specs/morphir-ukvn.5.40.html` section 5 (amended).

title: Elm frontend: declaration origins for unit metadata
description:
Record declaration origins in the Elm frontend so Elm units carry real metadata for the Scheme sidecar and source comments (spec section 5, `.dev/beads-specs/morphir-ukvn.5.40.html`).

- `pkgs/morphir-elm/frontend`: `compile_project_output` returns the IR plus one `DeclarationOrigin` per value declaration the output keeps: the Elm spelling, the source path, the range of the name, and the lifted parameters with their ranges. `compile_project` is unchanged.
- `pkgs/morphir-engine/elm`: a second profile, `library-origins` (`frontend.profile = "library-origins"`), attaches them as `value:<fqname>` metadata (`declaration` and `parameters` hints, `coordinate_profile` `elm-syntax-position-v1`, workspace-relative paths) plus a `morphir_elm_frontend` provenance record. The default `library` profile carries none, because a Morphir JSON checkpoint (the default for a `morphir.json` project) cannot carry unit metadata.

Added during execution of `morphir-ukvn.5.40`; the user chose to file it as a third task.

A selected modelTransport may narrow the extension's static claims: tuples and interpreted guarantee IDs are subsets of both claims and host offers, and selected limits cannot exceed either. The payload identifies its envelope contract revision, semantic IR version, logical model ID, codec, decoded byte length, digest and encoded content. Model identity and logical revision remain separate. Verify consistency with the decoded envelope and negotiated tuple. Compression, chunking and out-of-band file references are not prerequisites for this first flow.

Aggregate budgets. maxEncodedBytes and maxDecodedBytes bound the sum of all model, dependency and evidence payloads in one request or response, as well as each payload. Encoded bytes count base64 content; decoded bytes count the resulting bytes. maxDepth applies to each decoded document with its root at depth one; maxNodes bounds total decoded value nodes. Many small evidence entries cannot bypass the operation's budget. Independent frame/parser bounds still apply before allocation.

Transport preservation and transformation semantics differ. A forwarding host must retain unknown facts exactly. A transform must declare what it changes, retain unrelated metadata, and record lineage or invalidate facts whose owners it replaces. Source number precision and original/target naming can travel as metadata without granting provider authority or changing the consumer's numeric semantics.

StagingVerify hashes and inventory, then atomically stage descriptor, artifact and checksum files. Refuse conflicting existing output, unsafe entries and partial success. P1 supplies a native process packager independently of the historical WASM helper.
InstallationUse a controlled extension index and isolated MORPHIR_HOME. Publish/install an extension identity, not a raw executable, WASM path or arbitrary URL.
ActivationVerify installed record, lock, digest, platform, execution arguments and claims before running guest code. Reject guest initialization that differs from the installed identity or negotiated capabilities.
PublicationLocal bundle creation and controlled local-index acceptance are implementation work. Public tags, releases and irreversible publication require the maintainer's separate approval.

Implementation ownership stays explicit: common Rust distribution/SDK/host changes belong in finos/morphir-rust; umbrella CLI and shared protocol/schema changes belong in finos/morphir; MoonBit guest, build tasks and local acceptance belong here. Completion in one repository does not close the others.

10 / delivery

Land independently reviewable slices

C0 / PR #100

Parallel qualification

Split generated-library and Boolean frontend suites from native acceptance, keep both under ci-ok, preserve evidence and prove execution on fresh runners. Both new jobs passed in the PR run; remaining CI and merge approval are separate.

P0 / this compatibility study

Freeze the contracts and prove the data gap

Record pinned source evidence, compile SDK carrier probes, compile actual Boolean source through Ion replay and checked JSON export, and validate the architecture artifact. Include the expanded MEP gap analysis and 14 SDK/host assertions. This is evidence for the next slices, not an extension implementation.

P1 / A2 · landed #1050

Bundle native executables without Cargo assumptions

Canonical CLI native bundling landed at d74a506a. It snapshots and probes exact executable bytes, validates identity/version/platform and atomically stages descriptor, executable and checksum. The native slice leaves wider A2 runtime coverage open.

P2 / F4 guest · landed #107

Run the native MoonBit backend through MEP

Native adapter, bounded framing, describe/lifecycle, checked legacy JSON generation and build/bundle tasks landed at 1f91ec2. Installed Boolean consumer qualification and binary Ion artifact-sidecar preservation establish the native backend subset; they do not establish rich model frontend transport or F4 completion.

P3a / canonical contract · in progress

Specify model operations before runtime adoption

Bead morphir-opua.1.3.1.1 covers full-SemVer draft selection, explicit MorphirModel fields, reusable context/types, bilateral tuples and limits, evidence scope, regenerated canonical IR and 35 fixed reference cases. It changes no SDK/host runtime and makes no portable-guest or F4 claim.

P3b / SDK + host · next

Implement negotiation, retention and admission

Add the agreed bindings and host/guest offer handling. Check exact drafts/tuples, enforce bounds before allocation and parse, preserve opaque payload bytes, and admit required evidence under checking policy. Extend native MCK host/guest qualification through the existing runner.

P3c / MoonBit adapter · after shared runtime

Expose the rich frontend and model generator

Consume the agreed SDK/host contract, retain Ion enrichments and naming provenance, and keep checked JSON compatibility explicit. Qualify each implemented method before advertising it.

P4 / installed qualification

Prove local index, install, compile and generation

Use independently pinned host bytes and fresh installation state. Exercise seed/library profiles, naming, pure components, generated consumers, metadata replay and failure behavior. Record each repository's actual commit range and each supported OS/target/mode separately.

Portable route / B2 and B3 remain open

Qualify the agreed WASM or component adapter

Run a real Extism ABI spike before choosing that adapter. Follow B2/B3 for WIT/component integration. Native-process qualification does not waive an agreed portable-guest acceptance requirement. Close F4 only against the agreed A2 transport and full installed evidence.

11 / completion evidence

Require an installed round trip, including refusals

GateRequired evidence
BundleExact bytes, compiler/dependency identities, platform inventory and claims; reject tamper, wrong version/profile/platform, unknown critical claims and conflicting output.
Host independenceThe accepted upstream binary/source revision and executable hash are pinned separately from the MoonBit checkout. Installation state is fresh and isolated.
ProtocolHandshake state, malformed/oversized/split frames, Unicode byte counts, repeated requests, identity mismatch, supported ID behavior, shutdown and timeout/cleanup. Logs never corrupt frames.
SourceAll advertised seed/library Boolean rows, private entries, lets/calls, naming collisions, original/target names, stable diagnostics and source origins. No numeric profile claim.
MEP compatibilityAll combinations in the MEP matrix; exact critical-leaf rejection; omitted offers; unsupported tuples; capability preservation; JSON legacy compatibility; payload bounds/digest mismatch; canonical IR regeneration and drift checks.
MetadataHost compile → retained model → generation preserves original annotations, provenance, declaration/body owners and unknown neighboring Ion facts. Lossy JSON refuses before publication.

OperationsCancellation/timeout, operation budgets, rejected output paths, failed sinks and cleanup do not publish partial success. Optional instrumentation preserves results.
LandingRepository checks, exact-head CI and required merge-queue checks pass. Track common contract changes and MoonBit integration separately; releases require approval.

description:
### Task 9: Import a local folder

**Files:**
- Modify: `apps/morphir-workbench/browser/project-io.js`, `project-io.test.js`
- Modify: `apps/morphir-workbench/browser/main.mbt` ("Import folder" button, drop zone, `Msg::FolderPicked`, `Msg::FolderImported`)

- Modify: `apps/morphir-workbench/scripts/elm-workflow.js`

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: Task 3 `import-folder`; Task 2 `Project::from_request`.
- Produces:
  - `project-io.js` exports:
    - `readFiles(fileList, limits)` → `{ ok: true, files: [{path, content}] }` or `{ ok: false, message }`; uses `webkitRelativePath || name`; skips files over 1 MiB and files that are not valid UTF-8 text (`new TextDecoder('utf-8', { fatal: true })`), counting them in `skipped`; stops with an error past `limits.files` (2,000) or `limits.bytes` (16 MiB) before reading more.
    - `pickFolder(receive)`: an `input type=file webkitdirectory` click; calls `receive(JSON.stringify(await readFiles(input.files, LIMITS)))`.
    - `watchDrop(selector, receive)`: on `dragover` (preventDefault) and `drop` on the element, walks `DataTransferItem.webkitGetAsEntry()` directories recursively into a file list (same limits), then `receive(...)`.
  - Main: "Import folder" (button) and a drop zone (the file list area, `data-drop="project"`); a received file list is sent to the worker as `import-folder`; the reply's project replaces the Elm project (`Project::from_request`), its warnings and `skipped` count go to the panel, and the language switches to Elm. A failure notes the message and keeps the project. The native "Open workspace" button of the desktop app stays as it is.

### Task 4: Sample assets and their freshness check

**Files:**
- Create: `scripts/workbench-samples.mbtx`
- Create (generated): `apps/morphir-workbench/assets/samples/elm/index.json`, `.../elm/examples-tutorial.json`, `.../elm/elm-rentals.json`, `.../elm/records.json`
- Modify: `.config/mise/config.toml` (task `workbench:samples`), `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (step in job `elm-scheme`), `apps/morphir-workbench/scripts/build.js` (copy `assets/samples` recursively to `dist/samples`)
- Modify: `apps/morphir-workbench/README.md`

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: the Elm corpus `pkgs/morphir-elm/conformance/projects/<id>/` (`morphir.json`, `src/**/*.elm`) and the origin and license rows of `pkgs/morphir-elm/conformance/SOURCES.md`.
- Produces: assets in the formats of Task 2 (`Sample::from_json`, `sample_index`); `dist/samples/elm/*.json` served beside the page (`/try/samples/...` on the site).

Decision recorded in the plan: Scheme and MoonBit "samples" are today's built-in examples (already in the shell); the menu lists them from code, and only Elm samples are assets. This keeps the shell and worker free of embedded samples.

- [ ] **Step 1: Write the script** `scripts/workbench-samples.mbtx` (same style as `scripts/elm-parity-refresh.mbtx`: `moonbitlang/async` fs, `moonbitlang/core/json`):

```moonbit
// Writes the workbench's Elm samples from the Elm corpus: one asset for each sample under
// apps/morphir-workbench/assets/samples/elm/, and index.json. Run it from the repository root with
// `mise run workbench:samples`. CI fails when the committed assets differ from its output.

///|
import {
  "moonbitlang/async@0.22.1",
  "moonbitlang/async@0.22.1/fs",
  "moonbitlang/async@0.22.1/stdio",
  "moonbitlang/core/json",
  "moonbitlang/x@0.5.5/sys",
}

///|
let corpus : String = "pkgs/morphir-elm/conformance/projects"

///|
let output : String = "apps/morphir-workbench/assets/samples/elm"

///|
/// The samples, in menu order: corpus id, title, and the notice from SOURCES.md.
let samples : Array[(String, String, String)] = [
  (
    "examples-tutorial",
    "Rentals tutorial (morphir-examples)",
    "From finos/morphir-examples 74db4db, tutorial/step_3_catching_bugs. Apache-2.0, finos/morphir-examples.",
  ),
  (
    "elm-rentals",
    "Rentals rules (morphir-elm tests)",
    "From finos/morphir-elm 71ca7ee, tests-integration/cli/test-data/rentals. Apache-2.0, finos/morphir-elm.",
  ),
  ("records", "Records (parity corpus)", "From this repository's Elm parity corpus. Apache-2.0."),
]
```

Then `main`: for each sample, read `morphir.json` (name, `sourceDirectory`, `exposedModules`), list the `.elm` files under the source directory recursively, sort their paths by code unit (use the script's own `lexical` compare, as `elm-parity-refresh.mbtx` does — `String::compare` compares length first), re-root them under `src/`, and write the asset:

```json
{"version":1,"id":"<id>","title":"<title>","languageId":"elm","notice":"<notice>",
 "project":{"version":1,"name":"<name>","languageId":"elm","exposedModules":[...],
            "files":[{"path":"src/...","content":"..."}],"active":"<first file>"}}
```

Write it with `Json::stringify(indent=2)` (or the nearest API) plus a final newline, so diffs stay readable. Write `index.json` as `{"version":1,"samples":[{"id","title"},...]}` in menu order. Create the output folder if missing. Exit non-zero with a message when a corpus folder or `morphir.json` is missing.

- [ ] **Step 2: Add the task and run it.** In `.config/mise/config.toml`:

```toml
[tasks."workbench:samples"]
description = "Regenerate the workbench Elm samples from the Elm corpus"
run = "moon run scripts/workbench-samples.mbtx"
```

Run: `mise run workbench:samples && mise run workbench:samples && git status --short apps/morphir-workbench/assets/samples`
Expected: four new files; the second run changes nothing.

- [ ] **Step 3: Parse the real assets.** Add to `apps/morphir-workbench/project/json_test.mbt` a test that parses a copy of the smallest generated asset (`records.json`) pasted as a string literal, with `Sample::from_json`, and checks `id`, `notice` and one file path. The test pins the format the script writes.

- [ ] **Step 4: Copy assets in the build.** In `apps/morphir-workbench/scripts/build.js`, after the `.svg` loop, copy `assets/samples` recursively to `dist/samples` (`cpSync(src, dst, { recursive: true })` from `node:fs`).

Run: `node apps/morphir-workbench/scripts/build.js && ls apps/morphir-workbench/dist/samples/elm`
Expected: `index.json` and three sample files.

- [ ] **Step 5: CI freshness.** In `.github/workflows/ci.yml` job `elm-scheme`, after "Check the Elm parity corpus is fresh", add:

```yaml
      - name: Check the workbench samples are fresh
        run: |
          mise run workbench:samples
          git diff --exit-code apps/morphir-workbench/assets/samples
```

Match the indentation and environment of the neighbouring steps.

- [ ] **Step 6: Document** in the workbench README: the samples, their notices, and `mise run workbench:samples`.

- [ ] **Step 7: Format and commit**

```bash
moon fmt
git add scripts/workbench-samples.mbtx .config/mise/config.toml .github/workflows/ci.yml apps/morphir-workbench/assets/samples apps/morphir-workbench/scripts/build.js apps/morphir-workbench/project/json_test.mbt apps/morphir-workbench/README.md
git commit -m "feat(workbench): generate Elm samples from the corpus with a freshness check"
```

title: Elm wiring, Plan C: the workbench project editor and project I/O
description:
# Elm wiring, Plan C: the workbench project editor and project I/O

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** The workbench edits a project of several files for each language, loads built-in samples, imports a local folder with a `morphir.json`, and keeps the open project in browser storage.

**Architecture:** A pure MoonBit package, `finos/morphir-workbench/project`, holds the project model, its edits and its JSON formats (storage, worker request, sample asset). A new worker operation, `import-folder`, maps a folder to a project with the engine's own `morphir.json` discovery. The browser keeps one `Project` for each language in place of today's single source and drafts, adds a file list with inline controls, problem markers in the editor, a samples menu, a folder import and debounced storage.

**Tech Stack:** MoonBit 0.10.15 (`moon test`; the browser is js-only), Rabbita, CodeMirror 6, Playwright, Node test runner, mise.

**Spec:** `.dev/beads-specs/morphir-ukvn.5.22.4.md` section 6 (Plan C), with sections 4 (morphir.json discovery) and 5 (the worker's `project` request) as context. Plan B (`morphir-ukvn.5.22.4.2`, PR #103, `51a9764`) is merged.

## Global Constraints

- Branch from `origin/main` (`51a9764` or later). One PR for Plan C; open it only when the maintainer asks.
- Toolchain: `export MOON_HOME="$(mise where http:moonbit)" PATH="$(mise where http:moonbit)/bin:$PATH"` (MoonBit 0.10.15+943464bfa).
- Parse at the boundary: storage text, sample assets, folder files and worker replies become domain types (`@ids`) where they enter. Only the wire carries `String`.
- New public APIs use domain types for ids, names and paths.
- Use `|>` pipes, `..` cascades and method chains where they read better. Subject-first public functions so they pipe.
- No browser dialogs: never `alert`, `confirm` or `prompt`. Delete asks inline.
- `PerFile` languages (Scheme, MoonBit) stay at one file: "Add file" is disabled with a reason that names `morphir-ukvn.5.22.14`.
- Samples are static JSON assets, `apps/morphir-workbench/assets/samples/<language>/<id>.json`, fetched on demand; the worker and the shell do not embed them.
- A folder import is a copy; nothing is written back. Storage is a per-browser convenience; nothing is shared or sent.
- Every storage read and write is wrapped in `try`/`catch`. Without storage the workbench works in memory and shows "not saved".
- Connected mode (a Morphir host) keeps sending `source` (the active file); only the local worker gets `project`.
- Clear MoonBit warnings only in the modules a task touches. Run `moon fmt` before each commit; CI runs `mise run lint:moonbit`.
- New tests use `moonrockz/expect` 0.6.1 (`@expect`) imported `for "test"`/`for "wbtest"`: `@expect.expect_all(s => ...)` for several facts, `.at(...)`/`to_contain_json` for JSON, navigation (`single`, `first`, `element`), `label=` in loops. `to_raise(containing=)` does not see `@config.Invalid` text: catch and match the message instead. Property tests (`@expect.for_all`) where a law holds; example tests beside them.
- Stage files by path; never add untracked `pkg.generated.mbti` files. Conventional Commits, no AI attribution, no trailers. No git stash; no destructive git.
- `-f <file>` does not select tests in this moon version: run the package.

## Review Focus

1. **A stored project that is corrupt, from an older version, or names an invalid path** gives the default project and a panel note "Could not restore the saved project", never a blank page or a crash. Pinned in Tasks 2 and 10.
2. **A dropped or picked folder that is large or not an Elm project** (a `node_modules` tree, binary files, more than the file or byte limit) is refused with a message that says why, and files outside the source directory are ignored; the tab never freezes on an unbounded read. Pinned in Tasks 3 and 9.
3. **Rename or delete of the active file or of an exposed module** keeps the project consistent: the active file moves to an existing file, exposure follows the rename and is dropped on delete, and the last file cannot be deleted. Pinned in Task 1 (property test).
4. **Problems that name a file that no longer exists** (renamed after the compile) show in the panel with their path, clicking them does nothing harmful, and no other file shows their count. Pinned in Tasks 6 and 7.
5. **Switching language keeps each language's project**, and connected mode still sends `source`. Pinned in Task 5.

## File structure

| File | Responsibility | Task |
|---|---|---|
| `apps/morphir-workbench/project/moon.pkg`, `project.mbt` (new package `finos/morphir-workbench/project`) | `ProjectFile`, `Project`, `Layout`, `FileRules`, `ProjectError`, edits, module names | 1 |
| `apps/morphir-workbench/project/json.mbt` | storage codec, worker request, request import, sample asset, problem counts | 2 |
| `apps/morphir-workbench/folder_import.mbt` | worker `import-folder` operation | 3 |
| `scripts/workbench-samples.mbtx`, `.config/mise/config.toml`, `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `apps/morphir-workbench/assets/samples/**`, `apps/morphir-workbench/scripts/build.js` | sample assets and their freshness check | 4 |
| `apps/morphir-workbench/browser/main.mbt` | projects per language, requests, wiring of Tasks 6-10 | 5-10 |
| `apps/morphir-workbench/browser/project-files/` (new package) | file list, settings strip, edit state machine | 6 |
| `apps/morphir-workbench/browser/editor/code-editor.js`, `editor.mbt` | problem marks and reveal | 7 |
