title: Migrate Proton host and renderer to native envelopes
description: Coordinate the bundled Proton host and shared renderer on raw public-native request/reply envelopes. Use production bounded codecs, live stable jobs offers, explicit admission/execution effects, page revalidation after awaits, and all six workspace operations. Preserve picker tickets, capture retirement, original JSON/Ion bytes, HTTP and standalone behavior. Independent lifecycle MCK and actual packaged target advertisement remain separate gates.
design:
Workbench · native services · morphir-etg2.15

Proton owns the local service

Give the desktop app a native command connection, isolated execution and explicitly granted workspace access. Keep the shared Workbench UI and the qualified invocation, job and receipt semantics.

Design revision 25 · merged baseline d6282b4, including MoonBit 0.10.15, Krueger 0.8.0 from PR #96, Node 24.22.0 from PR #77, native workers/workspaces and the picker cleanup from PR #101 and offline native frame qualification from PR #102. The baseline also includes the shared Morphir model vocabulary from PR #104, native descriptor admission from PR #105 and native reply/effect admission from PR #106, the unified engine/Elm workbench compilation from PR #103 and MoonBit generator extension from PR #107. Native handshake and isolated typed jobs are complete. Read-only workspace grants and the public native-profile draft are merged. The bundled pair uses accepted public native envelopes from PR #109. Independent reply/client/owner lifecycle MCK and packaged-target qualification remain pending before public conformance advertisement.

What we have now

PR #91 provides renderer-bound native sessions. PR #93 owns isolated native typed evaluation jobs on qualified macOS Apple Silicon; browser compilation and explicit Local Scheme still use browser workers. Standalone and authenticated connected HTTP/RPC modes remain qualified. Read-only workspace grants, native descriptor admission and the native reply/effect boundary are merged. Coordinated public host/renderer activation remains pending.

Native discovery reuses the engine’s merged #88 workspace and morphir.json semantics. The desktop read path executes no configuration scripts and has no separate Elm compiler. Saved models pass through the shared compiled codec before replacing the explorer model.

Proposed integration

Mermaid architecture source
flowchart LR
  UI[Shared Workbench UI] --> Adapter[Planned native adapter]
  Adapter -->|Page-bound IPC| Host[Planned Proton command host]
  Host --> Owner[Shared immutable job owner]
  Owner -->|One claim| Worker[Planned isolated native worker]
  Worker --> Engine[Existing typed evaluator]
  Host -->|Native picker| Grants[Planned opaque workspace grants]
  Grants -->|Bounded read only| Files[Granted workspace files]

Transport and session ownership

One shared client state machine

Extract the request transport from JobClient, keeping receipt admission, unknown-submission handling, cancellation, reconnect and lost-release reconciliation in the existing client. HTTP and native transports supply the same admitted domain values.

Map native operations to session, submit, query, cancel and release. The renderer never receives internal claim or complete commands.

Typed Proton boundary

Pin Proton, CLI, contract package and helpers to 0.3.4. Register typed application commands with App::commands. Inspect CommandContext for the native window, source origin and current page instance. A JavaScript bridge property is discovery, not authorization.

Carry business payloads as bounded raw UTF-8 JSON text into the existing duplicate-aware decoder. Ordinary typed JSON decoding alone does not prove closed shape, bounds or duplicate rejection.

  1. The implemented private bootstrap uses bridgeVersion 0.1.0-draft.1 and opaque page-scoped identities. Qualified packages offer jobs and workspace; unqualified operations remain absent. Typed open/check/close commands accept string payloads and require native main-window/app-origin/page context. This is separate from the proposed public mapping. For that mapping, negotiate a proposed exact morphir/workbench/native mapping starting at 0.1.0-draft.1. Its final shape is an upstream design contribution, not a shipped claim.
  2. The native host creates identities and binds the session to the trusted main window and page instance. Validate that binding on every command and before delivering asynchronous results.
  3. A reload or navigation revokes the page session and grants, initiates owned-worker cleanup, and requires a new handshake. Do not promise cross-page or durable recovery in this slice.
  4. An explicit connected launch takes precedence and registers no native commands for the remote page. A development-server entry requires its own explicit exact-origin policy. Unrelated windows, frames and external navigation gain no native authority.
  5. A broken native connection after admission retains uncertainty. Do not silently retry on HTTP or the local browser worker. Standalone remains available when selected before execution.

Native execution and cleanup

Reuse apps/morphir-workbench/jobs/Host and the portable engine Session. The host captures the rich IR unit and typed input suite once, authorizes the public entry, and claims a job once. Run the existing typed evaluator in a packaged child executable, keeping evaluation off the CEF event loop.

ConcernRequired behavior
OwnershipNative session owns queue, child handles, snapshots and receipts. Renderer edits cannot mutate admitted work. Do not accept executable paths, shell commands or environment overrides from renderer input.
BoundsRetain the existing 1 MiB host business-frame limit, eight retained jobs and 16 MiB retained-evidence budget. Specify bounded framing for child I/O and cap stdout/stderr. Start with at most two active workers and a 30-second deadline; independently measure native allocation/process limits rather than borrowing the JavaScript heap-limit claim.
CancellationAcknowledge the request through the shared owner. Terminate the owned process using the platform process API, await confirmed exit and preserve a previously captured returned outcome if it wins the race. An unconfirmed stop is not a terminal receipt.
OutcomesAdmit returned values against captured declarations. Preserve Result.Err, SDK/model failures, provider failures and separate cleanup failures. Release only terminal jobs; preserve same-identity reconciliation when the release reply is lost.
ShutdownStop new claims, cancel queued work, stop and reap active children, then close the native session. Wire this into Proton lifecycle hooks. If cleanup fails, report it explicitly instead of claiming success.

This first native provider evaluates the qualified Scheme-backed typed pipeline. Elm/MoonBit generation does not imply generated Elm/MoonBit execution. Generated browser execution remains a separate phase.

Feasibility on MoonBit 0.10.15: a local native executable calls the existing typed evaluator with the pricing model and returns exact Decimal 37.5, without a Node runtime. Probe receipt. Production worker packaging, bounded IPC, resource limits and shutdown qualification subsequently landed in PR #93, with evidence below. The installed async process API documents structured child ownership and waiting for termination on cancellation; actual host behavior must still be tested.

Read-only workspace grants

Pinned Proton 0.3.4 exposes proton/core.CommandWindow::choose_directory(title, path) -> String?. Its facade routes through the trusted native window and maps an empty dialog result to None. Use that typed host API, with host-selected options, then recheck the captured native page/session after the asynchronous picker returns before issuing a grant. The command is bound and native filesystem containment acceptance passes. Real macOS packaged picker selection/cancellation, byte-exact original export Blobs and page-session qualification pass in PR #97; other packaged platforms remain unqualified.

The trusted native directory picker chooses a root. The host retains its canonical root and returns an opaque grant identity; a renderer-supplied path cannot create a grant. Grants are scoped to the current native page session and can be revoked.

  • Resolve project membership and morphir.json through the existing engine, including PR #88. Return project/model identities through the shared provider and project UI.
  • Use relative locators within a grant. Reject traversal and outside-root symbolic links, check canonical membership at open, and qualify replacement/symlink races with platform-specific file APIs. Do not claim that a string-prefix path check provides containment.
  • Bound directory discovery, file count, individual reads and aggregate source bytes. Align engine/project budgets before enabling the operation; existing 16 MiB browser model import and 1 MiB job submission are different boundaries.
  • Retain original IR format versions and rich Ion metadata. Surface revoked grants, missing files, invalid configuration and unavailable bindings as distinct diagnostics in the existing bottom panel.

Grant-scoped writes, background artifact publication, watches and persistent grants are later work. Explicit user exports use the separate native save dialog.

Publish the transport mapping upstream

FINOS already has the host HTTP profile and the transport-neutral invocation, jobs and terminal contracts. Reuse those shapes. Contribute the native command/session lifecycle, grant scope, operation mapping, error mapping and independent positive/negative fixtures to finos/morphir before advertising the native profile.

Freeze existing connected v1, HTTP host draft.1, jobs draft.1 and terminal draft.5. A native mapping must explicitly negotiate its own exact draft; it cannot quietly reinterpret the HTTP profile. Protocol review and independent qualification are part of the implementation.

Evidence needed before calling it supported

LaneAcceptance
Real packaged ProtonTyped command handshake, trusted window/origin/page identity, rejection of unknown commands, fresh page identity on reload, stale-page revocation, connected-page exclusion and renderer failure cleanup.
Native jobsIdentical exact values for fields/JSON/Ion; Result.Err and SDK failures; immutable snapshots; one claim; cancellation/result races; queue/deadline limits; crash/oversize/malformed child output; confirmed exit; lost release; app shutdown.
WorkspacePicker cancellation, ordinary and nested projects, #88 morphir.json handling, revoked grants, traversal, outside links, replacement races, unsupported files and bounded reads.
CompatibilityStandalone Chromium and existing packaged local workers; connected jobs-enabled gateway and unchanged jobs-disabled v1. Preserve editor drafts, explorer context, back navigation and bottom panels.
PlatformsmacOS Apple Silicon, Linux x64 and Windows x64 each need build/package and lifecycle evidence. Local macOS evidence does not qualify the others. Unsupported or unqualified operations remain unavailable.

Implementation checklist

Source seams and local evidence

  • Desktop entry and explicit loopback launch, pinned dependencies and isolated desktop workspace.
  • Shared bootstrap, job client and local/connected adapters.
  • Bounded native-reusable host admission, portable snapshot owner and qualified HTTP worker lifecycle.
  • Pinned dependency source: proton/command/typed_registrar.mbt, proton/core/pkg.generated.mbti and proton/README.md. The local module directly declares proton_contract@0.3.4; a transitive import alone fails MoonBit dependency checking.
  • Native compiler probe, packaging receipt and CEF probe acceptance. Initial direct-binary launch lacked runtime bundle configuration; acceptance uses the separately packaged probe and matching helpers.

Native session implementation

Commit 491385c implements the first native boundary. Typed application commands are registered only for the bundled main renderer, and are absent from explicit connected launches. Every call uses the native window/origin/page context. Reload revokes the page binding; close shuts it down. The UI shows Desktop local, and ?mode=standalone explicitly retains the browser path.

The shared job client now takes a bounded text transport. HTTP still uses fresh same-origin authentication and the compiled cursor still owns duplicate-aware decoding and receipt admission. A supplied text transport cannot bypass those boundaries. The initial PR #91 bootstrap advertised zero domain operations. PR #93 now offers operations:["jobs"] on qualified macOS Apple Silicon. The public native profile remains pending upstream mapping and independent qualification.

Current combined source 6524f68 includes main 02dfde0 and PR #89 MoonBit 0.10.15. Four authority/state tests pass per JavaScript, native, Wasm and Wasm GC. The model lives in a dependency-free root module shared with the desktop host; portable checks no longer invoke Proton prebuilds requiring GTK/X11. All 73 Node tests pass, including stale asynchronous admission. Repackaged Proton passes trusted caller context, invalid version/type/operation rejection, untrusted-origin denial, reload, stale identity, revocation and explicit standalone selection. All four actual Rust-host lanes pass again: Chromium and Proton, jobs on/off, including ten real submissions per jobs-enabled client with exact JSON/Ion values, cancellation and reconnect. Required lint/format/validation and full repository requalification pass on this source, including four-target tests, CLI/npm, compiler acceptance, 60 process-fault cases and builds. PR #91 squash merged at 02ed079069d3f6e6dab28b86c442b037a4499896. All 26 final-head contexts passed on 6524f68; no review findings or unresolved threads remained. The normal merge path required repository-disabled auto-merge, so the recorded roadmap approval authorized admin bypass. The fetched merged tree exactly matches the qualified combined source. title: Check native replies and explicit job effects
description: Implement the production public-native reply codec and explicit native job request path needed for the coordinated Proton migration. Reuse bounded duplicate-aware raw decoding, validate all portable operation reply shapes and correlate each completion to its originating operation. Share native descriptor admission with the reply codec. Preserve existing cursor semantics, distinguish authoritative effect none from unknown without fabricated HTTP statuses, and reconcile terminal release conservatively. Keep the shipped private bridge and public activation gates unchanged until the coordinated host/renderer migration and lifecycle/packaged qualification are complete.
design:
Workbench · native services · morphir-etg2.15

Proton owns the local service

Give the desktop app a native command connection, isolated execution and explicitly granted workspace access. Keep the shared Workbench UI and the qualified invocation, job and receipt semantics.

Design revision 23 · merged baseline 1fd0dde, including MoonBit 0.10.15, Krueger 0.8.0 from PR #96, Node 24.22.0 from PR #77, native workers/workspaces and the picker cleanup from PR #101 and offline native frame qualification from PR #102. The baseline also includes the shared Morphir model vocabulary from PR #104, native descriptor admission from PR #105 and native reply/effect admission from PR #106. Native handshake and isolated typed jobs are complete. Read-only workspace grants and the public native-profile draft are merged. Public adapter adoption and platform qualification remain pending.

What we have now

PR #91 provides renderer-bound native sessions. PR #93 owns isolated native typed evaluation jobs on qualified macOS Apple Silicon; browser compilation and explicit Local Scheme still use browser workers. Standalone and authenticated connected HTTP/RPC modes remain qualified. Read-only workspace grants, native descriptor admission and the native reply/effect boundary are merged. Coordinated public host/renderer activation remains pending.

Native discovery reuses the engine’s merged #88 workspace and morphir.json semantics. The desktop read path executes no configuration scripts and has no separate Elm compiler. Saved models pass through the shared compiled codec before replacing the explorer model.

Proposed integration

Mermaid architecture source
flowchart LR
  UI[Shared Workbench UI] --> Adapter[Planned native adapter]
  Adapter -->|Page-bound IPC| Host[Planned Proton command host]
  Host --> Owner[Shared immutable job owner]
  Owner -->|One claim| Worker[Planned isolated native worker]
  Worker --> Engine[Existing typed evaluator]
  Host -->|Native picker| Grants[Planned opaque workspace grants]
  Grants -->|Bounded read only| Files[Granted workspace files]

Transport and session ownership

One shared client state machine

Extract the request transport from JobClient, keeping receipt admission, unknown-submission handling, cancellation, reconnect and lost-release reconciliation in the existing client. HTTP and native transports supply the same admitted domain values.

Map native operations to session, submit, query, cancel and release. The renderer never receives internal claim or complete commands.

Typed Proton boundary

Pin Proton, CLI, contract package and helpers to 0.3.4. Register typed application commands with App::commands. Inspect CommandContext for the native window, source origin and current page instance. A JavaScript bridge property is discovery, not authorization.

Carry business payloads as bounded raw UTF-8 JSON text into the existing duplicate-aware decoder. Ordinary typed JSON decoding alone does not prove closed shape, bounds or duplicate rejection.

  1. The implemented private bootstrap uses bridgeVersion 0.1.0-draft.1 and opaque page-scoped identities. Qualified packages offer jobs and workspace; unqualified operations remain absent. Typed open/check/close commands accept string payloads and require native main-window/app-origin/page context. This is separate from the proposed public mapping. For that mapping, negotiate a proposed exact morphir/workbench/native mapping starting at 0.1.0-draft.1. Its final shape is an upstream design contribution, not a shipped claim.
  2. The native host creates identities and binds the session to the trusted main window and page instance. Validate that binding on every command and before delivering asynchronous results.
  3. A reload or navigation revokes the page session and grants, initiates owned-worker cleanup, and requires a new handshake. Do not promise cross-page or durable recovery in this slice.
  4. An explicit connected launch takes precedence and registers no native commands for the remote page. A development-server entry requires its own explicit exact-origin policy. Unrelated windows, frames and external navigation gain no native authority.
  5. A broken native connection after admission retains uncertainty. Do not silently retry on HTTP or the local browser worker. Standalone remains available when selected before execution.

Native execution and cleanup

Reuse apps/morphir-workbench/jobs/Host and the portable engine Session. The host captures the rich IR unit and typed input suite once, authorizes the public entry, and claims a job once. Run the existing typed evaluator in a packaged child executable, keeping evaluation off the CEF event loop.

ConcernRequired behavior
OwnershipNative session owns queue, child handles, snapshots and receipts. Renderer edits cannot mutate admitted work. Do not accept executable paths, shell commands or environment overrides from renderer input.
BoundsRetain the existing 1 MiB host business-frame limit, eight retained jobs and 16 MiB retained-evidence budget. Specify bounded framing for child I/O and cap stdout/stderr. Start with at most two active workers and a 30-second deadline; independently measure native allocation/process limits rather than borrowing the JavaScript heap-limit claim.
CancellationAcknowledge the request through the shared owner. Terminate the owned process using the platform process API, await confirmed exit and preserve a previously captured returned outcome if it wins the race. An unconfirmed stop is not a terminal receipt.
OutcomesAdmit returned values against captured declarations. Preserve Result.Err, SDK/model failures, provider failures and separate cleanup failures. Release only terminal jobs; preserve same-identity reconciliation when the release reply is lost.
ShutdownStop new claims, cancel queued work, stop and reap active children, then close the native session. Wire this into Proton lifecycle hooks. If cleanup fails, report it explicitly instead of claiming success.

This first native provider evaluates the qualified Scheme-backed typed pipeline. Elm/MoonBit generation does not imply generated Elm/MoonBit execution. Generated browser execution remains a separate phase.

Feasibility on MoonBit 0.10.15: a local native executable calls the existing typed evaluator with the pricing model and returns exact Decimal 37.5, without a Node runtime. Probe receipt. Production worker packaging, bounded IPC, resource limits and shutdown qualification subsequently landed in PR #93, with evidence below. The installed async process API documents structured child ownership and waiting for termination on cancellation; actual host behavior must still be tested.

Read-only workspace grants

Pinned Proton 0.3.4 exposes proton/core.CommandWindow::choose_directory(title, path) -> String?. Its facade routes through the trusted native window and maps an empty dialog result to None. Use that typed host API, with host-selected options, then recheck the captured native page/session after the asynchronous picker returns before issuing a grant. The command is bound and native filesystem containment acceptance passes. Real macOS packaged picker selection/cancellation, byte-exact original export Blobs and page-session qualification pass in PR #97; other packaged platforms remain unqualified.

The trusted native directory picker chooses a root. The host retains its canonical root and returns an opaque grant identity; a renderer-supplied path cannot create a grant. Grants are scoped to the current native page session and can be revoked.

  • Resolve project membership and morphir.json through the existing engine, including PR #88. Return project/model identities through the shared provider and project UI.
  • Use relative locators within a grant. Reject traversal and outside-root symbolic links, check canonical membership at open, and qualify replacement/symlink races with platform-specific file APIs. Do not claim that a string-prefix path check provides containment.
  • Bound directory discovery, file count, individual reads and aggregate source bytes. Align engine/project budgets before enabling the operation; existing 16 MiB browser model import and 1 MiB job submission are different boundaries.
  • Retain original IR format versions and rich Ion metadata. Surface revoked grants, missing files, invalid configuration and unavailable bindings as distinct diagnostics in the existing bottom panel.

Grant-scoped writes, background artifact publication, watches and persistent grants are later work. Explicit user exports use the separate native save dialog.

Publish the transport mapping upstream

FINOS already has the host HTTP profile and the transport-neutral invocation, jobs and terminal contracts. Reuse those shapes. Contribute the native command/session lifecycle, grant scope, operation mapping, error mapping and independent positive/negative fixtures to finos/morphir before advertising the native profile.

Freeze existing connected v1, HTTP host draft.1, jobs draft.1 and terminal draft.5. A native mapping must explicitly negotiate its own exact draft; it cannot quietly reinterpret the HTTP profile. Protocol review and independent qualification are part of the implementation.

Evidence needed before calling it supported

LaneAcceptance
Real packaged ProtonTyped command handshake, trusted window/origin/page identity, rejection of unknown commands, fresh page identity on reload, stale-page revocation, connected-page exclusion and renderer failure cleanup.
Native jobsIdentical exact values for fields/JSON/Ion; Result.Err and SDK failures; immutable snapshots; one claim; cancellation/result races; queue/deadline limits; crash/oversize/malformed child output; confirmed exit; lost release; app shutdown.
WorkspacePicker cancellation, ordinary and nested projects, #88 morphir.json handling, revoked grants, traversal, outside links, replacement races, unsupported files and bounded reads.
CompatibilityStandalone Chromium and existing packaged local workers; connected jobs-enabled gateway and unchanged jobs-disabled v1. Preserve editor drafts, explorer context, back navigation and bottom panels.
PlatformsmacOS Apple Silicon, Linux x64 and Windows x64 each need build/package and lifecycle evidence. Local macOS evidence does not qualify the others. Unsupported or unqualified operations remain unavailable.

Implementation checklist

Source seams and local evidence

  • Desktop entry and explicit loopback launch, pinned dependencies and isolated desktop workspace.
  • Shared bootstrap, job client and local/connected adapters.
  • Bounded native-reusable host admission, portable snapshot owner and qualified HTTP worker lifecycle.
  • Pinned dependency source: proton/command/typed_registrar.mbt, proton/core/pkg.generated.mbti and proton/README.md. The local module directly declares proton_contract@0.3.4; a transitive import alone fails MoonBit dependency checking.
  • Native compiler probe, packaging receipt and CEF probe acceptance. Initial direct-binary launch lacked runtime bundle configuration; acceptance uses the separately packaged probe and matching helpers.

Native session implementation

Commit 491385c implements the first native boundary. Typed application commands are registered only for the bundled main renderer, and are absent from explicit connected launches. Proton owns the local service

What we have now

PR #91 provides renderer-bound native sessions. PR #93 owns isolated native typed evaluation jobs on qualified macOS Apple Silicon; browser compilation and explicit Local Scheme still use browser workers. Standalone and authenticated connected HTTP/RPC modes remain qualified. Workspace grants are the current implementation phase and have not yet merged.

Mermaid architecture source
flowchart LR

Transport and session ownership

One shared client state machine

Extract the request transport from JobClient, keeping receipt admission, unknown-submission handling, cancellation, reconnect and lost-release reconciliation in the existing client. HTTP and native transports supply the same admitted domain values.

Map native operations to session, submit, query, cancel and release. The renderer never receives internal claim or complete commands.

Typed Proton boundary

Pin Proton, CLI, contract package and helpers to 0.3.4. Register typed application commands with App::commands. Inspect CommandContext for the native window, source origin and current page instance. A JavaScript bridge property is discovery, not authorization.

Carry business payloads as bounded raw UTF-8 JSON text into the existing duplicate-aware decoder. Ordinary typed JSON decoding alone does not prove closed shape, bounds or duplicate rejection.

  1. The implemented private bootstrap uses bridgeVersion 0.1.0-draft.1 and opaque page-scoped identities. Qualified packages offer jobs and workspace; unqualified operations remain absent. Typed open/check/close commands accept string payloads and require native main-window/app-origin/page context. This is separate from the proposed public mapping. For that mapping, negotiate a proposed exact morphir/workbench/native mapping starting at 0.1.0-draft.1. Its final shape is an upstream design contribution, not a shipped claim.
  2. The native host creates identities and binds the session to the trusted main window and page instance. Validate that binding on every command and before delivering asynchronous results.
  3. A reload or navigation revokes the page session and grants, initiates owned-worker cleanup, and requires a new handshake. Do not promise cross-page or durable recovery in this slice.
  4. An explicit connected launch takes precedence and registers no native commands for the remote page. A development-server entry requires its own explicit exact-origin policy. Unrelated windows, frames and external navigation gain no native authority.
  5. A broken native connection after admission retains uncertainty. Do not silently retry on HTTP or the local browser worker. Standalone remains available when selected before execution.

Native execution and cleanup

Reuse apps/morphir-workbench/jobs/Host and the portable engine Session. The host captures the rich IR unit and typed input suite once, authorizes the public entry, and claims a job once. Run the existing typed evaluator in a packaged child executable, keeping evaluation off the CEF event loop.

OwnershipNative session owns queue, child handles, snapshots and receipts. Renderer edits cannot mutate admitted work. Do not accept executable paths, shell commands or environment overrides from renderer input.
BoundsRetain the existing 1 MiB host business-frame limit, eight retained jobs and 16 MiB retained-evidence budget. Specify bounded framing for child I/O and cap stdout/stderr. Start with at most two active workers and a 30-second deadline; independently measure native allocation/process limits rather than borrowing the JavaScript heap-limit claim.
CancellationAcknowledge the request through the shared owner. Terminate the owned process using the platform process API, await confirmed exit and preserve a previously captured returned outcome if it wins the race. An unconfirmed stop is not a terminal receipt.
OutcomesAdmit returned values against captured declarations. Preserve Result.Err, SDK/model failures, provider failures and separate cleanup failures. Release only terminal jobs; preserve same-identity reconciliation when the release reply is lost.
ShutdownStop new claims, cancel queued work, stop and reap active children, then close the native session. Wire this into Proton lifecycle hooks. If cleanup fails, report it explicitly instead of claiming success.

  • Retain original IR format versions and rich Ion metadata. Surface revoked grants, missing files, invalid configuration and unavailable bindings as distinct diagnostics in the existing bottom panel.

Grant-scoped writes, background artifact publication, watches and persistent grants are later work. Explicit user exports use the separate native save dialog.

FINOS already has the host HTTP profile and the transport-neutral invocation, jobs and terminal contracts. Reuse those shapes. Contribute the native command/session lifecycle, grant scope, operation mapping, error mapping and independent positive/negative fixtures to finos/morphir before advertising the native profile.

title: Qualify native request frames through shared MCK
description:

design:
Workbench · native qualification · morphir-etg2.15.5.1

Qualify the bytes before the native adapter

Extend the shared Rust MCK with a narrow native request-frame operation. Test the production decoder through an explicit adapter, with fixed independent expectations and independently checked reports.

Design revision 4 · exact Workbench MCK 0.1.0-draft.7 · the published live native profile remains 0.1.0-draft.1. Merged in Morphir #1049 as 7545bf47 and MoonBit #102 as 7518ee8. Offline frame qualification is complete. The public native endpoint remains inactive.

What is complete

Upstream PR #1048 is merged as 5975da73. Three schemas and 210 structural cases pass. The 16 raw rejection expectations and 15 abstract lifecycle traces are published as unexecuted data.

The existing morphir mck workbench run/check commands own compatibility execution. Workbench hashes the bytes of cases.json. The runner sends input to an explicit adapter, keeps expected results private, and records observed results. The report checker reloads the corpus and recomputes qualification.

Qualification path

The shared runner, corpus loader and report checker already exist. The new native operation exercises the portable MoonBit request decoder through an explicit adapter. Expected results never reach the adapter.

Mermaid topology
flowchart LR
  Cases[Hashed cases: input and expected] --> Runner[Shared Rust MCK]
  Runner -->|Input only| Adapter[Explicit implementation adapter]
  Adapter -->|Raw bytes| Decoder[Production request decoder]
  Decoder -->|Admission observation| Adapter
  Adapter -->|Observation| Runner
  Runner --> Report[Saved observations and verdicts]
  Report --> Check[Independent report check]
  Cases --> Check

The first gate has a narrow meaning

ScopeWhat it establishes
Request framingRaw UTF-8 size, strict encoding, one JSON value, duplicate members at every depth, bounded parsing and the closed native request shape.
Nested JSON sourceWhole-document duplicate-aware decoding of model JSON and JSON argument source. This does not establish a valid Morphir model, declared invocation values or provider support.
Function admissionSeparate model/revision, public entry, argument/type and execution-provider checks. Frame acceptance does not accept a job or claim execution.
Packaged authoritySeparate actual Proton window/origin/page provenance, OS picker authority, filesystem races and confirmed child exit. Synthetic MCK inputs cannot establish these properties.

Operation and observations

Use exact MCK 0.1.0-draft.7, operation validate-native-frame, JSON adapter format only. Preserve all six historical drafts and their corpus bytes. Reuse the shared negotiation, process supervision and report machinery.

{
  "op": "validate-native-frame",
  "suite": "workbench",
  "contractVersion": "0.1.0-draft.7",
  "format": "json",
  "input": {
    "encoding": "utf8",
    "source": "{\"profile\":\"morphir/workbench/native\",\"contractVersion\":\"0.1.0-draft.1\",\"operation\":\"session.open\"}"
  }
}

Also admit hex for malformed UTF-8 and a closed, bounded prefix-repeat recipe for byte-budget cases. Materialize original bytes inside the adapter and exercise the production decoding boundary. Do not decode and reserialize the embedded frame first.

{"status":"ok","value":{"frameAccepted":true}}
{"status":"invalid","code":"native.frame.utf8"}

The implementation validates a closed success projection and six stable rejection codes: limit, utf8, json, shape, model and arguments, each prefixed with native.frame. A native rejection is an ordinary expected observation; adapter spawn, framing, timeout and shutdown failures remain report errors.

Rejection stages are frame byte limit, UTF-8, JSON decoding, closed request shape and nested JSON source. Keep those distinct from live native error envelopes and terminal job outcomes. Do not echo model or argument source in observations.

Corpus integrity and independent results

Convert the 16 raw negative expectations into executable cases and add valid counterparts, including escaped names without collisions. An adapter that rejects everything must fail. Keep input and expected results independently authored; never use the implementation under test to calculate its own expected verdict.

Inline small source/hex assets and bounded generation recipes in cases.json. Its current hash then covers the full executable input and expectation closure. Adding external assets requires a separately versioned closure contract. A compact case input is limited to 1 MiB; adapter response framing has a separate 16 MiB limit.

The shared strict JSON parser protects corpus/report integrity. Its 127-container and number-normalization behavior differs from the native boundary, so it is infrastructure rather than a native reference oracle.

Implementation checklist

At parent head 913118f8, merged as 7545bf47, and MoonBit head 612eae5, merged as 7518ee8, all 138 fixed cases pass Node/native debug and release. All six historical kits pass those four modes. Pure adapter tests pass JS, native, Wasm and Wasm GC. Parent validation passes 272 unit tests, 10 CLI tests, 15 transport tests, full schema checks with 71 new fixtures, Clippy and formatting. Regression tests cover rounded fractional integers and literal serde private-marker objects. Twenty-four malformed compact-input subprocess probes fail as infrastructure. MoonBit full repository checks pass all four target suites, CLI/compiler integration, 60 process-fault cases, builds, lint, formatting and validation. The isolated Proton 0.3.4 release host rebuild also passes; no new packaged platform qualification is claimed.

Following slices

Historical MCK literal-object hardening is tracked as morphir-utvg. A separate draft.1 saved-report reproduction confirms the older conversion path needs hardening. This contribution preserves those historical paths while closing the new draft.7 corpus, transport, observation and report boundaries.

Qualify client and owner lifecycle behavior through distinct operations. The client owns descriptor binding, invocation correlation, duplicate project-ID rejection, stale replies, unknown submission effects, lost reads and pending release. The owner owns page/picker generations, revocation, capture retirement, stale release and cleanup-gated execution.

Replace Q with a complete runnable model, declared revision, public entry, arguments and provider requirements. Replace P1 with exact JSON/Ion bytes, filename, format, length, SHA-256 and chunk boundaries. Driver-supplied synthetic context, picker completion and worker-exit events never become renderer-authorized live operations.

Public adapter adoption and per-platform packaged acceptance remain in the native services plan. A successful offline frame report alone never advertises the live native profile.

title: Elm wiring, Plan B: the workbench on the engine
description:
# Elm wiring, Plan B: the workbench on the engine

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** The workbench worker compiles and generates every language through `@engine.Engine`, so Elm (and any registered provider) works in the browser, with the IR, Model Explorer, generated output and per-file diagnostics.

**Architecture:** Four engine additions come first: a structured `Problem` on `Diagnostic`, an `on_unit` callback on `execute_content`, structured generation problems, and Scheme output from rich units with a warning. Then the worker parses each request into domain types, builds an in-memory project (`morphir.json` or a generated `morphir.toml`), and runs `discover`, `plan` and `execute_content`. The catalog comes from `Engine::languages()`. The browser keeps its single editor and gains Elm.

**Tech Stack:** MoonBit 0.10.15 (`moon test`, targets native, js, wasm, wasm-gc; the workbench is js-only), Rabbita, CodeMirror, Playwright, mise.

**Spec:** `.dev/beads-specs/morphir-ukvn.5.22.4.md` (section 5, Plan B), plus the maintainer decisions of 2026-10-16 in the comments of `morphir-ukvn.5.22.4`: Question 1 Option A (extend the engine), Question 2 Option A (Scheme from rich units with a warning). Scheme metadata support is out of scope (epic `morphir-ukvn.5.40`, GitHub #99).

## Global Constraints

- Branch from `origin/main` (`c6ef6dc` or later). One PR for Plan B; open it only when the maintainer asks.
- Toolchain: `export MOON_HOME="$(mise where http:moonbit)" PATH="$(mise where http:moonbit)/bin:$PATH"` (MoonBit 0.10.15+943464bfa).
- Parse at the boundary: worker JSON becomes `@ids` domain types where it enters. Only the wire carries `String`.
- New public APIs use domain types for ids, names and paths. Existing engine `String` fields stay (`morphir-ukvn.5.32`).
- Use `|>` pipes, `..` cascades and method chains where they read better. A pipe cannot feed a method of another receiver (`plan |> engine.execute_content(f)` does not compile); keep those calls plain.
- No document limit by default (`max_documents: None` means no limit).
- New tests use `moonrockz/expect` 0.6.1 (`@expect`), imported `for "test"`. Use `@expect.expect_all(s => { ... })` when a test checks several facts, so one run reports every failure; `.at("a.b[0]")` and `to_contain_json` for JSON replies; `.single()`, `.first()`, `.element(i)` and `unwrap_some()` to navigate; `expect_call(() => ...).to_raise(containing=...)` for errors; `label=` to name the case in a loop. Tests that a task only edits keep their style; this plan does not convert existing tests.
- Property tests: where a function has a law that must hold for every input (a round trip, an invariant, a mapping), test it with `@expect.for_all((input : T) => { ...matchers... })`. Generate from core types that have `@quickcheck.Arbitrary` and `Shrink` (`Int`, `UInt`, `Bool`, `Char`, `String`, `Array`, tuples) and map them to domain values inside the property. Give a property that runs the engine `count=25`. Keep example tests beside them for the cases a person reads first. Elm compiles (Task 8) stay example tests; they are slow and their inputs are not random text.
- Clear MoonBit warnings only in the modules a task touches. Run `moon fmt` before each commit; CI runs `mise run lint:moonbit`.
- Every engine package builds on native, js, wasm and wasm-gc.
- Stage files by path. Never add `pkg.generated.mbti` files that are untracked.
- Commits: Conventional Commits, plain English, no AI attribution, no `Co-Authored-By` or session trailers.
- Specs, plans and ledgers live in beads, not in the repository.

## Review Focus

1. **An Elm source in the single editor without a usable module header** (no `module` line, or a one-segment name such as `module Main`) gives a clear worker error that says how to fix it, never a crash or an empty result. Pinned in Task 6.
2. **Hostile request values** (a package name with `"` or `\`, a path with `..`, `\`, `:` or a leading `/`) are refused at parse time and cannot change the generated `morphir.toml` or overlay. Pinned in Task 6 by examples and by two property tests: `toml_string` round-trips any text, and an accepted package name round-trips through the generated `morphir.toml`.
3. **A generation refusal keeps the compiled model**: an Elm or MoonBit generator failure still returns `success: true`, the IR, `generationDiagnostics` with `code` and `nodePath`, and no artifacts. Pinned in Tasks 3 and 7.
4. **A frontend error in the second file of a project** reports that file's path and its one-based Elm range, and the panel shows the column without an off-by-one. Pinned in Tasks 8 and 9.
5. **An unknown language, provider or profile** is refused with a message that names it (`unavailable`, `frontend.unknown_provider`, `frontend.unknown_profile`), never a silent fallback to Scheme. Pinned in Task 7.

## File structure

| File | Responsibility | Task |
|---|---|---|
| `pkgs/morphir-engine/types.mbt` | `Problem`, `GenerationProblem`, `Diagnostic.problem`, `Diagnostic::code`, `Diagnostic::location`, `Backend.rich_units` | 1, 4 |
| `pkgs/morphir-engine/plan.mbt` | `execute_content`: problems, `on_unit`, generation problems, metadata warning; planner rule for rich units | 1–4 |
| `pkgs/morphir-engine/engine.mbt`, `checkpoints.mbt` | Diagnostic literals; `diagnostic_message` for `GenerationFailed` | 1, 3 |
| `pkgs/morphir-engine/generation.mbt` | `GenerationFailed`; Elm and MoonBit generators raise it | 3 |
| `pkgs/morphir-engine/problems_test.mbt` (new) | Tests of Tasks 1–4 | 1–4 |
| `apps/morphir/main.mbt`, `apps/morphir/scripts/test.js` | CLI JSON `code` and `location`; `--backend scheme` on a MoonBit project | 1, 4 |
| `apps/morphir-workbench/catalog.mbt` (new) | `catalog(engine)` from `Engine::languages()` | 5 |
| `apps/morphir-workbench/project.mbt` (new) | `ProjectRequest`, request parsing, Elm module header, snapshot, manifest, overlay | 6 |
| `apps/morphir-workbench/engine_compile.mbt` (new) | `workbench_engine`, `run_engine`, result JSON from the report | 7, 8 |
| `apps/morphir-workbench/pipeline.mbt` | `execute`, `execute_with`; old compile and generation code removed | 5, 7 |
| `apps/morphir-workbench/source_profiles.mbt`, `moonbit_generation.mbt` | Removed | 5, 7 |
| `apps/morphir-workbench/browser/main.mbt`, `browser/bottom-panel/panel.mbt` | Elm in the single editor; per-file problems; coordinate profiles | 9 |
| `apps/morphir-workbench/scripts/elm-workflow.js` | Browser test of an Elm compile | 9 |
| READMEs: engine, CLI, workbench | Docs of each change, in the task that makes it | 1–9 |

title: A2/F4: specify MoonBit extension packaging and qualify transport boundaries
description: Maintainer approved A2/F4 integration work after the independent CI split. Produce a source-backed HTML specification under local .dev with validated diagrams, current upstream contract inventory, package/install claims and identity rules, pure compiler/guest/transport ownership, explicit Ion-preferred and checked Morphir JSON transport, and implementation slices. Run focused compatibility probes against pinned upstream SDK/compiler instead of assuming a MoonBit Wasm artifact speaks Extism. Spec/plan/evidence live canonically in shared Beads; local .dev is never committed.
design:
Skip to specification
Morphir / MoonBit

A2 + F4 integration
Specification revision 0.6
16 October 2026

01 / Outcome and status02 / Current contract evidence03 / Component ownership04 / Guest runtime choice05 / Ion and checked JSON06 / MEP gap analysis07 / MEP call flows08 / Claims and sessions09 / Packaging and installation10 / Implementation slices11 / Acceptance matrix12 / Sources and records
Pluggable library pipeline / extension delivery

Deliver the MoonBit pipeline to an upstream Morphir host.

Package the existing frontend and generator behind a thin extension adapter, retain native Ion models, and prove installation and use through an independently pinned host.

Proposed integrationLanguage: moonbitNumeric work independentIon preferred; JSON supported

Owned by A2 morphir-ukvn.1.3 and F4 morphir-ukvn.1.10.5. Compatibility study morphir-ukvn.1.3.1. This specification does not claim an installed MoonBit extension, upstream Ion negotiation, a component guest, or a release.

01 / outcome

Move from an in-process implementation to an installable provider

The local engine and CLI already compile Boolean MoonBit libraries, retain source and naming metadata, evaluate them, and generate callable libraries. F4 makes that functionality available through the ecosystem extension lifecycle. It uses the same pure components; it does not create a second compiler.

First useful installed flow

  1. Build and bundle a pinned MoonBit guest.
  2. Publish to a controlled test extension index.
  3. Install into an isolated upstream MORPHIR_HOME.

Host independenceThe accepted upstream binary/source revision and executable hash are pinned separately from the MoonBit checkout. Installation state is fresh and isolated.
ProtocolHandshake state, malformed/oversized/split frames, Unicode byte counts, repeated requests, identity mismatch, supported ID behavior, shutdown and timeout/cleanup. Logs never corrupt frames.
SourceAll advertised seed/library Boolean rows, private entries, lets/calls, naming collisions, original/target names, stable diagnostics and source origins. No numeric profile claim.
MEP compatibilityAll combinations in the MEP matrix; exact critical-leaf rejection; omitted offers; unsupported tuples; capability preservation; JSON legacy compatibility; payload bounds/digest mismatch; canonical IR regeneration and drift checks.

Evidence and canonical records

  • Revision 0.6 model-evolution design evidence; historical revision 0.5 specification. Enum extensibility remains an available option.
  • Revision 0.5 MorphirModel terminology evidence; historical revision 0.4 specification. Morphir model is the domain term; IR describes its underlying semantic representation.

  • Revision 0.3 sequence evidence; historical revision 0.2 specification. Interactive sequence receipts validate the proposed drawings, not runtime execution.

  • Critical claim paths; session agreement; method admission.
  • Expanded probe source; 14 assertion results; revision 0.2 analysis receipt; historical revision 0.1 specification. Each receipt binds its own snapshot; the first receipt is preserved.
  • Current runtime and installation contract; claims and packaging versions.

Accepted domain terminology, specification revision 0.4.

The maintainer approved Morphir IR model / IRModel for the rich logical pipeline value, compilation unit for the complete source set compiled together for one package, distribution for the semantic package representation, and model envelope for the storage/transport representation.

The full HTML design now uses IRModel, morphir.frontend.compileModel and morphir.backend.generateModel throughout the proposed public contract, architecture and three call-flow sequences. Source inputs retain compilation-unit meaning. Proposed envelope fields use modelId. Existing JSON operations, loss guard, host/guest ownership, tuple admission, MEP version-policy analysis and A2/F4 dependencies remain unchanged. Method registration and shared wire types remain implementation work.

Current implementation mapping is explicit: MoonBit data.IRUnit, Ion contract ir-unit and unit_id retain their current names and behavior. Historical SDK probes and all r0.1/r0.2/r0.3 receipts are unchanged. A future implementation/API rename needs a source-compatibility and stored-format migration decision; this design revision does not claim that rename is implemented.

CONTEXT.md has local glossary definitions for Compilation unit, Morphir IR model and Model envelope. This is an unstaged tracked documentation change, not part of the already green CI PR #100. The definitions are also recorded below so they are available to agents on other machines before that documentation is committed.

Compilation unit: The complete source set compiled together for one Morphir package, with an explicit package and dependency context.
Morphir IR model: An identified logical pipeline value containing a versioned distribution, metadata, annotations and provenance. It is produced by compilation and can be transformed, analyzed, evaluated or consumed by a generator independently of its storage or transport encoding.
Model envelope: The representation used to store or transmit a Morphir IR model, with the format and integrity information required by that representation.

Validation: all four regenerated Archify artifacts pass validation, delivery, strict provenance checks and browser checks with no diagnostics. Maintainer-approved naming refinement, specification revision 0.5.

Morphir model is the canonical prose/domain term; MorphirModel is the proposed public type name. This supersedes the IRModel naming in revision 0.4. IR remains the term for the underlying semantic representation, its versions and compiler internals. Operation names remain morphir.frontend.compileModel and morphir.backend.generateModel. Compilation unit remains the source input; distribution remains the semantic package representation; model envelope remains the storage/transport representation.

The HTML vocabulary, contract prose, inline SVG, Mermaid flow and explorable architecture/sequence diagrams use MorphirModel. CONTEXT.md now defines Morphir model and uses it in the model-envelope definition. The definition allows models to be created and enriched as well as compiled, transformed, analyzed, evaluated or consumed by generation. Its tracked glossary change remains local, separate from CI PR #100.

The current data.IRUnit API and ir-unit/unit_id stored profile are explicitly mapped and retained. No runtime API or saved-format migration is implemented by this design update. Upstream registration and contract implementation remain pending. Historical specifications, probes and receipts are preserved; A2/F4 dependencies and completion states are unchanged.

Revision 0.6 captures the approved MorphirModel evolution direction and the maintainer's explicit language-tool awareness request.

Model design: structural variants use existing Distribution sum types; checked states/views describe independent guarantees rather than one linear phase enum; enrichments are extensible information. Components declare requires/establishes/preserves/invalidates. Evidence is scoped to model revision, dependency context, scope and producer. Rewrites may invalidate evidence. MEP state/evidence labels remain claims until admitted; unknown required guarantees prevent invocation while optional opaque facts can be preserved. Exact guarantee/state types, schemas and wire fields remain design/implementation work.

Toolbelt awareness, NOT adoption: MoonBit #non_exhaustive allows library enums to gain cases in later releases; downstream patterns cover known cases plus Type::.. for future cases. Distinct from extenum, which permits constructors from other packages. Neither implies unknown-wire-value preservation, a proven model guarantee, protocol support or authority. Maintainer explicitly said not to infer that we should or will use the feature.

Official reference: https://docs.moonbitlang.com/en/latest/language/fundamentals.html#non-exhaustive-enums, nightly edition observed 16 October 2026. Pinned compiler remains v0.10.15+943464bfa. Feature behavior on that pin has NOT been qualified; do that only if selecting the feature. No compiler upgrade or enum modification was requested or performed.

The full updated HTML is stored as this spike's design. Local anchors: .dev/designs/morphir-moonbit-f4-extension.html#model-evolution and #enum-extensibility. CONTEXT.md has model-revision, guarantee and enrichment definitions as local tracked edits; no language implementation details were added to the glossary. Existing data.IRUnit and stored profile remain unchanged. A2/F4 blockers/completion states unchanged.

title: Scheme backend: carry unit metadata in a sidecar file (Level 1)
description: When the Scheme backend generates from an IRUnit, write the .scm file and a sidecar Ion file with the unit's node metadata, provenance and annotations unchanged, like the MoonBit backend's symbols.10n (pkgs/morphir-moonbit/metadata.mbt). Scheme names definitions by canonical Morphir name, so the map from Morphir names to Scheme names is the identity; record it so tools can read it the same way as the MoonBit sidecar. Give the sidecar a profile name (for example morphir-scheme-symbols-v1) and a registered format. When this lands, remove the 'metadata dropped' warning that Plan B of morphir-ukvn.5.22.4 adds for Scheme from rich units. Tests: MoonBit and Elm units through the scheme target keep every metadata entry, byte-stable sidecar, no warning; a plain Scheme unit with no metadata writes no sidecar or an empty one (decide and document). Size: one task.
close_reason: Merged in 215e80f (finos/morphir-moonbit#108). Branch commits 0af6097 (unit entry and symbols sidecar), 4d1c7fb (engine unit backend), 937f579 (merge of Plan B: scheme extends rich_units and drops backend.metadata_dropped), 7330325 (owned origins only), 4d38211 (CLI smoke test). Tests: moon test green on native, js, wasm and wasm-gc for morphir-scheme, morphir-engine and morphir-elm; whole-workspace wasm-gc 1441/1441 after merging main; all CI checks green on 4d38211.

title: Scheme backend: metadata support
description:
Today the Scheme backend (pkgs/morphir-scheme/backend, emit_file) takes plain IR and ignores unit metadata. Plan B of morphir-ukvn.5.22.4 (maintainer decision 2026-10-16, Question 2 Option A) lets the engine generate Scheme from rich units (MoonBit, Elm) by using the unit's IR, dropping its metadata, and reporting a warning that names what was dropped. This epic adds metadata support so nothing is dropped and the Scheme text points back to the source.

A unit's metadata has three parts: node metadata (per declaration: source name, parameter names, source span), provenance (frontend profile, parser version, frontend warnings) and annotations.

Children:
- Level 1: carry the metadata through as a sidecar file. Removes the Plan B warning.
- Level 2: use the metadata in the Scheme text (source-name and position comments).

Out of scope: Level 3, source positions in Scheme runtime errors (several tasks; the workbench evaluates from IR, not Scheme text).

Parallel work: this epic can run beside Plan B. Coordinate on one point: the Scheme generation path for units. If this epic lands first, it defines the scheme generation entry that Plan B uses; if Plan B lands first, Level 1 extends Plan B's entry and removes its warning.
design:
Scheme backend: metadata support (sidecar and source comments)

Epic morphir-ukvn.5.40 · drafted 2026-10-16 · awaiting review · handoff issue finos/morphir-moonbit#99

  • Goal
  • Findings that shape the design
  • Non-goals
  • 1. A unit entry in the Scheme backend
  • 2. The sidecar (Level 1)
  • 3. Source comments (Level 2)
  • 4. Engine wiring
  • 5. Elm declaration origins (task 3)
  • Testing
  • Documentation
  • Verification
  • Beads

Goal

Scheme generated from a MoonBit or Elm unit keeps the unit's metadata and points back to the source.

  • Level 1 (morphir-ukvn.5.40.1): a sidecar file next to the .scm file carries the unit's node metadata, provenance and annotations unchanged, in the shape of the MoonBit backend's symbols.10n.
  • Level 2 (morphir-ukvn.5.40.2): above each define, a comment names the source spelling and position of the declaration.
  • Task 3 (new child, Elm origins): the Elm frontend records declaration origins, so Elm units get real sidecar entries and comments instead of empty ones.

Findings that shape the design

  • Plan B of morphir-ukvn.5.22.4 has not landed. No commit on main and no open PR gives the engine a Scheme path for IRUnit. This work defines that entry; there is no "metadata dropped" warning to remove.
  • The finos/morphir-scheme module cannot import finos/morphir-engine/data: the engine module depends on the Scheme module. The backend therefore defines its own portable unit type, as finos/morphir-moonbit does.
  • Elm units carry no node metadata today. pkgs/morphir-engine/elm/adapter.mbt wraps the compiled IR with IRUnit::new, so metadata and provenance are empty. The Elm frontend records positions only inside IR value attributes, and records no source spelling. Task 3 closes this gap.
  • The engine already registers the ion-binary data format with the .10n extension, and the MoonBit generator already labels symbols.10n with it.
  • The Scheme reader ends a line comment at \n only (reader.mbt). A comment is safe when its text holds no control character or line separator.

Non-goals

  • Level 3, source positions in Scheme runtime errors.
  • A change to canonical names, program behaviour or the output of emit_file on plain IR.
  • Naming recovery, naming facts or targetNames interpretation for Scheme. Scheme names are canonical, so there is nothing to recover.
  • Carrying the source IR inside the sidecar. The checkpoint backend carries IR.

1. A unit entry in the Scheme backend

Package finos/morphir-scheme/backend. The module finos/morphir-scheme gains the dependency moonrockz/ion@0.3.0 (the version the engine and the MoonBit generator use).

New public types, mirroring the Input contract of finos/morphir-moonbit. The struct is named Input, not Unit, because Unit is MoonBit's builtin type.

pub(all) struct NodeMetadata { node_id : String; data : @ion.IonValue }
pub(all) struct Input {
  unit_id : String
  ir : @ir.IRFile
  metadata : Array[NodeMetadata]
  annotations : Array[@ion.SymbolToken]
  provenance : Array[@ion.IonValue]
}
pub fn Input::new(unit_id : String, ir : @ir.IRFile) -> Input   // empty metadata and provenance
pub(all) struct Output { source : String; symbols : Bytes }
pub const SYMBOLS_PROFILE : String = "morphir-scheme-symbols-v1"
pub const SYMBOLS_SUFFIX : String = ".symbols.10n"
pub fn emit_unit(unit : Input, source_path~ : String? = None) -> Output raise

emit_unit emits the same forms as emit_file, in the same order, with a comment line before a define when the unit has a valid hint for it (section 3), and builds the sidecar (section 2). emit_file is unchanged and its output stays byte for byte identical. emit_unit(Input::new(id, ir)).source == emit_file(ir) for every IR, because a unit without metadata has no hints.

Internally emit_package takes a hint lookup (fqname to comment text or none). emit_file passes an empty lookup.

2. The sidecar (Level 1)

One binary Ion value, written with @ion_binary.write_binary_value, annotated morphir_scheme_symbols. Fields, in this order:

FieldValue
profile"morphir-scheme-symbols-v1"
naming_policy"scheme-canonical-identity-v1": the generated name of every symbol is its canonical Morphir name
unit_idthe unit id
source_annotationsthe unit's annotation tokens, in order, as Ion symbols
source_provenancethe unit's provenance values, in order, unchanged
source_nodesthe sorted owned node ids of the unit, from @identities.nodes(unit_id, ir)
metadataone {node_id, data} record per unit metadata entry, in the unit's order, data unchanged
symbolsone record per emitted define, in emission order (below)

A symbol record:

FieldValue
fqnamecanonical fqname, for example pricing:app/main#eligible
generated_namethe same string: the map is the identity
scheme_symbolthe symbol as written in the .scm file, r:<fqname> after symbol_text escaping
publictrue when the value's access and its module's access are both Public
source_nodevalue:<fqname>
generated_nodescheme:define:<fqname>
origins[source_node, source_node + "/body"]

Constructor registrations (%morphir-register-constructor) are not symbols; they define no name.

The sidecar has no warnings, naming_allocations, consumed_naming_facts, unvalidated_predicates or source_ir_json field. The README lists these differences from morphir-moonbit-symbols-v1 so a reader of both knows what to expect. Metadata is copied without ownership validation: the engine validates rich units when the frontend returns them, and the backend must not refuse what the engine accepted. Every input is ordered, so the bytes are a pure function of the unit: the sidecar is byte-stable.

File naming, decided by the engine (section 4): <unit>.scm and <unit>.symbols.10n, format ion-binary.

Plain units. emit_unit always returns a sidecar, even for a unit with no metadata, so a consumer of the backend API can rely on its presence. The engine calls emit_unit only for rich frontends, so a plain Scheme or IR JSON source keeps producing one .scm file and no sidecar. The README states both rules.

3. Source comments (Level 2)

For each emitted define with fqname F, the hint is the unit metadata entry with node id value:F.

Hint reading follows pkgs/morphir-moonbit/source_hints.mbt: a field counts only when it occurs exactly once in its struct; a span needs all four coordinates as non-negative integers with end not before start. In addition:

  • The entry is ignored when the unit has two or more entries for the same node id.
  • declaration.name must be a string that is non-empty, at most 256 characters, and holds no character below U+0020, no U+007F, no U+0085, no U+2028 and no U+2029. Otherwise the whole hint is ignored and no comment is written. This is what stops a hostile name (a newline, a carriage return) from ending the comment early. A ; in a name is harmless inside a line comment and is kept.
  • declaration.path, when present, is a string under the same rules. It names the source file of the declaration (Elm units span many files). When absent, the location uses source_path~, and when that is None, the unit id.
  • The span, when present and valid, adds :<start_line>:<start_column> after the path, as recorded, with no conversion. The coordinate_profile field of the hint names the convention and is not interpreted.

The comment is ;; <name> (<path>) or ;; <name> (<path>:<line>:<column>), on its own line directly above the (define ...) form. A name hint with no valid span still gets the path form. No name hint means no comment.

;; eligible (src/Main.mbt:2:0)
(define r:pricing:app/main#eligible (lambda () ...))

4. Engine wiring

Package pkgs/morphir-engine.

  • Backend gains emit_unit : ((@data.IRUnit, String) -> Array[GeneratedFile] raise)?. The second argument is the source path the engine reports for the unit (path in execute_content). Each GeneratedFile.path is relative to the job destination. register_backend keeps its signature and sets emit_unit to None.
  • New Engine::register_unit_backend(name, extension, emit, emit_unit). Engine::new() registers scheme with it: emit = @backend.emit_file; emit_unit converts the IRUnit to a backend Input, calls @backend.emit_unit(unit, source_path=Some(path)) and returns [<unit>.scm (Text, "scheme"), <unit>.symbols.10n (Binary, "ion-binary")].
  • Planning. A job is a unit job when its frontend is not a FileCompiler and its backend has emit_unit. The frontend.typed_backend_required refusal applies only when the frontend is rich, the job is not a checkpoint, and the backend has no emit_unit. A unit job keeps the checkpoint rules for transforms and exposed_modules ("metadata lineage is required"), since a transform would leave the metadata pointing at nodes that no longer exist. Job records unit_backend : Bool.
  • Execution. In the inference stage the unit flows through (the existing checkpoint flag includes unit jobs). In the backend stage a unit job calls emit_unit with {..checkpoint_unit, distribution: ir} and pushes one ContentArtifact per returned file at join(job.destination, file.path), with source = path and the file's format. Other jobs are unchanged.
  • Plan::requires_byte_write() returns true for a unit job, so hosts use a byte publisher. Engine::run (text-only legacy report) keeps refusing rich units.
  • No warning is reported for a unit job. Frontend warnings in provenance are reported as today.

5. Elm declaration origins (task 3)

Packages pkgs/morphir-elm/frontend and pkgs/morphir-engine/elm.

  • The frontend records, for each value declaration of a module kept in the output, its source name, source path, the range of the declaration's name node, and the names and ranges of the lifted parameters (the arguments that become IR inputs, as lower_value_definition lifts them). compile_project returns compile_project_output(...).ir and is otherwise unchanged. Origins are sorted by module path then name. The Elm frontend stays free of Ion. 
    pub(all) struct DeclarationOrigin {
  module_name : @ir.Path
  name : @ir.Name
  source_name : String
  path : String
  span : @ir.SourceLocation
  parameters : Array[(String, @ir.SourceLocation)]
}
pub(all) struct ProjectOutput { ir : @ir.IRFile; origins : Array[DeclarationOrigin] }
pub fn compile_project_output(sources, package_name, exposed, output~) -> ProjectOutput raise ElmFailed
  • The engine Elm adapter builds the rich unit from ProjectOutput: one metadata entry value:<fqname> per origin with declaration = {name, path, coordinate_profile: "elm-syntax-position-v1", start_line, start_column, end_line, end_column} and parameters = [ {name, path, coordinate_profile, ...} ], and one provenance record morphir_elm_frontend::{language: "elm", profile: "library", parser: "moonrockz/krueger", parser_version: "0.8.0", unit_id}. Annotations stay [morphir_pipeline]. Every node id is owned, so IRUnit::validate passes.
  • Coordinates are recorded as the parser gives them (rows and columns as @ir.SourceLocation already holds them for Elm value attributes). The coordinate_profile names the convention; nothing converts it.
  • Amended during execution. A Morphir JSON checkpoint, the default output of a morphir.json project, cannot carry unit metadata and is refused rather than made lossy. Origins are therefore a second Elm profile, library-origins, selected per project with frontend.profile; the default library profile is unchanged. Hint paths are workspace-relative (src/My/Pkg/Api.elm), as the engine reports MoonBit sources, so comments from both frontends read alike. Whether origins should become the default with a drop-with-warning JSON checkpoint, as Plan B does for Scheme, is a maintainer decision.
  • The MoonBit generator reads spelling hints only with MoonBit provenance (moonbit_origins), so MoonBit generated from Elm keeps its names. Its symbols.10n grows by the new metadata; the pinned size in pkgs/morphir-engine/elm/adapter_test.mbt is re-pinned if it moves.

Testing

Backend (pkgs/morphir-scheme/backend)

  • emit_unit on a unit with no metadata gives the emit_file text and a sidecar whose metadata and source_provenance are empty.
  • A unit with a declaration hint gives ;; eligible (src/Main.mbt:2:0) above the matching define and no other change.
  • A hint with a newline, a carriage return, U+2028 or an empty name gives no comment; a ; in the name is kept; a duplicate entry for one node id gives no comment; a bad span gives the path-only form; a declaration.path field wins over source_path~.
  • The sidecar reads back with @ion_binary.read_binary_value and re-encodes to the same bytes; two runs give the same bytes; the annotation, profile, metadata entries and provenance equal the input; the symbols list the emitted defines with identity names and the expected public flags.

Engine (pkgs/morphir-engine, moonbit/, elm/)

  • A MoonBit library unit through pipeline.backend = "scheme": two artifacts, formats scheme and ion-binary, requires_byte_write() true, no warnings, every metadata entry of the unit in the sidecar, the expected comment lines in the .scm text, and the text evaluates in a Scheme runtime to the same answers as before.
  • An Elm project through scheme: two artifacts, metadata entries equal to the frontend origins, comments with the Elm source name and path, for example ;; isEligible (src/Pricing/Main.elm:5:1).
  • A plain Scheme source through scheme: one artifact, text byte for byte as before.
  • A rich unit through ir-json still fails with frontend.typed_backend_required; a rich unit through scheme with a transform fails with the lineage message.
  • Elm frontend: compile_project_output origins for a small project cover kept modules only, with the expected names, paths, spans and parameters.

Documentation

  • pkgs/morphir-scheme/README.md: a section "Units, sidecar and source comments" with the API, the sidecar fields, the differences from the MoonBit profile, the plain-unit rule, the comment grammar and the hint rules.
  • pkgs/morphir-engine/README.md: the backends list and the "Rich source frontends" paragraph name the unit backend; register_unit_backend documented next to register_backend.
  • pkgs/morphir-engine/elm/README.md: the origins and provenance an Elm unit carries.

Verification

  • moon test in pkgs/morphir-scheme, pkgs/morphir-engine and pkgs/morphir-elm on native, js, wasm and wasm-gc.
  • moon fmt --check (the body of mise run lint:moonbit), moon info to refresh the committed pkg.generated.mbti files.
  • On this machine mise cannot install MoonBit for Windows ARM64; the installed ~/.moon/bin/moon.exe is used directly.

Beads

  • morphir-ukvn.5.40.1 is task 1 (sections 1, 2, 4 and the engine tests for Level 1).

description: Deliver native renderer-to-host commands for Proton 0.3.4, then isolated native Scheme jobs and read-only explicitly granted workspace access.
