design:
Workbench · native services · morphir-etg2.15

Proton owns the local service

Give the desktop app a native command connection, isolated execution and explicitly granted workspace access. Keep the shared Workbench UI and the qualified invocation, execution and receipt semantics.

Historical native implementation snapshot. Design revision 25 · merged baseline d6282b4, including MoonBit 0.10.15, Krueger 0.8.0 from PR #96, Node 24.22.0 from PR #77, native workers/workspaces and the picker cleanup from PR #101 and offline native frame qualification from PR #102. The baseline also includes the shared Morphir model vocabulary from PR #104, native descriptor admission from PR #105 and native reply/effect admission from PR #106, the unified engine/Elm workbench compilation from PR #103 and MoonBit generator extension from PR #107. Native handshake and isolated typed jobs are complete. Read-only workspace grants and the public native-profile draft are merged. The bundled pair uses accepted public native envelopes from PR #109. At that baseline, independent reply/client/owner lifecycle MCK and packaged-target qualification were pending. The protocol and lifecycle MCK slices have since delivered. Actual packaged Linux/Windows qualification remains open in morphir-etg2.15.5.8.

Current campaign status, 18 October 2026, after both codec merges

The original Workbench campaign remains active. Capability checking implementation morphir-etg2.16 is delivered: 7 of 7 tasks, 100%, 7:0 completed to remaining. Capability domain modeling morphir-etg2.17 is also delivered. Those closed tasks do not complete the broader campaign.

100%

Strict remains the default. Frozen compatibility identifiers keep their published spelling; current domain language uses capabilities, capability verification, capability validation and executions. The qualified HTTP gateway offers its own provider. Rust protocol v1 still advertises executions:false. Linux and Windows packaged hosts keep operations: []; this reconciliation grants no new runtime or native authority.

Workbench #143 is merged as 230e3de, and the coordinated codec/comparison contribution in Morphir #1066 is merged as 7920a6b6. Final-head CI passed in both repositories. The full merged Workbench check also passed, including concurrent #142 host-embedding changes; the Workbench/native sources match the qualified head. Parent main includes concurrent #1065 trait reference fixtures/documentation and its isolated mise task; its Workbench/MCK/runtime sources and relevant Cargo/SDK pins match qualified candidate aaa40334. The final 96-case corpus has exact 68/28 operation subsets; all 51 focused adapter tests pass on four targets. The 44 frozen-kit reports cover 7,428 observations, and eight subset reports add 384. This evidence does not finish the remaining worksheet, artifact, model-reference or packaged-target work. The current campaign audit records the delivery gates.

Earlier dated implementation snapshots below remain evidence of their original contracts and candidates. Read this section and the remaining-work checklist for current status, rather than interpreting a historical "next" statement as a new task selection.

Genuine remaining campaign work

All seven original morphir-etg2.15.5 children are closed. Public native mapping, shared UI adoption and independent frame/reply/client/owner lifecycle qualification are delivered. The parent stays open for the new packaged target task morphir-etg2.15.5.8. The stronger macOS test separately proves actual owner-spawned workers leave the OS table at reload, session close and normal AppKit quit, including an actual unreaped-child regression. Fallback package qualification does not establish Linux or Windows native workers or workspace grants. Durable restart recovery remains an explicit published exclusion.

What we have now

PR #91 provides renderer-bound native sessions. PR #93 owns isolated native typed evaluation jobs on qualified macOS Apple Silicon; browser compilation and explicit Local Scheme still use browser workers. Standalone and authenticated connected HTTP/RPC modes remain qualified. Read-only workspace grants, native descriptor admission and the native reply/effect boundary are merged. Coordinated public host/renderer activation remains pending.

Native discovery reuses the engine’s merged #88 workspace and morphir.json semantics. The desktop read path executes no configuration scripts and has no separate Elm compiler. Saved models pass through the shared compiled codec before replacing the explorer model.

Proposed integration

Mermaid architecture source
flowchart LR
  UI[Shared Workbench UI] --> Adapter[Planned native adapter]
  Adapter -->|Page-bound IPC| Host[Planned Proton command host]
  Host --> Owner[Shared immutable job owner]
  Owner -->|One claim| Worker[Planned isolated native worker]
  Worker --> Engine[Existing typed evaluator]
  Host -->|Native picker| Grants[Planned opaque workspace grants]
  Grants -->|Bounded read only| Files[Granted workspace files]

Transport and session ownership

One shared client state machine

Extract the request transport from JobClient, keeping receipt admission, unknown-submission handling, cancellation, reconnect and lost-release reconciliation in the existing client. HTTP and native transports supply the same admitted domain values.

Map native operations to session, submit, query, cancel and release. The renderer never receives internal claim or complete commands.

Typed Proton boundary

Pin Proton, CLI, contract package and helpers to 0.3.4. Register typed application commands with App::commands. Inspect CommandContext for the native window, source origin and current page instance. A JavaScript bridge property is discovery, not authorization.

Carry business payloads as bounded raw UTF-8 JSON text into the existing duplicate-aware decoder. Ordinary typed JSON decoding alone does not prove closed shape, bounds or duplicate rejection.

  1. The implemented private bootstrap uses bridgeVersion 0.1.0-draft.1 and opaque page-scoped identities. Qualified packages offer jobs and workspace; unqualified operations remain absent. Typed open/check/close commands accept string payloads and require native main-window/app-origin/page context. This is separate from the proposed public mapping. For that mapping, negotiate a proposed exact morphir/workbench/native mapping starting at 0.1.0-draft.1. Its final shape is an upstream design contribution, not a shipped claim.
  2. The native host creates identities and binds the session to the trusted main window and page instance. Validate that binding on every command and before delivering asynchronous results.
  3. A reload or navigation revokes the page session and grants, initiates owned-worker cleanup, and requires a new handshake. Do not promise cross-page or durable recovery in this slice.
  4. An explicit connected launch takes precedence and registers no native commands for the remote page. A development-server entry requires its own explicit exact-origin policy. Unrelated windows, frames and external navigation gain no native authority.
  5. A broken native connection after admission retains uncertainty. Do not silently retry on HTTP or the local browser worker. Standalone remains available when selected before execution.

Native execution and cleanup

Reuse apps/morphir-workbench/jobs/Host and the portable engine Session. The host captures the rich IR unit and typed input suite once, authorizes the public entry, and claims a job once. Run the existing typed evaluator in a packaged child executable, keeping evaluation off the CEF event loop.

ConcernRequired behavior
OwnershipNative session owns queue, child handles, snapshots and receipts. Renderer edits cannot mutate admitted work. Do not accept executable paths, shell commands or environment overrides from renderer input.
BoundsRetain the existing 1 MiB host business-frame limit, eight retained jobs and 16 MiB retained-evidence budget. Specify bounded framing for child I/O and cap stdout/stderr. Start with at most two active workers and a 30-second deadline; independently measure native allocation/process limits rather than borrowing the JavaScript heap-limit claim.
CancellationAcknowledge the request through the shared owner. Terminate the owned process using the platform process API, await confirmed exit and preserve a previously captured returned outcome if it wins the race. An unconfirmed stop is not a terminal receipt.
OutcomesAdmit returned values against captured declarations. Preserve Result.Err, SDK/model failures, provider failures and separate cleanup failures. Release only terminal jobs; preserve same-identity reconciliation when the release reply is lost.
ShutdownStop new claims, cancel queued work, stop and reap active children, then close the native session. Wire this into Proton lifecycle hooks. If cleanup fails, report it explicitly instead of claiming success.

This first native provider evaluates the qualified Scheme-backed typed pipeline. Elm/MoonBit generation does not imply generated Elm/MoonBit execution. Generated browser execution remains a separate phase.

Feasibility on MoonBit 0.10.15: a local native executable calls the existing typed evaluator with the pricing model and returns exact Decimal 37.5, without a Node runtime. Probe receipt. Production worker packaging, bounded IPC, resource limits and shutdown qualification subsequently landed in PR #93, with evidence below. The installed async process API documents structured child ownership and waiting for termination on cancellation; actual host behavior must still be tested.

Read-only workspace grants

Pinned Proton 0.3.4 exposes proton/core.CommandWindow::choose_directory(title, path) -> String?. Its facade routes through the trusted native window and maps an empty dialog result to None. Use that typed host API, with host-selected options, then recheck the captured native page/session after the asynchronous picker returns before issuing a grant. The command is bound and native filesystem containment acceptance passes. Real macOS packaged picker selection/cancellation, byte-exact original export Blobs and page-session qualification pass in PR #97; other packaged platforms remain unqualified.

The trusted native directory picker chooses a root. The host retains its canonical root and returns an opaque grant identity; a renderer-supplied path cannot create a grant. Grants are scoped to the current native page session and can be revoked.

  • Resolve project membership and morphir.json through the existing engine, including PR #88. Return project/model identities through the shared provider and project UI.
  • Use relative locators within a grant. Reject traversal and outside-root symbolic links, check canonical membership at open, and qualify replacement/symlink races with platform-specific file APIs. Do not claim that a string-prefix path check provides containment.
  • Bound directory discovery, file count, individual reads and aggregate source bytes. Align engine/project budgets before enabling the operation; existing 16 MiB browser model import and 1 MiB job submission are different boundaries.
  • Retain original IR format versions and rich Ion metadata. Surface revoked grants, missing files, invalid configuration and unavailable bindings as distinct diagnostics in the existing bottom panel.

Grant-scoped writes, background artifact publication, watches and persistent grants are later work. Explicit user exports use the separate native save dialog.

Publish the transport mapping upstream

FINOS already has the host HTTP profile and the transport-neutral invocation, jobs and terminal contracts. Reuse those shapes. Contribute the native command/session lifecycle, grant scope, operation mapping, error mapping and independent positive/negative fixtures to finos/morphir before advertising the native profile.

Freeze existing connected v1, HTTP host draft.1, jobs draft.1 and terminal draft.5. A native mapping must explicitly negotiate its own exact draft; it cannot quietly reinterpret the HTTP profile. Protocol review and independent qualification are part of the implementation.

Implementation checklist

Source seams and local evidence

  • Desktop entry and explicit loopback launch, pinned dependencies and isolated desktop workspace.
  • Shared bootstrap, job client and local/connected adapters.
  • Bounded native-reusable host admission, portable snapshot owner and qualified HTTP worker lifecycle.
  • Pinned dependency source: proton/command/typed_registrar.mbt, proton/core/pkg.generated.mbti and proton/README.md. The local module directly declares proton_contract@0.3.4; a transitive import alone fails MoonBit dependency checking.

Commit 491385c implements the first native boundary. Typed application commands are registered only for the bundled main renderer, and are absent from explicit connected launches. Every call uses the native window/origin/page context. Reload revokes the page binding; close shuts it down. The UI shows Desktop local, and ?mode=standalone explicitly retains the browser path.

Owned native evaluation workers

Typed evaluation in packaged Proton uses native-owned child workers on qualified macOS Apple Silicon. The native service reuses the shared job owner, immutable invocation snapshots and compiled receipt admission. Each child runs the packaged executable in worker mode without initializing CEF. title: Task 3: Preserve Float32 and Float64 arithmetic and conversion policies
description:
### Task 3: Preserve Float32 and Float64 arithmetic and conversion policies

## What to build

Add typed Float/Double source expressions and explicit numeric bridges. Preserve source Float32 rounding boundaries and exact source representation metadata; use existing Double where its contract matches. Add checked exact float-to-Int conversion and clearly named rounding/truncation alternatives in Int where needed.

## Acceptance criteria

- Basic arithmetic and comparisons match the source contract, with single evaluation and explicit Float32 rounding after each required operation.
- Verify 24-bit and 53-bit precision boundaries, signed zero, subnormals, fractional conversion and integer ranges.
- Nonfinite and exceptional execution outcomes use an explicit observation representation; current nonfinite IR literal refusal remains intact unless separately implemented and qualified.
- Float32/64 conversion additions carry extension metadata and separate conformance; rounding conversions never count as exact.
- Engine/CLI, Scheme, generated consumer and Ion replay exercise the same cases across qualified target/mode lanes, preserving existing profiles.

## Blocked by

Task 2.

title: Task 4: Resolve and qualify a curated numeric math SDK

### Task 4: Resolve and qualify a curated numeric math SDK

## What to build

Reuse shared pinned source binding resolver morphir-ukvn.1.10.12.4 rather than implementing a separate binding environment. Extend its finite immutable mapping of actual pinned MoonBit package/alias/signatures to canonical Morphir SDK declarations with the numeric operations qualified here. Add source and generator coverage for sqrt, pow, sin, cos and documented abs/rounding/conversion functions with matched semantics.

## Acceptance criteria

- Probe actual source/core/SDK syntax and signatures. An alias string cannot register an arbitrary package or native call.
- The pure frontend receives resolved bindings; adapter-owned resolution does not perform implicit dependency downloads or host execution during compilation.
- Pin the supplied package/tree identity and freeze the mapping in the selected profile. Unknown/wrong-signature/shadowed bindings refuse.
- Independently expected exact/domain cases and reference vectors compare source, Scheme and generated execution. Declare per-function exact-bit or ULP/error contracts before admission.
- Publish a source/evaluator/generator/target support matrix. Preserve classic/addition classification and metadata through checkpoints and generated receipts.

## Blocked by

Task 3 and shared pinned source binding resolver morphir-ukvn.1.10.12.4.

title: Task 5: Support explicit Decimal SDK library calculations
description:
### Task 5: Support explicit Decimal SDK library calculations

## What to build

A closed Decimal source binding supports exact construction, add/subtract/multiply, comparisons, rounding and an explicitly selected division API. This is an SDK type rather than a MoonBit built-in scalar. Retain original literal scale and spelling separately from numerical normalization.

## Acceptance criteria

- Explicit SDK package/type resolution and concrete signatures compile through engine/CLI, Scheme and generated libraries.
- Probe supported source calls and qualify numerical coefficients/exponents, trailing-zero/zero normalization, rounding ties and the SDK minimum exponent of -32.
- Select a division form whose return/default/error contract is supported by this source subset; do not imply general Maybe/pattern admission.
- Correctly owned precision and conversion metadata survives Ion replay; checked JSON behavior remains explicit.
- Publish the complete numeric profile only after its full admitted subset passes all required lanes.

## Blocked by

Task 4.

title: Task 6: Qualify installed numeric libraries and publish their evidence matrix

## What to build

An installed acceptance gate exercises every offered numeric profile through supported npm/native CLI distributions, actual generated consumers, checkpoints and typed SDK extension admission. Consolidate source type/function/target/mode evidence without confusing bindings with source support.

## Acceptance criteria

- Every public numeric entry has independent expected rows covering scalar boundaries, arithmetic, conversions, math domains and Decimal behavior. Generated visibility and wrapper ABI are checked.
- Compare original source, Scheme and generated execution on native, JS, Wasm and Wasm-GC debug/release as claimed; record actual installed OS/package coverage separately.
- Decode and inspect primary Ion text/binary receipts; checked JSON views retain exact numeric observations or reject unsupported conversion. Test replay with unknown metadata retained.
- Missing extensions, unsupported functions, bad numeric inputs, cancellation and operation-cost budget exhaustion refuse before publication.
- Verify enabled/disabled observations, warnings and .morphir/logs defaults with explicit path overrides retained. No new implicit host grants.
- Required repository checks and profile-specific installed acceptance pass on the actual PR revision; bead closure includes commits, exact evidence and limitations. This is a numeric-only completion gate. Task 1: Qualify signed Int32 libraries through the full local pipeline

morphir-ukvn.1.10.12.1.1 · in_progress

Hard prerequisites: morphir-ukvn.1.10.12.3, morphir-ukvn.1.10.12.2

What to build

Reuse shared typed-library foundation morphir-ukvn.1.10.12.3 and the existing N1 handoff. The shared milestone may land with this task, but it has separate scoped evidence and does not close N1. Complete the Int32-and-Bool library profile using explicit source types, literals, +, -, *, comparisons, immutable lets, conditionals and acyclic same-file calls. Existing SDK Int32 wrappers represent source boundaries; exact Morphir Int intermediates and explicit width normalization preserve source arithmetic. Version source representation metadata and attach it to correct type/value/declaration owners without changing neighboring facts.

Acceptance criteria

  • Use canonical MoonBit Int32 source spelling. Use compiler/core 0.10.15+943464bfa from prerequisite morphir-ukvn.1.10.12.2 and verify numeric parser admission before implementing the source profile. The previous 0.10.14+7d59c7ec9 compiler rejected the new names with diagnostic 4032. Preserve historical probe receipts as historical evidence; requalify the current spellings under the aligned pin.
  • Qualify legacy Int/UInt compatibility aliases separately where offered; preserve authored spelling and canonical resolved type in metadata, together with compiler/profile identity. Morphir arbitrary-precision Int and its SDK module retain their existing names.
  • Probe the pinned parser and compiler for admitted syntax, minimum/maximum literals and signed overflow/underflow. Record supported operators and diagnostics.
  • Compile mixed Bool/Int32 libraries through the real engine and CLI, preserving naming, public/private entries, evaluation order, origins, limits and existing Boolean defaults.
  • Expose the necessary existing Int32 conversions in the generator and evaluator. Add a separately classified source-width helper only if portable lowering cannot cover it. Check actual generated consumer wrapper ABI.
  • Demonstrate independent expected boundary values against original source, Scheme and generated MoonBit on all four targets/debug-release lanes selected for this profile.
  • Ion text/binary replay preserves source precision, conversion origin and unknown metadata; incompatible JSON export refuses loss. Warnings work with logs off.
  • Add the complete profile descriptor only after its promised subset passes; no claim for other numeric forms.

Blocked by

Shared typed-library foundation morphir-ukvn.1.10.12.3. The existing compiler-pin prerequisite is closed. This is a coordination/extraction of active N1 work, not a new competing implementation. No F4/A2 packaging requirement.

Runtime mapping: Morphir SDK Int16/Int32/Int64 use MoonBit Int16Value/Int32Value/Int64Value wrappers because the built-in names are reserved in 0.10.15. Conversion functions and semantic IR identities retain their contracts. Pin PR: https://github.com/finos/morphir-moonbit/pull/89.

Task 2: Support all scalar integer forms and explicit Int conversions

What to build

Numeric formatting/parsing and other numeric String calls are explicit follow-ups with only the relevant qualified numeric-type prerequisites. They must not recreate a blanket dependency on N2-N6.

A2/F4/MEP retain their existing integration gates and do not become local source prerequisites. Maintainer merge/release rules remain intact. New tasks are open and unassigned; none is claimed or marked complete by this scheduling change.

Durable record and local views

Beads is authoritative. The String implementation plan is morphir-ukvn.1.10.13.2; the existing String semantic-design task is linked as Task 1. Shared tasks remain under the numeric epic and have both numeric and String lane labels. The numeric design and rendered plan also record the revised dependency contract.

The HTML plan is the parallel String implementation plan. Local files under .dev/ are review artifacts and must not be committed. Every closure records repository commits, scoped tests and limitations.

title: MoonBit numeric libraries and math SDK support
description: Extend the MoonBit source frontend beyond Boolean libraries with scalar numeric types, explicit source representation metadata, Int conversions and versioned SDK extensions, preserving executable source arithmetic. Deliver independently qualified end-to-end slices through engine/CLI, Ion, Scheme and generated MoonBit. Numeric and String work proceed in parallel through shared typed-library and binding-resolution milestones; A2/F4 packaging remains separate. HTML specification and implementation plan are stored in this bead and its plan children; no implementation or release is claimed by creation.
design:
Skip to specification
Morphir / MoonBit

Numeric libraries
Specification revision 0.5
15 October 2026

01 / What this unlocks02 / Existing foundation03 / Component contracts04 / Numeric forms05 / Arithmetic and conversion06 / Precision and metadata07 / Classic SDK and additions08 / Source calls and selection09 / Ion and JSON10 / Delivery slices11 / Evidence and diagnostics12 / Parallel String delivery13 / Decisions and boundaries14 / Sources and tracker
A7 / numeric source capabilities

Numbers that retain their source meaning.

Compile typed MoonBit numeric libraries into Morphir, preserve their source precision, and execute them through the existing engine, SDK and MoonBit generator. Develop Strings in parallel through explicitly shared milestones.

Proposed implementationSource language: moonbitIon preferredMorphir JSON supported

Tracked by morphir-ukvn.1.10.12. Initial design baseline 6f9f7e8; the compiler upgrade is based on newer main 6025318. Selected compiler/core pin: 0.10.15+943464bfa. This document specifies future source support. Its compiler probe and diagrams do not establish numeric frontend support.

01 / outcome

Grow the library pipeline beyond Boolean decisions

Model quantities, prices, thresholds and calculations in ordinary MoonBit source. Keep the existing public/private functions, direct calls, immutable lets, readable naming and diagnostics. Add scalar typing and SDK resolution without making parsing, type checking, metadata or code generation depend on host I/O.

Signed 32-bit arithmetic→All scalar integers→Float and Double→Math and Decimal→Installed numeric qualification

A useful first library

pub fn total(quantity : Int32, unit_price : Int32) -> Int32 {
  let subtotal = quantity * unit_price
  if subtotal > 1000 { subtotal - 100 } else { subtotal }
}

Proposed accepted source. Arithmetic must retain the pinned compiler's signed 32-bit behavior. This example is not yet accepted by the current Boolean frontend.

Portable numbers, visible origin

Convert fixed-width values through the SDK Int family. Perform exact integer calculations in Morphir's arbitrary-precision representation. Preserve the original MoonBit type, width and spelling as addressed metadata.

When the source expression itself has bounded arithmetic, lower its wrap or other defined behavior explicitly. A mathematical intermediate can be arbitrary precision without changing the observable source result.

02 / current implementation

Most of the runtime foundation already exists

ComponentAvailable nowNumeric stage adds
Pure source frontendExplicit Bool signatures, acyclic same-file calls, lets, conditionals and source origins.Resolved scalar types, exact numeric literals, typed operators, finite SDK bindings.
Engine and CLILanguage/provider/profile selection, IRUnit hooks, observations, installed execution and Ion checkpoints.Additive profile descriptors, SDK requirements, numeric limits and end-to-end receipts.
SDK and Scheme248 classic typed bindings and Scheme adapters; arbitrary-precision Integer; signed Int8–Int64 wrappers; Float64 and numerical Decimal.Additional conversion contracts, source-width arithmetic where required, and separate extension conformance.
MoonBit generatorNumeric scalar construction and 57 audited SDK adapters, including arithmetic, comparisons, rounding and selected Decimal operations.Fixed-width and additional SDK adapters, explicit Float32 behavior, imported-source function mapping.
StringsSDK Text and Character plus String bindings exist; IR String literals already generate.An independently qualified source capability using the shared typed foundation and existing audited String adapters.

The 248 SDK bindings and 57 generator adapters describe different inventories. A binding becomes an advertised source capability only after source admission, lowering, evaluation, generation and selected target lanes have evidence.

03 / architecture

Extend contracts at their existing boundaries

The diagram shows the landed Boolean path that numbers will extend. Open the explorable version for source references and SVG export. Numeric semantics in the following sections are proposed.

Open the complete pipeline diagram. Its automated artifact and browser checks pass; no perceptual-review claim is made.

ContractResponsibilityConfiguration and replacement
Source type resolverResolve scalar spellings and explicit SDK aliases against an immutable environment. Distinguish a local shadow from a known SDK binding.A versioned source binding environment supplied by the adapter, without filesystem or network access in the pure compiler.
Numeric descriptionDescribe semantic IR type, original representation, exact literal parsing, bounds and conversion policy.A closed typed inventory shared by admission and lowering. Unknown descriptions refuse; metadata cannot register new executable behavior.
Operator loweringSelect exact arithmetic, explicit source-width normalization, floating operations or a named SDK call. Preserve evaluation order and single evaluation.Profile-bound semantics and explicit required SDK contracts. No mutable global numeric mode.
SDK specification and adaptersProvide typed signatures, implementations, Scheme bindings and generator adapters for an exact supported inventory.Classic specification remains available; additional capabilities require a separately identified extension profile.
Metadata producerAttach source representation and conversion receipts to the correct node owner, preserving other facts.A versioned payload contract, distinct from optional diagnostic logging and from executable semantics.
Host and engineFreeze selection and dependencies, enforce budgets, persist artifacts, execute approved operations and report evidence.Reuse existing host grants, provider admission, cancellation and output publication rules.
04 / source inventory

Use current MoonBit numeric names

The target inventory is ten scalar source types, using Int32 and UInt32 as the current preferred names. Current MoonBit accepts Int and UInt as compatibility aliases and its formatter uses the explicit-width names. These source names are distinct from Morphir's arbitrary-precision Int and its Int SDK module.

The maintainer selected compiler/core 0.10.15+943464bfa. Upgrade task morphir-ukvn.1.10.12.2 updates development, managed acquisition, embedding and telemetry pins together. The previous 0.10.14+7d59c7ec9 pin rejects Int32/UInt32; the explicit 0.10.15 probe accepts them. Fresh-cache CI exposed incompatible legacy manifests. The upgrade also selects parser 0.4.5, lexer 0.4.3 and compatible maintained dependencies; two small CLI libraries retain their behavior as attributed local workspace modules. Stable 0.10.15 does not enable LLVM, and the old LLVM nightly rejects current numeric names. That lane independently pins 0.10.15+1e9f6672d-nightly with matching compiler/core archive hashes. Boolean frontend and site qualification pass locally with the new dependencies. Broader qualification and PR #89 remain tracked by the upgrade task. Numeric frontend admission remains N1 work.

MoonBit formRepresentation factsProposed Morphir contractDelivery
Int32Signed 32-bit; legacy source alias IntExisting SDK Int32 boundary type and exact Morphir Int working values.N1
Int16, Int64Signed 16-bit, 64-bitExisting SDK Int16/Int64 boundaries and checked conversions.N2
Byte, UInt16, UInt32, UInt64Unsigned 8-bit, 16-bit, 32-bit, 64-bitAdded SDK Int-module unsigned boundary types and exact widening conversions.N2
BigIntSigned arbitrary precisionSDK Basics.Int; representation receipt names the MoonBit source form.N2
FloatIEEE binary32, 24 significand bits including the implicit leading bit for normal valuesAdded Float32 numeric boundary/operations, using an explicit round-to-binary32 operation at every required source rounding point.N3
DoubleIEEE binary64, 53 significand bits for normal valuesExisting SDK Basics.Float and qualified Float64 operations.N3
SDK DecimalLibrary type, not a MoonBit built-in scalarExisting SDK Decimal with its exact numerical coefficient/exponent semantics and separately retained source scale.N5

The MoonBit SDK runtime now names its fixed-width wrappers Int16Value, Int32Value and Int64Value, because 0.10.15 reserves the built-in names. Their canonical Morphir SDK type identities and conversion functions retain their contracts. See the SDK migration note. N1 must map semantic SDK boundary types to these actual MoonBit wrappers.

MoonBit has no native signed Int8 in this inventory; the classic SDK's Int8 remains supported as its own SDK type. SIMD vectors, arbitrary user-defined numeric traits and foreign numeric types are outside this stage. Future compiler additions require an inventory revision and evidence.

Finite integer literals are decoded exactly from their radix and suffix, without passing through machine Int or Double. Preserve authored radix, separators and suffix in metadata while writing a valid canonical Morphir literal. The type checker uses the resolved source type, not a digit-count guess.

Compiler probe evidence and its limits

The original probe below used compiler 0.10.15+943464bfa via PATH, as its unchanged receipt records. Revision 0.1 incorrectly attributed it to the repository pin. The new compatibility probe uses explicit compiler paths and records the old pin's rejection plus successful Int32/UInt32 identity functions on 0.10.15 across eight target/build-mode lanes. The separate current-name compatibility probe and Ion receipt record rejection of Int32/UInt32 by that pin. Probe source, primary Ion receipt and JSON inspection view cover ten identity signatures and three observations: signed Int maximum plus one, UInt maximum plus one, and Float 16777216 + 1. They establish only those source compiler observations. They do not qualify all integer operators, casts, parsing, SDK mapping or numeric source compilation.

05 / executable meaning

Widen exactly, then apply the operation the source asked for

SituationRequired behavior
Bounded integer → Morphir IntExact widening using the corresponding SDK conversion. Record source representation and conversion origin.
Morphir Int → bounded typeChecked narrowing through existing toInt* contracts or corresponding additions. Return absence or the declared failure form; do not silently wrap.
Source fixed-width arithmeticPreserve source behavior through explicit normalization/helpers. The original 0.10.15 probe observes Int and UInt alias addition wrapping; repeat the relevant Int32/UInt32 observations under the aligned compiler and probe every additional admitted operator and width.
Source machine cast or bit reinterpretationKeep distinct from checked SDK narrowing. Admit only individually specified and tested casts; initial source profiles may reject other methods with a clear diagnostic.
BigInt arithmeticExact arbitrary-precision operations, subject to resource budgets. Qualify source division and remainder rules before reusing a classic adapter.
Float32 arithmeticRound at the source's observable binary32 operation boundaries. Promoting to Double and rounding only the final result is insufficient.
Floating point → IntProvide a checked exact conversion and separately named rounding/truncation operations. Define fractional, nonfinite and range cases explicitly; never label a rounding conversion lossless.
Int → Float or DoubleIdentify whether the conversion is exact or rounding. Test beyond the 24-bit and 53-bit significand boundaries; do not silently narrow during literal parsing or JSON handling.
Division and exceptional valuesSpecify zero divisors, signed-minimum divided by minus one, NaN, infinity, subnormals and signed zero. Refuse an operation/profile if its target lanes cannot meet its declared behavior.
DecimalRetain the existing SDK's numerical semantics, including minimum exponent and half-even rounding. Source scale is a descriptive fact; it does not change arithmetic implicitly.

Metadata describes where a value came from. Executable IR determines how it behaves. A backend that does not interpret source precision must still evaluate the explicit lowered arithmetic correctly, or refuse an unsupported required SDK binding.

Use portable IR implementations for width normalization where practical, with audited runtime acceleration permitted under the same contract. Avoid an annotation that secretly changes ordinary Basics.add. Preserve eager lets, short-circuit Boolean guards and left-to-right single evaluation of function arguments.

06 / facts, attributes and ownership

Keep source precision queryable and correctly attached

Reuse the current V4 attribute extension maps and engine-owned native Ion metadata. Align future native projection with the upstream scoped-property-graph decision. Do not place declaration facts on a function-body expression merely because that expression has an attributes field.

FactContentsOwner and lifetime
Source numeric representationSource language, authored type spelling and canonical resolved type; integer/floating/decimal category; signedness; width or arbitrary precision; IEEE format and significand precision where relevant. For example, authored Int resolves to Int32 under the current alias contract. Retain the compiler/profile identity.Parameter/output type use or original expression. Copy origin links when lowering introduces a wrapper or temporary.
Authored numeric literalOriginal token spelling, radix, suffix, source location and canonical semantic value. Floating values retain an exact bit observation after source rounding where relevant.Original literal expression, with links from generated literal nodes.
Conversion receiptInput representation, output representation, exact/checked/rounded/reinterpreted policy, binding identity and source expression origin.Conversion expression and synthetic nodes implementing it. Dynamic per-invocation loss is an execution observation, not a compile-time claim.
SDK addition provenanceClassic baseline revision, extension contract/version, declaring module, canonical function identity and evidence status.SDK value/type declaration or specification. Call sites reference the declaration and required extension inventory.
Semantic type constraintsActual bounds or representation required by the type contract, using the shared numeric constraint vocabulary when supported.Relevant type node. Do not attach the original source width as a semantic bound to an arbitrary-precision result that can exceed it.
Illustrative Ion payload, not a registered predicate spelling
source_number::{
  contract: "moonbit-source-number-v1",
  source_language: "moonbit",
  source_type: "UInt64",
  representation: {kind: integer, signed: false, bits: 64},
  literal: {
    spelling: "18446744073709551615UL",
    radix: 10,
    canonical_integer: 18446744073709551615
  },
  conversion: {policy: exact_widening, destination: "Morphir.Int"}
}

Illustrates a metadata object's content. Final extension keys and predicate/type FQNames must be declared and versioned during N1/N2. An Ion annotation token does not itself declare or authenticate a Morphir predicate.

The current carriers are TypeAttributes.extensions, ValueAttributes.extensions and addressed IRUnit.metadata. New typed payloads must validate their own schema and preserve unknown neighboring metadata. Existing declaration/body metadata stores nested origins; reuse those owners without pretending every nested origin already has a portable native Node URI.

Upstream Decision 0019 places native node facts in attributes.facts, specification facts in annotations.facts, and explicit-subject declaration facts in $meta.@graph. That is a future-revision design, not permission to add those fields to the current V4.0 codec. A native projection must negotiate the actual IR/Ion revisions and preserve assertion ownership.

Descriptive source facts require schema validation. They cannot authorize optimized execution, register SDK functions or impersonate authenticated semantic providers. Any future optimizer interpretation must declare its interpreter, exact contracts and evidence through the existing metadata/provider admission boundary.

07 / compatibility

Extend Int while keeping the classic SDK identifiable

The classic Int module already contains Int8, Int16, Int32 and Int64, each with exact widening and checked narrowing. Reuse those definitions. Add missing numeric forms in the same conceptual conversion module, with fully qualified names and an explicit extension inventory.

Classic baseline

Keep the existing pinned morphir-elm inventory and sdk_specification() default behavior. Continue to report classic conformance against its actual oracle.

Existing signed conversion signatures and behavior do not become MoonBit-specific or change silently.

Additive numeric contracts

Proposed capability identifier morphir-sdk-moonbit-numeric-v1 identifies added unsigned types/conversions, Float32 construction/conversion and any source-width helpers.

Provide an explicit extended specification API/profile and separate manifest entries. The identifier is proposed; publishing a package version is separate work.

Function familyContractClassification
Existing signed fromInt*/toInt*Preserve current exact widening and checked narrowing.Classic SDK
Unsigned equivalents covering Byte/UInt16/UInt32/UInt64Exact nonnegative widening and checked range on return. Prefer width-based SDK identities; retain MoonBit source aliases in metadata.SDK addition
Float32/Float64 → Int conversionsExact checked conversion plus explicitly named rounding policies. Cover nonfinite/fractional cases. Reuse classic functions only when their semantics and signatures match.New functions marked as additions; existing classic functions retain their identity
Int → floating conversionsExpose rounding or exactness policy. Never use these conversions as an intermediate exact integer transport.Classify each actual binding
BigInt bridgeExact bridge to the existing Integer representation. Do not duplicate a public SDK identity merely to label its source language.Existing representation plus any genuinely new bridge binding
Source-width normalizationExplicit portable behavior distinct from checked narrowing. Generated/native implementations must meet the same contract.SDK addition if a public helper is needed

For every added declaration, record extension provenance as metadata/annotations in a supported carrier. Include the same identity in SDK-spec, runtime binding inventory, Scheme registration, generator coverage and capability requirements. Inventory JSON alone does not satisfy the requested IR metadata. No added binding may count as classic morphir-elm parity.

Prefer existing supported SDK implementations and MoonBit core. This design introduces no new third-party dependency. Cross-repository standardization in finos/morphir, morphir-elm or another backend remains separately tracked work.

08 / source admission

Resolve a finite SDK vocabulary through a frozen environment

Keep the source language moonbit. Retain existing Boolean profiles and their default. Add separately versioned complete profiles for signed Int32, integral libraries and numeric libraries as those slices become qualified. Profiles describe supported types/operators/functions; they do not become new language names.

Proposed IDs are moonbit-model-int32-library-v1, moonbit-model-integer-library-v1 and moonbit-model-numeric-library-v1. A profile's declared semantics remain stable. Offer it only when its complete advertised subset passes acceptance. Public capability output lists types and function families without dumping dependency descriptions into prose.

Allow SDK-qualified references only through an explicit immutable binding environment with source alias, actual MoonBit package identity, version/tree pin, source signature, canonical Morphir declaration and conversion policy. A textual alias such as @math alone does not prove it denotes core math. The engine adapter owns resolution; the pure compiler receives already resolved declarations.

First math functions are sqrt, pow, sin and cos, plus existing arithmetic, comparisons, abs and rounding/conversion families as individually qualified. Align actual core @math and SDK source call forms only after compiler/parser probes. Do not mechanically substitute similarly named functions when domain/error/rounding behavior differs.

Typed direct calls can mix Bool and supported numeric parameters/results. Same-file acyclic calls and immutable single-name lets remain the source structure. General imports, arbitrary methods, generics, recursion, mutation, effects, asynchronous calls and general record/pattern support are separate capabilities. Conversion functions returning Maybe/Result are SDK capabilities; admitting their source syntax requires an explicit matching source capability and cannot be inferred from SDK availability.

09 / storage

Prefer Ion and retain checked JSON boundaries

Use native Ion integer/decimal/float values in metadata and intermediate receipts, with binary Ion for compact installed qualification artifacts. Preserve source annotations, exact integer values, decimal spelling/scale and numeric bits through existing envelopes. Do not claim a source width from the compactness of an Ion encoding.

Morphir JSON is a supported interchange format. The current engine JSON codec rejects an IRUnit that contains engine metadata/provenance it cannot carry, with data.lossy_conversion. Keep that guard. A source-produced numeric unit therefore cannot automatically become a lossless bare Morphir JSON file merely because its IR attributes are JSON-shaped.

Use the existing checked JSON records/inspection views where appropriate. A future metadata-capable JSON adapter or explicit separately inventoried sidecar may be added, but is not assumed here. JSON loss tests must prove rejection or exact supported preservation, including integers beyond 2^53. No unconditional JSON fallback and no new native V4 fields under the old format version.

Nonfinite Float literals remain unsupported by the current generator. Runtime NaN/infinity results need an explicit tagged/bits observation at the execution boundary and a negotiated serialization contract. An Ion float's ability to store them does not establish IR literal or generated-code support.

10 / implementation plan

Each slice delivers a usable path through the engine

Each numeric slice includes frontend admission, typed IR, metadata, SDK/evaluator behavior, generator adapters, engine/CLI selection and focused differential tests. The final slice qualifies their combined installed behavior. Implementation is pending; the plan does not claim these capabilities already exist.

N1 / ready to implement / no packaging dependency

Signed Int32 library arithmetic

Verify compiler/core 0.10.15+943464bfa from prerequisite task morphir-ukvn.1.10.12.2 and probe parser admission for current Int32/UInt32 naming. Accept Bool and explicitly typed Int32 functions, integer literals, +/−/×, comparisons, if/lets/direct calls. Reuse SDK Int32 boundaries, exact working Int values and explicit signed-width normalization. Include a callable generated consumer, source precision receipts and Ion replay. Freeze parser/compiler observations for this subset. Qualify legacy aliases separately and preserve authored spellings.

N2 / after N1

All scalar integer forms and Int conversions

Add Int16, Int64, Byte, UInt16, UInt32, UInt64 and BigInt. Extend Int specification/runtime/metadata for unsigned forms. Qualify integer division/remainder per supported type, checked narrowing and source casts separately. Advertise an integral profile only for proven operations.

N3 / after N2

Float, Double and explicit conversion policies

Implement source floating literals/operations, Float32 rounding points and integer bridges. Add exceptional-value and signed-zero receipts. Preserve source precision and operation origins in checkpoints and generated symbols.

N4 / after N3

Curated math SDK calls

Freeze source alias/package binding, map sqrt/pow/sin/cos and selected numeric SDK functions, and add missing generator adapters. Compare domains, errors and results across source, Scheme and generated execution. Publish a per-function support matrix.

N5 / after N4

Decimal library calculations

Add an explicit Decimal SDK source binding and a small closed subset: exact construction, add/sub/mul, comparisons, rounding and a documented division form that does not imply general Maybe/pattern admission. Retain literal scale separately from numerical runtime normalization. Qualify the existing −32 exponent floor and default/error semantics.

N6 / after N5

Installed numeric libraries and evidence

Qualify all offered numeric profiles through installed npm/native CLI lanes, consumer ABI, Ion text/binary replay, checked JSON handling, required SDK extension admission and enabled/disabled observations. Produce the final machine-readable per-type/per-function/target evidence matrix.

Related workRelationshipNext requirement
F4 / A2 packagingIndependent of local numeric implementation.Use the qualified profile inventory when the agreed extension contract is available.
Shared generic inferenceNot required for explicitly typed scalar source.Reuse shared services if later profiles admit generic numeric abstractions.
Authenticated metadata providersDescriptive facts do not grant execution authority.Use existing admission for any future interpreter-driven optimization or external semantic vocabulary.
StringsParallel source lane; see the shared milestone dependencies below.Produce its full HTML specification and then qualify source text behavior.
11 / proof

Compare behavior and independently check the metadata

DimensionRequired evidence
Integer boundariesEvery min/max, one-step overflow/underflow, exact values above 2^53, UInt64 max, large BigInt, negative division/remainder and zero-divisor cases.
Floating behaviorBinary32/64 precision boundaries, non-associative examples, rounding/conversion edges, signed zero, subnormals, NaN and infinity outcomes. Exact bits for operations whose contract promises them.
Math functionsKnown values plus independently generated reference vectors. Declare per-function error/ULP limits for transcendental implementations; do not reuse a broad tolerance to hide integer or basic IEEE arithmetic differences. Compare domain/error categories exactly.
DecimalCoefficient/exponent precision, zero/trailing-zero normalization, rounding ties, division/default semantics and the SDK exponent floor. Separately verify retained literal scale.
Library behaviorPublic/private visibility, multiple entries, forward calls, mixed scalar signatures, shadowing, single evaluation and short circuit. Existing Boolean profiles retain their tests and default selection.
MetadataType-use/parameter/output ownership, distinct source and result representation, generated temporary origins, unknown-fact preservation and SDK addition classification. Ion replay preserves native rich values.
Installed targetsWasm, Wasm-GC, JS and native in debug/release for source/generation qualification. Installed platform lanes reuse the repository's supported OS/package contracts. Record actual lane coverage; do not infer it from a local probe.
Failure and resource boundsUnsupported type/operator/call, missing required SDK extension, source literal out of range, conversion failure, cancellation and over-budget numeric size all produce stable contextual failures before publication.

Add numeric token length, integer bit/exponent magnitude and operation-cost limits to existing byte/expression/call limits. A low-cost source expression such as a huge power can have an expensive result; admission and evaluator fuel must account for that. Use existing observer scopes and structured warnings. Logs, when enabled, default beneath .morphir/logs/; explicit user paths remain honored.

Ordinary exact widening emits no warning. Report a warning only for a real automatic recovery or an explicitly selected potentially lossy policy; include the source location, numeric forms, selected policy and a clear exact/checked alternative. Semantic refusals remain structured diagnostics with logs disabled. Proposed diagnostic identifiers must be finalized against existing namespaces during implementation.

12 / revised scheduling

Strings proceeds in parallel through shared capabilities

The maintainer authorized this scheduling revision on 17 October 2026. It supersedes revision 0.4's numbers-before-Strings requirement. String semantic design and Unicode probes can begin immediately. The numeric N1-N6 chain and its acceptance obligations remain intact.

BeadSliceExecutionHard prerequisites

Shared typed-library milestone morphir-ukvn.1.10.12.3 is extracted from active N1 without duplicating its work or changing its owner/status. Shared pinned binding resolution morphir-ukvn.1.10.12.4 is extracted from N4 with a narrow original-source/evaluator/generated consumer proof. N1 waits on the first; N4 waits on the second plus existing N3.

String basics uses the shared typed foundation and reviewed String design, and includes the first runnable MoonBit String workbench sample. Ordering needs String basics. Length/slices additionally need N1 Int32 qualification. The initial nonnumeric SDK subset additionally needs the shared resolver. Installed String qualification joins these slices independently of numeric N6.

The detailed scheduling record is the design of morphir-ukvn.1.10.13; implementation plan morphir-ukvn.1.10.13.2 links the existing semantic-design task. Source ordering, UTF-16/surrogate semantics, conversion errors and numeric-specific String calls still require per-operation specification and qualification. Backend String coverage alone does not admit source Strings. A2/F4/MEP remain separate.

13 / design decisions

Make the choices concrete before widening source admission

DecisionSelected directionImplementation check
Public fixed-width typesReuse SDK boundary wrappers and conversions, retaining original source form in metadata.N1 checks generated consumer ABI and exact parameter/result admission. Do not silently change wrappers into machine primitives.
Source names and arithmeticUse canonical MoonBit Int32/UInt32, retain authored legacy aliases, and preserve the aligned compiler's semantics with exact Morphir Int intermediates.Use the selected 0.10.15 compiler/core pin and verify parser admission in N1. Probe each admitted operation/type before advertising it. Original alias-spelling receipts record 0.10.15, despite revision 0.1's incorrect narrative attribution.
Source precision carrierVersioned attribute extensions and native Ion node metadata now; checked native graph projection later.Declare payload schema and actual node ownership. No native V4.1 claim from a V4.0 extension object.
SDK compatibilityKeep classic inventory/default API intact; opt into additional numeric specification/runtime capabilities.Separate provenance, support and conformance for every added function.
Math portabilityExplicit operation contracts and per-function qualification.Agree exact-bit versus bounded-error expectations from the actual source and SDK implementations, before enabling each binding.
Delivery scopeLocal engine/CLI and generated libraries first; no new release or upstream completion implied.Six numeric slices plus an independently specified parallel String lane, sharing typed frontend and binding-resolution milestones.

The compiler probe is intentionally small. Parser AST coverage, exact source casts, all width-specific division/overflow cases and transcendental error bounds remain implementation evidence to collect. These are acceptance obligations, not reasons to advertise a partially implemented broad profile.

14 / evidence and record

Source contracts and canonical work tracking

  • Current Boolean frontend contract, typed lowering and origin owners, and provider/profile registration.
  • Existing SDK Int conversions, SDK specification API, classic specification declarations, and SDK semantic boundaries.
  • Current generator SDK allowlist, scalar mapping, current attribute containers, and Ion codecs and JSON loss guard.
  • Current MoonBit numeric names and compatibility aliases and lexical reference. Current names are the design target. The original receipt records 0.10.15; the separate explicit-path probe distinguishes it from the repository's 0.10.14 pin. N1 must align and qualify compiler/core/parser pins before implementing the new source profiles.
  • Pinned compiler observations. Installed core string/README.mbt.md documents UTF-16 code units, shortlex comparison and surrogate-aware slice behavior; the evidence manifest records its exact bytes.
  • Upstream numeric constraints draft, Decision 0019, and metadata reference contract. These describe proposed native metadata revisions, not new claims for the current engine codec.
  • Numeric stage morphir-ukvn.1.10.12 owns this HTML specification. Six implementation tasks belong to plan morphir-ukvn.1.10.12.1, rendered locally as the implementation plan. Numeric and Strings stages are parented under Track 5 morphir-ukvn.5 and reference A7 morphir-ukvn.1.10 in their records, so local work does not inherit its packaging blocker. F4 morphir-ukvn.1.10.5 and A2 morphir-ukvn.1.3 keep their existing dependency. Strings morphir-ukvn.1.10.13 uses per-slice shared milestones; it no longer depends on completion of numeric qualification.

Specification, implementation plan and execution ledger are canonical in the shared beads tracker. Files beneath .dev/ are local review/rendering artifacts and must not be staged. Evidence identity manifest.

Revision 0.5 adds the maintainer-authorized parallel String scheduling contract while retaining numeric semantics and the six numeric acceptance slices. Revision 0.4 selects compiler/core 0.10.15+943464bfa, records the dedicated pin-upgrade prerequisite, fresh dependency migrations, independent LLVM pin and runtime wrapper Value names. Int32/UInt32 are the canonical source names; preserve authored aliases in metadata and verify parser admission in N1. The original probe retains its spellings and actual 0.10.15 identity; revision 0.1's incorrect attribution to the repository pin is corrected. Numeric representation preservation, executable arithmetic, additive SDK contracts, six delivery slices and the Strings follow-up remain in scope. No production numeric frontend implementation or package release is claimed.
