Morphir / MoonBit

Numeric libraries
Specification revision 0.1
15 October 2026

01 / What this unlocks02 / Existing foundation03 / Component contracts04 / Numeric forms05 / Arithmetic and conversion06 / Precision and metadata07 / Classic SDK and additions08 / Source calls and selection09 / Ion and JSON10 / Delivery slices11 / Evidence and diagnostics12 / Strings comes next13 / Decisions and boundaries14 / Sources and tracker
A7 / numeric source capabilities

Numbers that retain their source meaning.

Compile typed MoonBit numeric libraries into Morphir, preserve their source precision, and execute them through the existing engine, SDK and MoonBit generator. Follow numbers with Strings.

Proposed implementationSource language: moonbitIon preferredMorphir JSON supported

Tracked by morphir-ukvn.1.10.12. Based on MoonBit main 6f9f7e8, which matches fetched origin/main. This document specifies future source support. Its compiler probe and diagrams do not establish numeric frontend support.

01 / outcome

Grow the library pipeline beyond Boolean decisions

Model quantities, prices, thresholds and calculations in ordinary MoonBit source. Keep the existing public/private functions, direct calls, immutable lets, readable naming and diagnostics. Add scalar typing and SDK resolution without making parsing, type checking, metadata or code generation depend on host I/O.

Signed 32-bit arithmetic→All scalar integers→Float and Double→Math and Decimal→Installed qualification→Strings

A useful first library

pub fn total(quantity : Int, unit_price : Int) -> Int {
  let subtotal = quantity * unit_price
  if subtotal > 1000 { subtotal - 100 } else { subtotal }
}

Proposed accepted source. Arithmetic must retain the pinned compiler's signed 32-bit behavior. This example is not yet accepted by the current Boolean frontend.

Portable numbers, visible origin

Convert fixed-width values through the SDK Int family. Perform exact integer calculations in Morphir's arbitrary-precision representation. Preserve the original MoonBit type, width and spelling as addressed metadata.

When the source expression itself has bounded arithmetic, lower its wrap or other defined behavior explicitly. A mathematical intermediate can be arbitrary precision without changing the observable source result.

02 / current implementation

Most of the runtime foundation already exists

ComponentAvailable nowNumeric stage adds
Pure source frontendExplicit Bool signatures, acyclic same-file calls, lets, conditionals and source origins.Resolved scalar types, exact numeric literals, typed operators, finite SDK bindings.
Engine and CLILanguage/provider/profile selection, IRUnit hooks, observations, installed execution and Ion checkpoints.Additive profile descriptors, SDK requirements, numeric limits and end-to-end receipts.
SDK and Scheme248 classic typed bindings and Scheme adapters; arbitrary-precision Integer; signed Int8–Int64 wrappers; Float64 and numerical Decimal.Additional conversion contracts, source-width arithmetic where required, and separate extension conformance.
MoonBit generatorNumeric scalar construction and 57 audited SDK adapters, including arithmetic, comparisons, rounding and selected Decimal operations.Fixed-width and additional SDK adapters, explicit Float32 behavior, imported-source function mapping.
StringsSDK Text and Character plus String bindings exist; IR String literals already generate.A later source capability and additional audited String adapters.

The 248 SDK bindings and 57 generator adapters describe different inventories. A binding becomes an advertised source capability only after source admission, lowering, evaluation, generation and selected target lanes have evidence.

03 / architecture

Extend contracts at their existing boundaries

The diagram shows the landed Boolean path that numbers will extend. Open the explorable version for source references and SVG export. Numeric semantics in the following sections are proposed.

Open the complete pipeline diagram. Its automated artifact and browser checks pass; no perceptual-review claim is made.

ContractResponsibilityConfiguration and replacement
Source type resolverResolve scalar spellings and explicit SDK aliases against an immutable environment. Distinguish a local shadow from a known SDK binding.A versioned source binding environment supplied by the adapter, without filesystem or network access in the pure compiler.
Numeric descriptionDescribe semantic IR type, original representation, exact literal parsing, bounds and conversion policy.A closed typed inventory shared by admission and lowering. Unknown descriptions refuse; metadata cannot register new executable behavior.
Operator loweringSelect exact arithmetic, explicit source-width normalization, floating operations or a named SDK call. Preserve evaluation order and single evaluation.Profile-bound semantics and explicit required SDK contracts. No mutable global numeric mode.
SDK specification and adaptersProvide typed signatures, implementations, Scheme bindings and generator adapters for an exact supported inventory.Classic specification remains available; additional capabilities require a separately identified extension profile.
Metadata producerAttach source representation and conversion receipts to the correct node owner, preserving other facts.A versioned payload contract, distinct from optional diagnostic logging and from executable semantics.
Host and engineFreeze selection and dependencies, enforce budgets, persist artifacts, execute approved operations and report evidence.Reuse existing host grants, provider admission, cancellation and output publication rules.
04 / source inventory

Cover the pinned compiler's scalar numeric forms

The target inventory is ten scalar source types. A local compiler probe accepts explicit signatures and representative literals for all ten on compiler 0.10.14+7d59c7ec9. The implementation must also probe the pinned parser; compiler acceptance alone does not prove the parser exposes every required form.

MoonBit formRepresentation factsProposed Morphir contractDelivery
IntSigned 32-bitExisting SDK Int32 boundary type and exact Int working values.N1
Int16, Int64Signed 16-bit, 64-bitExisting SDK Int16/Int64 boundaries and checked conversions.N2
Byte, UInt16, UInt, UInt64Unsigned 8-bit, 16-bit, 32-bit, 64-bitAdded SDK Int-module unsigned boundary types and exact widening conversions.N2
BigIntSigned arbitrary precisionSDK Basics.Int; representation receipt names the MoonBit source form.N2
FloatIEEE binary32, 24 significand bits including the implicit leading bit for normal valuesAdded Float32 numeric boundary/operations, using an explicit round-to-binary32 operation at every required source rounding point.N3
DoubleIEEE binary64, 53 significand bits for normal valuesExisting SDK Basics.Float and qualified Float64 operations.N3
SDK DecimalLibrary type, not a MoonBit built-in scalarExisting SDK Decimal with its exact numerical coefficient/exponent semantics and separately retained source scale.N5

MoonBit has no native signed Int8 in this inventory; the classic SDK's Int8 remains supported as its own SDK type. SIMD vectors, arbitrary user-defined numeric traits and foreign numeric types are outside this stage. Future compiler additions require an inventory revision and evidence.

Finite integer literals are decoded exactly from their radix and suffix, without passing through machine Int or Double. Preserve authored radix, separators and suffix in metadata while writing a valid canonical Morphir literal. The type checker uses the resolved source type, not a digit-count guess.

Compiler probe evidence and its limits

Probe source, primary Ion receipt and JSON inspection view cover ten identity signatures and three observations: signed Int maximum plus one, UInt maximum plus one, and Float 16777216 + 1. They establish only those source compiler observations. They do not qualify all integer operators, casts, parsing, SDK mapping or numeric source compilation.

05 / executable meaning

Widen exactly, then apply the operation the source asked for

SituationRequired behavior
Bounded integer → Morphir IntExact widening using the corresponding SDK conversion. Record source representation and conversion origin.
Morphir Int → bounded typeChecked narrowing through existing toInt* contracts or corresponding additions. Return absence or the declared failure form; do not silently wrap.
Source fixed-width arithmeticPreserve source behavior through explicit normalization/helpers. The observed Int and UInt addition wrap; probe subtraction, multiplication, division, remainder and all additional widths before claiming them.
Source machine cast or bit reinterpretationKeep distinct from checked SDK narrowing. Admit only individually specified and tested casts; initial source profiles may reject other methods with a clear diagnostic.
BigInt arithmeticExact arbitrary-precision operations, subject to resource budgets. Qualify source division and remainder rules before reusing a classic adapter.
Float32 arithmeticRound at the source's observable binary32 operation boundaries. Promoting to Double and rounding only the final result is insufficient.
Floating point → IntProvide a checked exact conversion and separately named rounding/truncation operations. Define fractional, nonfinite and range cases explicitly; never label a rounding conversion lossless.
Int → Float or DoubleIdentify whether the conversion is exact or rounding. Test beyond the 24-bit and 53-bit significand boundaries; do not silently narrow during literal parsing or JSON handling.
Division and exceptional valuesSpecify zero divisors, signed-minimum divided by minus one, NaN, infinity, subnormals and signed zero. Refuse an operation/profile if its target lanes cannot meet its declared behavior.
DecimalRetain the existing SDK's numerical semantics, including minimum exponent and half-even rounding. Source scale is a descriptive fact; it does not change arithmetic implicitly.

Metadata describes where a value came from. Executable IR determines how it behaves. A backend that does not interpret source precision must still evaluate the explicit lowered arithmetic correctly, or refuse an unsupported required SDK binding.

Use portable IR implementations for width normalization where practical, with audited runtime acceleration permitted under the same contract. Avoid an annotation that secretly changes ordinary Basics.add. Preserve eager lets, short-circuit Boolean guards and left-to-right single evaluation of function arguments.

06 / facts, attributes and ownership

Keep source precision queryable and correctly attached

Reuse the current V4 attribute extension maps and engine-owned native Ion metadata. Align future native projection with the upstream scoped-property-graph decision. Do not place declaration facts on a function-body expression merely because that expression has an attributes field.

FactContentsOwner and lifetime
Source numeric representationSource language and resolved type; integer/floating/decimal category; signedness; width or arbitrary precision; IEEE format and significand precision where relevant.Parameter/output type use or original expression. Copy origin links when lowering introduces a wrapper or temporary.
Authored numeric literalOriginal token spelling, radix, suffix, source location and canonical semantic value. Floating values retain an exact bit observation after source rounding where relevant.Original literal expression, with links from generated literal nodes.
Conversion receiptInput representation, output representation, exact/checked/rounded/reinterpreted policy, binding identity and source expression origin.Conversion expression and synthetic nodes implementing it. Dynamic per-invocation loss is an execution observation, not a compile-time claim.
SDK addition provenanceClassic baseline revision, extension contract/version, declaring module, canonical function identity and evidence status.SDK value/type declaration or specification. Call sites reference the declaration and required extension inventory.
Semantic type constraintsActual bounds or representation required by the type contract, using the shared numeric constraint vocabulary when supported.Relevant type node. Do not attach the original source width as a semantic bound to an arbitrary-precision result that can exceed it.
Illustrative Ion payload, not a registered predicate spelling
source_number::{
  contract: "moonbit-source-number-v1",
  source_language: "moonbit",
  source_type: "UInt64",
  representation: {kind: integer, signed: false, bits: 64},
  literal: {
    spelling: "18446744073709551615UL",
    radix: 10,
    canonical_integer: 18446744073709551615
  },
  conversion: {policy: exact_widening, destination: "Morphir.Int"}
}

Illustrates a metadata object's content. Final extension keys and predicate/type FQNames must be declared and versioned during N1/N2. An Ion annotation token does not itself declare or authenticate a Morphir predicate.

The current carriers are TypeAttributes.extensions, ValueAttributes.extensions and addressed IRUnit.metadata. New typed payloads must validate their own schema and preserve unknown neighboring metadata. Existing declaration/body metadata stores nested origins; reuse those owners without pretending every nested origin already has a portable native Node URI.

Upstream Decision 0019 places native node facts in attributes.facts, specification facts in annotations.facts, and explicit-subject declaration facts in $meta.@graph. That is a future-revision design, not permission to add those fields to the current V4.0 codec. A native projection must negotiate the actual IR/Ion revisions and preserve assertion ownership.

Descriptive source facts require schema validation. They cannot authorize optimized execution, register SDK functions or impersonate authenticated semantic providers. Any future optimizer interpretation must declare its interpreter, exact contracts and evidence through the existing metadata/provider admission boundary.

07 / compatibility

Extend Int while keeping the classic SDK identifiable

The classic Int module already contains Int8, Int16, Int32 and Int64, each with exact widening and checked narrowing. Reuse those definitions. Add missing numeric forms in the same conceptual conversion module, with fully qualified names and an explicit extension inventory.

Classic baseline

Keep the existing pinned morphir-elm inventory and sdk_specification() default behavior. Continue to report classic conformance against its actual oracle.

Existing signed conversion signatures and behavior do not become MoonBit-specific or change silently.

Additive numeric contracts

Proposed capability identifier morphir-sdk-moonbit-numeric-v1 identifies added unsigned types/conversions, Float32 construction/conversion and any source-width helpers.

Provide an explicit extended specification API/profile and separate manifest entries. The identifier is proposed; publishing a package version is separate work.

Function familyContractClassification
Existing signed fromInt*/toInt*Preserve current exact widening and checked narrowing.Classic SDK
Unsigned equivalents covering Byte/UInt16/UInt/UInt64Exact nonnegative widening and checked range on return. Prefer width-based SDK identities; retain MoonBit source aliases in metadata.SDK addition
Float32/Float64 → Int conversionsExact checked conversion plus explicitly named rounding policies. Cover nonfinite/fractional cases. Reuse classic functions only when their semantics and signatures match.New functions marked as additions; existing classic functions retain their identity
Int → floating conversionsExpose rounding or exactness policy. Never use these conversions as an intermediate exact integer transport.Classify each actual binding
BigInt bridgeExact bridge to the existing Integer representation. Do not duplicate a public SDK identity merely to label its source language.Existing representation plus any genuinely new bridge binding
Source-width normalizationExplicit portable behavior distinct from checked narrowing. Generated/native implementations must meet the same contract.SDK addition if a public helper is needed

For every added declaration, record extension provenance as metadata/annotations in a supported carrier. Include the same identity in SDK-spec, runtime binding inventory, Scheme registration, generator coverage and capability requirements. Inventory JSON alone does not satisfy the requested IR metadata. No added binding may count as classic morphir-elm parity.

Prefer existing supported SDK implementations and MoonBit core. This design introduces no new third-party dependency. Cross-repository standardization in finos/morphir, morphir-elm or another backend remains separately tracked work.

08 / source admission

Resolve a finite SDK vocabulary through a frozen environment

Keep the source language moonbit. Retain existing Boolean profiles and their default. Add separately versioned complete profiles for signed Int32, integral libraries and numeric libraries as those slices become qualified. Profiles describe supported types/operators/functions; they do not become new language names.

Proposed IDs are moonbit-model-int32-library-v1, moonbit-model-integer-library-v1 and moonbit-model-numeric-library-v1. A profile's declared semantics remain stable. Offer it only when its complete advertised subset passes acceptance. Public capability output lists types and function families without dumping dependency descriptions into prose.

Allow SDK-qualified references only through an explicit immutable binding environment with source alias, actual MoonBit package identity, version/tree pin, source signature, canonical Morphir declaration and conversion policy. A textual alias such as @math alone does not prove it denotes core math. The engine adapter owns resolution; the pure compiler receives already resolved declarations.

First math functions are sqrt, pow, sin and cos, plus existing arithmetic, comparisons, abs and rounding/conversion families as individually qualified. Align actual core @math and SDK source call forms only after compiler/parser probes. Do not mechanically substitute similarly named functions when domain/error/rounding behavior differs.

Typed direct calls can mix Bool and supported numeric parameters/results. Same-file acyclic calls and immutable single-name lets remain the source structure. General imports, arbitrary methods, generics, recursion, mutation, effects, asynchronous calls and general record/pattern support are separate capabilities. Conversion functions returning Maybe/Result are SDK capabilities; admitting their source syntax requires an explicit matching source capability and cannot be inferred from SDK availability.

09 / storage

Prefer Ion and retain checked JSON boundaries

Use native Ion integer/decimal/float values in metadata and intermediate receipts, with binary Ion for compact installed qualification artifacts. Preserve source annotations, exact integer values, decimal spelling/scale and numeric bits through existing envelopes. Do not claim a source width from the compactness of an Ion encoding.

Morphir JSON is a supported interchange format. The current engine JSON codec rejects an IRUnit that contains engine metadata/provenance it cannot carry, with data.lossy_conversion. Keep that guard. A source-produced numeric unit therefore cannot automatically become a lossless bare Morphir JSON file merely because its IR attributes are JSON-shaped.

Use the existing checked JSON records/inspection views where appropriate. A future metadata-capable JSON adapter or explicit separately inventoried sidecar may be added, but is not assumed here. JSON loss tests must prove rejection or exact supported preservation, including integers beyond 2^53. No unconditional JSON fallback and no new native V4 fields under the old format version.

Nonfinite Float literals remain unsupported by the current generator. Runtime NaN/infinity results need an explicit tagged/bits observation at the execution boundary and a negotiated serialization contract. An Ion float's ability to store them does not establish IR literal or generated-code support.

10 / implementation plan

Each slice delivers a usable path through the engine

Each numeric slice includes frontend admission, typed IR, metadata, SDK/evaluator behavior, generator adapters, engine/CLI selection and focused differential tests. The final slice qualifies their combined installed behavior. Implementation is pending; the plan does not claim these capabilities already exist.

N1 / ready to implement / no packaging dependency

Signed Int32 library arithmetic

Accept Bool and explicitly typed Int functions, integer literals, +/−/×, comparisons, if/lets/direct calls. Reuse SDK Int32 boundaries, exact working Int values and explicit signed-width normalization. Include a callable generated consumer, source precision receipts and Ion replay. Freeze parser/compiler observations for this subset.

N2 / after N1

All scalar integer forms and Int conversions

Add Int16, Int64, Byte, UInt16, UInt, UInt64 and BigInt. Extend Int specification/runtime/metadata for unsigned forms. Qualify integer division/remainder per supported type, checked narrowing and source casts separately. Advertise an integral profile only for proven operations.

N3 / after N2

Float, Double and explicit conversion policies

Implement source floating literals/operations, Float32 rounding points and integer bridges. Add exceptional-value and signed-zero receipts. Preserve source precision and operation origins in checkpoints and generated symbols.

N4 / after N3

Curated math SDK calls

Freeze source alias/package binding, map sqrt/pow/sin/cos and selected numeric SDK functions, and add missing generator adapters. Compare domains, errors and results across source, Scheme and generated execution. Publish a per-function support matrix.

N5 / after N4

Decimal library calculations

Add an explicit Decimal SDK source binding and a small closed subset: exact construction, add/sub/mul, comparisons, rounding and a documented division form that does not imply general Maybe/pattern admission. Retain literal scale separately from numerical runtime normalization. Qualify the existing −32 exponent floor and default/error semantics.

N6 / after N5

Installed numeric libraries and evidence

Qualify all offered numeric profiles through installed npm/native CLI lanes, consumer ABI, Ion text/binary replay, checked JSON handling, required SDK extension admission and enabled/disabled observations. Produce the final machine-readable per-type/per-function/target evidence matrix.

Related workRelationshipNext requirement
F4 / A2 packagingIndependent of local numeric implementation.Use the qualified profile inventory when the agreed extension contract is available.
Shared generic inferenceNot required for explicitly typed scalar source.Reuse shared services if later profiles admit generic numeric abstractions.
Authenticated metadata providersDescriptive facts do not grant execution authority.Use existing admission for any future interpreter-driven optimization or external semantic vocabulary.
StringsNext source stage after N6.Produce its full HTML specification and then qualify source text behavior.
11 / proof

Compare behavior and independently check the metadata

DimensionRequired evidence
Integer boundariesEvery min/max, one-step overflow/underflow, exact values above 2^53, UInt64 max, large BigInt, negative division/remainder and zero-divisor cases.
Floating behaviorBinary32/64 precision boundaries, non-associative examples, rounding/conversion edges, signed zero, subnormals, NaN and infinity outcomes. Exact bits for operations whose contract promises them.
Math functionsKnown values plus independently generated reference vectors. Declare per-function error/ULP limits for transcendental implementations; do not reuse a broad tolerance to hide integer or basic IEEE arithmetic differences. Compare domain/error categories exactly.
DecimalCoefficient/exponent precision, zero/trailing-zero normalization, rounding ties, division/default semantics and the SDK exponent floor. Separately verify retained literal scale.
Library behaviorPublic/private visibility, multiple entries, forward calls, mixed scalar signatures, shadowing, single evaluation and short circuit. Existing Boolean profiles retain their tests and default selection.
MetadataType-use/parameter/output ownership, distinct source and result representation, generated temporary origins, unknown-fact preservation and SDK addition classification. Ion replay preserves native rich values.
Installed targetsWasm, Wasm-GC, JS and native in debug/release for source/generation qualification. Installed platform lanes reuse the repository's supported OS/package contracts. Record actual lane coverage; do not infer it from a local probe.
Failure and resource boundsUnsupported type/operator/call, missing required SDK extension, source literal out of range, conversion failure, cancellation and over-budget numeric size all produce stable contextual failures before publication.

Add numeric token length, integer bit/exponent magnitude and operation-cost limits to existing byte/expression/call limits. A low-cost source expression such as a huge power can have an expensive result; admission and evaluator fuel must account for that. Use existing observer scopes and structured warnings. Logs, when enabled, default beneath .morphir/logs/; explicit user paths remain honored.

Ordinary exact widening emits no warning. Report a warning only for a real automatic recovery or an explicitly selected potentially lossy policy; include the source location, numeric forms, selected policy and a clear exact/checked alternative. Semantic refusals remain structured diagnostics with logs disabled. Proposed diagnostic identifiers must be finalized against existing namespaces during implementation.

12 / committed follow-up scope

Strings is the next stage after numeric libraries

Strings gets its own specification and qualification after N6. Reuse the numeric stage's mixed-type signatures, direct-call resolution, metadata ownership and SDK capability inventory. Start with String parameters/results, literals, lets/calls, concatenation and equality; then qualify comparison, length, slicing and a curated String SDK subset.

The pinned MoonBit core describes String storage as UTF-16, so the issue is not a simple UTF-8 versus UTF-16 substitution. Its String comparison uses shortlex ordering, while the Morphir SDK provides Elm-compatible lexical ordering. Source slice behavior also trims split surrogate pairs, while the SDK Text model can retain isolated halves. Lower each source operation to its actual semantics and keep Morphir SDK calls under their own contracts.

Cover empty strings, supplementary characters, combining sequences, surrogate boundaries, lexical ordering, substring bounds and case mapping. Existing SDK Text::to_string may reject isolated surrogate halves at a host boundary; define that boundary explicitly rather than silently replacing text. General regex, interpolation, locale-sensitive operations, collections and arbitrary String methods need separate claims.

The order is numeric specification and implementation, numeric installed qualification, then the full Strings specification and implementation. F4 packaging can progress independently when A2 is ready.

13 / design decisions

Make the choices concrete before widening source admission

DecisionSelected directionImplementation check
Public fixed-width typesReuse SDK boundary wrappers and conversions, retaining original source form in metadata.N1 checks generated consumer ABI and exact parameter/result admission. Do not silently change wrappers into machine primitives.
Source arithmeticExplicitly preserve the pinned source semantics, with exact Int intermediates.Probe each admitted operation/type before advertising it. Unproven exceptional cases remain refused.
Source precision carrierVersioned attribute extensions and native Ion node metadata now; checked native graph projection later.Declare payload schema and actual node ownership. No native V4.1 claim from a V4.0 extension object.
SDK compatibilityKeep classic inventory/default API intact; opt into additional numeric specification/runtime capabilities.Separate provenance, support and conformance for every added function.
Math portabilityExplicit operation contracts and per-function qualification.Agree exact-bit versus bounded-error expectations from the actual source and SDK implementations, before enabling each binding.
Delivery scopeLocal engine/CLI and generated libraries first; no new release or upstream completion implied.Six numeric slices, followed by a separately specified Strings stage.

The compiler probe is intentionally small. Parser AST coverage, exact source casts, all width-specific division/overflow cases and transcendental error bounds remain implementation evidence to collect. These are acceptance obligations, not reasons to advertise a partially implemented broad profile.

14 / evidence and record

Source contracts and canonical work tracking

  • Current Boolean frontend contract, typed lowering and origin owners, and provider/profile registration.
  • Existing SDK Int conversions, SDK specification API, classic specification declarations, and SDK semantic boundaries.
  • Current generator SDK allowlist, scalar mapping, current attribute containers, and Ion codecs and JSON loss guard.
  • MoonBit numeric source forms and lexical reference. Online documentation can advance beyond the pinned compiler; local compiler/core probes are authoritative for this stage.
  • Pinned compiler observations. Installed core string/README.mbt.md documents UTF-16 code units, shortlex comparison and surrogate-aware slice behavior; the evidence manifest records its exact bytes.
  • Upstream numeric constraints draft, Decision 0019, and metadata reference contract. These describe proposed native metadata revisions, not new claims for the current engine codec.
  • Numeric stage morphir-ukvn.1.10.12 owns this HTML specification. Six implementation tasks belong to plan morphir-ukvn.1.10.12.1, rendered locally as the implementation plan. Numeric and Strings stages are parented under Track 5 morphir-ukvn.5 and reference A7 morphir-ukvn.1.10 in their records, so local work does not inherit its packaging blocker. F4 morphir-ukvn.1.10.5 and A2 morphir-ukvn.1.3 keep their existing dependency. Strings morphir-ukvn.1.10.13 depends on numeric qualification.

Specification, implementation plan and execution ledger are canonical in the shared beads tracker. Files beneath .dev/ are local review/rendering artifacts and must not be staged. Evidence identity manifest.

Revision 0.1 defines numeric representation preservation, executable arithmetic, additive SDK contracts, six delivery slices and the Strings follow-up. No production numeric frontend implementation or package release is claimed.

Morphir / MoonBit

Numeric libraries
Specification revision 0.2
15 October 2026

01 / What this unlocks02 / Existing foundation03 / Component contracts04 / Numeric forms05 / Arithmetic and conversion06 / Precision and metadata07 / Classic SDK and additions08 / Source calls and selection09 / Ion and JSON10 / Delivery slices11 / Evidence and diagnostics12 / Strings comes next13 / Decisions and boundaries14 / Sources and tracker
A7 / numeric source capabilities

Numbers that retain their source meaning.

Compile typed MoonBit numeric libraries into Morphir, preserve their source precision, and execute them through the existing engine, SDK and MoonBit generator. Follow numbers with Strings.

Proposed implementationSource language: moonbitIon preferredMorphir JSON supported

Tracked by morphir-ukvn.1.10.12. Based on MoonBit main 6f9f7e8, which matches fetched origin/main. This document specifies future source support. Its compiler probe and diagrams do not establish numeric frontend support.

01 / outcome

Grow the library pipeline beyond Boolean decisions

Model quantities, prices, thresholds and calculations in ordinary MoonBit source. Keep the existing public/private functions, direct calls, immutable lets, readable naming and diagnostics. Add scalar typing and SDK resolution without making parsing, type checking, metadata or code generation depend on host I/O.

Signed 32-bit arithmetic→All scalar integers→Float and Double→Math and Decimal→Installed qualification→Strings

A useful first library

pub fn total(quantity : Int32, unit_price : Int32) -> Int32 {
  let subtotal = quantity * unit_price
  if subtotal > 1000 { subtotal - 100 } else { subtotal }
}

Proposed accepted source. Arithmetic must retain the pinned compiler's signed 32-bit behavior. This example is not yet accepted by the current Boolean frontend.

Portable numbers, visible origin

Convert fixed-width values through the SDK Int family. Perform exact integer calculations in Morphir's arbitrary-precision representation. Preserve the original MoonBit type, width and spelling as addressed metadata.

When the source expression itself has bounded arithmetic, lower its wrap or other defined behavior explicitly. A mathematical intermediate can be arbitrary precision without changing the observable source result.

02 / current implementation

Most of the runtime foundation already exists

ComponentAvailable nowNumeric stage adds
Pure source frontendExplicit Bool signatures, acyclic same-file calls, lets, conditionals and source origins.Resolved scalar types, exact numeric literals, typed operators, finite SDK bindings.
Engine and CLILanguage/provider/profile selection, IRUnit hooks, observations, installed execution and Ion checkpoints.Additive profile descriptors, SDK requirements, numeric limits and end-to-end receipts.
SDK and Scheme248 classic typed bindings and Scheme adapters; arbitrary-precision Integer; signed Int8–Int64 wrappers; Float64 and numerical Decimal.Additional conversion contracts, source-width arithmetic where required, and separate extension conformance.
MoonBit generatorNumeric scalar construction and 57 audited SDK adapters, including arithmetic, comparisons, rounding and selected Decimal operations.Fixed-width and additional SDK adapters, explicit Float32 behavior, imported-source function mapping.
StringsSDK Text and Character plus String bindings exist; IR String literals already generate.A later source capability and additional audited String adapters.

The 248 SDK bindings and 57 generator adapters describe different inventories. A binding becomes an advertised source capability only after source admission, lowering, evaluation, generation and selected target lanes have evidence.

03 / architecture

Extend contracts at their existing boundaries

The diagram shows the landed Boolean path that numbers will extend. Open the explorable version for source references and SVG export. Numeric semantics in the following sections are proposed.

Open the complete pipeline diagram. Its automated artifact and browser checks pass; no perceptual-review claim is made.

ContractResponsibilityConfiguration and replacement
Source type resolverResolve scalar spellings and explicit SDK aliases against an immutable environment. Distinguish a local shadow from a known SDK binding.A versioned source binding environment supplied by the adapter, without filesystem or network access in the pure compiler.
Numeric descriptionDescribe semantic IR type, original representation, exact literal parsing, bounds and conversion policy.A closed typed inventory shared by admission and lowering. Unknown descriptions refuse; metadata cannot register new executable behavior.
Operator loweringSelect exact arithmetic, explicit source-width normalization, floating operations or a named SDK call. Preserve evaluation order and single evaluation.Profile-bound semantics and explicit required SDK contracts. No mutable global numeric mode.
SDK specification and adaptersProvide typed signatures, implementations, Scheme bindings and generator adapters for an exact supported inventory.Classic specification remains available; additional capabilities require a separately identified extension profile.
Metadata producerAttach source representation and conversion receipts to the correct node owner, preserving other facts.A versioned payload contract, distinct from optional diagnostic logging and from executable semantics.
Host and engineFreeze selection and dependencies, enforce budgets, persist artifacts, execute approved operations and report evidence.Reuse existing host grants, provider admission, cancellation and output publication rules.
04 / source inventory

Use current MoonBit numeric names

The target inventory is ten scalar source types, using Int32 and UInt32 as the current preferred names. Current MoonBit accepts Int and UInt as compatibility aliases and its formatter uses the explicit-width names. These source names are distinct from Morphir's arbitrary-precision Int and its Int SDK module.

The repository's pinned compiler 0.10.14+7d59c7ec9 predates this naming change. It accepts the older Int/UInt spellings but rejects Int32/UInt32 with undefined-type diagnostic 4032. N1 must first align compiler, core and parser pins with the current source names and qualify existing repository behavior. This document does not claim the current pin supports the new names.

MoonBit formRepresentation factsProposed Morphir contractDelivery
Int32Signed 32-bit; legacy source alias IntExisting SDK Int32 boundary type and exact Morphir Int working values.N1
Int16, Int64Signed 16-bit, 64-bitExisting SDK Int16/Int64 boundaries and checked conversions.N2
Byte, UInt16, UInt32, UInt64Unsigned 8-bit, 16-bit, 32-bit, 64-bitAdded SDK Int-module unsigned boundary types and exact widening conversions.N2
BigIntSigned arbitrary precisionSDK Basics.Int; representation receipt names the MoonBit source form.N2
FloatIEEE binary32, 24 significand bits including the implicit leading bit for normal valuesAdded Float32 numeric boundary/operations, using an explicit round-to-binary32 operation at every required source rounding point.N3
DoubleIEEE binary64, 53 significand bits for normal valuesExisting SDK Basics.Float and qualified Float64 operations.N3
SDK DecimalLibrary type, not a MoonBit built-in scalarExisting SDK Decimal with its exact numerical coefficient/exponent semantics and separately retained source scale.N5

MoonBit has no native signed Int8 in this inventory; the classic SDK's Int8 remains supported as its own SDK type. SIMD vectors, arbitrary user-defined numeric traits and foreign numeric types are outside this stage. Future compiler additions require an inventory revision and evidence.

Finite integer literals are decoded exactly from their radix and suffix, without passing through machine Int or Double. Preserve authored radix, separators and suffix in metadata while writing a valid canonical Morphir literal. The type checker uses the resolved source type, not a digit-count guess.

Compiler probe evidence and its limits

The original probe below used compiler 0.10.15+943464bfa via PATH, as its unchanged receipt records. Revision 0.1 incorrectly attributed it to the repository pin. The new compatibility probe uses explicit compiler paths and records the old pin's rejection plus successful Int32/UInt32 identity functions on 0.10.15 across eight target/build-mode lanes. The separate current-name compatibility probe and Ion receipt record rejection of Int32/UInt32 by that pin. Probe source, primary Ion receipt and JSON inspection view cover ten identity signatures and three observations: signed Int maximum plus one, UInt maximum plus one, and Float 16777216 + 1. They establish only those source compiler observations. They do not qualify all integer operators, casts, parsing, SDK mapping or numeric source compilation.

05 / executable meaning

Widen exactly, then apply the operation the source asked for

SituationRequired behavior
Bounded integer → Morphir IntExact widening using the corresponding SDK conversion. Record source representation and conversion origin.
Morphir Int → bounded typeChecked narrowing through existing toInt* contracts or corresponding additions. Return absence or the declared failure form; do not silently wrap.
Source fixed-width arithmeticPreserve source behavior through explicit normalization/helpers. The original 0.10.15 probe observes Int and UInt alias addition wrapping; repeat the relevant Int32/UInt32 observations under the aligned compiler and probe every additional admitted operator and width.
Source machine cast or bit reinterpretationKeep distinct from checked SDK narrowing. Admit only individually specified and tested casts; initial source profiles may reject other methods with a clear diagnostic.
BigInt arithmeticExact arbitrary-precision operations, subject to resource budgets. Qualify source division and remainder rules before reusing a classic adapter.
Float32 arithmeticRound at the source's observable binary32 operation boundaries. Promoting to Double and rounding only the final result is insufficient.
Floating point → IntProvide a checked exact conversion and separately named rounding/truncation operations. Define fractional, nonfinite and range cases explicitly; never label a rounding conversion lossless.
Int → Float or DoubleIdentify whether the conversion is exact or rounding. Test beyond the 24-bit and 53-bit significand boundaries; do not silently narrow during literal parsing or JSON handling.
Division and exceptional valuesSpecify zero divisors, signed-minimum divided by minus one, NaN, infinity, subnormals and signed zero. Refuse an operation/profile if its target lanes cannot meet its declared behavior.
DecimalRetain the existing SDK's numerical semantics, including minimum exponent and half-even rounding. Source scale is a descriptive fact; it does not change arithmetic implicitly.

Metadata describes where a value came from. Executable IR determines how it behaves. A backend that does not interpret source precision must still evaluate the explicit lowered arithmetic correctly, or refuse an unsupported required SDK binding.

Use portable IR implementations for width normalization where practical, with audited runtime acceleration permitted under the same contract. Avoid an annotation that secretly changes ordinary Basics.add. Preserve eager lets, short-circuit Boolean guards and left-to-right single evaluation of function arguments.

06 / facts, attributes and ownership

Keep source precision queryable and correctly attached

Reuse the current V4 attribute extension maps and engine-owned native Ion metadata. Align future native projection with the upstream scoped-property-graph decision. Do not place declaration facts on a function-body expression merely because that expression has an attributes field.

FactContentsOwner and lifetime
Source numeric representationSource language, authored type spelling and canonical resolved type; integer/floating/decimal category; signedness; width or arbitrary precision; IEEE format and significand precision where relevant. For example, authored Int resolves to Int32 under the current alias contract. Retain the compiler/profile identity.Parameter/output type use or original expression. Copy origin links when lowering introduces a wrapper or temporary.
Authored numeric literalOriginal token spelling, radix, suffix, source location and canonical semantic value. Floating values retain an exact bit observation after source rounding where relevant.Original literal expression, with links from generated literal nodes.
Conversion receiptInput representation, output representation, exact/checked/rounded/reinterpreted policy, binding identity and source expression origin.Conversion expression and synthetic nodes implementing it. Dynamic per-invocation loss is an execution observation, not a compile-time claim.
SDK addition provenanceClassic baseline revision, extension contract/version, declaring module, canonical function identity and evidence status.SDK value/type declaration or specification. Call sites reference the declaration and required extension inventory.
Semantic type constraintsActual bounds or representation required by the type contract, using the shared numeric constraint vocabulary when supported.Relevant type node. Do not attach the original source width as a semantic bound to an arbitrary-precision result that can exceed it.
Illustrative Ion payload, not a registered predicate spelling
source_number::{
  contract: "moonbit-source-number-v1",
  source_language: "moonbit",
  source_type: "UInt64",
  representation: {kind: integer, signed: false, bits: 64},
  literal: {
    spelling: "18446744073709551615UL",
    radix: 10,
    canonical_integer: 18446744073709551615
  },
  conversion: {policy: exact_widening, destination: "Morphir.Int"}
}

Illustrates a metadata object's content. Final extension keys and predicate/type FQNames must be declared and versioned during N1/N2. An Ion annotation token does not itself declare or authenticate a Morphir predicate.

The current carriers are TypeAttributes.extensions, ValueAttributes.extensions and addressed IRUnit.metadata. New typed payloads must validate their own schema and preserve unknown neighboring metadata. Existing declaration/body metadata stores nested origins; reuse those owners without pretending every nested origin already has a portable native Node URI.

Upstream Decision 0019 places native node facts in attributes.facts, specification facts in annotations.facts, and explicit-subject declaration facts in $meta.@graph. That is a future-revision design, not permission to add those fields to the current V4.0 codec. A native projection must negotiate the actual IR/Ion revisions and preserve assertion ownership.

Descriptive source facts require schema validation. They cannot authorize optimized execution, register SDK functions or impersonate authenticated semantic providers. Any future optimizer interpretation must declare its interpreter, exact contracts and evidence through the existing metadata/provider admission boundary.

07 / compatibility

Extend Int while keeping the classic SDK identifiable

The classic Int module already contains Int8, Int16, Int32 and Int64, each with exact widening and checked narrowing. Reuse those definitions. Add missing numeric forms in the same conceptual conversion module, with fully qualified names and an explicit extension inventory.

Classic baseline

Keep the existing pinned morphir-elm inventory and sdk_specification() default behavior. Continue to report classic conformance against its actual oracle.

Existing signed conversion signatures and behavior do not become MoonBit-specific or change silently.

Additive numeric contracts

Proposed capability identifier morphir-sdk-moonbit-numeric-v1 identifies added unsigned types/conversions, Float32 construction/conversion and any source-width helpers.

Provide an explicit extended specification API/profile and separate manifest entries. The identifier is proposed; publishing a package version is separate work.

Function familyContractClassification
Existing signed fromInt*/toInt*Preserve current exact widening and checked narrowing.Classic SDK
Unsigned equivalents covering Byte/UInt16/UInt32/UInt64Exact nonnegative widening and checked range on return. Prefer width-based SDK identities; retain MoonBit source aliases in metadata.SDK addition
Float32/Float64 → Int conversionsExact checked conversion plus explicitly named rounding policies. Cover nonfinite/fractional cases. Reuse classic functions only when their semantics and signatures match.New functions marked as additions; existing classic functions retain their identity
Int → floating conversionsExpose rounding or exactness policy. Never use these conversions as an intermediate exact integer transport.Classify each actual binding
BigInt bridgeExact bridge to the existing Integer representation. Do not duplicate a public SDK identity merely to label its source language.Existing representation plus any genuinely new bridge binding
Source-width normalizationExplicit portable behavior distinct from checked narrowing. Generated/native implementations must meet the same contract.SDK addition if a public helper is needed

For every added declaration, record extension provenance as metadata/annotations in a supported carrier. Include the same identity in SDK-spec, runtime binding inventory, Scheme registration, generator coverage and capability requirements. Inventory JSON alone does not satisfy the requested IR metadata. No added binding may count as classic morphir-elm parity.

Prefer existing supported SDK implementations and MoonBit core. This design introduces no new third-party dependency. Cross-repository standardization in finos/morphir, morphir-elm or another backend remains separately tracked work.

08 / source admission

Resolve a finite SDK vocabulary through a frozen environment

Keep the source language moonbit. Retain existing Boolean profiles and their default. Add separately versioned complete profiles for signed Int32, integral libraries and numeric libraries as those slices become qualified. Profiles describe supported types/operators/functions; they do not become new language names.

Proposed IDs are moonbit-model-int32-library-v1, moonbit-model-integer-library-v1 and moonbit-model-numeric-library-v1. A profile's declared semantics remain stable. Offer it only when its complete advertised subset passes acceptance. Public capability output lists types and function families without dumping dependency descriptions into prose.

Allow SDK-qualified references only through an explicit immutable binding environment with source alias, actual MoonBit package identity, version/tree pin, source signature, canonical Morphir declaration and conversion policy. A textual alias such as @math alone does not prove it denotes core math. The engine adapter owns resolution; the pure compiler receives already resolved declarations.

First math functions are sqrt, pow, sin and cos, plus existing arithmetic, comparisons, abs and rounding/conversion families as individually qualified. Align actual core @math and SDK source call forms only after compiler/parser probes. Do not mechanically substitute similarly named functions when domain/error/rounding behavior differs.

Typed direct calls can mix Bool and supported numeric parameters/results. Same-file acyclic calls and immutable single-name lets remain the source structure. General imports, arbitrary methods, generics, recursion, mutation, effects, asynchronous calls and general record/pattern support are separate capabilities. Conversion functions returning Maybe/Result are SDK capabilities; admitting their source syntax requires an explicit matching source capability and cannot be inferred from SDK availability.

09 / storage

Prefer Ion and retain checked JSON boundaries

Use native Ion integer/decimal/float values in metadata and intermediate receipts, with binary Ion for compact installed qualification artifacts. Preserve source annotations, exact integer values, decimal spelling/scale and numeric bits through existing envelopes. Do not claim a source width from the compactness of an Ion encoding.

Morphir JSON is a supported interchange format. The current engine JSON codec rejects an IRUnit that contains engine metadata/provenance it cannot carry, with data.lossy_conversion. Keep that guard. A source-produced numeric unit therefore cannot automatically become a lossless bare Morphir JSON file merely because its IR attributes are JSON-shaped.

Use the existing checked JSON records/inspection views where appropriate. A future metadata-capable JSON adapter or explicit separately inventoried sidecar may be added, but is not assumed here. JSON loss tests must prove rejection or exact supported preservation, including integers beyond 2^53. No unconditional JSON fallback and no new native V4 fields under the old format version.

Nonfinite Float literals remain unsupported by the current generator. Runtime NaN/infinity results need an explicit tagged/bits observation at the execution boundary and a negotiated serialization contract. An Ion float's ability to store them does not establish IR literal or generated-code support.

10 / implementation plan

Each slice delivers a usable path through the engine

Each numeric slice includes frontend admission, typed IR, metadata, SDK/evaluator behavior, generator adapters, engine/CLI selection and focused differential tests. The final slice qualifies their combined installed behavior. Implementation is pending; the plan does not claim these capabilities already exist.

N1 / ready to implement / no packaging dependency

Signed Int32 library arithmetic

First align and pin compiler/core/parser support for current Int32/UInt32 naming, checking existing repository behavior. Accept Bool and explicitly typed Int32 functions, integer literals, +/−/×, comparisons, if/lets/direct calls. Reuse SDK Int32 boundaries, exact working Int values and explicit signed-width normalization. Include a callable generated consumer, source precision receipts and Ion replay. Freeze parser/compiler observations for this subset. Qualify legacy aliases separately and preserve authored spellings.

N2 / after N1

All scalar integer forms and Int conversions

Add Int16, Int64, Byte, UInt16, UInt32, UInt64 and BigInt. Extend Int specification/runtime/metadata for unsigned forms. Qualify integer division/remainder per supported type, checked narrowing and source casts separately. Advertise an integral profile only for proven operations.

N3 / after N2

Float, Double and explicit conversion policies

Implement source floating literals/operations, Float32 rounding points and integer bridges. Add exceptional-value and signed-zero receipts. Preserve source precision and operation origins in checkpoints and generated symbols.

N4 / after N3

Curated math SDK calls

Freeze source alias/package binding, map sqrt/pow/sin/cos and selected numeric SDK functions, and add missing generator adapters. Compare domains, errors and results across source, Scheme and generated execution. Publish a per-function support matrix.

N5 / after N4

Decimal library calculations

Add an explicit Decimal SDK source binding and a small closed subset: exact construction, add/sub/mul, comparisons, rounding and a documented division form that does not imply general Maybe/pattern admission. Retain literal scale separately from numerical runtime normalization. Qualify the existing −32 exponent floor and default/error semantics.

N6 / after N5

Installed numeric libraries and evidence

Qualify all offered numeric profiles through installed npm/native CLI lanes, consumer ABI, Ion text/binary replay, checked JSON handling, required SDK extension admission and enabled/disabled observations. Produce the final machine-readable per-type/per-function/target evidence matrix.

Related workRelationshipNext requirement
F4 / A2 packagingIndependent of local numeric implementation.Use the qualified profile inventory when the agreed extension contract is available.
Shared generic inferenceNot required for explicitly typed scalar source.Reuse shared services if later profiles admit generic numeric abstractions.
Authenticated metadata providersDescriptive facts do not grant execution authority.Use existing admission for any future interpreter-driven optimization or external semantic vocabulary.
StringsNext source stage after N6.Produce its full HTML specification and then qualify source text behavior.
11 / proof

Compare behavior and independently check the metadata

DimensionRequired evidence
Integer boundariesEvery min/max, one-step overflow/underflow, exact values above 2^53, UInt64 max, large BigInt, negative division/remainder and zero-divisor cases.
Floating behaviorBinary32/64 precision boundaries, non-associative examples, rounding/conversion edges, signed zero, subnormals, NaN and infinity outcomes. Exact bits for operations whose contract promises them.
Math functionsKnown values plus independently generated reference vectors. Declare per-function error/ULP limits for transcendental implementations; do not reuse a broad tolerance to hide integer or basic IEEE arithmetic differences. Compare domain/error categories exactly.
DecimalCoefficient/exponent precision, zero/trailing-zero normalization, rounding ties, division/default semantics and the SDK exponent floor. Separately verify retained literal scale.
Library behaviorPublic/private visibility, multiple entries, forward calls, mixed scalar signatures, shadowing, single evaluation and short circuit. Existing Boolean profiles retain their tests and default selection.
MetadataType-use/parameter/output ownership, distinct source and result representation, generated temporary origins, unknown-fact preservation and SDK addition classification. Ion replay preserves native rich values.
Installed targetsWasm, Wasm-GC, JS and native in debug/release for source/generation qualification. Installed platform lanes reuse the repository's supported OS/package contracts. Record actual lane coverage; do not infer it from a local probe.
Failure and resource boundsUnsupported type/operator/call, missing required SDK extension, source literal out of range, conversion failure, cancellation and over-budget numeric size all produce stable contextual failures before publication.

Add numeric token length, integer bit/exponent magnitude and operation-cost limits to existing byte/expression/call limits. A low-cost source expression such as a huge power can have an expensive result; admission and evaluator fuel must account for that. Use existing observer scopes and structured warnings. Logs, when enabled, default beneath .morphir/logs/; explicit user paths remain honored.

Ordinary exact widening emits no warning. Report a warning only for a real automatic recovery or an explicitly selected potentially lossy policy; include the source location, numeric forms, selected policy and a clear exact/checked alternative. Semantic refusals remain structured diagnostics with logs disabled. Proposed diagnostic identifiers must be finalized against existing namespaces during implementation.

12 / committed follow-up scope

Strings is the next stage after numeric libraries

Strings gets its own specification and qualification after N6. Reuse the numeric stage's mixed-type signatures, direct-call resolution, metadata ownership and SDK capability inventory. Start with String parameters/results, literals, lets/calls, concatenation and equality; then qualify comparison, length, slicing and a curated String SDK subset.

The pinned MoonBit core describes String storage as UTF-16, so the issue is not a simple UTF-8 versus UTF-16 substitution. Its String comparison uses shortlex ordering, while the Morphir SDK provides Elm-compatible lexical ordering. Source slice behavior also trims split surrogate pairs, while the SDK Text model can retain isolated halves. Lower each source operation to its actual semantics and keep Morphir SDK calls under their own contracts.

Cover empty strings, supplementary characters, combining sequences, surrogate boundaries, lexical ordering, substring bounds and case mapping. Existing SDK Text::to_string may reject isolated surrogate halves at a host boundary; define that boundary explicitly rather than silently replacing text. General regex, interpolation, locale-sensitive operations, collections and arbitrary String methods need separate claims.

The order is numeric specification and implementation, numeric installed qualification, then the full Strings specification and implementation. F4 packaging can progress independently when A2 is ready.

13 / design decisions

Make the choices concrete before widening source admission

DecisionSelected directionImplementation check
Public fixed-width typesReuse SDK boundary wrappers and conversions, retaining original source form in metadata.N1 checks generated consumer ABI and exact parameter/result admission. Do not silently change wrappers into machine primitives.
Source names and arithmeticUse canonical MoonBit Int32/UInt32, retain authored legacy aliases, and preserve the aligned compiler's semantics with exact Morphir Int intermediates.Align compiler/core/parser pins in N1. Probe each admitted operation/type before advertising it. Original alias-spelling receipts record 0.10.15, despite revision 0.1's incorrect narrative attribution.
Source precision carrierVersioned attribute extensions and native Ion node metadata now; checked native graph projection later.Declare payload schema and actual node ownership. No native V4.1 claim from a V4.0 extension object.
SDK compatibilityKeep classic inventory/default API intact; opt into additional numeric specification/runtime capabilities.Separate provenance, support and conformance for every added function.
Math portabilityExplicit operation contracts and per-function qualification.Agree exact-bit versus bounded-error expectations from the actual source and SDK implementations, before enabling each binding.
Delivery scopeLocal engine/CLI and generated libraries first; no new release or upstream completion implied.Six numeric slices, followed by a separately specified Strings stage.

The compiler probe is intentionally small. Parser AST coverage, exact source casts, all width-specific division/overflow cases and transcendental error bounds remain implementation evidence to collect. These are acceptance obligations, not reasons to advertise a partially implemented broad profile.

14 / evidence and record

Source contracts and canonical work tracking

  • Current Boolean frontend contract, typed lowering and origin owners, and provider/profile registration.
  • Existing SDK Int conversions, SDK specification API, classic specification declarations, and SDK semantic boundaries.
  • Current generator SDK allowlist, scalar mapping, current attribute containers, and Ion codecs and JSON loss guard.
  • Current MoonBit numeric names and compatibility aliases and lexical reference. Current names are the design target. The original receipt records 0.10.15; the separate explicit-path probe distinguishes it from the repository's 0.10.14 pin. N1 must align and qualify compiler/core/parser pins before implementing the new source profiles.
  • Pinned compiler observations. Installed core string/README.mbt.md documents UTF-16 code units, shortlex comparison and surrogate-aware slice behavior; the evidence manifest records its exact bytes.
  • Upstream numeric constraints draft, Decision 0019, and metadata reference contract. These describe proposed native metadata revisions, not new claims for the current engine codec.
  • Numeric stage morphir-ukvn.1.10.12 owns this HTML specification. Six implementation tasks belong to plan morphir-ukvn.1.10.12.1, rendered locally as the implementation plan. Numeric and Strings stages are parented under Track 5 morphir-ukvn.5 and reference A7 morphir-ukvn.1.10 in their records, so local work does not inherit its packaging blocker. F4 morphir-ukvn.1.10.5 and A2 morphir-ukvn.1.3 keep their existing dependency. Strings morphir-ukvn.1.10.13 depends on numeric qualification.

Specification, implementation plan and execution ledger are canonical in the shared beads tracker. Files beneath .dev/ are local review/rendering artifacts and must not be staged. Evidence identity manifest.

Revision 0.2 corrects current source names to Int32/UInt32, preserves authored aliases in metadata and adds compiler/core/parser alignment to N1. The original probe retains its spellings and actual 0.10.15 identity; revision 0.1's incorrect attribution to the repository pin is corrected. Numeric representation preservation, executable arithmetic, additive SDK contracts, six delivery slices and the Strings follow-up remain in scope. No production numeric frontend implementation or package release is claimed.

Most of the runtime foundation already exists

ComponentAvailable nowNumeric stage adds
Pure source frontendExplicit Bool signatures, acyclic same-file calls, lets, conditionals and source origins.Resolved scalar types, exact numeric literals, typed operators, finite SDK bindings.

The 248 SDK bindings and 57 generator adapters describe different inventories. A binding becomes an advertised source capability only after source admission, lowering, evaluation, generation and selected target lanes have evidence.

03 / architecture

Extend contracts at their existing boundaries

The diagram shows the landed Boolean path that numbers will extend. Open the explorable version for source references and SVG export. Numeric semantics in the following sections are proposed.

Open the complete pipeline diagram. Its automated artifact and browser checks pass; no perceptual-review claim is made.

ContractResponsibilityConfiguration and replacement
Source type resolverResolve scalar spellings and explicit SDK aliases against an immutable environment. Distinguish a local shadow from a known SDK binding.A versioned source binding environment supplied by the adapter, without filesystem or network access in the pure compiler.

Host and engineFreeze selection and dependencies, enforce budgets, persist artifacts, execute approved operations and report evidence.Reuse existing host grants, provider admission, cancellation and output publication rules.
04 / source inventory

Use current MoonBit numeric names

The target inventory is ten scalar source types, using Int32 and UInt32 as the current preferred names. Current MoonBit accepts Int and UInt as compatibility aliases and its formatter uses the explicit-width names. These source names are distinct from Morphir's arbitrary-precision Int and its Int SDK module.

The maintainer selected compiler/core 0.10.15+943464bfa. Upgrade task morphir-ukvn.1.10.12.2 updates development, managed acquisition, embedding and telemetry pins together. The previous 0.10.14+7d59c7ec9 pin rejects Int32/UInt32; the explicit 0.10.15 probe accepts them. Existing repository and Boolean frontend qualification pass locally. Numeric frontend admission remains N1 work, and merging the upgrade remains separately tracked.

MoonBit formRepresentation factsProposed Morphir contractDelivery
Int32Signed 32-bit; legacy source alias IntExisting SDK Int32 boundary type and exact Morphir Int working values.N1
Int16, Int64Signed 16-bit, 64-bitExisting SDK Int16/Int64 boundaries and checked conversions.N2
Byte, UInt16, UInt32, UInt64Unsigned 8-bit, 16-bit, 32-bit, 64-bitAdded SDK Int-module unsigned boundary types and exact widening conversions.N2

DoubleIEEE binary64, 53 significand bits for normal valuesExisting SDK Basics.Float and qualified Float64 operations.N3
SDK DecimalLibrary type, not a MoonBit built-in scalarExisting SDK Decimal with its exact numerical coefficient/exponent semantics and separately retained source scale.N5

The MoonBit SDK runtime now names its fixed-width wrappers Int16Value, Int32Value and Int64Value, because 0.10.15 reserves the built-in names. Their canonical Morphir SDK type identities and conversion functions retain their contracts. See the SDK migration note. N1 must map semantic SDK boundary types to these actual MoonBit wrappers.

MoonBit has no native signed Int8 in this inventory; the classic SDK's Int8 remains supported as its own SDK type. SIMD vectors, arbitrary user-defined numeric traits and foreign numeric types are outside this stage. Future compiler additions require an inventory revision and evidence.

Finite integer literals are decoded exactly from their radix and suffix, without passing through machine Int or Double. Preserve authored radix, separators and suffix in metadata while writing a valid canonical Morphir literal. The type checker uses the resolved source type, not a digit-count guess.

Compiler probe evidence and its limits

The original probe below used compiler 0.10.15+943464bfa via PATH, as its unchanged receipt records. Revision 0.1 incorrectly attributed it to the repository pin. The new compatibility probe uses explicit compiler paths and records the old pin's rejection plus successful Int32/UInt32 identity functions on 0.10.15 across eight target/build-mode lanes. The separate current-name compatibility probe and Ion receipt record rejection of Int32/UInt32 by that pin. Probe source, primary Ion receipt and JSON inspection view cover ten identity signatures and three observations: signed Int maximum plus one, UInt maximum plus one, and Float 16777216 + 1. They establish only those source compiler observations. They do not qualify all integer operators, casts, parsing, SDK mapping or numeric source compilation.

05 / executable meaning

Widen exactly, then apply the operation the source asked for

SituationRequired behavior
Bounded integer → Morphir IntExact widening using the corresponding SDK conversion. Record source representation and conversion origin.
Morphir Int → bounded typeChecked narrowing through existing toInt* contracts or corresponding additions. Return absence or the declared failure form; do not silently wrap.
Source fixed-width arithmeticPreserve source behavior through explicit normalization/helpers. The original 0.10.15 probe observes Int and UInt alias addition wrapping; repeat the relevant Int32/UInt32 observations under the aligned compiler and probe every additional admitted operator and width.
Source machine cast or bit reinterpretationKeep distinct from checked SDK narrowing. Admit only individually specified and tested casts; initial source profiles may reject other methods with a clear diagnostic.
BigInt arithmeticExact arbitrary-precision operations, subject to resource budgets. Qualify source division and remainder rules before reusing a classic adapter.
Float32 arithmeticRound at the source's observable binary32 operation boundaries. Promoting to Double and rounding only the final result is insufficient.
Floating point → IntProvide a checked exact conversion and separately named rounding/truncation operations. Define fractional, nonfinite and range cases explicitly; never label a rounding conversion lossless.
Int → Float or DoubleIdentify whether the conversion is exact or rounding. Test beyond the 24-bit and 53-bit significand boundaries; do not silently narrow during literal parsing or JSON handling.
Division and exceptional valuesSpecify zero divisors, signed-minimum divided by minus one, NaN, infinity, subnormals and signed zero. Refuse an operation/profile if its target lanes cannot meet its declared behavior.
DecimalRetain the existing SDK's numerical semantics, including minimum exponent and half-even rounding. Source scale is a descriptive fact; it does not change arithmetic implicitly.

Metadata describes where a value came from. Executable IR determines how it behaves. A backend that does not interpret source precision must still evaluate the explicit lowered arithmetic correctly, or refuse an unsupported required SDK binding.

Use portable IR implementations for width normalization where practical, with audited runtime acceleration permitted under the same contract. Avoid an annotation that secretly changes ordinary Basics.add. Preserve eager lets, short-circuit Boolean guards and left-to-right single evaluation of function arguments.

06 / facts, attributes and ownership

Keep source precision queryable and correctly attached

Reuse the current V4 attribute extension maps and engine-owned native Ion metadata. Align future native projection with the upstream scoped-property-graph decision. Do not place declaration facts on a function-body expression merely because that expression has an attributes field.

FactContentsOwner and lifetime
Source numeric representationSource language, authored type spelling and canonical resolved type; integer/floating/decimal category; signedness; width or arbitrary precision; IEEE format and significand precision where relevant. For example, authored Int resolves to Int32 under the current alias contract. Retain the compiler/profile identity.Parameter/output type use or original expression. Copy origin links when lowering introduces a wrapper or temporary.
Authored numeric literalOriginal token spelling, radix, suffix, source location and canonical semantic value. Floating values retain an exact bit observation after source rounding where relevant.Original literal expression, with links from generated literal nodes.
Conversion receiptInput representation, output representation, exact/checked/rounded/reinterpreted policy, binding identity and source expression origin.Conversion expression and synthetic nodes implementing it. Dynamic per-invocation loss is an execution observation, not a compile-time claim.
SDK addition provenanceClassic baseline revision, extension contract/version, declaring module, canonical function identity and evidence status.SDK value/type declaration or specification. Call sites reference the declaration and required extension inventory.
Semantic type constraintsActual bounds or representation required by the type contract, using the shared numeric constraint vocabulary when supported.Relevant type node. Do not attach the original source width as a semantic bound to an arbitrary-precision result that can exceed it.
Illustrative Ion payload, not a registered predicate spelling
source_number::{
  contract: "moonbit-source-number-v1",
  source_language: "moonbit",
  source_type: "UInt64",
  representation: {kind: integer, signed: false, bits: 64},
  literal: {
    spelling: "18446744073709551615UL",
    radix: 10,
    canonical_integer: 18446744073709551615
  },
