}

Illustrates a metadata object's content. Final extension keys and predicate/type FQNames must be declared and versioned during N1/N2. An Ion annotation token does not itself declare or authenticate a Morphir predicate.

The current carriers are TypeAttributes.extensions, ValueAttributes.extensions and addressed IRUnit.metadata. New typed payloads must validate their own schema and preserve unknown neighboring metadata. Existing declaration/body metadata stores nested origins; reuse those owners without pretending every nested origin already has a portable native Node URI.

Upstream Decision 0019 places native node facts in attributes.facts, specification facts in annotations.facts, and explicit-subject declaration facts in $meta.@graph. That is a future-revision design, not permission to add those fields to the current V4.0 codec. A native projection must negotiate the actual IR/Ion revisions and preserve assertion ownership.

Descriptive source facts require schema validation. They cannot authorize optimized execution, register SDK functions or impersonate authenticated semantic providers. Any future optimizer interpretation must declare its interpreter, exact contracts and evidence through the existing metadata/provider admission boundary.

07 / compatibility

Extend Int while keeping the classic SDK identifiable

The classic Int module already contains Int8, Int16, Int32 and Int64, each with exact widening and checked narrowing. Reuse those definitions. Add missing numeric forms in the same conceptual conversion module, with fully qualified names and an explicit extension inventory.

Classic baseline

Keep the existing pinned morphir-elm inventory and sdk_specification() default behavior. Continue to report classic conformance against its actual oracle.

Existing signed conversion signatures and behavior do not become MoonBit-specific or change silently.

Additive numeric contracts

Proposed capability identifier morphir-sdk-moonbit-numeric-v1 identifies added unsigned types/conversions, Float32 construction/conversion and any source-width helpers.

Provide an explicit extended specification API/profile and separate manifest entries. The identifier is proposed; publishing a package version is separate work.

Function familyContractClassification
Existing signed fromInt*/toInt*Preserve current exact widening and checked narrowing.Classic SDK
Unsigned equivalents covering Byte/UInt16/UInt32/UInt64Exact nonnegative widening and checked range on return. Prefer width-based SDK identities; retain MoonBit source aliases in metadata.SDK addition
Float32/Float64 → Int conversionsExact checked conversion plus explicitly named rounding policies. Cover nonfinite/fractional cases. Reuse classic functions only when their semantics and signatures match.New functions marked as additions; existing classic functions retain their identity
Int → floating conversionsExpose rounding or exactness policy. Never use these conversions as an intermediate exact integer transport.Classify each actual binding
BigInt bridgeExact bridge to the existing Integer representation. Do not duplicate a public SDK identity merely to label its source language.Existing representation plus any genuinely new bridge binding
Source-width normalizationExplicit portable behavior distinct from checked narrowing. Generated/native implementations must meet the same contract.SDK addition if a public helper is needed

For every added declaration, record extension provenance as metadata/annotations in a supported carrier. Include the same identity in SDK-spec, runtime binding inventory, Scheme registration, generator coverage and capability requirements. Inventory JSON alone does not satisfy the requested IR metadata. No added binding may count as classic morphir-elm parity.

Prefer existing supported SDK implementations and MoonBit core. This design introduces no new third-party dependency. Cross-repository standardization in finos/morphir, morphir-elm or another backend remains separately tracked work.

08 / source admission

Resolve a finite SDK vocabulary through a frozen environment

Keep the source language moonbit. Retain existing Boolean profiles and their default. Add separately versioned complete profiles for signed Int32, integral libraries and numeric libraries as those slices become qualified. Profiles describe supported types/operators/functions; they do not become new language names.

Proposed IDs are moonbit-model-int32-library-v1, moonbit-model-integer-library-v1 and moonbit-model-numeric-library-v1. A profile's declared semantics remain stable. Offer it only when its complete advertised subset passes acceptance. Public capability output lists types and function families without dumping dependency descriptions into prose.

Allow SDK-qualified references only through an explicit immutable binding environment with source alias, actual MoonBit package identity, version/tree pin, source signature, canonical Morphir declaration and conversion policy. A textual alias such as @math alone does not prove it denotes core math. The engine adapter owns resolution; the pure compiler receives already resolved declarations.

First math functions are sqrt, pow, sin and cos, plus existing arithmetic, comparisons, abs and rounding/conversion families as individually qualified. Align actual core @math and SDK source call forms only after compiler/parser probes. Do not mechanically substitute similarly named functions when domain/error/rounding behavior differs.

Typed direct calls can mix Bool and supported numeric parameters/results. Same-file acyclic calls and immutable single-name lets remain the source structure. General imports, arbitrary methods, generics, recursion, mutation, effects, asynchronous calls and general record/pattern support are separate capabilities. Conversion functions returning Maybe/Result are SDK capabilities; admitting their source syntax requires an explicit matching source capability and cannot be inferred from SDK availability.

09 / storage

Prefer Ion and retain checked JSON boundaries

Use native Ion integer/decimal/float values in metadata and intermediate receipts, with binary Ion for compact installed qualification artifacts. Preserve source annotations, exact integer values, decimal spelling/scale and numeric bits through existing envelopes. Do not claim a source width from the compactness of an Ion encoding.

Morphir JSON is a supported interchange format. The current engine JSON codec rejects an IRUnit that contains engine metadata/provenance it cannot carry, with data.lossy_conversion. Keep that guard. A source-produced numeric unit therefore cannot automatically become a lossless bare Morphir JSON file merely because its IR attributes are JSON-shaped.

Use the existing checked JSON records/inspection views where appropriate. A future metadata-capable JSON adapter or explicit separately inventoried sidecar may be added, but is not assumed here. JSON loss tests must prove rejection or exact supported preservation, including integers beyond 2^53. No unconditional JSON fallback and no new native V4 fields under the old format version.

Nonfinite Float literals remain unsupported by the current generator. Runtime NaN/infinity results need an explicit tagged/bits observation at the execution boundary and a negotiated serialization contract. An Ion float's ability to store them does not establish IR literal or generated-code support.

10 / implementation plan

Each slice delivers a usable path through the engine

Each numeric slice includes frontend admission, typed IR, metadata, SDK/evaluator behavior, generator adapters, engine/CLI selection and focused differential tests. The final slice qualifies their combined installed behavior. Implementation is pending; the plan does not claim these capabilities already exist.

N1 / ready to implement / no packaging dependency

Signed Int32 library arithmetic

Verify compiler/core 0.10.15+943464bfa from prerequisite task morphir-ukvn.1.10.12.2 and probe parser admission for current Int32/UInt32 naming. Accept Bool and explicitly typed Int32 functions, integer literals, +/−/×, comparisons, if/lets/direct calls. Reuse SDK Int32 boundaries, exact working Int values and explicit signed-width normalization. Include a callable generated consumer, source precision receipts and Ion replay. Freeze parser/compiler observations for this subset. Qualify legacy aliases separately and preserve authored spellings.

N2 / after N1

All scalar integer forms and Int conversions

Add Int16, Int64, Byte, UInt16, UInt32, UInt64 and BigInt. Extend Int specification/runtime/metadata for unsigned forms. Qualify integer division/remainder per supported type, checked narrowing and source casts separately. Advertise an integral profile only for proven operations.

N3 / after N2

Float, Double and explicit conversion policies

Implement source floating literals/operations, Float32 rounding points and integer bridges. Add exceptional-value and signed-zero receipts. Preserve source precision and operation origins in checkpoints and generated symbols.

N4 / after N3

Curated math SDK calls

Freeze source alias/package binding, map sqrt/pow/sin/cos and selected numeric SDK functions, and add missing generator adapters. Compare domains, errors and results across source, Scheme and generated execution. Publish a per-function support matrix.

N5 / after N4

Decimal library calculations

Add an explicit Decimal SDK source binding and a small closed subset: exact construction, add/sub/mul, comparisons, rounding and a documented division form that does not imply general Maybe/pattern admission. Retain literal scale separately from numerical runtime normalization. Qualify the existing −32 exponent floor and default/error semantics.

N6 / after N5

Installed numeric libraries and evidence

Qualify all offered numeric profiles through installed npm/native CLI lanes, consumer ABI, Ion text/binary replay, checked JSON handling, required SDK extension admission and enabled/disabled observations. Produce the final machine-readable per-type/per-function/target evidence matrix.

Related workRelationshipNext requirement
F4 / A2 packagingIndependent of local numeric implementation.Use the qualified profile inventory when the agreed extension contract is available.

11 / proof

Compare behavior and independently check the metadata

DimensionRequired evidence
Integer boundariesEvery min/max, one-step overflow/underflow, exact values above 2^53, UInt64 max, large BigInt, negative division/remainder and zero-divisor cases.
Floating behaviorBinary32/64 precision boundaries, non-associative examples, rounding/conversion edges, signed zero, subnormals, NaN and infinity outcomes. Exact bits for operations whose contract promises them.
Math functionsKnown values plus independently generated reference vectors. Declare per-function error/ULP limits for transcendental implementations; do not reuse a broad tolerance to hide integer or basic IEEE arithmetic differences. Compare domain/error categories exactly.
DecimalCoefficient/exponent precision, zero/trailing-zero normalization, rounding ties, division/default semantics and the SDK exponent floor. Separately verify retained literal scale.
Library behaviorPublic/private visibility, multiple entries, forward calls, mixed scalar signatures, shadowing, single evaluation and short circuit. Existing Boolean profiles retain their tests and default selection.
MetadataType-use/parameter/output ownership, distinct source and result representation, generated temporary origins, unknown-fact preservation and SDK addition classification. Ion replay preserves native rich values.
Installed targetsWasm, Wasm-GC, JS and native in debug/release for source/generation qualification. Installed platform lanes reuse the repository's supported OS/package contracts. Record actual lane coverage; do not infer it from a local probe.
Failure and resource boundsUnsupported type/operator/call, missing required SDK extension, source literal out of range, conversion failure, cancellation and over-budget numeric size all produce stable contextual failures before publication.

Add numeric token length, integer bit/exponent magnitude and operation-cost limits to existing byte/expression/call limits. A low-cost source expression such as a huge power can have an expensive result; admission and evaluator fuel must account for that. Use existing observer scopes and structured warnings. Logs, when enabled, default beneath .morphir/logs/; explicit user paths remain honored.

Ordinary exact widening emits no warning. Report a warning only for a real automatic recovery or an explicitly selected potentially lossy policy; include the source location, numeric forms, selected policy and a clear exact/checked alternative. Semantic refusals remain structured diagnostics with logs disabled. Proposed diagnostic identifiers must be finalized against existing namespaces during implementation.

12 / committed follow-up scope

Strings is the next stage after numeric libraries

Strings gets its own specification and qualification after N6. Reuse the numeric stage's mixed-type signatures, direct-call resolution, metadata ownership and SDK capability inventory. Start with String parameters/results, literals, lets/calls, concatenation and equality; then qualify comparison, length, slicing and a curated String SDK subset.

The pinned MoonBit core describes String storage as UTF-16, so the issue is not a simple UTF-8 versus UTF-16 substitution. Its String comparison uses shortlex ordering, while the Morphir SDK provides Elm-compatible lexical ordering. Source slice behavior also trims split surrogate pairs, while the SDK Text model can retain isolated halves. Lower each source operation to its actual semantics and keep Morphir SDK calls under their own contracts.

Cover empty strings, supplementary characters, combining sequences, surrogate boundaries, lexical ordering, substring bounds and case mapping. Existing SDK Text::to_string may reject isolated surrogate halves at a host boundary; define that boundary explicitly rather than silently replacing text. General regex, interpolation, locale-sensitive operations, collections and arbitrary String methods need separate claims.

The order is numeric specification and implementation, numeric installed qualification, then the full Strings specification and implementation. F4 packaging can progress independently when A2 is ready.

13 / design decisions

Make the choices concrete before widening source admission

DecisionSelected directionImplementation check
Public fixed-width typesReuse SDK boundary wrappers and conversions, retaining original source form in metadata.N1 checks generated consumer ABI and exact parameter/result admission. Do not silently change wrappers into machine primitives.
Source names and arithmeticUse canonical MoonBit Int32/UInt32, retain authored legacy aliases, and preserve the aligned compiler's semantics with exact Morphir Int intermediates.Use the selected 0.10.15 compiler/core pin and verify parser admission in N1. Probe each admitted operation/type before advertising it. Original alias-spelling receipts record 0.10.15, despite revision 0.1's incorrect narrative attribution.
Source precision carrierVersioned attribute extensions and native Ion node metadata now; checked native graph projection later.Declare payload schema and actual node ownership. No native V4.1 claim from a V4.0 extension object.
SDK compatibilityKeep classic inventory/default API intact; opt into additional numeric specification/runtime capabilities.Separate provenance, support and conformance for every added function.
Math portabilityExplicit operation contracts and per-function qualification.Agree exact-bit versus bounded-error expectations from the actual source and SDK implementations, before enabling each binding.
Delivery scopeLocal engine/CLI and generated libraries first; no new release or upstream completion implied.Six numeric slices, followed by a separately specified Strings stage.

The compiler probe is intentionally small. Parser AST coverage, exact source casts, all width-specific division/overflow cases and transcendental error bounds remain implementation evidence to collect. These are acceptance obligations, not reasons to advertise a partially implemented broad profile.

14 / evidence and record

Source contracts and canonical work tracking

  • Current Boolean frontend contract, typed lowering and origin owners, and provider/profile registration.
  • Existing SDK Int conversions, SDK specification API, classic specification declarations, and SDK semantic boundaries.
  • Current generator SDK allowlist, scalar mapping, current attribute containers, and Ion codecs and JSON loss guard.
  • Current MoonBit numeric names and compatibility aliases and lexical reference. Current names are the design target. The original receipt records 0.10.15; the separate explicit-path probe distinguishes it from the repository's 0.10.14 pin. N1 must align and qualify compiler/core/parser pins before implementing the new source profiles.
  • Pinned compiler observations. Installed core string/README.mbt.md documents UTF-16 code units, shortlex comparison and surrogate-aware slice behavior; the evidence manifest records its exact bytes.
  • Upstream numeric constraints draft, Decision 0019, and metadata reference contract. These describe proposed native metadata revisions, not new claims for the current engine codec.
  • Numeric stage morphir-ukvn.1.10.12 owns this HTML specification. Six implementation tasks belong to plan morphir-ukvn.1.10.12.1, rendered locally as the implementation plan. Numeric and Strings stages are parented under Track 5 morphir-ukvn.5 and reference A7 morphir-ukvn.1.10 in their records, so local work does not inherit its packaging blocker. F4 morphir-ukvn.1.10.5 and A2 morphir-ukvn.1.3 keep their existing dependency. Strings morphir-ukvn.1.10.13 depends on numeric qualification.

Specification, implementation plan and execution ledger are canonical in the shared beads tracker. Files beneath .dev/ are local review/rendering artifacts and must not be staged. Evidence identity manifest.

Revision 0.3 selects compiler/core 0.10.15+943464bfa, records the dedicated pin-upgrade prerequisite and documents the runtime wrapper Value names. Int32/UInt32 are the canonical source names; preserve authored aliases in metadata and verify parser admission in N1. The original probe retains its spellings and actual 0.10.15 identity; revision 0.1's incorrect attribution to the repository pin is corrected. A useful first library

Portable numbers, visible origin

These source names are distinct from Morphir's arbitrary-precision Int and its Int SDK module.

The maintainer selected compiler/core 0.10.15+943464bfa. Upgrade task morphir-ukvn.1.10.12.2 updates development, managed acquisition, embedding and telemetry pins together. The previous 0.10.14+7d59c7ec9 pin rejects Int32/UInt32; the explicit 0.10.15 probe accepts them. Fresh-cache CI exposed incompatible legacy manifests. The upgrade also selects parser 0.4.5, lexer 0.4.3 and compatible maintained dependencies; two small CLI libraries retain their behavior as attributed local workspace modules. Stable 0.10.15 does not enable LLVM, and the old LLVM nightly rejects current numeric names. That lane independently pins 0.10.15+1e9f6672d-nightly with matching compiler/core archive hashes. Boolean frontend and site qualification pass locally with the new dependencies. Broader qualification and PR #89 remain tracked by the upgrade task. Numeric frontend admission remains N1 work.

MoonBit formRepresentation factsProposed Morphir contractDelivery
Int32Signed 32-bit; legacy source alias IntExisting SDK Int32 boundary type and exact Morphir Int working values.N1
Int16, Int64Signed 16-bit, 64-bitExisting SDK Int16/Int64 boundaries and checked conversions.N2
Byte, UInt16, UInt32, UInt64Unsigned 8-bit, 16-bit, 32-bit, 64-bitAdded SDK Int-module unsigned boundary types and exact widening conversions.N2
BigIntSigned arbitrary precisionSDK Basics.Int; representation receipt names the MoonBit source form.N2
FloatIEEE binary32, 24 significand bits including the implicit leading bit for normal valuesAdded Float32 numeric boundary/operations, using an explicit round-to-binary32 operation at every required source rounding point.N3
DoubleIEEE binary64, 53 significand bits for normal valuesExisting SDK Basics.Float and qualified Float64 operations.N3
SDK DecimalLibrary type, not a MoonBit built-in scalarExisting SDK Decimal with its exact numerical coefficient/exponent semantics and separately retained source scale.N5

The MoonBit SDK runtime now names its fixed-width wrappers Int16Value, Int32Value and Int64Value, because 0.10.15 reserves the built-in names. Their canonical Morphir SDK type identities and conversion functions retain their contracts. See the SDK migration note. N1 must map semantic SDK boundary types to these actual MoonBit wrappers.

MoonBit has no native signed Int8 in this inventory; the classic SDK's Int8 remains supported as its own SDK type. SIMD vectors, arbitrary user-defined numeric traits and foreign numeric types are outside this stage. Future compiler additions require an inventory revision and evidence.

Finite integer literals are decoded exactly from their radix and suffix, without passing through machine Int or Double. Preserve authored radix, separators and suffix in metadata while writing a valid canonical Morphir literal. The type checker uses the resolved source type, not a digit-count guess.

Compiler probe evidence and its limits

The original probe below used compiler 0.10.15+943464bfa via PATH, as its unchanged receipt records. Revision 0.1 incorrectly attributed it to the repository pin. The new compatibility probe uses explicit compiler paths and records the old pin's rejection plus successful Int32/UInt32 identity functions on 0.10.15 across eight target/build-mode lanes. The separate current-name compatibility probe and Ion receipt record rejection of Int32/UInt32 by that pin. Probe source, primary Ion receipt and JSON inspection view cover ten identity signatures and three observations: signed Int maximum plus one, UInt maximum plus one, and Float 16777216 + 1. They establish only those source compiler observations. They do not qualify all integer operators, casts, parsing, SDK mapping or numeric source compilation.

05 / executable meaning

Widen exactly, then apply the operation the source asked for

SituationRequired behavior
Bounded integer → Morphir IntExact widening using the corresponding SDK conversion. Record source representation and conversion origin.
Morphir Int → bounded typeChecked narrowing through existing toInt* contracts or corresponding additions. Return absence or the declared failure form; do not silently wrap.
Source fixed-width arithmeticPreserve source behavior through explicit normalization/helpers. The original 0.10.15 probe observes Int and UInt alias addition wrapping; repeat the relevant Int32/UInt32 observations under the aligned compiler and probe every additional admitted operator and width.
Source machine cast or bit reinterpretationKeep distinct from checked SDK narrowing. Admit only individually specified and tested casts; initial source profiles may reject other methods with a clear diagnostic.
BigInt arithmeticExact arbitrary-precision operations, subject to resource budgets. Qualify source division and remainder rules before reusing a classic adapter.
Float32 arithmeticRound at the source's observable binary32 operation boundaries. Promoting to Double and rounding only the final result is insufficient.
Floating point → IntProvide a checked exact conversion and separately named rounding/truncation operations. Define fractional, nonfinite and range cases explicitly; never label a rounding conversion lossless.
Int → Float or DoubleIdentify whether the conversion is exact or rounding. Test beyond the 24-bit and 53-bit significand boundaries; do not silently narrow during literal parsing or JSON handling.
Division and exceptional valuesSpecify zero divisors, signed-minimum divided by minus one, NaN, infinity, subnormals and signed zero. Refuse an operation/profile if its target lanes cannot meet its declared behavior.
DecimalRetain the existing SDK's numerical semantics, including minimum exponent and half-even rounding. Source scale is a descriptive fact; it does not change arithmetic implicitly.

Metadata describes where a value came from. Executable IR determines how it behaves. A backend that does not interpret source precision must still evaluate the explicit lowered arithmetic correctly, or refuse an unsupported required SDK binding.

Use portable IR implementations for width normalization where practical, with audited runtime acceleration permitted under the same contract. Avoid an annotation that secretly changes ordinary Basics.add. Preserve eager lets, short-circuit Boolean guards and left-to-right single evaluation of function arguments.

06 / facts, attributes and ownership

Keep source precision queryable and correctly attached

Reuse the current V4 attribute extension maps and engine-owned native Ion metadata. Align future native projection with the upstream scoped-property-graph decision. Do not place declaration facts on a function-body expression merely because that expression has an attributes field.

FactContentsOwner and lifetime
Source numeric representationSource language, authored type spelling and canonical resolved type; integer/floating/decimal category; signedness; width or arbitrary precision; IEEE format and significand precision where relevant. For example, authored Int resolves to Int32 under the current alias contract. Retain the compiler/profile identity.Parameter/output type use or original expression. Copy origin links when lowering introduces a wrapper or temporary.
Authored numeric literalOriginal token spelling, radix, suffix, source location and canonical semantic value. Floating values retain an exact bit observation after source rounding where relevant.Original literal expression, with links from generated literal nodes.
Conversion receiptInput representation, output representation, exact/checked/rounded/reinterpreted policy, binding identity and source expression origin.Conversion expression and synthetic nodes implementing it. Dynamic per-invocation loss is an execution observation, not a compile-time claim.
SDK addition provenanceClassic baseline revision, extension contract/version, declaring module, canonical function identity and evidence status.SDK value/type declaration or specification. Call sites reference the declaration and required extension inventory.
Semantic type constraintsActual bounds or representation required by the type contract, using the shared numeric constraint vocabulary when supported.Relevant type node. Do not attach the original source width as a semantic bound to an arbitrary-precision result that can exceed it.
Illustrative Ion payload, not a registered predicate spelling
source_number::{
  contract: "moonbit-source-number-v1",
  source_language: "moonbit",
  source_type: "UInt64",
  representation: {kind: integer, signed: false, bits: 64},
  literal: {
    spelling: "18446744073709551615UL",
    radix: 10,
    canonical_integer: 18446744073709551615
  },
  conversion: {policy: exact_widening, destination: "Morphir.Int"}
}

Illustrates a metadata object's content. Final extension keys and predicate/type FQNames must be declared and versioned during N1/N2. An Ion annotation token does not itself declare or authenticate a Morphir predicate.

The current carriers are TypeAttributes.extensions, ValueAttributes.extensions and addressed IRUnit.metadata. New typed payloads must validate their own schema and preserve unknown neighboring metadata. Existing declaration/body metadata stores nested origins; reuse those owners without pretending every nested origin already has a portable native Node URI.

Upstream Decision 0019 places native node facts in attributes.facts, specification facts in annotations.facts, and explicit-subject declaration facts in $meta.@graph. That is a future-revision design, not permission to add those fields to the current V4.0 codec. A native projection must negotiate the actual IR/Ion revisions and preserve assertion ownership.

Descriptive source facts require schema validation. They cannot authorize optimized execution, register SDK functions or impersonate authenticated semantic providers. Any future optimizer interpretation must declare its interpreter, exact contracts and evidence through the existing metadata/provider admission boundary.

07 / compatibility

Extend Int while keeping the classic SDK identifiable

The classic Int module already contains Int8, Int16, Int32 and Int64, each with exact widening and checked narrowing. Reuse those definitions. Add missing numeric forms in the same conceptual conversion module, with fully qualified names and an explicit extension inventory.

Classic baseline

Keep the existing pinned morphir-elm inventory and sdk_specification() default behavior. Continue to report classic conformance against its actual oracle.

Existing signed conversion signatures and behavior do not become MoonBit-specific or change silently.

Additive numeric contracts

Proposed capability identifier morphir-sdk-moonbit-numeric-v1 identifies added unsigned types/conversions, Float32 construction/conversion and any source-width helpers.

Provide an explicit extended specification API/profile and separate manifest entries. The identifier is proposed; publishing a package version is separate work.

Function familyContractClassification
Existing signed fromInt*/toInt*Preserve current exact widening and checked narrowing.Classic SDK
Unsigned equivalents covering Byte/UInt16/UInt32/UInt64Exact nonnegative widening and checked range on return. Prefer width-based SDK identities; retain MoonBit source aliases in metadata.SDK addition
Float32/Float64 → Int conversionsExact checked conversion plus explicitly named rounding policies. Cover nonfinite/fractional cases. Reuse classic functions only when their semantics and signatures match.New functions marked as additions; existing classic functions retain their identity
Int → floating conversionsExpose rounding or exactness policy. Never use these conversions as an intermediate exact integer transport.Classify each actual binding
BigInt bridgeExact bridge to the existing Integer representation. Do not duplicate a public SDK identity merely to label its source language.Existing representation plus any genuinely new bridge binding
Source-width normalizationExplicit portable behavior distinct from checked narrowing. Generated/native implementations must meet the same contract.SDK addition if a public helper is needed

For every added declaration, record extension provenance as metadata/annotations in a supported carrier. Include the same identity in SDK-spec, runtime binding inventory, Scheme registration, generator coverage and capability requirements. Inventory JSON alone does not satisfy the requested IR metadata. No added binding may count as classic morphir-elm parity.

Prefer existing supported SDK implementations and MoonBit core. This design introduces no new third-party dependency. Cross-repository standardization in finos/morphir, morphir-elm or another backend remains separately tracked work.

08 / source admission

Resolve a finite SDK vocabulary through a frozen environment

Keep the source language moonbit. Retain existing Boolean profiles and their default. Add separately versioned complete profiles for signed Int32, integral libraries and numeric libraries as those slices become qualified. Profiles describe supported types/operators/functions; they do not become new language names.

Proposed IDs are moonbit-model-int32-library-v1, moonbit-model-integer-library-v1 and moonbit-model-numeric-library-v1. A profile's declared semantics remain stable. Offer it only when its complete advertised subset passes acceptance. Public capability output lists types and function families without dumping dependency descriptions into prose.

Allow SDK-qualified references only through an explicit immutable binding environment with source alias, actual MoonBit package identity, version/tree pin, source signature, canonical Morphir declaration and conversion policy. A textual alias such as @math alone does not prove it denotes core math. The engine adapter owns resolution; the pure compiler receives already resolved declarations.

First math functions are sqrt, pow, sin and cos, plus existing arithmetic, comparisons, abs and rounding/conversion families as individually qualified. Align actual core @math and SDK source call forms only after compiler/parser probes. Do not mechanically substitute similarly named functions when domain/error/rounding behavior differs.

Typed direct calls can mix Bool and supported numeric parameters/results. Same-file acyclic calls and immutable single-name lets remain the source structure. General imports, arbitrary methods, generics, recursion, mutation, effects, asynchronous calls and general record/pattern support are separate capabilities. Conversion functions returning Maybe/Result are SDK capabilities; admitting their source syntax requires an explicit matching source capability and cannot be inferred from SDK availability.

09 / storage

Prefer Ion and retain checked JSON boundaries

Use native Ion integer/decimal/float values in metadata and intermediate receipts, with binary Ion for compact installed qualification artifacts. Preserve source annotations, exact integer values, decimal spelling/scale and numeric bits through existing envelopes. Do not claim a source width from the compactness of an Ion encoding.

Morphir JSON is a supported interchange format. The current engine JSON codec rejects an IRUnit that contains engine metadata/provenance it cannot carry, with data.lossy_conversion. Keep that guard. A source-produced numeric unit therefore cannot automatically become a lossless bare Morphir JSON file merely because its IR attributes are JSON-shaped.

Use the existing checked JSON records/inspection views where appropriate. A future metadata-capable JSON adapter or explicit separately inventoried sidecar may be added, but is not assumed here. JSON loss tests must prove rejection or exact supported preservation, including integers beyond 2^53. No unconditional JSON fallback and no new native V4 fields under the old format version.

Nonfinite Float literals remain unsupported by the current generator. Runtime NaN/infinity results need an explicit tagged/bits observation at the execution boundary and a negotiated serialization contract. An Ion float's ability to store them does not establish IR literal or generated-code support.

10 / implementation plan

Each slice delivers a usable path through the engine

Each numeric slice includes frontend admission, typed IR, metadata, SDK/evaluator behavior, generator adapters, engine/CLI selection and focused differential tests. The final slice qualifies their combined installed behavior. Implementation is pending; the plan does not claim these capabilities already exist.

N1 / ready to implement / no packaging dependency

Signed Int32 library arithmetic

Verify compiler/core 0.10.15+943464bfa from prerequisite task morphir-ukvn.1.10.12.2 and probe parser admission for current Int32/UInt32 naming. Accept Bool and explicitly typed Int32 functions, integer literals, +/−/×, comparisons, if/lets/direct calls. Reuse SDK Int32 boundaries, exact working Int values and explicit signed-width normalization. Include a callable generated consumer, source precision receipts and Ion replay. Freeze parser/compiler observations for this subset. Qualify legacy aliases separately and preserve authored spellings.

N2 / after N1

All scalar integer forms and Int conversions

Add Int16, Int64, Byte, UInt16, UInt32, UInt64 and BigInt. Extend Int specification/runtime/metadata for unsigned forms. Qualify integer division/remainder per supported type, checked narrowing and source casts separately. Advertise an integral profile only for proven operations.

N3 / after N2

Float, Double and explicit conversion policies

Implement source floating literals/operations, Float32 rounding points and integer bridges. Add exceptional-value and signed-zero receipts. Preserve source precision and operation origins in checkpoints and generated symbols.

N4 / after N3

Curated math SDK calls

Freeze source alias/package binding, map sqrt/pow/sin/cos and selected numeric SDK functions, and add missing generator adapters. Compare domains, errors and results across source, Scheme and generated execution. Publish a per-function support matrix.

N5 / after N4

Decimal library calculations

Add an explicit Decimal SDK source binding and a small closed subset: exact construction, add/sub/mul, comparisons, rounding and a documented division form that does not imply general Maybe/pattern admission. Retain literal scale separately from numerical runtime normalization. Qualify the existing −32 exponent floor and default/error semantics.

N6 / after N5

Installed numeric libraries and evidence

Qualify all offered numeric profiles through installed npm/native CLI lanes, consumer ABI, Ion text/binary replay, checked JSON handling, required SDK extension admission and enabled/disabled observations. Produce the final machine-readable per-type/per-function/target evidence matrix.

Related workRelationshipNext requirement
F4 / A2 packagingIndependent of local numeric implementation.Use the qualified profile inventory when the agreed extension contract is available.
Shared generic inferenceNot required for explicitly typed scalar source.Reuse shared services if later profiles admit generic numeric abstractions.
Authenticated metadata providersDescriptive facts do not grant execution authority.Use existing admission for any future interpreter-driven optimization or external semantic vocabulary.
StringsNext source stage after N6.Produce its full HTML specification and then qualify source text behavior.
11 / proof

Compare behavior and independently check the metadata

DimensionRequired evidence
Integer boundariesEvery min/max, one-step overflow/underflow, exact values above 2^53, UInt64 max, large BigInt, negative division/remainder and zero-divisor cases.
Floating behaviorBinary32/64 precision boundaries, non-associative examples, rounding/conversion edges, signed zero, subnormals, NaN and infinity outcomes. Exact bits for operations whose contract promises them.
Math functionsKnown values plus independently generated reference vectors. Declare per-function error/ULP limits for transcendental implementations; do not reuse a broad tolerance to hide integer or basic IEEE arithmetic differences. Compare domain/error categories exactly.
DecimalCoefficient/exponent precision, zero/trailing-zero normalization, rounding ties, division/default semantics and the SDK exponent floor. Separately verify retained literal scale.
Library behaviorPublic/private visibility, multiple entries, forward calls, mixed scalar signatures, shadowing, single evaluation and short circuit. Existing Boolean profiles retain their tests and default selection.
MetadataType-use/parameter/output ownership, distinct source and result representation, generated temporary origins, unknown-fact preservation and SDK addition classification. Ion replay preserves native rich values.
Installed targetsWasm, Wasm-GC, JS and native in debug/release for source/generation qualification. Installed platform lanes reuse the repository's supported OS/package contracts. Record actual lane coverage; do not infer it from a local probe.
Failure and resource boundsUnsupported type/operator/call, missing required SDK extension, source literal out of range, conversion failure, cancellation and over-budget numeric size all produce stable contextual failures before publication.

Add numeric token length, integer bit/exponent magnitude and operation-cost limits to existing byte/expression/call limits. A low-cost source expression such as a huge power can have an expensive result; admission and evaluator fuel must account for that. Use existing observer scopes and structured warnings. Logs, when enabled, default beneath .morphir/logs/; explicit user paths remain honored.

Ordinary exact widening emits no warning. Report a warning only for a real automatic recovery or an explicitly selected potentially lossy policy; include the source location, numeric forms, selected policy and a clear exact/checked alternative. Semantic refusals remain structured diagnostics with logs disabled. Proposed diagnostic identifiers must be finalized against existing namespaces during implementation.

12 / committed follow-up scope

Strings is the next stage after numeric libraries

Strings gets its own specification and qualification after N6. Reuse the numeric stage's mixed-type signatures, direct-call resolution, metadata ownership and SDK capability inventory. Start with String parameters/results, literals, lets/calls, concatenation and equality; then qualify comparison, length, slicing and a curated String SDK subset.

The pinned MoonBit core describes String storage as UTF-16, so the issue is not a simple UTF-8 versus UTF-16 substitution. Its String comparison uses shortlex ordering, while the Morphir SDK provides Elm-compatible lexical ordering. Source slice behavior also trims split surrogate pairs, while the SDK Text model can retain isolated halves. Lower each source operation to its actual semantics and keep Morphir SDK calls under their own contracts.

Cover empty strings, supplementary characters, combining sequences, surrogate boundaries, lexical ordering, substring bounds and case mapping. Existing SDK Text::to_string may reject isolated surrogate halves at a host boundary; define that boundary explicitly rather than silently replacing text. General regex, interpolation, locale-sensitive operations, collections and arbitrary String methods need separate claims.

The order is numeric specification and implementation, numeric installed qualification, then the full Strings specification and implementation. F4 packaging can progress independently when A2 is ready.

13 / design decisions

Make the choices concrete before widening source admission

DecisionSelected directionImplementation check
Public fixed-width typesReuse SDK boundary wrappers and conversions, retaining original source form in metadata.N1 checks generated consumer ABI and exact parameter/result admission. Do not silently change wrappers into machine primitives.
Source names and arithmeticUse canonical MoonBit Int32/UInt32, retain authored legacy aliases, and preserve the aligned compiler's semantics with exact Morphir Int intermediates.Use the selected 0.10.15 compiler/core pin and verify parser admission in N1. Probe each admitted operation/type before advertising it. Original alias-spelling receipts record 0.10.15, despite revision 0.1's incorrect narrative attribution.
Source precision carrierVersioned attribute extensions and native Ion node metadata now; checked native graph projection later.Declare payload schema and actual node ownership. No native V4.1 claim from a V4.0 extension object.
SDK compatibilityKeep classic inventory/default API intact; opt into additional numeric specification/runtime capabilities.Separate provenance, support and conformance for every added function.
Math portabilityExplicit operation contracts and per-function qualification.Agree exact-bit versus bounded-error expectations from the actual source and SDK implementations, before enabling each binding.
Delivery scopeLocal engine/CLI and generated libraries first; no new release or upstream completion implied.Six numeric slices, followed by a separately specified Strings stage.

The compiler probe is intentionally small. Parser AST coverage, exact source casts, all width-specific division/overflow cases and transcendental error bounds remain implementation evidence to collect. These are acceptance obligations, not reasons to advertise a partially implemented broad profile.

14 / evidence and record

Source contracts and canonical work tracking

  • Current Boolean frontend contract, typed lowering and origin owners, and provider/profile registration.
  • Existing SDK Int conversions, SDK specification API, classic specification declarations, and SDK semantic boundaries.
  • Current generator SDK allowlist, scalar mapping, current attribute containers, and Ion codecs and JSON loss guard.
  • Current MoonBit numeric names and compatibility aliases and lexical reference. Current names are the design target. The original receipt records 0.10.15; the separate explicit-path probe distinguishes it from the repository's 0.10.14 pin. N1 must align and qualify compiler/core/parser pins before implementing the new source profiles.
  • Pinned compiler observations. Installed core string/README.mbt.md documents UTF-16 code units, shortlex comparison and surrogate-aware slice behavior; the evidence manifest records its exact bytes.
  • Upstream numeric constraints draft, Decision 0019, and metadata reference contract. These describe proposed native metadata revisions, not new claims for the current engine codec.
  • Numeric stage morphir-ukvn.1.10.12 owns this HTML specification. Six implementation tasks belong to plan morphir-ukvn.1.10.12.1, rendered locally as the implementation plan. Numeric and Strings stages are parented under Track 5 morphir-ukvn.5 and reference A7 morphir-ukvn.1.10 in their records, so local work does not inherit its packaging blocker. F4 morphir-ukvn.1.10.5 and A2 morphir-ukvn.1.3 keep their existing dependency. Strings morphir-ukvn.1.10.13 depends on numeric qualification.

Specification, implementation plan and execution ledger are canonical in the shared beads tracker. Files beneath .dev/ are local review/rendering artifacts and must not be staged. Evidence identity manifest.

Revision 0.4 selects compiler/core 0.10.15+943464bfa, records the dedicated pin-upgrade prerequisite, fresh dependency migrations, independent LLVM pin and runtime wrapper Value names. Int32/UInt32 are the canonical source names; preserve authored aliases in metadata and verify parser admission in N1. The original probe retains its spellings and actual 0.10.15 identity; revision 0.1's incorrect attribution to the repository pin is corrected. Numeric representation preservation, executable arithmetic, additive SDK contracts, six delivery slices and the Strings follow-up remain in scope. No production numeric frontend implementation or package release is claimed.

title: Task 7: `Engine::run` reads Scheme projects from `morphir.toml` (bead `morphir-ukvn.5.33`)
description:
### Task 7: `Engine::run` reads Scheme projects from `morphir.toml` (bead `morphir-ukvn.5.33`)

Added during execution with the maintainer's approval. Maintainer rule: Scheme is a new project type and uses the new project system (`morphir.toml`); a `morphir.json` is always a morphir-elm project. The legacy embedding API `Engine::run` still reads `morphir.json` (and `morphir-workspace.json`) as a script-driven Scheme project; this task moves it to `morphir.toml`.

**Files:**
- Modify: `pkgs/morphir-engine/engine.mbt` (the `project_manifest` branch around lines 37-43, the discovery skip list around line 101, and the `Workspace(root)` arm around lines 178-200)
- Modify: `pkgs/morphir-engine/engine_test.mbt` (test "workspace and project manifests inherit script configuration"; new tests)
- Modify: `pkgs/morphir-engine/examples/main.mbt` (`demo/morphir.json`)
- Modify: `pkgs/morphir-engine/README.md` ("Legacy embedding API" section and the `Project(root)` / `Workspace(root)` rows; the split note added by Task 4)
- Possibly modify: `pkgs/morphir-engine/config.mbt` (`manifest`, `optional_string`) if they become unused; remove dead helpers rather than leave warnings.

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: `@configuration.parse(text, origin?) -> @configuration.Document raise`, `Document::text(path, fallback)`, `Document::strings(path)`, `Document::get(path)` (`pkgs/morphir-engine/config/config.mbt`).
- Produces: `Engine::run(host, Project(root))` reads `<root>/morphir.toml` `[project] name` (default `user`) and `source_directory` (default `src`). `Engine::run(host, Workspace(root))` reads `<root>/morphir.toml` `[workspace] members`, literal relative paths only (a member with `*`, `?`, `[` or `{` is a discovery diagnostic: `Engine::run workspace members must be literal paths: <member>`). Neither reads `morphir.json` or `morphir-workspace.json` any more. Every other key of `morphir.toml` is ignored by `Engine::run` (its pipeline settings still come from `morphir.config.scm` and the `config` argument).

- [ ] **Step 1: Write the failing tests**

In `pkgs/morphir-engine/engine_test.mbt`, change the existing test "workspace and project manifests inherit script configuration" so that its project files are TOML:

```moonbit
    ("morphir.toml", "[workspace]\nmembers = ['one', 'two']\n"),
    ...
    ("one/morphir.toml", "[project]\nname = 'one'\nsource_directory = 'src'\n"),
    ...
    ("two/morphir.toml", "[project]\nname = 'two'\nsource_directory = 'lib'\n"),
```

(the `morphir.config.scm` files and sources stay; the assertions stay unchanged). Add:

```moonbit
///|
test "Engine::run no longer reads morphir.json as a Scheme project" {
  let report = @engine.Engine::new().run(
    host([
      ("legacy/morphir.json", "{\"name\":\"legacy\",\"sourceDirectory\":\"src\"}"),
      ("legacy/src/main.scm", "41"),
    ]),
    @engine.Project("legacy"),
  )
  assert_false(report.successful())
  assert_true(report.diagnostics[0].message.contains("morphir.toml"))
}

///|
test "Engine::run workspace members must be literal paths" {
  let report = @engine.Engine::new().run(
    host([
      ("morphir.toml", "[workspace]\nmembers = ['packages/*']\n"),
      ("packages/a/morphir.toml", "[project]\nname = 'a'\n"),
      ("packages/a/src/main.scm", "41"),
    ]),
    @engine.Workspace("."),
  )
  assert_false(report.successful())
  assert_true(report.diagnostics[0].message.contains("literal paths"))
}
```

Adjust the first assertion of the first new test to the real message the code gives for a missing `morphir.toml` (it must name `morphir.toml`).

- [ ] **Step 2: Run the tests to see them fail**

Run (from `pkgs/morphir-engine`): `moon test --target native -f engine_test.mbt`
Expected: FAIL: `Engine::run` still reads `morphir.json` and `morphir-workspace.json`.

- [ ] **Step 3: Implement**

In `engine.mbt`:
- Project settings: replace `manifest(host, root, "morphir.json")` and the two `optional_string` calls with a parse of `<root>/morphir.toml`:

```moonbit
      if project_manifest {
        let path = join(root, "morphir.toml")
        if !(host.exists)(path) {
          raise @scheme.Invalid("Missing project manifest: " + path)
        }
        let document = (host.read)(path) |> @configuration.parse(origin=path)
        settings.package_name = document.text("project.name", "user")
        settings.source = normalize(document.text("project.source_directory", "src"))
      }
```

- Discovery skip list: skip `join(root, "morphir.toml")` instead of `morphir.json` and `morphir-workspace.json`.
- `Workspace(root)`: read `<root>/morphir.toml`, take `document.strings("workspace.members")`, refuse a member that contains `*`, `?`, `[` or `{` with the message in **Interfaces**, and keep the existing rules for each member (non-empty relative path, a subdirectory, no duplicates, `project(path, true, None, inherited)`).
- If `manifest` and `optional_string` in `config.mbt` have no other caller, delete them.

`examples/main.mbt`: replace `("demo/morphir.json", ...)` with `("demo/morphir.toml", "[project]\nname = 'demo'\nsource_directory = 'src'\n")`.

README (`pkgs/morphir-engine/README.md`): in "Legacy embedding API", show the example with `demo/morphir.toml`; the rows become `Project(root)`: `morphir.toml` `[project] name` and `source_directory` (defaults `user`, `src`); `Workspace(root)`: `morphir.toml` `[workspace] members`, literal paths. Remove the sentence that says `Engine::run` reads `morphir.json` as a Scheme project, and say that `morphir.json` is only ever an Elm project (read by `discover` and `plan`).

- [ ] **Step 4: Run the tests on all targets**

Run (from `pkgs/morphir-engine`): `for t in native js wasm wasm-gc; do moon test --target $t || break; done`, then `moon run examples --target native` (the example still prints its result), then `moon fmt` and `mise run lint:moonbit` (from the repository root).
Expected: PASS.

- [ ] **Step 5: Commit**

```bash
git add pkgs/morphir-engine/engine.mbt pkgs/morphir-engine/engine_test.mbt pkgs/morphir-engine/examples/main.mbt pkgs/morphir-engine/README.md
# plus pkgs/morphir-engine/config.mbt if helpers were removed
git commit -m "feat(engine)!: read Engine::run projects from morphir.toml, not morphir.json"
```

The commit body says: BREAKING CHANGE: `Engine::run` with `Project(root)` or `Workspace(root)` reads `morphir.toml`; `morphir.json` and `morphir-workspace.json` are no longer read by it.

title: Elm Wiring Plan A: Engine and CLI — Implementation Plan
description:
# Elm Wiring Plan A: Engine and CLI — Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** `morphir run` compiles an unchanged morphir-elm project (`morphir.json` and `src/**/*.elm`) with the Elm provider, and the engine lists its languages with typed ids.

**Architecture:** A new package `finos/morphir-engine/ids` holds the domain types (ids, names, paths) and the canonical-name function. The source-provider types use them. Workspace discovery maps `morphir.json` to an Elm project with a Morphir IR JSON checkpoint by default. `Engine::languages()` lists every source language without callbacks. The CLI registers the Elm provider. The Elm e2e harness runs from each corpus `morphir.json`.

**Tech Stack:** MoonBit 0.10.14 (pinned with mise), `moon test` on native, js, wasm and wasm-gc, Node 24 for the CLI smoke test.

**Spec:** `.dev/beads-specs/morphir-ukvn.5.22.4.md` (sections 2, 3 and 4). Bead `morphir-ukvn.5.22.4`.

## Global Constraints

- Branch `DamianReeves/elm-wiring`, from `origin/main` (`5640c8e`, which contains #82). All three plans of `.22.4` go on this branch; no PR until the maintainer asks.
- Toolchain: `export MOON_HOME="$(mise where http:moonbit)" PATH="$(mise where http:moonbit)/bin:$PATH"` before every `moon` command.
- No document limit by default: `max_documents: None` means no limit.
- Parse at the boundary: CLI flags, TOML, `morphir.json` and wire JSON become domain types where they enter. Only the wire carries `String`.
- Clear MoonBit warnings in the modules a task touches, and only there. Do not fix warnings in other modules.
- Every package a task changes builds and tests on `native`, `js`, `wasm` and `wasm-gc`.
- Commits use Conventional Commits in plain English, with no AI attribution, no `Co-Authored-By` and no `Claude-Session` lines.
- Do not commit specs, plans or ledgers. Do not add the untracked `pkg.generated.mbti` files.
- No destructive git commands. No bare `git stash`.
- Ergonomics: write call sites, examples, READMEs and tests with MoonBit's `|>` pipe (`x |> f(a)` is `f(x, a)`), the `..` cascade (calls a `Unit` method and keeps the receiver) and method chains where they read better than nested calls or repeated statements. New public functions take their subject as the first parameter, so they pipe (`"elm" |> @ids.LanguageId::parse`). Do not force a pipe where a plain call reads clearer. Probes on MoonBit 0.10.14 confirmed that `..register_source_provider(...)` works on a raising method and that `|>` works with `catch`. A pipe cannot feed a method of another receiver (`plan |> engine.execute_content(f)` does not compile: errors 4080, 4101, 4014), so such calls stay plain.

## Rulings on the spec (decided while writing this plan)

1. **The domain types live in `finos/morphir-engine/ids`, not in the engine root package.** The workspace package parses `morphir.json` and must use them, and the engine root imports the workspace package, so the root cannot hold them.
2. **`ProjectSources.package_name` is `SourcePackageName` (the name as written, for example `Parity.Modules`), not `@ir.Path`.** The Elm frontend matches module headers against the written name. `SourcePackageName::to_path()` gives the `@ir.Path`.
3. **`Source` keeps its `String` fields**, because every `PerFile` frontend and `Engine::run` share it. It is listed on `morphir-ukvn.5.32`.
4. **`ProviderId` keeps the current identifier rule** (non-empty, at most 256 characters, no control characters), not `owner/name`, because a frontend from `register_frontend` uses its language name as its provider id.
5. **`LanguageOffer.default_profile` is `ProfileId?` and `ProfileOffer.unit_limits` is `@data.Limits?`.** A frontend from `register_frontend` has no profile and no unit budget.
6. **`morphir.json` projects default to `pipeline.backend = "checkpoint"` with `pipeline.checkpoint_format = "morphir-json"`.** The planner refuses the `ir-json` backend for project compilers (`frontend.typed_backend_required`). The `morphir-json` checkpoint writes the same Morphir IR JSON (`@ir_json.write`) to `.morphir/out/compile.dest/<package path>.json`. A probe confirmed this, and confirmed that `--backend elm` and `--backend moonbit` still work with this checkpoint format.
7. **`Engine::languages()` leaves out the `ir-json` frontend and the data formats** (`morphir-json`, `ion-text`, `ion-binary`). Registration already refuses them as source languages.

## Review Focus

1. A `morphir.json` beside a `morphir.toml`: the TOML wins and the language is not forced to Elm (Task 4 pins it).
2. `exposedModules` with a dotted module (`Sub.Util`), a non-string item, or a missing key: the dotted module is accepted; the other two are config errors that name the file (Task 4).
3. A `morphir-workspace.json` whose members each have a `morphir.json`: every member is an Elm project (Task 4).
4. An explicit `--backend ir-json` on an Elm project: the CLI exits 2 with `frontend.typed_backend_required`, not a crash (Task 5).
5. `--frontend scheme` on a `morphir.json` project: the overlay wins, so a user can still force Scheme (Task 4).

---

title: Bind authenticated Workbench job transport
description: Follow the bounded host owner morphir-etg2.12 with a vertical authenticated transport and shared UI integration. Publish the resultant live profile upstream in finos/morphir, map exact snapshot/submission/query/cancel semantics to the existing receipt draft, reject duplicate and over-budget frames, preserve same-session reconciliation, schedule actual engine workers with provider grants and cleanup, and gate browser/Proton controls on authenticated negotiated offers. Existing connected v1 clients must retain compile/generate behavior. Real host acceptance must precede advertised live capability; retained Result.Err, SDK errors, primary failures and separate cleanup stay distinct. Native provider IPC, generated browser execution and restart recovery are separate follow-ups.
design:
Workbench · live execution · morphir-etg2.13

Authenticated host jobs

Connect the shared browser and Proton UI to the real host owner. Capture a model once, observe its receipts and cancel without losing the distinction between acknowledged intent and a final result.

Merged and qualified · transport phase complete

15 October 2026 · Revision 61 · Local plan beneath .dev/. Checkboxes report evidence and are read-only.

The vertical slice

The starting baseline is merged MoonBit 8d2b284 from PR #85 and upstream 1deaeb50 from PR #1046. The new exact host profile is morphir/workbench/host 0.1.0-draft.1. It wraps the existing jobs draft.1 and terminal draft.5 contracts, with one invocation ID, workbench. Existing connected v1 session manifests and JSON-RPC methods stay unchanged.

Latest observed main includes PR #86 at 6f9f7e8, which completes installed signed-provider qualification through CI limits, authenticated installed-provider acceptance and operations documentation. It changes no UI job code. The main update is incorporated cleanly at combined head 6274235, and required lint, MoonBit format and validation checks pass again. This strengthens installed-provider qualification; it does not grant metadata trust to the explicitly selected Scheme gateway.

Browser and Proton

Both clients use the same browser UI and compiled MoonBit receipt cursor. Connected evaluation appears only after an exact authenticated offer. The shared controls show submitted/running/terminal state, cancellation acknowledgement and disconnected evidence. The existing bottom panel presents output and diagnostics.

Local gateway and execution

An explicitly enabled same-origin loopback gateway authenticates every host endpoint through real Rust GET /api/session. It captures immutable inputs in the merged MoonBit owner and runs bounded Scheme evaluation in isolated worker threads.

Proton acceptance here proves the packaged shared UI against the loopback HTTP gateway. Native-provider IPC, generated standalone browser execution, durable recovery and automatic metadata trust remain separate work.

Source-backed host workflow

Inline SVG viewer pinned to committed host implementation 7974caf7a9f91c20e5e5cd5cd099b4aca29c434a. Repository evidence is verified against that commit. Browser integration is committed separately at 5a12b26; subsequent local documentation changes are not claimed as source evidence for the pinned diagram.

Mermaid source, including client reconnect
flowchart TD
  Launch[Real Rust launch exchange and HttpOnly cookie] --> Offer[Exact host descriptor and jobs offer]
  Offer --> Submit[One model source plus JSON or Ion argument list]
  Submit --> Auth[Loopback Host, exact Origin, fresh v1 authentication]
  Auth --> Capture[Admit and capture immutable snapshot]
  Capture --> Initial[Bound identity and sequence zero receipt]
  Initial --> Claim[Single execution claim]
  Claim --> Worker[Isolated bounded Scheme worker]
  Worker --> Exit[Worker exit and final cleanup]
  Exit --> Admit[Admit outcomes against captured declarations]
  Admit --> Terminal[Immutable terminal with separate cleanup]
  Terminal --> Release[Explicit terminal release]
  Initial --> Cancel[Cancellation request acknowledges intent]
  Cancel --> Stop[Terminate owned worker before cancelled publication]
  Stop --> Exit
  Initial --> Observe[Freshly authenticated query]
  Observe --> Terminal
  Observe --> Offline[Disconnect keeps last receipt]
  Offline --> Reconnect[Reauthenticate and compare exact same offer]
  Reconnect --> Observe
  Submit --> Unknown[Lost submission reply blocks another automatic submit]

HTTP contract and authority

RoutePurpose and binding
GET /api/workbench/sessionExact host descriptor containing a jobs offer bound to the freshly authenticated v1 session. Query is required; cancellation is optional.
POST /api/workbench/submitExact draft, model IR JSON text, public entry and tagged JSON or published Ion argument list. Reply binds expected identity, the fixed call inventory and initial submitted receipt.
POST /api/workbench/query
POST /api/workbench/cancel		Exact draft and full immutable identity. Return raw admitted receipts. Query does not advance revisions; cancellation records intent before worker termination.
POST /api/workbench/releaseExplicit terminal-only release. Capacity rejection retains existing jobs. A lost release reply can reconcile only after fresh authentication, the same admitted offer and an authenticated unknown-job response.

Each raw request and response is capped at 1 MiB UTF-8. Duplicate JSON members at every depth, invalid UTF-8, unknown members/versions and unsupported formats reject. JSON and Ion decoding retain the published value and aggregate budgets; the host preflights Ion structure before recursive parsing. Model source never becomes a filesystem path.

The gateway requires loopback Host and exact explicit mutation Origin, blocks cross-site Fetch Metadata and grants no CORS permission. It authenticates every job request through the real v1 upstream rather than cached UI state. A fresh host ID, authenticated session and explicit moonbit-scheme provider remain separate identities. A changed offer or session cannot adopt retained jobs.

Approval and active review

The maintainer approved the pair for squash merge after green CI and addressed comments, then explicitly reconfirmed the approved admin bypass for MoonBit. Both PRs have now landed after satisfying those conditions.

Both verified PR #87 UI findings are fixed and pushed at 85f57dafcc7db86ff327f39767750df66a4b33cc. Reproductions established the failures before the fix; replies record the fix and test evidence, and both addressed review threads are resolved. Actual Chromium and packaged Proton acceptance each pass ten submissions, covering retained edited function A drafts, stale/full results after A → B → A navigation, and a lost successful release response blocking compile/model replacement until authenticated resume of the same identity. All 64 Node tests and required validation pass. The full repository check now passes on this final source, including all four target unit/build checks, CLI/npm/compiler, 60 execution-fault cases and rich execution. Required lint/format/validation and all 64 Node tests pass.

What the controls mean

Host cancellation acknowledgement is not a cancelled outcome. A returned value can win the race. Worker exit and cleanup precede terminal publication; a crash after a result preserves that result with separate cleanup evidence. Output admission uses retained declarations, so worker mutations cannot alter expected output types.

A disconnect or timeout retains the last receipt. Resume fetches a fresh authenticated offer, checks the exact prior host/session/provider/version/operation set and queries the same identity. It never submits again. Unknown submission acceptance blocks another automatic submission. A delayed cancellation response for an old job must not disconnect a newer job.

The caller releases a terminal job explicitly. It retains final UI evidence while release is uncertain. The client treats only a freshly authenticated unknown-job reply under the same offer as reconciliation of a lost release response; a generic disabled endpoint or other 404 does not establish that release succeeded.

Current evidence

description: Implement the first authoritative host slice on merged MoonBit main 5640c8e: session-owned immutable execution snapshots, unique bound job/snapshot identities, bounded retention, query and cancellation acknowledgement, single execution claim, manifest-admitted terminal publication and terminal release. design:
Host-owned Workbench jobs

15 October 2026. morphir-etg2.12. MoonBit baseline 5640c8e includes merged job MCK #79, metadata admission evidence #81, Elm project support #82, provider revision pins #83 and installed signed-provider qualification #84. Parent Workbench contracts are merged through #1046 at 1deaeb50.

Host ownership before live controls

The client reducer and independent MCK qualify received evidence. This slice supplies the owner that captures actual execution input and produces receipts. The engine package finos/morphir-engine/execution/jobs adds a synchronous in-memory Session. A composing host owns one session per authenticated host/session/provider authority and serializes access. It must supply a fresh session identity when replacing an owner.

No new wire profile is needed for this internal API. Receipt draft.1 and terminal draft.5 remain unchanged. Authentication, provider grants, asynchronous scheduling and the browser/Proton transport are the following integration slice. The existing connected v1 manifest still offers no evaluation or live job controls.

Snapshot and execution flow

Mermaid source
flowchart LR
  Input[Rich IR unit and invocation suite] --> Capture[Capture immutable checkpoint and suite]
  Capture --> Admission[Admit public invocation and reserve terminal space]
  Admission --> Submitted[Host-owned submitted receipt]
  Submitted --> Claim[Claim execution once]
  Claim --> Worker[Existing evaluator or composing host worker]
  Worker --> Output[Admit outputs against captured declarations]
  Output --> Terminal[Immutable terminal and separate cleanup]
  Terminal --> Release[Explicit release of terminal storage]
  Submitted --> Cancel[Host cancellation acknowledgement]
  Cancel --> Query[Worker queries cancellation points]
  Terminal --> Client[Fresh query receipt for qualified client cursor]

The diagram's evaluator is actual acceptance evidence. It is not a deployed scheduler or authenticated adapter. A cancellation acknowledgement records intent only. A returned value can win the cancellation race; a disconnect or timeout creates no terminal.

State and bounds

Submission captures the full rich IR unit through the existing 4 MiB Ion checkpoint boundary and the suite through the 1 MiB invocation codec. It admits public entries and arguments before accepting ownership. Host-created job/snapshot IDs increase only after successful admission and never wrap. Every operation matches all five identity dimensions.

Defaults retain eight jobs and 16 MiB of serialized evidence; configured bounds are 1 to 64 jobs and 1 to 64 MiB. Every job reserves checkpoint bytes, suite bytes and a full 1 MiB receipt allowance. Later submissions cannot consume space needed for its terminal receipt. Only explicit terminal release frees capacity. Pending jobs are never silently evicted. Quotas bound retained serialization, not allocator overhead or temporary planning allocations.

Claiming yields an independently decoded plan exactly once. Completing a job reconstructs declarations from the retained snapshot, so edits to the worker's plan cannot change output types. Invalid updates leave the authoritative receipt unchanged. Identical terminal publication replays; conflicting publication rejects. Actual Result.Err remains returned data and SDK errors retain their model-error variant. Cleanup must finish before the composing host calls completion.

Twelve semantic tests pass per JS/native/Wasm/Wasm GC, including actual Scheme evaluation, exact arithmetic, Result.Err and SDK errors; mutation isolation, authority binding, cancellation races, output admission, retention reservation and explicit terminal release. Full repository lint/tests/compiler integration/build checks pass on the host-owner implementation. The final test-only interleaving addition passes all twelve focused tests per JS/native/Wasm/Wasm GC. Separate configuration/package validation also passes. The SVG passes automated Archify provenance and real-browser checks; HTML checklists pass at desktop/mobile widths and in print. This evidence establishes the host owner, without independently qualifying live host authentication or execution scheduling.

design:
Workbench job transition qualification

15 October 2026. morphir-etg2.11. Baselines: MoonBit d3feef8, parent aa1d9c22. The shared job profile and portable reducer are merged through PRs #1045/#74. This slice supplies independent qualification through the existing Rust MCK and explicit MoonBit adapters.

Separate expectations from implementation

The parent repository owns fixed input traces, expected observations, schemas, report admission and all verdicts. It never sends case IDs or expected values to the implementation under test. The MoonBit adapter calls the shipped job reducer and emits observations. No second reducer or compatibility runner is introduced.

Mermaid qualification flow
flowchart LR
  Kit[Parent-owned fixed cases and expectations] --> Runner[Existing Rust MCK]
  Runner -->|Input only| Adapter[MoonBit JSON-lines adapter]
  Adapter --> Reducer[Portable job receipt reducer]
  Reducer -->|Reduced state| Adapter
  Adapter -->|Actual projections| Runner
  Runner -->|Compare independent expectations| Report[Bounded evidence report]
  Report --> Recheck[Reload corpus and recompute verdicts]

The lifecycle contract stays unchanged. Its SVG diagram shows host receipt state, acknowledgement and terminal evidence; connection availability remains separate client state.

Exact draft mapping and trace shape

Offline Workbench MCK 0.1.0-draft.6 advertises only reduce-job and JSON. It maps the unchanged morphir/workbench/jobs 0.1.0-draft.1 receipt profile with nested terminal draft.5. The five historical MCK drafts keep their schemas and corpora unchanged and are requalified separately. No Ion receipt mapping or connected capability is added.

Input is exactly {offer,identity,calls,initial,actions}. Initial submission binds the authenticated-offer placeholder, expected authority and snapshot, and ordered calls. Up to 64 closed actions select observe, reconnect, disconnect or cancel-action. Syntax is admitted for the whole trace before execution. Each supplied receipt or reconnect offer is then admitted per action. A rejected action records its bounded code and retained cursor view, allowing later steps to prove that bad evidence did not change state.

Success retains the complete final receipt once, plus ordered bounded views of sequence, state, cancellation acknowledgement, connection and available cancellation action. Input and output each retain a 1 MiB budget. Parent output admission checks closed shapes, bounds, nested outcomes and final identity/view consistency. Fixed goldens establish transitions; the runner does not decode inputs to invent expectations.
