Back to the stage specification

Task 4 contract · revision 0.5 · 14 October 2026 · shared adapter and MoonBit qualification landed

Export an authenticated provider snapshot

The MoonBit host needs retained native Library bytes, metadata and contexts, plus a checked core projection. A successful restore or validation summary identifies an operation; it is not the snapshot contract.

The selected in-process contract is implemented and qualified. The retained-byte export is merged in Rust PR #295. Rust PR #296, merged as b0a9926, adds the checked projection and a signed test naming release; MoonBit PR #76 qualifies consumption and merged as dc15a77 after all head and integration checks passed. Task 4 selects the in-process adapter option. Binary Ion process framing is composed with host sessions in Task 5. Existing MVP assurance applies; installed authentication is not claimed.

What the current implementation gives us

Shared parent 23e7dfa pins Rust 15789aef26206b1180c4bcf804bdb1812d1ec91b. Its trusted-validation command restores a locked graph, reads the provider and emits counts/status. The package restore report carries a profile/version and release-directory pairs. It does not carry authenticated payload bytes, context inventory or the core/native projection pair.

Inside the Rust verifier, inventoried file bytes are checked against manifest content digests and retained in LibraryInput for semantic graph verification. That is the useful capture point. Export must become eligible only after complete graph verification and the trust backend's successful finalization. Capturing a buffer early does not itself authenticate it.

  • Restore report and release-directory pairs.
  • Verified bytes, staging and LibraryInput construction.
  • Fresh authentication, exact graph verification and backend finalization.

An adapter around existing disk restore could also be considered, but it must qualify the handoff, authenticated inventory binding and retained reads under its declared assurance profile. Reading arbitrary paths named by a report is insufficient. The preferred first contract exports the shared verifier's retained buffers directly.

Keep authority with the existing verifier

LayerOwnsReturns
Shared package libraryFresh repository/publisher authentication, exact locked graph, original inventory and selected trust-state semantics.An internal verified snapshot that becomes usable only after operation success.
Shared host serviceRequest correlation, bounded transport, checked native-to-core projection and exact artifact/profile identity.Versioned snapshot response through a trusted invocation.
MoonBit host adapterApproved process/root grants, project scope, response validation, cancellation and resource lifecycle.Scoped restore_library and load_context callbacks.
MoonBit consumerProvider declaration, subject, naming data and interpreter validation.Admitted naming facts and semantic receipts.

No new signature algorithm or package trust policy is implemented in the MoonBit consumer. A typed snapshot response is data; its provenance comes from the trusted service invocation, not from a field declaring authenticated=true.

The first implementation boundary

Rust PR #295, merged as adcbbdf, adds restore_snapshot(RestoreRequest) → RestoredSnapshot. The snapshot owns the exact original manifest, native payload and declared context resources for the entire verified graph. It returns only after publication and successful backend finalization. Existing restore reports retain their wire shape.

Private constructors, read-only accessors and no deserialization path keep the in-process result separate from untrusted stored data. File identities hash the original bytes. Debug output shows identities and lengths without raw payloads or contexts. The result retains the current local-library-mvp profile and 0.1.0-draft.1 revision.

Open the explorable SVG diagram. Its source links pin the committed implementation used by the merged foundation.

Verified locallyEvidence
Original-byte retentionPayload and context remain usable after source and restored files are deleted.
Authentic native metadataA signed 4.1 test provider with external context passes declaration admission using retained memory only.
Refusal and finalizationTampered dependency/context, failed state update and changed operation marker yield no returned snapshot; failed finalization removes promoted output in the tested case.
Freshness and compatibilityA previous snapshot cannot make a later authentication failure succeed; existing restore report bytes and MCK tests remain compatible.

The initial acme/metadata declaration/context fixture remains separate. The subsequent signed naming corpus in Rust PR #296 contains native morphir/naming; no production publisher or trust keys are selected.

Separate publisher release from native IR identity

The shared registry's PackagePath requires an authority-qualified name. A native IR name such as morphir/naming is a different identity. MoonBit PR #76 corrects the configuration parser to accept example.com/morphir/naming@1.0.0 as a published release selector. The host must independently require the restored native IR package to be morphir/naming and match any authored native payload revision pin.

example.com is an example authority. Production publisher identity and trust policy remain explicit selections; this design grants no default authority.

The selected in-process adapter contract

Rust PR #296 adds provider_snapshot::project_library(&SnapshotLibrary) → LibraryProjection. Its explicit codec is v4.1-document-metadata-to-v4.0/1. The adapter derives the core and original document-metadata body from the retained authenticated native bytes and contexts. It reparses the derived core and checks the typed distribution before returning it.

ViewContract
Native identityOriginal 4.1 payload SHA-256. The payload is retained unchanged; a derived view never replaces this revision.
Core viewExplicit v4.0 JSON boundary encoding for the current MoonBit semantic model. JSON remains supported. Host pipeline processing and the proposed process frame remain Ion first.
Document metadataOriginal authored $meta JSON body, with exact context bytes retained separately. Declarations come from the provider's native graph, not an invented closure file.
Unsupported conversionNode-local linked metadata and nonlexical parameter maps are refused. The map guard covers local/nested definitions and dependency signatures; it never sorts arguments silently.

The signed test release is example.com/morphir/naming@1.0.0. Its native IR package is morphir/naming, with the public naming/target-names value and closed frontend/backend record of Dict String String. Native revision 870af5f51087dfe6a13fdf10c3b856d879b53d650982612a7aede276060c0720 is independently checked by the Rust signed-fixture tests and MoonBit interoperability tests. The MoonBit test host is simulated; installed admission remains Task 6.

Task 4 is complete at this reviewed, qualified shared-API and signed-corpus boundary. Task 5 composes the binary Ion framing below, process identity, project grants, deadlines, cancellation and cleanup with the CLI host. This keeps process effects outside the pure projection component.

Proposed request

morphir_provider_snapshot_request_v1::{
  invocation: "host-generated unique request identity",
  projectScope: "opaque host-selected project identity",
  predicate: "expanded target-names URI, including any revision pin",
  release: {packagePath: "example.com/morphir/naming", version: "1.0.0"},
  assurance: "portable",
  inputs: {
    policyBytes: {{ /* bounded original policy bytes */ }},
    lockBytes: {{ /* bounded original full-lock bytes */ }}
  },
  grants: {
    registry: "host-approved local registry root",
    state: "host-approved existing initialized state root"
  }
}

This is a format sketch, not a finalized executable fixture. The host supplies bounded policy/lock snapshots, an exact release and accepted root grants. Package metadata cannot supply a service executable, grant additional roots or initialize trust state. A profile request is explicit; unsupported hardened assurance fails.

Use one bounded binary Ion frame per request/response as the preferred process transport. A long-lived process/session protocol needs its own sequencing and cancellation contract. A deliberately selected JSON framing must preserve byte arrays, exact integers and native Ion metadata without flattening. The shared package lock and signed JSON artifacts retain their existing formats.

Proposed response

morphir_provider_snapshot_response_v1::{
  invocation: "exact request identity",
  projectScope: "exact requested scope identity",
  release: {packagePath: "exact requested authority-qualified path", version: "exact version"},
  provider: {
    irPackageName: "morphir/naming",
    nativeFormat: "4.1.0",

    nativeBytes: {{ /* exact authenticated payload */ }},

  evidence: {

    assurance: "portable",
    policyIdentity: "identity of accepted policy snapshot",
    lockIdentity: "identity of replayed full lock",
    trustStateIdentity: "scoped verifier-owned state identity"
  }
}

The native IR payload digest is distinct from bundle/record/manifest identities. Match any predicate revision pin. Derive the semantic projection and native metadata from the retained native payload; inventory referenced contexts from that authenticated bundle. Reject an unsupported projection rather than changing the release header and treating the result as a native codec.

The first checked core codec is fixed by the in-process profile above; its process-envelope representation remains proposed. The current MoonBit semantic model uses its supported v4 core view; that fact does not qualify native 4.1 restoration. Production code must test projection from independent native fixtures and preserve unknown native metadata as authored.

Success and failure contract

  1. The host binds an effect-free project scope during planning.
  2. A required naming fact starts a fresh bounded service invocation.
  3. The shared verifier authenticates and verifies the complete exact graph.
  4. Only after successful verifier finalization does the service export the selected snapshot and its contexts.
  5. The host validates correlation, profile, release, byte digests and limits, then retains the snapshot through interpretation.
  6. The engine validates the declaration and assertion. The generator allocates names and stages output.
  7. The host disposes transfer/session resources before generated publication.

Failed verification, uncertain backend completion, malformed response, deadline/cancellation or failed cleanup yields no admissible snapshot. Successful trust-state refresh remains a shared-provider side effect even when later generation fails. Never roll back that state to conceal the side effect.

Stored snapshots and receipts remain useful for auditing or opaque checkpoint preservation. Each new interpretation must obtain fresh host admission; a previous response cannot be loaded as reusable authority. No ambient file, registry or network fallback is allowed.

What unlocks the integration task

Real signed providerA local authenticated test release with valid declaration/schema and independently expected generated names. Test trust keys never become user defaults.
Native service qualificationExact artifact/platform identity, bounded requests, cancellation/deadline, cleanup and selected-profile freshness/rollback evidence.

Binary Ion process framing and host-session execution are Task 5 composition; installed authentication remains Task 6. title: Task 5: Implement scoped host sessions and CLI composition
description:
### Task 5: Implement scoped host sessions and CLI composition

Connect a qualified provider through explicit host grants, effective configuration-origin path resolution and runtime capability probes. Bound process/response size/deadlines and cancellation; retain immutable bytes; dispose before publication. Record telemetry under existing log rules, defaulting beneath .morphir/logs and honoring explicit paths. Keep trust-state effects owned by the shared provider. Unsupported runtimes/profile requests fail clearly without downgrade. No automatic service acquisition or trust initialization.
design:
Stage specification · Task 4 adapter contract

Task 5 specification · revision 0.7 · 15 October 2026 · process composition implemented · local qualification complete · landed

Scoped provider sessions and CLI composition

Connect the engine's project-specific metadata capability to the shared authenticated restore adapter. The host owns process effects and grants. The interpreter consumes immutable views. Output publication waits for successful session disposal.

Lifecycle and byte-contract work landed in MoonBit PR 78, commit 40a58ba, after green head and merge-queue checks. The shared Ion service landed in Rust PR 297, commit 3f10962. The complete process/grants slice is in PR 80, on current main, head 419f945, with review and CI in progress.

Local native and JS clients each restored the signed provider for two independent projects and generated authenticated_ready. Missing grants, a wrong executable pin and invalid current authentication preserve previous output. Dry runs leave trust state unchanged. Default binary Ion logs and explicit paths outside the default directory both pass. Installed cross-platform authenticated qualification remains Task 6.

Keep each component responsible for one boundary

ComponentResponsibility
EngineFreeze project identity, effective selection and configuration origins. Bind capabilities without acquiring resources.
Host sessionResolve selections through explicit grants, probe the runtime, acquire lazily, bound transport, retain snapshots and dispose.
Shared Rust adapterOwn fresh repository authentication, lock/policy verification, trust-state effects and checked projection from retained bytes.
Metadata interpreterAdmit the native provider identity, declarations and contexts; interpret target naming without process or filesystem access.
PublisherBegin only after generation and session cleanup succeed, then follow the existing output transaction contract.

Acquire at execution, dispose before publication

Open the explorable SVG. This diagram is proposed behavior.

The binder records a project scope during planning. The first restore request acquires a session; unused projects require no process or scratch directory. A session may reuse its retained immutable graph during one operation. A later operation must authenticate again.

After engine execution, the host disposes every acquired session on success, failure and cancellation. Only successful execution and successful disposal can reach library validation and publisher.begin. Cleanup failure records a diagnostic and prevents publication. Preserve the original execution error alongside any cleanup error.

Selections are not grants

SelectionHost decision
Service executableResolve from its configuration origin. Admit an explicit executable identity through the host, freeze its identity for the operation and reject changes. Provider metadata cannot choose or replace the executable.
Policy and lockRead bounded immutable snapshots from accepted read grants. Retain their exact digest identities. No default trust initialization.
Registry and stateResolve against their own origins, then validate the host's accepted roots and required access. The shared provider owns trust-state updates.
Published releaseRequire an exact authority-qualified release, such as example.com/morphir/naming@1.0.0. Independently require native IR package morphir/naming and any authored payload revision pin.
AssuranceMap an explicit supported portable request to the qualified shared MVP profile. Refuse unsupported hardened requests without downgrade.

A project cannot inherit another project's capability closure or use its configured paths as new grants. Resolve file-origin paths relative to that file, with an explicit rule for CLI-origin selections. Keep diagnostic provenance so the user can fix the setting that caused refusal.

Grant the host explicitly

The CLI takes --metadata-grants FILE. The file is a host authority selected by the caller, separate from project configuration. No file is discovered automatically. Ion text and binary are the default formats; an explicitly named JSON file is supported. Relative grant paths resolve from this file's directory. Each grant names one exact workspace/project pair, with no wildcard.

{
  profile: "morphir-metadata-host-grants-v1",
  workspace: "/work/example",
  runtime: {
    node: "/tools/node", nodeSha256: "sha256:<raw digest>",
    helper: "/tools/morphir/build-provider/metadata.mjs",
    helperBundleSha256: "sha256:<bundle digest>"
  },
  projects: [{
    project: "one",
    service: "/tools/morphir-provider-snapshot", serviceSha256: "sha256:<raw digest>",
    policy: "/trust/policy.json", lock: "/work/example/one/morphir.lock",
    registry: "/registry/local", state: "/trust/state"
  }]
}
CheckRule
Selection originsFile-origin selections resolve from that file's directory. CLI-origin paths resolve from the invocation directory. Relative environment/unknown-origin paths refuse rather than guess.
Exact grantsEach selected service/read/registry/state path must equal its separately granted resolved path. A different project cannot borrow the grant.
Runtime pinsCheck Node and service raw SHA-256 independently in host code before and after the exchange. Hash regular files in bounded 64 KiB chunks, with a 512 MiB identity-read cap. This cap is separate from model payload limits.
Helper bundlePin the JSON array of filename/raw-hash pairs for WindowsJob.cs, metadata.mjs, supervision.mjs, windows-job.mjs, windows-job.ps1, in that order. These are host runtime components, not a service's self-attestation.
Runtime qualificationInitially qualify JS and native hosts. Wasm and WasmGC refuse this process path until their executable pin reads and supervisor composition are qualified. Pure wire support remains available on all four targets.

A host-owned scratch directory carries binary request/response files through the existing string-only process ABI. Small JSON control receipts are an explicit opt-out; they contain identities and lifecycle status only. Binary Ion never crosses a UTF-8 conversion. Unknown helper termination retains scratch and blocks publication until quiescence can be confirmed.

Binary Ion is the process envelope

Use one bounded binary Ion request and response for a one-shot child. Define and version the envelope before exposing a command. Include request identity, frozen project scope, exact release, accepted profile, policy/lock bytes and approved registry/state roots. Responses identify the same request, service and profile and carry the retained native graph, raw metadata/context inventory and explicit checked-core codec.

The existing platform.process returns strings. Add a bounded byte channel through the qualified supervisor; never decode binary Ion as UTF-8. Reject trailing frames, duplicate required fields, wrong types, missing inventories, oversized values and mismatched identities before installing capabilities.

Native JSON artifacts remain supported and retain their exact byte identities. The current semantic view uses the explicit v4.1-document-metadata-to-v4.0/1 JSON codec from Task 4. Carry these bytes as Ion blobs. Do not flatten native metadata into JSON or call the derived view the authenticated native artifact.

The implementation now freezes the one-shot service identity as morphir-package/provider-snapshot/0.1.0-draft.1, with executable morphir-provider-snapshot. Requests and responses are one annotated Ion 1.0 binary application value each. Limits are 4 MiB per request, 16 MiB per response, 128 Libraries, 256 contexts per Library and 1024 contexts across the graph. The host defaults to one 120-second project operation budget, capped at 600 seconds, including probe and cleanup. The CLI permits 6001 through 600000 milliseconds, reserving time for supervised teardown. A capability request is effect-free; every snapshot request freshly replays the exact full lock. The shared executable is merged source, with local host qualification. No released executable or installed cross-platform qualification is claimed. The current shared MVP assurance and its filesystem assumptions remain explicit.

Read the wire contract

Top-level annotationClosed fields
morphir_provider_capabilities_request_v1invocation, projectScope. No restore inputs or effects.
morphir_provider_snapshot_request_v1Correlation, exact release, assurance, granted registry/state/output absolute paths, immutable policy/lock blobs.
morphir_provider_capabilities_response_v1Correlation, service, profile, profileVersion, codec and exact integer request/response/graph/context limits.
morphir_provider_snapshot_response_v1Correlation, service/profile/codec identities, root release, raw policy/lock hashes, core blob, original metadata blob or null.blob, and complete libraries inventory.

Each Library retains its release, original manifest blob, native path, original native blob and raw native revision. Context entries retain canonical bundle path, raw hash and exact blob. No restored files are reopened to construct the shared response. Unknown or duplicate fields, nested wire annotations and trailing application values refuse. The host bounds binary structure before decoding, then checks frozen identities before installing views.

A context digest that identifies different inventory bases refuses rather than choosing relative-import semantics by array order. An inventory-relative reference from its admitted base selects the intended context. Returned context buffers and semantic views have independent ownership.

Probe behavior before enabling a provider

A generic process-supported flag is insufficient. Qualify byte transport, response bounds, cancellation, deadlines, descendant quiescence and the requested restore profile. Keep the process path unavailable on runtimes that cannot meet this contract. Do not fall back to unauthenticated metadata, an old snapshot or a weaker profile.

One operation budget covers probing, acquisition, restoration, transport and cleanup. Cancellation stops further work and tears down the child tree. Disposal verifies quiescence before removing host-owned scratch state. Failure to clean up refuses output publication; it does not erase a committed shared trust-state update.

Wire the host into the CLI

  1. Construct the effect-free project binder before engine.plan, using effective configuration and host grants.
  2. Keep dry runs free of restoration, process acquisition and trust-state changes.
  3. At execution, route restore_library through the scoped session and expose contexts only from its admitted inventory.
  4. Add the unconditional disposal gate between engine.execute_content and library validation/publication.
  5. Report actionable configuration, runtime, identity, transport and cleanup diagnostics through the existing host reporting path.

Embedding callers can continue to supply explicit capabilities. Static and project-bound authorities remain mutually exclusive. The CLI must not silently add an ambient provider.

Record lifecycle events without payloads

Emit bounded events for probe, acquire, restore, admission refusal, cancellation and disposal. Correlate operation and project identities, selected profile, result and durations. Exclude raw policies, locks, provider bodies, contexts and trust secrets from ordinary logs. Keep stdout reserved for framed service data or CLI results.

Logging stays off unless enabled. The low-configuration destination is beneath .morphir/logs/. Honor an explicitly selected log path under the existing host rules, including paths outside that default directory.

Implement and qualify in small slices

SliceRequired evidence
Host lifecycleEffect-free planning; lazy project-scoped acquisition; disposal after success, failure and cancellation; cleanup refusal prevents publisher.begin and preserves previous output.
Shared process adapterVersioned Ion fixture roundtrip with exact native/core/context bytes, fresh signed restoration, unsupported conversion refusal and no report-only trust shortcut.
Supervised binary transportOversize/truncated/trailing response refusal, bounded deadlines, cancellation, child-tree quiescence and executable identity mismatch.
CLI compositionImplemented and locally qualified on native/JS: origin-relative paths, explicit grants, separate project operations, dry-run behavior, default binary logs and explicit paths. Pure host suites pass 1246 native, 1181 JS, 1165 Wasm and 1165 WasmGC tests. CLI/npm and process supervision checks pass.
Task 6 handoffPin the merged executable/protocol identities and run installed cross-platform signed-provider acceptance. Pure and simulated tests do not claim installed authentication.

Code evidence for the starting point

The first lifecycle implementation is metadata_sessions.mbt, with eight lifecycle tests. This is a host embedding contract, not an installed process provider.

The current engine binder is in metadata_provider.mbt. The publication gate belongs in Host::run_content. The CLI plans and runs in main.mbt. Task 4's adapter specification records the shared API and signed fixture. These source pins distinguish the implemented lifecycle slice from the remaining Task 5 process composition.

Current process implementation

Commit a97e4b1 composes metadata/grants, the host process session and the binary supervisor bridge. The CLI keeps its original session owner from planning through execution. A disabled provider binds unavailable capabilities, preserving the existing diagnostic and acquiring no session; a configured shared restore without grants refuses explicitly. Follow-up head 419f945 probes JS pin-read support and preserves disabled-provider compatibility. PR #80 squash merged as 161abf4 after all 23 head checks and 22 merge-queue jobs passed. Task 5 is complete; installed qualification and full audit evidence continue in Task 6. Runtime operations remain unavailable on pure targets; their stub binds without filesystem or process imports. The local acceptance receipt is a development artifact, not authorization to reuse saved provider bytes.
notes:
Implementation reconnaissance for next slice: engine.ProjectMetadataScope/register_project_metadata_provider already freezes per-project selection and requires an effect-free binder. Host::run_content executes the engine before validate_libraries and publisher.begin, but currently has no provider-session disposal gate. Add host-owned lazy session acquisition with immutable retained payload/context inventory, and an unconditional disposal boundary after execution and before validation/publication. Cleanup failure must prevent publisher.begin; cancellation and engine failure must also dispose. CLI currently creates engine/plan before build-provider Host construction, so binder wiring belongs before engine.plan while resource acquisition remains execution-only. Existing platform process/supervision is reusable only after binary framing, child-tree quiescence, capability probes and configured service identity are qualified. Task4 selected in-process export; no existing process snapshot command is assumed.
Binary transport constraint confirmed in platform/js.mbt and native process adapter: current platform.process returns stdout/stderr Strings. Do not route binary Ion through this UTF-8 API. Add a bounded binary channel through the qualified supervisor, with an explicit envelope profile and unchanged byte blobs. Generic process_supported alone is insufficient to claim bounded binary framing, cancellation, descendant quiescence or the selected restore assurance. Preserve pure core admission and engine binder API while the host owns these process effects.

Stage specification · Task 4 adapter contract

Task 5 specification · revision 0.1 · 14 October 2026 · lifecycle slice implemented · process composition pending

Scoped provider sessions and CLI composition

Connect the engine's project-specific metadata capability to the shared authenticated restore adapter. The host owns process effects and grants. The interpreter consumes immutable views. Output publication waits for successful session disposal.

The first lifecycle slice is implemented in 351ed82: lazy project sessions, cleanup before publication, cancellation, diagnostic preservation and explicit retry after cleanup failure. Eight new lifecycle tests and the full four-target suites pass, along with CLI/npm smoke tests and required checks. The Rust in-process export and projection are its foundation. A process snapshot command does not exist yet, and a validation summary cannot substitute for one. Installed authenticated qualification remains Task 6.

Keep each component responsible for one boundary

ComponentResponsibility
EngineFreeze project identity, effective selection and configuration origins. Bind capabilities without acquiring resources.
Host sessionResolve selections through explicit grants, probe the runtime, acquire lazily, bound transport, retain snapshots and dispose.
Shared Rust adapterOwn fresh repository authentication, lock/policy verification, trust-state effects and checked projection from retained bytes.
Metadata interpreterAdmit the native provider identity, declarations and contexts; interpret target naming without process or filesystem access.
PublisherBegin only after generation and session cleanup succeed, then follow the existing output transaction contract.

Acquire at execution, dispose before publication

Open the explorable SVG. This diagram is proposed behavior.

The binder records a project scope during planning. The first restore request acquires a session; unused projects require no process or scratch directory. A session may reuse its retained immutable graph during one operation. A later operation must authenticate again.

After engine execution, the host disposes every acquired session on success, failure and cancellation. Only successful execution and successful disposal can reach library validation and publisher.begin. Cleanup failure records a diagnostic and prevents publication. Preserve the original execution error alongside any cleanup error.

Selections are not grants

SelectionHost decision
Service executableResolve from its configuration origin. Admit an explicit executable identity through the host, freeze its identity for the operation and reject changes. Provider metadata cannot choose or replace the executable.
Policy and lockRead bounded immutable snapshots from accepted read grants. Retain their exact digest identities. No default trust initialization.
Registry and stateResolve against their own origins, then validate the host's accepted roots and required access. The shared provider owns trust-state updates.
Published releaseRequire an exact authority-qualified release, such as example.com/morphir/naming@1.0.0. Independently require native IR package morphir/naming and any authored payload revision pin.
AssuranceMap an explicit supported portable request to the qualified shared MVP profile. Refuse unsupported hardened requests without downgrade.

A project cannot inherit another project's capability closure or use its configured paths as new grants. Resolve file-origin paths relative to that file, with an explicit rule for CLI-origin selections. Keep diagnostic provenance so the user can fix the setting that caused refusal.

Binary Ion is the process envelope

Use one bounded binary Ion request and response for a one-shot child. Define and version the envelope before exposing a command. Include request identity, frozen project scope, exact release, accepted profile, policy/lock bytes and approved registry/state roots. Responses identify the same request, service and profile and carry the retained native graph, raw metadata/context inventory and explicit checked-core codec.

The existing platform.process returns strings. Add a bounded byte channel through the qualified supervisor; never decode binary Ion as UTF-8. Reject trailing frames, duplicate required fields, wrong types, missing inventories, oversized values and mismatched identities before installing capabilities.

Native JSON artifacts remain supported and retain their exact byte identities. The current semantic view uses the explicit v4.1-document-metadata-to-v4.0/1 JSON codec from Task 4. Carry these bytes as Ion blobs. Do not flatten native metadata into JSON or call the derived view the authenticated native artifact.

The precise process profile name, executable entry point and concrete size/deadline defaults must be fixed and tested with the shared service implementation. They are not claims about an existing command. The current shared MVP assurance and its filesystem assumptions remain explicit.

Probe behavior before enabling a provider

A generic process-supported flag is insufficient. Qualify byte transport, response bounds, cancellation, deadlines, descendant quiescence and the requested restore profile. Keep the process path unavailable on runtimes that cannot meet this contract. Do not fall back to unauthenticated metadata, an old snapshot or a weaker profile.

One operation budget covers probing, acquisition, restoration, transport and cleanup. Cancellation stops further work and tears down the child tree. Disposal verifies quiescence before removing host-owned scratch state. Failure to clean up refuses output publication; it does not erase a committed shared trust-state update.

Wire the host into the CLI

  1. Construct the effect-free project binder before engine.plan, using effective configuration and host grants.
  2. Keep dry runs free of restoration, process acquisition and trust-state changes.
  3. At execution, route restore_library through the scoped session and expose contexts only from its admitted inventory.
  4. Add the unconditional disposal gate between engine.execute_content and library validation/publication.
  5. Report actionable configuration, runtime, identity, transport and cleanup diagnostics through the existing host reporting path.

Embedding callers can continue to supply explicit capabilities. Static and project-bound authorities remain mutually exclusive. The CLI must not silently add an ambient provider.

Record lifecycle events without payloads

Emit bounded events for probe, acquire, restore, admission refusal, cancellation and disposal. Correlate operation and project identities, selected profile, result and durations. Exclude raw policies, locks, provider bodies, contexts and trust secrets from ordinary logs. Keep stdout reserved for framed service data or CLI results.

Logging stays off unless enabled. The low-configuration destination is beneath .morphir/logs/. Honor an explicitly selected log path under the existing host rules, including paths outside that default directory.

Implement and qualify in small slices

SliceRequired evidence
Host lifecycleEffect-free planning; lazy project-scoped acquisition; disposal after success, failure and cancellation; cleanup refusal prevents publisher.begin and preserves previous output.
Shared process adapterVersioned Ion fixture roundtrip with exact native/core/context bytes, fresh signed restoration, unsupported conversion refusal and no report-only trust shortcut.
Supervised binary transportOversize/truncated/trailing response refusal, bounded deadlines, cancellation, child-tree quiescence and executable identity mismatch.
CLI compositionOrigin-relative paths, explicit grants, separate workspace project scopes, dry-run behavior, enabled logging defaults and explicit log paths.
Task 6 handoffPin the merged executable/protocol identities and run installed cross-platform signed-provider acceptance. Pure and simulated tests do not claim installed authentication.

Code evidence for the starting point

The first lifecycle implementation is metadata_sessions.mbt, with eight lifecycle tests. This is a host embedding contract, not an installed process provider.

The current engine binder is in metadata_provider.mbt. The publication gate belongs in Host::run_content. The CLI plans and runs in main.mbt. Task 4's adapter specification records the shared API and signed fixture. These source pins distinguish the implemented lifecycle slice from the remaining Task 5 process composition.

    project: "one",
    service: "/tools/morphir-provider-snapshot", serviceSha256: "sha256:<raw digest>",
    policy: "/trust/policy.json", lock: "/work/example/one/morphir.lock",
    registry: "/registry/local", state: "/trust/state"
  }]
}
CheckRule
Selection originsFile-origin selections resolve from that file's directory. CLI-origin paths resolve from the invocation directory. Relative environment/unknown-origin paths refuse rather than guess.
Exact grantsEach selected service/read/registry/state path must equal its separately granted resolved path. A different project cannot borrow the grant.
Runtime pinsCheck Node and service raw SHA-256 independently in host code before and after the exchange. Hash regular files in bounded 64 KiB chunks, with a 512 MiB identity-read cap. This cap is separate from model payload limits.
Helper bundlePin the JSON array of filename/raw-hash pairs for WindowsJob.cs, metadata.mjs, supervision.mjs, windows-job.mjs, windows-job.ps1, in that order. These are host runtime components, not a service's self-attestation.
Runtime qualificationInitially qualify JS and native hosts. Wasm and WasmGC refuse this process path until their executable pin reads and supervisor composition are qualified. Pure wire support remains available on all four targets.

A host-owned scratch directory carries binary request/response files through the existing string-only process ABI. Small JSON control receipts are an explicit opt-out; they contain identities and lifecycle status only. Binary Ion never crosses a UTF-8 conversion. Unknown helper termination retains scratch and blocks publication until quiescence can be confirmed.

Binary Ion is the process envelope

Use one bounded binary Ion request and response for a one-shot child. Define and version the envelope before exposing a command. Include request identity, frozen project scope, exact release, accepted profile, policy/lock bytes and approved registry/state roots. Responses identify the same request, service and profile and carry the retained native graph, raw metadata/context inventory and explicit checked-core codec.

The existing platform.process returns strings. Add a bounded byte channel through the qualified supervisor; never decode binary Ion as UTF-8. Reject trailing frames, duplicate required fields, wrong types, missing inventories, oversized values and mismatched identities before installing capabilities.

Native JSON artifacts remain supported and retain their exact byte identities. The current semantic view uses the explicit v4.1-document-metadata-to-v4.0/1 JSON codec from Task 4. Carry these bytes as Ion blobs. Do not flatten native metadata into JSON or call the derived view the authenticated native artifact.

The implementation now freezes the one-shot service identity as morphir-package/provider-snapshot/0.1.0-draft.1, with executable morphir-provider-snapshot. Requests and responses are one annotated Ion 1.0 binary application value each. Limits are 4 MiB per request, 16 MiB per response, 128 Libraries, 256 contexts per Library and 1024 contexts across the graph. The host defaults to one 120-second project operation budget, capped at 600 seconds, including probe and cleanup. The CLI permits 6001 through 600000 milliseconds, reserving time for supervised teardown. A capability request is effect-free; every snapshot request freshly replays the exact full lock. The shared executable is merged source, with local host qualification. No released executable or installed cross-platform qualification is claimed. The current shared MVP assurance and its filesystem assumptions remain explicit.

Read the wire contract

Top-level annotationClosed fields
morphir_provider_capabilities_request_v1invocation, projectScope. No restore inputs or effects.
morphir_provider_snapshot_request_v1Correlation, exact release, assurance, granted registry/state/output absolute paths, immutable policy/lock blobs.
morphir_provider_capabilities_response_v1Correlation, service, profile, profileVersion, codec and exact integer request/response/graph/context limits.
morphir_provider_snapshot_response_v1Correlation, service/profile/codec identities, root release, raw policy/lock hashes, core blob, original metadata blob or null.blob, and complete libraries inventory.

Each Library retains its release, original manifest blob, native path, original native blob and raw native revision. Context entries retain canonical bundle path, raw hash and exact blob. No restored files are reopened to construct the shared response. Unknown or duplicate fields, nested wire annotations and trailing application values refuse. The host bounds binary structure before decoding, then checks frozen identities before installing views.

A context digest that identifies different inventory bases refuses rather than choosing relative-import semantics by array order. An inventory-relative reference from its admitted base selects the intended context. Returned context buffers and semantic views have independent ownership.

Probe behavior before enabling a provider

A generic process-supported flag is insufficient. Qualify byte transport, response bounds, cancellation, deadlines, descendant quiescence and the requested restore profile. Keep the process path unavailable on runtimes that cannot meet this contract. Do not fall back to unauthenticated metadata, an old snapshot or a weaker profile.

One operation budget covers probing, acquisition, restoration, transport and cleanup. Cancellation stops further work and tears down the child tree. Disposal verifies quiescence before removing host-owned scratch state. Failure to clean up refuses output publication; it does not erase a committed shared trust-state update.

Wire the host into the CLI

  1. Construct the effect-free project binder before engine.plan, using effective configuration and host grants.
  2. Keep dry runs free of restoration, process acquisition and trust-state changes.
  3. At execution, route restore_library through the scoped session and expose contexts only from its admitted inventory.
  4. Add the unconditional disposal gate between engine.execute_content and library validation/publication.
  5. Report actionable configuration, runtime, identity, transport and cleanup diagnostics through the existing host reporting path.

Embedding callers can continue to supply explicit capabilities. Static and project-bound authorities remain mutually exclusive. The CLI must not silently add an ambient provider.

Record lifecycle events without payloads

Emit bounded events for probe, acquire, restore, admission refusal, cancellation and disposal. Correlate operation and project identities, selected profile, result and durations. Exclude raw policies, locks, provider bodies, contexts and trust secrets from ordinary logs. Keep stdout reserved for framed service data or CLI results.

Logging stays off unless enabled. The low-configuration destination is beneath .morphir/logs/. Honor an explicitly selected log path under the existing host rules, including paths outside that default directory.

Implement and qualify in small slices

SliceRequired evidence
Host lifecycleEffect-free planning; lazy project-scoped acquisition; disposal after success, failure and cancellation; cleanup refusal prevents publisher.begin and preserves previous output.
Shared process adapterVersioned Ion fixture roundtrip with exact native/core/context bytes, fresh signed restoration, unsupported conversion refusal and no report-only trust shortcut.
Supervised binary transportOversize/truncated/trailing response refusal, bounded deadlines, cancellation, child-tree quiescence and executable identity mismatch.
CLI compositionImplemented and locally qualified on native/JS: origin-relative paths, explicit grants, separate project operations, dry-run behavior, default binary logs and explicit paths. Pure host suites pass 1246 native, 1181 JS, 1165 Wasm and 1165 WasmGC tests. CLI/npm and process supervision checks pass.
Task 6 handoffPin the merged executable/protocol identities and run installed cross-platform signed-provider acceptance. Pure and simulated tests do not claim installed authentication.

Code evidence for the starting point

The first lifecycle implementation is metadata_sessions.mbt, with eight lifecycle tests. This is a host embedding contract, not an installed process provider.

The current engine binder is in metadata_provider.mbt. The publication gate belongs in Host::run_content. The CLI plans and runs in main.mbt. Task 4's adapter specification records the shared API and signed fixture. These source pins distinguish the implemented lifecycle slice from the remaining Task 5 process composition.

Current process implementation

Commit a97e4b1 composes metadata/grants, the host process session and the binary supervisor bridge. The CLI keeps its original session owner from planning through execution. A disabled provider binds unavailable capabilities, preserving the existing diagnostic and acquiring no session; a configured shared restore without grants refuses explicitly. Follow-up head 419f945 probes JS pin-read support and preserves disabled-provider compatibility. Runtime operations remain unavailable on pure targets; their stub binds without filesystem or process imports. The local acceptance receipt is a development artifact, not authorization to reuse saved provider bytes.

title: Task 6: Qualify installed authenticated consumption
description:
### Task 6: Qualify installed authenticated consumption

Test real signed provider admission with independently expected generated APIs, tampered bytes/signatures, wrong policy/lock/release/revision, required selected-profile freshness/rollback cases, context boundary faults, two-project isolation, no-fact compatibility, Ion rich metadata retention, checked JSON loss and cancellation/cleanup publication preservation. Qualify exact native/npm runtime/platform/service combinations before advertising them. Publish reviewed durable operational documentation through the site. Keep extension packaging, hardened provider qualification and a production signed naming release separate.
design:
Task 6 specification · revision 0.12 · 15 October 2026 · audit and initial installed slices merged · portable installed qualification complete

Qualify installed authenticated providers

Prove that an installed Morphir CLI produces a buildable MoonBit library using a freshly authenticated naming provider. Finish the host audit evidence required by R17, run signed positive and adversarial acceptance tests, and publish operational documentation through the documentation site.

Task 5 PR #80 is merged as 161abf4. The audit slice in PR #81 squash merged as 74be5b4, including newer main PR #79. All 23 head checks and the first 22-job integration passed. The refreshed integration was waiting for macOS runners and native completion. With recorded maintainer admin approval, the exact refreshed tree was locally validated across all four targets and CLI/npm smoke tests before merging. The landed tree matches that tested tree exactly. Rust service PR #297 is merged as 3f10962; MoonBit lifecycle and wire PR #78 is merged as 40a58ba. Local signed-provider tests are useful evidence, but they do not qualify an installed runtime/platform combination.

What changes for a user

A user selects a provider, policy, lock, registry and trust state in project configuration, then supplies an explicit host grant file to the installed CLI. A successful run honors the requested target name and generates a library that a separate MoonBit consumer can import and call. Refusals preserve prior generated output and explain the failed phase and repair.

Ion stays preferred for pipeline data and invocation logs. Morphir JSON remains supported, with an explicit checked loss boundary. The shared provider owns authentication and trust-state changes. The engine neither initializes trust nor retries through weaker assurance.

Keep audit evidence separate from naming

Open the explorable SVG. This diagram describes the target Task 6 separation. Its audit component is implemented locally; installed qualification remains open.

The local audit slice in 61fd5db reuses the bounded telemetry session and sink through a typed host audit adapter. Do not put serialized identity documents into Details.entry, overload execution correlation fields with new meanings, or add authentication authority to generic telemetry. A pure consumer observation hook reports context acquisition and declaration admission; it cannot grant capabilities. Host orchestration correlates those events with the scoped invocation.

Audit fieldMeaning and source
Schema and correlationVersioned typed record; telemetry run, host operation and frozen project-scope identities. No mutable cross-project receipt reuse.
ServiceProtocol service identifier and separately granted executable SHA-256. Record verification status explicitly; selecting a pin does not prove it was checked.
Native providerExact release and raw native revision from the accepted retained snapshot. Unavailable before successful snapshot validation. Never hash a derived core projection and call it the native revision.
Profile and assurancelocal-library-mvp, 0.1.0-draft.1, requested portable assurance and confirmed acceptance status. No hardened claim or downgrade.
Phase resultAcquisition, probe, restore, decode, context acquisition, declaration admission and cleanup. Each reports bounded duration and succeeded, refused or cancelled outcome with stable diagnostic code.
PublicationKeep snapshot acceptance, semantic admission and output publication distinct. A successful restore followed by failed declaration admission or cleanup is not a successful generated run.

Unknown evidence is absent or a typed null, never a guessed success. Audit callbacks cannot change naming, authentication or cleanup behavior. Contain sink failures using the existing dropped-record accounting and direct sink warning. Keep retention and field sizes bounded. No policy bodies, lock bodies, provider/context payloads, credentials or private keys enter the records.

When logging is enabled, the durable invocation evidence is part of the configured telemetry stream, with binary Ion as the default. The default frontend destination remains .morphir/logs/frontend.ionb. Explicit destinations and Ion text, JSON Lines and text opt-outs keep their current meaning. Existing observation records remain readable; new typed audit records have their own profile. The short-lived JSON supervisor receipt continues to serve transport validation only.

Logging off creates no durable audit file, cannot suppress diagnostics, and cannot affect generated source or semantic naming receipts. A saved invocation receipt is audit evidence and can never be restored as an authentication capability. A subsequent execution authenticates afresh.

Inspect the current audit contract

The local API is MetadataAuditSink and MetadataAuditRecord in the host package. TelemetrySession::metadata_audit_sink() connects the CLI to its selected local destination. The metadata package's ProviderObserver reports declaration-validation signals after restoration; the host forwards them only while the owning session is acquired.

morphir_metadata_invocation_v1::{
  profile: "morphir-metadata-invocation-v1",
  run_id: "<telemetry run>",
  operation: "<host operation>",
  project: "<project identity SHA-256>",
  phase: "decode",
  outcome: "succeeded",
  code: "",
  evidence: {
    service: "morphir-package/provider-snapshot/0.1.0-draft.1",
    service_sha256: "<raw executable SHA-256>",
    service_verified: true,
    release: "example.com/morphir/naming@1.0.0",
    native_revision: "<raw retained native SHA-256>",
    execution_profile: "local-library-mvp",
    profile_version: "0.1.0-draft.1",
    assurance: "portable",
    profile_verified: true
  },
  wall_seconds: 1792053527.0e0,
  duration_seconds: 0.01e0
}

Acquisition starts with evidence: null. After grant selection the record contains selected identities with verification flags false and native_revision: null. A successful probe records verified executable and profile identities. Only successful snapshot decoding supplies the native revision. These nulls are supported by the binary Ion serializer and covered by the early-evidence regression.

Record phases are acquire, probe, restore, decode, context, admission and cleanup. Outcomes are started, succeeded, refused and cancelled. Declaration admission validates the provider's identity, public declaration, type and schema. It does not claim generated output was published.

The session retains at most 256 audit records and 2048 total records. Invalid or overflowing records increment dropped accounting. File writes retain the existing bounded flush allowance. This remains optional audit evidence; a missing or failed sink cannot authorize, refuse or alter provider admission.

Provision a fresh signed test registry explicitly

The explicit provisioning slice is implemented in Rust PR #298, squash merged as 2cf4be2. Four TestDriver/Cucumber scenarios, the full package suite and doctests, parser regressions, formatting, warnings-denied Clippy and built CLI checks pass locally. CI passed with expected skipped jobs and automated review completed without findings. Its local and remote source branches are cleaned. The installed gate pins the merged shared source revision. This is test infrastructure, not a production trust default.

Add a reviewed opt-in test-trust provisioning mode to the shared signed fixture exporter. The default exporter must remain effect-free with respect to trust initialization. The opt-in creates only a caller-selected, fresh test destination, uses test-only keys, and refuses overwriting existing trust state. Production CLI and engine code do not call it.

Every adversarial case starts from an isolated fixture or an intentional documented sequence. Do not repair a failed sticky trust operation by copying old registry files over it. Record fixture revision and expected outcomes independently of provider reports. Keep test keys confined to test fixtures and never select a production publisher in this task.

Prove the installed path

Local signed qualification exposed a process-host gate that rejected valid revision-qualified target-name predicates before restoration. The focused fix shares the pure interpreter's existing declaration parser. Matching pins succeed after fresh authenticated restoration; wrong pins return metadata.provider_revision_mismatch and preserve prior outputs. The revision-pin fix in PR #83 squash merged as 974e701. All four target suites and signed JS/native positive and negative runs pass locally. Installed cross-platform qualification remains open.

Install the packed npm CLI into an empty temporary installation, outside repository scripts. Use its shipped helper bundle and compute the actual granted runtime/service/helper identities. Execute the installed JS CLI and the native CLI artifact against the same pinned shared service protocol. Build generated libraries and call the exact expected public function from a separate consumer.

CaseRequired assertion
Fresh signed admissionTwo project scopes generate and call authenticated_ready(), with matching references and semantic receipts. Both operations carry independent correlation and admitted native identity.
Bytes and signaturesTampered native archive/payload and invalid signed metadata refuse before replacement. Stable diagnostic identifies the verification phase.
Policy, lock, release and revisionEach wrong selection or digest fails independently. No prior admitted response or other project grant can supply missing authority.
Freshness and rollbackRun the selected portable profile's expiry, rollback and interrupted-operation cases against fresh/intentional state. Assert shared verifier outcomes and trust-state effects separately from publication.
Provider declarationsFour genuinely signed variants authenticate and decode successfully, then refuse incompatible type, subject role, object form or interpreter at semantic admission. Both projects preserve published bytes.
Context boundaryMissing or changed contexts, relative imports escaping inventory and ambiguous digest bases refuse. Either explicit signed inventory path resolves relative to its admitted base. Retained bytes stay independently owned.
No relevant factsDisabled and configured-but-unused providers work without acquisition. Dry-run and project listing launch no service and change no trust state.
Ion and JSON compatibilityIon text/binary checkpoints retain annotated rich metadata and unknown predicates. Explicit Morphir JSON succeeds only through its supported checked conversion; unsupported loss refuses clearly.
Cancellation and deadlinesCancel before/during restore and enforce bounded teardown, descendant quiescence and old-output preservation. Unconfirmed cleanup retains owned scratch and blocks publisher.begin.
Audit behaviorDecode real default binary Ion logs, check service/native/profile/assurance evidence, distinguish selected and verified identity, honor explicit paths, and prove logging on/off yields identical semantic artifacts.

Installed gate implementation

scripts/installed-provider-check.mbtx drives the clean pinned shared checkout, locked service/exporter build, installed npm tarball and copied native executable. Every adversarial case provisions fresh test trust; only previously published artifacts are copied as the byte-preservation oracle. Separate consumers import the exact generated files and independently call the expected API on JS/native targets. The primary receipt is annotated binary Ion with an explicit JSON inspection view. Real binary Ion audit records and rich annotated decimal/timestamp/blob/typed-null checkpoint values are decoded and checked by MoonBit.

The gate includes validly signed expiry and rollback fixtures, interrupted-state markers, independent project grants, wrong identities/policy/lock/release/revision, altered signed bytes, context boundaries, planning and no-fact compatibility. Mid-restore cancellation and deadlines use a deliberately blocked real service with an additional descendant. A separately pinned test-only helper fault claims unconfirmed quiescence after a real signed restore, proving retained scratch and publication blocking. These negative fixtures do not substitute fake authenticated responses.

The complete local gate passed all 48 cases, 24 per installed client, on darwin/arm64 with Node 24.22.0 and Rust 1.98.1. Independent consumers of both projects pass on JS/native. Actual binary Ion audit decoding and exact annotated rich Ion comparisons pass, along with required lint, formatting, configuration validation and site/browser checks. The runner and operations guide in PR #84 squash merged as 5640c8e, including review fix 156e35d. The clean-checkout preflight rejects untracked files before Cargo. A focused red/green boundary test verified that refusal and stale-success removal, then verified a clean pinned checkout reaches the build boundary. The review thread is addressed and resolved. The source-head Ubuntu 24.04/linux-x64 and macOS 15/darwin-arm64 CI jobs each passed all 48 installed cases, with 25 green head checks. That initial 48-case slice qualified its tested scope and left signed incompatible provider declarations and ambiguous context inventory for the final slice below. The durable operations guide is landed at docs/PROVIDER_OPERATIONS.md. Task 6 remained open after that initial slice.

Merge and verification evidence

Main had advanced through Elm PR #82. The exact combined tree 883ee8f passed local native 1391, JS 1327, Wasm 1310 and WasmGC 1310 tests, all 48 installed cases, binary Ion audit and rich metadata checks, and required lint/format/validation. Both PR source heads were fully green and reviews were resolved. Queue integration jobs were still pending. Recorded maintainer admin approval was used to squash merge #83 then #84, and both landed trees exactly match their verified integration trees.

Finish signed semantic and context qualification

Implementation landed through shared fixture PR #299 and MoonBit gate PR #86. The five new shared fixture scenarios failed before implementation; all nine acceptance scenarios, parser tests, full package tests and doctests, formatting and warnings-denied Clippy now pass. The complete initial local installed gate passes all 60 cases, 30 per client, including binary Ion audit decoding, rich Ion retention, independently compiled consumers and refusal byte preservation. A focused check verifies the strengthened audit ordering assertions against real records and rejects early refusal and wrong revision controls. The second complete local run on final assertion commit 87e856c also passes all 60 cases, including the new per-project decoded revision, service identity and ordered refusal checks. Shared fixture PR #299 is squash merged as ce68e7d, with all 13 success checks, expected skips and no automated review findings. Its source branches are cleaned, and its landed tree equals tested cc885b6. MoonBit head adea2cf pins that accepted source. The fresh local run on adea2cf against merged ce68e7d also passes all 60 cases, actual binary Ion audits, exact rich Ion checks and independent consumers. The final Ubuntu 24.04/linux-x64 and macOS 15/darwin-arm64 CI jobs each pass all 60 cases against accepted source. Both downloaded primary annotated binary Ion receipts decode, match their inspection views and include all final cases. All 26 source-head checks pass, with no review findings or unresolved threads. Full source-head local mise run check passes Wasm/WasmGC 1310 tests each, JS 1327, native 1391, CLI/compiler/execution checks and builds. The exact combined tree a7a98f3 with main 8d2b284 also passes the complete local check, formatting, validation and 60-case installed gate; combined unit counts are Wasm/WasmGC 1322 each, JS 1339 and native 1403. Local CLI, npm package, service, helper and model identities are unchanged. Maintainer-approved PR #86 squash merged as 6f9f7e8, whose tree exactly matches that tested combination. The normal merge command was rejected because repository queue auto-merge is disabled, so recorded admin-bypass approval was used after green head CI. No queue integration CI is claimed. Task 6 is complete.

The final slice adds explicit signed variants to the shared fixture exporter. Four variants independently change the output type, subject role, object form or interpreter before publisher and TUF signing. Each receives fresh test trust. A successful real-service restore and decode must precede the expected admission refusal, with both projects' published bytes preserved.

The context variant signs two inventory paths containing identical bytes. Digest-only lookup must refuse ambiguity. Separate positive cases select each path relative to the admitted native document base, generate both projects and compile independent consumers of the exact public API. No signed bytes, responses or trust databases are patched or copied to create authority.

The existing installed npm/native gate gains six cases per client, for 60 cases per platform. Ubuntu and macOS jobs must pass on the pinned shared fixture revision before Task 6 is closed. Local results and CI receipts remain distinct evidence.

Qualify exact combinations

Record OS and architecture, installed CLI integrity or native artifact digest, Node identity, MoonBit compiler/core identities, shared executable digest and source revision, helper bundle digest, profile/version and test-fixture revision. Green pure tests or a successful probe do not imply installed authentication qualification.

Start with Ubuntu and macOS native/npm lanes supported by current CI. The existing three-OS supervisor tests remain valuable but do not qualify Windows authenticated installation. Keep Windows, pure Wasm/WasmGC process hosting, LLVM-dependent combinations and hardened assurance unavailable or explicitly unqualified until their full acceptance row passes. Generated-library compiler targets and the runtime that hosts the CLI are separate dimensions.

Ship in reviewable slices

SliceDeliverable and check
6a · Typed audit evidenceHost audit types and pure observation hook, bounded telemetry integration, actual native identity accessor and CLI wiring. Four-target pure tests, enabled/disabled sink tests, unchanged naming and cleanup behavior.
6b · Explicit signed test provisioningShared fixture helper opt-in, refusal to overwrite state, test-only keys and documented fresh-state contract. Rust tests and warnings-denied lint checks.
6c · Installed signed qualificationPortable MoonBit .mbtx orchestration, real installed JS/native clients, independent generated consumer, adversarial cases and machine-readable evidence. Pin shared source and qualify CI platform rows.
6d · Operational documentationPublish configuration, grant/pin preparation, explicit trust provisioning, log inspection and repair examples on the site. State exact qualified combinations and limits. Validate site links and examples against the installed CLI.

Local audit evidence includes four-target suites, CLI/npm smoke checks, signed JS/native runs with two projects, decoded default binary Ion records, logging on/off semantic hash equality and wrong-pin refusal preserving trust/output. The current exported Capabilities struct adds provider_observer; callers can inherit the no-op from Capabilities::unavailable(). Local audit sinks are qualified by this slice; external exporters need explicit support for the new profile. Close Task 6 only after all slices and the parent specification's R17 are satisfied. Extension packaging, production signed naming publication and hardened qualification remain separate roadmap work. Each PR records its source range and checks in beads.

Read the component contracts

The host-session specification defines grants, path origins, process limits and cleanup. The snapshot contract defines retained native bytes and checked consumer views. The approved stage specification defines diagnostic and audit requirements.
acceptance_criteria: Versioned typed host audit evidence records selected versus verified service identity, admitted native revision, profile/version, assurance, correlated phase outcomes and duration through bounded existing telemetry; default binary Ion and explicit opt-outs/paths preserve semantics with logging off. Explicit opt-in signed test-fixture trust provisioning refuses existing state. Installed JS/native consumers call independently expected generated APIs and adversarial cases preserve prior output. Exact qualified runtime/platform/service combinations are retained as evidence. Operational docs are published through the validated site. R17 and all original Task6 cases are satisfied before closure.
notes:
Task5 handoff clarified 2026-10-15: R17 still requires explicit typed host evidence for service/executable identity, admitted native revision, selected profile/version and assurance, plus a durable binary Ion invocation receipt. Existing lifecycle observations and ephemeral JSON transport receipts do not complete R17. Implement and qualify this before closing Task6 or the parent stage; host timing/identity must stay out of semantic naming receipts/generated source. Task5 PR80 must land first. Fresh explicit test-only trust provisioning is required for installed signed fixtures; never reuse the deliberately invalid local host-signed-fixture state.
PR80 has 23 green head checks and is first in the merge queue. Task6 audit development starts on a separate local branch stacked on reviewed419f945; queued PR80 remains unchanged. Rebase the audit work onto merged main before publication.
Task6 audit slice is PR81 at61fd5dbd0f8dbf1b5ed43c14e242b1868a4e069f, rebased onto main161abf48411fc5976d7a0a9f1413767c22f2abe8 with exact tree equality to locally qualifieda544b8b. Task5 PR80 merged after23 green head checks and22 green queue jobs; source branch cleaned. Audit PR81 review and CI are now monitored. Original Task6 installed qualification, reviewed explicit fixture provisioning and operational docs remain open.
Shared fixture preparation is now finos/morphir-rust PR298, head 1a02876 on feat/provider-test-trust-fixtures. This follows 6dc71da with a red/green regression refusing misplaced leading options before output creation. Local full package tests/doctests, 4 BDD scenarios with TestDriver, example parser, format, warnings-denied all-targets Clippy and built CLI argument/preservation checks pass. PR298 review and CI monitored alongside queued MoonBit PR81. Neither the test fixture keys nor initialization is exposed as a production host default.
Installed qualification must include both matching and wrong authored predicate revision pins. Source evidence at MoonBit 61fd5db: morphir-metadata/addresses.mbt naming_predicate accepts the revision-qualified 4.1 target-names declaration, but morphir-host/metadata_process.mbt restore_library currently gates on exact equality with the unqualified TARGET_NAMES_PREDICATE. Thus the process path needs qualification/fix for pinned predicates; a matching pin should restore and a wrong pin should reach the existing metadata.provider_revision_mismatch admission diagnostic. This gate predates the audit-only PR81. Keep it in Task6 qualification scope and do not advertise complete installed pin support before the case passes.
close_reason: Delivered audit 74be5b4 and MoonBit qualification 974e701..6f9f7e8; shared fixtures 2cf4be2..ce68e7d. Final PR86 adea2cf has 26 green checks, no review findings, and 60 installed cases each on Ubuntu24.04/linux-x64 and macOS15/darwin-arm64. Both actual primary binary Ion receipts independently decoded and checked. Landed tree a7a98f3 equals locally verified combined main8d2b284: full check, lint/format/validation and all60 installed cases pass; unit suites native1403, JS1339, Wasm/WasmGC1322 each. Local client/package/service/helper/model identities unchanged. Maintainer approved86; recorded admin bypass used after queue auto-merge rejection, no queue integration CI claimed. Portable local-library-mvp only; production releases, extension packaging and hardened assurance remain separate.

Qualify installed authenticated providers

What changes for a user

A user selects a provider, policy, lock, registry and trust state in project configuration, then supplies an explicit host grant file to the installed CLI. A successful run honors the requested target name and generates a library that a separate MoonBit consumer can import and call. Refusals preserve prior generated output and explain the failed phase and repair.

Ion stays preferred for pipeline data and invocation logs. Morphir JSON remains supported, with an explicit checked loss boundary. The shared provider owns authentication and trust-state changes. The engine neither initializes trust nor retries through weaker assurance.

Keep audit evidence separate from naming

Open the explorable SVG. This diagram describes the target Task 6 separation. Its audit component is implemented locally; installed qualification remains open.

The local audit slice in 61fd5db reuses the bounded telemetry session and sink through a typed host audit adapter. Do not put serialized identity documents into Details.entry, overload execution correlation fields with new meanings, or add authentication authority to generic telemetry. A pure consumer observation hook reports context acquisition and declaration admission; it cannot grant capabilities. Host orchestration correlates those events with the scoped invocation.

Audit fieldMeaning and source
Schema and correlationVersioned typed record; telemetry run, host operation and frozen project-scope identities. No mutable cross-project receipt reuse.
ServiceProtocol service identifier and separately granted executable SHA-256. Record verification status explicitly; selecting a pin does not prove it was checked.
Native providerExact release and raw native revision from the accepted retained snapshot. Unavailable before successful snapshot validation. Never hash a derived core projection and call it the native revision.
Profile and assurancelocal-library-mvp, 0.1.0-draft.1, requested portable assurance and confirmed acceptance status. No hardened claim or downgrade.
Phase resultAcquisition, probe, restore, decode, context acquisition, declaration admission and cleanup. Each reports bounded duration and succeeded, refused or cancelled outcome with stable diagnostic code.
PublicationKeep snapshot acceptance, semantic admission and output publication distinct. A successful restore followed by failed declaration admission or cleanup is not a successful generated run.

Unknown evidence is absent or a typed null, never a guessed success. Audit callbacks cannot change naming, authentication or cleanup behavior. Contain sink failures using the existing dropped-record accounting and direct sink warning. Keep retention and field sizes bounded. No policy bodies, lock bodies, provider/context payloads, credentials or private keys enter the records.

When logging is enabled, the durable invocation evidence is part of the configured telemetry stream, with binary Ion as the default. The default frontend destination remains .morphir/logs/frontend.ionb. Explicit destinations and Ion text, JSON Lines and text opt-outs keep their current meaning. Existing observation records remain readable; new typed audit records have their own profile. The short-lived JSON supervisor receipt continues to serve transport validation only.

Logging off creates no durable audit file, cannot suppress diagnostics, and cannot affect generated source or semantic naming receipts. A saved invocation receipt is audit evidence and can never be restored as an authentication capability. A subsequent execution authenticates afresh.

Inspect the current audit contract

The local API is MetadataAuditSink and MetadataAuditRecord in the host package. TelemetrySession::metadata_audit_sink() connects the CLI to its selected local destination. The metadata package's ProviderObserver reports declaration-validation signals after restoration; the host forwards them only while the owning session is acquired.

  profile: "morphir-metadata-invocation-v1",
  run_id: "<telemetry run>",
  operation: "<host operation>",
  project: "<project identity SHA-256>",
  phase: "decode",
  outcome: "succeeded",
  code: "",
  evidence: {
    service: "morphir-package/provider-snapshot/0.1.0-draft.1",
    service_sha256: "<raw executable SHA-256>",
    service_verified: true,
    release: "example.com/morphir/naming@1.0.0",
    native_revision: "<raw retained native SHA-256>",
    execution_profile: "local-library-mvp",

    profile_verified: true

  duration_seconds: 0.01e0

Acquisition starts with evidence: null. After grant selection the record contains selected identities with verification flags false and native_revision: null. A successful probe records verified executable and profile identities. Only successful snapshot decoding supplies the native revision. Record phases are acquire, probe, restore, decode, context, admission and cleanup. Outcomes are started, succeeded, refused and cancelled. Declaration admission validates the provider's identity, public declaration, type and schema. It does not claim generated output was published.

The session retains at most 256 audit records and 2048 total records. Invalid or overflowing records increment dropped accounting. File writes retain the existing bounded flush allowance. This remains optional audit evidence; a missing or failed sink cannot authorize, refuse or alter provider admission.

Qualify installed authenticated providers
