comments.text:
Design before bd-plan stored .dev/designs/morphir-authenticated-provider-loading.html: Authenticated metadata providers · Morphir MoonBit
Morphir MoonBit documentation

Approved specification · revision 0.4 · 15 October 2026 · shared service landed · host process landed · audit slice in progress

Authenticated metadata providers in the MoonBit CLI

Let the installed CLI consume declared naming facts by obtaining the provider through an explicit, scoped host service. Keep package authority, metadata validation and target-name allocation as separate components.

Ion firstMorphir JSON supportedPer-project trustPluggable host

The user-visible result: a project can request a MoonBit target name in metadata, run the installed CLI with a configured authenticated provider, and get a buildable library using that exact name. Authentication failures produce a clear diagnostic before generated output replaces the previous destination.

This document specifies the next stage. The local contract slice now implements immutable provider selections and project-scoped binding in commits e9ddf69 and 4c79cdd, squash merged in PR #69 as e6015f9. Task 4 is now landed through Rust #295, Rust #296 and MoonBit #76: retained authenticated native bytes, a checked consumer projection and signed test naming-provider qualification. Task 5 lifecycle and binary wire contracts landed in PR #78, and the shared one-shot Ion service landed in Rust #297. Host grants, process composition and CLI integration landed in PR #80 as 161abf4, with local signed-provider qualification complete. Installed qualification and complete R17 audit evidence remain Task 6; no production publisher or trust defaults are selected.

1. Purpose and boundaries2. What exists today3. Proposed components4. Scoped capabilities5. Authentication contract6. Data and same-byte identity7. Configuration and defaults8. Invocation lifecycle9. Context acquisition10. Diagnostics and logging11. Acceptance evidence12. Reviewable delivery13. Decisions before integration14. Evidence and serving

1. Purpose and boundaries

Preserve model identity

Source spelling, Morphir identity, requested target name and allocated target name remain distinct. The provider declares the naming fact's meaning; it does not rename the model.

Authenticate the declaration

The host obtains the exact signed Library under an explicit package policy. The engine checks its declaration and the consumer assertion before applying naming intent.

Keep the pipeline modular

The engine stays free of filesystem, network and signature-verifier dependencies. A CLI adapter or another embedding host supplies the same portable capability contract.

The first consumer is the existing target-names binding for ValueDefinitions. This stage does not add general annotation execution, source annotation syntax, multi-file source compilation, extension packaging or richer type inference. Additional predicates need their own interpreter and acceptance evidence.

Signed Library data is inspected, never executed as a package hook or dynamically loaded interpreter. Authentication does not make an invalid declaration valid.

2. What exists today

ComponentLanded behaviorRemaining gap
MoonBit namingReadable defaults, exact requests, traceable recovery, warnings and compatibility mode.No change to naming policy is required for this stage.
Metadata consumerExplicit Capabilities, provider identity/type/schema checks, bounded contexts and assertion receipts.The application must supply freshly authenticated data.
Installed MoonBit CLIPreserves authored facts in Ion. Known naming facts fail with metadata.provider_unavailable when no provider is supplied.Construct and scope the real host service.
Shared Rust CLIAt upstream 23e7dfa, metadata validate-trusted calls exact locked local restore and validates provider declarations.Its output is a count/status report, not the same-byte provider snapshot required here.
Shared package workPortable local restore is the selected baseline; broader provider hardening and recovery have separate tracked work.Qualify the exact adapter, service version and platforms used by this CLI.

The current constructor captures metadata capabilities when registering the built-in generator. Its callback receives a predicate, not a project identity. A workspace-wide callback must not guess a project's trust policy from the predicate or IR unit ID.

Important upstream distinction: a successful validate-trusted report cannot be converted into RestoredLibrary by reading arbitrary files afterward. We need a service that retains and exports the authenticated bytes, or an equivalent in-process host adapter, with the snapshot contract in section 6.

3. Proposed components

The diagram is a proposed integration, not a map of implemented restoration. The last two components already exist; the scoped adapter and authenticated snapshot delivery are the new work.

OwnerResponsibilityMust not absorb
CLI compositionResolve configuration, check host grants, bind each selected project and wire telemetry/cancellation.Cryptographic trust-policy implementation.
MoonBit host adapterBound service invocation, validate its protocol, retain a scoped immutable snapshot and construct engine callbacks.Ambient registry lookups or trusting a user-authored report.
Shared restore providerAuthenticate repository/publisher authority, replay exact lock, enforce supported trust-state semantics and produce same-byte evidence.MoonBit target-name allocation.
Metadata consumerCheck provider identity, declaration, subject, object shape and required interpreter.I/O, service discovery or package hooks.
Generator and publisherAllocate consistently, record consumed facts and publish only after the required work succeeds.Silently ignoring a known naming request.

The initial CLI adapter should reuse an explicitly selected shared Rust service through the existing host process capability where available. This is a proposed delivery mechanism. A plain validation command is insufficient, and the service/export API needs an upstream review before implementation can claim interoperability.

4. Bind capabilities to a project session

R1. Add a project-scoped binding step to planned generation. Freeze the selected project, effective metadata configuration and host-approved grants with the plan. Bind a separate capability closure to that project's jobs; never dispatch solely by predicate, model package name or unit.id.

R2. Preserve Engine::new(metadata_capabilities=...) for existing single-scope embedding callers. The new factory/binder is additive and optional. Supplying both static and project-resolved authorities must be rejected as ambiguous unless an explicit precedence contract is reviewed. The contract slice selects the additive Engine::register_project_metadata_provider(bind) API, passing immutable ProjectMetadataScope values. Project isolation remains mandatory.

// Existing portable semantic boundary, unchanged in purpose:
Capabilities {
  restore_library: (expanded_predicate) -> RestoredLibrary,
  load_context: (reference, accepted_base) -> ContextDocument,
  target_names_interpreter: true,
}

// Proposed host-side binding; schematic, not a shipped API:
bind_project(frozen_project_scope, approved_host_grants)
  -> MetadataProviderSession { capabilities, dispose, receipt }

R3. Binding during planning has no restore, process launch, trust-state initialization or durable writes. Authentication happens when execution encounters a required fact. Projects without relevant facts continue to work without a restore provider. Explicitly invalid configuration fails planning.

R4. A session owns its snapshots, context inventories and scratch resources. It must not outlive the invocation, leak policy across projects or reuse previous-run admission. Each interpretation invokes fresh restoration as today; duplicate expanded predicates may reuse restoration only within that interpretation. Disposal failure blocks generated publication and reports any retained resource.

Project configuration selects among capabilities granted by the application. It cannot load arbitrary callback code, widen approved roots or bootstrap trust merely by naming a key. For the ordinary local CLI, an explicit invocation is the host grant under the documented local filesystem assumption. Restricted embeddings can refuse requests outside their own grants.

5. Authenticate packages before interpreting facts

R5. The selected provider must freshly authenticate the exact locked Library and its required dependency graph under explicit trusted-host policy. Release selection comes from a full lock and an allowlisted predicate-to-release binding. Package release versions remain separate from IR format and semantic names.

CheckAuthorityEvidence required
Repository and publisher acceptanceShared restore service and caller-supplied policy.Approved trust roots and accepted signed metadata, exact target/payload binding.
Freshness, rollback and trust stateShared provider's selected execution profile.Supported clock/expiry rules, trust-state identity and recovery behavior for that profile.
Locked graph and payload integrityShared package protocol.Exact release, dependency graph and authenticated payload identities; no lock rewrite.
Provider semanticsMoonBit metadata consumer.Public morphir/naming:naming#target-names, native format 4.1.0, closed frontend/backend dictionaries and its own native schema facts.
Consumer naming intentMetadata interpreter and allocator.Owned ValueDefinition, valid language IDs and target identifiers, consistent assertions and collision checks.

R6. A hash, context digest, signed-looking field, arbitrary receipt or package metadata never grants authority. The application trusts the installed service implementation and its protected invocation boundary; the returned record is not independently a proof object. Tests using simulated host capabilities must remain clearly distinguished from authenticated-service tests.

R7. First delivery may use explicitly selected portable filesystem assurance with caller-controlled local roots and no hostile concurrent replacement. It still enforces the chosen package authentication/trust-state contract. Hardened assurance, production recovery and power-loss claims require separate evidence. An unsupported hardened request fails; there is no automatic downgrade.

Refresh of accepted trust state may be a legitimate side effect of authentication even if generation later fails. Previous generated output must stay intact; the CLI must not roll back shared trust-state updates to make the invocation appear side-effect free.

6. Derive every view from the authenticated bytes

R8. A provider result contains an immutable native payload, its exact SHA-256 revision, native format and package identity, the semantic projection needed by the current consumer, native metadata and inventoried context bytes. All views derive from that same authenticated payload or its authenticated bundle inventory.

Native payload identity

The revision is the exact provider IR payload byte digest used by the provider document URI. Keep bundle/record digests separate. Do not hash a reserialized projection and call it the native revision.

Semantic projection

The current RestoredLibrary.core uses the supported v4 semantic model. Conversion from native 4.1 must be explicit and checked. It is not a claim that the existing codec restores native 4.1.

Native metadata

Retain the provider's own document graph without inventing declarations in a companion file. Preserve Ion annotations, typed nulls, exact integers and binary values whenever present.

R9. The preferred adapter envelope and invocation receipt are versioned binary Ion. Text Ion is a supported inspection form. Morphir JSON, signed registry JSON and morphir.lock remain supported in their existing contracts. Authentication hashes the original bytes regardless of their format; no conversion happens before byte verification.

A deliberately selected JSON control transport is acceptable only with a documented lossless representation for bytes, large integers, annotations and native metadata. Reject unsupported values rather than flattening them. Configuration may remain TOML. Choosing JSON at a boundary does not change the engine's Ion-first checkpoint policy.

// Proposed envelope fields, not a finalized shared wire schema:
profile: morphir_authenticated_provider_snapshot_v1
request: { invocation, project_scope, predicate, exact_release }
provider: { package, native_format, payload_sha256, document_uri }
payload: { native_bytes, semantic_projection, native_metadata }
contexts: [ { identity, sha256, bytes } ]
evidence: { service_identity, execution_profile, assurance, policy_identity,
            lock_identity, trust_state_identity, authenticated_at }

// Transferred evidence is meaningful only from the trusted service invocation.
// A stored envelope cannot be imported as authority on the next run.

R10. A process adapter validates request/response correlation, protocol version, release/revision and content digests, plus size/traversal bounds. Receive bytes through an owned pipe or a private host-owned transfer location with no mutable reopen gap. Keep the snapshot alive through interpretation; authenticate again on the next run. Derived projections and their format conversion require independent positive and negative tests.

7. Configuration should select a service, not define trust

Ordinary naming remains zero-configuration. Declared provider facts require an explicit host service and existing initialized trust state. There is no implicit network acquisition, installation, trust-root initialization or broad package restore.

# Proposed configuration vocabulary; not current CLI support.
[metadata]
provider = "shared-local-restore"
service = "/approved/tools/morphir-provider-host"
policy = ".morphir/trust/policy.json"
lock = "morphir.lock"
registry = "/approved/local-registry"
state = ".morphir/trust/state"
assurance = "portable"

[metadata.naming]
release = "example.com/morphir/naming@<published-exact-version>"
# A source predicate may additionally pin rev=sha256:<native-payload-digest>.

R11. Resolve each path from its owning configuration document, with explicit CLI paths resolved from invocation location. Use existing configuration precedence and preserve provenance. Freeze effective selections before effects. System/global host grants bound project choices; a project cannot redirect another project's service or trust state. Do not choose the first project's settings for an entire workspace.

R12. The disabled/default CLI service mode supplies unavailable capabilities. An embedding's explicitly supplied capabilities remain an application grant; a parsed disabled selection alone does not revoke or add them. No-fact generation and opaque metadata preservation stay unchanged. Selecting a supported provider but omitting a required field produces a configuration diagnostic naming the field and file. Unknown providers/profiles fail clearly. CLI flag names and host-policy syntax should be finalized in the contract PR, after checking existing ecosystem vocabulary.

RuntimeFirst-stage mechanismAdmission requirement
Native and Node CLIExplicit process adapter where the existing host offers process execution.Qualify the exact service artifact, adapter, OS/architecture and local assurance profile.
WASM-GC with supplied runnerOptional explicit host bridge.Separate bridge tests; Node support does not automatically qualify this path.
Plain WASI Preview 1No process-based adapter.Required provider fails unavailable unless an embedding supplies a separately qualified capability.
Browser / memory embeddingApplication-supplied callbacks.No filesystem/registry authority implied by having metadata or a browser UI.

8. Complete admission before generated publication

R13. Source reads, interpretation, generation and required builds retain existing cancellation and publication ordering. Check cancellation before/after service calls; the provider bounds its own running operation and confirms termination/disposal. No restore is started by workspace, project list or --dry-run.

R14. A required authentication, projection, context, declaration, naming or disposal failure prevents generated publication. Existing publishers retain their documented task-level replacement guarantees; this work does not promise cross-project atomic replacement. A two-project trust test must prove that project B cannot borrow project A's successful admission for the same predicate.

Checkpoint preservation is separate from interpretation. Loading an old checkpoint does not rename its identities or mark a stored provider receipt trusted. Ion payloads and unknown valid predicates remain preserved; the explicit Morphir JSON loss boundary continues to apply.

9. Context loading is a separate, bounded grant

R15. Relative .jsonld contexts come only from an accepted workspace root or verified archive inventory. Resolve symlinks under the selected assurance profile and reject escape. A metadata-supplied base cannot widen the grant. Content-addressed context IDs identify exact bytes, not a trusted declaration provider.

Keep the existing consumer bounds: 32 import levels, 256 resources per closure, 1 MiB per context and 100,000 expanded assertions per graph. Reject hash mismatches, duplicate object members, cycles, repeated resources and conflicting imports. No HTTP fetch is performed by the metadata consumer.

The adapter supplies provider contexts from the authenticated snapshot's inventory and consumer contexts from the explicitly accepted source snapshot. Keep their ownership separate. Missing contexts must not trigger an ambient registry or network lookup. An inlined context avoids I/O but does not bypass provider authentication.

The published registry release is authority-qualified and distinct from the native IR package morphir/naming. The concrete in-process capture API and the versioned process boundary are detailed in the Task 4 snapshot-export contract. The Task 5 host-session specification describes composition and cleanup before publication. Production authority remains an explicit selection.

10. Diagnostics, logs and invocation receipts

R16. Return stable diagnostic codes with project/source ownership, predicate/release when available, failed phase and a repair. Existing metadata.provider_unavailable, revision mismatch, declaration/type and interpreter diagnostics remain distinguishable. New host failures should use a consistent metadata.restore_* family; exact codes are frozen by contract tests.

FailureRepair shown to the user
Service unavailable or unsupported runtimeSelect a qualified host provider or use an embedding that supplies the capability.
Policy/state/lock missingName the missing configuration source; initialize trust through the shared workflow explicitly.
Authentication, expiry or rollback rejectionReport the shared verifier reason; refresh/repair trust through its supported workflow.
Release/revision mismatchAlign the exact locked release and authored predicate pin.
Invalid declaration or lossy projectionUse a provider release with the required native schema and supported projection.
Cleanup failureReport the retained host-owned resource for inspection; do not publish.

R17. Reuse the existing telemetry/event boundary. Correlate restore, snapshot decode, context acquisition, admission and cleanup with the invocation/project. Record duration, outcome, service identity, native revision, execution profile and assurance. Logging off must not hide diagnostics or change names, trust decisions or semantic artifact contents.

When enabled without an explicit destination, logs land under .morphir/logs/. Honor an explicit log path under existing host rules. Never log private keys, credentials, full policy documents or raw provider/context payloads. Timing/host-specific telemetry belongs in a separate invocation receipt so generated source and semantic naming receipts remain reproducible.

The invocation receipt defaults to binary Ion and records which host service/profile admitted which provider revision for which project. It is audit evidence, not reusable authority. Any update to shared trust state remains owned and reported by the shared provider.

11. What must pass before this is delivered

Evidence groupRequired casesWhat it proves
Pure contractUnavailable defaults; static compatibility; scoped factory; conflicting configuration; duplicate predicates; unknown predicate retention.Engine semantics and isolation independent of I/O.
Same-byte adapterWrong native digest, changed payload/metadata/context, mismatched response scope, malformed/oversized response, unsupported projection/protocol.No detached report, reread or format conversion can substitute other bytes.
Real authenticationSigned positive provider; invalid/untrusted signatures, tampered bytes, wrong release/lock/pin; expiry/rollback cases required by selected profile.Actual installed service admission, not simulated callbacks.
Context boundaryInventory success, missing context, digest mismatch, path escape, cycle/duplicates/limits; provider and consumer roots kept distinct.Bounded and scoped acquisition.
Workspace isolationTwo projects use the same predicate with different policies/releases; one accepted and one denied. Repeat in both orderings and concurrent embeddings.No global cache or borrowed trust.
Installed namingGenerate exact backend.moonbit export; compile and call from a separate consumer in readable and legacy modes; verify references and receipts.User-visible naming survives actual CLI admission.
Lifecycle and compatibilityDry-run has zero effects; no-fact projects unchanged; old checkpoints stable; Ion rich values retained; JSON loss rejection; cancellation/deadline/disposal failure preserves prior output.No regression to pipeline or publication behavior.
Distribution matrixNative and npm-installed Node lanes with pinned service artifacts; unsupported runtimes fail clearly; additional bridges require their own evidence.Only the tested OS/architecture/runtime/profile combinations are advertised.

R18. The positive installed lane needs a real authenticated morphir/naming test release and independently constructed expected output. Test-only signing keys remain fixtures and are never installed as user trust defaults. Production release/version choice and publishing are separate maintainer decisions.

Use focused compiler checks/tests for mechanics and semantic review for host authority, same-byte derivation and publication ordering. Required repository lint/format/validation checks pass before any push. Qualification claims identify exact commits, service/tool pins and execution profiles; native 4.1 transport, upstream MCK compatibility and hardened restoration are not inferred from a successful naming test.

12. Deliver in reviewable increments

IncrementConcrete changeLanding criterion
Contract PRProject-scoped generation binding, host service/snapshot contract, validated configuration vocabulary and unavailable diagnostics. Preserve existing constructor callers.Pure isolation and compatibility tests pass. Clearly remains unable to claim real authentication.
Integration PRQualified shared-service adapter, same-byte projection/context inventory, CLI composition, telemetry/disposal and installed success/failure qualification.Real signed positive and negative cases pass on each advertised runtime. Depends on reviewed service export and provider artifact.
Durable documentationPublish the reviewed contract and operating guide under docs/specs/ and docs/design/ as appropriate.Document delivered behavior, supported matrix and explicit limits. Site checks and browser preview pass.

Keep the working HTML and implementation ledger in beads with local renders under .dev/. The contract PR can land before the real provider adapter is ready. A7 extension packaging remains separate and blocked by A2; shared typing remains a separate plan.

13. Resolve these before real CLI admission

DecisionProposed directionRequired evidence / owner
Shared service/export ABISmall explicit host protocol over the existing Rust restore implementation; preferred binary Ion snapshot.Review with shared package/metadata owners. Current validate-trusted report does not supply this ABI.
Native 4.1 projectionService derives native metadata and supported core view from retained verified bytes.Checked conversion with independent expectations; reject unsupported constructs.
Provider artifactQualify a real signed test release first; select production release separately.Public declaration/schema, native payload revision, exact lock, accepted trust roots.
Host selection and scope APIPer-project plan binding, not a global mutable resolver.Review additive engine API and configuration-origin rules; two-project trust tests.
Initial runtime matrixStart with explicit native/Node adapters on qualified platforms; report unavailable elsewhere.Exact artifact/platform/profile tests. No blanket cross-platform promise.
Production hardening/recoveryRetain shared provider qualification boundaries.morphir-uhk3.24, morphir-uhk3.26 and morphir-iv3n.2.3.2; does not block drafting the contract.

14. Evidence, tracking and site preview

title: Task 14: GitHub Pages workflow and contributor docs
description:
### Task 14: GitHub Pages workflow and contributor docs

**Files:**
- Create: `.github/workflows/site.yml`
- Modify: `README.md` (add a "Project site" section)
- Modify: `docs/MISE_TASKS.md` (document the site tasks)

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: mise tasks `setup:site`, `build:site`, `check:site`, `test:site` (Tasks 12, 13).
- Produces: workflow `Site` with jobs `build` and `deploy`.

- [ ] **Step 1: Write the workflow**

`.github/workflows/site.yml`:

```yaml
name: Site

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths: &site-paths
      - 'docs/**'
      - 'site/**'
      - 'apps/morphir-site/**'
      - 'apps/morphir-workbench/**'
      - 'pkgs/*/README.md'
      - 'apps/*/README.md'
      - '.config/mise/**'
      - '.github/workflows/site.yml'
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]
    paths: *site-paths
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  build:
    name: Build site
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30
    env:
      SITE_MAIN: '1'
    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v6

      - name: Install pinned MoonBit
        shell: bash
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          MISE_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          curl -fsSL https://mise.run | sh
          export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"
          mise install http:moonbit node
          moonbit_dir="$(mise where http:moonbit)"
          moonbit_version="$(mise current http:moonbit)"
          # The binary archive omits core; install the matching complete toolchain.
          curl -fsSL https://cli.moonbitlang.com/install/unix.sh | \
            MOON_HOME="$moonbit_dir" bash -s -- "$moonbit_version"
          echo "$moonbit_dir/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"
          echo "MOON_HOME=$moonbit_dir" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
          echo "$HOME/.local/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"
          echo "$HOME/.local/share/mise/shims" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"

      - name: Install Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: '24.21.0'

      - name: Update Mooncakes registry
        run: moon update

      - name: Install site dependencies
        run: |
          npm ci --prefix apps/morphir-site
          npm ci --prefix apps/morphir-workbench
          npm exec --prefix apps/morphir-site -- playwright install --with-deps chromium

      - name: Build site
        run: node apps/morphir-site/scripts/build.js

      - name: Check site
        working-directory: apps/morphir-site
        run: moon run --target native check -- --dir ../../_site --base /morphir-moonbit/

      - name: Test site
        run: |
          (cd apps/morphir-site && moon test --target native \
            -p finos/morphir-site/model finos/morphir-site/content finos/morphir-site/views \
            finos/morphir-site/site finos/morphir-site/generate)
          npm test --prefix apps/morphir-site
          npm run test:browser --prefix apps/morphir-site

      - name: Upload Pages artifact
        if: github.event_name != 'pull_request' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
        uses: actions/upload-pages-artifact@v4
        with:
          path: _site

  deploy:
    name: Deploy site
    if: github.event_name != 'pull_request' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
    needs: build
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    permissions:
      pages: write
      id-token: write
    environment:
      name: github-pages
      url: ${{ steps.deployment.outputs.page_url }}
    concurrency:
      group: pages
      cancel-in-progress: false
    steps:
      - name: Deploy to GitHub Pages
        id: deployment
        uses: actions/deploy-pages@v5
```

Check the newest major versions of `actions/upload-pages-artifact` and `actions/deploy-pages` (`gh api repos/actions/deploy-pages/releases/latest --jq .tag_name`) and use them. GitHub may not accept YAML anchors in `on.*.paths`; if `actionlint` or GitHub rejects `&site-paths`, repeat the list under `pull_request`.

- [ ] **Step 2: Lint the workflow**

Run: `mise run lint:yaml`
Expected: no errors (line-length warnings at most).

title: Project Site Implementation Plan
description:
# Project Site Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** Publish finos/morphir-moonbit as a static GitHub Pages site (landing page, docs, blog, Try Morphir), generated in MoonBit with Rabbita server-side rendering plus small client islands.

**Architecture:** A new workspace module `apps/morphir-site` (`finos/morphir-site`). Pure packages (`model`, `content`, `views`, `site`) turn source files into output files; a native `generate` program does all file I/O; a JS `islands` program mounts the search box, theme toggle and mobile menu. Node scripts run Shiki highlighting, copy the workbench to `/try/`, serve the site locally and run a Playwright smoke test. A separate GitHub Actions workflow builds on pull requests and deploys on `main`.

**Tech Stack:** MoonBit 0.10.14 (pinned by mise), `moonbit-community/rabbita` 0.16.3, `moonbit-community/cmark` 0.4.11, `bobzhang/beautiful_mermaid` 0.2.0, `moonbitlang/async` 0.22.4, Node 24.21.0, `shiki` 4.5.0, `mermaid` 12.2.0, `esbuild` 0.28.2, `playwright` 1.58.2.

**Spec:** the design of beads epic `morphir-ukvn.5.29` (render with `mise run beads:plan -- spec morphir-ukvn.5.29 --render`).

## Global Constraints

- Base path `/morphir-moonbit/`; site URL `https://finos.github.io/morphir-moonbit/`; repository URL `https://github.com/finos/morphir-moonbit`. All three come from `site/site.json`, never from literals in code.
- Every route is written as `<route>/index.html`. Routes start and end with `/`.
- `cmark` is pinned to **0.4.11**. 0.4.12 does not compile on the pinned MoonBit 0.10.14 (it uses the `Int32` type).
- Front matter keys are exactly `title`, `date`, `authors`, `summary`, `order`, `draft`. Any other key is a build error.
- `docs/superpowers/**` is a forbidden path. Any file there is a build error.
- A page with `draft: true` is a build error when `SITE_MAIN=1`, and is skipped with a warning otherwise.
- The generator reports all problems of a run together, then exits with status 1.
- Mermaid fallback and unknown code languages are warnings, not errors.
- Each touched MoonBit module has no compiler warnings (repository rule). Derived traits on `pub` types need `pub extend T with Eq::{equal, not_equal}` and `pub extend T with @debug.Debug::{to_repr}`. Use `Map([])` for an empty map and `.to_owned()` to turn a `StringView` into a `String`. Write `x => Ctor(x)`, not `Ctor(_)`.
- `views` uses `inner_html` for reviewed content, so its `moon.pkg` sets `warnings = "-alert_experimental-alert_xss_vulnerable"`. No other package disables a warning.
- Run `moon fmt` before every commit (CI runs `moon fmt --check`).
- Commits: Conventional Commits, plain English, no AI attribution, no `Co-Authored-By`. End each commit message with the line `Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01V1gVYnXzJAw2r4x6xnwGKn`.
- The implementation never changes repository settings. A maintainer sets Settings, Pages, Source to "GitHub Actions".

## Review Focus

- **Non-ASCII content** (accented names in `authors`, emoji in headings): slugs drop non-ASCII letters, the feed and pages keep the text intact. Pinned in Task 3 (`slug("Café ünïcode")`) and Task 9 (feed escapes and keeps `Zoë`).
- **A doc that links to a heading in another doc** (`../adr/README.md#records`): the anchor must exist on the target page or the build fails. Pinned in Task 8 (`assemble` anchor test).
- **README links that leave `docs/`** (`../pkgs/morphir-ir/README.md`, `../AGENTS.md`): published targets become site routes, other repository files become GitHub URLs, and missing files fail. Pinned in Task 7.
- **Windows-style or trailing-slash paths in links** (`./adr/`, `../docs/./ARCHITECTURE.md`): normalised before lookup. Pinned in Task 7.
- **Search with no index or no match** (index fetch fails, query of only spaces): the box shows no results and no error. Pinned in Task 2 (`search` with blank query) and Task 11 (Playwright: query with no match shows "No results").

---

design:
# Morphir MoonBit project site on GitHub Pages Status: proposed, 2026-10-13. Track 5 (`morphir-ukvn.5`), label `repo:morphir-moonbit`. ## Goal Publish a project site for finos/morphir-moonbit on GitHub Pages at `https://finos.github.io/morphir-moonbit/`. The site has four parts: - A landing page. - Documentation, which includes the durable system designs and specifications (architecture, ADRs, designs, specs). - A blog. - A live "Try Morphir" page that embeds the existing Morphir Workbench. Authors write content in Markdown or HTML. The site is built with `moonbit-community/rabbita`. ## Decisions | Topic | Decision | |---|---| | Relation to morphir.finos.org | Project site for this repository, plus the embedded workbench. It links to morphir.finos.org for core Morphir concepts. It does not replace that site. | | Content source of truth | `docs/` stays the source of truth for documentation. Blog posts and site pages go in a new `site/` tree. Selected package READMEs are published when `site/site.json` opts them in. | | Rendering | Static generation with Rabbita server-side rendering (`App::render`), plus small client islands mounted with `App::mount`. There is no full-page hydration. | | Deployment | Every push to `main` builds and deploys. Pull requests build and check, but do not deploy. | | v1 features | Atom feed, client-side search, build-time code highlighting, Mermaid diagrams. | ### Rejected approaches - **Rabbita single-page app.** Pages are blank without JavaScript, search engines index poorly, deep links need a `404.html` redirect, and the bundle is larger. - **Full server-side rendering plus hydration.** The client must rebuild the same virtual DOM for every page, so it needs all page content in JavaScript. Hydration mismatches are possible. Islands give the same interactivity for less cost. ## Facts this design depends on - `moonbit-community/rabbita` 0.16.3, already used by `apps/morphir-workbench`, has `App::render(url~, head~, timeout~)` on non-JS targets. The API is marked `#internal(experimental)`. It also has `App::mount(element_id)` on the JS target. - `moonbit-community/cmark` 0.4.12 is a CommonMark toolkit. It depends on `moonbitlang/async` 0.22.4, which is the version the workspace uses. - `bobzhang/beautiful_mermaid` 0.2.0 renders Mermaid diagrams to SVG in MoonBit. It depends on `moonbitlang/async` 0.22.4 and prefers the native target. - CI already builds the native target on `ubuntu-latest`. ## Architecture ### Layout ``` apps/morphir-site/ # new workspace member, module finos/morphir-site moon.mod # rabbita 0.16.3, cmark 0.4.12, beautiful_mermaid 0.2.0, async 0.22.4 model/ (package) # Page, Post, DocNode, NavTree, SiteConfig: pure data, all targets content/ (package) # front matter, Markdown to HTML, HTML fragments, Mermaid to SVG, link rewrite views/ (package) # Rabbita components: layout, header, docs sidebar, post list, landing generate/ (main, native) # walks content, renders each route, writes _site/, atom.xml, search-index.json islands/ (main, js) # mounts the search box, theme toggle and mobile nav scripts/highlight.js # Shiki post-pass over _site/**/*.html fixtures/ # content tree and golden output for the generator test package.json # shiki, mermaid, esbuild, playwright (exact versions) site/ site.json # title, base path, navigation order, published package READMEs pages/index.html # landing page (fragment, see Content model) blog/YYYY-MM-DD-slug.md|html # blog posts docs/ # unchanged; new docs/design/ and docs/specs/ for system documents ``` `model` and `views` do no I/O. Only `generate` reads and writes files. This keeps the views testable on every target. ### Build `mise run build:site` runs these steps in this order: 1. Build `islands` for the JS target and bundle it with esbuild into `_site/assets/islands.js`. 2. Run `generate` on the native target. It writes all HTML pages, `site.css`, `blog/atom.xml` and `search-index.json` into `_site/`. 3. Run `scripts/highlight.js`, which highlights code blocks in place. 4. Build the workbench (`mise run build:workbench`) and copy its browser output into `_site/try/`. `_site/` is gitignored. ### Routes | Source | Route | |---|---| | `site/pages/index.*` | `/` | | `docs/.md` or `docs/.html` | `/docs//` | | `docs/README.md` or `docs/index.*`, when present | `/docs/` (otherwise the generator writes a docs index page) | | `pkgs//README.md` or `apps//README.md`, listed in `site.json` | `/docs/packages//` | | `site/blog/YYYY-MM-DD-slug.*` | `/blog/slug/` | | (generated) | `/blog/`, `/blog/atom.xml`, `/search-index.json` | | workbench build output | `/try/` | Each route is written as `/index.html`, so GitHub Pages serves it without a `.html` suffix. Route segments keep the file name as written, lower-cased. ### Base path `site.json` holds `base_path` (`/morphir-moonbit/`) and `site_url` (`https://finos.github.io/morphir-moonbit/`). Every generated link, asset reference and feed URL is built from these values. A custom domain later changes only these two values. ## Content model ### Front matter Markdown files use a block between two `---` lines at the top of the file. HTML files use a leading comment of the form ``, so the file stays valid HTML. | Key | Docs | Blog | Meaning | |---|---|---|---| | `title` | optional; fallback is the first `#` heading | required | Page title | | `date` | not used | required; `YYYY-MM-DD`; must match the file-name date | Publication date | | `authors` | not used | required | List of author names | | `summary` | optional | optional; fallback is the first paragraph | Text for the feed, search and cards | | `order` | optional | not used | Position in the docs sidebar; default sort is by title | | `draft` | optional | optional | `true` means the page is not published | The parser accepts only flat `key: value` lines and string lists (`[a, b]` or `- item` lines). It does not need a YAML library. An unknown key is a build error. ### Markdown Markdown is CommonMark through `cmark`. Headings get stable `id` anchors (lower-case, spaces to `-`, other punctuation removed; a duplicate gets `-2`, `-3` and so on). Fenced code blocks keep their language as `class="language-"`. ### HTML An `.html` file is a body fragment. The generator puts it inside the site layout. A file that contains an `` element is a full page. The generator copies it to its route as-is, without the layout. ### What is published - Every file under `docs/` with a `.md` or `.html` extension is published, except as below. This includes `adr/`, `ARCHITECTURE.md`, `QUICK_START.md`, `MISE_TASKS.md`, and the new `design/` and `specs/` directories. - Images and other files under `docs/` that a published page links to are copied with the same relative path. - Files named `*.mbt.md` are not published in v1. - `docs/superpowers/**` is a forbidden path. Any file there fails the build. Agent specs, plans and ledgers live in beads (see `AGENTS.md`), and this guard stops a tool default path from leaking into the site. - A page with `draft: true` is skipped. In a `main` build, the build fails if a draft page exists, so drafts do not sit on `main`. - To publish a spec that lives in beads as a system document, copy it into `docs/specs/` in a pull request. The pull request review is the publishing gate. ### Links - A relative link to a published `.md` or `.html` file is rewritten to its route, with the anchor kept. The source files keep relative `.md` links, so GitHub's own Markdown view continues to work. - A relative link to a repository file that the site does not publish (for example source code) is rewritten to `https://github.com/finos/morphir-moonbit/blob/main/`. - A link to a missing file, or to an anchor that does not exist on the target page, is a build error. ## Features ### Layout and styling One hand-written `site.css` with design tokens as CSS custom properties. There is no CSS framework. The colours and the Morphir mark come from the workbench, so `/try/` does not look foreign. The header has the logo, the links Docs, Blog, Try, and GitHub, the search box and the theme toggle. Docs pages have a sidebar built from the `docs/` tree and `order` values. The layout works at phone width. ### Landing page `site/pages/index.html` holds the hand-built hero, the "Try Morphir" call to action and three feature cards. The generator injects the newest three blog posts at a placeholder element, `
`. ### Search - The generator writes `search-index.json`. Each entry has `route`, `title`, `section` (Docs or Blog), `summary`, `headings` and `text`. `text` is plain text, cut to 2,000 characters per page. - The search island fetches the index the first time the search box gets focus. It ranks title matches first, then heading matches, then text matches, with case-insensitive token-prefix matching. It shows at most 10 results. - Keyboard: `/` focuses the box, the arrow keys move through results, Enter opens a result, Escape closes the list. - Without JavaScript, the placeholder contains a plain link to `/docs/`. ### Atom feed `/blog/atom.xml` is an Atom 1.0 feed with the newest 20 posts and their full HTML content. All text is XML-escaped. Every page head has ``. ### Code highlighting `scripts/highlight.js` uses `shiki` (exact version in `package.json`) to highlight every `
` element in `_site/**/*.html`. Languages: `moonbit`, `elm`, `scheme`, `json`, `shell`,
`toml`, `yaml`. If the `shiki` bundle has no MoonBit grammar, the script loads the grammar from `Yoorkin/shiki` or from
the MoonBit VS Code extension, pinned and copied into `apps/morphir-site/grammars/`. Output uses Shiki's dual light and
dark themes through CSS variables, so highlighting needs no client JavaScript. A block with an unknown language stays
plain, and the script prints a warning.

### Mermaid diagrams

A fenced block with the language `mermaid` is rendered to inline SVG at build time through `beautiful_mermaid`. If
rendering fails, the generator writes `
` with the diagram source, adds the pinned `mermaid` bundle
to that page only, and prints a warning that names the file and the diagram.

### Islands

All islands are in one bundle, `assets/islands.js`, with a target size of 25 KB gzip or less. Each island mounts on a
fixed element id:

| Id | Island |
|---|---|
| `site-search` | Search box and results |
| `site-theme` | Theme toggle: light, dark or system |
| `site-nav` | Mobile navigation menu |

If the bundle does not load, every page is still fully readable and navigable.

The theme is stored in `localStorage` (every access in `try`/`catch`) and applied as a `data-theme` attribute on
``. A short inline script in `` applies the stored theme before the first paint.

### Try Morphir

`/try/` is the workbench browser build, which runs without a server. The site build fails if the workbench
`index.html` uses an absolute asset path, because the workbench is served below `/try/`. The workbench keeps its own UI
and does not get the site layout. The site header links to it.

## CI and deployment

New workflow `.github/workflows/site.yml`:

- Triggers: `push` to `main` and `pull_request` to `main`, each with path filters on `docs/**`, `site/**`,
  `apps/morphir-site/**`, `apps/morphir-workbench/**`, `pkgs/*/README.md`, `apps/*/README.md`, `.config/mise/**` and
  the workflow file; and `workflow_dispatch`.
- Job `build`: install mise with the same steps as `ci.yml`, then `mise run build:site`, then `mise run check:site`.
  On `main` only, upload `_site/` with `actions/upload-pages-artifact`.
- Job `deploy`: on `main` only, needs `build`. It uses `environment: github-pages`,
  `permissions: { pages: write, id-token: write }` and `actions/deploy-pages`. Concurrency group `pages`, with
  `cancel-in-progress: false`.
- Action versions follow the style of `ci.yml`, and Renovate keeps them current.

The site workflow is separate from `ci.yml`, so a content-only pull request does not run the full MoonBit target matrix.

**Manual step.** A maintainer must set Settings, Pages, Source to "GitHub Actions" once. The implementation does not
change repository settings. The pull request description states this step.

### mise tasks

| Task | Action |
|---|---|
| `build:site` | The four build steps above |
| `check:site` | `moonx scripts/site-check.mbtx`: every internal `href` and `src` in `_site/` resolves, every page has a ``, `atom.xml` parses, no file exists under a forbidden path |
| `dev:site` | Build, then serve `_site/` at `http://127.0.0.1:4173/morphir-moonbit/`, with a rebuild when content changes |
| `test:site` | Unit, snapshot and generator tests, then the Playwright smoke test |

## Error handling

The generator collects all errors and reports them together at the end of a run, then exits with a non-zero status.
Each error names the file, and the line where known.

Build errors:

- Front matter with an unknown key or a bad value. A blog post without `title`, `date` or `authors`. A post date that
  does not match the file name.
- A broken internal link or anchor. A missing image.
- Two source files that map to the same route.
- A file under a forbidden path. A draft page in a `main` build.
- An `App::render` timeout.
- An Atom feed that does not parse.
- A workbench `index.html` with absolute asset paths.

Warnings (the build continues):

- A Mermaid diagram that falls back to the client renderer.
- A code block with an unknown language.

## Testing

- `model` and `content`: unit tests for front matter parsing, heading anchors, link rewriting, route mapping, blog
  slug and date, and the forbidden-path guard.
- `views`: snapshot tests with `inspect` over `App::render` output for the layout, a docs page, a blog post, the blog
  index and the landing page.
- `generate`: an integration test over `apps/morphir-site/fixtures/content/`, compared with golden files for the HTML
  pages, `atom.xml` and `search-index.json`.
- `check:site` runs against the real `_site/` in CI.
- Browser smoke test with Playwright (pinned, as in the workbench): the landing page loads, searching for "ADR" shows a
  result, the theme toggle changes `data-theme`, a Mermaid page shows an SVG, and `/try/` loads the workbench.

## Risks

- `App::render` is experimental. The site pins Rabbita 0.16.3 with the workbench. A Rabbita upgrade must pass the
  `views` snapshot tests before it merges.
- `beautiful_mermaid` may not support every diagram type. The client fallback covers this, and warnings make it
  visible.
- MoonBit highlighting depends on a grammar that Shiki may not bundle. The pinned grammar copy covers this.

## Out of scope for v1

Versioned documentation, pull-request preview deployments, translations, comments, analytics, publishing `*.mbt.md`
files, a custom domain, and migration of content from morphir.finos.org.

title: Qualify terminal execution outcome admission
description: Define exact Workbench draft.5 offline validate-outcomes admission with fixed parent-owned JSON/Ion-text cases. Preserve returned values including typed Result.Err, enumerated SDK model errors, runtime failures, cancellation and separate cleanup failures. Bind outcomes to admitted invocation/public declarations, preserve call order and exact suite metadata, validate every returned output, reject malformed or incomplete terminals and contradictory payloads. design:
Workbench terminal outcomes

13 October 2026. Bead morphir-etg2.8. MoonBit baseline 2566b44; parent baseline 23e7dfa4. This is the first execution-outcome and job-lifecycle increment, extending the shared offline Workbench profile with exact 0.1.0-draft.5 admission. Earlier drafts, generated-driver morphir-outcomes-v1 and connected protocol v1 remain frozen.

Purpose and boundary

Qualify a complete ordered terminal envelope against an admitted invocation suite and its authoritative public-entry manifest. This validates producer-supplied evidence; it does not run a function, authenticate a producer, establish model visibility from a name, or prove that a daemon job actually terminated. Live execution adapters and authoritative connected cancellation require separate evidence.

Mermaid source
flowchart LR
  A[Admit manifest and invocation suite] --> B[Decode terminal envelope]
  B --> C[Check call order and declared outputs]
  C --> D[Preserve primary outcome and cleanup]
  D --> E[Compare against fixed parent-owned goldens]

Draft.5 shape

Add validate-outcomes with input fields suite, manifest and outcomes. Suite and manifest use their existing JSON representations in both formats. Only outcomes becomes an Ion-text string for the Ion operation. Admit every declaration and argument before decoding outcomes. The envelope has exactly contractVersion, calls, cleanup and extensions.

{"contractVersion":"0.1.0-draft.5","calls":[
  {"id":"first","outcome":{"status":"returned","value":{"type":"int","value":"42"}}},
  {"id":"second","outcome":{"status":"failed","failure":{"stage":"invoke","code":"provider.crash","message":"Invocation failed"}}}
],"cleanup":{"stage":"cleanup","code":"provider.dispose","message":"Disposal failed"},"extensions":null}
Terminal variantMeaning
returned + typed valueValidate against the selected entry's output. Ordinary typed Result.Err stays returned data.
model-error + enumerated SDK codeOnly the existing five SDK error codes; declaration admission still applies.
failed + failure descriptorAcquire/build/invoke/evaluate/compare failure, with bounded stable code and message. Cleanup remains separate.
cancelledA supplied terminal cancellation claim. The future host adapter must establish authoritative cancellation before producing this variant.

Require one terminal per suite call in exactly the submitted order. Reject missing, duplicate, extra or swapped calls, nonterminal states, contradictory fields and wrong output types. A cleanup error can accompany any terminal inventory, including a fully returned suite; it never replaces or relabels returned values or the primary failure. Do not include a redundant success boolean. Do not mistake an admitted failed envelope for successful execution.

Reuse current 1 MiB input, 1,000-call, strict declaration and typed-value limits. Failure stages are enumerated; codes contain 1–128 UTF-16 units, messages 0–512. Cleanup descriptors require the cleanup stage, which primary failures cannot use. The outcomes contract keeps extensions as opaque encoded Ion: JSON uses the existing binary wrapper; Ion text uses a blob. Require exact bytes matching the admitted suite and preserve them without re-serialization. This does not claim broader binary/reverse-encoding qualification.

Implementation and qualification

Subsequent slices

title: Task 9: End-to-end Scheme → MoonBit and Scheme → Elm
description:
### Task 9: End-to-end Scheme → MoonBit and Scheme → Elm

**Files:**
- Create: `pkgs/morphir-engine/acceptance/inference/moon.pkg`, `pkgs/morphir-engine/acceptance/inference/main.mbt`, `pkgs/morphir-engine/acceptance/inference/corpus.mbt`
- Create: `pkgs/morphir-engine/scripts/test-scheme-inference.mjs`
- Create: `scripts/scheme-moonbit-check.mbtx`, `scripts/scheme-elm-check.mbtx`
- Modify: `.config/mise/config.toml`, `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `pkgs/morphir-engine/README.md`

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: `@engine.infer_unit` (Task 8), `@frontend.compile_file` (Task 7), `@generator.generate` (`finos/morphir-moonbit`, as `pkgs/morphir-moonbit/acceptance/main.mbt` calls it), `@elm.generate` (`finos/morphir-elm/backend`, as `pkgs/morphir-elm/acceptance/main.mbt` calls it).
- Produces: mise tasks `e2e:scheme-moonbit` and `e2e:scheme-elm`.

- [ ] **Step 1: Write the corpus**

`corpus.mbt`:

```moonbit
///|
/// Monomorphic Scheme programs. Each one must fill to concrete types, because the MoonBit generator has no
/// specialization. Pure generics, such as `(define (id x) x)`, are not in the corpus.
let corpus : Array[(String, String)] = [
  ("arithmetic", "(define (inc x) (+ x 1))\n(define (scale x) (* x 2))\n(define (half x) (/ x 2.0))\n(define answer (inc 41))"),
  ("strings", "(define (greet name) (string-append \"Hello, \" name))\n(define greeting (greet \"Morphir\"))"),
  ("lets", "(define (sum-sq a b) (let ((x (* a a)) (y (* b b))) (+ (+ x y) 0)))\n(define (chain a) (let* ((b (+ a 1)) (c (* b 2))) c))"),
  ("conditions", "(define (clamp x) (if (< x 0) 0 (if (> x 100) 100 x)))"),
  ("recursion", "(define (fact n) (if (= n 0) 1 (* n (fact (- n 1)))))\n(define (count n) (letrec ((go (lambda (k acc) (if (= k 0) acc (go (- k 1) (+ acc 1)))))) (go n 0)))"),
  ("lambdas", "(define (apply-twice x) (let ((f (lambda (y) (+ y 1)))) (f (f x))))"),
]
```

Before you go on, check each program with `@frontend.compile_file` and `@typing.infer` in a scratch test: every signature must fill with no type variable. Replace a program that does not fill concretely; do not weaken the check.

- [ ] **Step 2: Write the acceptance main**

`moon.pkg`:

```
pkgtype(kind: "executable")

import {
  "finos/morphir-engine" @engine,
  "finos/morphir-engine/data",
  "finos/morphir-ir" @ir,
  "finos/morphir-scheme/frontend",
  "finos/morphir-moonbit" @generator,
  "finos/morphir-elm/backend" @elm,
  "finos/morphir-typing" @typing,
}
```

`main.mbt` prints one JSON object: `{"moonbit": [{"name", "artifacts": [{"path", "content"}]}], "elm": [{"name", "files": [{"path", "content"}]}]}`. For each corpus entry: `compile_file(source, package_name="scheme/e2e", module_name=name)`; `@engine.infer_unit(@data.IRUnit::new(name, file), Fill, true)`; then `@generator.generate({unit_id: name, ir: unit.distribution, metadata: [], annotations: [], provenance: []})` (copy the exact call shape and the JSON writing of artifacts, with binary content as an array of byte values, from `pkgs/morphir-moonbit/acceptance/main.mbt`) and `@elm.generate(name, unit.distribution, @elm.Options::default())` (copy `project` from `pkgs/morphir-elm/acceptance/main.mbt`). Raise on any failure so that the process exits non-zero.

Run: `moon run pkgs/morphir-engine/acceptance/inference --target native | head -c 400`
Expected: JSON with six MoonBit libraries and six Elm projects.

- [ ] **Step 3: Write the harness**

`pkgs/morphir-engine/scripts/test-scheme-inference.mjs` takes one argument, `moonbit` or `elm`:
- Both: run `moon run pkgs/morphir-engine/acceptance/inference --target native` from the repository root and parse the JSON.
- `elm`: use the Elm binary from `pkgs/morphir-elm/scripts/node_modules` exactly as `pkgs/morphir-elm/scripts/test-elm-make.mjs` does (version check `0.19.1`, `elm make <sources> --output=<null> --report=json` in a temporary directory for each project), and fail with every failing project's report.
- `moonbit`: for each library, make a temporary workspace with `generated/` (the artifacts), a copy of `pkgs/morphir-sdk` as `sdk/` (copy the filter from `pkgs/morphir-moonbit/scripts/test-compiler.mjs`: skip `_build`, `.mooncakes`, `.git`, `node_modules`), and `moon.work` with `members=["./generated","./sdk"]`. Run `$MOON_HOME/bin/moon build --target native` in it (require `MOON_HOME`, as `test-compiler.mjs` does). Fail with the build output of every failing library.
- Print one line for each accepted library or project.

- [ ] **Step 4: Register the tasks**

`scripts/scheme-moonbit-check.mbtx` and `scripts/scheme-elm-check.mbtx`: copy `scripts/elm-make-check.mbtx`. The Elm one runs `npm ci --prefix pkgs/morphir-elm/scripts`, then `node pkgs/morphir-engine/scripts/test-scheme-inference.mjs elm`. The MoonBit one runs only `node pkgs/morphir-engine/scripts/test-scheme-inference.mjs moonbit`.

`.config/mise/config.toml`, after `test:elm`:

```toml
[tasks."e2e:scheme-moonbit"]
description = "Scheme with inference fill to MoonBit: moon build accepts the libraries"
run = "moon run scripts/scheme-moonbit-check.mbtx"

[tasks."e2e:scheme-elm"]
description = "Scheme with inference fill to Elm: elm make accepts the projects"
run = "moon run scripts/scheme-elm-check.mbtx"
```

`.github/workflows/ci.yml`, after the "Check generated Elm projects with elm make" step:

```yaml
      - name: Scheme with inference to MoonBit and Elm
        if: matrix.target == 'native'
        run: |
          mise run e2e:scheme-moonbit
          mise run e2e:scheme-elm
```

If the job sets `MOON_HOME` only for the compiler step, set it for this step the same way (`export MOON_HOME="${MOON_HOME:-$HOME/.moon}"`).

- [ ] **Step 5: Run the tasks**

Run: `MOON_HOME=$HOME/.moon mise run e2e:scheme-moonbit` and `mise run e2e:scheme-elm`
Expected: every library and project is accepted. If one fails, find the cause in inference, in the frontend or in a generator; do not remove the program from the corpus to make the task pass. Record a real generator gap as a follow-up bead and tell the controller.

- [ ] **Step 6: Document**

In `pkgs/morphir-engine/README.md`, add an "End to end" paragraph that names the two tasks and the corpus rule (monomorphic programs only; generic values need the specialization follow-up).

- [ ] **Step 7: Commit**

```bash
moon fmt && moon info
git add pkgs/morphir-engine scripts .config/mise/config.toml .github/workflows/ci.yml
git commit -m "test(engine): check Scheme through inference with moon build and elm make"
```

title: IR type inference Plan 2: engine stage, lineage and Scheme marker — Implementation Plan
description:
# IR type inference Plan 2: engine stage, lineage and Scheme marker — Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** Run language-neutral type inference as an engine stage (`pipeline.inference = off | fill | check`), keep metadata through a fill with marker-aware lineage, and make Scheme source reach the MoonBit and Elm generators with inferred types.

**Architecture:** `finos/morphir-ir` gets the unknown marker API, the logical path grammar and `logical_nodes` (logical paths that do not depend on compact or expanded encoding). The v3 migration marks classic let placeholders. `finos/morphir-typing` treats existing node types as facts in Fill. `finos/morphir-engine/data` builds `fill_lineage` from logical nodes. `finos/morphir-engine` runs the stage after transforms and before the backend. The Scheme frontend writes marked `t-<n>` placeholders and integer literal facts. An acceptance package and two `.mbtx` tasks prove Scheme → MoonBit (`moon build`) and Scheme → Elm (`elm make`).

**Tech Stack:** MoonBit 0.10.14 (moon, `moon check --deny-warn`, `moon test`, `moon fmt`, `moon info`), mise tasks, `.mbtx` scripts, Node.js for the build harnesses, Elm 0.19.1.

**Spec:** bead `morphir-ukvn.5.22.2` design, section 11 (local copy `.dev/beads-specs/morphir-ukvn.5.22.2.md`). Sections 1–10 give the context; where they disagree, section 11 wins.

## Global Constraints

- Branch `DamianReeves/typing-engine-stage`, from `origin/main` (`cebe2fb`, after #60). One PR, one commit for each task.
- Commits use Conventional Commits in plain English. No AI attribution, no `Co-Authored-By`, no `Claude-Session` trailer.
- All suites pass on `wasm`, `wasm-gc`, `js` and `native`. Run `moon` with directory paths, for example `moon test pkgs/morphir-typing --target native`.
- `moon check --deny-warn --target <t>` is clean in every package that a task touches. Do not fix warnings in other packages.
- Run `moon fmt` from the repository root before each commit (it also formats native-only packages).
- After an interface change, run `moon info` from the repository root and commit a changed `pkg.generated.mbti` only if git already tracks it (`git ls-files <path>`). Do not add untracked `pkg.generated.mbti` files.
- `mise run check` passes before the PR is opened.
- New task scripts are standalone `.mbtx` files in `scripts/`, registered in `.config/mise/config.toml`.
- The unknown marker is `TypeAttributes.extensions["morphir.inference"] = Text("unknown")`. Other signature variables are rigid.
- Never use destructive git commands or a bare `git stash`.

## Review Focus

1. A body node with metadata in a `.ion` checkpoint whose compact form becomes expanded after fill: the metadata must stay on the same logical node (Task 6 test "metadata survives compact to expanded", Task 8 test "inference fill on the checkpoint path keeps metadata on its logical nodes").
2. A fill under the default `pipeline.metadata_policy = "retain"` when origins carry metadata: `retain` raises for derived metadata, so the stage must not use the job policy. Ruling: the inference rewrite uses `MetadataPolicy::no_derived()`, which attaches no metadata to derived nodes (section 5: "No metadata is attached to them") (Task 6 and Task 8 tests).
3. A v3 file migrated to v4 and back: the marker on let placeholders must not break the downgrade (`unsupported_attributes_downgrade`) (Task 4 test "classic let placeholders are marked in v4 and the marker is dropped on the way back").
4. A Fill with a partial fact (`List a` where `a` is not in scope): the node gets `List Int`, and no `annotation_mismatch` is reported by the comparison after inference (Task 5 test "partial fact").
5. An invalid `pipeline.inference` value set in a project file: the error names the key and the file (Task 8 test "invalid inference value names its origin").

title: Traceable Morphir and MoonBit naming
description:
# Traceable Morphir and MoonBit naming

Implement the approved naming revision 3 from the A7 design, stored under morphir-ukvn.1.10. Source spelling, semantic identity, requested target spelling and allocated target spelling remain distinct. Default recoverable naming conflicts warn and continue. Ion is the engine checkpoint format; Morphir JSON keeps its existing checked loss boundary. Existing checkpoint identities are preserved on load.
design:
Back to the A7 pipeline design

Naming revision 10 · 9 October 2026

Readable identities, explicit target names

Ordinary public functions keep readable Morphir names. Preserve original source spelling and requested target spelling separately. When a name needs disambiguation, continue automatically with a traceable allocation and an actionable warning.

Task 1 implements readable frontend identities, checked binder allocation and structured warning recovery in squash-merged PR #59 at 8debc0e. Task 2 implements a shared readable target allocator in PR #60, squash merged at 65cc2b8. Task 3 adds declared target-name consumption through explicit host capabilities in PR #61, squash merged at 2a31e76 after review and merge-queue checks; Task 4 landed installed naming qualification in PR #63, squash cebe2fb, with the evidence below. PR #55 qualifies the previous library pipeline.

Keep each name’s purpose clear

Source spelling

is_ready is the exact identifier the author wrote. Preserve it with its source location, even when no target attribute is needed.

Morphir identity

is-ready is a name made of semantic segments. References and public entry selection use the canonical FQName.

Target spelling

is_ready is a MoonBit identifier. A target attribute selects this spelling without changing the Morphir identity.

Normalize source names into words and initialisms using an explicit frontend policy. Keep simple names such as eligible unchanged. Follow the v4 distinction between a word and an initialism, such as usd and USD. Canonical parsing stays strict; source normalization is a separate operation.

Use the upstream targetNames fact

The linked-metadata design already gives this naming example. A scoped @context maps the readable key targetNames to a declared predicate Node URI. Its @json coercion makes the entire frontend/backend record one typed fact.

{
  node_id: "value:example:main#ready",
  data: morphir_linked_metadata_v1::{
    document: "morphir://ir/pkg/example/annotations?format=4.1.0#/distribution",
    '$meta': {
      '@context': {
        targetNames: {
          '@id': "morphir://ir/pkg/morphir/naming?format=4.1.0#/module/naming/value/target-names",
          '@type': "@json"
        }
      },
      '@graph': [{
        '@id': "morphir://ir/pkg/example?format=4.0.0#/module/main/value/ready",
        targetNames: {
          frontend: { moonbit: "isReady" },
          backend: { moonbit: "chosen" }
        }
      }]
    }
  }
}

The annotation selects the current engine adapter. The local holder, containing assertion document and semantic subject stay separate. ValueDefinition names use the explicit-subject document graph. Current subjects use their input's exact 4.0 release; selecting a provider at 4.1 does not add native 4.1 codec support.

The frontend map retains the language-specific input spelling. The MoonBit backend consumes the resolved predicate’s backend.moonbit as an explicit request. Without that request, it may use frontend.moonbit as a readable allocation hint when the source language matches the target language. A hint can be adapted for target constraints; an explicit request keeps its exact spelling. Cross-language generation renders the semantic name and retains source spelling for traceability. Both maps are string-keyed Dict String String; moonbit is the language ID, independent of compiler profile. Both fields are required by the upstream closed record, with an empty map when no spelling is supplied. Language IDs follow ^[a-z][a-z0-9]*(?:-[a-z0-9]+)*$.

The generator validates the record, language IDs, target identifier and symbol collisions before consuming the request. It matches the expanded predicate identity, not the literal alias targetNames. Unsupported predicates and missing interpretation support remain preserved and explicitly unvalidated. Storage and a matching context digest alone do not prove trusted semantics. A known naming request that generation requires must fail if its required validation or interpreter is unavailable; it must not silently fall back to another spelling.

@targetName or @moonbit.targetName may remain an ergonomic source spelling if source syntax is added later. They would lower into this declared targetNames fact; the previous standalone attributes["moonbit.targetName"] map is superseded as the semantic contract. No source annotation syntax is currently admitted by the Boolean frontend.

The generator’s symbol table records the actual allocated spelling and any escape reason separately. Generation must preserve the authored request, its assertion owner and source origins. Keep original spelling, requested spelling and allocated spelling as distinct fields. An automatic allocation must not overwrite the authored targetNames fact. Missing source spelling is valid for imported or synthesized IR; use its semantic name and available lineage instead of inventing an original spelling.

Let the host admit the declaration provider

Task 3 selects morphir/naming:naming#target-names at native format 4.1.0. Its public ValueDefinition must return a closed frontend/backend record, both Dict String String. Its own native document graph declares subject-role = ValueDefinition, object-form = data and interpreter = target-name-language-ids through the built-in morphir/metadata schema vocabulary.

Explicit capability boundary

The engine has no signed-Library restore service today. Applications pass metadata_capabilities to the generator or Engine::new. That host callback must freshly authenticate and restore the signed Library, then derive its supported semantic projection, native metadata and revision from the same bytes. The consumer checks the provider's declaration and requested revision. Neither metadata, source claims, a digest nor an ambient registry installs trust. The binding is selected here; this repository does not claim a signed provider release.

Default capabilities are unavailable. The installed CLI preserves naming payloads in Ion checkpoints, but known naming facts fail clearly during generation until a host integrates authenticated restoration. The test host simulates this boundary and is never the default provider. Native 4.1, extension transport and upstream MCK qualification remain separate.

sequenceDiagram
  participant Input as Authored Ion checkpoint
  participant Adapter as Scoped fact adapter
  participant Host as Explicit host capability
  participant Names as Shared allocator
  Input->>Adapter: Retain holder, document, subject and authored data
  Adapter->>Adapter: Expand context and check closed record
  Adapter->>Host: Fresh authenticated provider restore
  Host-->>Adapter: Library projection, native facts and verified revision
  Adapter->>Adapter: Check declaration and required interpreter
  alt Known request cannot be admitted
    Adapter-->>Input: Error with owner and fix, no generated artifacts
  else Admission succeeds
    Adapter->>Names: Exact backend.moonbit request and assertion receipts
    Names->>Names: Reserve requests before automatic candidates
    Names-->>Input: Source, references, driver and symbol manifest agree
  end

The first supported subject role is a current, unpinned ValueDefinition in the input Library. Scoped aliases, compact prefixes, protected bindings and bounded context imports follow the upstream grammar. Context files require an explicit host loader with a confined root and symlink checks; the core checks exact SHA-256 bytes, cycles, repeated resources and import collisions. A metadata-supplied file base cannot widen the accepted root.

Equal assertions keep separate carrier and document receipts. Contradictory records fail; there is no last-writer rule. Unknown syntactically valid predicates remain authored and explicitly unvalidated. assertionSources selectors must match this document's expanded assertions and carry one complete source set. Receipts retain original, requested, candidate and allocated names separately. Read the checked adapter contract and host responsibilities.

Allocate names once, then reuse the mapping

Task 2 implementation · moonbit-readable-targets-v1

The portable generator defaults to readable values, nominal types, constructors, fields and locals. Usable same-language source spellings are hints; other inputs render semantic names. Reserve the complete namespace before allocation. Flattened collisions receive module qualifiers; keywords receive _value. Occupied recovery spellings receive _source_<token>, starting with four UTF-8 owner bytes in hex, extending one byte at a time, then a checked decimal ordinal.

Declarations, references, field access, invocation entries, drivers and the Ion symbol manifest share one mapping. Function-local namespaces are independent. Reserve user and visible global names before allocating argument, function and record temporaries. Receipts retain original hints, candidates, final spellings and reasons; structured warnings include final allocations for all related owners and source spans when available. Engine strict mode rejects naming recoveries before publication. Unknown metadata and origins stay unchanged.

[backends.moonbit] naming = "legacy-hex" retains the earlier exported ABI; "readable" is the default. Existing checkpoint identities are preserved without reverse-decoding. Synthetic structural-record type keys, private codec keys and generated package identity remain encoded. Aliases are lowered into their underlying type. Task 3 extends the same map with exact declared requests. Legacy mode selects automatic rendering; explicit requests retain their exact spelling in either mode.

Open the SVG diagram and export controls. The graph describes proposed behavior.

  1. Collect declarations and resolve their original spellings to owners before lowering references. Normalize semantic names across public and private declarations within each actual identity namespace.
  2. Keep unambiguous declarations readable. A normalization collision emits a warning and allocates distinct identities automatically. Each allocated name retains its readable base; its receipt maps back to the exact source spelling and location. A target attribute cannot repair an already merged semantic identity.
  3. Resolve local variables lexically before rendering. Give shadowed binders distinct identities and reserve user names before creating temporary names. Fresh names derive from the original binder or expression role, such as ready_shadow_1 or ready_equality_left_1. Use a deterministic scope-local discriminator when needed and retain the originating binder or expression in lineage. Routine hygienic freshening does not produce warning noise.
  4. Validate and reserve explicit target requests first. Reject invalid identifiers and contradictory requests with both owners and a fix. Automatic candidates work around these reservations. A declaration with no explicit request can use its same-language original spelling as a hint, then its semantic rendering as a fallback.
  5. For automatic candidates, qualify a conflicting flat-package symbol by module or owner first. Add a readable role or short discriminator only where necessary. Keyword or unsupported-name escapes and unexpected user-name collisions produce warnings with the final allocation. Expected temporary allocation does not.
  6. Use one immutable allocation result for declarations, references, invocation descriptors, generated drivers and symbol manifests. Never reconstruct names independently. Record naming-policy version and allocation reasons in provenance.
Default recovery policy

Recoverable naming conflicts warn and continue. The optional strict_naming=true API argument or pipeline.strict_naming=true engine configuration promotes these warnings to errors before publication. Source semantics, visibility and lexical binding must survive either policy. Contradictory exact target requests and unavailable required metadata validation remain errors.

Proposed deterministic declaration policy: reserve all unambiguous normalized identities, then choose the canonical snake-case source spelling as the plain-name owner within a collision group. If none exists, choose by exact UTF-8 spelling order. Other owners receive <readable-base>-source-<token>, with the token derived from the original spelling. Check every candidate against reserved identities and the whole group. Extend the discriminator on a collision; a digest alone never proves uniqueness. This selection is independent of declaration order. Task 1 freezes moonbit-readable-names-v1: the token is the first four UTF-8 bytes encoded as lowercase hexadecimal. Extend by one byte until unique, then add a checked decimal counter if the full spelling is still occupied. The token is a discriminator, not a digest. Golden tests cover occupied suffixes and source-order changes. Adding a new conflicting declaration may change an earlier allocation and must be reported as a public-name compatibility change.

Make the rules observable

CaseMorphir identityTarget behavior
eligibleeligibleReadable default. No attribute required when the renderer returns the desired spelling.

A known naming request that generation requires must fail if its required validation or interpreter is unavailable; it must not silently fall back to another spelling.

They would lower into this declared targetNames fact; the previous standalone attributes["moonbit.targetName"] map is superseded as the semantic contract. No source annotation syntax is currently admitted by the Boolean frontend.

The generator’s symbol table records the actual allocated spelling and any escape reason separately. Generation must preserve the authored request, its assertion owner and source origins. Missing source spelling is valid for imported or synthesized IR; use its semantic name and available lineage instead of inventing an original spelling.

Allocate names once, then reuse the mapping

Task 2 implementation · moonbit-readable-targets-v1
