- A type that came from an annotation keeps its alias references. Other types are written expanded.
- Generalized variables are named in traversal order: `a`, `b`, …, and class name plus letter (`comparableA`) for

### Problem

Node identities are JSON pointers into the v4 encoding (`@identities.nodes`). The writer uses compact forms when

node identities. `apply_rewrite` refuses a rewrite with no lineage (`data.lineage_required`).

- **`@identities.logical_nodes(unit_id, file)`:** returns each node's logical path, which does not depend on the
  encoding (for example `value:pkg:mod#name/body/apply/arg/0`), paired with its JSON-pointer id.
- **`@data.attribute_lineage(before : IRUnit, after : IRFile) -> Lineage`:**
  - It checks that the two trees are equal apart from attributes. If they are not, it refuses with
    `data.not_attribute_only`.
  - It joins nodes by logical path to build `retained` pairs.

- Any attribute-only pass can use this.

  error, reported with its provenance.

- **Plain backends:** the IR is replaced.
- **Checkpoint and generator path:** the IR goes through `apply_rewrite` with `attribute_lineage` and the job's
  metadata policy. Data inputs that carry metadata (`.ion`, `.ionb`) are covered.
- **Dependencies:** the specifications are the built-in SDK plus the distribution's `Dependencies`.

| --- | --- |

## 9. Amendments (Plan 1, 2026-10-07)

Where this section and the sections above disagree, this section wins.

   `parse_program_located`, which returns `Located` trees with character offsets. `SpecError` converts an offset to

   `Specs` distribution and decodes it once, on first use. That is simpler than generating MoonBit constructors,
   and it keeps the module free of any Scheme dependency.

   `finos/morphir-typing-tools`. Putting them in a published module would add a filesystem dependency
   (`moonbitlang/x`), and `finos/morphir-typing` would gain test dependencies on the fixture modules.

   typing reuse it.

## 1. Purpose and context

This is sub-project 2 of the Elm initiative (umbrella epic `morphir-ukvn.5.22`). It is built Morphir-first. Type
inference is a language-neutral Morphir capability, and every frontend and input uses it through the engine. The Elm

Producers that do not know their types cannot use typed backends today. The MoonBit generator refuses IR without

fails. The repository has no IR specification of the Morphir SDK. The only machine-readable SDK signatures are the
248 morphir-elm `vSpec` strings in `pkgs/morphir-sdk/conformance/bindings.json`.

### Success criteria

- **A, backend-ready types:** every `Value` and `Pattern` in a well-typed module gets a correct, fully applied
  `inferred_type`. An ill-typed module gets diagnostics with logical node paths.
- **B, parity with morphir-elm:** for the classic v1, v2 and v3 fixtures with their types stripped, the inferred
  types equal the types `morphir-elm make` wrote. Equality is up to alias expansion and renaming of type variables.
- **C, checking:** in check mode, the pass checks existing types and reports every disagreement.
- Scheme source with inference set to `fill` and the `moonbit` generator gives a library that `moon build` accepts.
  The same source with the `elm` generator gives projects that `elm make` accepts.
- All suites pass on `wasm`, `wasm-gc`, `js` and `native`.

| Unit | Module and package | Responsibility | Depends on |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Spec notation | `finos/morphir-scheme/spec` (new package) | Reads and writes the specification notation (section 3) to and from `@ir.PackageSpecification`. | `finos/morphir-scheme` reader, `finos/morphir-ir` |
| SDK specification | `pkgs/morphir-sdk-spec/sdk.scm` (source of truth); `finos/morphir-sdk-spec` (new module, generated v4 JSON) | `sdk_specification() -> @ir.PackageSpecification` for `morphir/SDK`. No Scheme runtime at use time. | `finos/morphir-ir` only. The runtime SDK `finos/morphir-sdk` keeps no dependencies (amendment 10). |

| Logical node paths | `finos/morphir-ir/identities` | `logical_nodes(unit_id, file) -> Array[(LogicalPath, String)]` | existing |
| Attribute lineage | `finos/morphir-engine/data` | `attribute_lineage(before, after) -> Lineage` for any rewrite that changes only attributes | existing |

- A bootstrap script, run once, turns the 248 `bindings.json` signatures into the first `sdk.scm`.

The notation is data. It is read with the Morphir Scheme reader and never evaluated. Each file holds one package.

(package "morphir/SDK"

    (type bool (custom (true) (false)))
    (type order (custom (lt) (eq) (gt)))
    (val add ((a number) (b number)) number)
    (val compose-left ((g (-> b c)) (f (-> a b)) (x a)) c)
    (val compare ((a comparable) (b comparable)) #order))
  (module list
    (type list (opaque) a)
    (type predicate (alias (-> a basics#bool)) a)
    (val map ((f (-> a b)) (list (#list a))) (#list b))
    (val foldl ((f (-> a b b)) (z b) (list (#list a))) b)))

| --- | --- |

| `(doc "text")` | Documentation for the module or the item that contains it. |
| `(type name body param…)` | A type specification. The trailing params are type variables. |
| `(val name ((arg type)…) result)` | A value specification. The inputs keep their order. `val` (not `def`) because a specification is a signature, not a definition. |
| `(annotation fqname arg…)` | A v4 annotation inside `type` or `val`. Arguments are data only. |

Type bodies: `(opaque)`, `(alias type)`, `(custom (ctor type…)…)`, `(derived base from-fqname to-fqname)`.

| --- | --- |

3. **The SDK specification is embedded as JSON.** `finos/morphir-sdk/spec` holds generated canonical v4 JSON of a
   `Specs` distribution and decodes it once, on first use. That is simpler than generating MoonBit constructors,
   and it keeps the module free of any Scheme dependency.
4. **Tooling home.** The bootstrap, generator and checker, and the oracle tests, live in the unpublished module
   `finos/morphir-typing-tools`. Putting them in a published module would add a filesystem dependency
   (`moonbitlang/x`), and `finos/morphir-typing` would gain test dependencies on the fixture modules.
5. **Callers supply the SDK.** `finos/morphir-typing` has no built-in SDK, because it depends only on
   `finos/morphir-ir`. Callers add `@sdk_spec.sdk_specification()` to the dependency map. In Plan 2 the engine does
   this; in this plan the tools module does.
6. **Logical paths are defined here and moved in Plan 2.** The logical path grammar is defined in

   typing reuse it.
7. **Errors stop the pass.** `infer` raises `InferenceFailed(Array[InferenceProblem])` when any problem exists, in
   either mode. The problems are collected across every binding group first.

   check matches `bindings.json` names through the same canonicalization the Elm mapping generator uses: split camel
   case and digit runs, then apply the `Name::from_words` initialism rule.

## 10. Amendments (execution and review, 2026-10-07)

Where this section and the sections above disagree, this section wins.

### SDK specification module

The SDK specification lives in its own module, `finos/morphir-sdk-spec`, in `pkgs/morphir-sdk-spec`. It is not a

- Check mode, fill's comparison of existing types, and the oracle use a declaration-scoped equivalence: one variable

- `sdkgen check` compares constraint classes.

  leaf.

1. **Lineage of filled signatures.** Fill replaces signature types that carry the unknown marker. Signature types are
   tree content, not attributes, so `attribute_lineage` as written in section 5 would refuse them. Decide how the
   lineage treats replaced signature types: as derived nodes, or with a separate signature rewrite step.
2. **Scheme marker names.** The Scheme frontend writes one placeholder name, `scheme-value`, for every input and
   output. Under the marker rule, one name is one variable, so all positions collapse to a single type. The Scheme

# IR type inference: design

Date: 2026-10-07. Status: approved; Plan 1 merged (#52, #58). Section 11 (Plan 2 design) is waiting for review.

## 1. Purpose and context

This is sub-project 2 of the Elm initiative (umbrella epic `morphir-ukvn.5.22`). It is built Morphir-first. Type
inference is a language-neutral Morphir capability, and every frontend and input uses it through the engine. The Elm
frontend (`morphir-ukvn.5.22.3`) is one consumer. It gets no private shortcut.

Producers that do not know their types cannot use typed backends today. The MoonBit generator refuses IR without
`inferred_type`. The Scheme frontend writes only the placeholder type variable `scheme-value`, so Scheme to MoonBit
fails. The repository has no IR specification of the Morphir SDK. The only machine-readable SDK signatures are the
248 morphir-elm `vSpec` strings in `pkgs/morphir-sdk/conformance/bindings.json`.

### Success criteria

- **A, backend-ready types:** every `Value` and `Pattern` in a well-typed module gets a correct, fully applied
  `inferred_type`. An ill-typed module gets diagnostics with logical node paths.
- **B, parity with morphir-elm:** for the classic v1, v2 and v3 fixtures with their types stripped, the inferred
  types equal the types `morphir-elm make` wrote. Equality is up to alias expansion and renaming of type variables.
- **C, checking:** in check mode, the pass checks existing types and reports every disagreement.
- Scheme source with inference set to `fill` and the `moonbit` generator gives a library that `moon build` accepts.
  The same source with the `elm` generator gives projects that `elm make` accepts.
- All suites pass on `wasm`, `wasm-gc`, `js` and `native`.

## 2. Architecture

| Unit | Module and package | Responsibility | Depends on |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Spec notation | `finos/morphir-scheme/spec` (new package) | Reads and writes the specification notation (section 3) to and from `@ir.PackageSpecification`. | `finos/morphir-scheme` reader, `finos/morphir-ir` |
| SDK specification | `pkgs/morphir-sdk-spec/sdk.scm` (source of truth); `finos/morphir-sdk-spec` (new module, generated v4 JSON) | `sdk_specification() -> @ir.PackageSpecification` for `morphir/SDK`. No Scheme runtime at use time. | `finos/morphir-ir` only. The runtime SDK `finos/morphir-sdk` keeps no dependencies (amendment 10). |
| Inference core | `finos/morphir-typing` (new module, `pkgs/morphir-typing`) | `infer` in fill and check modes (section 4) | `finos/morphir-ir` only |
| Logical node paths | `finos/morphir-ir/identities` | `logical_nodes(unit_id, file) -> Array[(LogicalPath, String)]` | existing |
| Attribute lineage | `finos/morphir-engine/data` | `attribute_lineage(before, after) -> Lineage` for any rewrite that changes only attributes | existing |
| Engine stage | `finos/morphir-engine` | `pipeline.inference = "off" \| "fill" \| "check"` | `finos/morphir-typing`, `finos/morphir-sdk/spec` |
| Scheme frontend | `finos/morphir-scheme/frontend` | Writes the unknown marker (section 4) on its placeholder types | — |

Tooling:
- A bootstrap script, run once, turns the 248 `bindings.json` signatures into the first `sdk.scm`.
- A `.mbtx` script regenerates `finos/morphir-sdk/spec` from `sdk.scm`.
- New task and automation scripts are standalone `.mbtx` files in `scripts/`, registered in
  `.config/mise/config.toml`, as `.github/AGENTS.md` requires.

Delivery is one spec with two plans:
1. Notation, SDK specification and inference core, including the classic-corpus oracle.
2. Logical paths, attribute lineage, the engine stage, the Scheme marker and end-to-end acceptance.

Out of scope: the Elm frontend; macros in the notation; type classes beyond Elm's four built-in constraints.
Inference across a package whose specification is missing is also out of scope; it is a diagnostic.

## 3. Specification notation

The notation is data. It is read with the Morphir Scheme reader and never evaluated. Each file holds one package.
Line comments, block comments and datum comments are allowed.

```scheme
(package "morphir/SDK"
  (module basics
    (type bool (custom (true) (false)))
    (type order (custom (lt) (eq) (gt)))
    (val add ((a number) (b number)) number)
    (val compose-left ((g (-> b c)) (f (-> a b)) (x a)) c)
    (val compare ((a comparable) (b comparable)) #order))
  (module list
    (type list (opaque) a)
    (type predicate (alias (-> a basics#bool)) a)
    (val map ((f (-> a b)) (list (#list a))) (#list b))
    (val foldl ((f (-> a b b)) (z b) (list (#list a))) b)))
```

### Forms

| Form | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `(package "pkg/path" module…)` | A `PackageSpecification`. The name is a canonical `Path`. |
| `(module name item…)` | A `ModuleSpecification`. The name is a canonical module path, for example `json/encode`. |
| `(doc "text")` | Documentation for the module or the item that contains it. |
| `(type name body param…)` | A type specification. The trailing params are type variables. |
| `(val name ((arg type)…) result)` | A value specification. The inputs keep their order. `val` (not `def`) because a specification is a signature, not a definition. |
| `(annotation fqname arg…)` | A v4 annotation inside `type` or `val`. Arguments are data only. |

Type bodies: `(opaque)`, `(alias type)`, `(custom (ctor type…)…)`, `(derived base from-fqname to-fqname)`.

### Type expressions

| Syntax | IR |
| --- | --- |
| A bare symbol, for example `a` or `comparable` | `Variable`. A `number`, `comparable`, `appendable` or `compappend` prefix also writes `TypeAttributes.constraints.typeclass`. |
| `#name`, `module#name`, `pkg:module#name` | A `Reference` in the same module, the same package, or any package |
| `(#name t…)`, `(module#name t…)`, `(pkg:module#name t…)` | A `Reference` with arguments, for example `(#list a)` |
| `(-> a b c)` | A curried `Function`, `a -> b -> c`. N-ary, right-associative. |
| `(tuple a b …)` | `Tuple` |
| `(record (field t)…)` | `Record` |
| `(record r (field t)…)` | `ExtensibleRecord` over `r` |
| `()` | `Unit` |

- Names follow the v4 canonical rules (`less-than`, `map-2`, `LT`) and are parsed with `Name::parse`. A name that is
  not canonical is refused.
- A head symbol that ends in `!` is reserved for macros, which a later pre-pass will expand into plain data. Until
  then the reader refuses it.
- A canonical printer always writes the same layout, and always the flat `->` form. For canonical input,
  read → print → read gives the same text.
- Errors are `SpecError { line, column, message }`.

## 4. Inference semantics

### Interface

`infer(file : IRFile, deps : Map[PackageName, PackageSpecification], mode : Fill | Check) -> Result`

- `morphir/SDK` is built in.
- `Library` dependencies come from its `Dependencies`.
- `Application` dependencies are derived from the dependency definitions it bundles.
- **Fill** returns IR in which every `Value` and `Pattern` has `inferred_type`. Signature types that carry the
  unknown marker are replaced by their solutions.
- **Check** returns the IR unchanged, plus diagnostics.

### Unknown marker

- A type variable whose `TypeAttributes.extensions` holds `"morphir.inference": "unknown"` is unknown. Inference may
  solve it to any type.
- Every other variable in a declared signature is rigid (a skolem), as in an Elm annotation.
- Classic IR has no markers, so it is checked strictly.
- The Scheme frontend writes the marker. The Elm frontend will write it for values without an annotation.

### Algorithm

Constraint-based Hindley-Milner, in the manner of morphir-elm's `Morphir.Type.Infer`: meta variables, union-find
substitution and an occurs check.

- **Top-level values:** they are grouped into strongly connected components across the package's modules, and the
  components are solved in dependency order.
- **Fully declared values:** a value whose signature has no unknown markers is used through its generalized scheme
  everywhere. This permits polymorphic recursion.
- **Values with unknowns:** inside a component they are monomorphic, and they are generalized afterwards.
- `LetDefinition` generalizes, which is let-polymorphism. `LetRecursion` is one group.
- If the body would narrow a rigid variable, the error is `rigid_variable`.

### Constraint classes

These apply to variables. They come from the name prefix or from `typeclass`, and they propagate through
unification.

| Class | Satisfied by |
| --- | --- |
| `number` | `Int`, `Float` |
| `comparable` | `Int`, `Float`, `Char`, `String`, `List c`, tuples of up to 3 comparables |
| `appendable` | `String`, `List a` |
| `compappend` | `String`, `List c` |

- `comparable` with `appendable` gives `compappend`.
- `number` with `comparable` gives `number`.
- Any other combination is `no_instance`.
- `Decimal` and `LocalDate` belong to no class.

### Literals

| Literal | Type |
| --- | --- |
| Integer | A fresh `number` variable |
| Float | `Float` |
| Decimal | `decimal#decimal` |
| String | `String` |
| Char | `Char` |
| Bool | `Bool` |
| Document | `Document` when the SDK defines it; otherwise `unsupported` |

### Records

`Record` and `ExtensibleRecord` unify through row variables.

| Value | Type rule |
| --- | --- |
| `Field(v, f)` | `v : { ρ \| f : α }` |
| `FieldFunction f` | `{ ρ \| f : α } -> α` |
| `UpdateRecord` | Keeps its target's type and constrains each field it sets |
| Record literal | Closed |

### Nominal types

Aliases expand during unification. Opaque and custom types are nominal. A constructor has the type
`args -> T params`.

### Other bodies

- `NativeBody` and `IncompleteBody` use their signature as declared.
- `ExternalBody` checks its fallback value against the signature.
- A `Hole` uses its declared type if present, otherwise a fresh variable.

### Output

- A type that came from an annotation keeps its alias references. Other types are written expanded.
- Generalized variables are named in traversal order: `a`, `b`, …, and class name plus letter (`comparableA`) for
  constrained variables. The output is deterministic.

## 5. Lineage and the engine stage

### Problem

Node identities are JSON pointers into the v4 encoding (`@identities.nodes`). The writer uses compact forms when
attributes are empty, for example a `TuplePattern` written as a tag plus an array. Filling `inferred_type` switches
such a node to its expanded form, which moves the pointers of its children. Attribute-only changes therefore move
node identities. `apply_rewrite` refuses a rewrite with no lineage (`data.lineage_required`).

### General solution

- **`@identities.logical_nodes(unit_id, file)`:** returns each node's logical path, which does not depend on the
  encoding (for example `value:pkg:mod#name/body/apply/arg/0`), paired with its JSON-pointer id.
- **`@data.attribute_lineage(before : IRUnit, after : IRFile) -> Lineage`:**
  - It checks that the two trees are equal apart from attributes. If they are not, it refuses with
    `data.not_attribute_only`.
  - It joins nodes by logical path to build `retained` pairs.
  - It records new attribute nodes, such as those under each `inferredType`, as `derived` from their owner. No
    metadata is attached to them.
- Any attribute-only pass can use this.

### Engine stage

- **Setting:** `pipeline.inference` takes `off` (default), `fill` or `check`. Any other value is a configuration
  error, reported with its provenance.
- **Position:** after the frontend and the transforms, before the backend, on every path.
- **Plain backends:** the IR is replaced.
- **Checkpoint and generator path:** the IR goes through `apply_rewrite` with `attribute_lineage` and the job's
  metadata policy. Data inputs that carry metadata (`.ion`, `.ionb`) are covered.
- **Dependencies:** the specifications are the built-in SDK plus the distribution's `Dependencies`.

## 6. Diagnostics

`InferenceProblem { code, node : LogicalPath, message, expected : Type?, found : Type?, source : SourceLocation? }`

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `type_mismatch` | Two types do not unify |
| `occurs` | Infinite type |
| `rigid_variable` | A body narrows an annotated variable |
| `no_instance` | No type satisfies the constraint class |
| `missing_field` | The record has no such field |
| `unknown_reference` | The reference is not defined or specified |
| `missing_dependency` | No specification for the referenced package |
| `arity` | Wrong number of arguments |
| `annotation_mismatch` | An existing `inferred_type` disagrees with inference (check mode) |
| `unsupported` | A construct inference does not handle |

- In the engine, each problem becomes a `Diagnostic` at stage `"inference"`. The message holds the code, the
  logical path, the expected and found types, and the source location.
- Each binding group stops at its first error. Other groups and modules continue.

## 7. Testing

### Notation

- Read → print → read gives the same result.
- Refusals: an unknown form, a non-canonical name, a reserved `!` head, a `val` with the wrong shape. Each refusal
  reports its line and column.
- Every type form maps to the expected IR.

### SDK specification

- Every one of the 248 `bindings.json` signatures, parsed from its `vSpec`, equals the matching `sdk.scm` entry, up
  to renaming of type variables. A missing or extra binding fails.
- The generated package is fresh.
- The hand-written types and constructors are spot-checked: `Maybe`, `Result`, `Order`, `Bool`, `List`, `Dict`,
  `Set`, `Char`, `String`, `Int`, `Float`, `Decimal`, `LocalDate`.

### Inference rules

There is a unit test for each of these:
- literals, application, lambdas;
- let-polymorphism, `LetRecursion`, component order;
- polymorphic recursion with annotations, rigid variables, the unknown marker;
- each class and each class combination;
- records: access, field functions, updates, rows, `missing_field`;
- aliases, opaque types, constructors;
- native, external and incomplete bodies, and holes;
- every diagnostic code, determinism, and the naming of variables.

### Oracle (criterion B)

- Classic v1, v2 and v3 fixtures: migrate, strip all `inferred_type` and signature types, fill, then compare.
- The same check runs over the Elm backend fixtures, the MoonBit fixtures and the Scheme corpus.

### Check mode (criterion C)

- Every classic fixture passes unchanged.
- In each fixture, one changed `inferred_type` is reported as `annotation_mismatch` at its node.

### Lineage

- Metadata survives when a compact node becomes an expanded one.
- A change to the tree shape is refused.

### Engine

- `pipeline.inference` is validated.
- `fill` works on a plain backend, and on the checkpoint path with `.ion` metadata, which stays on the same logical
  nodes.
- `check` turns problems into diagnostics.
- `off` leaves the IR unchanged.

### End to end

- Scheme with `fill` and `moonbit`: `moon build` accepts the library.
- Scheme with `fill` and `elm`: `elm make` accepts the projects.
- Both run as `.mbtx` mise tasks in CI.

## 8. Follow-ups

- Macros in the notation (`!`-headed forms).
- Decide whether `[backends.moonbit]` options should be strict (ruling 12 of the Elm backend work).
- The Elm frontend (`morphir-ukvn.5.22.3`) consumes this pass through the engine stage.

## 9. Amendments (Plan 1, 2026-10-07)

Where this section and the sections above disagree, this section wins.


1. **No `#name` reference form.** The Morphir Scheme reader rejects any token that starts with `#` other than its
   own literals (`reader.mbt`: "Unknown reader token"). Accepting `#list` would change the Scheme language for every
   program. References are therefore written `module#name` (the same package) or `pkg:module#name` (any package),
   for example `(list#list a)` and `basics#order`.
2. **Positions come from a new reader entry point.** `parse_program` returns `Datum` with no positions. Task 1 adds
   `parse_program_located`, which returns `Located` trees with character offsets. `SpecError` converts an offset to
   a line and column. `parse_program` is unchanged.
3. **The SDK specification is embedded as JSON.** `finos/morphir-sdk/spec` holds generated canonical v4 JSON of a
   `Specs` distribution and decodes it once, on first use. That is simpler than generating MoonBit constructors,
   and it keeps the module free of any Scheme dependency.
4. **Tooling home.** The bootstrap, generator and checker, and the oracle tests, live in the unpublished module
   `finos/morphir-typing-tools`. Putting them in a published module would add a filesystem dependency
   (`moonbitlang/x`), and `finos/morphir-typing` would gain test dependencies on the fixture modules.
5. **Callers supply the SDK.** `finos/morphir-typing` has no built-in SDK, because it depends only on
   `finos/morphir-ir`. Callers add `@sdk_spec.sdk_specification()` to the dependency map. In Plan 2 the engine does
   this; in this plan the tools module does.
6. **Logical paths are defined here and moved in Plan 2.** The logical path grammar is defined in
   `finos/morphir-typing/paths.mbt`. Plan 2 moves it to `finos/morphir-ir/identities` (`logical_nodes`) and makes
   typing reuse it.
7. **Errors stop the pass.** `infer` raises `InferenceFailed(Array[InferenceProblem])` when any problem exists, in
   either mode. The problems are collected across every binding group first.
8. **Canonical SDK names.** `sdk.scm` uses migrated canonical names (`map-2`, `from-int-8`, `LT`). The conformance
   check matches `bindings.json` names through the same canonicalization the Elm mapping generator uses: split camel
   case and digit runs, then apply the `Name::from_words` initialism rule.

## 10. Amendments (execution and review, 2026-10-07)

Where this section and the sections above disagree, this section wins.

### SDK specification module

The SDK specification lives in its own module, `finos/morphir-sdk-spec`, in `pkgs/morphir-sdk-spec`. It is not a
package of `finos/morphir-sdk`. Generated MoonBit libraries compile against `finos/morphir-sdk` alone, in a frozen

`sdk.scm` also declares `local-date`. Where `bindings.json` gives one value the same parameter name twice

### Criterion B oracle

Criterion B keeps the top-level signatures. It strips every node `inferred_type`, and every let-definition
placeholder signature. Classic IR does not separate annotated top-level signatures from inferred ones. Stripping them
gives correctly more general types, so a full strip cannot be the oracle.

### Criterion A oracle

Criterion A uses a full strip: signatures and node types. It also requires each original corpus to pass `Check`
unchanged.

### Classic let placeholders

morphir-elm writes `t-<digits>` variables as the signatures of lets with no annotation, and never rewrites them.
Inference reads these variables as rigid. The oracle marks them as unknown. The typing README documents that callers
must do the same.

### Soundness and checking

- Signature rigids belong to their declaration. Inside inference they are keyed `<decl-key>|<name>`, and output
  strips the owner. This closes a soundness hole in groups of undeclared values that share a variable name.
- Check mode, fill's comparison of existing types, and the oracle use a declaration-scoped equivalence: one variable
  bijection per declaration, signature rigids fixed, class sets compared.
- `sdkgen check` compares constraint classes.
- An unknown `typeclass` name is `unsupported`.
- `rigid_variable` comes from the solver whenever a body narrows a rigid. That includes class failures at a rigid
  leaf.

### Open questions for Plan 2

These must be settled in the Plan 2 design before planning starts:

1. **Lineage of filled signatures.** Fill replaces signature types that carry the unknown marker. Signature types are
   tree content, not attributes, so `attribute_lineage` as written in section 5 would refuse them. Decide how the
   lineage treats replaced signature types: as derived nodes, or with a separate signature rewrite step.
2. **Scheme marker names.** The Scheme frontend writes one placeholder name, `scheme-value`, for every input and
   output. Under the marker rule, one name is one variable, so all positions collapse to a single type. The Scheme
   marker step must write a distinct name for each position.
3. **Classic placeholders.** Decide whether migration from classic IR to v4 marks `t-<digits>` let placeholders for
   all callers.

## 11. Amendments (Plan 2 design, 2026-10-09)

Where this section and the sections above disagree, this section wins. It settles the open questions of section 10
and gives the Plan 2 design. Plan 2 starts from `main` at `65cc2b8` (after #58, #59 and #60).

### Q1: one marker-aware rewrite

- `@data.attribute_lineage` is replaced by `@data.fill_lineage(before : IRUnit, after : IRFile) -> Lineage`.
- `before` and `after` must be equal apart from attributes and apart from the variables of `before` that carry the
  unknown marker. Any other difference is refused with `data.not_attribute_only`.
- Nodes are joined by logical path. A joined node is `retained`.
- A marker variable that inference replaced keeps its id: the root of its replacement is `retained` from it. The new
  nodes under the replacement are `derived` from the marker variable node.
- Every new attribute node, such as those under each `inferredType`, is `derived` from its owner node.
- One fill is one `apply_rewrite` with one provenance record, component `"inference"`.

### Q2: distinct Scheme placeholder names

- The Scheme frontend writes `t-0`, `t-1`, … in place of `scheme-value`. The names are numbered in traversal order and
  counted for each declaration. Every placeholder carries the unknown marker.
- This is the same form that the oracle's `strip_full` writes. The marker rule does not change: one name is one
  variable within a declaration.

### Q3: classic placeholders are marked by migration

- The v3-to-v4 migration in `finos/morphir-ir/migration/v3` marks every variable whose canonical name is exactly
  `t-` followed by one or more digits, only in let-definition signatures. Top-level signatures are never marked.
- Every caller gets the same IR. The oracle uses the migration and its own `mark_classic_let_placeholders` is
  deleted.
- Known cost: a user let annotation that names a variable `t1` (canonical `t-1`) becomes unknown, so check mode is
  less strict at that position. It never rejects a valid program.

### Q4: node types are facts in Fill

The MoonBit generator has no specialization, and any type `Variable` is `moonbit.ambiguous_type`. An integer literal
infers as a fresh `number`, so most numeric Scheme code would stay class-polymorphic.

- In Fill, an existing `inferred_type` on a `Value` or `Pattern` is a constraint. When the node is inferred, its type
  is unified with the fact at the node path, before the binding group generalizes.
- Variables in a fact follow the hole rule: a variable in scope is rigid; any other variable is a fresh meta for each
  occurrence and keeps its class; a marked variable is a meta. A fact can be partial, for example `List a`.
- The node gets its solution, not its fact.
- A conflict is `annotation_mismatch` at the node, with expected = fact and found = inferred. It is the first error of
  its binding group.
- Check mode does not change: it compares.
- The Scheme frontend writes `inferred_type: morphir/SDK:basics#int` on integer literals. Scheme integers are exact,
  so this is a fact of the language.
- Pure generics, such as `(define (id x) x)`, stay generic and still fail in the MoonBit generator. A specialization
  component is a follow-up.

### Units

| Unit | Change |
| --- | --- |
| `finos/morphir-ir/identities` | `logical_nodes(unit_id, file) -> Array[(LogicalPath, String)]`. The grammar moves here from `morphir-typing/paths.mbt` and gains type steps for signatures and let signatures. `morphir-typing` reuses it. |
| `finos/morphir-ir/migration/v3` | Marks classic `t-<digits>` let placeholders (Q3). |
| `finos/morphir-typing` | Node facts in Fill (Q4). Uses the logical path grammar of `identities`. |
| `finos/morphir-engine/data` | `fill_lineage` (Q1). |
| `finos/morphir-engine` | `pipeline.inference = "off" \| "fill" \| "check"`, in TOML and in the Scheme `(pipeline …)` form. An invalid value is an error with its provenance through `option_origin`. Dependencies are `@sdk_spec.sdk_specification()` plus the distribution's own. |
| `finos/morphir-scheme/frontend` | Marked `t-<n>` names (Q2) and integer literal facts (Q4). |

### Engine stage

- Order in `execute_content`: read, frontend, exposed modules, components, transforms, **inference**, backend.
- Plain backend: in `fill`, `ir` is replaced; in `check`, `ir` does not change.
- Checkpoint or generator path: the filled file goes through `apply_rewrite` with `fill_lineage` and the job's
  `pipeline.metadata_policy`. Metadata stays on its logical nodes.
- `InferenceFailed` gives one `Diagnostic` for each problem, at stage `"inference"`. The message holds the code, the
  logical path, the expected and found types, and the source location. The file fails; other files continue.

### Testing

- `logical_nodes`: one path for each node kind; the same logical path before and after a compact node becomes
  expanded; every id is in `nodes()`; type steps in signatures and let signatures.
- Migration: `t-8` is marked in a let signature and not in a top-level signature; `t-x` and `t-1a` are not marked.
  Oracle criteria B and C still pass through the migration.
- Node facts: a literal with fact `Int` gives `Int`; `inc` gives `Int -> Int`; a conflicting fact is
  `annotation_mismatch` at the node; a fact variable in scope is rigid; a partial fact works; check mode does not
  change; all current typing tests pass.
- `fill_lineage`: an attribute-only fill retains every old id and derives the `inferredType` nodes; a marker variable
  that becomes `List Int` is retained and its new subnodes are derived from it; a non-marker change is refused;
  metadata survives a compact node becoming expanded.
- Engine: `pipeline.inference` validation with provenance (TOML and Scheme); `off` leaves the IR unchanged; `fill` on
  a plain backend; `fill` on the checkpoint path keeps `.ion` metadata on the same logical nodes; `check` gives
  stage `"inference"` diagnostics.
- Scheme frontend: distinct marked `t-<n>` names for each declaration; integer literal facts; no `scheme-value` in
  fixtures.

### End to end

- A monomorphic Scheme corpus: Int and Float arithmetic, strings, `let` and `let*`, lambdas, `letrec`, `if`, and SDK
  calls such as `string#length` and `list#map` with concrete lambdas.
- Two `.mbtx` mise tasks in `scripts/`, run in CI:
  - `e2e:scheme-moonbit`: `pipeline.inference = "fill"` with the `moonbit` generator, then `moon build` accepts the
    library.
  - `e2e:scheme-elm`: the same corpus with the `elm` generator, then `elm make` accepts the projects. It reuses the
    `elm make` setup of the Elm backend acceptance.
- All suites pass on `wasm`, `wasm-gc`, `js` and `native`. Every module the PR touches is clean under `--deny-warn`.

### Follow-ups

- A specialization component before the MoonBit generator, for generic values. New bead under `morphir-ukvn.5.22`.
- The Elm frontend (`morphir-ukvn.5.22.3`) writes the marker on values with no annotation and uses the stage.
- The open `morphir-ukvn.5.22.7` items stay there. The path-walker refactor becomes simpler with `logical_nodes`.

### Delivery

One PR from a new branch off `65cc2b8`, with one commit for each plan task.

# IR type inference: design

Date: 2026-10-07. Status: approved; Plan 1 merged (#52, #58). Section 11 (Plan 2 design) is waiting for review.

## 1. Purpose and context

This is sub-project 2 of the Elm initiative (umbrella epic `morphir-ukvn.5.22`). It is built Morphir-first. Type
inference is a language-neutral Morphir capability, and every frontend and input uses it through the engine. The Elm
frontend (`morphir-ukvn.5.22.3`) is one consumer. It gets no private shortcut.

Producers that do not know their types cannot use typed backends today. The MoonBit generator refuses IR without
`inferred_type`. The Scheme frontend writes only the placeholder type variable `scheme-value`, so Scheme to MoonBit
fails. The repository has no IR specification of the Morphir SDK. The only machine-readable SDK signatures are the
248 morphir-elm `vSpec` strings in `pkgs/morphir-sdk/conformance/bindings.json`.

### Success criteria

- **A, backend-ready types:** every `Value` and `Pattern` in a well-typed module gets a correct, fully applied
  `inferred_type`. An ill-typed module gets diagnostics with logical node paths.
- **B, parity with morphir-elm:** for the classic v1, v2 and v3 fixtures with their types stripped, the inferred
  types equal the types `morphir-elm make` wrote. Equality is up to alias expansion and renaming of type variables.
- **C, checking:** in check mode, the pass checks existing types and reports every disagreement.
- Scheme source with inference set to `fill` and the `moonbit` generator gives a library that `moon build` accepts.
  The same source with the `elm` generator gives projects that `elm make` accepts.
- All suites pass on `wasm`, `wasm-gc`, `js` and `native`.

## 2. Architecture

| Unit | Module and package | Responsibility | Depends on |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Spec notation | `finos/morphir-scheme/spec` (new package) | Reads and writes the specification notation (section 3) to and from `@ir.PackageSpecification`. | `finos/morphir-scheme` reader, `finos/morphir-ir` |
| SDK specification | `pkgs/morphir-sdk-spec/sdk.scm` (source of truth); `finos/morphir-sdk-spec` (new module, generated v4 JSON) | `sdk_specification() -> @ir.PackageSpecification` for `morphir/SDK`. No Scheme runtime at use time. | `finos/morphir-ir` only. The runtime SDK `finos/morphir-sdk` keeps no dependencies (amendment 10). |
| Inference core | `finos/morphir-typing` (new module, `pkgs/morphir-typing`) | `infer` in fill and check modes (section 4) | `finos/morphir-ir` only |
| Logical node paths | `finos/morphir-ir/identities` | `logical_nodes(unit_id, file) -> Array[(LogicalPath, String)]` | existing |
| Attribute lineage | `finos/morphir-engine/data` | `attribute_lineage(before, after) -> Lineage` for any rewrite that changes only attributes | existing |
| Engine stage | `finos/morphir-engine` | `pipeline.inference = "off" \| "fill" \| "check"` | `finos/morphir-typing`, `finos/morphir-sdk/spec` |
| Scheme frontend | `finos/morphir-scheme/frontend` | Writes the unknown marker (section 4) on its placeholder types | — |

Tooling:
- A bootstrap script, run once, turns the 248 `bindings.json` signatures into the first `sdk.scm`.
- A `.mbtx` script regenerates `finos/morphir-sdk/spec` from `sdk.scm`.
- New task and automation scripts are standalone `.mbtx` files in `scripts/`, registered in
  `.config/mise/config.toml`, as `.github/AGENTS.md` requires.

Delivery is one spec with two plans:
1. Notation, SDK specification and inference core, including the classic-corpus oracle.
2. Logical paths, attribute lineage, the engine stage, the Scheme marker and end-to-end acceptance.

Out of scope: the Elm frontend; macros in the notation; type classes beyond Elm's four built-in constraints.
Inference across a package whose specification is missing is also out of scope; it is a diagnostic.

## 3. Specification notation

The notation is data. It is read with the Morphir Scheme reader and never evaluated. Each file holds one package.
Line comments, block comments and datum comments are allowed.

```scheme
(package "morphir/SDK"
  (module basics
    (type bool (custom (true) (false)))
    (type order (custom (lt) (eq) (gt)))
    (val add ((a number) (b number)) number)
    (val compose-left ((g (-> b c)) (f (-> a b)) (x a)) c)
    (val compare ((a comparable) (b comparable)) #order))
  (module list
    (type list (opaque) a)
    (type predicate (alias (-> a basics#bool)) a)
    (val map ((f (-> a b)) (list (#list a))) (#list b))
    (val foldl ((f (-> a b b)) (z b) (list (#list a))) b)))
```

### Forms

| Form | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `(package "pkg/path" module…)` | A `PackageSpecification`. The name is a canonical `Path`. |
| `(module name item…)` | A `ModuleSpecification`. The name is a canonical module path, for example `json/encode`. |
| `(doc "text")` | Documentation for the module or the item that contains it. |
| `(type name body param…)` | A type specification. The trailing params are type variables. |
| `(val name ((arg type)…) result)` | A value specification. The inputs keep their order. `val` (not `def`) because a specification is a signature, not a definition. |
| `(annotation fqname arg…)` | A v4 annotation inside `type` or `val`. Arguments are data only. |

Type bodies: `(opaque)`, `(alias type)`, `(custom (ctor type…)…)`, `(derived base from-fqname to-fqname)`.

### Type expressions

| Syntax | IR |
| --- | --- |
| A bare symbol, for example `a` or `comparable` | `Variable`. A `number`, `comparable`, `appendable` or `compappend` prefix also writes `TypeAttributes.constraints.typeclass`. |
| `#name`, `module#name`, `pkg:module#name` | A `Reference` in the same module, the same package, or any package |
| `(#name t…)`, `(module#name t…)`, `(pkg:module#name t…)` | A `Reference` with arguments, for example `(#list a)` |
| `(-> a b c)` | A curried `Function`, `a -> b -> c`. N-ary, right-associative. |
| `(tuple a b …)` | `Tuple` |
| `(record (field t)…)` | `Record` |
| `(record r (field t)…)` | `ExtensibleRecord` over `r` |
| `()` | `Unit` |

- Names follow the v4 canonical rules (`less-than`, `map-2`, `LT`) and are parsed with `Name::parse`. A name that is
  not canonical is refused.
- A head symbol that ends in `!` is reserved for macros, which a later pre-pass will expand into plain data. Until
  then the reader refuses it.
- A canonical printer always writes the same layout, and always the flat `->` form. For canonical input,
  read → print → read gives the same text.
- Errors are `SpecError { line, column, message }`.

## 4. Inference semantics

### Interface

`infer(file : IRFile, deps : Map[PackageName, PackageSpecification], mode : Fill | Check) -> Result`

- `morphir/SDK` is built in.
- `Library` dependencies come from its `Dependencies`.
- `Application` dependencies are derived from the dependency definitions it bundles.
- **Fill** returns IR in which every `Value` and `Pattern` has `inferred_type`. Signature types that carry the
  unknown marker are replaced by their solutions.
- **Check** returns the IR unchanged, plus diagnostics.

### Unknown marker

- A type variable whose `TypeAttributes.extensions` holds `"morphir.inference": "unknown"` is unknown. Inference may
  solve it to any type.
- Every other variable in a declared signature is rigid (a skolem), as in an Elm annotation.
- Classic IR has no markers, so it is checked strictly.
- The Scheme frontend writes the marker. The Elm frontend will write it for values without an annotation.

### Algorithm

Constraint-based Hindley-Milner, in the manner of morphir-elm's `Morphir.Type.Infer`: meta variables, union-find
substitution and an occurs check.

- **Top-level values:** they are grouped into strongly connected components across the package's modules, and the
  components are solved in dependency order.
- **Fully declared values:** a value whose signature has no unknown markers is used through its generalized scheme
  everywhere. This permits polymorphic recursion.
- **Values with unknowns:** inside a component they are monomorphic, and they are generalized afterwards.
- `LetDefinition` generalizes, which is let-polymorphism. `LetRecursion` is one group.
- If the body would narrow a rigid variable, the error is `rigid_variable`.

### Constraint classes

These apply to variables. They come from the name prefix or from `typeclass`, and they propagate through
unification.

| Class | Satisfied by |
| --- | --- |
| `number` | `Int`, `Float` |
| `comparable` | `Int`, `Float`, `Char`, `String`, `List c`, tuples of up to 3 comparables |
| `appendable` | `String`, `List a` |
| `compappend` | `String`, `List c` |

- `comparable` with `appendable` gives `compappend`.
- `number` with `comparable` gives `number`.
- Any other combination is `no_instance`.
- `Decimal` and `LocalDate` belong to no class.

### Literals

| Literal | Type |
| --- | --- |
| Integer | A fresh `number` variable |
| Float | `Float` |
| Decimal | `decimal#decimal` |
| String | `String` |
| Char | `Char` |
| Bool | `Bool` |
| Document | `Document` when the SDK defines it; otherwise `unsupported` |

### Records

`Record` and `ExtensibleRecord` unify through row variables.

| Value | Type rule |
| --- | --- |
| `Field(v, f)` | `v : { ρ \| f : α }` |
| `FieldFunction f` | `{ ρ \| f : α } -> α` |
| `UpdateRecord` | Keeps its target's type and constrains each field it sets |
| Record literal | Closed |

### Nominal types

Aliases expand during unification. Opaque and custom types are nominal. A constructor has the type
`args -> T params`.

### Other bodies

- `NativeBody` and `IncompleteBody` use their signature as declared.
- `ExternalBody` checks its fallback value against the signature.
- A `Hole` uses its declared type if present, otherwise a fresh variable.

### Output

- A type that came from an annotation keeps its alias references. Other types are written expanded.
- Generalized variables are named in traversal order: `a`, `b`, …, and class name plus letter (`comparableA`) for
  constrained variables. The output is deterministic.

## 5. Lineage and the engine stage

### Problem

Node identities are JSON pointers into the v4 encoding (`@identities.nodes`). The writer uses compact forms when
attributes are empty, for example a `TuplePattern` written as a tag plus an array. Filling `inferred_type` switches
such a node to its expanded form, which moves the pointers of its children. Attribute-only changes therefore move
node identities. `apply_rewrite` refuses a rewrite with no lineage (`data.lineage_required`).

### General solution

- **`@identities.logical_nodes(unit_id, file)`:** returns each node's logical path, which does not depend on the
  encoding (for example `value:pkg:mod#name/body/apply/arg/0`), paired with its JSON-pointer id.
- **`@data.attribute_lineage(before : IRUnit, after : IRFile) -> Lineage`:**
  - It checks that the two trees are equal apart from attributes. If they are not, it refuses with
    `data.not_attribute_only`.
  - It joins nodes by logical path to build `retained` pairs.
  - It records new attribute nodes, such as those under each `inferredType`, as `derived` from their owner. No
    metadata is attached to them.
- Any attribute-only pass can use this.

### Engine stage

- **Setting:** `pipeline.inference` takes `off` (default), `fill` or `check`. Any other value is a configuration
  error, reported with its provenance.
- **Position:** after the frontend and the transforms, before the backend, on every path.
- **Plain backends:** the IR is replaced.
- **Checkpoint and generator path:** the IR goes through `apply_rewrite` with `attribute_lineage` and the job's
  metadata policy. Data inputs that carry metadata (`.ion`, `.ionb`) are covered.
- **Dependencies:** the specifications are the built-in SDK plus the distribution's `Dependencies`.

## 6. Diagnostics

`InferenceProblem { code, node : LogicalPath, message, expected : Type?, found : Type?, source : SourceLocation? }`

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `type_mismatch` | Two types do not unify |
| `occurs` | Infinite type |
| `rigid_variable` | A body narrows an annotated variable |
| `no_instance` | No type satisfies the constraint class |
| `missing_field` | The record has no such field |
| `unknown_reference` | The reference is not defined or specified |
| `missing_dependency` | No specification for the referenced package |
| `arity` | Wrong number of arguments |
| `annotation_mismatch` | An existing `inferred_type` disagrees with inference (check mode) |
| `unsupported` | A construct inference does not handle |

- In the engine, each problem becomes a `Diagnostic` at stage `"inference"`. The message holds the code, the
  logical path, the expected and found types, and the source location.
- Each binding group stops at its first error. Other groups and modules continue.

## 7. Testing

### Notation

- Read → print → read gives the same result.
- Refusals: an unknown form, a non-canonical name, a reserved `!` head, a `val` with the wrong shape. Each refusal
  reports its line and column.
- Every type form maps to the expected IR.

### SDK specification

- Every one of the 248 `bindings.json` signatures, parsed from its `vSpec`, equals the matching `sdk.scm` entry, up
  to renaming of type variables. A missing or extra binding fails.
- The generated package is fresh.
- The hand-written types and constructors are spot-checked: `Maybe`, `Result`, `Order`, `Bool`, `List`, `Dict`,
  `Set`, `Char`, `String`, `Int`, `Float`, `Decimal`, `LocalDate`.

### Inference rules

There is a unit test for each of these:
- literals, application, lambdas;
- let-polymorphism, `LetRecursion`, component order;
- polymorphic recursion with annotations, rigid variables, the unknown marker;
- each class and each class combination;
- records: access, field functions, updates, rows, `missing_field`;
- aliases, opaque types, constructors;
- native, external and incomplete bodies, and holes;
- every diagnostic code, determinism, and the naming of variables.

### Oracle (criterion B)

- Classic v1, v2 and v3 fixtures: migrate, strip all `inferred_type` and signature types, fill, then compare.
- The same check runs over the Elm backend fixtures, the MoonBit fixtures and the Scheme corpus.

### Check mode (criterion C)

- Every classic fixture passes unchanged.
- In each fixture, one changed `inferred_type` is reported as `annotation_mismatch` at its node.

### Lineage

- Metadata survives when a compact node becomes an expanded one.
- A change to the tree shape is refused.

### Engine

- `pipeline.inference` is validated.
- `fill` works on a plain backend, and on the checkpoint path with `.ion` metadata, which stays on the same logical
  nodes.
- `check` turns problems into diagnostics.
- `off` leaves the IR unchanged.

### End to end

- Scheme with `fill` and `moonbit`: `moon build` accepts the library.
- Scheme with `fill` and `elm`: `elm make` accepts the projects.
- Both run as `.mbtx` mise tasks in CI.

## 8. Follow-ups

- Macros in the notation (`!`-headed forms).
- Decide whether `[backends.moonbit]` options should be strict (ruling 12 of the Elm backend work).
- The Elm frontend (`morphir-ukvn.5.22.3`) consumes this pass through the engine stage.

## 9. Amendments (Plan 1, 2026-10-07)

Where this section and the sections above disagree, this section wins.


1. **No `#name` reference form.** The Morphir Scheme reader rejects any token that starts with `#` other than its
   own literals (`reader.mbt`: "Unknown reader token"). Accepting `#list` would change the Scheme language for every
   program. References are therefore written `module#name` (the same package) or `pkg:module#name` (any package),
   for example `(list#list a)` and `basics#order`.
2. **Positions come from a new reader entry point.** `parse_program` returns `Datum` with no positions. Task 1 adds
   `parse_program_located`, which returns `Located` trees with character offsets. `SpecError` converts an offset to
   a line and column. `parse_program` is unchanged.
3. **The SDK specification is embedded as JSON.** `finos/morphir-sdk/spec` holds generated canonical v4 JSON of a
   `Specs` distribution and decodes it once, on first use. That is simpler than generating MoonBit constructors,
   and it keeps the module free of any Scheme dependency.
4. **Tooling home.** The bootstrap, generator and checker, and the oracle tests, live in the unpublished module
   `finos/morphir-typing-tools`. Putting them in a published module would add a filesystem dependency
   (`moonbitlang/x`), and `finos/morphir-typing` would gain test dependencies on the fixture modules.
5. **Callers supply the SDK.** `finos/morphir-typing` has no built-in SDK, because it depends only on
   `finos/morphir-ir`. Callers add `@sdk_spec.sdk_specification()` to the dependency map. In Plan 2 the engine does
   this; in this plan the tools module does.
6. **Logical paths are defined here and moved in Plan 2.** The logical path grammar is defined in
   `finos/morphir-typing/paths.mbt`. Plan 2 moves it to `finos/morphir-ir/identities` (`logical_nodes`) and makes
   typing reuse it.
7. **Errors stop the pass.** `infer` raises `InferenceFailed(Array[InferenceProblem])` when any problem exists, in
   either mode. The problems are collected across every binding group first.
8. **Canonical SDK names.** `sdk.scm` uses migrated canonical names (`map-2`, `from-int-8`, `LT`). The conformance
   check matches `bindings.json` names through the same canonicalization the Elm mapping generator uses: split camel
   case and digit runs, then apply the `Name::from_words` initialism rule.

## 10. Amendments (execution and review, 2026-10-07)

Where this section and the sections above disagree, this section wins.

### SDK specification module

The SDK specification lives in its own module, `finos/morphir-sdk-spec`, in `pkgs/morphir-sdk-spec`. It is not a
package of `finos/morphir-sdk`. Generated MoonBit libraries compile against `finos/morphir-sdk` alone, in a frozen
workspace, so the runtime SDK must have no dependencies.

`sdk.scm` also declares `local-date`. Where `bindings.json` gives one value the same parameter name twice
(`result#map3`, `result#map4` and `result#map5`), the repeated name takes the next free number. The bootstrap and
the check use the same rule.

### Criterion B oracle

Criterion B keeps the top-level signatures. It strips every node `inferred_type`, and every let-definition
placeholder signature. Classic IR does not separate annotated top-level signatures from inferred ones. Stripping them
gives correctly more general types, so a full strip cannot be the oracle.

### Criterion A oracle

Criterion A uses a full strip: signatures and node types. It also requires each original corpus to pass `Check`
unchanged.

### Classic let placeholders

morphir-elm writes `t-<digits>` variables as the signatures of lets with no annotation, and never rewrites them.
Inference reads these variables as rigid. The oracle marks them as unknown. The typing README documents that callers
must do the same.

### Soundness and checking

- Signature rigids belong to their declaration. Inside inference they are keyed `<decl-key>|<name>`, and output
  strips the owner. This closes a soundness hole in groups of undeclared values that share a variable name.
- Check mode, fill's comparison of existing types, and the oracle use a declaration-scoped equivalence: one variable
  bijection per declaration, signature rigids fixed, class sets compared.
- `sdkgen check` compares constraint classes.
- An unknown `typeclass` name is `unsupported`.
- `rigid_variable` comes from the solver whenever a body narrows a rigid. That includes class failures at a rigid
  leaf.

### Open questions for Plan 2

These must be settled in the Plan 2 design before planning starts:

1. **Lineage of filled signatures.** Fill replaces signature types that carry the unknown marker. Signature types are
   tree content, not attributes, so `attribute_lineage` as written in section 5 would refuse them. Decide how the
   lineage treats replaced signature types: as derived nodes, or with a separate signature rewrite step.
2. **Scheme marker names.** The Scheme frontend writes one placeholder name, `scheme-value`, for every input and
   output. Under the marker rule, one name is one variable, so all positions collapse to a single type. The Scheme
   marker step must write a distinct name for each position.
3. **Classic placeholders.** Decide whether migration from classic IR to v4 marks `t-<digits>` let placeholders for
   all callers.

## 11. Amendments (Plan 2 design, 2026-10-09)

Where this section and the sections above disagree, this section wins. It settles the open questions of section 10
and gives the Plan 2 design. Plan 2 starts from `main` at `65cc2b8` (after #58, #59 and #60).

### Q1: one marker-aware rewrite

- `@data.attribute_lineage` is replaced by `@data.fill_lineage(before : IRUnit, after : IRFile) -> Lineage`.
- `before` and `after` must be equal apart from attributes and apart from the variables of `before` that carry the
  unknown marker. Any other difference is refused with `data.not_attribute_only`.
- Nodes are joined by logical path. A joined node is `retained`.
- A marker variable that inference replaced keeps its id: the root of its replacement is `retained` from it. The new
  nodes under the replacement are `derived` from the marker variable node.
- Every new attribute node, such as those under each `inferredType`, is `derived` from its owner node.
- One fill is one `apply_rewrite` with one provenance record, component `"inference"`.

### Q2: distinct Scheme placeholder names

- The Scheme frontend writes `t-0`, `t-1`, … in place of `scheme-value`. The names are numbered in traversal order and
  counted for each declaration. Every placeholder carries the unknown marker.
- This is the same form that the oracle's `strip_full` writes. The marker rule does not change: one name is one
  variable within a declaration.

### Q3: classic placeholders are marked by migration

- The v3-to-v4 migration in `finos/morphir-ir/migration/v3` marks every variable whose canonical name is exactly
  `t-` followed by one or more digits, only in let-definition signatures. Top-level signatures are never marked.
- Every caller gets the same IR. The oracle uses the migration and its own `mark_classic_let_placeholders` is
  deleted.
- Known cost: a user let annotation that names a variable `t1` (canonical `t-1`) becomes unknown, so check mode is
  less strict at that position. It never rejects a valid program.

### Q4: node types are facts in Fill

The MoonBit generator has no specialization, and any type `Variable` is `moonbit.ambiguous_type`. An integer literal
infers as a fresh `number`, so most numeric Scheme code would stay class-polymorphic.

- In Fill, an existing `inferred_type` on a `Value` or `Pattern` is a constraint. When the node is inferred, its type
  is unified with the fact at the node path, before the binding group generalizes.
- Variables in a fact follow the hole rule: a variable in scope is rigid; any other variable is a fresh meta for each
  occurrence and keeps its class; a marked variable is a meta. A fact can be partial, for example `List a`.
- The node gets its solution, not its fact.
- A conflict is `annotation_mismatch` at the node, with expected = fact and found = inferred. It is the first error of
  its binding group.
- Check mode does not change: it compares.
- The Scheme frontend writes `inferred_type: morphir/SDK:basics#int` on integer literals. Scheme integers are exact,
  so this is a fact of the language.
- Pure generics, such as `(define (id x) x)`, stay generic and still fail in the MoonBit generator. A specialization
  component is a follow-up.

### Units

| Unit | Change |
| --- | --- |
| `finos/morphir-ir/identities` | `logical_nodes(unit_id, file) -> Array[(LogicalPath, String)]`. The grammar moves here from `morphir-typing/paths.mbt` and gains type steps for signatures and let signatures. `morphir-typing` reuses it. |
| `finos/morphir-ir/migration/v3` | Marks classic `t-<digits>` let placeholders (Q3). |
| `finos/morphir-typing` | Node facts in Fill (Q4). Uses the logical path grammar of `identities`. |
| `finos/morphir-engine/data` | `fill_lineage` (Q1). |
| `finos/morphir-engine` | `pipeline.inference = "off" \| "fill" \| "check"`, in TOML and in the Scheme `(pipeline …)` form. An invalid value is an error with its provenance through `option_origin`. Dependencies are `@sdk_spec.sdk_specification()` plus the distribution's own. |
| `finos/morphir-scheme/frontend` | Marked `t-<n>` names (Q2) and integer literal facts (Q4). |

### Engine stage

- Order in `execute_content`: read, frontend, exposed modules, components, transforms, **inference**, backend.
- Plain backend: in `fill`, `ir` is replaced; in `check`, `ir` does not change.
- Checkpoint or generator path: the filled file goes through `apply_rewrite` with `fill_lineage` and the fixed
  policy `MetadataPolicy::no_derived()`, not the job's `pipeline.metadata_policy`: `retain` refuses metadata on
  derived nodes, and section 5 says derived type nodes get no metadata. Metadata stays on its logical nodes.
- `InferenceFailed` gives one `Diagnostic` for each problem, at stage `"inference"`. The message holds the code, the
  logical path, the expected and found types, and the source location. The file fails; other files continue.

### Testing

- `logical_nodes`: one path for each node kind; the same logical path before and after a compact node becomes
  expanded; every id is in `nodes()`; type steps in signatures and let signatures.
- Migration: `t-8` is marked in a let signature and not in a top-level signature; `t-x` and `t-1a` are not marked.
  Oracle criteria B and C still pass through the migration.
- Node facts: a literal with fact `Int` gives `Int`; `inc` gives `Int -> Int`; a conflicting fact is
  `annotation_mismatch` at the node; a fact variable in scope is rigid; a partial fact works; check mode does not
  change; all current typing tests pass.
- `fill_lineage`: an attribute-only fill retains every old id and derives the `inferredType` nodes; a marker variable
  that becomes `List Int` is retained and its new subnodes are derived from it; a non-marker change is refused;
  metadata survives a compact node becoming expanded.
- Engine: `pipeline.inference` validation with provenance (TOML and Scheme); `off` leaves the IR unchanged; `fill` on
  a plain backend; `fill` on the checkpoint path keeps `.ion` metadata on the same logical nodes; `check` gives
  stage `"inference"` diagnostics.
- Scheme frontend: distinct marked `t-<n>` names for each declaration; integer literal facts; no `scheme-value` in
  fixtures.

### End to end

- A monomorphic Scheme corpus: Int and Float arithmetic, strings, `let` and `let*`, lambdas, `letrec`, `if`, and SDK
  calls such as `string#length` and `list#map` with concrete lambdas.
- Two `.mbtx` mise tasks in `scripts/`, run in CI:
  - `e2e:scheme-moonbit`: `pipeline.inference = "fill"` with the `moonbit` generator, then `moon build` accepts the
    library.
  - `e2e:scheme-elm`: the same corpus with the `elm` generator, then `elm make` accepts the projects. It reuses the
    `elm make` setup of the Elm backend acceptance.
- All suites pass on `wasm`, `wasm-gc`, `js` and `native`. Every module the PR touches is clean under `--deny-warn`.

### Follow-ups

- A specialization component before the MoonBit generator, for generic values. New bead under `morphir-ukvn.5.22`.
- The Elm frontend (`morphir-ukvn.5.22.3`) writes the marker on values with no annotation and uses the stage.
- The open `morphir-ukvn.5.22.7` items stay there. The path-walker refactor becomes simpler with `logical_nodes`.

### Delivery

One PR from a new branch off `65cc2b8`, with one commit for each plan task.
