design:
# Elm frontend: design

Date: 2026-10-14. Status: approved (brainstorming and written spec, 2026-10-14). Plans 1 and 2 are done; Plan 3 is next.

## 1. Purpose and context

This is sub-project 3 of the Elm initiative (umbrella epic `morphir-ukvn.5.22`). The Elm backend
(`morphir-ukvn.5.22.1`) and language-neutral IR type inference (`morphir-ukvn.5.22.2`, PRs #60 and #66) are merged.
This sub-project adds the Elm frontend: Elm source to typed Morphir IR. Wiring (`morphir.json` discovery, CLI and
workbench) is `morphir-ukvn.5.22.4`.

The frontend is built Morphir-first. It parses with `moonrockz/krueger`, resolves names to Morphir FQNames, lowers to
v4 IR, and leaves types to the shared IR inference. It has no private type checker.

Facts from the code that shape the design:

- `moonrockz/krueger@0.5.0` has a complete elm-syntax 7.3.9 parser (`@krueger.parse_module`, dialect
  `Dialect::elm_0_19_1()`). Nearly every AST node is a `Node[T]` with a 1-based source range. Today only the Elm
  backend uses krueger, as a printer.
- The engine compiles one source file to one IR unit. It has no cross-file linking. An Elm project needs imports
  across modules.
- The SDK specification has 248 bindings (`pkgs/morphir-sdk-spec`). The only Elm to Morphir name table is the
  reverse one in `pkgs/morphir-elm/backend/mapping_builtin.mbt`.
- The checkpoint path, which every generator uses, refuses `project.exposed_modules` (`pkgs/morphir-engine/plan.mbt`).
- The repository has no Elm sources and no `morphir-elm make` outputs, except vendored classic IR without its source.
  `morphir-elm` 2.100.0 is on npm.

### Success criteria

- **A, parity:** for every corpus project, the IR of the frontend equals the IR of pinned `morphir-elm make`
  2.100.0 after normalization (section 6). Each known difference is pinned in `parity_gaps` with a reason and a bead.
- **B, round trip:** for every corpus IR and the vendored classic fixtures (rentals v1 and v2, greeting), IR to Elm
  (backend) to IR (frontend) gives the same normalized IR.
- **C, typed output:** the frontend output has an `inferred_type` on every `Value` and `Pattern`. The `elm`
  generator gives projects that `elm make` accepts. The `moonbit` generator gives libraries that `moon build` accepts,
  except generic values pinned until `morphir-ukvn.5.22.11`.
- **D, diagnostics:** every failure is a frontend diagnostic with a code, a message and a source range.
- All suites pass on `wasm`, `wasm-gc`, `js` and `native`.

## 2. Architecture

The frontend runs four passes: parse, resolve, lower, infer. Each pass is its own package with its own tests, so a
parity difference points to one pass.

| Unit | Package | Responsibility | Depends on |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Mapping | `finos/morphir-elm/mapping` | The SDK table in both directions: Morphir FQName to Elm name (backend) and Elm qualified name to FQName (frontend), for values, types, constructors and operators | `morphir-ir`, `morphir-sdk-spec` |
| Resolve | `finos/morphir-elm/frontend/resolve` | Project symbol table; every name to an FQName or a local | krueger `ast`, mapping |
| Lower | `finos/morphir-elm/frontend/lower` | Resolved krueger AST to v4 IR, one rule per construct | resolve, `morphir-ir` |
| Driver | `finos/morphir-elm/frontend` | `compile_project`: parse, module rules, resolve, lower, infer; diagnostics | all of the above, `morphir-typing` |
| Engine | `finos/morphir-engine` | `ProjectCompiler` source compiler kind, `elm` source provider, checkpoint access | driver |

The `mapping` package takes over `backend/mapping.mbt` and `backend/mapping_builtin.mbt`. The backend then imports
it. One generated table serves both directions.

## 3. Driver

`compile_project(sources : Array[ElmSource], package : Path, exposed : Array[ModuleName]) -> IRFile raise ElmFailed`,
where `ElmSource` has a relative path and the content.

1. **Parse.** Every source goes through `@krueger.parse_module` with `Dialect::elm_0_19_1()`. That dialect refuses
   ports, effect modules and infix declarations. A missing AST or any `Error` diagnostic is `elm.parse` at its range.
   All sources are parsed before the build stops.
2. **Module rules.** The module name must match the relative path (`A/B.elm` is `A.B`). The module name must start
   with the package name; the IR module path is the module name without the package prefix, as in morphir-elm. A
   violation is `elm.module_name`. An import cycle is `elm.import_cycle`. Resolution needs no module order, because
   the exports come from the syntax.
3. **Resolve** (section 4).
4. **Lower** (section 5).
5. **Infer.** `@typing.infer(file, sdk_deps, Fill)` runs over the whole Library. Each `InferenceProblem` becomes
   `elm.type` with the inference code, the node path and the source span.

Each pass collects all of its problems, then the build stops before the next pass. A failed build gives no IR.
`ElmFailed` holds `ElmProblem { code, message, path, range }` values, in source order.

## 4. Resolve

- **Exports** of a module come from its exposing list. `exposing (..)` exports every declaration. `T` exports an
  opaque type; `T(..)` also exports its constructors.
- **Scope order** for an unqualified name: locals (arguments, let names, pattern names), then the top-level names of
  the module, then names that imports expose, then Elm's default imports (`Basics` exposing everything, `List`
  exposing `List` and `(::)`, `Maybe` exposing `Maybe(..)`, `Result` exposing `Result(..)`, `String` exposing
  `String`, `Char` exposing `Char`, `Tuple`). A qualified name `Alias.name` uses the import alias or the module name.
- **Elm core and `Morphir.SDK.*`** names resolve through `mapping` to `morphir/SDK`.
- **Errors:** `elm.unresolved_name`; `elm.ambiguous_name` (two imports expose the same name and the use is
  unqualified); `elm.unsupported_module` (a third-party package, or an Elm core module that the SDK does not cover);
  `elm.unsupported_value` (an Elm core value with no SDK binding, named in the message); `elm.unsupported` (`Debug.*`,
  GLSL).

## 5. Lower

One function for each declaration, type annotation, expression and pattern kind. Each rule cites the rule of
morphir-elm `Morphir.Elm.IncrementalFrontend.Mapper` that it copies (the code path of `make`; `Morphir.Elm.Frontend` is
only the `--fallback-cli` path). Each node gets its krueger range as an IR source location.

### Types

| Elm | IR |
| --- | --- |
| `Typed` | `Reference` to the resolved FQName, with its arguments |
| `Unit` | `Unit` |
| `Tupled` | `Tuple` |
| `Record` | `Record` |
| `GenericRecord` | `ExtensibleRecord` |
| `FunctionTypeAnnotation` | `Function` |
| `GenericType` | `Variable` |

A variable whose name starts with `number`, `comparable`, `appendable` or `compappend` also gets the constraint
attribute `typeclass`, as the epic requires. The backend writes the prefix back. A let annotation uses the variables of
the enclosing annotation by the hole rule of `morphir-typing`: a name in scope is the same rigid variable.

### Declarations and access

- A type alias is a `TypeAliasDefinition`; a custom type is a `CustomTypeDefinition`. Doc comments are documentation.
- Module selection and module access follow `morphir-elm make` 2.100.0 (corrected by probes and its source during
  Plan 1, 2026-10-14). morphir-elm processes the exposed modules and the project modules they import, transitively;
  modules that nothing imports are not checked, except for parse errors and import cycles. The output keeps the
  exposed modules and the processed modules that they reach through type definitions and value-body references.
  A module named only in value signatures, used only through constructors, imported and unused, or not imported, is
  dropped. Exposed modules are Public; another output module is Public only when an exposed module shows one of its
  types in a public definition (first name per module, in Elm order), otherwise Private. The README `## Frontend`
  section of `pkgs/morphir-elm` states the full rule.
- Output modules for code generation (maintainer decision on I3, option b, 2026-10-14): `compile_project` takes
  `output? : OutputModules`. `Parity`, the default, keeps the selection above, so the output can name a type of a
  module it drops. `Referenced` also keeps every processed module that an output module names, transitively: in type
  definitions, value signatures, value bodies, patterns and inferred types. An added module keeps the access of the
  rule above. The parity tests use `Parity`; the engine's `elm` provider uses `Referenced`, so that generated Elm and
  MoonBit name no missing module (criterion C).
- A value or type is Public only if its module exposes it. An opaque export keeps the constructors Private.
- A `{-|` comment is a declaration's doc only when the declaration starts on the row right after the comment ends.
  Declaration docs keep their raw text between `{-|` and `-}`, with the spaces (`" A point. "`); a declaration
  without one gets `""`. The module doc is the first other `{-|` comment anywhere in the file, without its first 3
  and last 3 characters (`String.dropLeft 3 >> String.dropRight 3`); without one the module has no doc.
- Value inputs: the arguments, then the arguments of leading lambdas (also inside parentheses), while each is a plain
  variable and, for an annotated value, while the rest of the annotation is a function type. A type alias of a
  function type stops the inputs.
- An annotated value gets its signature from the annotation. An unannotated value and an unannotated let definition
  get marked `t-<n>` placeholders (the unknown marker of `morphir-ir`), one for each position, and inference fills them.

### Values

- Literals: Elm integer literals are `number`, so the frontend writes **no** `Int` fact (unlike Scheme). `True` and
  `False` are `BoolLiteral`, as in morphir-elm. Hex, float, char and string literals map directly.
- Operators and prefix operators become SDK function references through morphir-elm's fixed operator table
  (`mapOperator`: `++` is `basics#append`, `::` is `list#cons`, `>>`/`<<` are `composeRight`/`composeLeft`); `|>` and
  `<|` become plain applications. Negation is `basics#negate`, except that `-1` and `-2.5` fold into the literal.
- A whole-number literal that inference types as `Float` becomes a `FloatLiteral` (`Infer.fixNumberLiterals`).
- morphir-elm refuses top-level mutual recursion; the frontend accepts it (Elm does).
- `case` is `PatternMatch`. `if` is `IfThenElse`. Lambdas, tuples, lists, records, field access, field functions and
  record update map to their IR forms.
- A let block is split into `LetDefinition` chains, with `LetRecursion` for mutually recursive groups, in
  morphir-elm's dependency order (DFS post-order, or Kosaraju components when there is a cycle), not source order.
  Let definitions are never lifted. A destructuring let is `Destructure`.
- A value that inference leaves generic stays generic.

### Rules settled by the parity fixtures

Confirmed: an unannotated value gets plain type variables such as `t4` from morphir-elm, without the `number`
class, where IR inference gives a `number` variable. The normalizer compares type variables by position only, and
`parity_gaps` pins any class difference.

For a construct whose morphir-elm form is not yet confirmed, the parity fixtures decide, and the spec records the rule
when it is confirmed. Open now: record-alias constructors used as functions; `|>`, `<|`, `>>` and `<<`; the type of an
unannotated top-level number.

## 6. Testing

### Corpus

Each project is in `pkgs/morphir-elm/conformance/projects/<name>/`, with `morphir.json`, `src/**/*.elm` and
`expected/morphir-ir.json`. `SOURCES.md` records the origin of each project (own, finos/morphir-elm or
finos/morphir-examples), its commit and its license.

- **Own feature projects**, one per area: types and aliases; custom types and access; records and field functions;
  `case`; `let` with recursion and destructuring; operators and pipes; lambdas; cross-module imports and aliases; SDK
  modules; `Morphir.SDK.*` modules.
- **finos/morphir-elm test data**, for example rentals.
- **finos/morphir-examples.** A project that `morphir-elm make` cannot build, or that needs an upstream fix, is listed
  with the reason. Upstream PRs to finos/morphir-examples are drafted and wait for the maintainer's approval.

### Refresh

`scripts/elm-parity-refresh.mbtx` (mise task `elm:parity-refresh`) runs pinned `morphir-elm` 2.100.0 through npm on
each project and writes `expected/morphir-ir.json`. It also regenerates an embedded MoonBit data file, so that the
tests run on all four targets without file input. A CI job runs the refresh and fails on any difference.

### Parity test

For each project: compile with the frontend; migrate the expected classic IR to v4; normalize both (drop source
locations, rename type variables per declaration in first-occurrence order, sort maps); compare modules, access, docs,
type definitions, value bodies and the inferred type on every node. `parity_gaps` pins each known difference with a
reason and a bead, and the test fails when a pinned gap closes. An unannotated
definition's declared type in morphir-elm output comes from a first inference pass against an empty distribution, so
its placeholder variables are masked in the comparison; node types are compared everywhere.

### Round trip

For every corpus IR and the vendored classic fixtures: the Elm backend generates Elm; the frontend compiles it again;
the normalized result equals the normalized input.

### Unit and engine tests

- `mapping`, `resolve`, `lower` and the driver each have their own tests, including every error code.
- Engine e2e: `e2e:elm-moonbit` and `e2e:elm-elm` compile every corpus project through the engine with the `elm`
  provider (`pkgs/morphir-engine/acceptance/elm`, whose sources the refresh writes) and generate MoonBit and Elm.
  `moon build` and `elm make` must accept the output. Projects that do not generate yet, such as generic values that
  wait for `morphir-ukvn.5.22.11`, are pinned in a gaps map with a bead.

## 7. Engine

- A new `SourceCompiler` kind, `ProjectCompiler`, takes all sources of one language in a project and gives one
  `IRUnit`. The plan groups those files into one job. Public API: `SourceProfile.compile` becomes the enum
  `SourceCompile`, `PerFile` (one unit per file, as before) or `PerProject` (one call with `ProjectSources`: the
  project name and `exposed_modules` as written, and the sources in path order). The unit id of a project is its
  canonical name. A project compiler reports all problems with `RejectedSources`, one diagnostic per file. It needs a
  checkpoint or generator backend and refuses a single-file request. By default there is no document limit:
  `SourceCapabilities.max_documents` becomes `Int?`, `None` is no limit, and the CLI prints `documents per unit: no
  limit` (JSON `null`). No number stands for "no limit", and the old cap of 64 goes away. A provider may declare a
  limit (`Some(n)`, `n >= 1`); planning then refuses a project with more than `n` sources. The output budget
  `unit_limits` bounds a project unit. The Elm provider declares no limit.
- An `elm` source provider (package `finos/morphir-engine/elm`, provider `finos/morphir-elm`) registers language
  `elm`, extension `.elm` and profile `library`. It reads `project.name` as the package and
  `project.exposed_modules` as `exposed`, and asks the frontend for `Referenced` output modules. The engine core does
  not register it; CLI and workbench wiring is `morphir-ukvn.5.22.4`.
- The frontend chooses the output modules and sets access itself. The plan skips its own exposure step for a project
  compiler, and the checkpoint path accepts `exposed_modules` in that case. So Elm to `moonbit` and Elm to `elm` generation work.
- The frontend runs inference itself, so `pipeline.inference` is not needed for Elm. `check` still works on its
  output.

## 8. Out of scope

- Ports, effect modules, GLSL, `Debug.*` and infix declarations.
- Third-party Elm packages, and Elm core modules that the SDK does not cover.
- `morphir.json` `dependencies` (other Morphir IR packages).
- `morphir.json` discovery, CLI and workbench (`morphir-ukvn.5.22.4`).
- Specialization of generic values for MoonBit (`morphir-ukvn.5.22.11`).
- Incremental and partial compilation.

## 9. Plans

The plans accumulate on one branch, and the PR opens when the maintainer asks (changed 2026-10-14; first one PR
for each plan). After each plan, the part already built works and is tested.

1. **Plan 1, structure and types:** extract `mapping`; driver with parse, module rules and resolve; lower type
   definitions, signatures, access and docs; refresh task; own feature projects; parity harness for everything
   except value bodies.
2. **Plan 2, values:** lower expressions, patterns, lets and operators; inference in the driver; full-body parity;
   round-trip harness.
3. **Plan 3, engine and corpus:** `Referenced` output modules; `ProjectCompiler` kind and `elm` source provider;
   checkpoint access for project compilers; `e2e:elm-moonbit` and `e2e:elm-elm`; import of the finos/morphir-elm and
   finos/morphir-examples projects and the list of upstream PRs.

## 10. Risks

- **Unknown morphir-elm rules.** Some lowering rules are confirmed only by the fixtures. Mitigation: Plan 1 creates
  the refresh task first, so every later rule is checked against real output.
- **morphir-examples drift.** Some examples may not build with morphir-elm 2.100.0. Mitigation: list them with the
  reason; propose upstream PRs only with approval.
- **Inference gaps.** A morphir-elm type that IR inference does not reproduce is pinned in `parity_gaps` and filed
  under `morphir-ukvn.5.22.7`.
notes: Acceptance notes from the Elm backend work (2026-10-04): (1) Add an engine test that runs Elm source -> IR (elm frontend) -> moonbit generator end to end; the MoonBit generator needs typed IR (ValueAttributes.inferred_type, filled by morphir-ukvn.5.22.2) and a Library distribution. (2) The checkpoint path that every generation backend uses refuses transforms and project.exposed_modules (pkgs/morphir-engine/plan.mbt); an Elm frontend that maps morphir.json exposedModules to exposed_modules hits this limit, so lift it or map exposure differently.
close_reason: Plans 1-3 done and merged in finos/morphir-moonbit#82 (squash ab66764). Success criteria A-D met; known gaps pinned to the open child beads, which stay open as follow-ups.

  opaque type; `T(..)` also exports its constructors.

  the module, then names that imports expose, then Elm's default imports (`Basics` exposing everything, `List`
  exposing `List` and `(::)`, `Maybe` exposing `Maybe(..)`, `Result` exposing `Result(..)`, `String` exposing
  `String`, `Char` exposing `Char`, `Tuple`). A qualified name `Alias.name` uses the import alias or the module name.
- **Elm core and `Morphir.SDK.*`** names resolve through `mapping` to `morphir/SDK`.
- **Errors:** `elm.unresolved_name`; `elm.ambiguous_name` (two imports expose the same name and the use is
  unqualified); `elm.unsupported_module` (a third-party package, or an Elm core module that the SDK does not cover);
  `elm.unsupported_value` (an Elm core value with no SDK binding, named in the message); `elm.unsupported` (`Debug.*`,
  GLSL).

| --- | --- |

   violation is `elm.module_name`. An import cycle is `elm.import_cycle`. Resolution needs no module order, because
   the exports come from the syntax.
3. **Resolve** (section 4).
4. **Lower** (section 5).
5. **Infer.** `@typing.infer(file, sdk_deps, Fill)` runs over the whole Library. Each `InferenceProblem` becomes
   `elm.type` with the inference code, the node path and the source span.

  opaque type; `T(..)` also exports its constructors.

| Elm | IR |
| --- | --- |

| `Unit` | `Unit` |

| Elm | IR |

  (`mapOperator`: `++` is `basics#append`, `::` is `list#cons`, `>>`/`<<` are `composeRight`/`composeLeft`); `|>` and

  must accept the output. Generic values that wait for `morphir-ukvn.5.22.11` are pinned in a gaps map.

## 7. Engine

  `IRUnit`. The plan groups those files into one job.
- An `elm` source provider registers language `elm`, extension `.elm` and profile `library`. It reads
  `project.name` as the package and `project.exposed_modules` as `exposed`.

- The frontend runs inference itself, so `pipeline.inference` is not needed for Elm. `check` still works on its

- Third-party Elm packages, and Elm core modules that the SDK does not cover.
- `morphir.json` `dependencies` (other Morphir IR packages).
- `morphir.json` discovery, CLI and workbench (`morphir-ukvn.5.22.4`).
- Specialization of generic values for MoonBit (`morphir-ukvn.5.22.11`).
- Incremental and partial compilation.

## 9. Plans

One PR for each plan. After each plan, the part already built works and is tested.

1. **Plan 1, structure and types:** extract `mapping`; driver with parse, module rules and resolve; lower type
   definitions, signatures, access and docs; refresh task; own feature projects; parity harness for everything
   except value bodies.
2. **Plan 2, values:** lower expressions, patterns, lets and operators; inference in the driver; full-body parity;
   round-trip harness.
3. **Plan 3, engine and corpus:** `ProjectCompiler` kind and `elm` source provider; checkpoint access for project
   compilers; `e2e:elm-moonbit` and `e2e:elm-elm`; import of the finos/morphir-elm and finos/morphir-examples projects
   and the list of upstream PRs.

## 10. Risks

- **Unknown morphir-elm rules.** Some lowering rules are confirmed only by the fixtures. Mitigation: Plan 1 creates
  the refresh task first, so every later rule is checked against real output.
- **morphir-examples drift.** Some examples may not build with morphir-elm 2.100.0. Mitigation: list them with the
  reason; propose upstream PRs only with approval.
- **Inference gaps.** A morphir-elm type that IR inference does not reproduce is pinned in `parity_gaps` and filed
  under `morphir-ukvn.5.22.7`.

## 1. Purpose and context

This is sub-project 3 of the Elm initiative (umbrella epic `morphir-ukvn.5.22`). The Elm backend
(`morphir-ukvn.5.22.1`) and language-neutral IR type inference (`morphir-ukvn.5.22.2`, PRs #60 and #66) are merged.

v4 IR, and leaves types to the shared IR inference. It has no private type checker.

- `moonrockz/krueger@0.5.0` has a complete elm-syntax 7.3.9 parser (`@krueger.parse_module`, dialect
  `Dialect::elm_0_19_1()`). Nearly every AST node is a `Node[T]` with a 1-based source range. Today only the Elm
  backend uses krueger, as a printer.

  across modules.

  reverse one in `pkgs/morphir-elm/backend/mapping_builtin.mbt`.

  not register it; CLI and workbench wiring is `morphir-ukvn.5.22.4`.
- The frontend chooses the output modules and sets access itself. The plan skips its own exposure step for a project
  compiler, and the checkpoint path accepts `exposed_modules` in that case. So Elm to `moonbit` and Elm to `elm` generation work.
- The frontend runs inference itself, so `pipeline.inference` is not needed for Elm. `check` still works on its
  output.

## 8. Out of scope

- Ports, effect modules, GLSL, `Debug.*` and infix declarations.
- Third-party Elm packages, and Elm core modules that the SDK does not cover.
- `morphir.json` `dependencies` (other Morphir IR packages).
- `morphir.json` discovery, CLI and workbench (`morphir-ukvn.5.22.4`).
- Specialization of generic values for MoonBit (`morphir-ukvn.5.22.11`).
- Incremental and partial compilation.

## 9. Plans

One PR for each plan. After each plan, the part already built works and is tested.

1. **Plan 1, structure and types:** extract `mapping`; driver with parse, module rules and resolve; lower type
   definitions, signatures, access and docs; refresh task; own feature projects; parity harness for everything
   except value bodies.
2. **Plan 2, values:** lower expressions, patterns, lets and operators; inference in the driver; full-body parity;
   round-trip harness.
3. **Plan 3, engine and corpus:** `Referenced` output modules; `ProjectCompiler` kind and `elm` source provider;
   checkpoint access for project compilers; `e2e:elm-moonbit` and `e2e:elm-elm`; import of the finos/morphir-elm and
   finos/morphir-examples projects and the list of upstream PRs. Each plan accumulates on one branch; the PR opens when
   the maintainer asks.

## 10. Risks

- **Unknown morphir-elm rules.** Some lowering rules are confirmed only by the fixtures. Mitigation: Plan 1 creates
  the refresh task first, so every later rule is checked against real output.
- **morphir-examples drift.** Some examples may not build with morphir-elm 2.100.0. Mitigation: list them with the
  reason; propose upstream PRs only with approval.
- **Inference gaps.** A morphir-elm type that IR inference does not reproduce is pinned in `parity_gaps` and filed
  under `morphir-ukvn.5.22.7`.

# Elm frontend: design

Date: 2026-10-14. Status: approved (brainstorming and written spec, 2026-10-14). Plans 1 and 2 are done; Plan 3 is next.

## 1. Purpose and context

This is sub-project 3 of the Elm initiative (umbrella epic `morphir-ukvn.5.22`). The Elm backend
(`morphir-ukvn.5.22.1`) and language-neutral IR type inference (`morphir-ukvn.5.22.2`, PRs #60 and #66) are merged.
This sub-project adds the Elm frontend: Elm source to typed Morphir IR. Wiring (`morphir.json` discovery, CLI and
workbench) is `morphir-ukvn.5.22.4`.

The frontend is built Morphir-first. It parses with `moonrockz/krueger`, resolves names to Morphir FQNames, lowers to
v4 IR, and leaves types to the shared IR inference. It has no private type checker.

Facts from the code that shape the design:

- `moonrockz/krueger@0.5.0` has a complete elm-syntax 7.3.9 parser (`@krueger.parse_module`, dialect
  `Dialect::elm_0_19_1()`). Nearly every AST node is a `Node[T]` with a 1-based source range. Today only the Elm
  backend uses krueger, as a printer.
- The engine compiles one source file to one IR unit. It has no cross-file linking. An Elm project needs imports
  across modules.
- The SDK specification has 248 bindings (`pkgs/morphir-sdk-spec`). The only Elm to Morphir name table is the
  reverse one in `pkgs/morphir-elm/backend/mapping_builtin.mbt`.
- The checkpoint path, which every generator uses, refuses `project.exposed_modules` (`pkgs/morphir-engine/plan.mbt`).
- The repository has no Elm sources and no `morphir-elm make` outputs, except vendored classic IR without its source.
  `morphir-elm` 2.100.0 is on npm.

### Success criteria

- **A, parity:** for every corpus project, the IR of the frontend equals the IR of pinned `morphir-elm make`
  2.100.0 after normalization (section 6). Each known difference is pinned in `parity_gaps` with a reason and a bead.
- **B, round trip:** for every corpus IR and the vendored classic fixtures (rentals v1 and v2, greeting), IR to Elm
  (backend) to IR (frontend) gives the same normalized IR.
- **C, typed output:** the frontend output has an `inferred_type` on every `Value` and `Pattern`. The `elm`
  generator gives projects that `elm make` accepts. The `moonbit` generator gives libraries that `moon build` accepts,
  except generic values pinned until `morphir-ukvn.5.22.11`.
- **D, diagnostics:** every failure is a frontend diagnostic with a code, a message and a source range.
- All suites pass on `wasm`, `wasm-gc`, `js` and `native`.

## 2. Architecture

The frontend runs four passes: parse, resolve, lower, infer. Each pass is its own package with its own tests, so a
parity difference points to one pass.

| Unit | Package | Responsibility | Depends on |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Mapping | `finos/morphir-elm/mapping` | The SDK table in both directions: Morphir FQName to Elm name (backend) and Elm qualified name to FQName (frontend), for values, types, constructors and operators | `morphir-ir`, `morphir-sdk-spec` |
| Resolve | `finos/morphir-elm/frontend/resolve` | Project symbol table; every name to an FQName or a local | krueger `ast`, mapping |
| Lower | `finos/morphir-elm/frontend/lower` | Resolved krueger AST to v4 IR, one rule per construct | resolve, `morphir-ir` |
| Driver | `finos/morphir-elm/frontend` | `compile_project`: parse, module rules, resolve, lower, infer; diagnostics | all of the above, `morphir-typing` |
| Engine | `finos/morphir-engine` | `ProjectCompiler` source compiler kind, `elm` source provider, checkpoint access | driver |

The `mapping` package takes over `backend/mapping.mbt` and `backend/mapping_builtin.mbt`. The backend then imports
it. One generated table serves both directions.

## 3. Driver

`compile_project(sources : Array[ElmSource], package : Path, exposed : Array[ModuleName]) -> IRFile raise ElmFailed`,
where `ElmSource` has a relative path and the content.

1. **Parse.** Every source goes through `@krueger.parse_module` with `Dialect::elm_0_19_1()`. That dialect refuses
   ports, effect modules and infix declarations. A missing AST or any `Error` diagnostic is `elm.parse` at its range.
   All sources are parsed before the build stops.
2. **Module rules.** The module name must match the relative path (`A/B.elm` is `A.B`). The module name must start
   with the package name; the IR module path is the module name without the package prefix, as in morphir-elm. A
   violation is `elm.module_name`. An import cycle is `elm.import_cycle`. Resolution needs no module order, because
   the exports come from the syntax.
3. **Resolve** (section 4).
4. **Lower** (section 5).
5. **Infer.** `@typing.infer(file, sdk_deps, Fill)` runs over the whole Library. Each `InferenceProblem` becomes
   `elm.type` with the inference code, the node path and the source span.

Each pass collects all of its problems, then the build stops before the next pass. A failed build gives no IR.
`ElmFailed` holds `ElmProblem { code, message, path, range }` values, in source order.

## 4. Resolve

- **Exports** of a module come from its exposing list. `exposing (..)` exports every declaration. `T` exports an
  opaque type; `T(..)` also exports its constructors.
- **Scope order** for an unqualified name: locals (arguments, let names, pattern names), then the top-level names of
  the module, then names that imports expose, then Elm's default imports (`Basics` exposing everything, `List`
  exposing `List` and `(::)`, `Maybe` exposing `Maybe(..)`, `Result` exposing `Result(..)`, `String` exposing
  `String`, `Char` exposing `Char`, `Tuple`). A qualified name `Alias.name` uses the import alias or the module name.
- **Elm core and `Morphir.SDK.*`** names resolve through `mapping` to `morphir/SDK`.
- **Errors:** `elm.unresolved_name`; `elm.ambiguous_name` (two imports expose the same name and the use is
  unqualified); `elm.unsupported_module` (a third-party package, or an Elm core module that the SDK does not cover);
  `elm.unsupported_value` (an Elm core value with no SDK binding, named in the message); `elm.unsupported` (`Debug.*`,
  GLSL).

## 5. Lower

One function for each declaration, type annotation, expression and pattern kind. Each rule cites the rule of
morphir-elm `Morphir.Elm.IncrementalFrontend.Mapper` that it copies (the code path of `make`; `Morphir.Elm.Frontend` is
only the `--fallback-cli` path). Each node gets its krueger range as an IR source location.

### Types

| Elm | IR |
| --- | --- |
| `Typed` | `Reference` to the resolved FQName, with its arguments |
| `Unit` | `Unit` |
| `Tupled` | `Tuple` |
| `Record` | `Record` |
| `GenericRecord` | `ExtensibleRecord` |
| `FunctionTypeAnnotation` | `Function` |
| `GenericType` | `Variable` |

A variable whose name starts with `number`, `comparable`, `appendable` or `compappend` also gets the constraint
attribute `typeclass`, as the epic requires. The backend writes the prefix back. A let annotation uses the variables of
the enclosing annotation by the hole rule of `morphir-typing`: a name in scope is the same rigid variable.

### Declarations and access

- A type alias is a `TypeAliasDefinition`; a custom type is a `CustomTypeDefinition`. Doc comments are documentation.
- Module selection and module access follow `morphir-elm make` 2.100.0 (corrected by probes and its source during
  Plan 1, 2026-10-14). morphir-elm processes the exposed modules and the project modules they import, transitively;
  modules that nothing imports are not checked, except for parse errors and import cycles. The output keeps the
  exposed modules and the processed modules that they reach through type definitions and value-body references.
  A module named only in value signatures, used only through constructors, imported and unused, or not imported, is
  dropped. Exposed modules are Public; another output module is Public only when an exposed module shows one of its
  types in a public definition (first name per module, in Elm order), otherwise Private. The README `## Frontend`
  section of `pkgs/morphir-elm` states the full rule.
- Output modules for code generation (maintainer decision on I3, option b, 2026-10-14): `compile_project` takes
  `output? : OutputModules`. `Parity`, the default, keeps the selection above, so the output can name a type of a
  module it drops. `Referenced` also keeps every processed module that an output module names, transitively: in type
  definitions, value signatures, value bodies, patterns and inferred types. An added module keeps the access of the
  rule above. The parity tests use `Parity`; the engine's `elm` provider uses `Referenced`, so that generated Elm and
  MoonBit name no missing module (criterion C).
- A value or type is Public only if its module exposes it. An opaque export keeps the constructors Private.
- A `{-|` comment is a declaration's doc only when the declaration starts on the row right after the comment ends.
  Declaration docs keep their raw text between `{-|` and `-}`, with the spaces (`" A point. "`); a declaration
  without one gets `""`. The module doc is the first other `{-|` comment anywhere in the file, without its first 3
  and last 3 characters (`String.dropLeft 3 >> String.dropRight 3`); without one the module has no doc.
- Value inputs: the arguments, then the arguments of leading lambdas (also inside parentheses), while each is a plain
  variable and, for an annotated value, while the rest of the annotation is a function type. A type alias of a
  function type stops the inputs.
- An annotated value gets its signature from the annotation. An unannotated value and an unannotated let definition
  get marked `t-<n>` placeholders (the unknown marker of `morphir-ir`), one for each position, and inference fills them.

### Values

- Literals: Elm integer literals are `number`, so the frontend writes **no** `Int` fact (unlike Scheme). `True` and
  `False` are `BoolLiteral`, as in morphir-elm. Hex, float, char and string literals map directly.
- Operators and prefix operators become SDK function references through morphir-elm's fixed operator table
  (`mapOperator`: `++` is `basics#append`, `::` is `list#cons`, `>>`/`<<` are `composeRight`/`composeLeft`); `|>` and
  `<|` become plain applications. Negation is `basics#negate`, except that `-1` and `-2.5` fold into the literal.
- A whole-number literal that inference types as `Float` becomes a `FloatLiteral` (`Infer.fixNumberLiterals`).
- morphir-elm refuses top-level mutual recursion; the frontend accepts it (Elm does).
- `case` is `PatternMatch`. `if` is `IfThenElse`. Lambdas, tuples, lists, records, field access, field functions and
  record update map to their IR forms.
- A let block is split into `LetDefinition` chains, with `LetRecursion` for mutually recursive groups, in
  morphir-elm's dependency order (DFS post-order, or Kosaraju components when there is a cycle), not source order.
  Let definitions are never lifted. A destructuring let is `Destructure`.
- A value that inference leaves generic stays generic.

### Rules settled by the parity fixtures

Confirmed: an unannotated value gets plain type variables such as `t4` from morphir-elm, without the `number`
class, where IR inference gives a `number` variable. The normalizer compares type variables by position only, and
`parity_gaps` pins any class difference.

For a construct whose morphir-elm form is not yet confirmed, the parity fixtures decide, and the spec records the rule
when it is confirmed. Open now: record-alias constructors used as functions; `|>`, `<|`, `>>` and `<<`; the type of an
unannotated top-level number.

## 6. Testing

### Corpus

Each project is in `pkgs/morphir-elm/conformance/projects/<name>/`, with `morphir.json`, `src/**/*.elm` and
`expected/morphir-ir.json`. `SOURCES.md` records the origin of each project (own, finos/morphir-elm or
finos/morphir-examples), its commit and its license.

- **Own feature projects**, one per area: types and aliases; custom types and access; records and field functions;
  `case`; `let` with recursion and destructuring; operators and pipes; lambdas; cross-module imports and aliases; SDK
  modules; `Morphir.SDK.*` modules.
- **finos/morphir-elm test data**, for example rentals.
- **finos/morphir-examples.** A project that `morphir-elm make` cannot build, or that needs an upstream fix, is listed
  with the reason. Upstream PRs to finos/morphir-examples are drafted and wait for the maintainer's approval.

### Refresh

`scripts/elm-parity-refresh.mbtx` (mise task `elm:parity-refresh`) runs pinned `morphir-elm` 2.100.0 through npm on
each project and writes `expected/morphir-ir.json`. It also regenerates an embedded MoonBit data file, so that the
tests run on all four targets without file input. A CI job runs the refresh and fails on any difference.

### Parity test

For each project: compile with the frontend; migrate the expected classic IR to v4; normalize both (drop source
locations, rename type variables per declaration in first-occurrence order, sort maps); compare modules, access, docs,
type definitions, value bodies and the inferred type on every node. `parity_gaps` pins each known difference with a
reason and a bead, and the test fails when a pinned gap closes. An unannotated
definition's declared type in morphir-elm output comes from a first inference pass against an empty distribution, so
its placeholder variables are masked in the comparison; node types are compared everywhere.

### Round trip

For every corpus IR and the vendored classic fixtures: the Elm backend generates Elm; the frontend compiles it again;
the normalized result equals the normalized input.

### Unit and engine tests

- `mapping`, `resolve`, `lower` and the driver each have their own tests, including every error code.
- Engine e2e: `e2e:elm-moonbit` and `e2e:elm-elm` compile every corpus project through the engine with the `elm`
  provider (`pkgs/morphir-engine/acceptance/elm`, whose sources the refresh writes) and generate MoonBit and Elm.
  `moon build` and `elm make` must accept the output. Projects that do not generate yet, such as generic values that
  wait for `morphir-ukvn.5.22.11`, are pinned in a gaps map with a bead.

## 7. Engine

- A new `SourceCompiler` kind, `ProjectCompiler`, takes all sources of one language in a project and gives one
  `IRUnit`. The plan groups those files into one job. Public API: `SourceProfile.compile` becomes the enum
  `SourceCompile`, `PerFile` (one unit per file, as before) or `PerProject` (one call with `ProjectSources`: the
  project name and `exposed_modules` as written, and the sources in path order). The unit id of a project is its
  canonical name. A project compiler reports all problems with `RejectedSources`, one diagnostic per file. It needs a
  checkpoint or generator backend, refuses a single-file request and accepts at most `max_documents` sources (up to
  1024).
- An `elm` source provider (package `finos/morphir-engine/elm`, provider `finos/morphir-elm`) registers language
  `elm`, extension `.elm` and profile `library`. It reads `project.name` as the package and
  `project.exposed_modules` as `exposed`, and asks the frontend for `Referenced` output modules. The engine core does
  not register it; CLI and workbench wiring is `morphir-ukvn.5.22.4`.
- The frontend chooses the output modules and sets access itself. The plan skips its own exposure step for a project
  compiler, and the checkpoint path accepts `exposed_modules` in that case. So Elm to `moonbit` and Elm to `elm` generation work.
- The frontend runs inference itself, so `pipeline.inference` is not needed for Elm. `check` still works on its
  output.

## 8. Out of scope

- Ports, effect modules, GLSL, `Debug.*` and infix declarations.
- Third-party Elm packages, and Elm core modules that the SDK does not cover.
- `morphir.json` `dependencies` (other Morphir IR packages).
- `morphir.json` discovery, CLI and workbench (`morphir-ukvn.5.22.4`).
- Specialization of generic values for MoonBit (`morphir-ukvn.5.22.11`).
- Incremental and partial compilation.

## 9. Plans

The plans accumulate on one branch, and the PR opens when the maintainer asks (changed 2026-10-14; first one PR
for each plan). After each plan, the part already built works and is tested.

1. **Plan 1, structure and types:** extract `mapping`; driver with parse, module rules and resolve; lower type
   definitions, signatures, access and docs; refresh task; own feature projects; parity harness for everything
   except value bodies.
2. **Plan 2, values:** lower expressions, patterns, lets and operators; inference in the driver; full-body parity;
   round-trip harness.
3. **Plan 3, engine and corpus:** `Referenced` output modules; `ProjectCompiler` kind and `elm` source provider;
   checkpoint access for project compilers; `e2e:elm-moonbit` and `e2e:elm-elm`; import of the finos/morphir-elm and
   finos/morphir-examples projects and the list of upstream PRs.

## 10. Risks

- **Unknown morphir-elm rules.** Some lowering rules are confirmed only by the fixtures. Mitigation: Plan 1 creates
  the refresh task first, so every later rule is checked against real output.
- **morphir-examples drift.** Some examples may not build with morphir-elm 2.100.0. Mitigation: list them with the
  reason; propose upstream PRs only with approval.
- **Inference gaps.** A morphir-elm type that IR inference does not reproduce is pinned in `parity_gaps` and filed
  under `morphir-ukvn.5.22.7`.

  modules that nothing imports are not checked, except for parse errors and import cycles. The output keeps the
  exposed modules and the processed modules that they reach through type definitions and value-body references.
  A module named only in value signatures, used only through constructors, imported and unused, or not imported, is
  dropped. Exposed modules are Public; another output module is Public only when an exposed module shows one of its
  types in a public definition (first name per module, in Elm order), otherwise Private. The README `## Frontend`
  section of `pkgs/morphir-elm` states the full rule.
- Output modules for code generation (maintainer decision on I3, option b, 2026-10-14): `compile_project` takes
  `output? : OutputModules`. `Parity`, the default, keeps the selection above, so the output can name a type of a
  module it drops. `Referenced` also keeps every processed module that an output module names, transitively: in type
  definitions, value signatures, value bodies, patterns and inferred types. An added module keeps the access of the
  rule above. The parity tests use `Parity`; the engine's `elm` provider uses `Referenced`, so that generated Elm and
  MoonBit name no missing module (criterion C).
- A value or type is Public only if its module exposes it. An opaque export keeps the constructors Private.
- A `{-|` comment is a declaration's doc only when the declaration starts on the row right after the comment ends.
  Declaration docs keep their raw text between `{-|` and `-}`, with the spaces (`" A point. "`); a declaration
  without one gets `""`. The module doc is the first other `{-|` comment anywhere in the file, without its first 3
  and last 3 characters (`String.dropLeft 3 >> String.dropRight 3`); without one the module has no doc.
- Value inputs: the arguments, then the arguments of leading lambdas (also inside parentheses), while each is a plain
  variable and, for an annotated value, while the rest of the annotation is a function type. A type alias of a
  function type stops the inputs.
- An annotated value gets its signature from the annotation. An unannotated value and an unannotated let definition
  get marked `t-<n>` placeholders (the unknown marker of `morphir-ir`), one for each position, and inference fills them.

### Values

- Literals: Elm integer literals are `number`, so the frontend writes **no** `Int` fact (unlike Scheme). `True` and
  `False` are `BoolLiteral`, as in morphir-elm. Hex, float, char and string literals map directly.
- Operators and prefix operators become SDK function references through morphir-elm's fixed operator table
  (`mapOperator`: `++` is `basics#append`, `::` is `list#cons`, `>>`/`<<` are `composeRight`/`composeLeft`); `|>` and
  `<|` become plain applications. Negation is `basics#negate`, except that `-1` and `-2.5` fold into the literal.
- A whole-number literal that inference types as `Float` becomes a `FloatLiteral` (`Infer.fixNumberLiterals`).
- morphir-elm refuses top-level mutual recursion; the frontend accepts it (Elm does).
- `case` is `PatternMatch`. `if` is `IfThenElse`. Lambdas, tuples, lists, records, field access, field functions and
  record update map to their IR forms.
- A let block is split into `LetDefinition` chains, with `LetRecursion` for mutually recursive groups, in
  morphir-elm's dependency order (DFS post-order, or Kosaraju components when there is a cycle), not source order.
  Let definitions are never lifted. A destructuring let is `Destructure`.
- A value that inference leaves generic stays generic.

### Rules settled by the parity fixtures

Confirmed: an unannotated value gets plain type variables such as `t4` from morphir-elm, without the `number`
class, where IR inference gives a `number` variable. The normalizer compares type variables by position only, and
`parity_gaps` pins any class difference.

For a construct whose morphir-elm form is not yet confirmed, the parity fixtures decide, and the spec records the rule
when it is confirmed. Open now: record-alias constructors used as functions; `|>`, `<|`, `>>` and `<<`; the type of an
unannotated top-level number.

## 6. Testing

### Corpus

Each project is in `pkgs/morphir-elm/conformance/projects/<name>/`, with `morphir.json`, `src/**/*.elm` and
`expected/morphir-ir.json`. `SOURCES.md` records the origin of each project (own, finos/morphir-elm or
finos/morphir-examples), its commit and its license.

- **Own feature projects**, one per area: types and aliases; custom types and access; records and field functions;
  `case`; `let` with recursion and destructuring; operators and pipes; lambdas; cross-module imports and aliases; SDK
  modules; `Morphir.SDK.*` modules.
- **finos/morphir-elm test data**, for example rentals.
- **finos/morphir-examples.** A project that `morphir-elm make` cannot build, or that needs an upstream fix, is listed
  with the reason. Upstream PRs to finos/morphir-examples are drafted and wait for the maintainer's approval.

### Refresh

`scripts/elm-parity-refresh.mbtx` (mise task `elm:parity-refresh`) runs pinned `morphir-elm` 2.100.0 through npm on
each project and writes `expected/morphir-ir.json`. It also regenerates an embedded MoonBit data file, so that the
tests run on all four targets without file input. A CI job runs the refresh and fails on any difference.

### Parity test

For each project: compile with the frontend; migrate the expected classic IR to v4; normalize both (drop source
locations, rename type variables per declaration in first-occurrence order, sort maps); compare modules, access, docs,
type definitions, value bodies and the inferred type on every node. `parity_gaps` pins each known difference with a
reason and a bead, and the test fails when a pinned gap closes. An unannotated
definition's declared type in morphir-elm output comes from a first inference pass against an empty distribution, so
its placeholder variables are masked in the comparison; node types are compared everywhere.

### Round trip

For every corpus IR and the vendored classic fixtures: the Elm backend generates Elm; the frontend compiles it again;
the normalized result equals the normalized input.

### Unit and engine tests

- `mapping`, `resolve`, `lower` and the driver each have their own tests, including every error code.
- Engine e2e: `e2e:elm-moonbit` and `e2e:elm-elm` compile every corpus project through the engine with the `elm`
  provider (`pkgs/morphir-engine/acceptance/elm`, whose sources the refresh writes) and generate MoonBit and Elm.
  `moon build` and `elm make` must accept the output. Projects that do not generate yet, such as generic values that
  wait for `morphir-ukvn.5.22.11`, are pinned in a gaps map with a bead.

## 7. Engine

- A new `SourceCompiler` kind, `ProjectCompiler`, takes all sources of one language in a project and gives one
  `IRUnit`. The plan groups those files into one job. Public API: `SourceProfile.compile` becomes the enum
  `SourceCompile`, `PerFile` (one unit per file, as before) or `PerProject` (one call with `ProjectSources`: the
  project name and `exposed_modules` as written, and the sources in path order). The unit id of a project is its
  canonical name. A project compiler reports all problems with `RejectedSources`, one diagnostic per file. It needs a
  checkpoint or generator backend and refuses a single-file request. It has no document limit:
  `SourceCapabilities.max_documents` becomes `Int?`, a project compiler must declare `None`, and the CLI prints
  `documents per unit: no limit` (JSON `null`). No number stands for "no limit". A file compiler keeps a number from 1
  to 64. The output budget `unit_limits` bounds a project unit.
- An `elm` source provider (package `finos/morphir-engine/elm`, provider `finos/morphir-elm`) registers language
  `elm`, extension `.elm` and profile `library`. It reads `project.name` as the package and
  `project.exposed_modules` as `exposed`, and asks the frontend for `Referenced` output modules. The engine core does
  not register it; CLI and workbench wiring is `morphir-ukvn.5.22.4`.
- The frontend chooses the output modules and sets access itself. The plan skips its own exposure step for a project
  compiler, and the checkpoint path accepts `exposed_modules` in that case. So Elm to `moonbit` and Elm to `elm` generation work.
- The frontend runs inference itself, so `pipeline.inference` is not needed for Elm. `check` still works on its
  output.

## 8. Out of scope

- Ports, effect modules, GLSL, `Debug.*` and infix declarations.
- Third-party Elm packages, and Elm core modules that the SDK does not cover.
- `morphir.json` `dependencies` (other Morphir IR packages).
- `morphir.json` discovery, CLI and workbench (`morphir-ukvn.5.22.4`).
- Specialization of generic values for MoonBit (`morphir-ukvn.5.22.11`).
- Incremental and partial compilation.

## 9. Plans

The plans accumulate on one branch, and the PR opens when the maintainer asks (changed 2026-10-14; first one PR
for each plan). After each plan, the part already built works and is tested.

1. **Plan 1, structure and types:** extract `mapping`; driver with parse, module rules and resolve; lower type
   definitions, signatures, access and docs; refresh task; own feature projects; parity harness for everything
   except value bodies.
2. **Plan 2, values:** lower expressions, patterns, lets and operators; inference in the driver; full-body parity;
   round-trip harness.
3. **Plan 3, engine and corpus:** `Referenced` output modules; `ProjectCompiler` kind and `elm` source provider;
   checkpoint access for project compilers; `e2e:elm-moonbit` and `e2e:elm-elm`; import of the finos/morphir-elm and
   finos/morphir-examples projects and the list of upstream PRs.

## 10. Risks

- **Unknown morphir-elm rules.** Some lowering rules are confirmed only by the fixtures. Mitigation: Plan 1 creates
  the refresh task first, so every later rule is checked against real output.
- **morphir-examples drift.** Some examples may not build with morphir-elm 2.100.0. Mitigation: list them with the
  reason; propose upstream PRs only with approval.
- **Inference gaps.** A morphir-elm type that IR inference does not reproduce is pinned in `parity_gaps` and filed
  under `morphir-ukvn.5.22.7`.

design:
# Elm backend with krueger: design

Date: 2026-10-02. Status: approved 2026-10-02. Amended during planning (section 9).

## 1. Purpose and context

This is sub-project 1 of the Elm initiative (see the umbrella epic). The initiative gives finos/morphir-moonbit an Elm
frontend and an Elm backend that use [moonrockz/krueger](https://github.com/moonrockz/krueger). The order is:

1. Elm backend (this spec): current Morphir IR to Elm source.
2. IR type inference: a language-neutral Hindley-Milner pass over Morphir IR.
3. Elm frontend: Elm source to typed Morphir IR, with parity against `morphir-elm make`.
4. Wiring: `morphir.json` project discovery, CLI and workbench.

The backend comes first. It gives a visible result quickly, it does not need type inference, and its output is the
round-trip harness for sub-projects 2 and 3.

krueger 0.4.0 parses Elm 0.19.1 into the elm-syntax 7.3.9 AST and prints an AST as Elm in the elm-format 0.8.7
layout (`print_file`, width 120 by default). The printer raises `PrintError` with a `NodePath` when an AST cannot
print as valid Elm. It prints doc comments but not regular comments.

### Success criteria

- `pipeline.backend = "elm"` generates an Elm project from current IR through `Engine::plan` and `Engine::execute`.
- In the `model` profile, `elm make` accepts the generated project for every fixture in the golden corpus that
  contains no refused construct.
- Every generated file parses with `krueger.parse_module` with no diagnostics, in both profiles.
- The same input gives the same output bytes.

## 2. Architecture

### Package

New workspace member `pkgs/morphir-elm`, module `finos/morphir-elm`. It depends on `finos/morphir-ir` and
`moonrockz/krueger@0.4.0`. Like `finos/morphir-moonbit`, it has no engine, host, filesystem, process or network
imports. This sub-project adds only `backend/`. Sub-project 3 adds `frontend/` beside it.

| Unit | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| `backend/names` | Morphir `Name`, `Path` and `FQName` to Elm identifiers and module names. The Elm module name is the package path followed by the module path. Reserved words get the suffix `_`. Constrained type variables get their Elm prefix. |
| `backend/mapping` | The `Mapping` table from `FQName` to `Operator`, `Function` or `Type`, each with an optional import. It holds the built-in partial SDK table, merges overrides and removes entries. |
| `backend/lower` | Current IR types, values, patterns and definitions to krueger AST. The profile decides how references resolve. |
| `backend/project` | One `.elm` file for each IR module, plus `elm.json` and `morphir.json`. |
| `backend/generate` | Entry point `generate(Input, Options) -> Output`. Calls `@printer.print_file` for each module. Raises `ElmGenerationError`. |

`Options` holds `profile`, `placeholders`, `width`, `elm_package`, `mapping` and `packages` (section 4).

### Engine changes

- `GenerationBackend.generate` gets a third parameter: the backend options table from `[backends.<name>]`.
- A generation backend supplies a schema for its table. The engine validates the table and reports unknown keys and
  bad values as configuration diagnostics, with the provenance from `config.Document`.
- The MoonBit generator accepts the new parameter and ignores it. Its behavior does not change.
- `Engine::new` registers the generation backend `elm` beside `moonbit`.

### Out of scope

The frontend, type inference, `morphir.json` discovery, CLI flags other than configuration, workbench UI, regular
comments, and the IR to Elm to IR round trip. The round trip comes with sub-project 3.

## 3. Profiles and SDK mapping

There are two profiles.

- `model` (default) generates a Morphir Elm model project. References with a mapping entry use idiomatic Elm, for
  example `+` for `morphir/SDK:basics#add` and `List.map` for `morphir/SDK:list#map`. This is the inverse of the
  morphir-elm frontend.
- `literal` ignores the mapping. Every reference stays fully qualified, for example
  `Morphir.SDK.Basics.add a b`. It is a debug view of the IR.

The `model` profile does not need a full mapping of the Morphir SDK. The built-in table covers only the references
that have a clear Elm idiom. A reference with no mapping entry stays a qualified reference with its `import`, for
example `Morphir.SDK.LocalDate.addDays`. The `finos/morphir-elm` Elm package supplies those modules, and
`backend/project` adds it to `elm.json` only when the generated code uses an unmapped `Morphir.SDK` reference. A
missing mapping entry never stops generation.

The mapping is data. Configuration can override or extend the built-in table for any `FQName`, not only SDK
references, so a user can map references in their own package to existing Elm code. An empty entry removes a built-in
entry, and the reference falls back to the qualified form.

## 4. Configuration

```toml
[pipeline]
backend = "elm"

[backends.elm]
profile = "model"            # "model" (default) | "literal"
placeholders = "refuse"      # "refuse" (default) | "debug-todo"
width = 120
elm-package = "finos/morphir-elm 22.0.2"

[backends.elm.mapping]
"morphir/SDK:basics#add" = { operator = "+" }
"morphir/SDK:list#map" = { function = "List.map" }
"morphir/SDK:decimal#decimal" = { type = "Decimal.Decimal", import = "MyCo.Decimal as Decimal" }
"morphir/SDK:basics#max" = {}

[backends.elm.packages]
"acme/common" = { package = "acme/common 1.0.0" }
"acme/local" = { source = "../acme-local/src" }
```

- `elm-package` is the Elm package and version for unmapped `Morphir.SDK` references. The default is the
  `finos/morphir-elm` version in that repository's `elm.json` (22.0.2 on 2026-10-02). The implementation plan
  confirms that the version is published on package.elm-lang.org before it becomes the default.
- A `mapping` key is an IR `FQName` in canonical text form. A value has exactly one of `operator`, `function` or
  `type`, and an optional `import`. A malformed key or value is the configuration diagnostic `invalid_mapping`.
- `packages` maps a Morphir dependency package to an Elm package with a version, or to a source directory, for
  `elm.json`. A dependency with no entry does not stop generation. The `elm make` check reports it.
- In the `literal` profile, a non-empty `mapping` gives a warning, not an error.

## 5. Lowering rules

### Distributions and modules

- `Library` and `Application` generate every module of the package. For `Application`, each entry point becomes the
  doc-comment attribute `@entryPoint <kind>` on its target value. krueger reads doc-comment attributes, so the
  frontend can restore entry points.
- `Specs` generate type declarations. Value specifications have no body, so they follow the placeholder policy.
- References into dependency packages stay qualified.
- Public types and values are exposed. Private ones are not. A custom type with private constructors is exposed as
  `T`, not `T(..)`.
- Module documentation becomes the module doc comment. Member documentation becomes the doc comment of the
  declaration.

### Types

- A `Reference` with a mapping entry uses it. Any other `Reference` is qualified.
- `Record`, `ExtensibleRecord`, `Function` and `Unit` map directly to their Elm forms.
- A `Tuple` with more than three elements is refused with `tuple_arity`. Elm 0.19 rejects such tuples.
- A type variable with a `constraints` entry in its `TypeAttributes` gets the Elm prefix of that constraint
  (`number`, `comparable`, `appendable` or `compappend`). An unconstrained variable whose name starts with one of
  these prefixes is renamed so that Elm does not read it as constrained.
- Type aliases stay aliases. Custom types keep their constructor order.
- Derived types are refused with `derived_type`. A follow-on bead covers them.

### Values

- A chain of `Apply` becomes one `Application`.
- A mapped operator with both arguments becomes an `OperatorApplication`. With fewer arguments it becomes a prefix
  operator, for example `(+) a`.
- `LetDefinition`, `LetRecursion` and `Destructure` merge into one `let` block where scoping allows.
- `FieldFunction` becomes `.field`.
- Elm requires a variable as the target of a record update. `UpdateRecord` with any other target binds the target to
  a fresh name in a `let` first.
- `Int` literals keep the exact lexeme. A value outside the Elm range is refused through the printer's
  `UnrepresentableInt`.
- `Decimal` literals are refused with `decimal_literal` until a construction mapping exists.
- Fresh names never capture names in scope.

### v4-only constructs

- `Annotation` becomes the doc-comment attribute `@<fqname> <arguments>`.
- `ExternalBody` with a fallback value emits the fallback, plus `@external <platform> <name>` for each binding.
- `Hole`, `IncompleteBody`, `NativeBody`, `ExternalBody` without a fallback, and `Specs` values follow the
  placeholder policy:
  - `placeholders = "refuse"` (default) raises `ElmGenerationError` with code `placeholder`.
  - `placeholders = "debug-todo"` emits `Debug.todo "<reason>"`. `elm make` accepts this, but
    `elm make --optimize` does not.

### Determinism

Declarations keep IR order. Imports are sorted. The same input and options give the same bytes.

## 6. Errors

`ElmGenerationError { code, node_path, detail }`, where `node_path` identifies the IR node. The codes are:

| Code | Cause |
| --- | --- |
| `tuple_arity` | Tuple with more than three elements |
| `derived_type` | Derived type definition |
| `decimal_literal` | Decimal literal with no construction mapping |
| `placeholder` | Construct with no body while `placeholders = "refuse"` |
| `invalid_mapping` | Mapping entry that is not valid at generation time, for example an operator that krueger does not know |
| `print` | krueger `PrintError`, with the IR node path of the AST node that failed |

A `print` error means that the lowering made an AST that is not valid, so it is a backend defect. Tests treat any
`print` error as a failure.

Generation of a module stops at its first error. All modules are tried, so one run reports every failing module.

## 7. Testing

- **Unit tests**: `names` (case, reserved words, constraint prefixes), `mapping` (merge, override, removal) and each
  lowering rule in both profiles, as snapshot tests of the printed Elm.
- **Golden corpus**: the classic v3 reference models in `pkgs/morphir-ir/conformance/fixtures` and the SDK examples,
  migrated to current IR and generated in both profiles. Output snapshots must be stable.
- **Parse-back law**: every generated file parses with `krueger.parse_module` with no diagnostics. This runs on all
  MoonBit targets.
- **`elm make` acceptance**: `pkgs/morphir-elm/scripts/test-elm-make.mjs` runs `elm make` on the generated `model`
  projects, with the npm `elm` 0.19.1 package pinned in `package.json`. Mise task `test:elm` runs it, in the same
  pattern as `test:compiler`, and CI runs the task. `literal` output gets only the parse-back law.
- **Engine tests**: options table pass-through, schema validation and diagnostics, and `elm` registration through
  `Engine::plan` and `Engine::execute`. The MoonBit generator tests stay unchanged and must pass.

## 8. Follow-on work

- Derived types (`derived_type`) and decimal literal construction (`decimal_literal`).
- Sub-projects 2, 3 and 4 of the initiative.

## 9. Amendments

These come from facts found while writing the implementation plan (2026-10-02). Where this section and the sections above disagree, this section wins.

1. **Package-type `elm.json`.** An application `elm.json` must list every indirect dependency with an exact version,
   which needs a solver. A package `elm.json` takes version ranges, so the generator writes `"type": "package"`.
   Because of this, `[backends.elm.packages]` entries take only `{ package = "author/name 1.2.3" }`. The
   source-directory form is a follow-on.
2. **Option key spelling.** `elm_package`, not `elm-package`, to match the snake_case keys in the rest of the
   configuration (`source_directory`, `out_dir`).
3. **Doc-comment attributes follow the krueger grammar.** An attribute name is `lower ("." lower)*` and its value is
   Elm data. The generator writes an `attributes` code block with `@morphir.entry { kind = "main", name = "..." }`,
   `@morphir.annotation { fqname = "...", ... }` and `@morphir.external { platform = "...", name = "..." }`.
4. **Constraint attribute.** Key `typeclass` in `TypeAttributes.constraints`. The value is `Text` or `Array` of
   `Text`. `["appendable", "comparable"]` becomes `compappend`. Any other set is `elm.unsupported_constraint`.
5. **More error codes.** `elm.int_literal` (lexeme outside Int64), `elm.document_literal`, `elm.literal_pattern`
   (float or decimal pattern, which Elm rejects), `elm.unsupported_constraint`, `elm.name_collision` (two IR names
   give one Elm name in a module), `elm.invalid_option`, `elm.cancelled`.
6. **Generation backend contract.** `GenerationBackend` gets `validate_options : (Json) -> Unit raise` and
   `targets : Array[String]`. A generator with no targets defaults to `pipeline.validation = "source-only"`, and
   `"required"` is refused with `build.unsupported_target`. The MoonBit generator declares
   `["wasm", "wasm-gc", "js", "native"]` and keeps its behavior.
7. **Built-in mapping source.** The table is generated from `pkgs/morphir-sdk/conformance/bindings.json`: every
   binding whose `semanticSource` is `elm/core 1.0.5` maps to the elm/core function of the same name, plus a
   hand-written list of types, constructors and operators. Other SDK references stay qualified.
8. **`elm.print` node path.** The path names the IR declaration whose AST did not print. The generator finds it by
   printing each declaration alone after `print_file` fails.
9. **No signatures on `let` functions.** Elm reads type variables in a `let` annotation as new rigid variables, so
   generated `let` functions have no signature.
10. **No shadowing.** Elm rejects a local name that shadows another name in scope. The lowering renames such names
    (`x` becomes `x_1`).
11. **Existing fixture corpus in engine tests.** The `finos/morphir-moonbit/fixtures` IR builders are already a
    dependency of `finos/morphir-engine` tests. The engine tests run the `elm` generator over them, so the Elm module
    does not depend on `finos/morphir-moonbit`.

| `backend/project` | One `.elm` file for each IR module, plus `elm.json` and `morphir.json`. |
| `backend/generate` | Entry point `generate(Input, Options) -> Output`. Calls `@printer.print_file` for each module. Raises `ElmGenerationError`. |

`Options` holds `profile`, `placeholders`, `width`, `elm_package`, `mapping` and `packages` (section 4).

### Engine changes

- `GenerationBackend.generate` gets a third parameter: the backend options table from `[backends.<name>]`.
- A generation backend supplies a schema for its table. The engine validates the table and reports unknown keys and
  bad values as configuration diagnostics, with the provenance from `config.Document`.
- The MoonBit generator accepts the new parameter and ignores it. Its behavior does not change.
- `Engine::new` registers the generation backend `elm` beside `moonbit`.

### Out of scope

The frontend, type inference, `morphir.json` discovery, CLI flags other than configuration, workbench UI, regular
comments, and the IR to Elm to IR round trip. The round trip comes with sub-project 3.

## 3. Profiles and SDK mapping

There are two profiles.

- `model` (default) generates a Morphir Elm model project. References with a mapping entry use idiomatic Elm, for
  example `+` for `morphir/SDK:basics#add` and `List.map` for `morphir/SDK:list#map`. This is the inverse of the
  morphir-elm frontend.
- `literal` ignores the mapping. Every reference stays fully qualified, for example
  `Morphir.SDK.Basics.add a b`. It is a debug view of the IR.

The `model` profile does not need a full mapping of the Morphir SDK. The built-in table covers only the references
that have a clear Elm idiom. A reference with no mapping entry stays a qualified reference with its `import`, for
example `Morphir.SDK.LocalDate.addDays`. The `finos/morphir-elm` Elm package supplies those modules, and
`backend/project` adds it to `elm.json` only when the generated code uses an unmapped `Morphir.SDK` reference. A
missing mapping entry never stops generation.

The mapping is data. Configuration can override or extend the built-in table for any `FQName`, not only SDK
references, so a user can map references in their own package to existing Elm code. An empty entry removes a built-in
entry, and the reference falls back to the qualified form.

## 4. Configuration

```toml
[pipeline]
backend = "elm"

[backends.elm]
profile = "model"            # "model" (default) | "literal"
placeholders = "refuse"      # "refuse" (default) | "debug-todo"
width = 120
elm-package = "finos/morphir-elm 22.0.2"

[backends.elm.mapping]
"morphir/SDK:basics#add" = { operator = "+" }
"morphir/SDK:list#map" = { function = "List.map" }
"morphir/SDK:decimal#decimal" = { type = "Decimal.Decimal", import = "MyCo.Decimal as Decimal" }
"morphir/SDK:basics#max" = {}

[backends.elm.packages]
"acme/common" = { package = "acme/common 1.0.0" }
"acme/local" = { source = "../acme-local/src" }
```

- `elm-package` is the Elm package and version for unmapped `Morphir.SDK` references. The default is the
  `finos/morphir-elm` version in that repository's `elm.json` (22.0.2 on 2026-10-02). The implementation plan
  confirms that the version is published on package.elm-lang.org before it becomes the default.
- A `mapping` key is an IR `FQName` in canonical text form. A value has exactly one of `operator`, `function` or
  `type`, and an optional `import`. A malformed key or value is the configuration diagnostic `invalid_mapping`.
- `packages` maps a Morphir dependency package to an Elm package with a version, or to a source directory, for
  `elm.json`. A dependency with no entry does not stop generation. The `elm make` check reports it.
- In the `literal` profile, a non-empty `mapping` gives a warning, not an error.

## 5. Lowering rules

### Distributions and modules

- `Library` and `Application` generate every module of the package. For `Application`, each entry point becomes the
  doc-comment attribute `@entryPoint <kind>` on its target value. krueger reads doc-comment attributes, so the
  frontend can restore entry points.
- `Specs` generate type declarations. Value specifications have no body, so they follow the placeholder policy.
- References into dependency packages stay qualified.
- Public types and values are exposed. Private ones are not. A custom type with private constructors is exposed as
  `T`, not `T(..)`.
- Module documentation becomes the module doc comment. Member documentation becomes the doc comment of the
  declaration.

### Types

- A `Reference` with a mapping entry uses it. Any other `Reference` is qualified.
- `Record`, `ExtensibleRecord`, `Function` and `Unit` map directly to their Elm forms.
- A `Tuple` with more than three elements is refused with `tuple_arity`. Elm 0.19 rejects such tuples.
- A type variable with a `constraints` entry in its `TypeAttributes` gets the Elm prefix of that constraint
  (`number`, `comparable`, `appendable` or `compappend`). An unconstrained variable whose name starts with one of
  these prefixes is renamed so that Elm does not read it as constrained.
- Type aliases stay aliases. Custom types keep their constructor order.
- Derived types are refused with `derived_type`. A follow-on bead covers them.

### Values

- A chain of `Apply` becomes one `Application`.
- A mapped operator with both arguments becomes an `OperatorApplication`. With fewer arguments it becomes a prefix
  operator, for example `(+) a`.
- `LetDefinition`, `LetRecursion` and `Destructure` merge into one `let` block where scoping allows.
- `FieldFunction` becomes `.field`.
- Elm requires a variable as the target of a record update. `UpdateRecord` with any other target binds the target to
  a fresh name in a `let` first.
- `Int` literals keep the exact lexeme. A value outside the Elm range is refused through the printer's
  `UnrepresentableInt`.
- `Decimal` literals are refused with `decimal_literal` until a construction mapping exists.
- Fresh names never capture names in scope.

### v4-only constructs

- `Annotation` becomes the doc-comment attribute `@<fqname> <arguments>`.
- `ExternalBody` with a fallback value emits the fallback, plus `@external <platform> <name>` for each binding.
- `Hole`, `IncompleteBody`, `NativeBody`, `ExternalBody` without a fallback, and `Specs` values follow the
  placeholder policy:
  - `placeholders = "refuse"` (default) raises `ElmGenerationError` with code `placeholder`.
  - `placeholders = "debug-todo"` emits `Debug.todo "<reason>"`. `elm make` accepts this, but
    `elm make --optimize` does not.

### Determinism

Declarations keep IR order. Imports are sorted. The same input and options give the same bytes.

## 6. Errors

`ElmGenerationError { code, node_path, detail }`, where `node_path` identifies the IR node. The codes are:

| Code | Cause |
| --- | --- |
| `tuple_arity` | Tuple with more than three elements |
| `derived_type` | Derived type definition |
| `decimal_literal` | Decimal literal with no construction mapping |
| `placeholder` | Construct with no body while `placeholders = "refuse"` |
| `invalid_mapping` | Mapping entry that is not valid at generation time, for example an operator that krueger does not know |
| `print` | krueger `PrintError`, with the IR node path of the AST node that failed |

A `print` error means that the lowering made an AST that is not valid, so it is a backend defect. Tests treat any
`print` error as a failure.

Generation of a module stops at its first error. All modules are tried, so one run reports every failing module.

## 7. Testing

- **Unit tests**: `names` (case, reserved words, constraint prefixes), `mapping` (merge, override, removal) and each
  lowering rule in both profiles, as snapshot tests of the printed Elm.
- **Golden corpus**: the classic v3 reference models in `pkgs/morphir-ir/conformance/fixtures` and the SDK examples,
  migrated to current IR and generated in both profiles. Output snapshots must be stable.
- **Parse-back law**: every generated file parses with `krueger.parse_module` with no diagnostics. This runs on all
  MoonBit targets.
- **`elm make` acceptance**: `pkgs/morphir-elm/scripts/test-elm-make.mjs` runs `elm make` on the generated `model`
  projects, with the npm `elm` 0.19.1 package pinned in `package.json`. Mise task `test:elm` runs it, in the same
  pattern as `test:compiler`, and CI runs the task. `literal` output gets only the parse-back law.
- **Engine tests**: options table pass-through, schema validation and diagnostics, and `elm` registration through
  `Engine::plan` and `Engine::execute`. The MoonBit generator tests stay unchanged and must pass.

## 8. Follow-on work

- Derived types (`derived_type`) and decimal literal construction (`decimal_literal`).
- Sub-projects 2, 3 and 4 of the initiative.
