Desktop + browserDesign proposalMoonBit / Rabbita / Proton

One workbench.
Three ways to run Morphir.

Explore models, try source snippets, and run worksheets in a shared application shell. Start entirely in the browser, connect to a local Morphir daemon, or use a native desktop app.

Share the experience

A shared shell with distinct model, playground, and workspace views.

Make execution visible

The user knows which runtime owns the model and each job.

Keep capabilities explicit

Each host advertises the operations it can actually perform.

01

Intent & scope

Build a Morphir workbench using the MoonBit UI stack demonstrated by Proton and OpenSeek. Preserve the portable Morphir engine, and put environment-specific execution and storage behind a service contract.

First workflow · proposed

Model Explorer

Import an IR distribution, navigate packages and modules, inspect types and values, enter typed inputs, and evaluate a portable function. The same fixture should work in every execution mode.

This is the initial scope assumption. Workspace builds follow once the shared execution boundary works.

Additional experience

Try Morphir

Start from an example or blank snippet, edit source, compile to IR, inspect types and generated output, or run a worksheet with results beside its expressions.

Workspace builds remain another experience. Keep room for future tools by letting each experience contribute its own sidebar and main view.

The user has accepted a shared application shell, runtime adapters, collapsible navigation, a contextual model tree, and a Try Morphir experience inspired by the TypeScript Playground and Scastie. Package names, protocol details, persistence behavior, and delivery stages below are proposals. This document describes a product to build; its diagrams do not demonstrate an implemented application.

Vocabulary follows CONTEXT.md. A workspace owns project membership and output ownership; a distribution is a delivered IR package; an artifact is a backend output. Here, “UI” means the interactive application. “Frontend” retains its compiler meaning inside a Morphir pipeline.

Merge readiness and current main

The maintainer approved squash merges of parent PR #1033 and MoonBit PR #42 when checks are green, including an administrator bypass where policy requires it. Main now contains PR #40 at 32f2033; merge 7e3fd35 integrates its rich MoonBit source units into this continuation. The engine/CLI explicitly registers the bounded Boolean source frontend. PR #41 subsequently landed at b1a0298 with all 19 CI contexts successful. It adds installed MoonBit source lowering to Ion and independent Boolean truth-table comparison through original source, Scheme and generated execution across required targets in debug/release. The fresh DamianReeves/workbench-invocation-admission continuation starts from merged main 40587e6 and includes both frontend phases. The local Workbench still compiles Scheme, so exposing MoonBit source selection in the browser/Proton worker remains a separate follow-up. No new connected capabilities are advertised.

Combined local verification passes. Parent PR #1033 merged at 95c1aecb after all 17 final-head contexts completed successfully, skipped or neutral. MoonBit PR #42 merged at 40587e6 after all 20 final-head contexts passed on 7e3fd35. No unresolved review threads remained. The approved admin bypass was used for the parent required-review rule; MoonBit merged normally. Both PR watchers observed MERGED and stopped.

02

Shell & experiences

The application shell owns experience navigation, runtime selection, jobs, and settings. The active experience supplies its contextual sidebar and main view. A model tree appears when exploring a model; it does not become permanent navigation for every tool.

Visual identity · adopted

Morphir's blue and orange

Use the cube mark and wordmark from FINOS Morphir. The live Morphir site sets primary blue to #00a3e2 and secondary orange to #ff6a00. White and neutral gray keep editors and model details readable. Orange marks the main compile or run action; blue marks navigation, selection, and links.

Brand blueAction orangeReadable blueNeutral surface

Use the site's darker blue #00729e for small text and focus outlines. Pair orange buttons with #1c1e21 text. Keep the logo's original vector colors, #16a2dc and #f26a21. Functional cube, code, and sidebar icons are workbench SVG drawings, not official Morphir brand assets. Labels stay available to assistive technology when the sidebar collapses.

All icons ship locally in the browser and Proton bundle. This HTML embeds the same SVG assets and rendered Mermaid diagrams, so it opens offline. The homepage's photographic hero is a reference for brand tone; editor panels use plain surfaces.

One navigation shell, experience-specific context

Shell regionModel ExplorerTry MorphirFuture experiences
Global navigationPersistent experience switcher, settings, runtime selector, and jobs. Expanded sidebar shows labels; compact rail retains accessible buttons and tooltips.
Contextual sidebarPackage/module/type/value tree, model search, selected distributionExamples, snippet files/outline, supported language and run settingsThe experience supplies its own panel or leaves it empty.
Main viewDefinition, relationships, documentation, typed evaluationSource/output split or worksheet with inline resultsNo model-explorer layout requirement
Collapse preferenceExpanded by default; preserve selected tree item and scroll positionCompact by default; remember the user's expansion choiceExperience default plus user override

Each experience registers an identity, route, main view, contextual sidebar contribution, commands, and required capabilities. The shell supplies pane controls and shared services; it does not assume a model is open. Switching experience and switching execution runtime are independent actions.

The same sidebar contains distinct global and contextual regions. Collapsing it hides contextual content and reduces global navigation to a compact rail. On small screens, use an overlay drawer with a persistent toolbar toggle, focus containment, Escape to close, and focus restored to the opener. Collapse never clears a draft or stops a job.

Try Morphir has two proposed layouts

TypeScript Playground reference

Compile / inspect

Editable source on one side; IR, types, generated artifacts, and diagnostics on the other. Choose examples, a supported source language, IR version, and target. Debounce compilation only when the provider supports bounded execution; make Run explicit.

Open the successful compiled revision in Model Explorer without replacing the source draft. This transition carries model identity and revision, not a filesystem requirement.

TypeScript Playground

Scastie reference

Worksheet / run

Run snippets with typed results aligned to expressions, plus output and diagnostics. Keep results tied to the executed revision so edits cannot make old annotations look current. Cancel or supersede earlier runs when the user requests a new one.

Language/runtime versions, dependencies, and worksheet instrumentation come from advertised capabilities. The Scastie interaction style does not imply a hosted execution service or arbitrary-library support.

Scastie worksheet and execution model

Proposed grouping: compile/inspect and worksheet/run are layouts within Try Morphir. The experience registry permits making them separate experiences if product testing favors that. Source editing needs an editable editor component; OpenSeek's readonly viewer alone does not provide it.

Sharing exports a portable snippet containing source, declared language/options, and allowed dependency metadata. A share link never includes daemon session secrets, local filesystem locators, or browser storage handles. Opening a shared snippet does not run it automatically. Large snippets can use a downloaded snippet file before any hosted storage is introduced.

  1. OpenImport an IR file or choose an available workspace. Show its identity and original IR version.
  2. ExploreSearch definitions, follow references, and keep a breadcrumb and navigation history.
  3. EvaluateBuild inputs from supported IR types. Validate them before starting a job.
  4. InspectRead typed results, diagnostics, and artifacts without losing the selected definition.

Interaction rules

Selection belongs in the URL where possible. Preserve search and evaluation drafts when switching definitions. Keep focus visible and support keyboard navigation, accessible labels, and native editing shortcuts.

On narrow screens, navigation becomes a drawer and evaluation becomes a full-width panel. On narrow screens, scroll diagrams and the workbench sketch horizontally inside their frames.

States that need real design

Empty model, invalid IR, unsupported version, unavailable runtime binding, unsupported input type, cancelled job, disconnected daemon, and failed publication each need their own explanation and recovery action.

When a capability is missing, show why the action is unavailable. Do not send an unsupported request and wait for failure.

03

Execution modes

Mode is a choice about where data and execution live. Make it explicit when opening a model. Switching modes creates a new runtime session; transferring a model between sessions is a separate, visible action.

“In this browser”

Serve static application assets. Run portable Morphir operations in a dedicated worker against an imported, in-memory model. Add browser persistence and offline asset caching after the first execution proof.

Data
Imported files, memory snapshots, then optional IndexedDB persistence.
Execution
MoonBit JS is the first candidate; compare WASM-GC after the worker contract works.
Boundary
Browser APIs and explicit imports. Host-only bindings and system subprocesses are unavailable.

“Local daemon”

The daemon owns workspace files, engine sessions, tooling, and jobs. Initially serve the same UI assets from the daemon's loopback origin. A separately hosted browser client requires a later connection and pairing design.

Data
Daemon-owned workspace snapshots and artifact storage; UI keeps navigation and drafts.
Execution
Session manifest over HTTP; connected JSON-RPC 2.0 requests and notifications over WebSocket. Durable job extensions remain proposed.
Boundary
Authenticated session, allowed origin and host validation, explicit workspace grants.

“Desktop runtime”

Package the shared web UI inside Proton. A native service executes through Morphir hosts and reports results over the Proton bridge. The desktop app may also connect to an existing daemon using the same daemon adapter.

Data
Granted local workspaces and application state in platform-specific directories.
Execution
Native Morphir service behind IPC, or the explicitly selected daemon.
Boundary
Native dialogs, menus, windows, and bridge permissions belong to the desktop shell.
Target behavior by host. Entries describe intended capabilities, not completed support.
CapabilityStandalone browserBrowser + daemonProton desktop
IR exploration & portable evaluationWorker executionDaemon executionNative or daemon execution
Local filesExplicit file import and exportDirectory handles are an optional browser enhancement.Through granted daemon workspacesThrough native dialogs and granted roots
Workspace buildsAdvertised in-memory compilers and generatorsNo general system toolchain or implicit package resolution.Host-advertised tooling and targetsHost-advertised tooling and targets
Live file watchingNo baseline OS watcherDaemon workspace eventsNative or daemon workspace events
Job lifetimeOwned by the browser sessionOwned by daemon; reconnect and query statusOwned by selected service; explicit close policy
OutputDownload or browser persistenceHost publication with reported guaranteesHost publication or native export

A daemon disconnect never silently moves a job into the browser. Keep its last known state and reconnect to the same service identity. An explicit “Use a browser copy” action creates a separate snapshot and explains what was transferred.

04

Architecture

Share the UI and domain contract. Keep transport, native integration, persistence, and scheduling in adapters. The engine continues to accept explicit host capabilities.

Shared application and domain logicRuntime-owned state and capabilitiesTransport adapter

Existing modules and planned adapters

Module / applicationOwnsIntegration constraint
apps/morphir-workbenchShared shell, explorer, source editors, input controls, bounded result presentation and local worker pipelineThe UI display tree and current JSON input schema are private; migrate typed execution boundaries through explicit adapters.
pkgs/morphir-executionPortable invocation values, suite validation, comparison policies and observation contractsReuse the versioned Ion and lossless tagged JSON codecs; no DOM, filesystem or native telemetry dependency.
pkgs/morphir-engine/executionPublic-entry planning, generated invocation manifests, provider execution and optional Scheme comparisonHost injects provider capabilities. Boundary functions and unsupported generated types fail before acquisition.
pkgs/morphir-host and apps/morphirExplicit toolchain/provider integration, temporary execution workspaces, receipts and CLI execute/verifyThe existing process provider uses native/Node facilities. A browser provider requires its own verified implementation.
apps/morphir-workbench-desktopProton packaging of the shared frontend and workerNative service, granted workspace access and daemon attachment are planned adapters; keep their dependencies out of portable UI packages.
Future workbench service and connected profile adapterModel/revision handles, jobs, worksheet source maps and negotiated transportCompose existing execution values and host contracts. Publish transport additions with finos/morphir and coordinate finos/morphir-ui.
Existing support

Reuse the engine and hosts

Morphir hosts already supply mounts, cancellation, events, limits, and publication. The embedded toolchain supplies asynchronous browser compilation and Wasm execution. These are foundations, not an existing UI service.

The engine is synchronous. A UI adapter must schedule it away from the UI thread and explicitly bridge asynchronous providers.

Upstream stack

Use Rabbita and Proton deliberately

Rabbita supplies the UI model and effect mechanisms. Warren is a candidate for local web development. Proton handles the native shell and desktop packaging; it does not mandate the frontend build tool.

Keep Proton modules on a compatible lockstep release. Its documented source-built targets are macOS Apple Silicon, Windows x64, and Linux x64. Additional architectures need their own feasibility checks. Source

OpenSeek provides an architecture reference and a possible reusable readonly viewer. Import public viewer APIs if evaluation proves useful; keep Morphir navigation and service semantics owned here. Source editing is not established by the current readonly viewer. Viewer documentation

06

Jobs & recovery

The service owns execution. The UI observes a job and its last authoritative state. Navigation, reconnecting, and cancelling must not create duplicate jobs or claim outputs were published when they were only generated.

Cancellation and close

For standalone evaluation, use a dedicated job worker or explicit shared cancellation state. A cancellation message cannot interrupt a synchronous loop in the same worker. Terminating a dedicated worker is a valid bounded fallback; restore the model from its saved snapshot for the next job.

A daemon owns its jobs beyond the lifetime of a tab. Desktop close behavior must follow the selected service's ownership policy and show active local jobs before quitting.

Revision and publication

Bind jobs to the exact model or workspace snapshot. Tag results with that revision and show when the current selection has advanced. Reject stale requests that cannot be resolved to their requested snapshot.

Pipeline events distinguish generated artifacts, staging, and committed destinations. Reuse host publication guarantees and report partial commits; the UI cannot manufacture an atomicity guarantee.

Reconnect and retry require explicit retention and idempotency policies. Retrying a request whose response was lost must return the existing job or a clear “outcome unknown” response. It must not automatically start a second build or evaluation.

Local-daemon connection

Start with UI assets served by the daemon on loopback, an authenticated session, validated host and origin, and explicit workspace grants. Reuse the upstream one-time launch-token exchange, redirect, session cookie, session manifest, and authenticated WebSocket. Keep long-lived credentials out of URLs and logs, and prevent the single-use launch token from persisting in browser history. Daemon jobs remain authoritative if the page closes.

The current connected host validates its exact loopback origin; a hosted HTTPS client connecting to localhost is a separate milestone. Validate browser local-network permissions, origin and mixed-content behavior, session pairing, and reconnect behavior on the supported browsers before promising that route.

Integration rules from the merges

  • Reuse the public invocation manifest as the generated execution authority. Local generic aliases and dynamic Scheme values may remain available through their own runtime capability even when the generator rejects them.

Declaration details preserve documentation and access metadata, render readable signatures and ordered parameters, and list record fields and custom constructors. Input fields are now the default. The same semantic schema generates primitive controls, multiline String fields, Boolean/constructor selectors and nested record/tuple/list groups. Portable arguments helpers apply edits against its latest value, preserve numeric spelling and exact integer text, and keep incomplete numeric drafts editable. Invalid or incompatible JSON remains intact when switching modes; an explicit Reset inputs action restores defaults. Forms with more than 200 input nodes defer to JSON rather than generating a large DOM.

Each evaluation starts in a fresh dedicated worker with the existing runtime limits, a 15-second deadline and separate 16-MiB source/argument limits. Its result is independent of compile and worksheet output. Input changes mark an earlier result as outdated; replies for other functions or replaced models cannot replace the current result. The Explorer toolbar includes Cancel. Specifications, native/external/incomplete definitions, recursive inputs, private constructors and unavailable types explain their unsupported status. title: Task 3: Verify a representative pricing model with rich typed values
description:
### Task 3: Verify a representative pricing model with rich typed values

Type: AFK. Blocked by: Task 2.

Complete the boundary value profile for the nongeneric E1 pricing slice and generate public input/output codecs. Reuse the same typed IR lowering information and symbol identities instead of parsing generated source. Exercise exact numeric and structural values and explicitly mapped model errors through all required targets, evaluator, engine and CLI.

Acceptance criteria:
- A checked-in multi-module pricing model and suite covers records/updates, custom constructors, lists, tuples, Maybe/Result, captured closures inside the model and fully applied curried calls.
- Arbitrary Int and exact Decimal survive Ion and JSON provider boundaries. Float64 signed zero, subnormals, infinities and NaNs retain evidence; exact and explicitly selected approximate policies behave as documented.
- SDK UTF-16 text/character cases, including representation boundaries, round-trip without lossy Unicode conversion.
- Missing/extra/duplicate record fields, wrong constructor ownership or payload arity, unresolved aliases and boundary closures fail typed validation. Unsupported generic/open-record/SDK cases produce precise diagnostics.
- Compare model Result.Err as a value, mapped SDK domain errors as model errors, and unknown exceptions as provider failures. Do not normalize arbitrary error text into semantic error codes.
- The representative model produces the same outcomes on every required target and the live evaluator in debug and release. A shared-SDK limitation is stated in the result's conformance profile.
- Rich unknown Ion metadata/annotations survive suite/outcome serialization without entering ordinary Morphir JSON semantic fields. Source-model metadata lineage is preserved.
- Diagnostic logs identify the entry/stage/error code without implicitly capturing typed arguments or result values. Opt-in payload capture is independently configured and redacted; debug level alone does not enable it.
- Metrics use bounded stage/target/provider/outcome dimensions and versioned descriptors. Run IDs, FQNames, file paths, digests and free-text errors never become metric labels; test cardinality overflow accounting.
- Enabling/disabling telemetry does not alter generated library bytes, semantic comparisons, cache identities or required receipt contents. Correlation IDs and timing stay outside semantic identity inputs.

title: Task 4: Make failed verification preserve prior output and clean up execution
description:
### Task 4: Make failed verification preserve prior output and clean up execution

Type: AFK. Blocked by: Task 3.

Complete the execution-session lifecycle, bounded process supervision and publication behavior using real fault scenarios. Keep failed attempts visible in reports while preserving the previous accepted task output. Reuse E1 path/membership validation and publication recovery with execution-specific evidence.

Acceptance criteria:
- Cancellation and deadlines stop and await the process tree, then dispose scratch state; cover platform-supported descendant termination rather than assuming direct-child kill is enough.
- Input/result/diagnostic limits, malformed/truncated protocol files, missing/extra/duplicate call replies, stale artifacts, wrong lease/suite/target identities and source/dependency mutation cannot pass verification.
- Cleanup failure retains the original cause and prevents a successful publication claim. Use-after-dispose and invalid state transitions fail deterministically.
- Every required call/target has exactly one terminal status. A partial target matrix or matching provider failures never count as parity.
- No compiler/evaluator/runner work holds the publication lock. All required results and cleanup succeed before atomic per-task publication of sources and Ion verification evidence.
- Model mismatch, runtime trap, compiler failure, cancellation and publication failure preserve the prior task output according to existing recovery rules; normal execute calls return results without replacing generation output.
- Reports retain actual typed outcomes and mismatch paths while bounded diagnostics remain separate from result framing.
- Exercise unavailable/throwing sinks, queue overflow, exporter failure, recursive logging, cancellation during drain, hanging flush and repeated shutdown. Every dropped record is accounted for, memory stays bounded, and the original execution result remains intact.
- Every started stage has one logical terminal observation on success, typed failure, cancellation and cleanup failure, independent of whether sampled telemetry is delivered. Required statuses remain complete if all telemetry is disabled or dropped.
- Drain async telemetry outside pure stages and publisher locks, preserving original span timestamps/IDs. Use a separate bounded flush allowance; never hang process exit waiting for telemetry. Exporter self-diagnostics use a non-recursive health path.
- Verify trace parentage, retries with distinct attempts, and independent concurrent run contexts without global-provider contamination. Avoid double-counting terminal events or sampling metrics with traces.

description:
### Task 5: Establish independent semantic conformance evidence

Type: AFK. Blocked by: Task 3.

Add independently derived expected cases for semantics most vulnerable to shared SDK mistakes, and exercise the configured evaluator-provider boundary. Locate and pin a runnable Rust evaluator implementation if available. Use a versioned JSON adapter for its explicitly supported type/IR intersection and keep that transport choice local to the provider.

Acceptance criteria:
- Independent expectations cover exact arithmetic, negative division/modulus, argument ordering, lazy boolean branches, closure capture, record updates, constructor payloads and selected UTF-16/Float64 cases.
- Expected-case provenance and version are recorded independently of generator execution; fixtures are not generated from the implementation under test.
- A live Rust lane, if established, records source/binary identity, protocol/version, supported types and error mappings, and runs the same model/call subset after a proven lossless IR conversion.
- Unsupported evaluator types, missing binary or unavailable compatible revision are explicit coverage outcomes, never successful comparisons. A required evaluator selection fails planning when unavailable.
- Default live Scheme coverage, independent expectations and Rust coverage remain separate in receipts and CI summaries. E2 completion does not claim Rust parity where only local evidence exists.
- An injected disagreement with either live evaluator or independent expectation fails the conformance gate and reports the precise call/path.
- Compare representative runs with no-op and recording observers using deterministic test clocks and IDs. Prove the same semantic outcomes and required evidence; keep observation-order assertions limited to real lifecycle guarantees.
- Validate Ion-to-JSON/OTLP field projection with out-of-range integers, exact decimals, binary/rich annotations and unsupported values. Lossy conversion must be explicit, counted and policy-governed, not silent stringification.

### Task 6: Gate the complete installed CLI execution lifecycle in CI

Type: AFK. Blocked by: Tasks 4 and 5.

Integrate the complete target matrix, representative model, failure behavior and structured output into repository checks. Document configuration, invocation formats, provider capabilities, exact supported coverage and how to reproduce evidence from a clean checkout or installed package. Reconcile E2 completion with actual target and evaluator evidence.

Acceptance criteria:
- Clean-checkout and installed npm tests use packaged drivers/helpers/codecs and explicitly supplied pinned dependencies; no repository-relative helper is accidentally used by installed acceptance.
- Standard Morphir JSON and Ion text/binary model inputs feed the same invocation suite. Human, JSON, JSON Lines and dry-run modes agree on planned/actual effects.
- Required JS, Wasm GC, native C and LLVM lanes run debug/release acceptance on supported CI hosts; unsupported capability is a failure for a required lane. Do not mark E2 complete with an unresolved LLVM scope decision.
- CI retains concise identity and comparison receipts and proves a deliberate mismatch fails; broad E1 tests, compiler gates and provider regressions remain green.
- Run repository lint, format, validation and appropriate four-target suites before pushing implementation changes. Record exact revisions, compiler/core/SDK/Ion/runtime/evaluator identities and commit ranges in beads.
- Completion applies to finos/morphir-moonbit only. Rust CLI integration, WIT/host-language packaging, browser execution, expanded generator language coverage and release publishing remain separately tracked.
- Exercise local Ion log files, stderr text and explicit JSON Lines logging from the installed CLI while stdout remains valid result output. No exporter, endpoint or outbound telemetry is enabled implicitly.
- Add a supported native OpenTelemetry adapter integration gate for correlated spans/logs, metric export and bounded flush against a local capture endpoint/collector. Pin the actual accepted archive/dependencies and test OTLP HTTP protobuf/JSON as selected; do not advertise unsupported gRPC or compression.
- Keep collector tests separate from portable tests. Other hosts use the portable observation contract with supported sinks; report adapter capability precisely instead of silently falling back.
- Measure disabled and enabled instrumentation overhead on a fixed representative workload and record the baseline/environment. Establish an evidence-based budget before enforcing a threshold; do not invent a performance percentage.

title: E2 generated-model execution and evaluator parity
description:
# E2 generated-model execution and evaluator parity

## Merge reconciliation · 01 October 2026

Current merged baseline is finos/morphir-moonbit main 563177a. PR #31 delivered E1 at fc9cd3c; PR #32 delivered E2 Tasks 1-3 at 5e6d2f1; PR #33 delivered the browser/Proton workbench at 563177a. Structured result views are local continuation commit 722a126, not main. E2 Tasks 4-6 remain in progress/open; the completed UI acceptance does not close their lifecycle/publication, independent semantic conformance, installed debug/release CI or native OTel collector gates.

Reuse the merged morphir-execution values, suites, comparison policies, public invocation manifests and engine Provider/Session APIs for workbench integration. Ion remains preferred for processing and evidence; Morphir JSON stays supported. The UI's generated input schema and bounded result tree remain private presentation adapters. Dynamic Scheme/worksheet behavior and generated typed-library capabilities stay explicit. Node/native process providers cannot run in browser workers; browser generated execution and Proton native IPC need separate host acceptance. Retain the stable pin for JS/Wasm GC/native C and the separately verified LLVM nightly/core pin with no target substitution.

Coordinate upstream transport, job/revision/worksheet semantics and live Rust-host acceptance through morphir-etg2, whose design now contains the reconciled workbench integration plan. Required semantic outcomes bypass telemetry; model Result.Err and enumerated SDK model errors stay distinct from validation, provider, cancellation and cleanup failures. Keep primary and cleanup causes visible when Task 4 lands. MoonBit merges do not implement the Rust CLI or establish independent SDK conformance.

The original planning/research text below is historical. Later task evidence and this reconciliation supersede its missing-LLVM diagnosis and initial next-task status. The E2 design stored on morphir-ukvn.5.3 is revision 0.5; task implementation scope and ownership are unchanged.

Parent: morphir-ukvn.5.3. Roadmap authority: morphir-ukvn section 4. Design: .dev/designs/morphir-moonbit-e2.html revision 0.2. Baseline: fc9cd3c, PR #31 squash merge. Branch: DamianReeves/morphir-e2-execution. Damian authorized moving to E2 and resumed the work on 2026-10-01.

Deliver a modular, configurable invocation path for E1-generated libraries and compare the same model/calls across Wasm GC, native C, native LLVM and JavaScript. Typed in-process contracts and binary Ion intermediates are preferred; standard Morphir JSON stays supported. JSON-only provider transport must use an explicit lossless projection. Preserve exact Int/Decimal, Float64 edge cases and SDK UTF-16 semantics.

Instrumentation and logging are required from the first slice, per Damian's follow-up. Prefer moonbitlang, moonbit-community, bobzhang, moonrockz and mizchi packages. Reuse the typed host event seam with a portable, host-injected observation contract; keep clocks, sinks, sampling, async drain and shutdown in the host. Required outcomes/receipts bypass telemetry filtering and delivery. Ion is the default enabled file-log format; stderr text, JSON Lines and OTLP are explicit projections. Preserve stdout exclusively for the CLI result protocol.

Research snapshot 2026-10-01: live Mooncakes registry reports moonbit-community/opentelemetry 0.1.7; inspected archive SHA-256 51c7ad32e1344cae45cedfa8d5ee3836d3e22f17ff4796a45a8394917568033f. Root/API/SDK/OTLP packages restrict backend to native and span end/log emission are async. Two published trace-interface tests passed in an isolated workspace using the pinned compiler, async 0.22.4 and protobuf 0.1.2, with upstream deprecation warnings. This establishes only a narrow native smoke test, not full exporter compatibility. Prefer it as an optional native adapter, not a portable engine dependency. Reuse moonrockz/ion 0.3.0. bobzhang/jsonl and jqlog are native inspection tools; mizchi/x is a possible host-I/O facade with target-specific stubs; tonyfettes/xlog is a secondary native-only logging candidate outside the preferred publisher list but hosted under moonbit-community. Package manifests, archive hashes, searches and test evidence live in .dev/e2-execution/observability/. No runtime dependencies were added by this research.

Use the repository's live Scheme evaluator for baseline parity, with runtime accelerators disabled and shared-SDK limitations recorded. Independent expected cases are mandatory. A Rust differential lane requires a proven runnable pin and supported wire/type intersection; the inspected checkout is a placeholder, so do not claim that lane exists. If a maintainer requires Rust specifically for E2 acceptance, keep E2 open until that gate runs. No changes to upstream Rust behavior are implied by this repository's completion.

Feasibility evidence: a minimal main printing 42 runs on wasm-gc, native and js with MOON_HOME=/Users/damian/.moon and compiler 0.10.14+7d59c7ec9. LLVM fails: toolchain warns that LLVM is experimental/nightly-only and cannot find core/_build/llvm/release/bundle/prelude/prelude.mi. Follow-up built the matching LLVM core successfully in a complete temporary toolchain copy; linking then failed with "LLVM backend is disabled". The pinned compiler cannot supply this lane. Select and verify a separate LLVM-capable compiler/core pin through explicit provider configuration, retaining the existing pin for other lanes until compatibility is proven. No target substitution. Diagnostics: .dev/e2-execution/llvm-probe.log and llvm-private-run.log. The installed toolchain was not modified.

Each slice is AFK within these boundaries and delivers a callable path. A required capability that cannot be supplied needs an explicit scope decision. Complete task beads only with commit range and focused test evidence. Canonical plan is rendered from beads and never edited locally; execution ledger also lives in beads. Merges and releases require applicable maintainer authorization.
notes: 2026-10-01: Damian authorized moving to E2 and resumed work. Revision 0.1 HTML design and six-slice implementation plan prepared on DamianReeves/morphir-e2-execution from fc9cd3c. Initial scalar toolchain probe passed Wasm GC, native C and JS; LLVM lacks its bundled core and requires a matching toolchain/core feasibility decision. Local Scheme evaluator is the default live comparison; independent expected cases are required, and Rust coverage must be proven separately.

Scope finos/morphir-moonbit only; no release or upstream Rust extension completion.

title: Task 1: Invoke and compare a scalar generated library through the CLI
description:
### Task 1: Invoke and compare a scalar generated library through the CLI

Type: AFK. Blocked by: E1, already complete.

Build the first complete path from a model and an Ion invocation suite to JavaScript execution and a live Scheme comparison through the actual CLI. Introduce portable execution values, suite/outcome profiles, public invocation manifests and the adapter generator. Generate a separate consumer driver that imports the actual public library and reads argument values at runtime. Extend explicit dependency preparation to include pinned Ion protocol dependencies. Register a process execution session and a local evaluator adapter. Expose additive execute/verify commands with human, JSON and JSON Lines reports and a side-effect-free dry run.

Acceptance criteria:
- A public scalar entry accepts caller-supplied ordered arguments, runs generated JS and matches the evaluator; changing arguments does not regenerate or recompile the driver.
- Ion text and binary suites round-trip exact Int, Bool and Unit; the explicit JSON profile round-trips the same values without Double coercion. Model JSON input remains supported.
- Public/private access, wrong arity, wrong types, duplicate call IDs, empty verification suites and unsupported profile versions fail before compiler effects.
- Library, manifest, adapter, suite and executable identities remain distinct and correlated. A custom test provider uses the same contracts without MoonBit filesystem assumptions in the engine.
- Process build workspace remains leased through execution and is disposed on success/failure. Build-only behavior and E1 receipts remain compatible.
- Scheme invocation has finite fuel/depth limits, uses the same transformed IR and records its semantic profile. A deliberately wrong generated outcome causes a mismatch report and nonzero verification status.
- Record LLVM compiler/core feasibility and locate or explicitly classify the unavailable Rust evaluator pin. Neither optional investigation blocks the JS slice, and neither is silently reported passed.
- Focused portable tests run on existing repository targets; a real native/Node CLI acceptance and installed JS driver exercise the complete scalar path.
- Include a versioned ObservationContext/Observation/Observer contract with a cheap enabled guard and a no-op default. Preserve the existing Host.event callback via typed adapters; do not infer event identity from phase strings.
- The same CLI path emits correlated start/end observations, stage duration, structured local logs and bounded metric measurements. Use host-provided monotonic/wall clocks and ID generation; instrument orchestration boundaries without introducing clock/I/O imports into the generator.
- Enabled file logging defaults to the versioned binary Ion observation profile, with text/JSON Lines opt-outs and bounded rotation/retention. Human logs use stderr. Tests parse complete --json and --json-lines stdout while logging is enabled and find no log contamination.
- Filtering occurs before expensive formatting; redaction occurs before enqueue/export. Payloads, source text, environment values, credentials and absolute paths are excluded by default. Exact rich Ion fields use a separate extension field and explicit export projection.

title: Resolve float lexeme equality in Ion semantic cases
description:
The v4 `FloatLiteral` model compares floats by numeric value; its retained lexeme is not part of identity (`ecosystem/morphir-rust/crates/morphir-core/src/ir/v4/literal.rs`). The Ion writer retains that lexeme, while MCK `@semantic` round trips compare Ion bytes. A JSON input `4e0` is read by the Rust adapter as FloatLiteral and canonically returned as `4e+0`; the kit reference `(float "4.0")` would differ despite equal numeric value. PR #1022 only checks the `4.0` rule and does not claim cross-lexeme equivalence.

Decide and implement a consistent canonical Ion float rule or semantic normalization. Keep spelling checks byte-exact, add a cross-lexeme semantic regression, verify both adapters, and record any contract change before closing morphir-1qhu.7.

01 / A7

Grow source support on the landed pipeline

The next local capability is a single-file Boolean library: several explicitly typed functions, immutable local bindings and direct calls. It feeds the existing typed IR, Ion checkpoint, MoonBit generator, build and verification stages.

Landed foundation

L1 landed · PR #48 merged

A useful example is a public eligibility function calling a private helper. 03 / A7

Give each phase a precise input and output

Explore the implemented pure phases as an SVG diagram. The viewer is standalone and works offline. Each phase is a pure in-memory transformation; the host owns source reads, compiler execution and artifact publication.

The current seed compiler combines body checking and lowering. The library compiler separates them through internal typed views. The opt-in library API landed in PR #48. PR #50 landed the L2 engine/CLI profile selector. No general inference service is introduced.

04 / A7

Compose pure phases around a rich source boundary

Phase or ownerInputOutput and responsibility
Source hostSelected path and explicit logical identityOne immutable source snapshot and bounded text. No hidden filesystem, registry or process calls in the frontend.
Parser adapterText and pinned parser identityFrontend-owned syntax view with source locations; fail on syntax reports or recovered nodes. Keep upstream AST types private to the adapter.
Declaration collectorSyntax module and selected profileFrontend-owned library declarations containing every unique function signature, visibility and origin. Collect before checking bodies so forward calls are legal.
ResolverDeclaredModule and lexical bodiesResolved functions with distinct binding identities and direct call targets. Maintain ordered lexical scopes; drop unresolved bodies. The checker collects the complete call graph.
Profile checkerResolvedModule and Boolean profile rulesCheckedLibrary guarantees Boolean bodies, exact call arity and an acyclic graph. Validate all declarations, including private or unreachable ones. No general Hindley-Milner inference in this slice.
IR lowererCheckedModuleOne typed current Library IR plus native Ion annotations, node origins and provenance. No guessed types, placeholders or inlining.
Engine adapterLibraryOutput, selected language/provider/profile and host-owned unit IDIRUnit through the existing source callback envelope. Core validates identity, metadata ownership and budgets.
Generator/build/executionExisting typed IR contractsReuse E1/E2 providers, entry manifests, dependency pins, bounded leases and comparison. Compiler acceptance remains a host capability.

Add a library API without changing the seed API

Keep compile(Input, Limits, ...), its Output.entry/Output.public, default profile and accepted language unchanged. L1 adds compile_library, LibraryLimits and LibraryOutput. LibraryOutput retains unit ID, current IR, metadata, annotations and provenance, and exposes a canonically ordered list of public entry FQNames. The generated execution manifest remains the authority for invokable entries and their codecs. Do not choose the first declaration as an implicit entry.

One file produces one logical public module with each declaration's original visibility. An all-private library may compile and generate with an empty public-entry list. An execution request for a private or absent entry fails explicitly. No source package dependencies or module merges are implied by this contract.

Keep composition configurable without spreading language policy

The parser, collector, resolver, checker and lowerer have named pure contracts and are composed by the selected provider/profile for the MoonBit language. Start with internal implementations and tests. If hosts later supply alternate implementations, require explicit contract/profile identities and the same conformance suite; replacing a phase cannot silently weaken admission. Applications choose and register the adapter. Engine core, the generator and host providers remain independent of MoonBit syntax.

Reuse the existing source compilation callback and IRUnit envelope. Extend registration and planning to distinguish language, provider and profile; the current flat registration name cannot represent those independently. Adapt existing registrations as default selections rather than renaming languages to avoid a registry collision. Preserve the rich-unit loss guards at JSON component boundaries. Declaration, local-binding and call-site origins live in native Ion metadata; semantic typing belongs in current IR attributes. The pure compiler records source language and semantic profile; the host adds the resolved provider identity and capability evidence to its receipt. Preserve the seed provenance field named frontend with its existing profile-valued meaning. New records distinguish those concepts explicitly instead of silently reinterpreting historical metadata.

05 / A7

Grow the seed into a Boolean library

The landed moonbit-model-bool-v1 accepts exactly one function with explicit Boolean parameters and result. It rejects calls and local bindings. The implemented moonbit-model-bool-library-v1 is opt-in and preserves those Boolean operator rules.

fn ready(active : Bool, suspended : Bool) -> Bool {
  active && !suspended
}

pub fn eligible(active : Bool, suspended : Bool, vip : Bool) -> Bool {
  let allowed : Bool = ready(active, suspended)
  allowed && vip
}

pub fn default_eligible() -> Bool {
  eligible(true, false, true)
}

This is the proposed acceptance seed. The original-source design probe compiles this exact source and checks eight eligibility combinations plus the zero-argument result on Wasm, Wasm GC, JS and native in debug and release. L1 now has a separate six-library differential gate that checks 13 public entries and 42 rows against original source, independent tables, Scheme and generated code. The public functions are selectable entries; the private helper stays callable inside its module and inaccessible to external consumers.

ConstructLibrary profile decisionRule
Top-level declarationsOne or more ordinary functionsExplicit named positional Bool parameters and Bool return. Preserve plain pub exports and default, unexported functions. Reject explicit priv syntax, overloads and duplicate names.
Function callsDirect, fully applied calls within the fileUnqualified declared target, exact arity, Boolean arguments, Boolean result. Forward calls allowed. Zero-argument calls supported. No function values, partial applications, labelled/optional parameters or qualified calls.
Immutable bindingsSequential let bindings with one named binderOptional Bool annotation; initializer checked as Bool. Initializer sees the previous scope, and the new binder is visible only in the remaining body. Shadowing uses a new binding identity. Reject destructuring and local function declarations.
ExpressionsExisting Boolean expressions plus calls and letsLiterals, lexical references, grouping, Bool constraints, if/else, !, &&, ||, == and !=. Require a Boolean final expression; no arbitrary discarded statement expressions.
Call graphAcyclicReject direct and indirect recursion across every declaration, even in unreachable branches. Compute cycles without recursive host-stack traversal.
Types and effectsSame restricted pure languageNo numeric/string/compound types, generics, traits, mutation, async, exceptions, FFI, loops or early return.
PackagesOne file, one moduleNo imports, cross-file calls, dependency discovery or multi-document linking. Existing engine jobs remain independent.
Compiler-validity finding

Compiler 0.10.14+7d59c7ec9 rejects priv fn with diagnostic 3005, "No 'private' visibility for function." Default fn supplies the unexported helper used here. The previous seed adapter accepted the parser's Priv visibility variant. Commit 5965313 fixes that admission mismatch. The seed and library APIs reject it, and the acceptance gate records compiler diagnostic 3005.

Make names and evaluation order explicit

Collect the full declaration table before resolving any body. Resolve a name in the current lexical scope first. A Boolean local or parameter that shadows a function makes a call to that spelling a non-callable-target error. A bare function reference is unsupported; only direct call syntax admits it. Duplicate parameters fail. Repeated let spellings may shadow earlier bindings and must never overwrite their IR identity.

Retain the injective UTF-8 encoding for global names. Assign a distinct deterministic binder identity per declaration and lexical binding position, with separate namespaces for source bindings and lowering temporaries. Record the original spelling and source span in Ion. Formatting can change coordinates; this is not a promise of stable node identity across arbitrary source edits.

Lower zero-input locals to strict LetDefinition values. Evaluate a binding initializer once before its body. Lower direct calls to typed Reference/Apply nodes, with curried function types on references and intermediate applications, and Bool on the final result. A zero-argument function uses its zero-input value reference. Preserve function/argument order and short circuiting. Do not inline callees or expand the call graph into expression trees.

The existing generator already lowers zero-input local definitions to eager values and introduces application temporaries. The library gate must verify the emitted result and the Scheme path, rather than infer source equivalence from those implementation details alone.

Use bounded compilation, not implied bounded evaluation

Enforced hard maximumScope
65,536 UTF-8 bytes; 64 declarationsWhole source unit
16 parameters; 256 let bindersEach function
4,096 visited source expressions; 1,024 call sitesAggregate across all bodies
Expression depth 64; call-graph depth 32Checked before publication, including private declarations

LibraryLimits may lower these maxima. Check cancellation between phases and during bounded traversals. Choose the primary diagnostic in fixed phase order, then declaration/expression order within each pass, with a source span where available. Failure publishes no partial unit. The synchronous parser still needs host isolation for a hard interruption/allocation guarantee. An acyclic graph can perform substantial repeated work, so execution continues to use its own deadlines and budgets.

Broader source support follows separate evidence

Records and custom types should reuse language-neutral IR typing where appropriate. Shared inference is tracked as morphir-ukvn.5.22.2; this explicitly annotated Boolean library does not depend on it. MoonBit-specific numeric widths, overflow, conversions, strings, effects and recursion each need their own source semantics and independent compiler acceptance. 06 / A7

Use Ion internally and preserve JSON compatibility

Source files remain MoonBit text. The parser's in-memory AST is not a generic JSON intermediate. The accepted frontend output is typed IR inside the existing IRUnit envelope; checkpoints default to binary Ion and can explicitly use Ion text.

Attach native Ion metadata for source spans, original names and profile identity to stable declaration/body IDs. Preserve unknown annotation tokens and source provenance across components. Version the coordinate convention and record the source digest; do not assume parser offsets equal UTF-8 byte offsets. Verify coordinates with non-ASCII and multiline fixtures before claiming exact mapping.

Morphir JSON remains supported for semantic IR and downstream tools. A JSON boundary must use the existing loss-detection or metadata sidecar policy. Source origins and rich Ion values must not vanish in a generic JSON conversion. JSON and JSON Lines CLI result framing remain distinct from internal pipeline storage.

A future cache key includes source bytes, logical package/module identity, parser/source pin, semantic profile, dependency inventory, lowering version and relevant budgets. Cache hits require complete verified evidence. No cache is necessary for the first slice.

07 / A7

Keep capabilities and instrumentation explicit

Parsing and lowering have no host I/O. Hosts supply snapshots and enforce input-byte limits before parsing. Bound AST size/depth, declarations, diagnostic count and generated artifacts; traversal limits do not prove a streaming or pre-allocation parser guarantee. Cancellation is checked at stage boundaries and bounded traversals. A synchronous parser cannot promise prompt interruption during a long parse; hostile-input isolation needs a separate worker or process capability.

The landed observation slice morphir-ukvn.1.10.6 reuses the portable contract. The pure frontend accepts an optional scope with a disabled default. A frontend span contains parse, declaration profile-check and expression checking/lowering spans. The Boolean profile has no import resolver; do not report a resolve stage it does not perform. The engine adapter accepts a host-owned observer. CLI --log enables the existing bounded local sink with automatic directories. Source compilation defaults to .morphir/logs/frontend.ionb under the discovered project/workspace; execute, verify and conform default to .morphir/logs/execution.ionb under cwd. Explicit --log-file paths take precedence and remain unchanged, including outside that folder. No extra escape rejection is imposed. The default sink uses binary Ion and also allows Ion text, JSON Lines or text, with matching filename extensions. Creation runs only in the bounded flush worker. Standalone WASI/Wasm GC CLI hosts retain their explicit clock-capability rejection for requested local delivery; pure host-supplied observation and normal source compilation still work. Dry-run uses a disabled observer and does not open logs. Frontend cancellation must end active spans as cancelled while preserving its original diagnostic. Sink failure must leave model outputs, metadata/provenance and diagnostics unchanged. Disabled observation performs no clock, ID or sink work. Record terminal outcomes and durations with bounded dimensions such as frontend/profile/stage/outcome. Keep source text, argument values and diagnostic free text out of default telemetry attributes. Required diagnostics and execution evidence are never sampled away.

Local Ion logs, stderr text and explicit JSON Lines sinks remain available. The native OpenTelemetry adapter is opt-in with binary, pin, helper and endpoint; supported HTTP/JSON host coverage stays Linux/x64 and macOS/arm64. Pure frontend packages never import the native exporter. Missing required capability fails planning.

Instrument real library phases

For the L1 library compiler, a frontend span contains parse, declaration profile-check, resolve, body profile-check and lower spans. L1 adds a portable Resolve stage with stable name resolve; the existing seed keeps its current stage sequence. The two profile-check occurrences have fixed positions around resolution. The current observation contract has no phase dimension; L1 adds no names or free-form fields. Do not emit per-function names, graph edges, source snippets or node metadata as default telemetry.

Every started phase has one success, failure or cancellation terminal event. Resolution/type failures retain the original source diagnostic. Cancellation must not return a partially checked module or IRUnit. Disabled observation and optional sink failures retain the existing neutrality guarantees. Reuse source .morphir/logs/frontend.ionb defaults and explicit path overrides; no new log directory or exporter is needed.

Back to the A7 pipeline design

Proposed naming revision · 8 October 2026

Readable identities, explicit target names

Ordinary public functions keep readable Morphir names. Source spelling remains in origins, and a declaration-owned moonbit.targetName attribute carries the MoonBit spelling when the default rendering needs help.

This is a design proposal. Current frontend and generator code still use hex encoding. PR #55 qualifies the existing library pipeline; it does not change naming.

Keep each name’s purpose clear

Source spelling

is_ready is the exact identifier the author wrote. Preserve it with its source location, even when no target attribute is needed.

Morphir identity

is-ready is a name made of semantic segments. References and public entry selection use the canonical FQName.

Target spelling

is_ready is a MoonBit identifier. A target attribute selects this spelling without changing the Morphir identity.

Normalize source names into words and initialisms using an explicit frontend policy. Keep simple names such as eligible unchanged. Follow the v4 distinction between a word and an initialism, such as usd and USD. Canonical parsing stays strict; source normalization is a separate operation.

Put target names in declaration metadata

The pipeline already has an owned metadata entry for each value declaration. Extend its data payload with an attributes struct, alongside the existing declaration and parameter origins.

{
  node_id: "value:example/policy:rules#is-ready",
  data: {
    declaration: { name: "is_ready", source: { /* existing location */ } },
    attributes: { "moonbit.targetName": "is_ready" },
    parameters: [ /* existing origins */ ]
  }
}

This is a declaration attribute carried by IRUnit.metadata. It is not a body-expression attribute, an Ion envelope annotation, or a new field in the v4 value-definition schema. The generator reads it through a typed accessor that validates the owner, attribute shape and target identifier.

Use moonbit.targetName as the language-specific key for this revision. A generic targetName convention needs a separate shared contract for target selection and precedence. Unknown attributes remain intact.

Source attributes describe the requested spelling. The generator’s symbol table records the actual allocated spelling and the reason for any escape. Generated metadata must not overwrite the original request or source origins.

Allocate names once, then reuse the mapping

Open the SVG diagram and export controls. The graph describes proposed behavior.

  1. Collect source declarations and normalize their semantic names before lowering references. Detect normalized-name collisions across public and private declarations.
  2. Keep readable names for unambiguous declarations. For ambiguous source spellings, retain a readable base and add a deterministic escape only to the affected identities. Preserve both source spellings and diagnose the collision group. Freeze the precise escape algorithm with golden examples before implementation.
  3. Resolve local variables lexically. Preserve distinct binder identities where shadowing requires them; give synthetic temporaries a reserved allocation domain. Public declaration readability must not compromise binding hygiene.
  4. Reserve and validate explicit MoonBit target names first. Reject invalid or conflicting explicit requests with both owners identified. Automatic allocation must work around reserved names.
  5. Render ordinary names readably. Apply an escape only for a keyword, target collision, synthetic name, unsupported spelling or flattened namespace conflict. Include namespaces only when needed to distinguish declarations.
  6. Use the resulting symbol table for emitted declarations, every reference, invocation descriptors, generated drivers and symbol manifests. The driver must stop independently reconstructing v_ plus hex.

Make the rules observable

CaseMorphir identityTarget behavior
eligibleeligibleReadable default. No attribute required when the renderer returns the desired spelling.
is_ready aloneis-readyKeep is_ready through the target attribute when it differs from the default renderer.
is_ready and isReady togetherDistinct identities with the readable is-ready baseNormalization must never merge the functions. Preserve separate target spellings and add an explicit, stable IR disambiguation.
quote in two modulesDistinct FQNamesQualify only the conflicting generated names if the backend keeps a flat package.
Shadowed ready localsDistinct binder identitiesReadable base plus scope disambiguation where required; the initializer still resolves in the preceding scope.
Two explicit target attributes request the same symbolUnchanged semantic identitiesFail with both owners. Do not silently rewrite an explicit target request.

Preserve the mapping at pipeline boundaries

Ion text and binary checkpoints already retain the metadata payload. The generator already copies source metadata into its binary Ion symbol receipt; consuming target attributes is new work. Identity transforms preserve the entries. Structural transforms must use the existing lineage contract to move or derive owned metadata and record removed nodes.

Morphir JSON remains supported. A bare semantic JSON document cannot carry engine metadata, and the current whole-unit exporter rejects that loss. A JSON component can continue to operate under the engine’s checked metadata-preservation policy. Do not silently discard a target attribute needed to reproduce a generated API.

A standalone v4 specification will not automatically contain this metadata: ValueDefinition.to_specification() returns empty annotations today. A future metadata-aware specification projection can translate the attribute into a Morphir annotation under an agreed FQName. That projection is separate from the definition schema and must not be claimed as implemented here.

Existing checkpoints keep their existing canonical identities when loaded. Do not reverse-decode old source-<hex> names automatically, since they may be intentional names in other IR. New source output records the naming-policy version in provenance. Changing public entry IDs and generated symbol names requires a documented compatibility choice before rollout.

Qualify the change through the installed library

Reuse the six-library acceptance suite and its independent semantic expectations. Add naming cases for normalization collisions, initialisms, keyword escapes, namespace conflicts, explicit-target conflicts, shadowed binders and source-order changes. Compile generated public consumers that call the readable exports directly. Check that generation, invocation and manifests agree on the allocated symbols.

Round-trip the target attributes through both Ion codecs, preserve unknown metadata, exercise lineage ownership and retain JSON loss checks. Run the existing original-source, Scheme and generated execution comparisons on every required target and mode. Public/private visibility, logging neutrality and publication-failure preservation remain acceptance requirements.

Before implementation, freeze the normalization grammar, deterministic suffix algorithm, policy version and compatibility mode. The storage choice is settled in this proposal: declaration-owned attributes in pipeline metadata.

Current code behind the proposal

  • Frontend source-name encoding and lexical resolution.
  • Declaration-owned origins and canonical name grammar.
  • IRUnit and metadata ownership, Ion envelope, codecs and JSON loss checks.
  • Generator names, symbol metadata, invocation symbol reconstruction.
  • Value specifications and definitions. Shared Morphir v4 naming and annotation specifications were inspected in the local ecosystem checkout.
Local design artifact. Naming behavior is proposed; current library qualification and release status remain in the A7 design.

The linked-metadata design already gives this naming example. A scoped @context maps the readable key targetNames to a declared predicate Node URI. Its @json coercion makes the entire frontend/backend record one typed fact.

{
  node_id: "value:example/policy:rules#is-ready",
  data: {
    declaration: { name: "isReady", source: { /* existing location */ } },
    attributes: {
      '@context': {
        targetNames: {
          '@id': "morphir://ir/pkg/acme/metadata?format=4.0.0#/module/naming/value/target-names",
          '@type': "@json"
        }
      },
      facts: {
        targetNames: {
          frontend: { moonbit: "isReady" },
          backend: { moonbit: "isReady" }
        }
      }
    }
  }
}

This is a proposed IRUnit.metadata adapter payload. The acme/metadata URI is the upstream example vocabulary, not a production provider selected by this design. Before implementation, select the actual predicate declaration and its supported subject roles. The local declaration owner stays explicit; projection must not pretend that a ValueDefinition is an attributed body expression.

The frontend map retains the language-specific input spelling. The MoonBit backend consumes only the resolved predicate’s backend.moonbit request. It does not treat a frontend spelling as a backend override. Both maps are string-keyed Dict String String; moonbit is the language ID, independent of compiler profile. Both fields are required by the upstream closed record, with an empty map when no spelling is supplied. Language IDs follow ^[a-z][a-z0-9]*(?:-[a-z0-9]+)*$.

The generator validates the record, language IDs, target identifier and symbol collisions before consuming the request. It matches the expanded predicate identity, not the literal alias targetNames. Unsupported predicates and missing interpretation support remain preserved and explicitly unvalidated. Storage and a matching context digest alone do not prove trusted semantics. A known naming request that generation requires must fail if its required validation or interpreter is unavailable; it must not silently fall back to another spelling.

@targetName or @moonbit.targetName may remain an ergonomic source spelling if source syntax is added later. They would lower into this declared targetNames fact; the previous standalone attributes["moonbit.targetName"] map is superseded as the semantic contract. No source annotation syntax is currently admitted by the Boolean frontend.

The generator’s symbol table records the actual allocated spelling and any escape reason separately. Generation must preserve the authored request, its assertion owner and source origins.

Allocate names once, then reuse the mapping

  2. Keep readable names for unambiguous declarations. For ambiguous source spellings, retain a readable base and add a deterministic escape only to the affected identities. Preserve both source spellings and diagnose the collision group. Freeze the precise escape algorithm with golden examples before implementation.
  3. Resolve local variables lexically. Preserve distinct binder identities where shadowing requires them; give synthetic temporaries a reserved allocation domain. Public declaration readability must not compromise binding hygiene.
  4. Reserve and validate explicit MoonBit target names first. Reject invalid or conflicting explicit requests with both owners identified. Automatic allocation must work around reserved names.
  5. Render ordinary names readably. Apply an escape only for a keyword, target collision, synthetic name, unsupported spelling or flattened namespace conflict. Include namespaces only when needed to distinguish declarations.
  6. Use the resulting symbol table for emitted declarations, every reference, invocation descriptors, generated drivers and symbol manifests. The driver must stop independently reconstructing v_ plus hex.

Make the rules observable

CaseMorphir identityTarget behavior
eligibleeligibleReadable default. No attribute required when the renderer returns the desired spelling.
is_ready aloneis-readyKeep is_ready through the target attribute when it differs from the default renderer.
is_ready and isReady togetherDistinct identities with the readable is-ready baseNormalization must never merge the functions. Preserve separate target spellings and add an explicit, stable IR disambiguation.

Two explicit target attributes request the same symbolUnchanged semantic identitiesFail with both owners. Do not silently rewrite an explicit target request.

Separate native metadata from engine storage

CarrierUpstream meaningMoonBit integration
attributes.factsNode-local facts on Type and Value expressions; the enclosing node is the subject.Use the node’s own identity. Never move a declaration naming request onto its body just to obtain attributes.
annotations.entries and annotations.factsSpecification labels and facts have their own context. An annotation entry is distinct from a graph fact.A metadata-aware specification projection must preserve the intended subject and keep entries separate from naming facts.
$meta.@graphExplicit-subject facts. The containing document owns each assertion, even when its subject is elsewhere.Use this native carrier for a naming fact about a value definition when its schema has no declaration attributes.

Ion text and binary checkpoints already retain arbitrary metadata payloads. The generator already copies source metadata into its Ion symbol receipt; consuming linked naming facts is new work. Identity transforms preserve entries. Structural transforms use the existing lineage contract and must also account for authored carrier, subject and assertion provenance. Local value: IDs need an explicit mapping to portable Morphir Node URIs; they are not interchangeable spellings.

Morphir JSON remains supported. Our current semantic-only codec cannot export engine metadata and retains its loss guard. Upstream’s opt-in V4.1 single-file JSON, YAML and Ion metadata preview is a separate capability. A future checked native adapter can carry facts in JSON rather than discard them. Do not extend V4.0 or the current engine envelope merely by accepting an unknown native field.

The upstream corpus targets IR 4.1.0 and exact Ion 0.1.0-draft.2. The engine checkpoint is morphir-pipeline-v1, and has no implied claim to that native Ion profile. Specification extraction currently creates empty annotation arrays and must not be claimed to project metadata automatically.

Preserve unknown facts and contexts. Equal graph facts can have multiple separately owned assertions; conflicting target requests require an explicit generator diagnostic, rather than last-writer precedence. Existing V3/V4 decorator sidecars remain supported overlays. Reading them does not migrate them, merge them into native facts or retire them.

Existing checkpoints keep their canonical identities when loaded. Do not reverse-decode old source-<hex> names automatically. New source output records the naming-policy version in provenance. Changing public entry IDs and generated symbol names still requires a documented compatibility choice.

Add naming cases for normalization collisions, initialisms, keyword escapes, namespace conflicts, explicit-target conflicts, shadowed binders and source-order changes. Compile generated public consumers that call the readable exports directly. Check that generation, invocation and manifests agree on the allocated symbols.

Round-trip the scoped target-name facts through both engine Ion codecs, preserve unknown metadata, exercise lineage ownership and retain JSON loss checks. Reuse upstream reference cases metadata-0004, 0025, 0048, 0049, 0053, 0063, 0071 and 0072 for typed objects, language IDs, opaque strings, equality and interpreter availability. Preserve the independent expected results; local tests do not become an MCK claim automatically. Run the existing original-source, Scheme and generated execution comparisons on every required target and mode. Public/private visibility, logging neutrality and publication-failure preservation remain acceptance requirements.

Before implementation, freeze the normalization grammar, deterministic suffix algorithm, policy version and compatibility mode. The engine storage remains declaration-owned metadata, but the semantic contract follows the upstream scoped targetNames fact. Native projection, the provider vocabulary and subject-role admission must be fixed before implementation.

Upstream decisions and tracked work

Reference snapshot: finos/morphir at 23e7dfa, checked 8 October 2026. The earlier local checkout was 5c5307d and predates the linked-metadata increment. Pinned source receipt records file identities.

EntryHow it governs this design
Decision 0019
Linked metadata design		Scoped facts, targetNames, assertion ownership, typed data and decorator coexistence. Replaces the proposed ad hoc naming-property map.
Attributes
Annotations
File metadata		Keep core node attributes, specification annotation entries and document metadata distinct. Earlier draft examples do not independently expand V4.0 schemas.
Metadata reference corpus
Node addresses		Pin language-ID validation, one typed object, predicate roles, interpreter availability and portable subject identities. Reference cases are separate from passing implementation claims.
PR #997
#999, preview delivered		Upstream early-access runtime and CLI support exists. This does not mean the MoonBit codecs or generator implement the same capability.
#1000, broader qualification
#1001, trusted providers
#944, package annotations		Keep broader coverage, trusted semantic admission and package-specification annotation decisions as explicit tracked boundaries. Do not claim them from local storage or syntax validation.

The MoonBit A7 naming revision consumes these contracts rather than redefining them.

  • Declaration-owned origins and canonical name grammar.
  • IRUnit and metadata ownership, Ion envelope, codecs and JSON loss checks.
  • Generator names, symbol metadata, invocation symbol reconstruction.

Ordinary public functions keep readable Morphir names. Preserve original source spelling and requested target spelling separately. When a name needs disambiguation, continue automatically with a traceable allocation and an actionable warning.

  node_id: "value:example/policy:rules#is-ready",
  data: {
    declaration: { name: "isReady", source: { /* existing location */ } },
    attributes: {
      '@context': {
        targetNames: {
          '@id': "morphir://ir/pkg/acme/metadata?format=4.0.0#/module/naming/value/target-names",
          '@type': "@json"
        }
      },
      facts: {
        targetNames: {
          frontend: { moonbit: "isReady" },
          backend: { moonbit: "isReady" }
        }
      }
    }
  }
