This is a proposed IRUnit.metadata adapter payload. The acme/metadata URI is the upstream example vocabulary, not a production provider selected by this design. Before implementation, select the actual predicate declaration and its supported subject roles. The local declaration owner stays explicit; projection must not pretend that a ValueDefinition is an attributed body expression.

The frontend map retains the language-specific input spelling. The MoonBit backend consumes the resolved predicate’s backend.moonbit as an explicit request. Without that request, it may use frontend.moonbit as a readable allocation hint when the source language matches the target language. A hint can be adapted for target constraints; an explicit request keeps its exact spelling. Cross-language generation renders the semantic name and retains source spelling for traceability. Both maps are string-keyed Dict String String; moonbit is the language ID, independent of compiler profile. Both fields are required by the upstream closed record, with an empty map when no spelling is supplied. Language IDs follow ^[a-z][a-z0-9]*(?:-[a-z0-9]+)*$.

The generator validates the record, language IDs, target identifier and symbol collisions before consuming the request. It matches the expanded predicate identity, not the literal alias targetNames. Unsupported predicates and missing interpretation support remain preserved and explicitly unvalidated. Storage and a matching context digest alone do not prove trusted semantics. A known naming request that generation requires must fail if its required validation or interpreter is unavailable; it must not silently fall back to another spelling.

@targetName or @moonbit.targetName may remain an ergonomic source spelling if source syntax is added later. They would lower into this declared targetNames fact; the previous standalone attributes["moonbit.targetName"] map is superseded as the semantic contract. No source annotation syntax is currently admitted by the Boolean frontend.

The generator’s symbol table records the actual allocated spelling and any escape reason separately. Generation must preserve the authored request, its assertion owner and source origins. Keep original spelling, requested spelling and allocated spelling as distinct fields. An automatic allocation must not overwrite the authored targetNames fact. Missing source spelling is valid for imported or synthesized IR; use its semantic name and available lineage instead of inventing an original spelling.

Allocate names once, then reuse the mapping

Open the SVG diagram and export controls. The graph describes proposed behavior.

  1. Collect declarations and resolve their original spellings to owners before lowering references. Normalize semantic names across public and private declarations within each actual identity namespace.
  2. Keep unambiguous declarations readable. A normalization collision emits a warning and allocates distinct identities automatically. Each allocated name retains its readable base; its receipt maps back to the exact source spelling and location. A target attribute cannot repair an already merged semantic identity.
  3. Resolve local variables lexically before rendering. Give shadowed binders distinct identities and reserve user names before creating temporary names. Fresh names derive from the original binder or expression role, such as ready_shadow_1 or ready_equality_left_1. Use a deterministic scope-local discriminator when needed and retain the originating binder or expression in lineage. Routine hygienic freshening does not produce warning noise.
  4. Validate and reserve explicit target requests first. Reject invalid identifiers and contradictory requests with both owners and a fix. Automatic candidates work around these reservations. A declaration with no explicit request can use its same-language original spelling as a hint, then its semantic rendering as a fallback.
  5. For automatic candidates, qualify a conflicting flat-package symbol by module or owner first. Add a readable role or short discriminator only where necessary. Keyword or unsupported-name escapes and unexpected user-name collisions produce warnings with the final allocation. Expected temporary allocation does not.
  6. Use one immutable allocation result for declarations, references, invocation descriptors, generated drivers and symbol manifests. Never reconstruct names independently. Record naming-policy version and allocation reasons in provenance.
Default recovery policy

Recoverable naming conflicts warn and continue. An optional strict naming policy promotes these warnings to errors before publication. Source semantics, visibility and lexical binding must survive either policy. Contradictory exact target requests and unavailable required metadata validation remain errors.

Proposed deterministic declaration policy: reserve all unambiguous normalized identities, then choose the canonical snake-case source spelling as the plain-name owner within a collision group. If none exists, choose by exact UTF-8 spelling order. Other owners receive <readable-base>-source-<token>, with the token derived from the original spelling. Check every candidate against reserved identities and the whole group. Extend the discriminator on a collision; a digest alone never proves uniqueness. This selection is independent of declaration order. Freeze the token encoding, digest inputs and collision fallback with golden cases before implementation. Adding a new conflicting declaration may change an earlier allocation and must be reported as a public-name compatibility change.

Make the rules observable

CaseMorphir identityTarget behavior
eligibleeligibleReadable default. No attribute required when the renderer returns the desired spelling.
is_ready aloneis-readyUse is_ready as a same-language automatic hint. An explicit backend request can pin it; no request is synthesized merely to preserve the original spelling.
is_ready and isReady togetherDistinct identities with the readable is-ready baseWarn and continue. Keep is-ready for is_ready, and allocate is-ready-source-<token> for isReady. Original spellings may yield distinct MoonBit symbols is_ready and isReady without extra target mangling.
quote in two modulesDistinct FQNamesQualify only the conflicting generated names if the backend keeps a flat package.
Shadowed ready localsDistinct binder identitiesUse ready and a fresh ready_shadow_1 where required. Reserve user spellings and advance the discriminator on conflicts. The initializer still resolves in the preceding scope; ordinary shadowing needs no warning.
Two explicit target attributes request the same symbolUnchanged semantic identitiesFail with both owners. Do not silently rewrite an explicit target request.

Show the recovery and the fix

A structured naming diagnostic carries a stable code, severity, stage, all involved owners and source locations, the colliding candidate, final allocations and suggested fixes. Proposed code moonbit_frontend.name_normalization_collision identifies the source-to-IR edge case. Backend keyword escapes and automatic target collisions use separate codes. Keep the warnings alongside successful output rather than raising FrontendError::Invalid.

warning moonbit_frontend.name_normalization_collision
  is_ready and isReady normalize to is-ready in example/policy:rules
  related locations: both declaration name spans
  continuing with:
    is_ready → is-ready
    isReady  → is-ready-source-<token>
  fix: rename one declaration so its semantic words differ,
       for example is_ready_now → is-ready-now
  targetNames.backend alone cannot fix this IR identity collision

For a target-only conflict, suggest distinct backend.moonbit spellings or a source/module rename. For a keyword, show the escaped name and a valid target spelling. Suggested edits must pass parsing, normalization and reservation checks before they are offered as applicable fixes. Do not automatically edit source files. Exact target conflicts fail with these same details rather than changing the requested public API.

Add a successful-output warning channel to both frontend contracts and their engine adapters. The engine already has ContentReport.warnings, but its diagnostic record only carries path, stage and message. Extend or adapt the reporting contract to preserve structured codes, related spans and fixes; do not flatten them away. Human CLI warnings go to stderr, while structured consumers receive structured warning records without corrupting artifact or JSON stdout. Optional logs may mirror the events but are not the warning delivery mechanism.

Allocation reasons and origins survive Ion checkpoints and symbol receipts. Warning replay at a checkpoint or generation boundary must be explicit and deduplicated within a run by code and owning allocation, so resumption remains explainable without repeated messages. Qualification covers direct frontend calls, engine/CLI processing, checkpoint replay and the installed library path. A normal readable declaration emits no naming warning.

Back to the A7 pipeline design

Naming revision 4 · 8 October 2026

Readable identities, explicit target names

Ordinary public functions keep readable Morphir names. Preserve original source spelling and requested target spelling separately. When a name needs disambiguation, continue automatically with a traceable allocation and an actionable warning.

Task 1 now implements readable frontend identities, checked binder allocation and structured warning recovery on the working branch. The generator’s target encoding and upstream targetNames consumption remain separate follow-ups. PR #55 qualifies the previous library pipeline.

Keep each name’s purpose clear

Source spelling

is_ready is the exact identifier the author wrote. Preserve it with its source location, even when no target attribute is needed.

Morphir identity

is-ready is a name made of semantic segments. References and public entry selection use the canonical FQName.

Target spelling

is_ready is a MoonBit identifier. A target attribute selects this spelling without changing the Morphir identity.

Normalize source names into words and initialisms using an explicit frontend policy. Keep simple names such as eligible unchanged. Follow the v4 distinction between a word and an initialism, such as usd and USD. Canonical parsing stays strict; source normalization is a separate operation.

Use the upstream targetNames fact

The linked-metadata design already gives this naming example. A scoped @context maps the readable key targetNames to a declared predicate Node URI. Its @json coercion makes the entire frontend/backend record one typed fact.

{
  node_id: "value:example/policy:rules#is-ready",
  data: {
    declaration: { name: "isReady", source: { /* existing location */ } },
    attributes: {
      '@context': {
        targetNames: {
          '@id': "morphir://ir/pkg/acme/metadata?format=4.0.0#/module/naming/value/target-names",
          '@type': "@json"
        }
      },
      facts: {
        targetNames: {
          frontend: { moonbit: "isReady" },
          backend: { moonbit: "isReady" }
        }
      }
    }
  }
}

This is a proposed IRUnit.metadata adapter payload. The acme/metadata URI is the upstream example vocabulary, not a production provider selected by this design. Before implementation, select the actual predicate declaration and its supported subject roles. The local declaration owner stays explicit; projection must not pretend that a ValueDefinition is an attributed body expression.

The frontend map retains the language-specific input spelling. The MoonBit backend consumes the resolved predicate’s backend.moonbit as an explicit request. Without that request, it may use frontend.moonbit as a readable allocation hint when the source language matches the target language. A hint can be adapted for target constraints; an explicit request keeps its exact spelling. Cross-language generation renders the semantic name and retains source spelling for traceability. Both maps are string-keyed Dict String String; moonbit is the language ID, independent of compiler profile. Both fields are required by the upstream closed record, with an empty map when no spelling is supplied. Language IDs follow ^[a-z][a-z0-9]*(?:-[a-z0-9]+)*$.

The generator validates the record, language IDs, target identifier and symbol collisions before consuming the request. It matches the expanded predicate identity, not the literal alias targetNames. Unsupported predicates and missing interpretation support remain preserved and explicitly unvalidated. Storage and a matching context digest alone do not prove trusted semantics. A known naming request that generation requires must fail if its required validation or interpreter is unavailable; it must not silently fall back to another spelling.

@targetName or @moonbit.targetName may remain an ergonomic source spelling if source syntax is added later. They would lower into this declared targetNames fact; the previous standalone attributes["moonbit.targetName"] map is superseded as the semantic contract. No source annotation syntax is currently admitted by the Boolean frontend.

The generator’s symbol table records the actual allocated spelling and any escape reason separately. Generation must preserve the authored request, its assertion owner and source origins. Keep original spelling, requested spelling and allocated spelling as distinct fields. An automatic allocation must not overwrite the authored targetNames fact. Missing source spelling is valid for imported or synthesized IR; use its semantic name and available lineage instead of inventing an original spelling.

Allocate names once, then reuse the mapping

Open the SVG diagram and export controls. The graph describes proposed behavior.

  1. Collect declarations and resolve their original spellings to owners before lowering references. Normalize semantic names across public and private declarations within each actual identity namespace.
  2. Keep unambiguous declarations readable. A normalization collision emits a warning and allocates distinct identities automatically. Each allocated name retains its readable base; its receipt maps back to the exact source spelling and location. A target attribute cannot repair an already merged semantic identity.
  3. Resolve local variables lexically before rendering. Give shadowed binders distinct identities and reserve user names before creating temporary names. Fresh names derive from the original binder or expression role, such as ready_shadow_1 or ready_equality_left_1. Use a deterministic scope-local discriminator when needed and retain the originating binder or expression in lineage. Routine hygienic freshening does not produce warning noise.
  4. Validate and reserve explicit target requests first. Reject invalid identifiers and contradictory requests with both owners and a fix. Automatic candidates work around these reservations. A declaration with no explicit request can use its same-language original spelling as a hint, then its semantic rendering as a fallback.
  5. For automatic candidates, qualify a conflicting flat-package symbol by module or owner first. Add a readable role or short discriminator only where necessary. Keyword or unsupported-name escapes and unexpected user-name collisions produce warnings with the final allocation. Expected temporary allocation does not.
  6. Use one immutable allocation result for declarations, references, invocation descriptors, generated drivers and symbol manifests. Never reconstruct names independently. Record naming-policy version and allocation reasons in provenance.
Default recovery policy

Recoverable naming conflicts warn and continue. The optional strict_naming=true API argument or pipeline.strict_naming=true engine configuration promotes these warnings to errors before publication. Source semantics, visibility and lexical binding must survive either policy. Contradictory exact target requests and unavailable required metadata validation remain errors.

Proposed deterministic declaration policy: reserve all unambiguous normalized identities, then choose the canonical snake-case source spelling as the plain-name owner within a collision group. If none exists, choose by exact UTF-8 spelling order. Other owners receive <readable-base>-source-<token>, with the token derived from the original spelling. Check every candidate against reserved identities and the whole group. Extend the discriminator on a collision; a digest alone never proves uniqueness. This selection is independent of declaration order. Task 1 freezes moonbit-readable-names-v1: the token is the first four UTF-8 bytes encoded as lowercase hexadecimal. Extend by one byte until unique, then add a checked decimal counter if the full spelling is still occupied. The token is a discriminator, not a digest. Golden tests cover occupied suffixes and source-order changes. Adding a new conflicting declaration may change an earlier allocation and must be reported as a public-name compatibility change.

A structured naming diagnostic carries a stable code, severity, stage, all involved owners and source locations, the colliding candidate, final allocations and suggested fixes. Proposed code moonbit_frontend.name_normalization_collision identifies the source-to-IR edge case. Backend keyword escapes and automatic target collisions use separate codes. Keep the warnings alongside successful output rather than raising FrontendError::Invalid.

warning moonbit_frontend.name_normalization_collision
  is_ready and isReady normalize to is-ready in example/policy:rules
  related locations: both declaration name spans
  continuing with:
    is_ready → is-ready
    isReady  → is-ready-source-<token>
  fix: rename one declaration so its semantic words differ,

  targetNames.backend alone cannot fix this IR identity collision

Suggested edits must pass parsing, normalization and reservation checks before they are offered as applicable fixes. Do not automatically edit source files. Exact target conflicts fail with these same details rather than changing the requested public API.

Optional logs may mirror the events but are not the warning delivery mechanism.

Allocation reasons and origins survive Ion checkpoints and symbol receipts. Maintainer requirements, 2026-10-15: numeric source support is the next proposed local frontend capability, with Strings explicitly following numbers. This is an additive A7 scope requirement; it does not reopen completed Boolean tasks or remove F4/A2 packaging dependencies. Keep source language moonbit and describe supported forms through profiles/capabilities.

Preserve source numeric representation when lowering to Morphir arbitrary-precision values through existing attributes/metadata. Capture the resolved source type, signedness, width or arbitrary precision, floating representation and precision where relevant, original literal spelling and source identity, and conversion provenance at the correct type/value/declaration owners. Preserve these facts through Ion checkpoints, compatible checked JSON boundaries and generated symbol/origin receipts. Reuse upstream numeric constraint vocabulary where it applies; distinguish upstream draft designs from implemented contracts. Source representation facts must not silently become semantic bounds on every derived arbitrary-precision result. Width-sensitive source arithmetic, overflow and floating-point rounding must be explicit executable behavior or diagnosed unsupported, rather than relying on optional opaque metadata.

Use the existing Morphir SDK Int module as the conversion home and extend its inventory to cover all numeric forms supported by the pinned MoonBit compiler, after enumerating that inventory. Existing classic signed Int8/16/32/64 from/to functions remain classic SDK bindings. New unsigned/floating/other conversions must be clearly identified through annotations/attributes/metadata and a versioned SDK extension inventory as additions beyond the pinned morphir-elm SDK, with provenance, semantics, capability requirements and separate conformance evidence. Integer widening is exact; reverse narrowing is checked. Fractional, out-of-range and nonfinite float-to-Int cases require explicit conversion policies and must not be described as lossless. Cross-repository adoption is separate work.

After numeric libraries/math SDK qualification, add a Strings stage: typed String parameters/results, literals, immutable bindings/direct calls, concatenation, equality/comparison and a documented String SDK subset. Reuse existing SDK Text/String bindings while explicitly reconciling MoonBit String and Morphir/Elm UTF-16 code-unit, character/traversal, slicing and ordering semantics. Qualify Unicode boundary cases and source/evaluator/generated execution parity. Numeric and String stages each require an HTML specification under .dev before implementation, with canonical specs/plans/ledgers in beads.

title: MEP Contract as a Gleam Model Implementation Plan
description:
# MEP Contract as a Gleam Model Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** Add `spec/mep/`, where `contract/src/mep.gleam` models today's MEP protocol types, `generated/mep.ir.json` is the committed Morphir IR of that model, and CI fails when the two drift.

**Architecture:** The contract is a small Gleam project that the umbrella CLI compiles with its built-in Gleam frontend (`--ir-version 4 --types-only`); no `gleam` binary is needed. A mise task refreshes the committed IR. A Rust test in `crates/morphir/tests/` compiles the contract into a temporary directory, checks that every protocol type is present, and compares the result with the committed file byte for byte; the existing `morphir CLI (test + integration)` job runs it once `spec/mep/**` is in its path filter.

**Tech Stack:** Gleam (source language only), Morphir CLI (`crates/morphir`), the Gleam frontend in `ecosystem/morphir-rust/crates/morphir-gleam-binding`, Rust integration tests, mise, GitHub Actions.

**Spec:** beads `morphir-opua.1` design (render with `mise run beads:plan -- spec morphir-opua.1 --render`), sections for checkpoints 8, 9, 11 and 12, and work item B7. Issue finos/morphir#964, bead `morphir-opua.1.2.1`.

## Scope

In this plan: the handshake, capabilities, claims, compile, diagnostics and generate types that `morphir-extension-sdk` defines today (`ecosystem/morphir-rust/crates/morphir-extension-sdk/src/protocol.rs`, `src/types.rs`, `src/claims/`), the method names and error codes, the README with the versioning rule and the wire mapping, the committed IR and its drift check.

Not in this plan (existing beads): Rust types generated from the IR (`morphir-opua.1.2.2`), JSON Schema fixes (`.1.2.3`), the WIT backend and `generated/wit/` (`.1.2.4`), Python backend gaps (`.1.2.5`), `BitArray` in the Gleam frontend (`.1.2.6`), the MEP conformance suite and `spec/mep/mck/` content (`.1.2.7`), the typed IR payload (`morphir-opua.1.3.1`). Also out: workspace discovery payloads (they live in `morphir_workspace`, not the SDK), validate and transform payloads, and the JSON-RPC 2.0 envelope itself (a standard, not MEP).

## Decisions this plan makes inside the spec

1. **Arbitrary JSON is a recursive `Json` type** in the model (`JsonNull`, `JsonBool`, `JsonInt`, `JsonFloat`, `JsonString`, `JsonArray`, `JsonObject`). The Gleam frontend has no `Dynamic`, and a placeholder would hide what the wire carries. The WIT backend (`.1.2.4`) will need a non-recursive mapping for it (checkpoint 9 notes WIT rejects recursion); that bead records the choice.
2. **Flattened extra members are an explicit `extra: Dict(String, Json)` field** on `ExtensionCapabilities` and `CompileOptions`, with a doc comment saying they sit beside the named members on the wire. Reserved and legacy key rejection stays a codec rule, documented, not modelled.
3. **Labels are snake_case in Gleam and lowerCamelCase on the wire by default.** Every exception is written in the doc comment of its type and in the README's wire mapping table: `ExtensionInfo` keeps snake_case (`min_sdk_version`), enum spellings (`cli`, `frontend`, `error`, `compiled`), `PeerKind`'s fallback to `Unspecified`, `multiDocument` written only when true, `exposedModules` absent versus empty. A later codec bead generates the mapping; this plan only states it.
4. **Constructor names are unique across the module** and never shadow the prelude: severities are `ErrorSeverity`, `WarningSeverity`, `InfoSeverity`, `HintSeverity`; extension types are `FrontendExtension`, `BackendExtension`, `TransformExtension`, `ValidatorExtension`, `WorkspaceExtension`.
5. **One source file**, `contract/src/mep.gleam`, grouped by section comments, as checkpoint 11 lays out. The IR package is `morphir/mep` (checkpoint 12).
6. **The drift check is a Rust test, not a new CI job.** The committed file is a copy of `.morphir/out/compile.dest/morphir-ir.json`; `morphir compile -o spec/mep/generated` is not used because install refuses to overwrite a file it has no ledger entry for on a fresh checkout.

## Global Constraints

- Records use labelled fields (checkpoint 9: positional fields become `arg-1`).
- Compile with `--ir-version 4 --types-only` and an explicit `--config spec/mep/contract/morphir.toml`.
- Do not add Gleam to `[tools]` or CI; the built-in frontend is self-contained.
- The README states the pre-1.0 rule verbatim in meaning: before 1.0.0, a breaking change bumps the minor version and an additive or backward-compatible change bumps the patch version; published contracts carry no prerelease tags. The handshake sends the canonical `MAJOR.MINOR` form (today `"0.1"`). The claims format version (`0.1.0-draft.2`) is separate.
- Commits: Conventional Commits, no AI attribution, no `Co-Authored-By`, plain English, no em dashes.
- Track progress in beads with `mise run beads:plan -- ledger <plan-epic> "<line>"`.

## Review Focus

1. **A type or field the SDK sends that the model lacks.** Pinned by the task 1 to 3 coverage tests, which list every expected type and, for the records most likely to drift, every field label.
2. **A committed IR that does not match a fresh compile on another machine.** Pinned by task 4's byte comparison running in CI on Linux, with config discovery isolated from the user's environment.
3. **A wire spelling that the model silently changes.** Pinned by the README table in task 4 and a test that every type with a non-default wire rule names it in its doc comment.
4. **A constructor that shadows the prelude or collides with another.** Pinned by the compile itself in each task (the frontend rejects duplicates) and by Decision 4.
5. **CI not running the check when only `spec/mep/**` changes.** Pinned by task 4's filter change and a `tests/ci` check if the repo tests its filters.

---

## File map

| File | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| `spec/mep/README.md` | What MEP is, versioning rule, wire mapping, scope, how to regenerate |
| `spec/mep/contract/morphir.toml` | Morphir project: name `morphir/mep`, `source_directory = "src"`, `[frontend] language = "gleam"` |
| `spec/mep/contract/gleam.toml` | Gleam project for editors and optional real type-checking |
| `spec/mep/contract/.gitignore` | `/build/`, `/.morphir/` |
| `spec/mep/contract/src/mep.gleam` | The contract |
| `spec/mep/generated/mep.ir.json` | Committed IR |
| `crates/morphir/tests/mep_contract.rs` | Coverage and drift tests |
| `.config/mise/config.toml` | `spec:mep` and `spec:mep-check` tasks; `check` aggregate |
| `.github/workflows/ci.yml` | `spec/mep/**` in the path filter that selects the CLI test job |
| `CHANGELOG.md` | `[Unreleased]` entry |

## Branch and pull request

One umbrella branch, `feat/mep-spec-contract`, from `origin/main`. One PR to `main` after the whole-branch review. Refers to #964 and #960.

title: Morphir Host Phase A, Part 4 Implementation Plan
description:
# Morphir Host Phase A, Part 4 Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** Finish Phase A. `morphir-daemon` becomes a client of `morphir-host` with no MEP handshake, codec, registry or session actor of its own, and the three items deferred from part 3 land in `morphir-host`.

**Architecture:** The last duplicates in `morphir-daemon` are deleted after their behaviour tests move to `morphir-host-native`, where the real implementations already live. HTTP stays a way to reach an extension, as an `HttpChannel` behind a feature of `morphir-host-native`. `CallError` separates connect, handshake and decode failures. `Pool` gains a clock-free idle eviction. The umbrella CLI then drops the workarounds it carries for those gaps.

**Tech Stack:** Rust 2024, tokio, async-trait, async-lock, jsonrpsee 0.26 (HTTP client and test server only), Extism, cargo, mise.

**Spec:** `.dev/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-23-morphir-host-library-design.md` (with `.dev/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-23-cross-language-extension-sdk.md`). Part 3 ledger: `.dev/docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-24-morphir-host-phase-a-part-3.ledger.md`.

**Tracking:** beads, not GitHub discussions. Epic `morphir-opua.1.1` (Phase A, finos/morphir#959). This plan closes `morphir-opua.1.1.2` (finos/morphir-rust#237) and `morphir-opua.1.1.6` (finos/morphir-rust#240). Each task below has its own bead under those two; the GitHub issues stay open as mirrors until the work merges.

## Scope of this plan

In part 4:

- `CallError` gets `Connect`, `Handshake` and `Invalid` in place of `Open`. `Pool` does not retry a decode failure.
- `Pool::tick` and `Pool::evict_idle` give idle eviction without a clock, so `morphir-host` stays wasm32-clean.
- `HttpChannel` in `morphir-host-native` (feature `http`) replaces `ConnectedDaemonSession`.
- The daemon's real-extension tests move to `morphir-host-native`, on `activate` and `Session`.
- `morphir-daemon` keeps only `DaemonError`, `ExtensionLoader`, `VirtualPathConfig`, `FileSandbox` and `workspace`. Everything else in `extensions/` is deleted, with the `kameo`, `jsonrpsee` and `extism` dependencies.
- The #237 close-out: one test that a process guest and a native guest answer the same `Session::compile`.
- Umbrella: pin move, the new `CallError` arms, the start-failure side channel removed, the idle sweep on `Pool::evict_idle`.

Out of scope, recorded as beads elsewhere:

- `HostServices` (guest calls back to the host). No JSON-RPC guest calls the host today, and part 1 moved it next to the component imports. It becomes a Phase D bead under `morphir-opua.1.4`, linked from #237.
- A `NativeConnection` that skips JSON. `InvocationMode::NativeDirect` already gives the CLI typed calls with no JSON; `NativeChannel` covers the protocol path.
- Legacy top-level `documents` normalization. Since 0.4.0-beta.6 the SDK requires `sources` and ignores a top-level `documents`, pinned by `crates/morphir-extension-sdk/tests/compile_request.rs` (`top_level_documents_without_sources_reports_missing_sources`, `sources_ignores_unknown_top_level_documents`). #237's item is superseded by that decision.

## Decisions this plan makes inside the spec

1. **#240 "daemon tests pass unchanged" is met by moving the tests, not by keeping the API.** The daemon tests drive `activate_transport`, `InvokeOutcome` and `Session<T, Loaded>`, which are the duplicates #240 removes. Every behaviour they pin is kept by a ported test with the same name in `morphir-host-native`. No compatibility shims.
2. **`CallError` variants** (pre-1.0, so a breaking change is a minor bump of the crate):

   ```rust
   #[non_exhaustive]
   pub enum CallError {
       Rejected(HostError),  // the guest or host refused; session still ready
       Failed(HostError),    // the session broke; the connection closed its channel
       Invalid(HostError),   // the guest answered, the result did not decode or failed the host checks; session closed in order
       Connect(HostError),   // Pool only: `open` failed, no guest was started or reached
       Handshake(HostError), // Pool only: the guest started but the MEP handshake failed
   }
   ```

   `Invalid` is not retried by `Pool`: the same guest build gives the same bad answer. `CheckedConnection` reports a failed result check as `Invalid` too (part 4 ruling R1).
3. **Idle eviction counts ticks, not time.** `std::time::Instant` panics on `wasm32-unknown-unknown`, and `morphir-host` takes no clock dependency. The caller calls `Pool::tick` on its own timer and `Pool::evict_idle(n)` evicts every slot unused for at least `n` ticks. A slot is in use while its lock is held, so eviction skips it with `try_lock`, and an evicted session is always closed in order.
4. **`HttpChannel` is native and feature-gated.** jsonrpsee is not wasm-portable. Feature `http` of `morphir-host-native`, off by default, so the CLI build does not pull the HTTP client.

## Global Constraints

- `morphir-host` must pass `cargo check -p morphir-host --target wasm32-unknown-unknown` and must not depend on tokio (except dev), `morphir-daemon`, `morphir-host-native`, `morphir-distribution`, or any language binding.
- `morphir-host-native` must not depend on `morphir-daemon`.
- Every trait a browser client implements keeps `MaybeSend` plus the paired `cfg_attr(async_trait)` attributes.
- Wire sequences unchanged. Existing CLI error texts unchanged except where a task names the change and the CHANGELOG records it.
- Commits: Conventional Commits. No AI attribution, no `Co-Authored-By`. Plain English docs, no em dashes.
- Local process tests flake in parallel on this machine; judge real-process failures with `--test-threads=1`.

## Review Focus

1. **A retry that repeats a bad answer, or no retry for a lost guest.** Pinned by the task 1 pool tests: `Invalid` is returned once with one open; `Failed` still reopens once.
2. **An idle sweep that closes a guest in use, or never closes one.** Pinned by task 2 tests: a slot whose lock is held is skipped; a slot unused for `n` ticks is closed in order; a call after eviction opens a fresh guest.
3. **A lost behaviour when the daemon tests move.** Pinned by task 4: every `#[test]`/`#[tokio::test]` name in the moved files exists in the new files (a name-diff check in the step), and the mise tasks run the new locations.
4. **HTTP failures reported as the wrong state.** Pinned by task 3: a refused connection and a timeout are `Indeterminate` with cause `Transport`; a JSON-RPC error reply is an error response, not a channel failure.
5. **A CLI text change nobody recorded.** Pinned by task 7: the playground start and handshake texts keep their current exact wording without the side channel.

---

## File map

finos/morphir-rust (`ecosystem/morphir-rust/`):

| File | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/morphir-host/src/connection.rs` | `CallError` variants |
| `crates/morphir-host/src/session.rs` | `Session::call` returns `Invalid` |
| `crates/morphir-host/src/pool.rs` | Connect/handshake split, no retry on decode, `tick`, `evict_idle` |
| `crates/morphir-host/tests/{session,pool}.rs` | Tests for the above |
| `crates/morphir-host-native/src/http.rs` | `HttpChannel` (feature `http`) |
| `crates/morphir-host-native/examples/mep-http-backend.rs` | Moved test server |
| `crates/morphir-host-native/tests/*_extension.rs`, `tests/process_describe.rs`, `tests/fixtures/` | Moved real-extension tests and fixtures |
| `crates/morphir-daemon/src/**` | Duplicates deleted |
| `crates/morphir-elm-binding/tests/{frontend,acceptance,wasm}.rs` | Fixture paths |
| `.mise/tasks/{test/daemon,test/process,test/extism,extension/artifact/*}`, `.github/ci-impact.toml` | New test locations |
| `CHANGELOG.md` | Removed/Changed entries |

finos/morphir (umbrella):

| File | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/morphir/src/extensions/guest.rs`, `commands/ui/provider/extension.rs` | New `CallError` arms |
| `crates/morphir/src/commands/ui/provider/pool.rs` | Side channel removed; sweep on `Pool::evict_idle` |
| `CHANGELOG.md` | Pin move and any text change |

## Branches and pull requests

1. Tasks 1 to 6: one finos/morphir-rust branch from `origin/main` (`feat/morphir-host-phase-a-close`). One PR after a whole-branch review. Refers to finos/morphir-rust#237 and #240.
2. Task 7: one umbrella branch after that PR merges, based on `milestone/v0.4.0-beta.9` and updated with `origin/main`; the PR targets `milestone/v0.4.0-beta.9`. Pin the submodule to the merge commit. (finos/morphir-rust has no milestone branch, so the tasks 1-6 PR targets its `main`.)

---

title: morphir-host Phase A, part 3: Registry, Pool, and the CLI off the daemon session Implementation Plan
description:
# morphir-host Phase A, part 3: Registry, Pool, and the CLI off the daemon session Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** Resolve providers with a portable `morphir_host::Registry`, reuse workbench guests with a portable `morphir_host::Pool`, keep the daemon's error texts across channels, and move every remaining CLI extension path off `morphir-daemon`'s registry, typestate session, and actor.

**Architecture:** `morphir-host` gains `Registry`, the `GuestSource` trait, `Resolved`, and `Pool<K>` (checkpoints 5, 14, 19). It depends on `morphir-core` for IR version matching and stays wasm32-clean. `morphir-host-native` gains `NativeSource` (next to `NativeChannel`) and `InstalledSource`. `ChannelError` gains a `cause`, so a transport failure that began as an I/O or JSON error keeps its text at the daemon boundary (part 2 ruling R8). The umbrella CLI builds a `morphir_host::Registry`, calls resolved sources, and serves the workbench through `Pool`. After this plan the CLI depends on `morphir-daemon` only for `DaemonError` text mapping; part 4 removes the daemon's registry, typestate session, actor, and transport copies.

**Tech Stack:** Rust 2024 (`rust-version = "1.98"`), `async-trait` 0.1, `async-lock` 3 (portable async mutex), `morphir-core` (format versions), `morphir-distribution`, `morphir-common`, `morphir-extension-sdk`, tokio (tests and native only).

**Spec:** discussion 949, checkpoints 5, 10, 14, 18, 19 (local `.dev/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-23-morphir-host-library-design.md`). Part 1 plan #976, part 2 plan #983 and their closing checkpoints. Tracking: epic #958, Phase A #959, finos/morphir-rust#238 (Registry), finos/morphir-rust#239 (Pool), #963 (rest).

---

## Scope of this plan

In part 3:

- `ChannelError` and `HostError::Channel` carry a `cause` so I/O and JSON texts survive (part 2 R8).
- `Registry`, `GuestSource`, `Resolved`, `ProviderMetadata`, `ProviderOrigin`, `InvocationPolicy`, `InvocationMode`, `CapabilityMetadataScope` in `morphir-host`, ported from the daemon with the same rules and texts.
- `NativeSource` and `InstalledSource` in `morphir-host-native`. `NativeSource` stays native because in-process guests run on a blocking worker (`spawn_blocking`), as `NativeChannel` does.
- `Pool<K>` in `morphir-host`, with the 8 behaviours of the workbench's `SessionReuseInvoker`.
- CLI: registry, compile, generate, `extension list`, playground catalog, workbench invoker, and the UI workspace provider move to the host crates. `builtin_provider`, `open_*_session`, `open_loaded`, `installed_loaded`, `session_failure`, `failed_session_message`, and `ui/provider/sessions.rs` are deleted.
- The two missing CLI tests from part 2 (UI installed workspace provider; installed provider rejected-call text).

Part 4 gets its own plan: delete the daemon's `ExtensionRegistry`, typestate `Session`, kameo actor, `ExtensionSession`/`SpawnedProcessSession`/`SpawnedProcessTransport`, `ExtismTransport`, `NativeMepTransport`, `activate_transport`, `ExtensionResponseExt`, and move `ConnectedDaemonSession` to an HTTP `Channel`. Those are now used only inside `morphir-daemon` and its tests.

## Decisions this plan makes inside the spec

1. `GuestSource` is a trait with one `connect` method that returns a boxed `GuestConnection`. The registry never activates anything itself.
2. `Pool` is keyed by provider id and stores a fingerprint (`"{id}@{version}:{origin:?}:{mode:?}"`, as today). A `CallError::Failed` plays the role of the daemon's `SessionLost`: evict, reopen once, retry once. `CallError::Rejected` keeps the session.
3. Registry errors are `HostError::Invalid(text)` with the daemon's texts. At the CLI boundary they pass through `DaemonError::from`, so the `Extension error: ` prefix stays (part 2 R6).
4. `ChannelCause::{Transport, Io, Json}`. `From<HostError> for DaemonError` maps a `Channel` error with cause `Io` or `Json` to `DaemonError::Other(anyhow!(message))`, whose display is the message unchanged, so the CLI prints `IO error: ...` again instead of `Extension error: IO error: ...`.

## Global Constraints

- `morphir-host` must pass `cargo check -p morphir-host --target wasm32-unknown-unknown` and must not depend on tokio (except dev), `morphir-daemon`, `morphir-host-native`, `morphir-distribution`, or any language binding. It may depend on `morphir-core` (checkpoint 19) and a portable async mutex (`async-lock`).
- `morphir-host-native` must not depend on `morphir-daemon`.
- Every trait a browser client implements keeps `MaybeSend` plus the paired `cfg_attr(async_trait)` attributes.
- Resolution rules and texts are unchanged: language or target filter, advertised IR version normalization, installed over built-in, ambiguity and no-match texts, duplicate-id text, invocation policy.
- Wire sequences unchanged. Existing CLI error texts unchanged, now including the `IO error: ...` / `JSON error: ...` texts part 2 R8 changed.
- The workbench keeps: one guest per provider id reused across compile and generate, evict and retry once on a lost session, keep the session on a rejection, `abandon` after a timeout, replacement when the provider fingerprint changes, one-shot calls for direct (native typed) providers, the 120 s invocation timeout.
- Commits: Conventional Commits. No AI attribution, no `Co-Authored-By`. Plain English docs, no em dashes.
- Local process tests flake in parallel on this machine; judge real-process failures with `--test-threads=1`.

## Review Focus

1. **Resolution drift.** A provider that resolved before must resolve the same way (same provider, same mode, same texts). Pinned by porting all 20 daemon `provider_registry` tests to `morphir-host` in task 2.
2. **A pool that keeps a dead guest or drops a live one.** Pinned by the 8 ported workbench behaviours in task 4 and the CLI playground tests in task 7.
3. **Lost I/O text again.** Pinned by the task 1 test that an I/O-rooted channel failure displays `IO error: ...` through `DaemonError::from`.
4. **Weaker validation for installed providers.** `InstalledSource::connect` must return the same `CheckedConnection` as `activate`. Pinned by the task 3 parity test and the traversal test in the umbrella.
5. **Held locks across await points in `Pool`** that block unrelated providers. Pinned by the task 4 test `a_slow_provider_does_not_block_another`.

---

## File map

finos/morphir-rust (`ecosystem/morphir-rust/`):

| File | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/morphir-host/src/channel.rs`, `src/error.rs` | `ChannelCause`, `cause` on `ChannelError` and `HostError::Channel` |
| `crates/morphir-host/src/registry.rs`, `src/registry/types.rs` | `Registry`, `GuestSource`, `Resolved`, metadata and policy types |
| `crates/morphir-host/src/pool.rs` | `Pool<K>` |
| `crates/morphir-host/tests/registry.rs`, `tests/pool.rs` | Ported behaviour tests |
| `crates/morphir-host-native/src/installed.rs`, `src/native.rs` | `InstalledSource`, `NativeSource` |
| `crates/morphir-daemon/src/error.rs` | `From<HostError>` keeps I/O and JSON texts |

finos/morphir (umbrella):

| File | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/morphir/src/extensions.rs`, `src/extensions/guest.rs` | Registry built from host sources; calls through `Resolved` |
| `crates/morphir/src/commands/{compile.rs, compile/prepare.rs, generate.rs, extension.rs}` | Use `morphir_host` registry types |
| `crates/morphir/src/commands/ui/provider/playground.rs` | Catalog and invoker on host types |
| `crates/morphir/src/commands/ui/provider/pool.rs` | New `PooledInvoker` (replaces `sessions.rs`) |
| `crates/morphir/src/commands/ui/provider/extension.rs` | Installed workspace provider through `InstalledSource`, with a test |

## Branches and pull requests

1. Tasks 1 to 4: one finos/morphir-rust branch from `origin/main` (`feat/morphir-host-registry-pool`). One PR after a whole-branch review. Refers to #238, #239.
2. Tasks 5 to 7: one umbrella branch from `origin/main` after that PR merges. Pin the submodule to the merge commit. Refers to #963, #959.

title: Task 1: Keep the cause of a channel failure
description:
### Task 1: Keep the cause of a channel failure

**Files:**
- Modify: `crates/morphir-host/src/channel.rs`, `src/error.rs`, `src/jsonrpc.rs`, `src/testing.rs`, `src/probe.rs` (any `ChannelError`/`HostError::Channel` construction)
- Modify: `crates/morphir-host-native/src/{native.rs, extism/channel.rs, process/channel.rs, process/child.rs}` and tests constructing `ChannelError`
- Modify: `crates/morphir-daemon/src/error.rs`, `src/extensions/process/describe.rs`
- Test: `crates/morphir-host/tests/connection.rs`, `crates/morphir-daemon/src/error.rs` (unit)

**Interfaces:**
- Produces:
  ```rust
  /// What a transport failure began as.
  #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Default)]
  pub enum ChannelCause {
      /// The transport itself failed: a timeout, a closed pipe the host detected, a stopped guest.
      #[default]
      Transport,
      /// An I/O error. The message starts with `IO error: `.
      Io,
      /// A JSON encoding or decoding error. The message starts with `JSON error: `.
      Json,
  }
  pub struct ChannelError { pub message: String, pub state: ChannelState, pub cause: ChannelCause }
  HostError::Channel { message: String, state: ChannelState, cause: ChannelCause }
  impl ChannelCause { pub fn of(error: &HostError) -> Self } // Io -> Io, Json -> Json, Channel{cause} -> cause, else Transport
  ```
- `From<ChannelError> for HostError` copies `cause`. Every place that turns a `HostError` into a `ChannelError` (for example `ProcessChannel::fail`, `ExtismChannel`'s `indeterminate`) sets `cause: ChannelCause::of(&error)`. Combined messages (`"; process cleanup also failed"`, `"; transport abort also failed"`) keep the first error's cause.
- `From<HostError> for DaemonError`: `Json -> Json`, `Io -> Io`, `Channel { cause: Io | Json, message, .. } -> DaemonError::Other(anyhow::anyhow!(message))`, else `Extension(text)`.

- [ ] **Step 1: Write the failing tests**
  - Host (`tests/connection.rs`): a `MemoryChannel` that fails `receive` with `ChannelError { message: "IO error: broken pipe".into(), state: ChannelState::Stopped, cause: ChannelCause::Io }`; the call fails with `CallError::Failed(HostError::Channel { cause: ChannelCause::Io, .. })`.
  - Daemon (`src/error.rs` unit test): `DaemonError::from(HostError::Channel { message: "IO error: broken pipe".into(), state: ChannelState::Stopped, cause: ChannelCause::Io }).to_string() == "IO error: broken pipe"`; with `cause: ChannelCause::Transport` the text is `"Extension error: IO error: broken pipe"` (unchanged behaviour for transport causes); a JSON cause keeps `"JSON error: ..."`.
  - Host-native (`src/process/channel.rs` unit test, unix): a `ProcessChannel` whose guest exits at once; `send` of a request fails and the error's `cause` is `Io` when the write hit `EPIPE` (skip-assert the cause if the race yields "closed stdout before a response frame", which is a `Transport` cause; assert one of the two outcomes with its matching cause).
- [ ] **Step 2: Run them and see them fail** (`cargo test -p morphir-host -p morphir-host-native -p morphir-daemon --lib --tests`): compile errors on `cause`.
- [ ] **Step 3: Implement** the type, the `of` helper, every construction site (list them with `rg -n 'ChannelError \{|HostError::Channel \{' crates`), and the daemon mapping. `MemoryChannel::fail` keeps taking a `ChannelError`. Daemon `anyhow` is already a dependency.
- [ ] **Step 4: Run** `cargo test -p morphir-host -p morphir-host-native`, `cargo test -p morphir-daemon --lib --tests -- --test-threads=1`, clippy on the three crates with `--all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`, the wasm32 check, fmt.
- [ ] **Step 5: Commit** `feat(host): keep what a transport failure began as`.

- Modify: `crates/morphir/src/commands/extension/probe.rs`, `crates/morphir/src/commands/extension.rs` (`describe_publish_artifact`)
- Modify: `crates/morphir/tests/support/process_bundle.rs`

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: `morphir_host::{describe, Description, DescriptionSource}`, `morphir_host_native::process::{ProcessChannel, ProcessLaunch}`.
- The probe keeps its outputs: `ProbeSource::Describe` or `ProbeSource::SessionFallback`, the same `check_claims` / `check_session` calls, and the same `DistributionError::Probe(text)` mapping.

- [ ] **Step 1: Change the three call sites**

In each of `probe.rs::claims`, `describe_publish_artifact`, and `tests/support/process_bundle.rs::from_executable`, replace:

```rust
let transport = SpawnedProcessTransport::spawn(launch).await.map_err(...)?;
let description = transport.describe(<params>).await.map_err(...)?;
```

with:

```rust
let channel = morphir_host_native::process::ProcessChannel::spawn(launch)
    .await
    .map_err(|error| <same mapping as spawn today>)?;
let description = morphir_host::describe(channel, &host_config(), &<the launch id>)
    .await
    .map_err(|error| <same mapping as describe today>)?;
```

`ProcessLaunch` now comes from `morphir_host_native::process`. Match on `morphir_host::DescriptionSource` in place of the daemon's type. In `tests/support/process_bundle.rs`, use `crate::...::host_config()` if the support module can reach it; otherwise build `morphir_host::HostConfig::new(PeerInfo { kind: PeerKind::Cli, name: "morphir-cli".into(), version: env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION").into() })` there, so the test support stops hardcoding `MEP_VERSION`.

Expected: every test named in `tests/cli_integration/extension_probe.rs` and `tests/support/process_publish.rs` passes.

- [ ] **Step 3: Commit**

```bash
git add crates/morphir ecosystem/morphir-rust Cargo.lock
git commit -m "feat(cli): probe and describe extensions through morphir-host"
```

**Interfaces:**
- Produces in `crate::extensions::guest` (crate-private):

```rust
/// A checked MEP connection to one provider, ready to open.
pub(crate) type ProviderConnection =
    morphir_host_native::CheckedConnection<morphir_host::JsonRpcConnection<Box<dyn morphir_host::Channel>, morphir_host::ExpectedChecks>>;

/// Open a connection to a configured process provider.
pub(crate) async fn configured(launch: ProcessLaunch, provider: &str) -> Result<ProviderConnection, CliError>;

/// Open a connection to a resolved provider that speaks MEP
/// (`NativeMep`, `ProcessMep` or `WasmMep`).
pub(crate) async fn resolved(
    home: &MorphirHome,
    workspace: &Path,
    provider: &str,
    mode: InvocationMode,
    native: Option<&NativeExtension>,
    installed: Option<&InstalledExtensionSnapshot>,
) -> Result<ProviderConnection, CliError>;

/// Open, make one call, close. Errors keep the CLI's texts.
pub(crate) async fn call_once<P: Serialize, R: DeserializeOwned>(
    connection: ProviderConnection,
    provider: &str,
    method: &str,
    request: P,
) -> Result<R, CliError>;

/// Open and read what the provider negotiated, then close.
pub(crate) async fn negotiate(connection: ProviderConnection, provider: &str) -> Result<NegotiatedProvider, CliError>;
```

- Error texts (unchanged from today):
  - spawn: `Failed to start provider '{provider}': {error}`
  - handshake failure: `Provider '{provider}' failed during initialize: {error}`
  - rejected call: `Provider '{provider}' rejected '{method}': {error}`, plus `; orderly shutdown also failed: {close}` when the orderly close fails
  - failed call: `Provider '{provider}' failed during {method}: {error}`
  - shutdown failure after success: `Provider '{provider}' failed during shutdown: {error}`
  - installed verification: `Failed to verify installed provider '{provider}': {error}`; activation: `Failed to activate installed provider '{provider}': {error}`
- `Session::call` returns `CallError::Rejected` or `CallError::Failed`; map `Rejected` to the rejected text and `Failed` to the failed text. The old `"; transport state is indeterminate"` suffix appears when the host error is `HostError::Channel { state: Indeterminate, .. }`.

- [ ] **Step 1: Write a failing test that pins the rejected-call text**

In `crates/morphir/src/extensions.rs` tests, add a test that compiles through a configured process provider script that answers `morphir.frontend.compile` with an RPC error, and asserts the exact text `Provider 'fixture' rejected 'morphir.frontend.compile': RPC error -32001: does not compile`. Reuse the unix script pattern already used by `gleam_legacy_selector_preserves_an_installed_provider_with_that_id` or the `extension_probe.rs` fixture guest; mark it `#[cfg(unix)]`.

Run it on the current code first. It must PASS before the change (it pins today's text). Record that run.

- [ ] **Step 2: Implement `guest.rs` and rewire the call sites**

- `probe_process(launch, provider)`: `guest::negotiate(guest::configured(launch, provider).await?, provider)`.
- `invoke_process(launch, provider, method, request)`: `guest::call_once(guest::configured(launch, provider).await?, provider, method, request)`.
- `invoke_frontend`, `invoke_backend`, `invoke_workspace_discovery`: keep the `NativeDirect` arm. Replace the `NativeMep` and `ProcessMep | WasmMep` arms with `guest::call_once(guest::resolved(home, workspace, id, mode, resolved.native_extension(), resolved.installed_snapshot()).await?, id, method, request)`.
- `guest::resolved` for `NativeMep` uses `NativeChannel::new(native)`; for installed modes it calls `activate_installed_snapshot(home, snapshot)` then `morphir_host_native::activate(artifact, workspace)`.
- `ui/provider/extension.rs::invoke_installed`: open `guest::resolved(...)` for the snapshot, `Session::open`, check the negotiated workspace capability with the same test as today, call `methods::WORKSPACE_DISCOVER`, close. Keep its error texts.
- Delete the typestate helpers listed above and the `morphir_daemon::extensions` imports they needed.

- [ ] **Step 3: Run the CLI gates and the compatibility suites**

Run: `cargo fmt --package morphir --package integration-tests --check && cargo clippy --locked --package morphir --package integration-tests --all-targets -- -D warnings && cargo test --locked --package morphir -- --test-threads=4`
Expected: all pass, including the new text-pinning test and `generate_rejects_traversal_from_an_installed_provider_without_writing`.
Run: `mise run ci:fetch-published-bundles && cargo build --locked --release --package morphir && mise run test:host-compatibility`
Expected: avro, openapi, python and rust pass locally. `elm_reference` and `scala_elm` need Linux x86_64 or `MORPHIR_ELM_EXTENSION_BIN` / `MORPHIR_SCALA_ELM_EXTENSION_BIN`; PR CI runs them.


title: morphir-host Phase A, part 2: native channels, probe, and CLI one-shot calls Implementation Plan
description:
# morphir-host Phase A, part 2: native channels, probe, and CLI one-shot calls Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** Put the process, Extism, and in-process native transports behind `morphir_host::Channel` in a new crate `morphir-host-native`, move the describe probe and the negotiation checks into `morphir-host`, and run every CLI one-shot extension call (compile, generate, workspace discovery, install probe, publish describe, configured providers) through `morphir_host::Session`.

**Architecture:** `morphir-host` stays portable. It gains `Channel::abort`, `ExpectedChecks` (the daemon's full negotiation rules, moved), and `describe` (the install probe with session fallback, moved). The new crate `morphir-host-native` owns everything that needs tokio processes, Extism, or non-portable validation crates: `ProcessLaunch`, framing, staging, `ProcessChannel`, `ExtismChannel`, `NativeChannel`, result validation, and `activate`. `morphir-daemon` keeps its public API and delegates to both crates. The umbrella CLI then drops its typestate one-shot paths. The workbench session pool and the provider registry stay on the daemon until part 3.

**Tech Stack:** Rust 2024 (`rust-version = "1.98"`), tokio (`process`, `io-util`, `time`, `rt`), `extism` 1, `tempfile` 3, `semver` 1, `async-trait` 0.1, `morphir-extension-sdk`, `morphir-core`, `morphir-distribution`, `morphir-workspace`.

**Spec:** design record https://github.com/finos/morphir/discussions/949, checkpoints 5, 6, 10, 14 and 18 (local `.dev/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-23-morphir-host-library-design.md`). Part 1 plan and its rulings: https://github.com/finos/morphir/discussions/976. Tracking: epic #958, Phase A #959, finos/morphir-rust#237 (rest), finos/morphir-rust#240 (transports part), #963 (rest).

---

## Scope of this plan

In part 2:

- `morphir-host`: `Channel::abort`, `impl Channel for Box<C>`, `ExpectedChecks` and the expectation types, and `describe`.
- New crate `morphir-host-native` (checkpoint 18): process launch, framing and staging, `ProcessChannel`, `NativeChannel`, `ExtismChannel` with the Extism container, result validation, `CheckedConnection`, and `activate`.
- `morphir-daemon` delegates to the moved code. Its public API does not change.
- Umbrella CLI: install probe, publish describe, configured providers, installed providers (`ProcessMep`, `WasmMep`), native MEP providers, and the workbench workspace provider run through `morphir_host::Session`.

Part 3 gets its own plan:

- `Registry` and `GuestSource`, and provider resolution out of `ExtensionRegistry` (#238).
- `Pool`, and the workbench leaves `sessions.rs` and `SessionHandle` (#239).
- `morphir-daemon` drops its typestate session and actor, and removes `ExtensionResponseExt` (#240 rest).

## Decisions this plan makes inside the spec

1. `Channel` gains `abort` with a default that calls `close`. Part 1 used `close` for both an orderly close after `exit` and an abort after a protocol failure. A process channel must kill its child on abort, but wait for it on close. Waiting after a failure would hang for the full request timeout.
2. `describe` lives in portable `morphir-host`, not in `morphir-host-native`. It needs only the SDK and `semver`, so a browser host can probe too.
3. Method-result validation (compile IR checks, generated artifact paths) moves to `morphir-host-native`, because it needs `morphir-core` and `morphir-distribution`. `CheckedConnection` wraps any `GuestConnection` and applies it. A validation failure closes the session in order, the same way a decode failure does (part 1 ruling R6). The daemon aborted instead. Both end the session and report the error.
4. The daemon's Extism host functions (`MorphirHostFunctions`) are stubs today. They move unchanged. This plan does not implement them.
5. The CLI keeps `NativeDirect` calls (typed Rust calls on built-in providers) as they are. They are not MEP sessions.

## Global Constraints

- Crates: `ecosystem/morphir-rust/crates/morphir-host` (portable) and `ecosystem/morphir-rust/crates/morphir-host-native` (new). Workspace members are `crates/*`. Add `morphir-host-native` to root `default-members`, to the README crate table, and to every `.github/ci-impact.toml` `crates` list that names `morphir-daemon` (part 1 lesson: `classify.py` only tests `default-members`).
- `morphir-host` must still pass `cargo check -p morphir-host --target wasm32-unknown-unknown` and must not depend on tokio (except as a dev-dependency), `morphir-daemon`, `morphir-host-native`, `morphir-distribution`, `morphir-core`, or any language binding.
- `morphir-host-native` must not depend on `morphir-daemon`. `morphir-daemon` depends on `morphir-host-native`.
- Every trait a browser client implements keeps the `MaybeSend` plus paired `cfg_attr(async_trait)` pattern.
- The wire sequence to released guests does not change:
  - Session: `morphir.initialize` (id 1), calls (ids 2, 3, ...), `morphir.shutdown`, `morphir.exit`.
  - Probe: `morphir.extension.describe` (id 1). Fallback: `morphir.initialize` (id 2), `morphir.initialized` notification, `morphir.extension.capabilities` (id 3), `morphir.shutdown` (id 4), then `morphir.exit`.
  - Frames: `Content-Length: {len}\r\n\r\n{json}`.
- Existing error texts stay byte-identical. The daemon and CLI tests match them.
- The CLI's own message formats stay: `Provider '{provider}' rejected '{method}': {error}`, `Provider '{provider}' failed during {operation}: {error}`, `Failed to start provider '{provider}': {error}`.
- Commits: Conventional Commits. No AI attribution, no `Co-Authored-By`.
- Doc comments in plain English. No em dashes.
- Local process tests are flaky in parallel on this machine (100 ms timeouts). Run real-process suites with `--test-threads=1` when judging a failure.

## Review Focus

1. **An abort that waits.** After a protocol failure a process channel must kill the child promptly, not wait up to 30 s. Pinned by the task 1 test `a_protocol_failure_aborts_rather_than_closes` and the task 5 test `abort_kills_the_child_without_waiting`.
2. **A second `exit`.** The daemon's process `terminate` sent `morphir.exit` itself. `JsonRpcConnection::close` now sends it through `send`, so `ProcessChannel::close` must not send another. Pinned by the task 5 test `close_after_exit_waits_without_a_second_exit`.
3. **Probe wire sequence drift.** Released guests (Elm 0.3.1, scala-elm) fall back to the session path with exact ids. Pinned by the task 3 test `fallback_uses_the_released_ids_and_order` and by the host compatibility suite in task 9.
4. **Weaker validation after the move.** Installed providers must still get discovery locks, legacy backend rules, and artifact path checks. Pinned by the moved daemon tests in tasks 2 and 7 and by the task 9 test that generates through an installed provider with a traversal artifact (`generate_rejects_traversal_from_an_installed_provider_without_writing`, already in the umbrella).
5. **Staging leaks.** Verified bytes are staged in private temp directories. A channel must keep the staging directory alive until the child exits, and remove it after. Pinned by the moved test `verified_bytes_stage_under_the_explicit_managed_directory` and the umbrella test `staging_is_private_under_home_and_removed_after_success_or_failure`.

---

## File map

finos/morphir-rust (`ecosystem/morphir-rust/`):

| File | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/morphir-host/src/channel.rs` | `Channel::abort`, `impl Channel for Box<C>` |
| `crates/morphir-host/src/jsonrpc.rs` | Use `abort` on failure |
| `crates/morphir-host/src/testing.rs` | `MemoryChannel` counts aborts |
| `crates/morphir-host/src/expected.rs` | `ExpectedExtension`, `PersistedExtensionCapabilities`, `CapabilityExpectation`, `ExpectedChecks`, `validate_negotiation` (moved) |
| `crates/morphir-host/src/probe.rs` | `describe`, `Description`, `DescriptionSource`, `permits_fallback`, `check_capability_kinds` (moved) |
| `crates/morphir-host-native/Cargo.toml` | New crate |
| `crates/morphir-host-native/src/lib.rs` | Exports |
| `crates/morphir-host-native/src/process/{mod.rs,launch.rs,frame.rs,stage.rs,child.rs,channel.rs}` | Launch, framing, staging, child, `ProcessChannel` |
| `crates/morphir-host-native/src/native.rs` | `NativeChannel` |
| `crates/morphir-host-native/src/extism/{mod.rs,container.rs,host_functions.rs,channel.rs}` | Extism container (moved), `ExtismChannel` |
| `crates/morphir-host-native/src/results.rs` | Result validation (moved), `CheckedConnection` |
| `crates/morphir-host-native/src/activate.rs` | `activate`, `ActivatedGuest` |
| `crates/morphir-daemon/src/extensions/**` | Delegate to the two crates, keep the public API |

finos/morphir (umbrella):

| File | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/morphir/Cargo.toml` | Add `morphir-host-native` |
| `crates/morphir/src/extensions.rs` | One-shot calls through `morphir_host::Session` |
| `crates/morphir/src/extensions/guest.rs` | New: open a checked connection for a resolved or configured provider, map errors to `CliError` |
| `crates/morphir/src/commands/extension/probe.rs`, `commands/extension.rs` | `describe` through `ProcessChannel` |
| `crates/morphir/src/commands/ui/provider/extension.rs` | Workspace provider through a session |
| `crates/morphir/tests/support/process_bundle.rs` | `describe` through `ProcessChannel` |

## Branches and pull requests

1. Tasks 1 to 7: one branch of finos/morphir-rust from `origin/main` in the submodule checkout (`git -C ecosystem/morphir-rust switch -c feat/morphir-host-native origin/main`). One PR after a whole-branch review. It refers to #237 and #240.
2. Tasks 8 and 9: one umbrella branch from `origin/main` after that PR merges and main CI passes on the merge commit. Pin the submodule to the merge commit. The PR refers to #963 and #959.

title: morphir-host Phase A, part 1: portable session core Implementation Plan
description:
# morphir-host Phase A, part 1: portable session core Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** Create the portable `morphir-host` crate with a sans-IO MEP session core. Run the daemon's existing session controller on top of that core without changing its behaviour. Make every CLI path offer one host identity and one version list.

**Architecture:** `morphir-host` holds the MEP handshake as a synchronous state machine (`SessionCore`): an event goes in and one action comes out. Two async shells drive the core. The first is the existing typestate `Session<T, S>` in `morphir-daemon`, which keeps its public API, so the CLI and the daemon's 60+ session tests become the regression suite for the core. The second is a new portable `JsonRpcConnection` over a `Channel` trait. It has no tokio code and compiles for `wasm32-unknown-unknown`. The CLI then takes its peer name and version list from one `HostConfig`.

**Tech Stack:** Rust 2024 (workspace `rust-version = "1.98"`), `serde`/`serde_json`, `thiserror` 2, `async-trait` 0.1, `tokio` (tests only in `morphir-host`), `morphir-extension-sdk`, `morphir-workspace`.

**Spec:** the design record is https://github.com/finos/morphir/discussions/949 (checkpoints 1 to 17). It is also in the local notes: `.dev/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-23-morphir-host-library-design.md`. Tracking: epic finos/morphir#958, Phase A finos/morphir#959. This plan covers finos/morphir-rust#236, part of finos/morphir-rust#237, and the host-identity part of finos/morphir#963.

---

## Scope of this plan

Phase A is too large for one plan. This plan is part 1. Part 1 alone produces software that works and is tested.

In part 1:

- `morphir-host` crate with `HostConfig`, `HostError`, `Negotiated`, envelope validation, `SessionChecks`, `SessionCore`, `Channel`, `GuestConnection`, `JsonRpcConnection`, `Session`, the one-shot helpers, and a `MemoryChannel` test double.
- `morphir-daemon`'s typestate controller runs on `SessionCore`. Its public API does not change.
- The CLI uses one `host_config()` for every `initialize` and `describe`.

Part 2 gets its own plan after part 1 merges:

- Move the process stdio, Extism, and native transports out of `morphir-daemon` and behind `Channel` (#240).
- Move `describe` with session fallback (the install probe) into `morphir-host`.
- `Registry` and `GuestSource`, and the move of provider resolution out of `ExtensionRegistry` (#238).
- Move CLI compile and generate onto `morphir-host` sessions (the rest of #963).
- `Pool`, and the workbench leaves `sessions.rs` (#239).

## Decisions this plan makes inside the spec

Check these during review. Each one narrows the spec. None of them changes a checkpoint.

1. `SessionCore::handle` returns one `Action`, not a `Vec<Action>`. MEP sessions have one request in flight, so every event produces exactly one action.
2. `GuestConnection` has a generic `call(method, params)`. `Session` provides the typed `compile` and `generate`. A later `ComponentConnection` maps method names to WIT exports.
3. `HostServices` is not in part 1. No MEP guest calls the host over JSON-RPC today, so a `HostServices` trait would have no caller. It arrives with the component imports in Phase D.
4. The core does not send `morphir.initialized` in a normal session. The daemon does not send it today, and released guests were tested without it. Only the describe fallback sends it, and that code stays in the daemon in part 1.
5. Method-result validation (compile IR checks, generated artifact paths) stays in `morphir-daemon`. It depends on `morphir-core` and `morphir-distribution`, which are not proven portable. `SessionCore` validates the envelope and the negotiation only.

## Global Constraints

- Crate location: `ecosystem/morphir-rust/crates/morphir-host` (finos/morphir-rust). Workspace members are `crates/*`, so no workspace edit is needed.
- `morphir-host` must pass `cargo check -p morphir-host --target wasm32-unknown-unknown`. It must not depend on tokio (except as a dev-dependency), `morphir-daemon`, `morphir-distribution`, `morphir-core`, or any language binding.
- Traits that a browser client implements use `MaybeSend` (it means `Send` on native targets and nothing on `wasm32`), with `#[cfg_attr(not(target_arch = "wasm32"), async_trait)]` and `#[cfg_attr(target_arch = "wasm32", async_trait(?Send))]`.
- MEP versions: offer `SUPPORTED_MEP_VERSIONS` from `morphir-extension-sdk` (currently `["0.1"]`). Never hardcode `"0.1"` outside tests.
- The client supplies the peer. The only `"morphir-cli"` literal in `crates/morphir/src` after task 7 is the one in `host_config()`.
- Error texts that exist today stay byte-identical. Examples: `RPC error {code}: {message}`, `Extension selected protocol version '{v}' that the host did not offer`, `Extension response ID {a} did not match request ID {b}`.
- The wire sequence to released guests stays identical: `morphir.initialize` (id 1), calls (ids 2, 3, ...), `morphir.shutdown`, then `morphir.exit` from the transport.
- Commits: Conventional Commits. No AI attribution, no `Co-Authored-By` lines (EasyCLA).
- Code style: match surrounding code. Doc comments in plain English. No em dashes.

## Review Focus

These failure modes follow from the spec, but ordinary unit tests would miss them. Each line names the task whose test pins it.

1. **Released guests see a different wire sequence.** Examples: an extra `morphir.initialized`, or ids that no longer start at 1. Elm 0.3.1, scala-elm M08, and the published WASM backends would then break. Pinned by the task 4 test `a_session_numbers_requests_in_the_released_order` and by the host compatibility suite in task 7.
2. **Error text changes break CLI tests and user scripts that match messages.** Pinned by exact-string asserts in task 2 (envelope), task 3 (guards), and the unchanged daemon suite in task 4.
3. **A guest RPC error ends the session.** The workbench keeps one guest across clicks, so a rejection must keep the session ready. Pinned by the task 3 test `a_guest_rpc_error_rejects_the_call_and_keeps_the_session` and the daemon actor test `a_rejected_invocation_keeps_the_session_usable`.
4. **A transport failure reports the wrong proven state.** `Indeterminate` must not become `Stopped`, and a failed channel must not be closed a second time. Pinned by the daemon test `retains_an_indeterminate_state_after_an_uncertain_exchange_failure` (task 4) and the task 5 test `a_transport_failure_does_not_close_the_channel_again`.
5. **A later change pulls tokio or a native-only crate into `morphir-host`.** The browser build then breaks without anyone noticing. Pinned by the CI wasm32 check added in task 1.

title: feat(host-native): reach an extension over HTTP with HttpChannel
description:
### Task 3: `HttpChannel` replaces `ConnectedDaemonSession`

Bead: `morphir-opua.1.1.6.3`.

**Files:**
- Create: `crates/morphir-host-native/src/http.rs`
- Modify: `crates/morphir-host-native/Cargo.toml` (feature `http = ["dep:jsonrpsee"]`, `jsonrpsee = { version = "0.26", features = ["http-client"], optional = true }`; dev-dependency `jsonrpsee` with `server`, `macros`), `crates/morphir-host-native/src/lib.rs` (`#[cfg(feature = "http")] pub mod http;`)
- Move: `crates/morphir-daemon/examples/mep-http-backend.rs` (and its `examples/support/` if used) to `crates/morphir-host-native/examples/`, with `required-features = ["http"]`
- Move and port: `crates/morphir-daemon/tests/connected_daemon_extension.rs` to `crates/morphir-host-native/tests/http_channel.rs`
- Modify: `.mise/tasks/test/daemon` (rename to `.mise/tasks/test/http`, build the example from `morphir-host-native --features http`, run `--test http_channel -- --ignored`)

**Interfaces:**
- Produces: `morphir_host_native::http::{HttpChannel, HttpEndpoint}`:

```rust
pub struct HttpEndpoint {
    pub id: String,
    pub url: String,
    pub request_timeout: Duration, // default 30 s, as ConnectedDaemonSession
}

impl HttpChannel {
    /// Validate the endpoint (non-empty id, parseable URL) and build the client.
    pub fn connect(endpoint: HttpEndpoint) -> Result<Self, HostError>;
    /// A checked connection expecting extension `endpoint.id`.
    pub fn connection(self) -> CheckedConnection<JsonRpcConnection<Box<dyn Channel>, ExpectedChecks>>;
}
```

Channel behaviour (copy the contract of `crates/morphir-daemon/src/extensions/connected.rs:101-155`):
- `send(Outgoing::Request)`: POST the method with the params object, buffer the reply for `receive`, re-stamp the caller's id on it. Non-object params: buffer an `invalid_params` error response, send nothing.
- `send(Outgoing::Notification)`: ignored (no `morphir.exit` over HTTP, as today).
- A JSON-RPC error reply (`ClientError::Call`): buffered as `ExtensionResponse::error(code, message)`.
- Any other client error: `ChannelError { state: Indeterminate, cause: ChannelCause::Transport, message }`.
- `close()`: `Stopped` when the last buffered reply answered `morphir.shutdown` successfully, otherwise `Indeterminate`.
- `abort()`: no-op.

- [ ] **Step 1: Port the tests first.** Copy the 4 `#[ignore]` tests from `connected_daemon_extension.rs` into `tests/http_channel.rs`, rewritten over `Session::open(HttpChannel::connect(endpoint)?.connection(), &config)` and `session.compile(...)`. Keep their names. Add two non-ignored unit tests in `http.rs` with a local `jsonrpsee` server on `127.0.0.1:0`: a JSON-RPC error reply becomes an error response (`CallError::Rejected` at the session), and a closed port gives `ChannelError { state: Indeterminate, cause: Transport }`.
- [ ] **Step 2: Run to verify they fail** (`cargo test -p morphir-host-native --features http`): unresolved `http` module.
- [ ] **Step 3: Implement** `http.rs` as specified.
- [ ] **Step 4: Run** `cargo test -p morphir-host-native --features http`, then `mise run test:http`. Expected: PASS, including the 4 ignored tests through the mise task.
- [ ] **Step 5: Commit** `feat(host-native): reach an extension over HTTP with HttpChannel`.

---

HOW TO START IN A NEW WORKTREE
  git worktree add ../morphir-<topic> -b feat/<topic> origin/main
  cd ../morphir-<topic> && git submodule update --init ecosystem/morphir-rust
  bd prime; bd show morphir-1qhu; bd show morphir-1qhu.7; bd update morphir-1qhu.7 --claim
Superpowers specs/plans go through bd-plan (AGENTS.md "Superpowers artifacts live in beads"); drafts stay in .dev/.

WORKING RULES THE USER SET
- One thing at a time. One PR at a time, no parallel builds or agents fighting over cargo.
- Scoped gates while iterating (cargo test -p <crate> --test <name>, clippy -p morphir); keep build output short (grep test result / error).
- Push branches and open PRs without asking. Blanket squash+admin merge for morphir-1qhu PRs once CI is green and every review comment has a reply. Merge by hand, not gh auto-merge.
- Watch every PR you open in the background until merged; restart the watcher after each push.
- Codex comments: react eyes, verify, reply; thumbs-up only for real issues.
- No AI attribution in commits/PRs (EasyCLA). Commit trailer: Refs https://github.com/finos/morphir/issues/946
- Nested .claude/worktrees: pre-push fmt hook fails on cargo metadata; push with MORPHIR_SKIP_HOOKS=1 after running cargo fmt --check yourself.
- After closing beads: mise run beads:publish && git push origin beads-sync.
