title: Scheme pipeline and spec notation: error detail, name suggestions and annotation printing
description:
Writing the checked transform-script and specification-notation chapters (morphir-ukvn.5.45.4, pkgs/morphir-scheme/pipeline/README.mbt.md and spec/README.mbt.md) exposed behaviours that look like bugs. The chapters document each as current behaviour; fix them, update the examples and regenerate the docs tests (scheme-docs:generate).

- `ir-read`, `json-read` and `ir-value-read` report a failure with only the error type, for example `finos/morphir-ir/wire.CodecError.Invalid`, with no detail or location. (The backend has the same gap for invalid literals; see morphir-ukvn.5.50.)
- Specification notation: the canonical-name suggestion can repeat the input, as in "name `less_than` is not canonical (use `less_than`)". A name such as `a!` in a type parameter, constructor or input position gets that message instead of "reserved for macros".
- Specification notation: annotation names print fully qualified (`my/pkg:m#x`) even inside their own package, unlike every other reference.

comments.author: Damian Reeves
comments.text: Also: the '(use ...)' suggestion branches in read_path (spec/package.mbt:30-35), read_name (spec/names.mbt:16-21) and read_reference (spec/names.mbt:54-59) are dead code. Name::parse, Path::parse and FQName::parse (morphir-ir/common/names.mbt) accept only canonical text and round-trip it unchanged, so the suggestion can never differ from the input. Either remove the branches or make the parsers accept non-canonical spellings and suggest the canonical one. Found by the Task 7 review.

title: Scheme backend: diagnostics and evaluate/emit gaps found by the running IR chapter
description:
Writing the checked running-IR chapter (morphir-ukvn.5.45.4, pkgs/morphir-scheme/backend/README.mbt.md) exposed backend behaviours that look like bugs or weak diagnostics. The chapter documents each as current behaviour; fix them, update the chapter's examples and regenerate the docs tests (scheme-docs:generate).

- `replace_accelerator` on an SDK value changes `evaluate` but not the emitted text: the SDK's `r:` thunks never consult the accelerator, so the two ways of running IR disagree.
- Pattern-mismatch errors include literal quotes, for example `"No matching pattern"`.
- A tagged value with no arguments prints with a trailing space: `#<morphir/SDK:maybe#nothing >`.
- An invalid literal's error is only `finos/morphir-ir/wire.CodecError.Invalid`, without the detail.
- Some errors are reported as unbound identifiers but name no identifier, for example `Unbound identifier: No runtime binding or fallback for <fqname>`. Give them their own message or error kind.
- `register_native` records no arity, so neither calls nor `link_file` check a native's argument count.
- A second `install` with accelerators fails with `Duplicate native binding: accelerator:morphir/SDK:basics#add`. Make install idempotent or document the one-install rule with a clear message.

comments.author: Damian Reeves
comments.text: More evaluate/emit divergences found by the Task 6 review: (1) a non-boolean and/or operand raises 'Expected Morphir Bool' on the direct path (sdk_values.mbt:33 via native.mbt:154,162) but 'Morphir condition must be boolean' in emitted text (emit.mbt:224, runtime.mbt:140); (2) evaluate_native builds literals without the codec check (native.mbt:141-145), so evaluate(DecimalLiteral("abc")) returns a decimal value while emit_expression raises the codec error (emit.mbt:58-60). The two ways of running IR should agree on results and messages.

comments.author: Damian Reeves
comments.text: Four more evaluate/emit divergences found while fixing the Task 6 chapter (the chapter's table lists all eight): (1) integer literals: +5 and 007 run under evaluate but fail as emitted text, and abc or 1.5 give 'Expected integer' under evaluate but the codec error as text; (2) non-finite floats run under evaluate and print as NaN.0 or Infinity.0, contradicting the core rule that only finite reals exist; (3) accelerator calls nested past the emitter's 256-level IR limit run under evaluate but fail as text (130 nested add calls already exceed it).

title: Scheme frontend: compile-time diagnostics and acceptance gaps found by the models chapter
description:
Writing the checked models chapter (morphir-ukvn.5.45.4, pkgs/morphir-scheme/frontend/README.mbt.md) exposed frontend behaviours that look like bugs or weak diagnostics. The chapter documents each as current behaviour; fix them, update the chapter's examples and regenerate the docs tests (scheme-docs:generate).

- Qualified references: `module#name` (without a package) is refused; only `package:module#name` works. Decide whether the short form should resolve against the current package, and document the decision.
- A name outside Morphir's naming rules (for example `even?` or `myName`) fails with `finos/morphir-ir/common.NameError.InvalidName`; the message does not name the offending identifier or its location.
- Unknown names such as `and`, `or`, `cond` and `map` lower to variables and fail only at run time (`Unbound identifier: v:and`). The frontend should reject an unbound name at compile time.
- An `if` condition that is not a boolean passes the frontend unless it is a literal, and fails only at run time.
- `compile_expression` leaves its type placeholders as `scheme-value` without the unknown marker; only `compile_file` numbers them. Make the two consistent.
- The duplicate-parameter message leaves out the parameter name.

comments.author: Damian Reeves
comments.text: Also: unary minus on a Float fails. The frontend lowers (- x) as subtract(IntegerLiteral 0, x) (frontend.mbt:357-362), and the backend's subtract refuses mixed Integer and Real operands (backend/sdk_basics.mbt:193-220), so (- 2.5) fails with 'incompatible numeric operands'. Lower unary minus to a negate of the operand's own type, or use a literal 0 of the operand's type. Found by the Task 5 review of morphir-ukvn.5.45.4.

title: Scheme core: fix R6RS deviations found by the language reference
description:
Writing the checked core language reference (morphir-ukvn.5.45.4, pkgs/morphir-scheme/README.mbt.md) exposed behaviours of the core evaluator that look like bugs or unintended differences from R6RS. The chapter documents each as current behaviour; fix them and update the chapter's examples, then regenerate the docs tests (scheme-docs:generate).

- `error` builds its message with value_to_string, so a string argument keeps its quotes: (error "Not found:" 'key) gives "Not found:" key. Expected: strings displayed without quotes.
- `equal?` compares numbers by value, (equal? 1 1.0) is #t (R6RS: #f, exactness differs), and (equal? car car) is #f (a procedure should equal itself).
- `integer?` is #f for 2.0 (R6RS: #t).
- `string->number` raises on "1/0" (Division by zero) and "1e400" (Nonfinite number) instead of returning #f. The reader raises Invalid, not Syntax, for the literals 1/0 and 1e400.
- `.5` reads as a symbol instead of a number.
- The arity message reads "car: expected 1 arguments" (plural for one).

Deliberate limits that are documented and not part of this bug: if requires an alternative, map takes one list, letrec refuses a binding that reads another binding's value early, special-form names cannot be shadowed in head position.

title: Commit every pkg.generated.mbti and check it in CI, with AGENTS.md guidance
description:
## Problem

MoonBit writes a `pkg.generated.mbti` public-interface file for each package. The repository commits 42 of these files, but 77 packages have none committed and no ignore rule. Every checkout that builds or runs `moon info` is left with about 77 untracked files (seen in the firefish workspace, 2026-10-17, which had to be cleaned by hand before deletion).

## What MoonBit advises

The official agent guide (github.com/moonbitlang/moonbit-agent-guide, SKILL.md, section "Interface files"):

> `pkg.generated.mbti` files are compiler-generated summaries of each package's public API surface. ... They are generated using `moon info` and useful for code review. When you have a commit that does not change public APIs, `pkg.generated.mbti` files will remain unchanged, so it is recommended to put `pkg.generated.mbti` in version control when you are done. Do not modify `pkg.generated.mbti` directly, including whitespace-only cleanup; regenerate it with `moon info` and review its diff as the public API signal.

## Work

1. On a clean branch from `main`, run `moon info` (with the pinned toolchain from `.config/mise/config.toml`) and commit every `pkg.generated.mbti`, about 77 new files. Check that the 42 committed files do not change, or explain any diff as an existing public API drift.
2. Add a mise task (for example `check:mbti`) that runs `moon info` and then `git diff --exit-code -- '*.mbti'` and fails on untracked `.mbti` files too (`git status --porcelain -- '*pkg.generated.mbti'` is empty). Add it to `mise run check` and the pre-push hook, and add a CI step in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`. Make it work on Windows as well as Unix.
3. Update `.github/AGENTS.md` (the file root `AGENTS.md` points to for general configuration and pre-push checks):
   - Under "Pre-Push Requirements" / "Required Checks", add the interface check: run `moon info`, commit every changed or new `pkg.generated.mbti` in the same commit as the code change, and review its diff as the public API signal.
   - State the rules from the MoonBit guide: commit `pkg.generated.mbti` for every package; never edit it by hand, including whitespace; regenerate it with `moon info`.
   - Note that a new package must commit its `pkg.generated.mbti` in the PR that adds it.
4. Do not add `pkg.generated.mbti` to `.gitignore`.

## Done when

- `git status` is clean after `moon info`, `moon check` and `moon test` on all targets in a fresh checkout.
- The new check fails when a public API changes without its `.mbti` diff, and when a package has an untracked `pkg.generated.mbti`.
- `.github/AGENTS.md` carries the guidance above.

title: Scheme frontend: clear error for named let
description: The Scheme frontend (pkgs/morphir-scheme/frontend) refuses named let, as documented, but the error is an accident of parsing: compiling (let loop ((n 3)) n) fails with "Expected proper syntax list" instead of a message that says named let is unsupported. Found while writing the checked docs chapter (morphir-ukvn.5.45.4, frontend/README.mbt.md expects that text today). Fix: recognize a symbol after let and raise Unsupported with a clear message (for example "named let is not supported by the frontend"), then update the chapter's ;; error: expectation and regenerate the docs tests.

comments.author: Damian Reeves
comments.text: Also covers lambdas with a rest parameter: they fail with the same placeholder message, Expected proper syntax list (found by the models chapter, morphir-ukvn.5.45.4 Task 5). Give them a clear unsupported-form message too.

title: Exclude ignored local checkouts from YAML lint
description: The YAML lint task uses find and scans ignored .dev checkouts and .mooncakes packages. In this workspace it reaches deliberately invalid Morphir YAML fixtures under .dev/f4-extension-integration/implementation/morphir and fails before checking the active repository. This predates the Ion upgrade and does not reproduce on a fresh CI checkout without those local artifacts. Upgrade validation uses a local ignored .yamllint that extends the tracked policy and excludes only .dev/.mooncakes; no repository tooling change is included in the dependency PR. Follow up by making the portable lint task honor intended source scope; if changing the existing shell task, follow AGENTS guidance to migrate it to a MoonBit script. Preserve detection of invalid project YAML and verify ignored fixture checkouts do not affect the result.

title: Scheme modules: backend emits one module per Morphir module
description: Make the Scheme backend emit one Racket-style module per Morphir module (provide/require, readable names) instead of flat r:<fqname> defines, keeping the symbols sidecar and source comments from morphir-ukvn.5.40. Uses the shared module layer from sub-project 1.

title: Scheme modules: evaluator namespaces for transform scripts
description: Racket-style namespaces in the Morphir Scheme evaluator: require/provide between transform-script modules and morphir.config.scm, using the shared module layer from sub-project 1. Needs a host capability to read script modules; the evaluator has no filesystem access today. Until then the evaluator refuses the new forms with a clear error.

title: IR identities: owned module and value identities for Application distributions
description:
`@identities.nodes` (`pkgs/morphir-ir/identities/nodes.mbt`) creates `module:` and `value:` identities only for a `Library` distribution. For an `Application`, a unit owns no declaration identities, so metadata cannot attach to its declarations and the Scheme sidecar lists no origins for the symbols it emits (PR #108 drops the origins rather than point at ids the unit does not own).

Give Application distributions the same identities, for the application package and each dependency implementation, and decide the id scheme for dependency packages. The engine uses `@identities.nodes` to validate metadata ownership (`IRUnit::validate`), so the change reaches every rich-unit consumer.

Found by the Codex review of finos/morphir-moonbit#108. No MoonBit or Elm frontend produces applications today.

title: Move engine and workbench tests to moonrockz/expect
description:
Plan B of morphir-ukvn.5.22.4 (plan epic morphir-ukvn.5.22.4.2) writes its new tests with moonrockz/expect 0.6.1 but does not convert existing tests. This bead converts the rest, so a failing test reports every broken fact at once and names where it came from.

Scope today: pkgs/morphir-engine has 27 test files with about 739 assert_eq/assert_true/assert_false calls; apps/morphir-workbench has 22 test files with about 454.

How:
- Add moonrockz/expect@0.6.1 to the module's moon.mod and "moonrockz/expect" to the for "test" and for "wbtest" imports of each package converted (Plan B adds it to pkgs/morphir-engine, apps/morphir-workbench and browser/bottom-panel).
- A test with several facts: @expect.expect_all(s => { ... }). JSON replies: .at("a.b[0]") and to_contain_json. Collections: single(), first(), element(i), value_at(key). Errors: expect_call(() => ...).to_raise(containing=...). Loops: label= per case.
- Types shown by @expect need Debug; add derive(Debug) where a package owns the type.
- Keep behaviour: a conversion must not weaken a check (no assert replaced by a looser matcher). Keep inline snapshots (inspect, debug_inspect) where they review a whole output.
- One package per commit; run moon test on native, js, wasm and wasm-gc (workbench: js) and moon fmt.

Do after Plan B merges, to avoid conflicts with its edits. Can split into one child per package if it grows.

comments.author: Damian Reeves
comments.text: Also add property tests (@expect.for_all over core quickcheck types) where a converted test checks a law: round trips, invariants, mappings. Plan B (morphir-ukvn.5.22.4.2) shows the pattern in Tasks 1, 4, 6, 7 and 9.

title: Scheme backend: source-name and position comments from metadata (Level 2)
description: Use node metadata in the generated Scheme text: above each define, a comment with the source name and source position, for example ';; eligible (src/Main.mbt:2:0)'. Add a unit-level entry (for example emit_unit) so emit_package can look up the source spelling of each declaration; emit_file on plain IR keeps its output unchanged. Comments only: program behaviour and canonical names do not change. Ignore missing, duplicate or invalid hints, as the MoonBit backend's source_hints.mbt does. Tests: MoonBit and Elm units give the expected comments; plain Scheme output is unchanged byte for byte; a hostile hint (newline or ';' in a name) cannot break out of the comment. Size: one to two tasks. Independent of Level 1; both can run in parallel.
close_reason: Merged in 215e80f (finos/morphir-moonbit#108). Branch commit fa9459d (source-name and position comments; hostile hints ignored). Tests: moon test green on native, js, wasm and wasm-gc for morphir-scheme, morphir-engine and morphir-elm; whole-workspace wasm-gc 1441/1441 after merging main; all CI checks green on 4d38211.

title: Clear MoonBit 0.10.15 deprecation warnings
description: After the 0.10.15 upgrade (morphir-ukvn.5.34), moon check reports 71 deprecated warnings: morphir-core 49, morphir-ir 10, morphir-site 8, morphir-host 5, morphir-engine 2, morphir-sdk 1, morphir-scheme 1. Main kinds: @list.empty()/List literal -> @list.List([...]) (23), renamed APIs (33), StringView to_string -> to_owned (9), 'not(x)' -> !x (7). Clear them module by module when a change touches the module (warnings-in-touched-modules rule), or in one sweep if the maintainer asks.

title: Discovery: name morphir.json when it is not valid JSON
description: Follow-up of morphir-ukvn.5.22.4 Plan A (final review). legacy() in pkgs/morphir-engine/workspace/workspace.mbt reports every field error with the morphir.json path, but a file that is not valid JSON raises the JSON parser error, which may not name the file. Wrap the parse so the error says 'morphir.json is not valid JSON: <path>: <parser message>', with a test in workspace/legacy_test.mbt. Pre-existing behaviour, not a regression.

title: CLI: pass the telemetry observer to the Elm source provider
description: Follow-up of morphir-ukvn.5.22.4 Plan A (final review). apps/morphir/main.mbt registers the MoonBit provider with observer=logs.observer() but the Elm provider without one: @elm_adapter.provider() (pkgs/morphir-engine/elm/adapter.mbt) has no observer parameter, so morphir run --log records no Elm frontend events. Add an observer? : @observe.Observer parameter to the Elm adapter (as the MoonBit adapter has), emit frontend lifecycle events, pass it from the CLI, and test it like the MoonBit frontend logs in apps/morphir/scripts/test.js.

title: Engine::run: read Scheme projects from morphir.toml, not morphir.json
description: Maintainer direction (2026-10-15, during morphir-ukvn.5.22.4 Plan A): Scheme is a new project type and uses the new project system (morphir.toml); a morphir.json is always a morphir-elm project. The legacy embedding API Engine::run (pkgs/morphir-engine/engine.mbt:37-43, the Project(root) and Workspace modes with morphir-workspace.json and morphir.config.scm) still reads morphir.json as a script-driven Scheme project. Change Engine::run to read Scheme project settings from morphir.toml (or route it through discover/plan), stop reading morphir.json there, and update its users: pkgs/morphir-engine/engine_test.mbt (one/morphir.json, two/morphir.json), pkgs/morphir-engine/examples/main.mbt (demo/morphir.json), the engine README 'Legacy embedding API' section and the morphir.json split text added by Plan A Task 4. Decide whether morphir-workspace.json stays for Elm workspaces only.

comments.author: Damian Reeves
comments.text: Taken into Plan A of morphir-ukvn.5.22.4 as Task 7 (morphir-ukvn.5.22.4.1.7), maintainer approved 2026-10-15. Workspace(root) reads morphir.toml [workspace] members (literal paths only).

title: Workbench: projects of several files for PerFile languages (Scheme, MoonBit)
description: Follow-up of morphir-ukvn.5.22.4. The .22.4 project editor allows several files only for PerProject languages (Elm). A PerFile language compiles each file to its own unit, so the workbench must show several IR units (IR view, Model Explorer, generated output). Design how, then lift the one-file limit for Scheme and MoonBit.

title: Engine: replace the remaining String ids and names with domain types
description: Follow-up of morphir-ukvn.5.22.4 (Elm wiring), which types the new Engine::languages() API and the source-provider types it touches. The rest of the engine still uses String for language, provider, profile and backend ids, package and module names and paths: Config, planning, backends, register_frontend and generation. Retype them with the .22.4 types (LanguageId, ProviderId, ProfileId, BackendId, FileExtension, SourcePath, SourceModuleName, @ir.Path), parsing at the CLI, TOML and wire boundaries.
notes:
Plan A of morphir-ukvn.5.22.4 keeps these String until this bead: Source (path, relative_path, package_name, module_name; shared by PerFile frontends and Engine::run), SourceFrontendSelection (Plan::source_frontends descriptor), Frontend.provider/profile, register_frontend/register_unit_frontend names, Config, and planning/backends. The new types live in finos/morphir-engine/ids.
Also from Plan A review: languages.mbt compares 'ir-json' by string literal; no test for a ProjectCompiler frontend through register_frontend; @ids length limits count UTF-16 units (match source_constraint); languages() omits register_frontend frontends whose names do not parse (pinned by a test) — remove that catch when names are typed.

title: MoonBit symbols.10n grows with the square of nesting depth and exceeds the 4 MiB output budget at 45 if branches
description: Found in the final review of Plan 3 (item I2). An Elm value with an if/else-if chain of 45 branches, through the Elm provider and the MoonBit backend, fails with 'moonbit.byte_limit at my/pkg: Generated artifacts exceed the byte budget' (Limits::default max_bytes 4 MiB). library.mbt is small (about 15 KB at 40 branches); symbols.10n holds the Ion identity metadata, and each identity is a JSON-pointer path whose length grows with depth, so the size grows with the square of the depth: 10 branches 417 KB, 20 branches 1.2 MB, 30 branches 2.4 MB, 40 branches 4.0 MB. The checkpoint and Elm backends accept 53 branches. Decide whether symbols.10n should keep every structural identity, use shorter (relative or interned) paths, or have a budget of its own. Pinned by the adapter test 'review I2: the MoonBit metadata budget stops an if with 45 branches' (pkgs/morphir-engine/elm/adapter_test.mbt).
design:
Keep referenced identities in MoonBit sidecars

morphir-ukvn.5.22.3.27 · 17 October 2026 · Implemented in the working tree

  • Decision
  • Measurements
  • Strategies
  • Format and optional interning
  • Verification and limits

Decision

Omit the exhaustive source_nodes inventory. Retain IDs in the records that own metadata or reference a node: metadata, generated symbols, origins, naming allocations and consumed naming facts. The canonical source IR snapshot continues to preserve embedded attributes, extensions and source locations. Keep the 4 MiB total artifact budget and the pinned, sortable profile morphir-moonbit-symbols-2026-10-17.

Generation still validates metadata references against the complete source model. Establishing that a referenced node exists does not require serializing every possible node ID. Repository inspection found no MoonBit consumer that needed the exhaustive inventory beyond its preservation test.

An unannotated constant retains its declaration and body IDs in its symbol record and origins. A branch with separately attached metadata retains the branch ID in its metadata record. Serialization containers and attribute fields without separate references need no additional entries.

Measurements

Measurements use if_chain_files through the real Elm provider and MoonBit backend in pkgs/morphir-engine/elm/adapter_test.mbt, on the native target. Sizes are bytes of the complete binary Ion sidecar. The parent-relative prototype was measured before the date-based label replaced its provisional label; the final column uses the dated profile.

BranchesOriginal flat inventoryParent-relative prototypeNo inventory, selected
10416,87650,99716,871
201,224,605104,67634,190
302,406,738158,35651,510
403,963,402212,17068,964
45Generation refused239,08077,694
53Not measured282,15791,683

At 40 branches, the original source_nodes field alone costs 3,894,434 bytes for 9,242 identities. The source snapshot costs 54,291 bytes and naming allocations cost 14,187 bytes. Identity collection enumerates the unit JSON tree and declaration-local trees; storing every full ancestor path repeatedly dominated output size. The final complete sidecar is 98.3% smaller than the original.

Strategies

StrategyAssessment
IDs on owning and referencing recordsSelected. Keeps all information used by current consumers and avoids a redundant inventory. Complete IR attributes remain in the retained source snapshot. Direct strings remain readable.
Sparse inventory of referenced IDsPossible, but duplicates IDs already present in the records. Add a table only when a consumer or measured sharing benefit requires it.
Parent references or shared-prefix lengthsEffective compression of a required inventory. The initial fix demonstrated this, but preserving a complete inventory proved unnecessary. The parent-path encoder and its reconstruction-only test have been removed.
Alias, anchor or interning table for repeated namesAllowed future strategy. Can share IDs across records, beyond the old inventory. Requires an explicit encoding declaration and expansion step, reducing readability. No indirection table is emitted by the current encoder.
Reconstruct a complete inventory from the source snapshotAvailable to tools that need structural enumeration, provided they use compatible IR codecs and identity rules. Ordinary sidecar consumers need only follow explicit references.
Raise or separate the metadata budgetUnnecessary for this fix and would not remove the original cause of growth.
Intern complete inventory paths as Ion symbolsUnique paths still repeat ancestor text inside the symbol table. Does not address the original inventory problem. Sharing repeated semantic names across records is a different, potentially useful optimization.

Format and optional interning

The annotation remains morphir_moonbit_symbols. The profile uses a fixed YYYY-MM-DD format-revision date, independent of artifact creation time. All existing fields retain their shapes except that source_nodes is absent. IDs and names remain full strings in the current encoding. Earlier flat and parent-relative inventories are superseded.

{
  "profile": "morphir-moonbit-symbols-2026-10-17",
  "metadata": [{
    "node_id": "value:demo:main#choose/body/IfThenElse/then",
    "data": {"rule": "approved-amount"}
  }],
  "symbols": [{
    "source_node": "value:demo:main#choose",
    "origins": ["value:demo:main#choose", "value:demo:main#choose/body"]
  }]
}

This abbreviated example presents Ion fields in JSON notation. Native Ion metadata, including annotations and rich scalar values, remains unchanged in the actual sidecar.

A future alias or interning encoding must declare its use explicitly, assign deterministic document-local references and expand to the exact original strings. Readers must reject dangling or cyclic references and must not guess whether an ordinary string is an alias. Unknown Ion metadata remains opaque and must not be rewritten. Tools presenting an interned artifact should provide an expanded view to restore readability. Those rules permit sharing repeated names without changing the meaning of identities.

Verification and limits

  • The original 45-branch failure and excessive growth were reproduced before the first fix.
  • The new preservation test failed while the exhaustive inventory was still present and passed after its removal.
  • A metadata-free constant retains its declaration mapping and origins without a node inventory.
  • Metadata attached to structural leaf IDs survives, including Unicode unit IDs and escaped attribute keys. The decoded source snapshot equals the original source IR JSON, preserving embedded attributes.
  • Unknown and duplicate metadata targets still fail ownership validation. Existing tests cover native Ion values, ordered annotations, naming facts and rewrite provenance.
  • Integration regressions require successful generation at 45 and 53 branches, metadata below 128 KiB and less than threefold metadata growth when the chain doubles from 10 to 20 to 40 branches.
  • The total artifact budget is tested at its exact boundary. Existing determinism tests compare reordered inputs.

The fix does not change the in-memory identity collector or the frontend depth limit. Retained source snapshots, large authored metadata, naming facts and generated source can still consume the output budget. The Scheme sidecar has its own profile and inventory contract and is unchanged.

title: Propose the finos/morphir-examples fixes upstream

title: Engine: replace the fixed tree limits with unit fuel and drop the fixed node count
description: pkgs/morphir-ir/identities/nodes.mbt (collect) raises identity.tree_limit (Identity depth or count exceeded) when the JSON of an IR unit has more than 100000 nodes or a depth over 128. The IR of elm-reference-model (Elm parity corpus, imported from finos/morphir-elm 71ca7ee; the morphir-elm output has about 180000 JSON nodes, depth 63) is over the count. The SDK gaps (morphir-ukvn.5.22.3.19 to .22) stop the frontend first, so no pin shows this yet. A probe without the modules that use the missing SDK modules gave, for both backends of the engine end to end (pkgs/morphir-engine/acceptance/elm): src [frontend] identity.tree_limit: Identity depth or count exceeded. A larger project gives one unit, so the limit is on the size of a project. Decide whether the identity limit should follow the data limits of the unit or grow with it. With the count limit raised in a probe, the MoonBit backend stopped at moonbit.unsupported_type at type:morphir/reference/model:issues/issue-349#result: Generic alias (morphir-ukvn.5.22.11).
design:
## Design: replace fixed tree limits with unit fuel (Scala 3.10 style)

Reference: Scala 3.10 compiler fuel (https://www.scala-lang.org/news/3.10/#compiler-fuel). Scala fuel is a nesting counter, not a total-work budget. Each nested entry of a fuel-checked operation costs one unit, and the unit comes back on exit. The default is 550 and `-Xmax-fuel` changes it. When fuel runs out, compilation stops with "Recursion limit exceeded" and lists the recurring operations. Fuel does not make recursion stack-safe: more fuel without more stack (`-Xss`) can still overflow.

### Two separate problems

1. **Node count (100000).** elm-reference-model has about 180000 JSON nodes at depth 63. The count blocks it, not the depth. Nesting fuel does not touch the count.
2. **Depth (128).** The depth limits protect the stack. A probe with every cap lifted overflowed at a 398-element `::` chain on js (morphir-ir v4 JSON `write_value`) and on wasm (morphir-elm backend `lower_apply`). Native and wasm-gc passed.

### Current limits (they disagree)

| Limit | Value | Where | Owner |
|---|---|---|---|
| Parser nesting of expressions, types and patterns | 150 (75 source levels for constructor and type applications) | krueger `src/parser/cursor.mbt` `MAX_DEPTH`, `Cursor::nested` | krueger |
| Chain depth and AST depth per declaration | 400 | krueger `src/parser/depth.mbt` `MAX_AST_DEPTH`, `Cursor::chain`, check in `src/parser/file.mbt` | krueger |
| Printer levels | 400 | krueger `src/printer/errors.mbt` `max_level` (`TooDeep`) | krueger |
| Identity JSON depth and node count | 128, 100000 (fixed consts) | `pkgs/morphir-ir/identities/nodes.mbt` `MAX_DEPTH`, `MAX_NODES` | morphir-moonbit (engine) |
| Data tree depth and value count | 128, 100000 (unit limits) | `pkgs/morphir-engine` `default_unit_limits()`, data envelope | morphir-moonbit (engine) |
| Codec registry encode limits | 4 MiB, 128, 100000 | checkpoint backend codec registry | morphir-moonbit (engine) |

### Plan

**Step 1. Remove the fixed node count (engine, this repo).** Delete `MAX_NODES` and the value-count limit. The unit byte limit (16 MiB) bounds size. This matches the document-limit rule: no limit by default; a declared limit is optional. This step alone unblocks elm-reference-model once its SDK gaps (.19 to .22) close.

**Step 2. One nesting fuel per unit (engine, this repo).** Replace the depth limits of the identity walk, the data envelope and the codec registry with one fuel value per unit compile:
- A unit-scoped counter: decrement on entry to a fuel-checked walk, increment on exit. MoonBit has no implicit parameters, so prefer a counter scoped to the compile over a context argument on every walk. The engine is single-threaded per compile.
- The default stays below the smallest safe stack of all targets (js and wasm overflow near 398 levels of the current walks), with margin.
- `UnitLimits` gets a fuel field. A provider can declare a value, and the CLI and workbench can override it (like `-Xmax-fuel`). The CLI shows the effective value.
- When fuel runs out: diagnostic `engine.fuel_exhausted`, naming the walk that ran out and the fuel value, and telling the user how to raise it. Replaces `identity.tree_limit` and `data.tree_limit` for depth.

**Step 2b. A stack setting beside the fuel (host, this repo).** As Scala keeps `-Xmax-fuel` apart from `-Xss`, the Morphir CLI gets a stack setting beside the fuel setting. Raising the fuel without more stack can overflow; the CLI says so and suggests the stack setting.
- One budget for the whole pipeline: the engine passes the unit fuel to krueger (moonrockz/krueger#51), so parse, lowering, IR encoding, identity collection and printing all spend from it. Each walk spends in proportion to its stack use per level; a stack-safe walk spends 0.
- Fuel measures the stack in use at one time: a walk that runs after another starts with the full budget; walks on the stack together share it.
- The stack setting is the host's job, per target: native runs the compile on a thread with the requested stack size; the js CLI launches Node with `--stack-size`; wasm and wasm-gc hosts set the engine's stack (for example `wasmtime -W max-wasm-stack`). The browser workbench cannot change the stack, so it keeps the default fuel.
- The default fuel is calibrated against the smallest default stack of the four targets, so that the default never overflows.

**Step 3. Make the deep walks iterative, walk by walk.** A walk with an explicit stack does not use the call stack, so it stops spending fuel. The default rises as the walks convert.
- This repo: identity `collect` (easy), IR v4 JSON `write_value` and the JSON reader, Elm frontend lowering, Elm backend `lower_apply` and the other backend lowering walks, and the MoonBit generator walks.
- krueger: see below.

### What belongs to krueger (moonrockz/krueger)

krueger has three fixed limits (table above). Morphir cannot change them from outside. `Cursor::nested` and `Cursor::chain` already count like Scala fuel (up on entry, down on exit); only the maximum is fixed. krueger 0.4.0 (moonrockz/krueger#41) already made the pretty engine and expression printing stack-safe, and the declaration depth walk is iterative. krueger 0.6.0 is a maintenance release with no depth change. Filed:
- **K1, moonrockz/krueger#51.** The caller sets the parser limits (150, 400) and the printer limit (400). The defaults stay. The Elm frontend then passes the unit fuel.
- **K2, moonrockz/krueger#52.** One stable code and the limit value for the three TOO MUCH NESTING refusals. Today they are messages ("nesting too deep", "chain too long") or the general declaration codes KR-PARSE-003/004/008. The frontend maps the code to `engine.fuel_exhausted`.
- **K3, moonrockz/krueger#53.** Stack-safe AST encoder (`src/ast/encode.mbt`) and pattern and type printing. The recursive-descent parser (limit 150) is the largest change and can stay last.

K1 to K3 block nothing in Steps 1 and 2. Until K1 exists, the effective nesting for Elm source is the lowest of the unit fuel, 150 parser levels and 400 AST levels.

### Ownership

Steps 1 to 3 are engine work in morphir-moonbit, tracked directly under Track 5 (morphir-ukvn.5); there is no open engine epic. They do not depend on the CLI and workbench wiring (.22.4). K1 to K3 are krueger work, tracked as GitHub issues in moonrockz/krueger.

### Tests

- Pin today's behaviour first: the adapter test `review I2: the unit limits are the identity limits, which an if with 54 branches exceeds` (pkgs/morphir-engine/elm/adapter_test.mbt) changes to a fuel test.
- A unit over 100000 nodes and under 16 MiB compiles after Step 1.
- Fuel exhaustion gives `engine.fuel_exhausted` with the walk name, on all four targets, never a stack overflow.
- A raised fuel value passes a deeper unit on native and wasm-gc.
- Each walk converted in Step 3 gets a test deeper than the old overflow point (398) on js and wasm.

comments.author: Damian Reeves
comments.text: Widened to cover depth (final review of Plan 3, item I2). IRUnit::validate calls @identities.nodes, whose limits are fixed (JSON depth 128, 100000 nodes) whatever the unit limits are. The Elm provider declared depth 1024 and 1000000 values, which no unit could reach, so default_unit_limits() now declares the real limits: 16 MiB, depth 128, 100000 values. Measured with if/else-if chains through the Elm provider: 53 branches pass, 54 fail with 'data.tree_limit: Depth exceeds the limit of 128' (before the change, about 55 failed with identity.tree_limit). The checkpoint backend also encodes with the default limits of its codec registry (4 MiB, depth 128, 100000 values), and the MoonBit generator calls @identities.nodes with the fixed limits. A probe with every cap lifted found that deep nesting is not stack-safe: a 398-element :: chain (the parser allows AST depth 400) overflows the stack on js (morphir-ir/versions/v4/json write_value) and on wasm (morphir-elm/backend lower_apply); native and wasm-gc pass. So passing the unit limits through needs iterative (or depth-bounded) IR JSON writing and Elm lowering first. Pinned by the adapter test 'review I2: the unit limits are the identity limits, which an if with 54 branches exceeds' (pkgs/morphir-engine/elm/adapter_test.mbt). The identity and data tree-limit diagnostics now name the exceeded limit and its value.

title: Scheme compile_expression writes unmarked scheme-value let signatures
description: pkgs/morphir-scheme/frontend/frontend.mbt compile_expression (used by scheme->ir in pkgs/morphir-scheme/pipeline/bridge.mbt) still writes unmarked, shared scheme-value let signatures. Plan 2 of morphir-ukvn.5.22.2 changed only compile_file to write marked t-<n> placeholders. A transform that builds a let with scheme->ir followed by pipeline.inference = fill gives rigid_variable. Per-declaration numbering cannot be reused here, because the names would collide with the declaration's t-<n>; choose a distinct marked naming scheme (or renumber after splicing). Found by the Plan 2 final review.

title: Clear MoonBit warnings across the workspace and deny warnings in CI
description: moon check reports about 388 warnings on the default target (2026-10-08). Most are implicit_impl_as_method on derived traits (add pub extend X with Eq/Debug), deprecated APIs (StringView to_string -> to_owned, fn closures -> arrow functions, StringBuilder::new -> StringBuilder(), try? -> try/catch noraise), and unused items. The biggest source is pkgs/morphir-core/ir (about 256). Plan: count by package and kind, fix package by package, then make CI fail on warnings (moon check --deny-warn, or a module warn-list in moon.mod / moon.pkg). Policy from Damian (2026-10-08): no broad fix in feature PRs; each PR clears warnings in the modules it touches.
notes: TelemetrySession::local (finos/morphir-host observability.mbt:53) gives reserved_keyword warnings at apps/morphir/main.mbt:186 and execution.mbt:145; rename when clearing warnings.

title: IR inference follow-ups from the Plan 1 reviews
description:
Deferred minor findings from Plan 1 of IR type inference (morphir-ukvn.5.22.2.1). Each was judged safe to wait.
- Report cyclic aliases from dependencies only where they are used.
- Suppress annotation_mismatch on dependants of failed undeclared groups.
- LetRecursion siblings share annotation rigids; annotated siblings are monomorphic inside the group.
- Let-annotation rigids print without typeclass (fix before MoonBit end to end).
- Generic message for a nested rigid; message grammar ('1 arguments').
- Recursive Tarjan; path order is UTF-16; Specs check skips cyclic aliases.
- Hole type variables become unregistered rigids.
- One path walker instead of three copies (paths.mbt, driver_output Walker, oracle strip.mbt); document the type: root.
- Spec notation: misplaced type doc message; duplicate parameter names accepted; trailing forms error; round-trip coverage; printer limits.
- vspec and sdkgen: error-path tests, argv handling, parse fallback in bootstrap, unique_parameter_names test.
- Reader: line_column edge tests (offset 0, past end, CRLF), dotted-tail located test.
- Oracle: a let signature with any placeholder is skipped whole; Application bundled definitions and IncompleteBody are not walked.

comments.author: Damian Reeves
comments.text:
Residuals from the Plan 1 final re-review (d5fa23f..9c620c3). Fix the first one before Plan 2 puts fill in the engine.
1. Fill drops a class given only by the typeclass attribute from a rigid owned by another member of the same group. Probe: f : ?p -> ?q; f x = g x and g : (a, typeclass=number) -> ?s; g y = add y (f y). Fill writes f : a -> a, and Check of the result fails with rigid_variable. Cause: fill calls enter(d) after solve clears rigid_classes. Fix: declare every group member's rigids in fill and add the probe as a test.
2. Unknown typeclass ordering: in solve, run the unknown_class check on every member before declare_rigids. The order [g, f] gives rigid_variable instead of unsupported.
3. An undeclared member's scheme keeps another member's rigid without generalizing it. This is strict.
4. A let-annotation rigid whose class comes only from typeclass loses that class in the fill output. This is cosmetic.
5. A dropped-class mismatch prints the same text on both sides. Print the class when only the classes differ.

title: Decide strict vs ignored [backends.moonbit] options
description: Ruling 12 of the Elm backend work (PR #45): the MoonBit generator ignores its [backends.moonbit] table, as spec section 2 says. Alternative: refuse unknown keys like elm does (typos caught early, consistent behavior), which needs a spec amendment and a ~5-line change with a test.

title: Support entry-root reachability and Morphir tree-shaking
description:
Support tree-shaking as a separately planned Morphir feature. Define language-neutral reachability from explicit entry roots and conservatively remove only declarations proven unnecessary before downstream generation or packaging. Keep this outside the current Workbench invocation-admission PRs.

Follow value references, helper functions, type aliases, custom types and constructor ownership, recursive groups and required SDK dependencies. Specify library-export versus selected-entry roots and conservative behavior for external/native/opaque dependencies. Preserve retained identities, documentation, source/provenance mappings and IR metadata. Expose removed/retained reachability evidence useful to tooling and the model explorer.

Prove semantic equivalence for retained entries with independent fixtures, including recursion, shared helpers and model outcomes. Demonstrate reduced generated artifacts without making incidental compiler dead-code elimination the Morphir contract. Coordinate with permissive admission so statically unreachable code can be excluded from its admitted scope; do not equate static pruning with runtime detection of untaken branches. Track in the ecosystem roadmap, with initial MoonBit and parent-spec work; other implementation adoption remains explicit.
acceptance_criteria: Approved reachability/root policy; conservative recursion, type, constructor and external dependency handling; retained-entry semantic equivalence and artifact reduction proved independently; metadata/provenance retained; adoption and relation to permissive admission explicitly scoped.

title: Runtime capabilities: verification and validation
description:
Plan an explicit opt-in policy for runtime capability checks as code executes that does not reject an otherwise supported selected call solely because a declaration is unused or an unsupported branch is never executed. Keep current exact Workbench draft.3 strict and unchanged. Distinguish the selected entry's typed input boundary from support for internal IR bodies and dormant declarations.

Specify which checks can be deferred and which must precede execution. Public entry authorization, request identities, duplicate/envelope integrity and resource limits remain mandatory. Unsupported operations reached at runtime must fail with a stable diagnostic, never silently coerce or skip work. Validate actual returned values through the planned output/outcome boundary. Name and negotiate policy explicitly across engine, offline MCK and future host/UI adoption; do not advertise it until independently qualified.

Tests must distinguish unused entries, unreachable dependencies, untaken conditional branches and the same unsupported branches when taken. Cover recursive/custom types, native/external references and SDK model-error versus Result.Err semantics. Static reachability may share implementation with the separate tree-shaking feature, but runtime reachability remains a separate concern. Future work; no behavior or frozen contract changes in PR #1035/#44.

Current terminology: runtime capabilities. Capability verification gathers scoped implementation evidence; capability validation checks selected-function/model-revision/run requirements under policy. Historical protocol/API identifiers remain unchanged. Accepted ruling morphir-q3ip; current canonical HTML design and six-task plan supersede the original planning wording. Implementation morphir-etg2.16 remains 1 of 6 delivered.
design:
Runtime capabilities: verification and validation

morphir-etg2.6 · 17 October 2026 · planning complete; implementation tracked separately

  • Capabilities, verification and validation
  • Integration with current main
  • Goal and scope
  • Evidence and completion
  • Capability validation and execution flow
  • Policy and exact negotiation
  • Checks that always happen
  • Deferral and reached failures
  • Validate actual results with the validated context
  • Capture policy through asynchronous execution
  • Acceptance matrix
  • Upstream contract and qualification
  • Measured budgets and SDK limits
  • Workbench behavior
  • Implementation sequence
  • Source evidence and limits
  • Connected checking policies

Capabilities, verification and validation

Runtime capabilities describe what a particular runtime can execute. Capability verification gathers scoped evidence that an implementation behaves as claimed under an exact contract, implementation version and platform. Contract and MCK test results provide evidence; they are not a formal proof, a claim about every possible input, or validation of business rules.

Capability validation checks whether the selected runtime satisfies the requirements of a particular run, selected function and model revision. Its checking policy determines scope and timing: Whole model before running checks executable support up front; As code executes allows represented unsupported executable semantics to remain dormant and rejects them if reached. Both retain mandatory whole-source integrity, identity and resource checks and the complete selected input/output type closure before execution. Arguments, outputs, receipts and authorization still have their own validation rules.

Provider-authored capability claims remain distinct from verification evidence. An offline MCK adapter claim describes its exact test suite; it is not a live provider/session offer. A successful selected run does not expand the runtime capability set. Changing the checking policy changes when and where requirements are checked.

The earlier capabilities vocabulary change retained compatibility identifiers, including admission, morphir/workbench/admission and AdmissionPolicy. Task 7 is a separately approved breaking pre-1.0 migration to execution terminology. It replaces current job-based APIs and wire contracts without aliases, duplicate fields or compatibility routes. Strict/permissive checking semantics and capability advertisements do not expand as a result.

Integration with current main

Latest main integration: PR #127 at 3b7ccd029c89ef5e3fe6173490c97906dfcae6e7 adds native MEP morphir.frontend.compileModel for the existing moonbit-model-bool-library-v1 source profile. Compilation and generation negotiate separate transport tuples; rich Ion preserves source provenance, while lossy JSON export rejects. This is a source-compilation capability, separate from Scheme execution policy and Workbench native/HTTP execution offers. The integration preserved the original six-task sequence; the maintainer has now added Task 7 before the remaining transports; completion checkboxes follow qualified merges. Task 4 retains source-profile-specific UI support; Tasks 5 and 6 now have separately qualified exact policy mappings and end-to-end evidence, recorded below. Merged setup PR #129 at 83283be6f7f761c2b5026f030df7af4e9b86129c also completes pinned Unix installs and adds Linux ARM64 setup qualification. This changes toolchain provisioning, not the remaining UI/policy tasks or packaged-desktop evidence. Local source support also advances through PR #130 at cac8f85f55e80f1c27b5b45137c974530d639179: the Workbench prefers moonbit-model-library-2026-10-17, a dated cumulative Bool/String/Int32 snapshot. Source-profile selection and checking policy remain separate controls. Task 4 must preserve pinned/narrow profiles and drafts, test bounded String/Int32 policy executions and retain the new SDK type checks. Native MEP compilation still advertises its separate Boolean library profile; local UI support never upgrades a remote offer. All integration qualification passes, including the full root check, current browser workflow, 20 worker/provider controls, 124 Node tests, native MEP process/consumer, TypeScript and the independently rechecked six-lane draft.13 corpus. PR #128 and paired #1059 are merged; delivered trees match the qualified sources.

Goal and scope

A selected public Morphir function should run under an explicit permissive policy when unsupported code remains unused or is in a genuinely untaken branch. If evaluation reaches an unsupported operation, it fails deterministically. Strict remains the default. This document specifies proposed behavior and delivery gates; runtime behavior is unchanged by the planning task.

Initially qualify the bounded Scheme evaluator. This policy is independent of source language: Scheme, Elm or MoonBit source can participate only after producing accepted IR with a supported selected boundary. It does not imply generated JavaScript/Wasm/native execution, wider SDK support or any new platform capability.

Tree-shaking stays in morphir-ukvn.6. This policy retains original source and does not promise smaller artifacts, dead-code elimination or rollback of effects. Actual packaged-platform qualification remains in morphir-etg2.15.5.

Evidence and completion

The planning milestone is morphir-etg2.6. Implementation belongs to morphir-etg2.16, so completing this design does not mark the feature implemented. Completion in the implementation plan follows qualified and merged deliveries.

Capability validation and execution flow

Explore the proposed policy workflow. Current eager generation/linking are source-backed constraints; new policy routing and runtime traps are proposed.

Mermaid topology
flowchart TD
  A[Capture source, calls and explicit policy] --> B[Whole-source framing, identities and limits]
  B --> C{Effective policy}
  C -->|strict default| D[Existing strict whole-library plan]
  C -->|explicit permissive| E[Selected public boundary closure]
  E --> F[Immutable bounded Scheme plan]
  F --> G{Operation reached?}
  G -->|supported| H[Execute normally]
  G -->|known unsupported| I[Failed: unsupported_reached]
  H --> J[Validate actual output and terminal inventory]
  I --> J
  J --> K[Publish against captured boundary context]

Policy and exact negotiation

Use a closed internal policy type with Strict and Permissive. Proposed normative profile: morphir/workbench/admission 0.1.0-draft.1. The effective policy is resolved once when the run is validated. An omitted field means strict only in a mapping that explicitly defines that omission. Unknown policy, profile, exact version, suffix, field or unsupported runtime selection rejects. Explicit permissive never silently falls back.

Separate the new Scheme plan from the existing generated-library Plan and driver. Do not invent an empty generated library to satisfy that API. The new plan retains original accepted IR, calls, authoritative public boundary context, policy/profile, evaluator/provider and identity. Replanning copies the accepted selection to a new plan identity; existing executions remain unchanged.

{
  "admission": {
    "profile": "morphir/workbench/admission",
    "contractVersion": "0.1.0-draft.1",
    "policies": [
      "strict",
      "permissive"
    ]
  }
}

This descriptor fragment is a design proposal for a newly versioned host/native mapping. Existing closed draft.1 mappings reject it. Task 7 replaces the pre-1.0 execution identity and receipt names while preserving their validation, lifecycle and outcome semantics. A visible policy echo belongs in the new submission/plan projection, not an extra frozen receipt field.

Checks that always happen

Parse and bound the entire source, including dormant code. Preserve accepted IR versions and grammar, envelope integrity, duplicate declaration/name/identity rejection, unambiguous lookup, resource accounting and source snapshot retention. Deferral is for represented unsupported semantics; it cannot recover malformed source or ambiguous authority.

Resolve every selected entry from actual IR and visibility, never a renderer-supplied manifest. Validate exact arity and tagged arguments. Validate the complete selected input and output type closure, including all variants, constructors, registry references and recursive relationships. Function-valued or unsupported selected boundaries reject even if the particular value is empty, None, a different constructor, a model error or a later failed/cancelled outcome. Unrelated declarations need bounded structural validation but need not all satisfy this provider's execution-support rules.

Type-only manifest extraction must be independent of body/code generation. Internal references do not grant public-call authorization. Native/external functions require existing host-authorized bindings; policy creates no filesystem, process, network, native callback or provider authority.

Use existing bounded codecs and runtime limits without increasing them. A new exact contract must state byte/unit/depth/node metrics and limits explicitly: whole-source and transport budgets, selected closure dimensions, argument/output budgets, optional-extension bytes, runtime steps/depth/frames and terminal/message bounds all apply. Dormant source and planned traps still count toward traversal and resource budgets. Resource or parser errors retain their original classes. Interpreter-only source/manifest traversal has its own explicit bounds; it must not borrow target artifact-size limits as a proxy. The existing typed Scheme limits are 1,000,000 steps, depth 128 and 100,000 frames; emission traversal currently limits depth to 256. File preparation and invocation share one active runtime budget. Thunks, nested calls and traps do not reset that budget or bypass cancellation.

Deferral and reached failures

Prepare definitions on demand, preserving their canonical identities and original source. Separately, lower known unsupported expressions to bounded traps at their original evaluation positions. Lazy declaration preparation solves an unused declaration; expression traps solve a hole or unsupported operation inside a loaded function's untaken branch. Static reachability alone cannot prove runtime branch selection.

Preserve the evaluator's order and laziness for each supported construct. Untaken conditional or short-circuit branches do not execute. Eager function arguments, bindings and pattern guards execute according to normal semantics, even when their result or variable name is unused. Do not catch arbitrary generator, parser, provider or resource failures and replace them with traps. Fully applied and/or have existing special short-circuit semantics; first-class and partially applied calls keep normal application semantics. Lambda creation does not execute its body; local let/letrec right-hand sides remain eager.

The unsupported inventory must explicitly cover constructor metadata and external fallback selection. Current Scheme loading eagerly registers all constructors with an arity cap of 256. Lazy value bodies alone do not solve an unrelated unsupported constructor. Define bounded on-demand metadata preparation without waiving the selected boundary closure. Generic signatures and alias cycles retain explicit supported/rejected status; finite named recursive ADTs require bounded complete closure. Native candidate order and arity checks remain deterministic. A chosen native implementation may leave an unsupported fallback dormant, but failure of that invoked native never triggers fallback.

{
  "status": "failed",
  "failure": {
    "stage": "evaluate",
    "code": "execution.unsupported_reached",
    "message": "Unsupported operation reached"
  }
}

Reserve that code for actually reached, explicitly represented unsupported semantic operations. A missing authorized binding keeps its binding diagnostic; a wrong type, exhausted budget, malformed input, unavailable provider, crash or build failure keeps its own classification. SDK model errors remain enumerated model errors. Ordinary typed Result.Err remains returned data. MCK report Unsupported means a missing capability and is not this runtime terminal failure.

Bound human detail with existing terminal limits; no source text, paths, stack traces or secrets in stable diagnostics. Preserve completed effect accounting when a later operation fails. The policy supplies no rollback guarantee.

Validate actual results with the validated context

Frozen draft.5 validate-outcomes revalidates the entire declaration graph before any terminal, including failed/cancelled. Do not send an original permissively deferred manifest through that operation and skip its rejection. Define a new policy-aware admission/outcome path that retains the sound selected-boundary closure and validates actual terminal evidence against that immutable context.

Reuse unchanged tagged-value and terminal-envelope codecs internally. Validate actual outputs, all supplied call identities in order, call count, extensions and independent cleanup. Do not claim the old whole-manifest operation qualified the deferred model. Cancellation and failed evidence never waive validation of the selected boundary. No runtime failure is encoded as a dummy value, new SDK model error or a successful Result.Err.

Capture policy through asynchronous execution

Freeze source, entry, tagged arguments, accepted boundary context, exact policy/profile and evaluator/provider at submission. The same effective selection must reach the actual engine plan, execution state, worker claim, execution and completion-time replanning/terminal validation. Resolve defaults once. A UI edit, reconnect, capability refresh, lease/claim or provider replacement cannot mutate an accepted execution.

A new replan retains the selected policy with a new plan identity, or rejects if the new provider cannot honor it. Query, cancellation and release do not replan or execute again. Preserve existing once-only claim and uncertain-submission behavior. Independent fixed observations must inspect real captured policy and actual terminal results; controlled receipt/completion replay does not prove propagation through a worker.

Upstream contract and qualification

Publish the normative policy and fixed expectations back to finos/morphir. Propose an isolated exact offline MCK version, currently the next available 0.1.0-draft.11, with the narrow JSON-only operation run-selected-scheme for Task 1. Its immutable fixture kit provides evidence only for selected public boundary planning and execution beside unused unsupported declarations, including observed decode/plan/evaluate refusals. It does not qualify the full policy, runtime branch semantics, terminal inventory, a provider or UI capability. Task 2 uses exact 0.1.0-draft.12 and run-capability-policy for the applicable Library-only Scheme policy semantics; it never modifies frozen draft.11. The 182 fixed cases separate 87 actual-execution observations from 95 supplied-completion validation observations. The latter validate retained context without executing the model, authenticating an execution or establishing actual cancellation. Confirm every next free exact version at implementation time; do not repurpose another effort's version. Transport version, policy profile, evaluator capability and host/native mapping version are separate identities.

The shared Rust runner/checker owns corpus validation, bounded input-only dispatch, fixed expected observations, comparisons, corpus hashes, ordered case/format/operation inventory and report rechecking. Parent-owned models and expected results are independent of the adapter. Keep every frozen draft unchanged. No MoonBit or TypeScript verdict engine, expected-result dispatch, clock-based settling or adapter-supplied public authority.

Task 1 may establish evidence for an internal focused tracer, but public capability advertisement waits for Task 2's complete applicable semantics corpus and independent report checks. Initial local lanes are named explicitly and tested in debug/release. JSON transport may contain explicitly identified JSON or Ion-text arguments; that does not establish general Ion binary/reverse-encoding qualification.

Native and HTTP adoption need new exact closed mappings and actual end-to-end evidence. After Task 7, native/HTTP execution bundles 0.2.0-draft.1 stay strict and reject added policy members. The existing Rust protocol v1 and the regression proving no evaluation capability is inferred from v1 alone remain unchanged. A real TypeScript gateway/provider test establishes that host's behavior only. Generated backend execution and each packaged OS/architecture need their own implementation and qualification before advertisement.

Measured budgets and SDK limits

Source, selected-type, value and encoded-byte limits and interpreter fuel/depth/frame budgets remain mandatory. They do not establish a hard process-memory or CPU quota over opaque SDK internals. SDK operations such as String.repeat may allocate before result validation. Allocation/cancellation hardening is tracked separately in morphir-be5t. Worker deadlines and process controls have their own scope.

Retained constructor metadata above arity 256 is a preparation resource refusal, including dormant branches; unrelated constructors remain pruned. Actual Scheme Decimal results follow the existing SDK coefficient/exponent normalization law, preserving numeric value without a cohort/scale guarantee. Supplied completion validation performs no arithmetic and retains accepted wire representation. Accepted implementation decision: morphir-8n2g.

Workbench behavior

Reuse existing evaluation controls, reusable editors, typed fields/JSON/Ion inputs and terminal/diagnostic bottom panel. Keep the policy choice compact and explicit, with strict selected by default. Dynamic Scheme and worksheet mode remain separate from typed capability validation as code executes. Preserve original IR and generation diagnostics when typed Scheme evaluation can be supported independently of generation.

Scope capability to the actual runtime, entry and boundary. Before submission, a runtime or restored draft that cannot honor the requested selection shows an incompatibility reason and requires an explicit compatible choice. Never silently change policy. A running execution displays its captured selection and retains it after edits. Existing results, focus/navigation, cancellation, stale-result protection and code-area space remain covered by real browser and Proton acceptance.

Implementation sequence

Seven-slice implementation plan. Tasks 3 and 4 follow Task 2. The breaking execution migration, Task 7, follows those delivered slices and blocks native Task 5 and HTTP Task 6. The planning task can close after the design, implementation records, review and sync are complete. The implementation epic stays open. Merge/publication follow the existing maintainer approval rules.

SliceBlocked byDelivery
1. Run a supported function alongside unsupported codePlanning completeA supported public Int42 entry can be planned and evaluated beside a valid but unsupported unused declaration under an explicit private permissive selection. Omitted and explicit strict keep their existing behavior. This is the first internal tracer; no public runtime capability is advertised yet.
2. Report unsupported code only when execution reaches itTask 1The same known unsupported expression succeeds when its branch is not evaluated and fails with failed/evaluate/execution.unsupported_reached when reached. Supported results remain fully typed, and the complete local policy corpus passes independent checking before the local capability is exposed.
3. Retain the chosen runtime and checking policy for each executionTask 2A submitted policy, source, selected entry, arguments, boundary context and evaluator/provider selection are captured once. UI edits, reconnect, claim and replan cannot silently switch an accepted execution to another policy or runtime.
4. Expose capability checks in the standalone WorkbenchTask 2Explorer and Try Morphir offer an explicit policy choice for a selected public function only when the local evaluator supports it. A known unsupported operation in an untaken branch can evaluate; reaching it produces the existing terminal diagnostic presentation.
7. Replace Workbench job terminology with executionTask 3, Task 4Current Workbench clients and hosts use execution vocabulary end to end. This is an intentional pre-1.0 breaking migration: old job names, duplicate identity fields, wrappers and routes are removed, with no compatibility aliases or silent fallback.
5. Carry capability checks through desktop executionsTask 3, Task 4, Task 7A qualified native Proton session can explicitly negotiate and execute a permissive execution through its owned worker. Task 7 supplies the breaking execution contract; strict remains the default and unqualified combinations reject.
6. Carry capability checks through connected executionsTask 3, Task 4, Task 7A policy-aware authenticated HTTP host can advertise and honor an explicit permissive submission. Task 7 supplies the breaking execution contract. Strict-only execution providers keep their explicit support limits without permissive fallback.

Runtime audit and shared-contract audit retain detailed source citations. Source and module paths are implementation pointers, not public protocol names. This is a source-backed proposal; no runtime, protocol or platform support is introduced by this HTML document.

Domain-model correction morphir-etg2.17 is delivered in PR #134, squash 2222c9e. Tasks 5 and 6 retain the runtime/session lifecycle modeling work. Reuse the closed CapabilityPolicy type, decode evaluator identities and exact policy profiles into domain values, and model mutually exclusive runtime/session states explicitly. Keep validation and decisions in a functional core; transport and host effects belong in adapters. The separate Task 7 execution migration intentionally breaks pre-1.0 job-based contracts without compatibility aliases; unrelated historical identifiers remain outside that rename. Correction checklist and findings.

Desktop capability checking policies

morphir-etg2.16.5 is qualified and squash merged in both repositories: Workbench #136 and shared protocol #1061. The exact native 0.2.0-draft.2 offer enables the two checking policies for the bounded Scheme evaluator. The default stays Whole model before running; As code executes reports unsupported executable behavior when reached. Both policies retain source integrity and complete selected input/output boundary checks.

Submission captures the policy, provider, selected function and inputs once. Controlled MCK observations, actual workers and real picker checks are separate evidence. Other desktop platforms and native save-dialog behavior require their own qualification. This work does not add tree shaking or expand the evaluator capability set.

title: Elm backend follow-ups from the whole-branch review
description:
Follow-up items from the whole-branch review of the Elm backend (plan morphir-ukvn.5.22.1.1, range 1f8c9ad..bdeac81). None of these blocked the merge. Each one is a known limitation or a polish item.

Generation and validity:
- M2: elm_package_name does not apply Elm's package-name rules. A leading digit is rejected by elm make, and initialisms become s-d-k.
- M3: annotations on TypeSpecification and ModuleSpecification are dropped silently. Only value-specification annotations are written.
- M4: parse_mapping_entry does not check import text, the shape of function and type names, or operators against the krueger dialect. A mistake surfaces as elm.print instead of elm.invalid_mapping.
- M5 / T4: an import with an alias and one without, for the same module, overwrite each other. Keep a set of aliases for each module.
- M8: doc comments add a leading space and a blank line, which causes drift in the round trip in sub-project 3.
- T7: if all modules are private, they are exposed anyway. Zero modules gives an empty exposed-modules list. Output.dependencies can hold duplicates. morphir.json exposedModules uses a slice based on the prefix. The summary slice can cut a surrogate pair.
- T6: duplicate constructor names across types are not detected. Entry points with foreign targets and EntryPoint.doc are dropped. Native hint and description are lost. The print-error detail is a debug dump. The collision scan is O(n^2).
- T3: ElmPackageRef checks only the shape. range() falls back to major 0. Package keys are not validated. The builtin mapping is built twice in from_json.
- T8: there is no engine-level test of a refused elm generation diagnostic. The toml_json array path has no index. inf and nan floats are not checked. The build.unsupported_target message names the default target.
- T9: the README repeats the elm_package default. test-elm-make.mjs gives no hint when moon or node_modules is missing. There is no Linux arm64 elm binary. The Windows elm.exe path is untested.

Tests to add:
- constraint_of refusal paths; options edge cases; Value and Constructor resolution; specification types; tuple arity 0 and 1; scope restore after an error; LetRecursion; NaN float handling.
- Warnings: derive implicit_impl_as_method on ElmGenerationError and MappingEntry. Use `pub extend X with Eq::{...}` as pkgs/morphir-moonbit/types.mbt does.
