title: Scheme language docs: deferred polish from the language reference work
description:
Minor items deferred during morphir-ukvn.5.45.4 (Scheme language reference as package-level docs, branch DamianReeves/scheme-language-docs, commits 08dcb81..a446c1d). Each was reviewed and judged polish; none blocks the docs. Items fixed later in the same branch are not listed.

Site (apps/morphir-site)
- The both-kinds test covers only a package root and uses to_any_satisfy, so it does not prove the generic duplicate-route error is suppressed; add a sub-package case.
- nav_entries' PackagePart arm is not exercised through prepare.
- The README candidate paths duplicate classify's root conventions.
- The listed-chapter-has-no-README check (site/pages.mbt:210-220) also fires for a chapter skipped as a draft or one that already failed, and names site/site.json twice.

Generator (pkgs/morphir-typing-tools/schemedocs)
- The difference message reads "expected end of file, found end of file" for a missing final newline; the rewritten branches are untested beyond the three pinned cases.
- A chapter with zero examples emits an unused harness.
- The unreadable-chapter error drops the underlying IO error.
- The scheme-docs scripts copy the sdk-spec scripts.
- Duplicate file paths within one ;; file: project are not detected.
- example_at attributes blank lines before a header, and trailing text, to the preceding example.
- next_scheme_block_is_file matches only the exact opening fence, so a notest block between two file: blocks is skipped by the lookahead.
- discover.mbt's struct Plan is not priv and appears in pkg.generated.mbti.

Chapters (pkgs/morphir-scheme)
- The core procedure tables' example cells are not checked; only the blocks after them are.
- No checked example for the letrec early read, 4/2 reading as 2, or +5 being accepted.
- The core Embedding table omits the negative-arity messages of register_native_binding and replace_native_binding.
- A few sentences join two ideas (define shorthand and variadic note; the Limits paragraphs).
- Hard-wrapped prose fragments; doc_file helper ordering in docs_run_test.mbt; backend and frontend test imports reference each other's packages.
- frontend: the fill type_mismatch sentence for (* 2.5 2) is unchecked prose; the main-inputs sentence should say the last trailing expression's lambda.
- backend: the 256-level depth divergence row has no pinning check.

Pre-existing (not from this branch): deprecation warnings from morphir-ir/versions/v4/json, morphir-ir/wire, morphir-sdk/list and pipeline/bridge.mbt:25 appear in test output.

title: Workbench: minor follow-ups from the PR #111 reviews
description:
Minor findings parked during the reviews of finos/morphir-moonbit#111 (merged as 9c28e2b; Plan C morphir-ukvn.5.22.4.3 and the explorer redesign morphir-ukvn.5.22.4.4). None blocks; all were judged Minor. The review files lived in a deleted workspace, so the findings are copied here.

## Project explorer (apps/morphir-workbench/browser/project-files)
- Compaction keys a row by its innermost folder: deleting the last loose file of `src` changes the row from `src` to `src/Shop`, and a collapsed `src` is forgotten. A rename of a compacted row shows only the last segment.
- `build_tree` removes duplicates with `seen.contains` (quadratic) and runs at least three times per render (`visible`, `current`, `tree_view`). Noticeable at the 2,000-file import limit. Use a set and build the tree once per render.
- The "exposed" marker is an arrow that reads like "open in new tab".
- Mobile: the explorer takes about half of the first screen; give the band a maximum height with its own scroll.
- Chords use `KeyboardEvent.key`, so Mod+P does not fire on layouts where P is a non-Latin letter; fall back to `code`.
- `rename_folder` merges into an existing folder (file rules decide collisions); document it and pin it with a test.
- The palette combobox has `aria-expanded="true"` with an empty list; the inline Delete row puts buttons inside a `treeitem`.
- `removed_key` and `save_attempts` are test-only fields on the production `Model`.
- The palette lists 4 to 7 "Open sample: ..." entries in the default command list; the menu's "New from sample:" prefix repeats on every item (a `role="group"` labelled by the heading would say it once).
- An unknown sample id still bumps `sample_request` and cancels a pending Elm sample (reachable only from a stale menu).
- No Playwright step walks the menu's sample section with the arrow keys or checks disabled entries.

## Worker and pipeline (apps/morphir-workbench)
- Stage `evaluate`: `evaluate_model` and `evaluate_typed_with` read `entry` and `arguments`; a request missing one is labelled `workbench.internal_error`, not an invalid request. After `compile_reply`, a `run` operation keeps stage `reply`.
- `transport.ts` throws a synchronous `TypeError` for a `null` project (the old code rejected with the 16 MiB message).
- `Array.isArray(files)` on `unknown` narrows to `any[]` in `transport.ts`; use a guard over `unknown[]`.
- `native-session.ts` turns an object `project` on a `project` operation into `openProject('')`; reject it instead.
- Folder import: the pre-read guard in `readFiles` adds the size of a file that later turns out to be binary (a folder of large binaries can stop early; the limit is never exceeded).

## Failure details (browser/bottom-panel)
- `failure_detail` stringifies the whole IR only to count characters for omitted models.
- Details keys are strings such as `log-12`; an enum fits the domain-types rule. Definition rows and report lines are built twice.
- The raw reply is cut at 8,000 characters without a surrogate-safe cut.

## Binary Ion decode (apps/morphir-workbench/ion_decode.mbt)
- A timestamp's fractional-seconds coefficient (type 6) is not under the 64 KiB number limit.
- `least_text` gives no estimate for numbers, so the text budget is checked only after each number's text is built.
- The nested-annotation test may also pass if the reader itself rejects the chain, so it does not prove the walk refuses it.
- Playwright cannot reach a corrupt or non-Ion generated binary; those cases are covered by moon tests only.

## Build and tests
- The minified bundles (browser.js, job-core.js, worker.js) have no source maps; the handwritten bundles use `linked`.
- One `test:workbench` run timed out at the explorer workflow's last step (palette, "Reset project..." never selected); six later runs passed. `runCommand` now waits 10 s and prints the palette state if it recurs.
- The desktop app (Proton) was not run with the redesign; only its frontend build was checked.
- Loading a sample or importing a folder replaces a project without asking and without undo.

title: Elm wiring Plan A: test and style follow-ups
description:
Deferred minor review notes of morphir-ukvn.5.22.4 Plan A (none blocks merge, per the final review):
- plan.mbt: no test for the plan-time error of a malformed project.name or project.exposed_modules in a TOML Elm project.
- workspace/legacy_test.mbt: the bad-input test checks only that the message names morphir.json, not the field.
- engine.mbt Engine::run Workspace arm pipes into a closure (|> document => {...}); a plain statement reads better. No test for Workspace(root) without morphir.toml.
- elm/adapter_test.mbt: if_chain_files repeats the morphir.json literal instead of using elm_files; elm_report ignores format when backend is empty.
- acceptance/elm/main.mbt: discover gets only ["", directory]; nested member directories would be missed.
- source_providers_test.mbt: terse abort("ext") message.
- Duplicate exposedModules entries are accepted (morphir-elm does the same; decide).

title: Elm frontend accepts a self-referential let value that Elm refuses
description: The frontend lowers 'let loop = \n -> loop n in ...' (a let value, not a function, whose body refers to itself) to a LetRecursion. Elm 0.19.1 refuses it (a value cannot refer to itself; write 'loop n = loop n'). The backend now prints let functions with their arguments, which hides this in the round trip. Decide whether the frontend refuses it with a diagnostic, as Elm does. Found by the Plan 2 Task 8 review.

title: Elm frontend: morphir-elm reports ModuleCycleDetected when an SDK module path closes a cycle; the frontend does not
description: morphir-elm 2.100.0 builds the module DAG by module path only, so a project module whose path equals an SDK module path (for example basics or list) can close a cycle and fail with ModuleCycleDetected. The frontend does not copy this. Decide whether to copy the failure for parity or document the divergence (README Frontend rules).

title: website:install uses npm install; the CLI job's migrate:validate now depends on it
description: migrate:validate (finos/morphir rust-mirror-stage-1) depends on website:install because website/scripts/validate-migrated-ir.js needs ajv and ajv-formats. website:install runs npm install (unpinned) rather than npm ci, and it puts a full Docusaurus dependency install on the CLI job's critical path. Either switch website:install to npm ci --ignore-scripts, or give the validator a tiny tools/ Bun script with its own pinned ajv so the CLI job installs nothing from website/.

title: morphir CLI: unit test for install's ledger_path
description: crates/morphir/src/commands/install.rs gained ledger_path (forward-slash ledger keys so Windows installs recognise their own output). It is covered only indirectly by the nested-copy test; add a direct unit test asserting a Windows-style path renders with forward slashes.

title: morphir-rust: re-vendor the naming corpus (qualifiedModuleNameCases)
description: tools/gen-naming-corpus.ts also writes ecosystem/morphir-rust/tests/fixtures/naming-conformance.json. The parent corpus gained qualifiedModuleNameCases (package:module string form, decision 0015 consequences) but the vendored copy in morphir-rust was left untouched because that submodule is pinned separately. Run mise run fixtures:naming-corpus inside a morphir-rust change, commit the vendored copy there, and update the pointer; mise run fixtures:naming-corpus-check fails until then.
close_reason: finos/morphir-rust#149 (933fcf5) re-vendored the corpus; the parent repins it in finos/morphir#813 and the corpus check passes.

title: morphir-typescript release packaging tests fail under Git Bash on Windows (MSYS tar vs drive-letter paths)
description: scripts/release/package-ir.test.ts and package-mck.test.ts spawn 'tar' with absolute Windows paths. Under PowerShell that resolves to C:\Windows\system32\tar.exe (bsdtar) and all 27 tests pass; under Git Bash it resolves to MSYS GNU tar, which reads 'C:' as a remote host and exits 2, failing 3 tests ('tar failed with exit code 2'). Options: pass --force-local when GNU tar is detected, convert to POSIX paths under MSYS, or resolve tar via a Windows-first lookup. Add a note to the contributing docs meanwhile.

title: document-tree-files.md: cross-reference module access and list deps/ in the layout summary
description: Final-review nit from plan 2c. The Access Control section (docs/spec/ir/schemas/v4/document-tree-files.md, roughly lines 706-719) does not mention the module-level access member that the ModuleManifestFile now carries (written only when Private), and the layout summary near lines 1140-1155 still lists only pkg/ although deps/<package path>/... is now normative. Add the cross-reference and the deps/ row.

title: kb sync push: export target does not check symlinked subdirectories
description: sync push writes to resolve(target, path) where target is a user-named export directory, normally the upstream checkout. A symlinked subdirectory there would be followed. Same class as the mirror containment bugs fixed in #108, but deliberately left alone: the export target is not the mirror, and real upstream checkouts legitimately contain symlinks, so tightening it risks refusing valid exports. Decision (Damian, 2026-08-28): not hardening this now. Revisit if push ever writes somewhere less trusted than a checkout the user named, or if we grow a case where an export target is attacker-influenced.
